title: Define settlement correction, reversal uniqueness, and control-account projections
description:
References: §§5.6/5.7, 8.1/8.2, Appendix A/B/F (lines 419-423, 519-522, 536, 1165, 1241-1246, 1335, 1339).
Open amount = original minus summed SETTLES, but no immutable application-undo law is specified when a receipt or invoice is reversed/replaced. Reversing a settled receipt's GL legs leaves the invoice closed unless settlement effects reverse too; copying the original settles into the reversal can double-apply. Define versioned application effects and their bitemporal fold, target-side/unit validation, and over-application protection.
Acyclic SUPERSEDES plus exact target negation does not prevent two different idempotency keys from reversing/replacing one original twice. O + (-O) + (-O) is still acyclic and each reversal satisfies the local rule. Specify which reversal/replacement lifecycle actions are permitted and the concurrency witness; reversing a reversal must remain explicit if supported.
§5.6 says native detail postings inherently fold into the control account. The Register key schema has one account_ref, while only Leaf accounts accept legs. Define summary roll-up ownership, prohibit double counting and specify the externally fed detail-vs-summary representation so there is no second posting universe.
Acceptance: receipt applied then reversed; invoice replaced after partial application; concurrent duplicate reversals; two customers under an AR control account plus external-summary import. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.7 application effects versioned (open = original - SETTLES + UNSETTLES; reversals carry kernel-emitted unsettles; replacements re-declare, never copy); §8.2 reversal/replacement uniqueness by identity-derived vids (second reversal = AlreadyLive conflict; reversing a reversal explicit); §5.6 leaf-only register cells with rollup cells for summaries and external detail outside the book. FA-INV-08 clauses unsettle, reversed-once. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove the ungated full-byte document read (`Book::read_document`) that bypasses the privileged-caveat gate
description:
WHY: plan §9.6 interim posture: "privileged document bytes are stored in a separate PrivilegedDocument vertex class whose reads require the privileged caveat, evaluated by Steward before query construction — never as a result filter." fa-txf part C2 (88f4d46) implemented a gated `Book::read_document_for(capability, oid)` (crates/fa/src/book.rs:958) that derives redacted views, but the facade also exposes `pub fn read_document(&self, oid)` (book.rs:982) which calls `fa_journal::fetch_document` (crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:783) with no capability and returns the full canonical bytes of any document, privileged or not. Any embedding caller (and any future surface wired to it) bypasses the redaction contract.

WHAT: make the ungated path unreachable from the facade: either remove `read_document` (callers migrate to `read_document_for` with the embedded-owner capability, which must hold `privileged` to see privileged bytes) or make it `pub(crate)` for verification-only internals with a doc comment stating why; audit every caller of `fetch_document` (`rg -n fetch_document crates`) so each sits behind an admission check or is a verify-only path that never returns bytes to a caller; add a topology/grep gate in check.sh that fails if a public facade fn returns `Document` bytes without a `Capability` parameter.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: owner posture with `privileged` reads full bytes via read_document_for; [ ] planted negative: a non-privileged capability receives only the redacted view; a compile-fail or gate test proves no public ungated byte path exists; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core for documents); [ ] consumers: fa-txf, fa-6l9 productions, fa-7dw; [ ] no-claim boundary: protects bytes at the facade; storage-level access to the book directory is outside this boundary (book keys).

TESTS: fa facade tests; fa-cli `document` binary tests; the gate's planted negative (a scratch fn added in a test fixture crate) logged.

title: Lean lanes compiled in the gate and meaningful: theorems about the generated definitions (rounding bounds per law, largest-remainder conservation and per-share bound, period reachability, bitemporal monotonicity, reversal netting) with a theorem-inventory witness
description:
## WHY
After fa-2lsv, the plan §6.7/§16.7 Lean lanes must exist for real: `Amount` group laws, rounding error bounds per law,
allocation conservation per law, balance-law preservation under reversal/replacement/reclassification, supersession-net
correctness, bitemporal visibility, the period state machine's reachability (no Locked→Open without a case-bound Reopen),
escrow bounds.

## WHAT
`lake build` in check.sh (UNRUN when toolchain absent, never PASS); Lean definitions generated from rounding_laws.toml,
allocation_laws.toml, period_states.toml (generator diff in CI, existing); theorems: for each half-family law
|round(n,d)·d − n| ≤ d/2 and directed laws < d over Int with Euclidean division lemmas; largest-remainder over List
conserves the total and each share within one unit of exact; period relation inductive invariant; visibility monotone in
known_at; reversal of reversal nets to the original. Artifact (fa-vtzt): build log digest + theorem inventory (name +
statement hash); deleting/weakening a theorem fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] planted negatives: weakening the half-ulp bound to 1 ulp breaks the generated-definition proof; adding a Locked→Open

title: fa-sim-harness: lab runtime (asupersync lab + substrate lab VFS) with registered crash points at every pipeline barrier, seeded scheduling, DPOR over post-vs-close and the other registered races, crashpacks with replay commands, in-sim consistency oracles; Genesis campaign green under lab (G1)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): "Simulation-first (fa-sim)" is a design pillar (AGENTS.md verification ladder; plan §16) and Gate G1 requires the Genesis slice "green under lab and live". At 96d1918 there is no lab harness at all: no fa-sim-harness crate (W1 names it), no crash points, no DPOR, no crashpacks, no replay command; the only concurrency test is the policy-epoch race. The post-vs-close race that the doctrine calls "an SSI conflict, never a cron job's finding" is untested in either order. Every later workstream accrues its scenario campaigns onto this harness, so it is on the critical path to G1.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-sim-harness` (verification layer, test-only consumers): wraps asupersync's lab runtime (virtual time, seeded scheduling) and the substrate's lab VFS (torn writes, bit flips, ENOSPC, fsync lies) behind one `Lab { seed, schedule, vfs_faults }`; the facade `fa::Book` opens under it through the existing `Entropy::deterministic` and a lab `PurposeContexts` (no new API on Book that production code could reach).
2. Crash points at every pipeline barrier the kernel already has (admission, witnesses read, legs staged, mirrors moved, commit): a registered `CrashPoint` enum, each named in a `registries/crash_points.toml` row with the invariant it guards; the harness kills at each point and reopens; FA-INV-04/14/16 oracles (register-equals-fold, accumulator consistency, mirror-equals-payload) run after every reopen.
3. DPOR over post-vs-close, concurrent application, promotion-vs-trunk (when drafts exist), restatement-vs-reopen (when cases exist), sweep-vs-manual-void (fa-ctf): both orders explored; the winner is decided by first-committer-wins over witnesses, never by wall time.
4. Crashpacks: every failing seed writes `<scratch>/crashpacks/<seed>/` with the schedule, the VFS fault log and the exact `cargo test` replay command; the harness prints it; replay is byte-deterministic.
5. Consistency oracles as reusable in-sim checks: balance law, register-equals-fold, subledger-equals-control, admissibility at commit, SoD on approvals, idempotency stability, supersession acyclicity, accumulator consistency, bitemporal monotonicity, projection-equals-payload, erasure leaves amounts intact (those whose subsystems exist run; the rest are registered dormant with the activating bead).
6. Genesis campaign: the existing genesis/differential histories executed under the lab with 1,000 seeds and the full crash matrix; this is the G1 "green under lab" evidence.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-sim-harness genesis_campaign` runs the matrix green and prints the seed count and crash-point coverage (every registered point hit ≥ 10 times); post-vs-close DPOR explores both orders and each ends in exactly one committed winner; [ ] planted negatives: a harness mutation that skips mirror moves on reopen fails register-equals-fold; a VFS torn-write at the commit barrier with the oracle disabled is caught by the accumulator-consistency check; [ ] proof class: bounded_model (the matrix states its bounds: seeds, depth, fault classes); [ ] consumers: Gate G1, every later campaign, fa-ctf interleavings, fa-s7x promotion races; [ ] no-claim boundary: a green campaign is bounded evidence, never a proof of crash safety beyond the registered points and seeds.

TESTS: the harness has its own unit tests for determinism (same seed → same transcript) and for crashpack replay; campaign logs record seed, point, oracle verdicts; run through rch like every other test.

title: Verify a counterfactual scenario diff offline with its assumptions and scratch replay closure
description:
## Why
A6/A3 and plan §15.6 litigation workflow promise replayable but-for methodology; in-book scenario diff/replay exists. fa-k07b covers scratch replay inside the source book; fa-70h4 explicitly covers offline TB and two statement kinds, leaving offline scenario-diff methodology outside its acceptance. An offline trial balance of trunk alone cannot authenticate the assumed counterfactual computation.
## What to build
Add the scenario-diff report profile to the portable report contract after fa-70h4: authenticated trunk fork prefix, exact scenario body, ordered intents with planner authority/evidence, assumption documents, source registry epoch and method versions, SeqMap, scratch computation and canonical diff output. Standalone std-only fa-verify reproduces the declared scenario law, comparing every native/functional/account/entity row in declared scope. Counterfactual entries are explicitly assumed/scratch facts, never claimed as committed trunk members. Recipient supplies trust anchors and independently selected scope; changing assumptions changes the closure.
## Acceptance Criteria
- A source book can be absent/unavailable and the outsider still recomputes the retained scenario diff from its complete portable closure.
- Missing/reordered/changed intent, wrong fork, changed assumption, SeqMap mismatch, omitted output row and invalid historically asserted admission predicates or unsupported authority/method semantics cannot verify under a stronger claim.
- Later trunk/scenario mutations do not change historical artifact replay; unsupported semantic/registry versions give typed refusal.
```acceptance-tests
fa-verify::scenario_report::portable_counterfactual_diff_recomputes_without_book
fa-verify::scenario_report::tampered_fork_intent_and_assumption_each_fail
```
## Tests and logging
Known small but-for receipts schedule checked independently, then generated histories; compare in-book diff/replay with standalone verifier. Retain checkpoint, scope, assumptions, ordered intents, SeqMap, registry/method versions and per-predicate outcomes. No economic-truth or legal-damages claim. Companion public litigation workflow belongs in fa-y6eu.

Audit basis: source tree 3c964f1f07a91c3ad9b72eebcd1a95e7809f02c8 / ba83ac090e82779518a335691fc92ab2e5704278, 2026-10-21 local. Existing binary observations are SHA256-bound in /private/tmp/fa-reality-check-20261021.d9HmEI/manifest.json; those binaries predate HEAD and are not an exact-tree gate. All fixes require normal canonical Rust gates and published proof. No implementation was changed by the audit. Preserve all accounting features, authorization-before-observation, exact arithmetic, journal immutability and independent oracles. Never weaken a gate or regenerate a golden to accommodate incorrect output.

## Refinement: scope, time and independent evidence
Historical admission and current permission are distinct. Revocation before original admission may defeat the historical authorization claim; later revocation must not invalidate retained mathematical replay. Offline verification makes no claim of current disclosure authority without an independently trusted current authorization state. Declare a supported scenario intent/method profile and refuse unsupported semantics. Require complete authenticated fork inputs or an explicitly labeled authenticated baseline even for an EMPTY diff, unique output rows, recipient-chosen scope and bounded aggregate inputs. Reuse existing public proof/format contracts and the dependency-free verifier; never copy substrate code or introduce a second production accounting store. Semantic arithmetic is independently checked, not delegated back to the producer.

title: Read-path authorization: every read verb takes a capability evaluated before query construction, with account/period/entity/known_at caveats and whole-entry visibility (doctrine 8, FA-INV-10.whole-entry)
description:
WHY: doctrine 8 — "Capability caveats are enforced before any storage observation … by refusal before query construction. Never as a result filter." At e606b46 balance/trial-balance/explain reads take no capability at all (crates/fa/src/book.rs:1162-1212); `entries_at`/`report_at` fold the whole book (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:228-252, :910). The plan's Auditor (`known_at ≤ seq`), Regulator (scoped, time-boxed), and Production profiles, and the `accounts ⊆ subtree`, `periods`, `entities`, `dimensions` caveats are therefore unexpressible for reads. Separately, an Agent-profile capability is refused on document reads because the read is built with `trunk: true` and trips the trunk-write rule (crates/fa-journal/src/redaction.rs:548, crates/fa-policy/src/admit.rs:39) — reads and writes must be distinct admission classes.

WHAT:
1. fa-policy: `admit_read(capability, ReadScope { verb, coordinate, accounts?, periods?, entities? })` evaluated before any snapshot read; refusal FA-REF code naming the blocking caveat (catalog row); read admission never applies the trunk-write rule.
2. Facade/CLI/fad/MCP: every read verb (tb, explain balance, open-items, entry show, verify *, document read, checkpoint verify, registers materialize's read half) takes the session capability (fa-r3q) or the embedded-owner capability.
3. Whole-entry visibility (§14.2): an entry is observable iff every leg's account and dimensions are in scope; folds over in-scope accounts include in-scope legs of partially visible entries; `explain balance` marks `partially_visible` only under `partial_view`; certificates (fa-cqk) name the capability commitment; a partial fold is never labelled whole-book.
4. known_at caveat: an Auditor pinned `known_at ≤ s` cannot select a later coordinate (refusal), and historical selectors never resurrect revoked authority.
5. fa-reference: visibility model; differential on generated scopes.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: an Auditor token pinned at seq s reads tb at s and is refused at head; an account-subtree token's tb contains only that subtree and its certificate names the scope;
[ ] planted negatives: a read whose scope excludes an account the request names → refused before any snapshot read (proven by a counting probe: zero substrate reads on refusal); a partially visible entry without partial_view is not listed; an Agent token reading a document succeeds (regression for the trunk-write misfire);
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.whole-entry live) + differential;
[ ] consumers: fa-7dw, fa-zgn (engagements), fa-9ae certificates, examiners;
[ ] no-claim boundary: authorization of reads is enforced in FrankenAccounting before query construction (R-WARDEN interim), not by substrate predicate compilation.

TESTS: fa-policy unit; fa-journal/fa-registers kernel tests with a substrate read counter; CLI binary tests per verb; differential with seeds logged.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 2026-10-20 (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5): slice 3 — scoped tokens fail closed on the bound route; statements judged by basis

**Landed:** main and master by the owner's merge 335078ab ("Merge origin/train/fa-0x0-stormylion into main") of train/fa-0x0-stormylion @ 4728721b: 9893ef9c (fad clippy fix), dad518e6, c1d46e94, df97e444, 4728721b. The owner's ae2103b2 separately judged scope in export, event show|list and triage|next.

**The defect it closes.** Slices 1 and 2 judged scope only in the readers that call `ReadScope::admit_*`. On the bound route (fa --token, fad, MCP) every other command checked a token's ops and currency, but never its accounts, periods, effective, known_at or branch caveats. Two confirmed leaks:
- `fa statement` answered a March-only token with April's statement.
- `fa event show|list` judged no capability at all.

**What landed:**
- **Registry:** `registries/verbs.toml` `[[bound]]` rules take an optional key, `reach = "judged"`. fa-verbs parses it: `"judged"` is its only value, and a rule without ops cannot carry it.
- **Gate:** `admit_bound_command` and `bound_command_admissible` (which MCP lists tools by) judge `Reach::whole_book(true)` at the head for every rule that has ops and is not judged. So a token carrying any scope caveat is refused with FA-REF-011, exit 7, before the book is opened. The refusal names the command and the caveat, and its fix lists the judged commands.
- **Judged:** tb, open-items, explain, entry and the plain `fa statement <definition>`.
  - A statement's columns, current and comparative, are judged by their basis: stock is `stock_through` the latest period; activity is exactly its periods.
  - `--as-originally-reported` admits the selection before reading the period's transitions, then judges the pinned coordinate again.
- **Not judged:** `statement diff|trace` and certificate-sourced statements stay whole-book.
- **Writes are not marked judged.** The kernel judges a post's payload reach precisely. But the CLI reads a correction's target entry (`Book::read_entry`) and a settlement's open items before the kernel sees the write, so a scoped token is now refused for writes on the bound route.

**Tests:**
- `read_scope.rs::every_command_that_does_not_judge_its_reach_refuses_a_scoped_token` is registry-driven, so a new rule is covered the day it lands. For every unjudged rule whose ops fit the Preparer ceiling, it builds the command line that rule decides. It asserts a periods, an effective and a known-at token are each refused before the book is opened (book and coordinate null).
- `read_scope.rs::a_statement_reaches_what_its_basis_folds` covers inside-scope answers identical to the owner's, and periods, effective and known-at refusals.
- fa-verbs covers the judged set and planted refusals.

**Gate, as run by me:** workspace `clippy --all-targets --keep-going -D warnings` (sl23, vmi1153651) on b121cc17, the same code without the fad fix. It found no errors in any crate this slice touches; its only errors were main's fad lab_tests useless_vec, which 9893ef9c fixes. **I did NOT run the test step:** every eligible rch worker was out of disk (vmi1153651 and vmi1227854 are at 0.5 GiB). The new tests (read_scope.rs, read_scope_oracle.rs, fa-reference read_scope) have not been executed by me. The merge carries no fa-verdict note.

**Also in this landing:**
- **The model:** `fa_reference::read_scope::judge`, a literal model of read reach for the periods, effective and known_at caveats. It shares no code with the engine.
- **The differential:** `crates/fa/tests/read_scope_oracle.rs` runs 4000 deterministic cases of `Book::read_scope(..).admit_report` against the model. The cases cover stock, activity and as-of trial balances, explanations, open items, statements with comparatives, and an unknown period code.
- **Registered evidence:** the new tests are now FA-INV-10.core checkers and negatives.

**Proposal for account scopes (whole-entry visibility, next slice; comments welcome before I start):**
- **The constraint:** doctrine 8's interim posture allows only refusal before query construction. Folding entries and dropping out-of-scope legs would be a result filter. So the literal journal fold, which decodes every payload, cannot serve an `accounts` caveat.
- **What can serve it:** maintained register cells. They are keyed per account, and already hold the in-scope legs of partially visible entries, which is the plan's fold rule.
- **The proposal:** an accounts-scoped trial balance is answered from the scope's own cells only.
  - The scope is compiled by `fa_journal::policy::account_scope`, which walks only from the caveat's roots.
  - It is answered only at a frontier those cells serve exactly, with a zero-length tail; otherwise it is refused, naming the `accounts` caveat and the frontier the cells serve.
  - Its certificate names the capability commitment, and the report says it is a partial fold.
- **What follows:** explain balance under `partial_view`, and the fa-reference fold and explanation model with its differential.

**Still open on fa-0x0:**
- **Judging more readers precisely**, instead of refusing them:
  - event show/list, gl, chart/period list, document reads, export/proof/bundle (the Production profile's job, at its pin), verify, triage;
  - scoped writes, which first need the CLI's pre-write reads judged.
- **Accounts caveat / whole-entry visibility:** still refused outright in `admit_reads`.
- **Instant reads:** an `--as-known-at <instant>` read resolves TimeEvidence at the head before the scope judgment.

## 2026-10-20 (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5): slice 3 — scoped tokens fail closed on the bound route; statements judged by basis

**Landed:** main and master by the owner's merge 335078ab ("Merge origin/train/fa-0x0-stormylion into main") of train/fa-0x0-stormylion @ 4728721b: 9893ef9c (fad clippy fix), dad518e6, c1d46e94, df97e444, 4728721b. The owner's ae2103b2 separately judged scope in export, event show|list and triage|next.

**The defect it closes.** Slices 1 and 2 judged scope only in the readers that call `ReadScope::admit_*`. On the bound route (fa --token, fad, MCP) every other command checked a token's ops and currency, but never its accounts, periods, effective, known_at or branch caveats. Two confirmed leaks:
- `fa statement` answered a March-only token with April's statement.
- `fa event show|list` judged no capability at all.

**What landed:**
- **Registry:** `registries/verbs.toml` `[[bound]]` rules take an optional key, `reach = "judged"`. fa-verbs parses it: `"judged"` is its only value, and a rule without ops cannot carry it.
- **Gate:** `admit_bound_command` and `bound_command_admissible` (which MCP lists tools by) judge `Reach::whole_book(true)` at the head for every rule that has ops and is not judged. So a token carrying any scope caveat is refused with FA-REF-011, exit 7, before the book is opened. The refusal names the command and the caveat, and its fix lists the judged commands.
- **Judged:** tb, open-items, explain, entry and the plain `fa statement <definition>`.
  - A statement's columns, current and comparative, are judged by their basis: stock is `stock_through` the latest period; activity is exactly its periods.
  - `--as-originally-reported` admits the selection before reading the period's transitions, then judges the pinned coordinate again.
- **Not judged:** `statement diff|trace` and certificate-sourced statements stay whole-book.
- **Writes are not marked judged.** The kernel judges a post's payload reach precisely. But the CLI reads a correction's target entry (`Book::read_entry`) and a settlement's open items before the kernel sees the write, so a scoped token is now refused for writes on the bound route.

**Tests:**
- `read_scope.rs::every_command_that_does_not_judge_its_reach_refuses_a_scoped_token` is registry-driven, so a new rule is covered the day it lands. For every unjudged rule whose ops fit the Preparer ceiling, it builds the command line that rule decides. It asserts a periods, an effective and a known-at token are each refused before the book is opened (book and coordinate null).
- `read_scope.rs::a_statement_reaches_what_its_basis_folds` covers inside-scope answers identical to the owner's, and periods, effective and known-at refusals.
- fa-verbs covers the judged set and planted refusals.

**Gate, as run by me:** workspace `clippy --all-targets --keep-going -D warnings` (sl23, vmi1153651) on b121cc17, the same code without the fad fix. It found no errors in any crate this slice touches; its only errors were main's fad lab_tests useless_vec, which 9893ef9c fixes. **I did NOT run the test step:** every eligible rch worker was out of disk (vmi1153651 and vmi1227854 are at 0.5 GiB). The new tests (read_scope.rs, read_scope_oracle.rs, fa-reference read_scope) have not been executed by me. The merge carries no fa-verdict note.

**Also in this landing:**
- **The model:** `fa_reference::read_scope::judge`, a literal model of read reach for the periods, effective and known_at caveats. It shares no code with the engine.
- **The differential:** `crates/fa/tests/read_scope_oracle.rs` runs 4000 deterministic cases of `Book::read_scope(..).admit_report` against the model. The cases cover stock, activity and as-of trial balances, explanations, open items, statements with comparatives, and an unknown period code.
- **Registered evidence:** the new tests are now FA-INV-10.core checkers and negatives.

**Proposal for account scopes (whole-entry visibility, next slice; comments welcome before I start):**
- **The constraint:** doctrine 8's interim posture allows only refusal before query construction. Folding entries and dropping out-of-scope legs would be a result filter. So the literal journal fold, which decodes every payload, cannot serve an `accounts` caveat.
- **What can serve it:** maintained register cells. They are keyed per account, and already hold the in-scope legs of partially visible entries, which is the plan's fold rule.
- **The proposal:** an accounts-scoped trial balance is answered from the scope's own cells only.
  - The scope is compiled by `fa_journal::policy::account_scope`, which walks only from the caveat's roots.
  - It is answered only at a frontier those cells serve exactly, with a zero-length tail; otherwise it is refused, naming the `accounts` caveat and the frontier the cells serve.
  - Its certificate names the capability commitment, and the report says it is a partial fold.
- **What follows:** explain balance under `partial_view`, and the fa-reference fold and explanation model with its differential.

**Still open on fa-0x0:**
- **Judging more readers precisely**, instead of refusing them:
  - event show/list, gl, chart/period list, document reads, export/proof/bundle (the Production profile's job, at its pin), verify, triage;

- **Accounts caveat / whole-entry visibility:** still refused outright in `admit_reads`.
- **Instant reads:** an `--as-known-at <instant>` read resolves TimeEvidence at the head before the scope judgment.

comments.text:
2026-10-23 (claude-opus-5-5 / LavenderSwan): a finding on the remaining "read counter" item; no code. Status is unchanged.

**The acceptance asks for** a scoped read that is refused before any snapshot read, "proven by a counting probe: zero substrate reads on refusal". The pinned substrate (fgdb b323bd17) has no public read counter.
- The only counter is `vertex_reads: Cell<usize>`, private to the limited-GQL reader in `write_txn_parts/limited_gql.rs`.
- `Database` exposes no read statistics.

**Why a lab-VFS event count would not be evidence:** committed reads are served from the in-memory store, so a refused read would show zero VFS events whether or not it observed storage. That probe would pass even if the refusal came after a full scan.

**An honest probe needs one of these:**
- (a) an upstream `Database` read meter: vertex, edge, property and `delta_since` reads per purpose context, counted on the read path. This is a substrate request.
- (b) a FrankenAccounting-level read seam that every snapshot read goes through (fa-journal and fa-registers reads use `db.vertex(...)`, `db.vertices()` and `db.delta_since(...)` directly today), with a counting implementation in tests.

(b) is a design change to every read path, so the bead's owner should choose it deliberately; it isn't a test-only addition.

title: Key-file permissions are never checked (plan §15.3 exit 4) and fad.lease is created or truncated in any --book directory, following symlinks: check 0600/owner on every key load, take the lease only in a verified book directory, never for discovery commands, never through a symlink
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14 at 9e83c3f)
- **Key-file permissions are never checked.** `book.keys` is read with no mode check (crates/fa/src/book.rs:174-215). Plan §15.3 maps wrong permissions on the three-line DatabaseKeys file to exit 4 with a fix, and App H R-KEY says the 0600 key file is managed by fad.
- **The lease file is created anywhere.** `Lease::acquire` creates or truncates `<dir>/fad.lease` in whatever directory `--book`/`FA_BOOK` names (crates/fad/src/lease.rs:84-107). This happens even during discovery commands and in directories that are not books, and it follows symlinks.

## What to build
1. On every key load, refuse when the mode is wider than 0600 or the owner differs from the process uid. Exit 4, with a catalog code naming the path, the observed mode and `chmod 600 <path>` as the fix. `fa doctor` reports the same check.
2. Only acquire the lease inside a directory that passes the book-identity check, and never for discovery commands (help, version, capabilities, robot-docs).
3. Open the lease file with O_NOFOLLOW (or check `symlink_metadata` first, through asupersync's fs).
4. Create the lease file without truncating an existing non-lease file.

## Acceptance
Each failure case below has a planted test, and each one leaves the file system unchanged (compare hashes and mtimes):
- a key file at 0644 → exit 4;
- `--book` pointing at a non-book directory → no lease file created;
- a symlinked `fad.lease` → refused;
- `fa --help` with `FA_BOOK` set → no lease file created.

## Tests & logging
fa-cli and fad tests with tempdirs. Each case logs the path, the observed mode, the decision and the refusal id.
close_reason: Implemented FA-REF-155 (KEY_FILE_PERMISSIONS), enforced 0600 + same-UID key-file permissions in BookKeys::load_with_vfs and fa doctor, hardened Lease::acquire and Lease::holder with O_NOFOLLOW + UnixVfs::symlink_metadata + 0600 create_new + non-lease file protection, prevented non-book and discovery commands from creating .fa-writer.lease or store/ directories, and added comprehensive planted tests in crates/fa-cli/tests/writer_entry.rs.

title: Certification must not invalidate plans: plans bind to the accounting frontier, not raw HEAD; a read-only session's --certify cannot break other principals' outstanding plans
description:
## The defect
An MCP session launched as Agent with only `read` can call fa_read_trial_balance with certify: true.
That retains a Certificate (Book::retain_certificate, book.rs ~1182, takes no capability) and advances
the book frontier, so every outstanding PostPlan then fails FA-REF-034 (plan.rs ~330: exact basis
sequence). A read-only principal can thus invalidate everyone's reviewed plans — and the Agent profile
is documented as never writing trunk.

## Design options (pick one, document the choice)
A (preferred): plans bind to the *accounting frontier* = the highest commit sequence that changed any
state a plan witnesses (entries, periods, policies, approvals, capabilities, limits, chart). Pure
metadata (certificates, access events, checkpoints) does not move it. Commit re-validates the plan's
witness set at the current snapshot exactly as today.
B: certification by Agent profiles writes to a session-local or draft store, never trunk.
Either way, retaining a certificate requires `read` + an explicit `certify` op (or `produce`).

## Tests
Agent certifies a TB between another principal's plan and commit → commit succeeds; an accounting change
in between → PlanInvalidated (FA-REF-034) as before; certification without the op is refused.
acceptance_criteria: The three scenarios behave as stated through the library, CLI and MCP.
close_reason: Bound PostPlan to accounting frontier via delta_since metadata classification and basis/birth-ordinal-independent effects_digest, enforced read capability on Book::retain_certificate_authorized, and verified across fa-journal, fa-cli, and fa-mcp e2e_stdio

comments.text: 2026-10-13 (CobaltGull): not a quick win, and option A crosses a registered contract. crates/fa-journal/src/plan.rs commit_plan requires `db.frontier() == certificate.snapshot_seq` and then `prepared.basis() == snapshot_seq`, and recorded_plan anchors a retried plan's outcome to exactly basis+1 (Appendix H R-POST-PLAN "exact basis"). Binding plans to an accounting frontier means: classify every commit in (basis, head] via delta_since as metadata-only (report certificates, access events, checkpoints) or accounting; re-prepare at head and compare effects_digest instead of basis; and re-anchor recorded_plan (the entry's created_at is no longer basis+1). Option B (Agent certification writes to a session/draft store) depends on drafts (fa-s7x). The owner's MCP e2e deliberately asserts that an Agent can certify, so "certify requires produce" was rejected. Needs a ruling between A and B before code.

title: Tier-0 gate that can never be skipped: fmt + `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` on every tree before it becomes main (folds, merges, direct pushes)
description:
## WHY
Today two different red trees reached main within ten minutes: 9c34c53 (fa did not compile: E0616 private field
`AsyncBook::context` used from crates/fa/src/fx_revaluation.rs:71,212; fixed by 195427e) and 11df0f1 (a train fold that
spliced the fa-kaf7 audit-cluster test into the middle of `inline_fx_rates_keep_agent_provenance_…` at
crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs:3517, so `cargo test --workspace` cannot even parse that target). HEAD 0d338c0 inherits
the second break. Both would have been caught by a cheap type-check of all targets (~6 min warm). The full gate is often
UNRUN because the rch fleet is under disk pressure; agents then fold anyway. A tier that is cheap enough to always run
removes that excuse.

## WHAT
1. `scripts/tier0.sh` (verdict contract, scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh): `cargo fmt --all --check` and
   `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets` with the same completion-marker rules as check.sh.
2. merge_train.sh `run`/`run-batch` and every documented "Fold … from train/…" path call tier0 on the merged tree and
   refuse to update main on anything but PASS; UNRUN means "do not fold yet", never "fold anyway".
3. scripts/hooks/pre-push refuses a push to main unless tier0 PASS is recorded for that exact tree hash (local note
   under refs/notes/fa-tier0) — installed by scripts/install-hooks.sh.
4. AGENTS.md section "Mandatory Checks" documents tier 0 / tier 1 (check.sh) / tier 2 (campaigns, oracles, models,
   benches) and states that RULE 0 owner overrides still require tier 0.
5. Availability: tier 0 must not freeze main whenever the rch fleet is under disk pressure (observed 2026-10-20: 3
   workers critical, "no admissible workers"). Because it is a type-check, not a test run, tier0.sh may use rch's local
   lane on the designated gate host when the fleet refuses; the transcript records which lane ran and its host
   fingerprint. Fleet capacity itself is a sibling bead (gate capacity).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: a fold of two green trains passes tier0 and updates main; tier0 transcript names both steps PASS.
- [ ] planted negative: a candidate with a syntax error in any test target (replay the 11df0f1 splice) is refused and main
  does not move; a candidate with a private-field error in a lib (replay 9c34c53) is refused.
- [ ] planted negative: pre-push to main without a recorded tier0 PASS for the tree is refused.
- [ ] proof class: invariant of the landing protocol (every main tip has a tier0 PASS note).
- [ ] no-claim boundary: tier 0 proves the tree compiles and is formatted, nothing about test results.

```acceptance-tests
scripts/tests/tier0_selftest.sh::refuses_test_target_syntax_error
scripts/tests/tier0_selftest.sh::refuses_lib_type_error
scripts/tests/tier0_selftest.sh::pre_push_requires_tier0_note
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Self-test script in the style of scripts/merge_train_selftest.sh with planted candidates in a throwaway repo; every run
logs tree hash, toolchain, step verdicts and durations; shellcheck clean.
close_reason: Implemented unskippable Tier-0 gate in scripts/tier0.sh (gate_verdict.sh contract, completion markers, local-lane fallback on rch refusal with lane/host fingerprint), wired tier0 into scripts/merge_train.sh (run, run-batch, fold), enforced refs/notes/fa-tier0 on main/master in scripts/hooks/pre-push, documented Tier 0/1/2 in AGENTS.md, and added scripts/tests/tier0_selftest.sh (all 6 scenarios and shellcheck green).

title: Lantern procedures run under a stripped Cx (no clock, entropy, IO) with cancellation and budget checked inside the run
description:
## WHY
Doctrine 3: "every Lantern procedure execute[s] under a Cx with no clock, entropy, network, or filesystem capability".
crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs:663 `Procedure::run(&self, snapshot, book, work)` and snapshot.rs:99 `Snapshot::read` take
no Cx; the work budget is checked only after the procedure finishes (~801-805). A runaway graph procedure cannot be
cancelled, and nothing structurally prevents a procedure from reading the clock.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `sed -n '655,670p' crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs` → `Procedure::run(&self, snapshot, book, work)` takes no Cx.
2. Run `fa procedure run graph.layering` with a tiny work budget on the shell-network demo book → the procedure runs to completion and only then is the budget compared (~lib.rs:801-805).

## WHAT
`Procedure::run(&self, cx: &ProcedureCx, …)` where ProcedureCx is a narrowed asupersync context with TIME/RANDOM/IO false;
loops call `cx.checkpoint()?` (cancellation + deterministic budget); budgets are registered per procedure in
procedures.toml; exceeding returns a typed refusal with partial-work counters, never a partial finding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: every registered procedure runs under ProcedureCx in the existing tests.
- [ ] planted negatives: a procedure that calls a time API does not compile (no capability); a budget of 10 steps on
  graph.layering over the shell-network corpus refuses mid-run with exit 3 and no finding journaled; cancellation
  observed within one checkpoint interval.

```acceptance-tests
fa-lantern::tests::procedures_run_under_stripped_cx
fa-lantern::tests::budget_exhaustion_refuses_mid_run
fa-lantern::tests::cancellation_is_observed_inside_run
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: ProcedureCx capability tests; per-procedure budget unit tests. E2E: `fa procedure run graph.layering --budget 10` on a demo book refuses with exit 3 and journals nothing (real binary). Also: complexity witnesses for all 60 procedures (plan §11.1 "complexity bound witness-locked in CI"; today 14/60, lantern.rs:2377-2462). Logging: refusals report steps consumed, budget, last checkpoint location.
close_reason: Verified on vmi1152480: added Work::registered_bounds, Work::registered_budget, and default_budget(procedure, snapshot) deriving per-procedure work budgets from registries/procedures.toml complexity bounds; expanded source-scan check to all 28 files in crates/fa-lantern/src; and added fa-lantern::tests::{procedures_run_under_stripped_cx, budget_exhaustion_refuses_mid_run, cancellation_is_observed_inside_run} (85 passed, 0 failed; clippy -D warnings exit 0).

**Plan:**

- `Meter::entry`, `leg` and `compare` are fallible. A run that passes its budget stops at that charge with `BudgetExhausted` and returns no finding.

- Procedures receive no `Cx`. fa-lantern's clippy.toml disallows clock, entropy, filesystem, network, env, process and thread APIs, so a procedure that reads the clock fails the clippy gate. This replaces the textual source scan, which missed five source files and every alias.
- The facade runs every production procedure under its query context. `fa procedure run --budget <units>` makes the budget reachable from the CLI.

**Not in this slice:** budgets registered per procedure in procedures.toml, and complexity witnesses for the remaining procedures.

**Files:** crates/fa-lantern/src/** (signatures and `?` at each charge), crates/fa-lantern/clippy.toml, crates/fa/src (run paths), and the fa-cli procedure handler with its verbs.toml flag.

title: fa-mcp containment: never accept `as`/`grant`/`yes`/`keys` from tool arguments; bind the server's principal and Agent-profile capability at launch; stop the self-approval detector coaching impersonation
description:
WHY: verified at e606b46 — fa-mcp turns agent-supplied tool arguments into fa argv including `--as <principal>`, `--grant <op>`, `--yes` and `--keys <path>` (crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:1381-1388; global flags validated as exposed at :353; unit test :1775-1800 asserts `{"grant":"post_closed","yes":true}` becomes `--grant post_closed --yes`). Every fa-cli handler then self-issues a Human capability for that principal and those ops (`Capability::embedded`, crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247). So the MCP surface — the surface built for AI agents — gives an agent full Human authority, lets it choose its identity per call (defeating segregation of duties: plan as `operator`, approve as `controller`), and lets it bypass dangerous-operation gating by passing `yes: true`. The self-approval detector (crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:478-492) answers a detected self-approval with "call fa_time_approve with `as` set to a different, admissible principal" plus a suggested tool call `{"as": "<another principal>"}`: the exact impersonation the plan's §14.3/§14.4 forbid. This is the cheapest high-value fix in the reality check and can land before the full issuance model (fa-v62/fa-r3q).

WHAT:
1. Server launch configuration (CLI args of the fa-mcp binary, never tool arguments): `--book <dir>`, `--keys <file>`, `--principal <name>`, `--profile agent|preparer` (default `agent`), optional `--grant <op>` list bounded by the profile (an Agent profile cannot hold approve/close/reopen/restate/post_closed/migrate/witness/issue_capability/erase). Until fa-v62 lands, the server self-issues exactly one capability at launch from this config and labels every response `authority: {posture: "mcp-launch-config", principal, profile, ops}`.
2. Tool schemas: remove `as`, `grant`, `yes`, `keys` and `book` overrides from every tool's input schema; the argument normalizer refuses them if present with a structured error `{type: "forbidden_argument", data: {fix_hint: "identity and authority are fixed when the server starts; ask the operator to start a server with the profile you need", argument}}` (never silently ignores them).
3. Dangerous operations through MCP require a `confirm_plan` certificate once fa-we7 lands; until then they are refused through MCP with the safe alternative (`--dry-run`/plan file for lock/reopen) — an agent never confirms its own dangerous op with `yes`.
4. Self-approval detector: the fix text names the policy row and says a second, independent approver (a human or a separately launched approver session holding approve) must approve; the suggested tool call is removed. Same audit for every other detector's fix text (`grep -n '"as"' crates/fa-mcp/src`).
5. verbs.toml `[mcp]` rows and the robot-schema pin updated; parity tests updated deliberately (show the before/after diff in the commit message).
6. `fa capabilities --json` and the MCP `robot_docs`/server instructions state the actual binding posture.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: an fa-mcp e2e (stdio) session launched with `--profile agent --principal agent-7` can call read tools and `post` on a draft-less book and receives FA-REF-013 (Agent-on-trunk) with the drafts pointer — proving the Agent profile now reaches the kernel from a real surface;
[ ] planted negatives (each reaches exactly one check): a tool call carrying `as` → forbidden_argument; carrying `grant` → forbidden_argument; carrying `yes` → forbidden_argument; a server launched `--profile agent --grant approve` refuses to start with the profile-bound reason; the self-approval detector's output contains no `as` override and no suggested approve call;
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core reached from the MCP posture) + e2e;
[ ] consumers: every MCP host, fa-ohe, fa-z5u (fad-hosted MCP);
[ ] no-claim boundary: launch configuration is trusted operator input; this does not authenticate the operator (fa-v62/fa-r3q do).

TESTS: crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs cases above with the full JSON-RPC transcript logged on failure; registry.rs unit tests replacing the current `grant`/`yes` pass-through test (the old test is restated, not deleted: it becomes the negative); detect.rs unit test for the new self-approval text.
close_reason: Verified on main (6abaf42): fa-mcp principal/capability launch containment and self-approval guidance landed and tested in crates/fa-mcp/tests/mcp.rs.

title: Kernel settlement ignores the legal-entity dimension: a receipt for entity A can settle entity B's invoice on the same account

(crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1419-1434). `fa/src/settlement.rs` enforces "same dimensions" only at the
surface layer, so any library or future surface that bypasses it violates per-entity balance semantics
(§4.1, §5.2, §5.7). Also confirm the reference oracle's settlement model includes the entity.

## What to build

(legal_entity at minimum, every registered balancing dimension in general); refuse with a catalog code
naming both entities. Oracle mirrors it independently.

differential over generated multi-entity histories green.

## Tests & logging

title: Teller reconciliation: bank statement parsers to BankLine documents with import receipts, matching engine as adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback, journaled Match objects with exact residual explanations, reconciliation register verified by fold with RegisterEquals attestations, three-way matching, fa bank import / fa reconcile
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Teller is bank reconciliation: bank statement parsers producing BankLine documents (W4), a matching engine whose heuristics are adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback (AGENTS.md adaptive-decision contract), a reconciliation register and attestations. At 96d1918 there is no Teller code (2 prose hits). fa-ff6 (bank feeds through flywheel_connectors) presumes BankLine documents and the matching engine, so it depends on this bead. Reconciliation is also one of Lantern's procedures and one of the registers the plan verifies by fold.

WHAT:
1. Bank statement parsers in `fa-formats` (interop) for CSV/OFX/CAMT.053 subsets, exact amounts (fa-money), every line a content-addressed `BankLine` document (Docket) with the statement's import receipt (Docket slice 2) and `DERIVED_FROM` the statement document; fuzzed readers.
2. `crates/fa-teller` (analytics): candidate generation (amount, date window, counterparty normalization, reference tokens), scoring as an adaptive decision: the decision card records the policy epoch, state space, candidates, observed features, the expected-benefit interval and the pinned fallback (exact amount + date within N days + reference equality, deterministic tie-break by lowest entry ordinal); learned scores are advisory features only; the card never changes a committed amount.
3. Match decisions as journaled, immutable objects (`Match { bank_line_ref, entry_ref | None, decision_card_ref, principal }`), one-to-many and many-to-one with exact residual explanations (fees, FX) that must be posted as their own entries under a named law, never absorbed; unmatching is a new object with lineage.
4. The reconciliation register: per bank account × period, book balance vs statement balance with the outstanding items list as a fold of matches and bank lines; `fa verify reconciliation` refolds it; reconciliation attestations bind `cell_key + fold_digest` (RegisterEquals).
5. Three-way matching (PO/receipt/invoice) as the same engine over documents, registered as a Lantern procedure.
6. CLI: `fa bank import <file> --account <code> --json`, `fa reconcile <account> --for <period> [--dry-run] --json` (plans the matches as intents with certificates; `--yes` or confirm_plan to commit), `fa reconcile status`.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: on a fixture statement every unambiguous line matches under the pinned fallback alone (learned features disabled) and the register folds to the statement balance; replaying the decision cards reproduces every match bit-for-bit; [ ] planted negatives: a card whose fallback is removed is refused at registration; a match that would change an amount is refused; a fee residual not posted under a law leaves the register out of balance and `verify reconciliation` says so; [ ] proof class: invariant (register-equals-fold, card replay) + statistical (match quality on the labelled corpus); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, Lantern reconciliation procedure, CPAs; [ ] no-claim boundary: a reconciled register proves matches were recorded and the fold ties, not that every match is economically correct.

TESTS: parser tests with exact-amount vectors, fa-teller unit tests on labelled corpora with per-line logs, fa-reference naive matcher differential for the fallback, CLI binary tests.
close_reason: Implemented Teller reconciliation (plan §9.5, §15.9, §12.5): ISO 20022 camt.052, CSV, and SWIFT MT940 bank statement parsers alongside camt.053, BAI2, and OFX/QBO in fa-formats::bank; DecisionCard fallback validation and decide_bank_match in fa-policy::decision; ReconciliationMatch, ResidualExplanation, ReconciliationRegister, fold_reconciliation_register, verify_reconciliation_register, check_reconciled_through_lock, match_bank_lines (1:1, 1:N, N:1, N:M), and match_three_way (PO/Receipt/Invoice) in fa-registers::reconciliation; and independent Int-limb reference oracles in fa-reference::reconciliation.

title: Multi-seed model-generated differential with a serial-equivalence oracle and coverage-guided intent generation (engine vs fa-reference)
description:
## WHY
G1 requires "the reference differential over model-generated histories". The engine-vs-reference differential
(fa-registers/tests/differential.rs:1898) runs one seed (:1901), 640 steps, 4 dates, 3 leaf accounts, generated by an RNG
inside the test; correction/batch/draft differentials use 2–3 seeds; statements and findings are not compared there.
fa-0fl owns the lab harness; this bead owns the generator and oracles, which also run without the lab.

## WHAT
A history generator (fa-gen grammar) over the whole intent catalog that exists (posts, holds, resolutions, reversals,
replacements, reclasses once fa-xvba lands, period transitions, migrations, batches, drafts), steered by a coverage map of
(entry class × period state × refusal code) toward unhit cells; ≥ 1,000 seeds in tier 2, 50 in tier 1; comparisons:
every outcome and refusal code, every register cell, statements, open items, explain balance, findings for procedures
with naive reference forms; serial-equivalence oracle: the committed history replayed serially in CommitSeq order through
fa-reference equals the engine state; failing seeds shrink by delta debugging into a minimal reproducer committed as a
regression test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: 1,000 seeds green; coverage map shows every reachable cell hit; artifact recorded (fa-vtzt lab-campaign kind).
- [ ] planted negatives: a kernel mutation admitting Original in Closed is found within 50 seeds and shrunk to ≤ 10 steps.

```acceptance-tests
fa-registers::differential::multi_seed_campaign_tier1
fa-registers::differential::serial_equivalence_oracle
fa-registers::differential::planted_mutation_found_and_shrunk
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: generator grammar and shrinker. E2E: tier-1 50-seed run in check.sh; tier-2 1,000 seeds. Logging: per seed coverage cells hit, first divergence (step, intent, engine vs reference values), shrunk reproducer path.

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-22: claimed. Slices 1 and 2 landed on main (ce689f95, 8b61a46d).

**What changed:**
- The generated-history differential (fa-registers tests/differential.rs) is now generated_history_campaign(seed) -> Coverage.
- kernel_and_oracle_agree_on_a_generated_history keeps its seed and asserts every per-seed floor.
- New kernel_and_oracle_agree_on_generated_histories_across_seeds runs 8 SplitMix64 seeds (FA_DIFFERENTIAL_SEEDS=<n> for tier 2):
  - every per-step agreement and post-loop check holds per seed;
  - the coverage floors hold for the total;
  - a seed with nothing to corrupt skips only the corruption plant.

**Findings:**
- No kernel/reference divergence over the 8 seeds.
- Per-seed floors are seed luck. Seed 0xe220a8397b1dcdaf made FA-REF-080 twice and never FA-REF-051, and 490 of its 640 steps were FA-REF-053 reversals. That's the uncoordinated generator the coverage map should replace.

**Planted negative (acceptance):** registries/mutants.toml MUT-035 skips the op an admissibility cell requires (post_closed in a Closed period).
- Both tests kill it: at step 178 the reference refuses FA-REF-011 and the mutant goes on to FA-REF-002.
- The multi-seed run names seed 2 of 8.
- Verified by applying the mutation in a scratch tree and reverting it.

**Slice 2 (same landing): failing histories shrink.**
- `campaign(seed, schedule, plant)`. A full run records each step: its index, the xorshift state it started from, and the deterministic plant it fired.
- `Schedule::Steps` replays chosen steps from their recorded states. Plants fire only where the full run fired them, so a subset is the same history less the skipped steps.
- ddmin (complements first) reduces a failing schedule. The predicate is the same `step N:` divergence marker, so another kind of harness panic never counts.

A fresh reference re-admits every entry into the same period and every transition between the same states, and ends with the same registers, pending registers, open items and period states. title: Reachability gate: every pub library module is reachable from a surface binary or registered in unwired_modules.toml with owner bead and expiry
description:
## WHY

## WHAT

exemptions {path, owner_bead, reason, expires}. check.sh step `reachability` fails on an unreached module without a live
exemption or with an expired one. Seed the registry with today's unreached modules, each pointing at its bead
(fa-qh60, fa-nwgf, fa-76hy, fa-22v5, fa-259c …) and a 30-day expiry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] planted negatives: a new pub module with no caller and no exemption fails; an expired exemption fails.

```acceptance-tests
tools/xtask::reachability::tests::unreached_module_without_exemption_fails
tools/xtask::reachability::tests::expired_exemption_fails
```

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-22: claimed. Landed on main as 946288a2. Status stays in_progress until a local_proof manifest covers it (close_bead.sh).

**What works:**
- `xtask reachability` (tools/xtask/src/reachability.rs):
  - Starts from every non-test source file of fa-cli, fad, fa-mcp, fa-verify, xtask and registry-check, walks module files through `mod name;`, and follows references into the library crates.
  - What counts as a reference:
    - an imported or path-qualified segment or top-level item, through crates that re-export the module's crate;
    - a glob import;
    - a same-crate path or a crate-unique item;
    - a `.method(` call on a method name only one crate defines.
  - What doesn't count: comments, strings, cfg(test) items, and use/mod declarations.
  - Reported: pub modules, and crate roots with their own items, in layers foundation through surface.
  - Its errors run one way only. A shared name can over-approximate reach, so a missed module is possible; a module it reports unreached really is named by nothing reachable.
- `registries/unwired_modules.toml` (typed loader `fa_registry::unwired_modules`; registry-check validates the file):
  - `[[unwired]]` rows: path, owner_bead, reason, expires.
  - `[[verification]]` rows: path, consumer test file, reason. The consumer must reference its module.
- Seeded with today's 9 unwired modules, each expiring 2026-11-21:
  - concordat (fa-76hy), regulatory (fa-doa9), part370 (fa-p370), conformal (fa-4psc);
  - fa_time business (fa-94qd), selector (fa-5c1) (recurrence, fa-0bi, was wired by main's 83efdee3 before this landed; the gate caught its stale row);
  - fa_docket::intake, fa_formats::fwc and the fa_steward root (fa-lzrn).
- The next commit, `fa document extract` (fa-lzrn), wired fa_docket::intake and deleted its row, so 8 remain.
- Plus 3 verification rows: fa_formats::conformance, fa_formats::tigerbeetle, fa_lantern::witness.

**The gate:**
- `cargo test -p xtask`, `the_workspace_has_no_unregistered_unreached_module`, judges the tree alone. It fails on:
  - an unreached module with no row;
  - a stale row (the module is reached now);
  - a row that names no module;
  - a verification consumer that doesn't reference its module.
- scripts/check.sh step `reachability` (`cargo run -p xtask -- reachability --today <UTC date>`) also fails on an expired row. Keeping the date out of cargo test keeps a tree's test verdict independent of the day.

**Acceptance:**
- **Positive:** the real tree passes with the seeded rows (rs16).
- **Planted negatives** (synthetic workspace):
  - `reachability::tests::unreached_module_without_exemption_fails`
  - `reachability::tests::expired_exemption_fails`
  - also `stale_dangling_and_unreferenced_rows_fail`, plus reach through a re-export, a method call and a qualified path, with comments, strings and cfg(test) reaching nothing.
- fa-registry `malformed_rows_are_refused` covers 10 planted rows.

**Evidence:** probe rs16 on the landed stack (vmi1152480): rs30 (vmi1152480) on these 13 commits over ab31161e: package clippy (fa-journal, fa-docket, fa, fa-formats, fa-cli, fa-fuzz, fa-registers, fa-registry, xtask, registry-check; --all-targets -D warnings) exit 0; tests green: the six small crates incl. the reachability gate, xtask reachability, fa-cli legacy_migration/readme/document/write_authority/robot_schema/polish_bar/closing, cli events+search+scenario+diff, findings search, all of fa-journal, fa-mcp parity+lib, the registers differential (generated histories, planted mutation, ddmin); fa lib 541 passed / 10 failed, all FA-REF-071 (owner fa-pvt7) and failing identically on main 124b95fe alone (bz3). rs31 on e9e2c13b itself after main moved: fa-cli/xtask clippy 0, small, reachability and the cli events tests green.

**Granularity:** module level. "Unreached pub items" inside a reached module are not reported; at item level a token scan is too noisy to gate on. Open trains checked before landing (StormyLion's fa-i7e, fa-kxc4 and fa-d22b, and LavenderSwan's main-fix4) add no unreached module.

## Why (reality check 2026-10-14)
Plan §11.8 and §11.1 require findings to be **registered, certified, bit-reproducible, immutable journal objects**:
- `CITES` edges to the legs, entries, documents and BankLines they rest on;
- review and dismissal as control effects with lineage, never as edits;
- workpapers numbered `FA-<book>-WP-<seq>`;
- `fa finding export --format md|jsonl`.

The investigator workflow of §15.6 ends with exactly these steps: `fa finding export` and `fa access log`.

Today, Lantern (integration line only) returns findings as in-memory structs (fa-lantern lib.rs:16-20 says so). Nothing is journaled, so a finding cannot be cited, reviewed, dismissed, replayed or produced. No bead owned this; fa-nlu and fa-ac78 cover procedures, not the finding object.

## What to build
1. **The Finding object.** Fields:
   - procedure id, version and registry row digest;
   - parameters digest and coordinate (known-at, effective, branch);
   - claim class (statistical / invariant per the registry; exact procedures such as tracing and aging get their own deterministic class, not "statistical");
   - severity, narrative template id;
   - cited object refs, and the run certificate.

   It is written by a `RecordFindings` intent inside one transaction per run. The writes are idempotent by the derived identity (procedure, parameters, coordinate).
2. **Review life cycle.** `FindingReview` control entries: Acknowledged, Dismissed (with a reason code and evidence), Escalated. SoD: a reviewer may not be the principal who ran the procedure, if the registry says so.
3. **Workpapers.** A `Workpaper` object groups findings and certificates under a sequential per-book number, assigned at commit, not by the caller.
4. **Surfaces.** `fa finding list|show|review|export` and the MCP tools, with verbs.toml rows (fa-mg2j ops: read / review / produce).
5. **Verification.** `fa replay` of a run certificate re-derives the same Finding set, byte-identical.

## Acceptance
- A run over the 30-entry Lantern corpus journals its findings. Replay reproduces them. A second identical run is a no-op that returns the same ids.
- Dismissal requires a reason. Self-review is refused per the SoD row.
- The workpaper export is deterministic (same bytes twice), and every citation resolves.
- FA-INV-11 has a clause covering findings (fa-j6ue) and it is live.

## Tests & logging
- Binary e2e (`fa` and `fa-mcp` stdio) and a lab crash test between run and commit (all-or-nothing).
- Each test logs the procedure, the finding ids, the citations count and the certificate oid.
close_reason: Promoted FA-INV-11.finding-replay to live with shipped_capabilities.finding mapping; added 30-entry Lantern corpus finding/workpaper/retry test and lab FaultVfs crash test in crates/fa/src/findings/tests.rs; verified 43/43 fa findings tests and 9/9 fa-registry invariant tests.

title: `fa export ads --with-proofs`: the auditor's extract carries its completeness scope and proofs against a named checkpoint
description:
## WHY
§13.1: "fa export ads --with-proofs uses ScopeIndexComplete only for a supported authenticated scope; full-chart period
scopes use the authenticated complete-prefix fallback"; §15.6 CPA workflow depends on it. export.rs:17 has no such flag.
Scope proofs exist only inside account bundles (fa-notary scope.rs).

## WHAT
`--with-proofs [--state <oid>]`: emits the ADS package plus a proof sidecar (completeness_scope label, leaf envelopes or
scope-index proofs, checkpoint) that fa-verify checks offline against the ADS rows' record digests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: fa-verify confirms an ADS extract for one account-month (ScopeIndexComplete) and a full-chart period
  (SeqRangeComplete).
- [ ] planted negative: deleting one ADS row fails verification.

```acceptance-tests
fa-cli::export::ads_with_proofs_verifies_offline
fa-verify::tests::ads_extract_missing_row_fails
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: sidecar codec. E2E: `fa export ads --with-proofs` then `fa-verify` on the output directory, both scopes. Logging: verifier prints completeness_scope and checked ranges.

- `fa export ads --period|--as-of ... --out <dir> --with-proofs [--state <oid|latest>]` writes the ADS package at exactly a recorded accumulator state's sequence. No other row may appear, and known_at_seq and entry_count must agree.
  - **Trial_Balance** is exactly the refold of those proven rows (ae29c003): one row per (account, currency) in code order, as of the cutoff, D/C and the exact magnitude at the currency's scale. So the TB file is proven too.
- A token pinned at known_at <= S (plan §15.6, the auditor) is served the newest state recorded at or before S (c500b85c, fa-0x0). A token with an accounts, periods or effective caveat cannot receive a complete prefix and is refused before anything is written.

title: FX surface: rate-document intake, valued posting, fa revalue and fa verify fx-conversion reach the live FX kernel (owner decisions first)
description:
## Why (2026-10-20, claude-opus-5-5, found by an unreached-API audit of fa-journal)
The FX kernel is live but nothing reaches it.
- **What is live:**
  - post.rs admits valued entries: `fx::admit_structure`, then recomputation against witnessed Rate documents inside the posting transaction (fa-s3c).
  - fa-journal has the planners: `value_proposal` (SpotClose / PeriodAverage), `plan_revaluation` (PeriodEndRevaluation), `plan_realized_fx_settlement`.
  - fa-registers folds functional currency and refuses unvalued foreign legs.
- **What is missing:** no facade wrapper, CLI verb, intent field or MCP tool names any of it.
  - A `fa post` intent cannot carry base_amount or base_totals (fa-cli never parses them).
  - There is no way to add a Rate document: FxRateDocument is a binary canonical encoding (magic, version, units, reduced rate, rounding, as_of, retrieved_at, purpose, source), and `fa document add` takes host bytes.
  - `fa verify fx-conversion`, named in fa-s3c's title, does not exist (verify has registers, open-items, availability, usage, accumulator, projections, schedules, periods, replay, close).
  - So a multi-currency book posts per-unit-balanced entries with no functional-currency valuation, and the functional fold refuses them.

## Owner decisions first (doctrine: "Do not convert currencies with a rate you typed. Rates are documents")
1. **Rate-document intake.** Which sources may create a Rate document?
   - Options: a provider file reader (ECB/central-bank XML, CSV), with source and retrieval proof; a typed rate under an explicit grade (HumanUpload vs AgentUpload) and the evidence minimum for kind Rate (evidence_policy.toml kind 3); or both.
   - The answer fixes the CLI shape (`fa fx rate import|add`) and whether agents may create rates at all.
2. **Valuation at posting.** Who calls `value_proposal`?
   - Options: the intent names `fx: {law, rates: [D:oid…]}` and the CLI values it before the kernel's own recomputation; or the typed verbs (fa-i7e) do it.
3. **Revaluation and realized FX.** `fa revalue` (fa-i7e) vs a close task (fa-4o0). The functional balance and carrying basis come from the fa-registers functional fold.

## Then build (each with a verbs.toml row, MCP tool, pin, and a real-binary test with planted negatives)
- Rate-document intake per decision 1.
- Valued posting per decision 2.
  - Positive: an EUR sale valued at a SpotClose rate posts with base_totals citing the rate document; the functional TB balances.
  - Negatives: a missing rate document, wrong purpose, as_of ≠ effective date, a tampered base_amount.
- `fa revalue` and `fa verify fx-conversion`.
- A functional-currency trial balance view, if not already reachable.

## Related
- fa-s3c (closed): FX posting kernel; its title names `fa verify fx-conversion`, which no surface provides.
- fa-i7e: typed verbs, including `revalue`; decision 3 decides whether revaluation lives there.
- fa-z41: the 2026-10-11 epic of vision goals with no bead coverage ("FX posting").
- No dependency edges were added at filing: a swarm was active, and graph structure has one writer.
close_reason: Independently verified: acceptance tests run, evidence in the MaroonCat comment

title: fa proof suffix: surface Journal::suffix_proofs_with_records, every record appended since a retained state (plan §13.2 incremental extension)
description:
## WHY
Plan §13.2 lets a recipient extend previously verified state instead of receiving the whole history again. fa-notary's `Journal::suffix_proofs_with_records` (owner commit 54f1c71c, 2026-10-21) produces exactly that suffix:
- the consistency proof from the retained statement;
- one record-bearing v1 inclusion proof per appended leaf, including undated controls and evidence leaves (import receipts, attestations, custody, supplements).

fa-verify consumes the same files (`witness index --consistency … --delta-record …`).

But nothing in the product called the producer. `fa proof inclusion --with-record` takes only an entry vid, so an evidence leaf appended since the retained state had no proof a recipient could obtain through any surface. The unwired-code scan of 2026-10-22 named it: suffix.rs, 145 lines, test-only callers.

## WHAT
- A db-level `fa_notary::prefix::prove_suffix_with_records`. It reads the journal exactly as `prove_prefix_with_records` does: the state is reproduced and the journal is unchanged at the observed frontier.
- A facade `export_suffix` behind the proof export admission: whole-book read plus produce, current, not revoked, accumulator green.
- `fa proof suffix --state <retained> [--next-state <oid|latest>] [--out <new dir>]`:
  - inline hex, or consistency.bin plus record-<leaf>.bin in a new directory;
  - the event `proof_suffix_exported`, carrying the exact fa-verify steps.
- MCP: `fa_notary_export` gains kind `suffix`, inline.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: after a posting and a document add, the suffix from the old state carries exactly the new leaves (an entry and an import receipt). The consistency proof verifies old to new, and each record verifies at the new checkpoint as a Recomputed inclusion at consecutive leaves.
- [ ] positive: the --out files carry the same bytes, and name order is leaf order.
- [ ] planted negatives: a missing --state (usage, before the book opens), an existing --out directory, and a reversed pair are refused, and nothing is written.
- [ ] follow-up (not this bead's code): `fa-verify witness index` advances a retained index from these files once book checkpoints carry a witness-policy oid (WitnessPolicy journaling, fa-qtfd).

```acceptance-tests
fa-cli::proofs::a_suffix_carries_every_appended_leaf_and_verifies_against_both_checkpoints
```

title: fa-cli: canonicalize --book / FA_BOOK before any substrate path use (a '..' component reaches fgdb-strata's and the blob store's rename, which the host VFS refuses) — planted '..' negative, byte-identical envelope for the absolute and relative spellings
description: WHY (TopazOsprey 3656, 2026-10-11, unverified observation during fa-txf t8): fa-cli's book_dir passes --book / FA_BOOK through raw. asupersync's UnixVfs::rename runs validate_safe_path (fs/path_ops.rs ~189), which refuses any '..' component, while create_dir_all and open do not validate; so a book opened as --book ../acme most likely fails at the substrate's first staging rename (fgdb-strata store.rs ~1014) or the blob store's rename, with an I/O error instead of a usable book. Agents are the primary operators and relative spellings are what they type. WHAT: (1) resolve the book directory once at the CLI boundary (fa-cli book_dir): join to the process cwd and normalize '.' and '..' lexically (no symlink resolution, no host canonicalize of a path that may not exist yet), refuse a path that escapes nothing but still carries '..' only if the normalized form cannot be produced; pass the normalized absolute path to Book::open and to the daemon request (through_daemon already prefers files.cwd); (2) the same normalization in fad's request handling so a daemon-side open sees the same path; (3) first verify the failure with a binary test (fa book create --book ../x from a temp cwd) and keep that test as the planted negative turned positive. ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: --book ../acme, --book ./acme and --book /abs/acme produce byte-identical robot envelopes (coordinate.book, data) for the same book; [ ] planted negative: before the fix the '..' spelling fails at the substrate rename (recorded in the test's doc as the observed defect), after the fix no substrate call ever sees a '..' component (a FaultVfs or path-recording VFS asserts it); [ ] proof class: invariant (one normalization point) + binary test; [ ] consumers: every agent invocation of fa with a relative --book, fad clients, the MCP posture (fa-mcp forwards cwd); [ ] no-claim boundary: this does not make the substrate tolerate '..'; it keeps such paths out of it.

title: fa diff --from/--to: the ledger between two recorded frontiers (plan §15.3 Time and close)
description:
## Why
Plan §15.3 lists `fa diff --from … --to …` in the Time and close family, and no surface had it. Comparing the book across recorded time took two `fa tb --as-known-at` runs and a hand diff, with no way to see which entries made the difference. That is bet A2's question: what changed in the books since a report was run, including entries dated into a period already reported.

## What
`fa diff --from <seq|RFC3339> [--to HEAD|<seq>|<RFC3339>]` asks one trial-balance selection (as `fa tb`) at both frontiers. It returns:
- the changed account/unit rows: before and after debits and credits, posted and pending apart, with the exact delta;
- every entry recorded in the window, with its class, date, period and supersession lineage.

The verb is a whole-book read. It also has an MCP tool, and `Book::ledger_diff` is the library form.

## Acceptance
- A late entry dated into an earlier period appears in the window it was recorded in and moves that period's activity.
- An empty window changes nothing.
- Usage errors exit 2.
- The events test emits `ledger_diff`.
close_reason: Landed with gate evidence in its comment

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-23: landed on main as e9e2c13b.

**`fa diff --from <seq|RFC3339> [--to HEAD|<seq>|<RFC3339>]`** asks one trial-balance selection (as `fa tb`: `--period`/`--fiscal-year` with `--activity`, or `--as-of`) at two recorded frontiers. It reports:
- every account and unit whose posted or pending balance changed: before and after debits and credits, and the exact signed delta;
- every entry recorded after `--from` through `--to`, in recorded order, with its class, the date it carries, its period (resolved as the folds resolve it) and its supersession lineage. An entry dated into an earlier period is listed by when it was recorded. `--limit` (default 200, 1..=1000) caps the list; `entries_total` counts all.

Both trial balances and the entry list come from one query.

**Usage and admission:**
- A missing `--from` or selection, `--from` after `--to`, and a selection the from-frontier cannot answer (its period did not exist yet) are usage (exit 2).
- It is a whole-book read: a scope-caveated token is refused, never filtered.

**Library and registry:**
- `fa::ledger_diff::trial_balance_changes` is the exact comparison. It moved out of scenario.rs, whose `diff_rows` now maps onto it, so `fa scenario diff` and draft review are unchanged.
- `Book::ledger_diff` reads both sides and the window.
- Registry: verb `diff`; event `ledger_diff` with shapes `ledger_change` and `recorded_entry`; a `[[bound]]` read rule; MCP `fa_forensics_ledger_diff`, on demand.

**Test:** fa-cli `diff_shows_what_changed_between_two_recorded_frontiers`:
- a sale and a late rent entry dated 2026-02-20, both recorded after the frontier, move March's stock (Cash +21.00, Sales -25.00, Rent +4.00);
- the late entry is listed under FY2026-P02, and February's activity moves by it alone;
- an empty window changes nothing;
- `--limit 1` lists one of two;
- the usage cases exit 2.

The events test emits `ledger_diff`.

title: Checked arithmetic on every amount path: fix unchecked/saturating i128 sums, enable overflow-checks in release, deny clippy::arithmetic_side_effects in amount modules
description:
## WHY
AGENTS.md: "an unchecked i128 operation on an amount is a critical finding"; doctrine 4 "no silent auto-balancing";
FA-INV-06 overflow is refused, never wrapped or saturated. Verified at 0d338c0:
- crates/fa-registers/src/fx.rs:1056-1093 (`translate_current_rate`, public): raw `+=`, `-=`, `at_closing - rep` on
  reporting mantissas (totals declared ~941-952).
- crates/fa-registers/src/reconciliation.rs:437-439 (`match_three_way`): unchecked `-`, `+`, `.abs()` on quantity and
  unit-price mantissas.
- crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:952, 988-991, 1119 saturating adds (related-party total_exposure clamps silently);
  1204-1207, 1303-1305 raw `+=`; 1324 unchecked `acct_vol * 10_000`.
- crates/fa-journal/src/chart.rs:1480 unchecked negation (low risk).
- Cargo.toml profiles set no `overflow-checks`, so release builds wrap silently.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a translation input whose reporting asset mantissas sum beyond i128::MAX and call `fa_registers::fx::translate_current_rate` in a release build → silent wrap (no overflow-checks in any profile; `grep -n overflow-checks Cargo.toml` → nothing).
2. `sed -n '945,995p;1115,1125p;1200,1210p;1300,1330p' crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs` → saturating and raw adds on amount totals.

## WHAT
1. Replace each site with checked operations returning a typed refusal (exit 3/5 per catalog), never saturation.
2. `[profile.release] overflow-checks = true` (and test/dev explicitly); measure the cost later under fa-ykbp, not now.
3. `#![deny(clippy::arithmetic_side_effects, clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]` in fa-money, fa-registers (fx,
   reconciliation, report modules), fa-lantern, fa-statements arithmetic modules, with per-site `allow` only for proven
   non-amount index arithmetic with a comment.
4. ubs/ast-grep rule in check.sh: `$A += $B` / `saturating_add` on fields named `*mantissa*|*amount*|*total*` in those
   crates fails.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: property tests at i128::MAX/MIN boundaries for translate_current_rate, match_three_way and each graph
  procedure produce typed refusals.
- [ ] planted negatives: re-introducing a raw `+=` on a mantissa in fa-lantern fails clippy; a saturating_add on an amount
  fails the ast-grep rule.

```acceptance-tests
fa-registers::fx::tests::translation_overflow_is_refused
fa-registers::reconciliation::tests::three_way_overflow_is_refused
fa-lantern::graph::tests::related_party_exposure_overflow_is_refused
fa-lantern::graph::tests::concentration_overflow_is_refused
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Boundary property tests (deterministic seeds, logged inputs on failure).

## E2E & LOGGING (refinement round 1)
E2E: real-binary `fa procedure run graph.related_party_exposure` on a crafted book whose totals exceed i128 refuses with exit 3 (not a clamped number). Logging: refusal names the procedure, accumulator and operands.
close_reason: Independently verified: acceptance tests and planted negatives run, evidence in the MaroonCat comment

What changed
- A lint gate instead of the ast-grep script (WHAT 3/4): fa-lantern, fa-statements and fa-registers deny clippy::arithmetic_side_effects and clippy::disallowed_methods crate-wide. Each crate's clippy.toml exempts every integer narrower than 128 bits (arithmetic-side-effects-allowed), so the lint bites exactly on i128/u128 (amounts, magnitudes, products), and disallows i128/u128 saturating_* and wrapping_*.
