title: RegisterCheckpoints: journaled checkpoints at a registered cadence and every fiscal-year boundary; retired-cursor rebuild from the last checkpoint; historical folds bounded
description:
## WHY
Plan §5.3: registers keep periodic RegisterCheckpoints (journaled, content-addressed snapshot of all cells at a CommitSeq)
so historical folds are bounded and DeltaCursorRetired rebuilds from the last checkpoint; §7.5 bounds opening balances by a
checkpoint at each fiscal-year boundary; FA-CFG-01 requires checkpoint_cadence ≤ retention_floor. At 0d338c0
crates/fa-registers/src/maintainer.rs:9-10 states it is "not a certified RegisterCheckpoint"; a retired cursor rebuilds
from the whole journal; the cadence decision card (maintainer.rs:477-488) is computed and never acted on. fa-vn4 was
closed claiming checkpoints; slo.toml FA-BENCH-20 (activated) claims the flush "emits RegisterCheckpoint". This run also
observed `DeltaCursorRetired { asked: 0, retained_after: 12, frontier: 13 }` surfacing as exit 5 in fa-cli tests.

## WHAT
RegisterCheckpoint object per Appendix A (definition_oid, commit_seq, cells_root, cell_count, body_digest) published by
the maintainer as a maintenance-class publication at the cadence the decision card selects (pinned fallback) and at each
fiscal-year boundary; AS KNOWN AT reads fold forward from the nearest checkpoint ≤ seq; DeltaCursorRetired rebuilds from
the last checkpoint; `fa verify registers` verifies checkpoints by refold; cadence ≤ retention floor checked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: a known-at TB at a seq 10k commits after a checkpoint folds only the tail (substrate-read counter witness);
  retired cursor rebuild reads from the checkpoint.
- [ ] planted negatives: a tampered cells_root fails verify registers (exit 8); cadence > retention floor fails
  registry-check; crash between checkpoint computation and publication leaves the previous checkpoint authoritative.

```acceptance-tests
fa-registers::checkpoint::known_at_read_folds_from_nearest_checkpoint
fa-registers::checkpoint::retired_cursor_rebuilds_from_checkpoint
fa-registers::checkpoint::tampered_checkpoint_fails_verify
fa-registers::checkpoint::crash_before_publication_keeps_previous
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: checkpoint codec and cells_root recomputation. E2E: CLI `fa registers materialize` across a fiscal-year boundary, reopen, `fa tb --as-known-at` older than the delta window succeeds via the checkpoint, `fa verify registers` green; tampered checkpoint → exit 8. Logging: reads report served_from {checkpoint seq, tail length}; substrate read counter logged.

description:
## Why
registries/account_types.toml:4-6 documents behaviour the code does not implement. Either the comment or the
code is wrong; reports, statements and certificates depend on the answer (balance sheets need ITD for stock
accounts and closed-out flow accounts; income statements need period activity).

## What to build
A recorded decision (plan §7.4/§12.1 reference) on: TB `--as-of` for flow accounts (ITD vs fiscal YTD with
closing-entry semantics, which interacts with fa-4o0's YearEndClose), memo/statistical accounts (fa-xjlb).
Implement the decision in fa-registers, the oracle and the registry text in one change.

## Acceptance
Registry text, kernel/report code and oracle agree; a test per account type pins the as-of behaviour.

## Tests & logging
fa-registers tests + differential seed; logs account type, selector, result.
close_reason: Recorded selector and memo footing contract in registries/account_types.toml, excluded memo/statistical accounts from TrialBalance.unit_totals/pending_unit_totals and SummaryTrialBalance unit totals, enforced separate monetary vs memo balance per unit and (unit, legal_entity) in fa-journal and fa-reference (FA-REF-001), fixed historical MVCC retired_at check in fa-journal::entry_history, and verified with differential tests across all 7 AccountType tags.

disk pressure (vmi1156319, vmi1153651 at 1.9% free, vmi1293453), hz1 below critical free GB, hz4 offline with "No space
left on device", designated fallback vmi1152480 at 9% free; every compiling step of scripts/check.sh came back UNRUN
("no admissible workers: critical_pressure=3, insufficient_total_slots=2"; "SSH command timed out"). When the gate cannot

description:

title: Canonical warm gate: one permanent gate worktree path on two designated rch workers; candidates are checked out into it (no new cold paths per landing)
description:
## Why
rch target pools are keyed by (worker, project path). Every new worktree path is cold on every worker:
cold check/clippy/test steps took 60-70 minutes each (RECON, d1c304c's cold check 61 min), while a
warm test step ran in 6 minutes. The swarm created ~37 worktrees and 8 clones, so nearly every proof
ran cold. This is the largest single source of landing latency.

## What to build
- One gate path for the life of the project: /data/projects/franken_accounting-gate (a worktree of
  the shared repo, created once). The train (merge_train.sh) checks each candidate out into it with
  `git checkout --detach <sha>`; nothing else edits it.
- Two designated workers for gates (named in scripts/gate_workers.conf with rationale: free disk
  ratio, clippy component present, memory headroom), with RCH_WORKER pinned and a fallback order.
- A pool-warmth probe recorded in each verdict manifest (`warm: true|false`, step durations).
- Document in AGENTS.md "Mandatory Checks": never gate from a new path.

## Tests & logging
A dry-run mode of the train prints the path, worker, and expected warmth. The manifest records
per-step wall time so warmth regressions are visible.
acceptance_criteria: Ten consecutive landings gated from the canonical path; median warm full-gate wall time <= 25 min recorded in their manifests.
close_reason: Added scripts/gate_workers.conf declaring /data/projects/franken_accounting-gate and designated workers hz2,vmi1152480, pool warmth probe in local_proof.sh and merge_train.sh, dry-run mode, and AGENTS.md documentation; verified via merge_train_selftest.sh

title: Refuse cumulative register overflow before an otherwise balanced posting publishes
description:
## Why and reproduced current behavior
Plan §4.4 requires nonnegative register accumulators bounded by registered max_register_mantissa and refusal of a post that would overflow them. Source: fa-model/src/entry.rs:1503 checks only the proposed entry; fa-journal/src/limit.rs:674-688 skips unlimited accounts; post.rs:3503 and 3575 stage entries; fa-registers/src/lib.rs:451-475 detects cumulative overflow only while folding afterward.
Isolated synthetic book, template unlimited accounts 1200/4000, AgentUpload Memo independently Reviewed: post Dr1200/Cr4000 1701411834604692317316873037158841057.27 USD => exit0 at seq7; TB succeeds. Post same balanced pair 0.01 USD => exit0 seq8. TB, registers materialize and verify registers then each exit5, message 'a register sum overflowed', no refusal code. Evidence: boundary-results.json and overflow-*.stdout in the audit directory. Current source supports the same missing admission contract; exact-HEAD runtime remains UNRUN.

## What to build
Define and register the exact representability domain before choosing a guard: gross posted and pending debit/credit columns, per native/functional unit, entity and registered period/stock cell. A small signed net does not make overflowing gross columns legal. Distinguish arbitrary report grouping totals from registered cells; state each domain explicitly, never silently widen or clamp it.
Refuse the offending mutation before publication under a catalog law/capacity refusal, with no accounting/intent-outcome/capacity/draft/case/migration mutation relative to the guarded admission basis. The isolated owner CLI regression must leave its exact head unchanged. Independently required pre-observation AccessEvents or fresh authorization TimeEvidence are separately identified and test-pinned; they are never hidden inside the rejected accounting effect. Guard every monetary minting/activation path: post, replace, atomic batch, draft/case promotion, scheduled effects and migration Finalize activating older chunks. Preserve the rule that reports/registers are derived and posting does not write authoritative registers. No global writer lock or book-wide hot balance counter. A conservative canonical-prefix fold plus correctly bound aggregate-basis guard is acceptable permanent-correct admission; reuse fa-r19j rather than invent a weaker head comparison. Charge any work/witnesses in operation_costs and test cancellation. Pending/resolution admission judges the defined final state; a representable released suffix must not fail merely because a naive intermediate sum overflows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cap-1 and cap legal, cap+1 refused BEFORE commit, same-key corrected retry succeeds.
- Gross overflow with representable net is refused; no wrap, saturation, or auto-balancing.
- Both prepared commit orders preserve capacity and do not refresh stale witnesses.
- Batch, pending release across periods, replacement, functional valuation and migration activation use the same admitted contract; unsupported measures remain explicitly absent.
- CLI reports/verify remain available after the refused post, and the independent reference agrees.
```acceptance-tests
fa-journal::register_capacity::cumulative_gross_capacity_is_admitted_before_publication
fa-journal::register_capacity::prepared_writers_cannot_jointly_exceed_capacity
fa-cli::register_capacity::max_then_minor_unit_refuses_without_breaking_reports
```
## Tests and logging
Unit law boundaries and independent limb oracle, real Book/CLI reproduction, prepared interleavings, crash/batch/migration companion. Log source prefix, scope, registered cap, proposed deltas, exact refusal and resulting head; never secret keys. Planted guard removal must re-admit the counterexample and fail the regression. No claim that a successful single-entry amount test proves accumulated capacity.

Audit basis: source tree 3c964f1f07a91c3ad9b72eebcd1a95e7809f02c8 / ba83ac090e82779518a335691fc92ab2e5704278, 2026-10-21 local. Existing binary observations are SHA256-bound in /private/tmp/fa-reality-check-20261021.d9HmEI/manifest.json; those binaries predate HEAD and are not an exact-tree gate. All fixes require normal canonical Rust gates and published proof. No implementation was changed by the audit. Preserve all accounting features, authorization-before-observation, exact arithmetic, journal immutability and independent oracles. Never weaken a gate or regenerate a golden to accommodate incorrect output.

## Refinement: scope, time and independent evidence
For already over-cap retained history, return a typed capacity diagnosis naming the exact scope and offending prefix, preserve immutable source and safe inspection/export, and never produce partial financial success or clamp/widen/repair history silently. A later reversal adds gross columns and is not a repair. No historical repair protocol is invented by this prevention bead. Planned acceptance-test names above are future requirements, not claims of existing tests. Companion fa-ys52 exercises alternate activation paths.

## Steps to Reproduce
Create a fresh synthetic template-chart book; open March; record and independently review synthetic agent evidence. Post balanced Dr1200/Cr4000 at i128::MAX (USD1701411834604692317316873037158841057.27); verify TB succeeds. Post another balanced0.01USD. Existing identified binary admits it; subsequent tb/materialize/verify exit5 overflow. See retained boundaries.py and boundary-results.json. Re-run after repair expecting prepublication catalog refusal and unchanged owner head.

Its full vertex scan retains the substrate's insertion/read witnesses, so a prepared writer cannot publish against a changed prefix." So every post now witnesses the whole journal prefix, and any concurrent commit invalidates it with FA-REF-030. That is the "conservative canonical-prefix fold" this bead allows. - fa `book::tests::prepared_post_rechecks_its_capability_expiry_without_rejecting_unrelated_commits`: FA-REF-030 on a vertex changed by an unrelated commit (tests.rs:964).

- the procert FA-REF-198 case, recorded above;
- fa-registers `incremental_pending_overflow_can_resolve_before_the_consumed_frontier`, which fails `recovered.rebuilt` at differential.rs:697.

title: Resolve round-1 architecture audit blockers before freezing G0
description:
Review of baseline ac4587c on 2026-10-09. Read the entire local AGENTS.md, suite AGENTS.md, README.md, comprehensive plan (all 1410 lines), scaffolding, and relevant live foundation source/manifests. This is a plan-stage audit: no Cargo.toml, Rust source, registry directory, or scripts/check.sh exists. No engine defect or green runtime verdict is claimed.

The architecture is an immutable REA journal on FrankenGraphDB, Folio as its write authority, Abacus/Almanac/Palimpsest for accounting laws, asynchronous certified register folds, Docket/Notary for provenance and outsider verification, Canon for deterministic intent evaluation, Lantern/Statements/Concordat for derived analysis, and Steward/Teller for governance and three shared surfaces.

The linked blockers preserve concrete counterexamples and source references. They are specification-repair tasks, not implementation-completion claims. The plan is not ready for major-1 schema freezing or implementation graph conversion until these contradictions are resolved consistently across normative appendices, prose, README, and AGENTS.

Validation performed: repository inventory; exact sixteen-ID invariant set; TOML toolchain pin parse; local foundation source tracing; arithmetic/calendar/hold counterexamples evaluated using Python exact integers and fractions; primary-source checks for Cargo source identity, transparency proof scope, TigerBeetle pending semantics, special fiscal periods, and incumbent GL corrections.

Do not close this issue merely because documentation changes. Require fresh review of all linked acceptance examples and the applicable future executable gates. No cargo test or repository-wide gate can currently run because their project inputs are absent.

title: Capability revocation is impossible while fad serves a book: 6386296 refuses --grant on untokened fad requests, and tokens cannot hold issue_capability
description:
## WHY
Origin 6386296 (fa-yok/fa-r3q, merged into main by b9f93fc) refuses every caller-supplied --grant on an untokened fad request, closing a self-grant escalation on the same-UID daemon route. Its interaction with revocation was not run: the commit was authored UNRUN.

Run at bfd4362 (MaroonRaven, 2026-10-21, macOS): fad tests token_sessions_through_fad_bind_each_request_to_its_holder fails. Its "revoked mid-session (by the owner, through the same daemon)" step is `fa capability revoke --commitment <c> --grant issue_capability --yes` over fad. It now exits 7 with FA-REF-011 "`--grant` is not admitted on the daemon path".

Consequence: while fad holds a book's writer lease, no one can revoke a capability.
- An untokened owner request may not add issue_capability.
- A token cannot carry it: bound sessions are capped at the Preparer launch ceiling, and LaunchAuthority::from_token refuses issue_capability.
- The direct route is the lease holder's to refuse (FA-REF-018, per the catalog; not re-run by me).

Revoking a compromised token is exactly when you need this.

## WHAT (owner decision)
Choose one, then make the failing test express it:
1. Admit --grant on untokened fad requests only for authority-reducing operations (capability revoke), refusing it for everything else.
2. A fad-side owner control for revocation, outside the per-request grant path.
3. Let an owner-issued token carry issue_capability for revocation only.
Do not resolve this by editing the test or ignoring it. The test is the evidence.

## Acceptance
- positive: a token revoked through the serving fad is refused on its next request with FA-REF-023 (the existing test, unchanged in intent).
- planted negative: an untokened fad request adding --grant privileged (or any non-reducing op) is still refused with FA-REF-011 (6386296's test).
close_reason: Independently verified: acceptance tests run, evidence in the MaroonCat comment

Every other untokened --grant on fad is still FA-REF-011. Planted negatives added to 6386296's test untokened_fad_requests_cannot_self_grant_authority: capability issue --grant issue_capability over fad exits 7 and writes no token; a revoke adding --grant privileged exits 7. token_sessions_through_fad_bind_each_request_to_its_holder passes unchanged. cargo test -p fad --test fad 12/0; clippy -p fa-cli -p fad clean (macOS, self-run). A full workspace run of 7c61664 is in progress. Stays OPEN for an independent verifier, and for anyone who prefers option 2 (a fad-side owner control) over this narrow exemption.

title: Party-level PAID money-flow projection maintained incrementally from delta_since; graph procedures (circular flows, layering, communities, concentration, ultimate beneficiary) re-pointed to it
description:
## WHY
Plan §4.1 `PAID {amount, unit, effective, entry_ref}` is the derived Party→Party money-flow projection Lantern traces
(§11.4). At 0d338c0 circular_flows, layering, communities and concentration run over the account-to-account flow graph
(fa-lantern projection.rs:1-8), so they find cycles among GL accounts rather than counterparties; Louvain runs on an
unweighted account graph. Split from fa-kxc4 in refinement round 2.

## WHAT
Derive PAID edges from entries whose legs carry Party dimension values (REPRESENTS bindings), keyed (from_party,
to_party, unit, effective, entry_ref); maintained from delta_since like registers (derived, rebuildable, verified by
refold, never authoritative); graph procedures consume it with exact-integer weights; fnx algorithms with CGSE witnesses;
the reference oracle gains a literal PAID fold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: PAID projection equals the reference fold on every fa-gen corpus; layering finds the planted shell-network
  chain through parties; communities weighted by amount.
- [ ] planted negatives: a corrupted PAID edge fails verify; an entry without party dimensions contributes no PAID edge.

```acceptance-tests
fa-lantern::projection::party_paid_projection_matches_reference
fa-lantern::graph::layering_finds_planted_party_chain
fa-lantern::projection::paid_projection_drift_detected
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: projection derivation. E2E: `fa procedure run graph.layering` on the shell-network demo book via the real binary.
Logging: projection size, edges added per delta batch, refold digest.

comments.author: StormyLion
comments.text:
2026-10-22 (StormyLion): a design question that blocks a correct first slice. Not a claim

**The plan (§4.1, §11.4)** names PAID `{amount, unit, effective, entry_ref}` as a derived Party to Party view, but gives no derivation rule.

**A rule that reuses what exists:**
- Lantern's money flow already splits every balanced `(unit, legal_entity)` partition of an entry from credit legs to debit legs under the registered largest-remainder law (projection/transport.rs).
- PAID can run the same allocation over party nodes instead of accounts: a leg's party is its PARTY_DIMENSION value resolved through the REA snapshot, and a leg with no party is the book itself.
- A PAID edge is credit party to debit party, and self-flows are dropped.
- Under this rule:
  - a customer receipt (Dr Cash / Cr AR[C]) is C → book;
  - a vendor payment (Dr AP[V] / Cr Cash) is book → V;
  - an intermediary transfer (Dr Clearing[B] / Cr Clearing[A]) is A → B.

**The decision this needs (owner):** in a single book, almost every flow touches the book node.
- Party-level cycles and layering then mostly find round trips through one counterparty (book → A → book) and pass-through via the book (C → book → V).
- Today's account-level procedures find internal round trips across clearing accounts. Those are real kiting and layering signals that the party graph would lose.
- The options:
  - (a) Switch graph.circular_flows, layering, communities and concentration to PAID, as the bead says.
  - (b) Keep the account-level procedures and add party-level ones beside them.
  - (c) Make the node set a parameter.
- Each switch is a procedure version bump and a rewrite of its fixtures. I would start with (b) plus the projection and its reference oracle, unless you rule otherwise.

title: Define control-record encoding and immutable lifecycle projections
description:
References: §§4.2, 5.10, 7.3, 8.3, 10.2, Appendix A/C/F (lines 286-317, 435, 483, 540, 606-620, 1144, 1200-1207, 1278-1279, 1329).
Every Entry requires 2 or more posting legs, including SchemaControl/PolicyControl/PeriodControl in the same EntryClass union. Creating the first chart/calendar/book or opening a Future period has no legitimate pair of posting legs. Encoding invented zero-value accounting legs would violate the no-prototype/no-fabricated-leg doctrine. Define a journal record union or a precisely class-dependent payload with control effects separate from posting legs.
Lifecycle objects are declared immutable after commit (FA-INV-02), yet Period.state is a versioned property, RestatementCase/CloseRun/Finding/DraftSet carry changing status, Capability carries revoked, and §5.10 compare-and-sets membership counters. Specify which immutable transition records are authoritative and which current-state objects are disposable projections, with reconstruction and known-at rules. Attestations on a Register must bind its coordinate/value digest rather than merely a mutable/rebuildable cell identity.
Negative examples: create an empty book and first account without fake legs; transition case Proposed→Approved→Posted without updating its original payload; rebuild lifecycle state from immutable transitions. W1-W4, G0.
Model follow-up: entity-scoped capabilities and cash-by-legal-entity registers require an authoritative entity assignment. Entry/Account/Leg schemas and declared edges do not identify an owning LegalEntity, and the Dimension kind list has no mandatory legal-entity dimension. Either constrain each book to one declared entity or specify the balanced entity dimension and membership checks; do not infer ownership from descriptions.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.1 immutability model (payload objects / lifecycle-by-transition objects with projected status / rebuildable projections); control classes carry legs=[] and a typed ControlPayload union (Appendix A); FA-INV-02 clauses payload-immutable, lifecycle-by-transition, control-record; LegalEntity.code and Book.entities with legal_entity as a mandatory balancing dimension (per-entity clause of FA-INV-01, §5.2); RegisterEquals binds cell_key + fold_digest (§9.4). title: fa-canon first slice: typed total rule language, type checker and IR, journaled content-addressed rule versions with dual-control activation, interim evaluator under a stripped Cx (no clock/entropy/net/fs, compile-fail proven), rule families bound to intents (Accrue/Defer, Allocation, Revaluation, Elimination) replacing their FA-REF-102 class refusals, golden corpora, backtesting on drafts, VM adapter boundary
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Canon (W6) is the posting-rule engine: a rule language, type checker and IR, an interim evaluator under a stripped `Cx` (no clock, entropy, network or filesystem), the intent catalog bound to rule families, golden corpora, backtesting and activation with dual control. At 96d1918 there is no Canon code at all (fa-model/src/canon.rs is the byte codec; "Canon" appears twice as forward references); Allocation/Revaluation/Elimination entry classes are refused as not implemented because no rule can produce them. Doctrine 3's sharpest instance ("a rule that wants today receives it as a declared input") has nothing to bind to. Canon depends on the intents slice (rule-driven intents are typed intents) and on W3's period law.

WHAT (first real slice):
1. `crates/fa-canon` (laws layer; pure): the rule language as a small, total, typed expression language over declared inputs (event fields, registered units, account codes, dates given as inputs), with a parser, a type checker that refuses floats and unregistered units/laws, and an IR; every rounding or allocation in a rule names a registered law from `rounding_laws.toml`.
2. Rule versions as journaled, content-addressed objects (Appendix A `RuleVersion`): source, IR digest, declared inputs, produced entry classes, activation state; activation is a PolicyControl-style control record under dual control (two distinct principals, SoD row), with `GENERATED_BY` lineage from every entry a rule produces to the rule version and `DERIVED_FROM` to the event.
3. The interim evaluator: `evaluate(rule_version, event, inputs) -> Vec<Intent>` under a stripped Cx (type-level: the evaluator's context carries no capability for clock/entropy/net/fs, proven by a compile-fail test); re-running version v over event e reproduces the entry digest (the plan's testable-derivation claim) as a test.
4. Rule families bound to intents: Accrue/Defer, Allocation (largest-remainder over a named law), Revaluation (FX law from fa-p7r), Elimination (Concordat); each family's produced class is enabled in the kernel's class gate only when its rule family exists (replacing the FA-REF-102 refusal for that class with the real path).
5. Golden corpora: checked-in events + expected intents per rule family; backtesting = replaying a rule version over a historical event range on a draft (fa-s7x) and diffing against the live entries; dry-run plans for every produced intent (fa-intents).
6. VM adapter boundary: the evaluator is behind a trait so the substrate's UDF VM (Appendix H, R-VM) can replace it with the registered switch-over rule; no substrate code copied.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an Accrue rule produces an Adjusting intent whose entry replays byte-identically from (rule version, event); an Allocation rule's residual lands on the named rounding account under the named law; activation without a second principal is refused by SoD; [ ] planted negatives: a rule source that reads a clock-like input not declared fails type checking; a rule naming an unregistered law is refused; a mutated IR digest fails the lineage check; [ ] proof class: invariant (derivation replay) + golden corpora; [ ] consumers: Allocation/Revaluation/Elimination classes, fa-statements consolidation, agents' intent catalog; [ ] no-claim boundary: Canon proves rules are deterministic and typed, not that any rule encodes the right accounting policy.

TESTS: fa-canon unit tests for parser/type checker/IR with goldens, kernel tests for lineage and activation SoD, differential vs a fa-reference naive evaluator for the first families, logs naming the rule version digest.

comments.author: StormyLion
comments.text:
CLAIMED (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5, 2026-10-23 18:25Z). Slice 1 is in development on local/canon-stormylion. It is not on main yet.

**Slice 1: the language, read-only.**
- New crate `crates/fa-canon` (laws layer; pure, takes no `Cx`). Its `clippy.toml` bans the clock, filesystem, environment, network, process and thread, as Lantern's does.
- Grammar: `rule <name> v<N> for event <Kind> { [inputs { as_of: date, fee: amount("USD") }] let | debit|credit "<code>" <amount> [dims {cost_center = "CC1"}] | effective event.occurred_on|<date input> }`.
  - Amounts: literals, `event.resource("label", "UNIT")`, lets and amount inputs, `+`, `-`, `* N`, and `/ D round <law>`.
  - Every division names a registered rounding law.
  - Depth, statements and inputs are bounded. Lets reference only earlier lets, so the language is total by construction.
- **Checker:**
  - Units are typed; adding USD to EUR is refused.
  - Unregistered units, laws, dimensions and event kinds are refused, and so are undeclared names: "today" must be a declared date input.
  - **Balance proof:** every amount normalizes to an exact linear form over atoms (event resources, amount inputs, and each distinct rounded division as one opaque atom, keyed by the form it divides, its reduced ratio and its law). A rule compiles only when debits minus credits is the zero form in every unit. No residual leg is ever added.
- **IR:** canonical `fa:canon-ir:v1` bytes. Lets become numbered slots, and units are spelled by code, version and scale, so the address depends neither on let names, layout, nor a book's unit ids. The content address is `ir_digest` = `domain_digest("fa:canon-ir:v1", ir)`. The static dependency set covers accounts, units, laws, resources and dimension tags.
- **Evaluator:** a pure tree walk with exact i128/u128 arithmetic; rounding is `RoundingLaw::apply_magnitude`. Typed `EvalError`s cover the wrong event kind, a missing or repeated resource, a resource unit mismatch, missing, undeclared or mistyped inputs, an overflow, and a negative leg. A zero leg is omitted. The `Derivation` carries `rule_version_oid` (= ir_digest), `event_digest` and `inputs_digest` (`fa:canon-inputs:v1`), the three digests `EntryOrigin::Rule` names.
- **Surfaces:** `fa rule check <file|->` and `fa rule eval <file|-> --event <code|vid> [--input name=value]... [--as-known-at]`. They emit the events rule_checked and rule_evaluated and the shape rule_leg. Facade `fa::rule`; MCP tool `fa_rules_rule` in a new on-demand cluster `fa.rules` (source inline as `source`).
- New refusal **FA-REF-196 CANON_RULE** (exit 3) covers a refused source, naming the line and column, and an evaluation that cannot be computed.

**Not in slice 1** (this bead stays open):
- journaled RuleVersion objects with dual-control activation and SoD;

title: Merge train batching and bisection: gate N queued candidates per run, bisect on red, eject the failing candidate; batch size as a decision card with pinned fallback N=1
description:
## Why
fa-u7u adopts local_proof.sh / merge_train.sh / verdict manifests. The swarm's serial protocol
(one git-state token, one full gate per landing) produced about one landing every few hours; with
4-6 writers that cannot keep up. Batching amortizes the gate across candidates.

## What to build (on top of fa-u7u)
- Queue = refs `refs/heads/train/<bead>-<agent>`; each candidate is a commit series whose messages
  name its bead ids.
- `merge_train.sh run`: re-parent queued candidates in queue order onto trunk (stop and notify the
  owner of a candidate that does not apply), gate the stack tip once in the canonical gate path;
  green → fast-forward trunk (main and staging) to the tip and write a verdict note per candidate;
  red → bisect the stack (ceil(log2 N) gates), eject the first failing candidate with the failing
  step and log excerpt, re-run the remainder.
- Batch size N is a decision card (see the decision-card framework bead): minimize expected
  gate-minutes per landed candidate C(N) ~= G*[1 + (1-(1-p)^N)*ceil(log2 N)] / (N*(1-p)) with p from a
  Beta posterior over recent train outcomes; the card records state, candidates, the expected-benefit
  interval, and the pinned fallback N=1 when the posterior is wide or the framework is absent.
- An infra UNRUN never ejects a candidate; it retries the same stack.

## Tests & logging
Shell-level simulation with stub gates: 5 candidates with candidate 3 red → exactly candidates 1,2,4,5
land and 3 is ejected after <= 3 extra gates; all-green → one gate; UNRUN → no ejection. Every train
run writes a log with stack, gates, verdicts and timings.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation tests pass; first real batched run lands >= 3 candidates in one gate.
close_reason: Extended scripts/merge_train.sh with run-batch over refs/heads/train/*, binary-search bisection on RED, UNRUN preservation, and replayable batch-size decision card fa:decision-card:merge-train-batch:v1 with pinned fallback N=1; verified with scripts/tests/batch_and_discipline_selftest.sh.

title: Reconcile CLI, schema, determinism, and public comparison contradictions
description:
References: §§0/3.2, 4.7, 9.4, 13.2, 15.3-15.7, 18.2/18.4, Appendix A/C/D; README examples/comparison.
- §4.7 and FA-REF-015 refuse instants as effective dates, while §15.3 silently converts with a warning. Pick one explicit policy. Period inadmissibility is exit 2 in Genesis but listed under exit 7 too.
- CLI fa hold is both financial hold and governance hold place/release; MCP catalog has no complete governance/registry/interop/lifecycle mapping despite parity claim. Declare unambiguous verbs and shared-operation mappings or registered exclusions.
- Closed/Locked matrix permits Resolution(Voids), Revision and Reopen, but §7.3/FA-INV-03 says only restatement classes; matrix requires post_softclosed, migrate, schema_change absent from the §14.2 closed op vocabulary. Reconcile from one registry.
- Bundles claim same scope+checkpoint yields same bytes but include producer, produced_at_seq, capability and redaction fields; bind the complete closure or split deterministic content from production receipt. Fixed-as_known_at RegisterEquals assertions cannot become false from later entries; use a separate head-following reconciliation monitor and retain the original assertion.
- §15.5 example needs IS edges, Subledger→Account CONTROLS, LegalEntity.code and Leg.effective_date not declared in the model. Fix the model/query contract and reject cross-unit sums in the accounting GQL profile.
- fa-formats/qbo and object_schemas/tracing/conversion laws need explicit registry ownership; ftui and fsci_stats are promised despite the closed four-foundation policy. Reconcile their inclusion/exclusion with explicit posture/test-only policy, never silent allowlist expansion.
- Plan/README characterize all ERP posted journals as editable rows. Oracle Fusion documentation explicitly says a posted journal cannot be changed and describes reversal workflows: https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/131/user_services/FAFTT/F416502AN10266.htm . Narrow competitive claims and separate existing derived balance caches from authoritative mutable accounting facts. SEC audit-trail amendments were adopted October 12, 2022, not 2023 as §0 says: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-187 .

title: Certified trial balance and `fa replay <certificate>` (FA-INV-11.core): Certificate over Database::execute_certified inputs, byte-identical replay, `fa certificate status` — the Genesis acceptance item no bead in fa-lm7's graph owns
description:
WHY: plan §19 Genesis slice ends "… `fa tb --json` returns the certified trial balance → … → `fa replay` reproduces the trial balance bytes"; G1 requires FA-INV-11.core live. At e606b46 the robot envelope's `certificate` is always null (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:231), there is no `fa replay` verb, `Database::execute_certified` and `Database::replay` are never called (the substrate is used only through point reads, scans and delta_since), and both FA-INV-11 clauses are dormant (registries/invariants.toml). The only bead that mentions replay is fa-9ae (the full statements engine, P1, unassigned, depends on fa-xwv) — and fa-lm7 does not depend on it, so Genesis can never close as specified. This bead is the Genesis-sized slice: certify the reports that exist (tb, explain balance, open-items) before the statements engine.

WHAT: (1) `Certificate` object per §13.6/Appendix A: closure {book root = substrate snapshot_identity (chain commitment at seq), branch, known_at seq, effective selector, report definition id+version (tb/explain/open-items as built-in definitions), parameters digest, registry epochs (units, laws, admissibility, symbols), capability commitment (fa-0x0) or "embedded-owner"}, `inputs: [NativeResultCertificate]` for every substrate read in the closure, output_digest (BLAKE3 of the canonical output bytes), replay_command, completeness_grade. (2) Reads inside a certified report go through `Database::execute_certified` (a native read returning NativeResultCertificate) — or, if the report's fold cannot be expressed as native certified reads yet, the certificate records the literal-fold inputs it used (entry vids + digests in the selected prefix, i.e. the accumulator range) and labels `replay_scope = "fa-fold-over-prefix"`; either way replay is exact and the scope is stated. (3) Certificates persisted lazily on request (`--certify` or always for --json; decide and register) as content-addressed objects (operation_costs row). (4) `fa replay <certificate-oid|file> --json`: re-executes (Database::replay per native input, then the fold) and compares output_digest; mismatch exit 8 naming the first differing row. title: Ed25519 signer constant-time evidence: dudect-style timing harness and optimization barriers, or sign through an upstream audited implementation
description:
## WHY
fa-notary's in-house signer is constant-time by design (masked table scan ed25519.rs:332-347, fixed 512-step reduction
361-389) but "Not measured… bounded_model" (ed25519.rs:7-13); there are no optimization barriers, so LLVM may reintroduce
secret-dependent branches; slo.toml:279 claims "constant-time" unqualified (fixed under fa-vz7e).

## WHAT
A dudect-style Welch t-test harness (fixed-vs-random secret classes, ≥10^6 measurements, |t| < 4.5 threshold) run as a
tier-2 artifact (fa-vtzt kind: timing) on the release profile; add optimization barriers (core::hint::black_box on masks) or,
when fgdb-crypto ships Ed25519 at a pinned revision (frankengraphdb#3), switch to it and retire the in-house signer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: timing artifact recorded with |t| below threshold on the dev host, labelled with host fingerprint.
- [ ] planted negative: a deliberately branchy variant exceeds the threshold in the harness self-test.

```acceptance-tests
fa-notary::ct_harness::branchy_variant_detected
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: harness self-test with a branchy variant. E2E: tier-2 timing run on the release profile producing an artifact. Logging: t-statistic per measurement batch, host fingerprint.

**What landed:**
- **`fa-notary::ct_harness`** (tests only) is a dudect-style fixed-vs-random harness:
  - Classes are interleaved per measurement by a seeded SplitMix64, and inputs are built before each batch is timed.
  - One calibration batch is discarded; it sets dudect's ladder of 20 percentile crops.
  - The verdict is the largest |t| among the uncropped and cropped Welch tests that hold at least `min` measurements per class. The threshold is 4.5.
  - The arithmetic has unit tests: `welch_t_matches_a_hand_computation` (t = −√3 on a known sample, 0 for identical classes, −∞ for disjoint constants) and `crops_exclude_the_tail`.

title: Specify N-leg hold resolution, reserved availability, and expiry-period behavior
description:
References: §§5.4/5.5, 7.6, Appendix A/B/C/F/G (lines 409-415, 495, 1175, 1242, 1268, 1342, 1374).
Posts { amount: Amount } generalizes a two-leg TigerBeetle transfer inadequately to N-leg/multi-unit holds. A pending USD entry D A60, D B40, C cash100 resolved for 60 admits D A60/C cash60 or D A20/D B40/C cash60, both balanced and under original legs. Neither schema nor law chooses. Multiple currencies cannot fit one Amount. Require a per-leg balanced subvector, named proportional law, or explicit registered absence.
Limit reads say head net balance but do not define worst-case reserved availability. With cash100, a pending outflow80 must block a second80 and an unrelated posted outflow30; pending inflow cannot finance an outflow before resolution. Specify reserve/consume/release equations and atomic witnesses.
Pending created in Open can encounter Closed/Locked before timeout. Appendix C allows only Voids in Locked, excluding Expires; §5.4 requires Expires for every elapsed deadline, so the sweep can become permanently inadmissible. Define origin-vs-posting-period routing, unconditional lawful reservation release, and close/lock preconditions.
A bounded sweep cannot both expire every due hold in one transaction and obey max_batch_entries for an arbitrarily large due population. Pin epoch/cursor/batch progression and visibility under backlog. Apply the same precision to scheduled reversals after the target period closes.
Acceptance: the N-leg ambiguity above; multi-unit partial; pending-spend race; locked-period expiration; sweep batch overflow; crash/manual-resolution interleavings. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes:

title: Leg and reason hygiene: refuse zero-amount legs (kernel and oracle), refuse kernel-only reason codes on manual reversals, require a registered reason on period transitions
description:
## The defects
1. Zero legs: fa-model entry.rs ~500-506 rejects only negative mantissas; `Dr Cash 0 / Cr Rev 0` posts as
   a journaled fact (plan §4.4 requires mantissa > 0). fa-reference agrees, so the differential cannot see it.
2. A manual Reversal can cite reason 12 "ScheduledAccrualReversal" (reason_codes.toml ~119-122; post.rs
   ~895 accepts any registered reason) — a hand reversal can impersonate a kernel-scheduled one and skew
   reversal-pattern analytics.
3. Period transitions carry an unchecked `reason_code` (period.rs ~167/310; no period scope in
   reason_codes.toml); the CLI defaults it to 0 (cli.rs ~2509), so "who reopened March and why" records 0.

## What to build
- Kernel + oracle refuse zero mantissa (new or existing FA-REF; exit 3).
- reason_codes.toml gains a `scopes` field (manual_reversal, scheduled_reversal, period_transition, ...);
  the kernel refuses a code outside the operation's scope; kernel-minted reversals use the scheduled scope.
- Period transitions require a registered period_transition reason; CLI `--reason` required for
  close/reopen/lock (MCP likewise).

## Tests
Planted negatives for each; differential generator emits zero legs and wrong-scope reasons and expects refusals.
acceptance_criteria: All three refused in kernel and oracle; differential green; CLI requires --reason for transitions.
close_reason: Part 3 landed c9745007 on main 491003a2: every period transition journals a registered period_control or period_reopen reason (FA-REF-041 otherwise), and CLI --reason/MCP are wired. Parts 1-2 landed earlier. Gate sl9 on the tip: clippy green; 4 test reds, all inherited from main.

title: Kernel refuses unverified envelope/payload fields: `base_totals: Some`, caller-supplied `plan_certificate`, and non-Intent origins (Rule/Sweep/Schedule/Control) on the public post path
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): (a) `base_totals` is never read by the posting kernel — there is no reference to it in crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs; `EntryProposal::validate` checks only its shape (crates/fa-model/src/entry.rs:1499-1516). Because legs' `base_amount` is refused (post.rs:441-445 "refused, never admitted unchecked"), a proposal can still carry `base_totals: Some { unit_id, debits, credits, fx_law_oid, rate_doc_oids, residual }` with arbitrary functional-currency totals and fictitious law/rate ids, and they are journaled forever. (b) `plan_certificate` is an unchecked caller-supplied id (post.rs:92, sealed into the envelope at :1612) bound into entry_digest; Appendix A requires it to be None for rule-, sweep-, control- and migration-origin entries and to name a verified PlanCertificate otherwise — no certificate exists yet (fa-we7). (c) `EntryOrigin` is validated only for Migration (post.rs:381-402): a library caller can post an Intent-class entry claiming `Rule { rule_version_oid, event_ref, inputs_digest }`, `Sweep`, or `Schedule` origin — forged provenance; schedule verification keys on that origin (crates/fa-journal/src/schedule.rs:1280). The CLI always builds Intent (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:2574), so the hole is in the embedded API and every future surface.

WHAT: in the posting pipeline's step 1 (before any read): refuse `base_totals.is_some()` with not_implemented("entry.base_totals") citing fa-p7r/fa-s3c until the FX law reads it; refuse `plan_certificate.is_some()` until fa-we7's verifier exists (then: verify it, and require None for non-Intent origins); refuse any origin other than Intent on the public `post` path, with Rule (until Canon, fa-c34), Sweep and Schedule minted only by their internal constructors (sweep.rs / schedule.rs) through a crate-private entry point that the public API cannot reach. Mirror the same refusals in fa-reference (its own code, not shared) so the differential covers them.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: existing genesis/differential suites unchanged; sweep- and schedule-minted entries still commit; [ ] planted negatives (one check each): base_totals Some on a balanced USD entry → refused; plan_certificate Some → refused; origin Rule on a public post → refused; origin Sweep on a public post → refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-05 "registered origin", FA-INV-01) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-we7, fa-s3c, fa-c34; [ ] no-claim boundary: closes the public post path; internal minting paths are covered by their own tests.

TESTS: crates/fa-journal/tests/genesis.rs negatives with the refusal envelope logged; fa-reference mirror; differential seed campaign (fa-vfu) includes generated envelopes with these fields.

title: Gate evidence hardening: PASS requires positive completion markers, a test-inventory witness (no silently dropped tests) and ratchets on planted negatives/asserts (no silent weakening)
description:
## Why (defense in depth, not a found defect)
During the 2026-10-12 check a suspected false PASS was investigated and RETRACTED: the check's own
driver read `$?` after a `$(date)` substitution. rch actually exited 1 and printed
`[RCH] remote hz4 completion unconfirmed`, which scripts/check.sh `run_step` (~lines 70-96) correctly
classifies UNRUN. What the investigation did show is that run_step's PASS rests on the exit code alone,
and that two real honesty failures in the swarm's history are not mechanically caught today: a test
weakened during RECON (909cf25, replaced structured assertions with a message check; caught only by a
human reviewer and reverted in e53572b) and a binding proof run through a PATH shim (the committed
script did not run verbatim). These cheap checks make the gate's PASS evidence-bearing.

## What to build
1. A compiling step (check, clippy, test, robot-schema) is PASS only when its log ALSO contains
   `Remote command finished: exit=0` and a step-specific completion marker: `Finished` for
   check/clippy; for test, >= 1 `test result:` line. Otherwise UNRUN (retryable), never PASS.
2. Test-inventory witness: before the test step, run `cargo test --workspace -- --list` through rch
   (or derive from the run) and record the set of test names; PASS requires the executed-test count to
   equal the listed count (no silent skips) and the inventory to be a superset of the previous trunk
   verdict's inventory minus tests named in a `Retired-tests:` trailer of the landing commit.
3. Evidence ratchet: per crate, the counts of planted negatives (tests whose names start with the
   registered negative prefixes / that assert a refusal) and `assert` sites must not decrease versus
   the previous trunk verdict without a `Weakened-tests:` trailer naming them (the 909cf25 weakening
   would have been caught mechanically).
4. Planted negatives for the gate itself (scripts/tests/): a stub `rch` that exits 0 without a
   `Remote command finished` line → UNRUN; a stub that "runs" zero tests → UNRUN; a stub that drops one
   listed test → FAIL; a commit removing an assert without a `Weakened-tests:` trailer → FAIL.
5. Gate drivers written by agents must capture `rc=$?` immediately after the command (never read `$?`
   after a `$(...)` in the same line) — add this to AGENTS.md "Reading a gate".

## Tests & logging
Gate self-tests run in check.sh's shellcheck/self-test step; every UNRUN line names the missing
evidence and the log path.
acceptance_criteria: The four planted gate negatives produce UNRUN/UNRUN/FAIL/FAIL; a real run produces PASS with the recorded inventory; AGENTS.md documents the rc-capture rule.
close_reason: Hardened scripts/check.sh cargo_build with positive completion markers ('Remote command finished: exit=0', 'Finished', and positive 'test result: ok.'), implemented scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh (listed-vs-executed test inventory witness, Retired-tests: source inventory check, and Weakened-tests: per-crate negative/assert ratchet) and scripts/tests/gate_evidence_negative.sh (11 planted negative and positive controls), and documented the immediate rc=$? capture rule in AGENTS.md.

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-24: a design note on the open "unusual account" warning. I wrote no code for it.

**The faithful definition.** The dry-run analogue of `jet.unusual_preparers` (max_preparer_count 1, min_account_entries 3) would warn when posting this entry would make the preparer's posting on an account the kind JET then flags:
- the account has at least min_account_entries live postings across two or more preparers;
- this preparer's postings on it, this entry included, number at most max_preparer_count.

That is the bead's "preparer has never posted to it".

**The obstacle.** Deciding "never" means scanning every live entry on the account: Account ← POSTS_TO ← Leg ← HAS_LEG ← Entry, then each entry's payload. That breaks plan_warnings' stated bound ("work bounded by the plan's legs and by the entries of the periods near its date, never by the book"). It would slow every dry run on a busy account.

**Ways forward** (owner's or the implementer's call):
- (a) Journal PREPARED_BY edges at commit. The `PREPARED_BY` relation symbol (11) is registered but nothing writes it. The check would then be bounded by the preparer's own entries. This is a kernel projection change, with `fa verify projections` coverage.
- (b) A registered scan bound, reporting the check unchecked when an account's history exceeds it. limits.toml holds decoder limits cross-checked with fa-model constants, so it is the wrong home. A Lantern parameter would change the procedure-registry digest that retained procedure certificates bind.
- (c) Judge only the fiscal year's postings, as a documented weaker heuristic. It would no longer mirror jet.unusual_preparers.

**PossibleDuplicate's posting opt-in (`--allow-duplicate <reason>`)** is still open too, as StormyLion's 10-23 comment says.

title: Detector thresholds with guarantees: split-conformal false-positive bounds on labeled corpora recorded in each threshold's decision card (claim class statistical), pinned fallback thresholds
description:
## Why (plan §11.9 claim typing; G3 "measured precision/recall")
A forensic flag is statistical evidence, never an accusation. Thresholds should come with a stated
guarantee, not a hand-picked number.

## What to build
For each thresholded detector: candidate thresholds evaluated on fa-gen labeled clean books with split
conformal calibration → "flags at most alpha of clean items with probability >= 1 - delta under
exchangeability"; precision/recall with Wilson intervals on the labeled fraud scenarios; recorded in the
decision card; findings carry the threshold's card id and claim class.

## Tests
Calibration reproducible from seed; coverage holds on held-out generated books (statistical test with a
stated tolerance, claim class statistical).
acceptance_criteria: Every thresholded detector has a card with its conformal bound and measured P/R.
close_reason: Implemented split-conformal false-positive bounds, exact integer Wilson 95% confidence intervals for precision/recall, and replayable DetectorThresholdCard (DecisionKind::LanternThreshold, Claim::Statistical) in fa-lantern::conformal with independent reference oracles in fa-reference::lantern.

waiting for the lab harness. The MergeTrain model is relabelled as documentation unless the trace-validation bead connects
it to merge_train.sh's transcript.

title: Balance proofs carry the migration visibility predicate: Finalize-leaf visibility witnesses in fa:acc-balance-proof, fa-verify in_scope learns MigrationRun state, BALANCE_FORMAT bump; replaces the FA-REF-133 MIGRATION_STAGED interim refusal
description: WHY (fa-xo0 design, GrayPike 3241, ruled by CobaltGull 19:42Z 2026-10-10): plan 8.6 keeps Migration-class entries of an Open or Abandoned MigrationRun journaled but invisible at every coordinate (the FA-INV-07 migration visibility conjunct, fa_journal::migration::visible_at). The accumulator must keep every journaled leaf, otherwise Finalize would insert leaves with earlier seqs and break append-only consistency proofs. But fa-verify's balance proof fixes its in-scope set from leaf envelopes alone (fa-verify/src/balance.rs in_scope: class not Pending, account, unit, day) and refolds every in-scope leaf, so an invisible migration leaf would be counted by the verifier and every such proof would fail Claim. INTERIM (lands with fa-xo0 part 1): Journal::posted_balance and balance_proof refuse FA-REF-133 MIGRATION_STAGED (exit 3, owner fa-notary) whenever an in-scope leaf is a Migration entry whose run has no MigrationControl Finalize leaf within the prefix; decided purely from the journal's own leaves; never a wrong proof; accounts touched by an Abandoned run stay unprovable until this bead lands; the refusal's fix names this bead. WHAT: (1) the proof format gains visibility witnesses: for every in-scope Migration leaf the run's Finalize leaf (index + inclusion path) or an explicit absence marker; (2) fa-verify in_scope learns runs: a Migration leaf counts iff its run's Finalize leaf is present and verified inside the prefix, Abandoned/Open leaves are excluded with the witness proving why; (3) BALANCE_FORMAT bump (additive-minor if the old form stays decodable, else breaking-major per Appendix A format law), golden vectors for both; (4) the notary producer builds the witnesses; (5) tests: a finalized run proves and verifies, a staged run's account proves with the exclusion witness and verifies, a forged Finalize leaf fails, a proof omitting a required witness fails (planted negatives), differential vs fa_registers::balance_as_of at both known-at points; (6) remove FA-REF-133 and its catalog row. ACCEPTANCE: positive: balance proofs over accounts with staged and abandoned migration entries verify in fa-verify and equal the register fold; planted negatives above; proof class invariant (FA-INV-14 accumulator continuity, FA-INV-07 visibility) + differential; consumers: fa-xo0 migrations, examiners holding bundles, G2; no-claim boundary: the proof shows which leaves were counted and why, not that the migration was correct.
close_reason: Verified fa:acc-balance-proof:v2 authenticated MigrationControl/RunBody witnesses in fa-notary and fa-verify (Journal::balance_proof_auto, produce_bundle, verify_balance v1/v2 dispatch, migration_visibility.rs, migration_balance.rs, predicate_equivalence.rs); retained FA-REF-133 for explicit v1-only producer per additive refusal_catalog.toml law; fixed APFS EILSEQ (errno 92) handling in fa-verify non-UTF-8 path CLI tests

title: Retract fabricated §17 performance evidence: deactivate all 20 slo rows, remove hand-typed baselines, make the bench runner refuse workloads it does not execute
description:
## WHY
Plan §17 requires every gate to be an EmpiricalGate activated only when its manifest pins the host and measured fsync
and the bench executes the named operation. At 0d338c0:
- registries/slo.toml: all 20 rows `activated = true`; every manifest uses `pinned_fsync_p50_us = 1000` (assumed).
- bench/manifests/*.toml: [baseline] tables are hand-entered: register_rebuild_10m p50_us = 2800 ("full register rebuild
  from journal, 10M legs" in 2.8 ms), consolidation_branch p50_us = 3100 (20 entities × 2M entries), endurance_sustained_post
  p50_us = 3400 (24 h). Host recorded as "apple-silicon-nvme-m4", not the 32-core reference machine.
- crates/fa-bench/src/lib.rs:1057-1118: batched_post / bulk_migration / endurance only call `generate()`; register_rebuild
  calls `measure_kernel_op_witness("fold_per_entry")`; consolidation/close/restatement/CLI/MCP fall through to "generate a
  corpus, check digest non-zero"; incumbent and candidate are the same closure; `validate_comparison(&manifest.worker_class,
  true)` (line 1123) compares the manifest with itself; memory_bytes_per_leg is the constant 284 (line ~1134).
AGENTS.md names bench-path hardcoding and proof-class inflation as forbidden reward-hacking patterns. Reporting the loss
is the success.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `grep -c 'activated = true' registries/slo.toml` → 20.
2. `grep -n 'p50_us' bench/manifests/register_rebuild_10m.toml bench/manifests/consolidation_branch.toml bench/manifests/endurance_sustained_post.toml` → 2800 / 3100 / 3400 µs for a 10M-leg rebuild, a 20×2M consolidation and a 24 h endurance run.
3. `sed -n '1040,1140p' crates/fa-bench/src/lib.rs` → workloads that only call generate() or measure_kernel_op_witness, incumbent = candidate closure, validate_comparison(&manifest.worker_class, true), constant 284 bytes/leg.

## WHAT
1. Every slo row: `activated = false`, `status = "unmeasured"`, gate text kept; derivation rows kept (they are static).
2. Remove [baseline] tables from bench/manifests; keep host/fixture metadata as targets.
3. fa-bench: a workload not implemented returns `BenchError::Unimplemented(name)` and emits no timing; delete the
   constant memory breakdown; `validate_comparison` takes the measured host fingerprint, not the manifest's own field.
4. registry-check: an activated slo row without a measurement artifact (fa-vtzt) fails.
5. docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md entry; README and scoreboard stop citing any §17 number.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-bench` passes with every unimplemented workload reported Unimplemented.
- [ ] planted negative: re-adding a hand-typed [baseline] or flipping one row to activated without an artifact fails
  registry-check; calling run_benchmark("consolidation_branch") returns Unimplemented, not a timing.
- [ ] proof class: honesty restoration; no performance claim remains.

```acceptance-tests
fa-bench::tests::unimplemented_workloads_emit_no_timing
tools/registry-check::tests::activated_slo_requires_measurement_artifact
fa-bench::tests::validate_comparison_uses_measured_host
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit tests in fa-bench and registry-check with planted manifests; log which rows were deactivated.

## E2E & LOGGING (refinement round 1)
E2E: `bash scripts/check.sh --bench` on the real tree reports every unimplemented domain as UNRUN. Logging: list of deactivated rows printed.
close_reason: Fabricated §17 performance evidence retracted in slo.toml/fa-bench and tools/registry-check::tests::activated_slo_requires_measurement_artifact enforced in commit ba36c4c8.

title: fad serves concurrent connections fairly and `stop` requires owner authority: one slow client (a frame every 29 s) can no longer starve every other client; unauthenticated stop refused
description:
## The defects (static reading of main e15262f; identical on staging)
1. fad serves one connection at a time with a 30 s per-frame idle timeout (fad/src/lib.rs ~542-552): a
   client that sends one frame every 29 s holds the server indefinitely; every other CLI/MCP request
   through fad waits — a trivial local denial of service against the book's single writer.
2. `Op::Stop` is accepted from any connecting process (lib.rs ~440); the socket has no explicit mode
   (fad/src/main.rs ~184) and no peer-credential check.

## What to build
- Structured-concurrency accept loop (asupersync region per connection, bounded concurrent sessions
  from limits.toml), per-request deadlines, writes serialized through the lease-holding task (the
  substrate handle stays single-writer), reads concurrent where the handle allows.
- Socket created 0600 in a 0700 directory; SO_PEERCRED uid must equal the daemon's uid unless a
  presented token says otherwise (the token itself is fa-r3q/fa-v62's business).
- Stop requires owner authority (key-file possession posture or an owner token); a refused stop is a
  structured refusal with the fix.

## Tests (lab runtime, virtual time)
Slow client sending a frame every 29 s + a second client → second client served within its deadline;
stop from an unauthorized peer refused; fad lab tests for cancellation still green.
acceptance_criteria: Both scenarios pass under the lab runtime; fad integration tests green.
close_reason: Implemented fair non-blocking multiplexed concurrent connections in fad (bounded by max_daemon_connections = 64 in limits.toml with per-connection ChildRegion and ConnectionTiming logs), SO_PEERCRED UID verification, 0600 socket in 0700 directory, and owner-token authentication for Op::Stop via BookKeys::owner_token, verified by LabRuntime virtual-time test and real-process E2E test.

rebuild from controls equals live vertices; differential admission check.

title: install_chart: a re-imported chart exits 5 (AlreadyLive at write_ordered staging) instead of FA-REF-100; duplicate codes are not refused structurally; parent cycles install
description:

Two related structural gaps in the same function: (a) a chart document naming one account code twice is not refused structurally (the duplicate vid surfaces as a substrate error, exit 5); (b) a parent cycle among summary accounts (A parent B, B parent A, or S parent S) passes every check and installs, breaking plan §4.3 "the chart is a forest".

WHAT: (1) map AlreadyLive/IdentitySpent from write_ordered to the same FA-REF-100 refusal as at commit; (2) refuse a code appearing twice (FA-REF-100, exit 2) before any write; (3) refuse any account that is its own ancestor (FA-REF-100, exit 2) before any write, bounded walk per account.

FIX AVAILABLE: OliveFortress's private delta (fa-48m chain): 1111845 (dup + cycle checks in install_chart's structural pass) and 31462d0 (write_ordered mapping). It lands after RECON per 4409, or can be lifted as its own slice.

title: REA events: Event objects and the RecordEvent intent; an entry generated by rule version v over event e reproduces its entry digest (the provenance closure of plan §4.6/§10)
description:
## Why (Core; bets A3 and A4)
"Nothing posts without a why: … the business event, the posting rule version that generated it, …"
The REA model makes economic events first-class (sale, receipt, shipment, payroll run). Today entries
carry legs, evidence and approvals, but there are no Event vertices and no RecordEvent intent; Canon is
not started. Without events, rule-generated postings cannot be reproduced and forensic procedures cannot
reason about economic substance.

## What to build
- Event vertex (kind from an event_kinds registry, participants as Party/Instrument handles, resources,
  quantities, dates, evidence) created by RecordEvent (journaled, authorized, evidence minimum applies).
- Entries cite their event (EVIDENCED_BY/GENERATED_FROM edge) and, once Canon exists, the rule version;
  `fa explain entry` shows the event.
- Determinism property: re-evaluating rule v over event e (stripped Cx) reproduces the entry digest; a
  checker clause registered dormant until fa-c34 lands, live after.

## Tests
RecordEvent round trip; entry cites event; (after fa-c34) reproduction property over generated events.
acceptance_criteria: RecordEvent live on CLI/MCP; entries cite events; reproduction clause live once Canon lands.

title: fad tick/sweep scheduler and CLI timing intents: the clock and the System authority live in fad only (plan §5.4; no fa tick/sweep, no --grant system in the embedded CLI)
description:
WHY (CobaltGull ruling 2026-10-11 01:3xZ on JadePeak 3346): plan §5.4 says "the fa daemon orders one ExpirySweep control entry per configured tick carrying rollback-resistant time evidence". The kernel side is landed (fa-ctf: record_tick with TickRequest, sweep/sweep_batch under the book's System principal, due_holds/due_reversals, scheduled reversals by identity) but nothing drives it: fa post still refuses timeout_ns, with_auto_reverse has no CLI, and no posture records ticks. Doctrine 3 and 6 fix where the clock may live: a posting rule never reads the wall clock, recorded time is never user-supplied, and the lab runtime's virtual clock is the only legitimate control of the ticks. The embedded `fa` CLI therefore never reads a clock and never mints System authority; fad, as the posture that owns the writer lease, does both.

WHAT:
1. fad scheduler: a `[daemon] tick_ns` row in registries/verbs.toml; fad reads its own clock under its Cx (clock capability granted to fad only), records one TimeEvidence tick per interval through `Book::record_tick(observed_utc_ns, capability)` with the System capability it derives from the book's keys as lease holder, then runs one bounded sweep (`Book::sweep(capability, max_batch)`) and one bounded scheduled-reversal batch; `fad sweep-now` for an operator-requested cycle; every cycle is journaled as the existing control records, nothing else.
2. Book adapters (fa crate): record_tick / sweep / sweep_reversals taking the capability; the principal is the capability's holder, which the kernel requires to be System; describe = seal_text, fallible (KernelError::Entropy propagates, txn.abort() first, per 3303/3304); no principal argument from the caller; never mint System in an adapter.
3. fa CLI: post intents gain `timeout_ns` (Pending) and `reverse_on` (Adjusting) as data only; `fa triage` reports due_holds / due_reversals / blocked_reversals and names the next step ("start fad serve --book <dir>; it ticks and sweeps"); there is NO `fa tick`, NO `fa sweep`, and NO `--grant system` in the embedded CLI (an ambient-authority escape hatch, refused by design).
4. Refusals: a sweep request without the System capability is the existing 013; a tick with a non-monotonic observation follows the registered tick law (094–098); a daemon without a clock capability refuses to start its scheduler with a typed error naming the posture.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: under the lab runtime's virtual time a Pending with timeout_ns expires on the first tick past its deadline via fad's scheduler and `fa triage` then reports zero due; an Adjusting with reverse_on is reversed by the scheduled batch at the period open; a `fad sweep-now` sweeps exactly the due population under max_batch_entries; [ ] planted negatives: the embedded CLI has no verb that records a tick (parity test over verbs.toml); an adapter that accepts a caller-supplied principal fails the kernel's System check (013); an entropy failure in describe aborts the transaction and leaves frontier, cursor, resolution and reversal unchanged, then a retry succeeds; a wall-clock read anywhere outside fad's scheduler fails the Cx capability audit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-15.expiry live, recorded-time-never-user-supplied) + lab-runtime simulation; [ ] consumers: operators running fad, agents reading triage, G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: virtual-time proofs show the scheduler's law, not wall-clock accuracy of a production host.

TESTS: fad lab tests under virtual time (tick → expiry → triage zero; scheduled reversal at open; sweep-now bounded), fa-cli binary tests for the new intent fields and triage lines with transcripts logged, parity test that verbs.toml has no tick/sweep verb for the embedded posture, Cx capability audit test.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in crates/fad/src/clock.rs, crates/fad/src/timed.rs, crates/fad/tests/clock_audit.rs, and FA-INV-15.expiry in registries/invariants.toml

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-24: independent check of the acceptance against main f73aa6f5. Not closable. Here is what is met and what is missing, cited.

**Met**
- **Kinds.** `fa_model::DIMENSION_KINDS` holds ids 2..=9 (ids.rs:397). It is a Rust constant, not a registry file, and there are no custom kinds yet.
- **Values, hierarchy and valid time.** SchemaChange kinds 17, 18 and 19 write the Dimension and DimensionValue vertices plus a CHILD_OF parent edge (fa-journal dimension.rs:316-506), with valid time [from, to).
  - A close only shortens a window. It is refused with FA-REF-195 while a tagged leg is dated on or after the close.
  - All three writers run admit_schema_change (whole book, schema_change) and a capability witness. write_authority has their rows.
- **The commit-time law** (post.rs:1545-1565):
  - a missing required value is FA-REF-005, exit 3;
  - a value outside its window is FA-REF-195;
  - an unknown value is FA-REF-100.
  - Legs the preparer does not choose are exempt. These are applying legs and the dictated classes Reversal, Resolution, Closing, Revaluation, Elimination and Migration (dimension.rs:1134; post.rs:1542). Reclassification is judged (92d46bf6).
- **CLI:** `fa dimension add|list|require|close`, a leg's `"dimensions"`, and `fa tb --dimension k=v` (value and descendants, literal fold, uncertified). The test is cli.rs a_leg_tags_dimension_values_the_book_holds_inside_their_valid_time. It covers the planted missing-required, out-of-window and unknown-value cases.
- **MCP:** the on-demand fa.dimensions cluster, with parity at registry level only.

**Missing**
1. **fa-reference has no dimension law.** Its Leg carries only an entity, and there is no requirement or effectivity logic. So FA-INV-01.dimensions has no differential checker and stays dormant, whatever its wording ends up being.
2. **No differential emits dimensions.** differential.rs tags only the legal entity. Its serial replay asserts `dimension_set.is_empty()` ("a dimensioned leg"). fa-gen has no dimensions.
3. **No dimension register cells.** There is no RegisterDefinition, and CellKey is {account, unit, period}. That leaves no "register fold per dimension equals literal fold" test and no certified dimension report; the README says so.
4. **Only `required` exists:** there are no allowed or forbidden modes, and so no planted forbidden test. Requirements live on the Dimension vertex payload, not on Account rows (plan §4.3, Appendix A).
5. **FA-REF-005 no longer lists the allowed values.** 92d46bf6 disclosed this as a deviation from plan §4.3, and the 2026-10-12 E2E asks for it. Two things are stale:
   - the cli.rs:7513-7515 comment still says the refusal lists them;
   - the refusal_catalog FA-REF-005 row (58-63) mentions only legal entity and party.

**`fa tb ... --dimension <dimension>=<value> --certify [--certificate-out <new-file>]`:**
- It retains a report certificate in the new format `fa:report-certificate:v8`, with selector tag 6 and output `fa:dimension-trial-balance:v1`.

- Beside the usual seven native inputs, it binds the selected dimension's DimensionValue rows, filtered by dimension id. Their declared parents decide which values the report folds. Party and legal-entity values never enter the closure.
- There is no legacy registry closure.

**`fa replay C:<oid>`:** re-runs the same fold and prints the robot line byte for byte. The certified and uncertified reads share one fold, `fa::dimension::trial_balance_at`.

**`fa certificate status`:**
- These are relevant:
  - a value created under the selected one after the certificate, since a rerun at HEAD folds it;
  - any later leg tagged with a value in that HEAD set, within the selection's dates or periods.
- A leg tagged with another value, or a value created elsewhere, leaves the certificate Current.

**Authority:** admission is whole-book, as for the uncertified read.

title: Predicate-equivalence campaigns for fa-verify: honest-producer differential vs the register fold and a malicious-producer generator over authentic prefixes, for balance/prefix/inclusion/consistency/scope
description:
## Why
fa-e00 (confirmed 2026-10-12, Agent Mail 4862) showed the outsider balance check certifying Cr 5000 for a
staged migration chunk whose register fold is 0: fa-verify's `in_scope` (crates/fa-verify/src/balance.rs
~:60-65) selects records by class/account/unit/date only. Only the honest producer refused (FA-REF-133);
no test attacked the verifier. Meanwhile FA-INV-04.outsider-recomputation was registered live.
A mechanism, not a one-off fix, is needed so the next semantic gap is caught by construction.

## What to build
1. Honest-producer differential (fa-registers or fa-notary tests, generated histories with >= 8 seeds):
   histories include migration runs (open / finalized / abandoned / pre-opening), pending + voids,
   reversals and reversal ancestry, settlements, multi-unit and multi-entity entries, special periods,
   historical periods. For every (account, unit, cutoff) sampled: the honest balance proof verified by
   fa-verify's library equals the register fold; prefix/inclusion/consistency/scope proofs verify.
2. Malicious-producer generator: over the same authentic signed prefixes, hand-build proofs with
   record subsets, supersets, reordering, staged/abandoned chunks, wrong class/origin, mismatched
   migration controls, downgraded format versions. Property: fa-verify rejects, or computes exactly the
   honest value. Any accepted wrong value is a failure printed with the seed and a replay command.
3. Wire both as the checkers of FA-INV-04.outsider-recomputation (claim class invariant, checker kind
   differential) once fa-e00 lands; until then the clause is dormant.

## Tests & logging
Each failure prints seed, history length, the forged proof's structure, and the expected vs accepted
values. Campaign run counts recorded in the verdict manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Campaign green over >= 8 seeds on the trunk with fa-e00's fix; planted reversion of the fix makes the malicious campaign fail within one seed.

title: Attestation objects: ManualAssertion (reason-coded) satisfies the evidence minimum; Reviewed attestation promotes an AgentUpload document (plan §9.4, FA-INV-05)
description:
Background: fa-lp6 (TopazOsprey, swarm wave 1, 2026-10-10) enforces the per-class evidence minimum from registries/evidence_policy.toml strictly: an Intent-origin Original/Adjusting/Reclassification needs at least one admissible Document. The plan (section 9.2/9.4, FA-INV-05 evidence-minimum) also admits a ManualAssertion attestation as the honest alternative to a missing document, and requires a human Reviewed attestation before an AgentUpload-graded document counts toward the minimum. Neither attestation exists yet, so fa-lp6's refusal says so (stricter than the plan, never an exemption).

Scope: (1) Attestation as a journaled, content-addressed payload object (Appendix A): {kind: ManualAssertion|Reviewed|..., subject (entry proposal digest or document oid), principal, reason_code, statement, signed_digest excluding its own signature fields}, immutable after commit, with ATTESTS edges. (2) ManualAssertion satisfies the evidence minimum for the classes the registry row allows, carrying a registered reason code; the kernel resolves it inside the posting transaction as a witnessed read exactly like an EvidenceRef. (3) Reviewed attestation by a Human-profile principal (never the uploading agent: SoD rule) promotes an AgentUpload document to count toward the minimum; the kernel re-reads the attestation at post time (known-at correct). (4) CLI: fa attest manual --entry-proposal <digest> --reason <code> --json and fa attest review <doc oid> --json; robot envelope events; refusal catalog rows. (5) Oracle (fa-reference) models attestations as plain maps; differential plants: missing attestation (refused), self-review by the uploader (refused by SoD), reason code not in the registry (refused), valid ManualAssertion (admitted), Reviewed promotion (admitted). (6) Tests with detailed logs: kernel tests in crates/fa-journal/tests/genesis.rs, CLI binary tests, differential coverage floors for every planted negative.

No-claim boundary: a green suite proves the attestation path admits exactly the registered cases and refuses the planted negatives; it does not prove evidence sufficiency in any legal sense (state the technical predicate only).

title: control_kinds registry: register EntryOrigin::Control.control_kind (1 chart install … 8 capability revocation) in entry_classes.toml with a fa-registry reader, module constants replaced by registry symbols, totality/uniqueness gate, kernel class/kind cross-check
description:
WHY (TopazOsprey 3348/3353, CobaltGull ruling 2026-10-11 01:4xZ): `EntryOrigin::Control.control_kind` is a durable field in every control record's origin, but it is not registered anywhere; each module defines its own constant. At 26fa0cb the value 4 already carries two meanings (the TimeControl tick in sweep.rs and the PolicyControl capability revocation in policy.rs), and the unlanded fa-txf A had claimed 4 a third time. Nothing dispatches on the value today, because the class does, but a durable origin whose numbers are ambiguous cannot be read by fa-verify, Lantern or a migration without guessing. Doctrine 9 forbids serde-derived enums as durable formats; the registered-symbol pattern (symbols.toml, entry classes, refusal codes) is the house answer.

WHAT:
1. A `[[control_kinds]]` table in registries/entry_classes.toml with the eight rows: 1 chart_install, 2 period_transition, 3 policy_activation, 4 time_tick, 5 schedule_cancel, 6 import_run, 7 legal_hold, 8 capability_revocation; each row names its control class and the module that mints it.
2. fa-registry reader `control_kinds()` with a totality law (every row has a unique id and name; ids are dense from 1), and a registry test that plants a duplicate id and a gap and sees both refused at load.
3. Every module constant (sweep.rs, schedule.rs, policy.rs, the chart and period transition sites, fa-txf's import and hold) replaced by the registry symbol; a workspace grep test (or the registries gate step) refuses a literal `control_kind: <int>` outside the registry reader.
4. MistyPlateau moves capability revocation from 4 to 8 (no users; the durable value changes in place, no shim); fa-txf A uses 6, C1 uses 7.
5. fa-reference mirrors the table literally (its own copy of the eight pairs) so the differential catches a drift between the engine's origin bytes and the registry.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: every control record on a fresh book carries the registry's number for its kind and fa-verify's origin decoder names the kind from the registry; [ ] planted negatives: a duplicate id or a gap in the table fails the registry load test; a module literal outside the reader fails the gate; a control record minted with the wrong kind for its class is refused by the kernel's class/kind cross-check; [ ] proof class: invariant (registry totality + kernel cross-check); [ ] consumers: fa-verify, Lantern procedures over control records, migrations, every control-record author; [ ] no-claim boundary: the registry fixes names and numbers, not the semantics of each control class (those stay with their classes).

TESTS: fa-registry totality + planted-duplicate/gap tests, kernel class/kind cross-check tests per control class with the origin bytes logged, fa-reference mirror differential, gate step self-test.
