title: Missing detectors: graph.kiting (δ-temporal cycles over BankLine value dates), graph.ponzi_motif (cohort flows), duplicates.near, numbers.round_amount_density, sample.stratified on the CLI, jet.weekend_holiday with holiday tables and Principal.kind
description:
## WHY
§11.2–11.7 name these; at 0d338c0 kiting has no procedure (README:669 admits it), ponzi_motif, duplicates.near and
round_amount_density are absent, sample.stratified is library-only ("not on the CLI yet"), and jet.weekend is
weekends-only on effective/document dates without holidays or Principal.kind (procedures.toml:77).

## WHAT
graph.kiting: temporal cycles across bank instruments where a deposit's funding item clears after the deposit is drawn,
modelled on BankLine value dates and a float window parameter (δ-temporal motif search); graph.ponzi_motif: investor
cohorts by first inflow, new-money-to-redemption ratio per period over the party projection (fa-kxc4); duplicates.near with
registered amount tolerance and description similarity; numbers.round_amount_density; sample.stratified on CLI/MCP;
jet.weekend_holiday using fa-94qd holiday tables and recorded-time with Principal.kind filter. Each calibrated by fa-4psc.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: kiting detects the planted three-instrument kite in the fa-gen bank scenario; ponzi_motif detects the
  planted cohorts.
- [ ] planted negatives: clean retailer yields no kiting/ponzi findings; a cycle outside the float window is not flagged.

```acceptance-tests
fa-lantern::kiting::detects_planted_three_instrument_kite
```

title: Write-path authorization completeness: every journal-writing operation (chart import, period create, book create, document add, register advance/materialize/rebuild, certificate retention, checkpoint, holds) requires a named op on a presented capability, declared in verbs.toml, enforced before any observation
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14 at 9e83c3f)
`ctx.capability` is consulted only for transitions, approve, post, reverse (cli.rs:2522, 2692, 3502, 3952),
checkpoint (notary.rs:364) and proof export (proof.rs:143). Chart import (the plan says schema_change),
period create, book create, document add, register rebuilds and certificate retention run with no
capability at all — so authenticating `--as` (fa-v62/fa-r3q) alone would not gate them. MCP's bound-surface
admission (`admit_bound_command`, cli.rs:1162-1196) hard-codes the op per command in Rust instead of the
registry (§15.1). `registers advance`/`materialize` need only Read+Verify yet publish, so the default Agent
profile invalidates a Preparer's outstanding plans (wider than fa-1nx). Library `Book` methods for these
operations take no capability (fa-0x0 covers reads only).

## What to build
1. verbs.toml: every verb/subcommand row carries `requires_ops = [...]` and `writes = true|false`; the parity
   gate fails if a writing handler has no ops or the CLI/MCP admission differs from the row.
2. One admission function used by CLI, fad and MCP that reads the row, checks the presented capability
   (holder, book, ops, expiry, journaled revocation) BEFORE opening protected state; delete the hard-coded
   match in admit_bound_command.
3. Library: every writing `Book`/`AsyncBook` method takes `&Capability` (or the session handle of fa-v62)
   and checks the same ops; a no-capability writer is a compile error, not a convention.
4. Classify register maintenance and certificate retention as writes (ops `maintain`, `certify`), so a
   read-only profile cannot advance the frontier (resolves fa-1nx's wider form).

## Acceptance
- Generated matrix test: for every writing verb × {no capability, capability missing the op, expired,
  revoked, other book, correct} → refused (exit 7, FA-REF-011 with the missing op) except the last, and the
  journal frontier is unchanged on every refusal (point-read of the head before/after).
- MCP parity test asserts each advertised tool is usable under at least one launch profile or is a
  registered exclusion (kills the 7 dead tools found 2026-10-14).

## Tests & logging
Matrix test logs (verb, capability case, exit, refusal id, frontier before/after); binary e2e through `fa`,
`fad` and `fa-mcp` stdio.

comments.text:
## 2026-10-19 (claude-opus-5-5): allocate and register commands admit current authority before they observe or write (88e62ab3, 1b94b6a4, 3da42f32). Status: still OPEN

### Current state (read at 2f51e48e, handler by handler)
- **Owner route:** `ctx.capability` builds `Capability::embedded(principal, implied + --grant)`, so a handler's own implied ops can never fail there.
- **Bound route (MCP or `--token`):** `admit_bound_command` (cli.rs) checks only the ops from the hard-coded `bound_command_ops` match. It does not read verbs.toml and does not check expiry, revocation or a books caveat. Handlers that need those use `open_admitted` plus `Book::read_scope` or a kernel admission.

Gaps in that reading:
1. **allocate (fixed here).** The basis document was written through `Book::add_document` (no capability) before any capability-checked call. On the explicit-total path nothing was checked first. A revoked or expired read+post token therefore wrote the document, and only then did the kernel refuse.
2. **registers advance/materialize and verify registers (CLI admission fixed here; library open).** None of the three admitted anything. The bound route checked only the Read+Verify ops, so a revoked token read whole-book folds and published cells. `Book::{advance,materialize,rebuild}_registers` still take no capability. Item 4 of this bead (a `maintain` op) adds a durable op tag, so it needs a decision.
3. **document add on the owner route** stays `add_document`, the documented trusted owner intake (upload.rs module doc). The bound route already uses `preflight_intake` and `upload_document`.
4. **tb/statement/open-items/explain `--certify`** retain under `read` only. fa-1nx closed that by decision: plans bind to the accounting frontier, and the owner's MCP e2e asserts that an Agent can certify. I left it alone.
5. **Item 1** (`requires_ops` rows in verbs.toml, with `bound_command_ops` generated from them) and **item 3** (no capability-free writer in the library) are not started.

### This slice (88e62ab3)
- `fa allocate` (`--intent` and `--review`) opens with `open_admitted` plus `read_scope`.
- The basis document goes through `Book::upload_document` under the caller's capability (post, book scope, expiry, revocation witness), with the uploader and grade derived from it. The grades are the same 3/4 the handler used to hard-code, and the oid depends only on kind and bytes.
- **Planted negative** (`authority_cli` revoked-token test): `allocate --intent` with a well-formed explicit allocation is refused FA-REF-023 (exit 7) before the book is disclosed, and the head is unchanged.
- **Positive:** the existing owner-route allocation workflow (cli.rs explicit and balance review → approve → commit) runs on the upload path.
- **Not claimed:** `--dry-run` still records the basis document, which a later `fa commit --plan` cites.

### Register commands (1b94b6a4)
- `registers advance`, `registers materialize` and `verify registers` admit exactly as `fa verify periods` does, inside `open_admitted` and before observation: `admit_read`, `require(verify)`, whole-book reach on trunk, then `read_scope` (not expired or revoked).
- **Planted negatives** (same revoked-token test): all three are refused FA-REF-023 (exit 7), with the book undisclosed and the head unchanged. Under the old code, advance published cells and verify exited 0.
- **Still covered:** the FA-REF-011 op refusals and the MCP e2e advance/verify. fad's timed maintenance calls the library and is unaffected.
- **Remaining:** the library register methods' capability and the `maintain` op (item 4), plus items 1 and 3.

### Central current-authority admission for bound sessions (3da42f32)
An audit of the handlers that open with plain `ctx.books.open` found about 20 read paths where a revoked or expired bound token that still holds `read`/`verify`/`produce` read book data. The bound route checked only that the ops were held. The paths: `entry show` (sealed description opened), every `explain` subcommand, `tb` without `--summary`, named `statement`, `open-items`, `triage`/`next`, `procedure run`, `export` (the whole journal), and `verify accumulator|projections|availability|open-items|schedules|replay`. The envelope coordinate was stamped before any check.

- **The fix:** `Book::admit_current(&Capability)` checks the books caveat, then `fa_journal::policy::current_at` at the head (not expired, not revoked, a holder-bound token issued here). It needs no op and judges no scope. `BookSource::open` runs it for every bound session before the book is read, its coordinate stamped, or a scenario materialized. Handlers that already admit through `open_admitted` are unchanged. The owner route presents per-handler embedded capabilities and is unaffected.
- **Planted negatives** (revoked-token test): `tb --period`, `entry show`, `explain period`, `triage`, `verify accumulator`, `verify projections` and `verify replay` are each refused FA-REF-023 (exit 7), with the book and coordinate null and the head unchanged. Under the old code they read the book.
- **Unchanged:** the `--token` CLI and fad tests still get FA-REF-023 after revocation (now at open), and a live issued token still reads and plans.
- **Remaining:**
  - Scope caveats (periods/accounts/known-at) on handlers without ReadScope are still each handler's to enforce; this check covers currency, not reach.
  - `retain_report_certificate` writes `--certificate-out` (notary.rs:193) before `retain_certificate_authorized` (:195). For bound sessions `admit_current` now runs first; the order should still be check-then-write.

Gates: k13 at the landed tip 3da42f32 (main and master, non-force; worker vmi1149989, -j 1): `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` exit 101, 2307 passed and 3 failed. All three were red on main before this stack: registry-check `real_workspace_registries_pass` (major = 2 in object_schemas/book.toml from 575f9ce5 and bank_import.toml from fd68920a), fa-registry `the_catalog_and_every_declared_refusal_agree_three_ways` (DOCUMENT_INTAKE raised with exit refusal by fd68920a), and fa `certificate_status_detects_period_catalog_changes_without_a_new_entry` (journaled period births, 575f9ce5). That attribution rests on inputs: this stack changes none of those files or raise sites, and all three passed in the 2237/0 gate at 64a3ec20. It was not re-executed on 2f51e48e. registry-check fails at its object-schema step; the typed registry, disk and claims-lint steps that cover this stack's verbs/scoreboard/invariants edits run before it. UBS 0 critical on the changed .rs files. Not run: scripts/check.sh, cargo deny. rustfmt: this stack's hunks are clean; main's existing drift is left alone.

title: `fa verify accumulator` must detect post-checkpoint rewrites and retirements of journal vertices (it rebuilds from historical snapshots and is blind to later in-place changes)
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): `verify_accumulator` rebuilds each AccumulatorState from `Journal::read(…, Some(st.through_seq))` (crates/fa-notary/src/state.rs:518), i.e. `vertices_at(through_seq)`; the substrate returns the version visible at that sequence (frankengraphdb crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs:4441-4448). A later write that replaces an Entry vertex's payload property (with recomputed digests) or retires the vertex is therefore invisible to verification, while trial balances at head use the altered data. The kernel never writes such versions (payload immutability, FA-INV-02), so this is exactly the adversary tamper evidence exists for (a privileged process or a second writer with the book keys). Only a new `checkpoint` (prefix-extension check at head) or the maintainer's delta guard would notice. The README says verification "recompute[s] the stored chain from the journal" — true only for the historical view.

WHAT: verification also reads the head view of every leaf vertex in the checkpointed prefix and requires: not retired, payload bytes and _fa_digest at head equal the checkpointed record digest, no later version of a payload property (use the substrate's version history if exposed; otherwise compare head vs at-seq bytes); a mismatch is exit 8 with a finding naming the vertex and the first differing sequence. Cost is O(prefix) per verify — state it in the output and in operation_costs.toml (fa-i5s). Add the same head-vs-historical check to `fa verify registers` input selection.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: clean books verify; [ ] planted negatives (real storage writes through the substrate API in a test, bypassing Folio): rewrite an entry payload with recomputed digests after a checkpoint → exit 8; retire an entry vertex → exit 8; rewrite a Leg mirror only → caught by INV-16 check (fa-avx), not this one; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-14.consistency strengthened) ; [ ] consumers: fa-70o, auditors, fa-verify bundles (the bundle path must carry the same guarantee); [ ] no-claim boundary: detects rewrites inside the book directory; a wholesale replacement of the directory is detected only by witnessed checkpoints (fa-l3c).

TESTS: crates/fa-cli/tests/notary.rs with the substrate write performed by a test helper, transcripts logged.

O(prefix) operation_costs.toml row remains tracked by fa-i5s.

title: substrate: fgdb-sim FaultVfs path-alias identity gap (namespace debts use literal PathBuf equality: create_dir_all("keys/nested") records ""/"keys" while a dot-anchored save syncs "."/"./keys") — upstream fix + re-pin; until then every FaultVfs crash regression states the anchoring it relies on as a no-claim line
description: WHY (WhiteCreek 3567, 2026-10-11 05:06Z, source review of fgdb-sim/src/vfs.rs sync_dirents ~1265/1298 and create_dir_all ~1807 at the pinned substrate rev): FaultVfs's durability namespace debts are keyed by literal PathBuf equality. A caller that creates 'keys/nested' records parent debts under '' and 'keys'; a lawful save of 'keys/nested/book.keys' that anchors at '.' syncs '.' and './keys', so the debts stay unmatched and the simulated crash verdict depends on path spelling, not on fsync semantics. Unix fsync is not implicated; this is a simulation alias-identity gap (it also affects caller-precreated unanchored book/blob ancestors). Doctrine 10: the substrate is consumed, never forked or patched here; no app-side fake-fsync workaround. WHAT: (1) file the defect upstream in frankengraphdb (fgdb-sim) with the exact repro (two spellings of one directory, one debt, one sync); (2) when the fix lands, bump the fgdb-sim/fgdb rev together (same rev law, franken-stack.lock) and re-run every FaultVfs regression; (3) until then, every FaultVfs-based crash regression in this repo (fa-txf blob durability fence; fa-0fl crash campaign) states in its test doc and in the bead's no-claim line that it proves the anchored spelling it uses and nothing about alias spellings. title: fa-verify trusts producer-authored envelope fields for out-of-scope leaves: a dishonest producer can omit entries and a false balance verifies as `recomputation` — make scope membership recomputed or fraud-provable, and label the premise until then
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14 at 9e83c3f)
`in_scope` (crates/fa-verify/src/balance.rs:73) selects balance-proof candidates from envelope fields
`class`, `account_vids`, `unit_ids`, `effective_day`. Those fields are re-derived from the record
(`check_record`) only for SELECTED leaves. The same applies to v2's MigrationControl selection
(migration_balance.rs:122) and to `ProductionScope::selects` (proof/production.rs:59).
Failure: a book owner running a modified notary writes an envelope for a real expense entry with class=2
(Pending), or drops the account from `account_vids`, or moves `effective_day` past the cutoff. The root
commits to that envelope, so the trusted checkpoint covers it; the balance proof omits the entry; `fa-verify
balance` accepts the false balance with `scope: recomputation`. Productions likewise omit entries while
`seq_range_complete` passes; in v2, mislabelling a Finalize control hides a finalized migration.
Plan §13.2 says an authenticated index root "is not by itself proof that the index was derived correctly …
index-to-journal recomputation remains mandatory for a recomputation claim". FA-INV-04.outsider-
recomputation is registered `live`/`invariant` (invariants.toml:354-365). No negative test exists.
This is the same class as fa-e00 (P0): the outsider verifier is the product's A3 promise.

## What to build (pick one per proof kind, record the ruling)
A. Payload-complete scope (simple, sound now): the proof carries every leaf's record (complete-prefix with
   payloads), and the verifier derives every envelope field from the record before selection. Size grows
   linearly; disclose the bound (current 64 MiB cap ≈ 450k entries).
B. Fraud-provable sorted scope index (scales): the producer commits a sorted Merkle index keyed by
   (account, unit, effective_day, seq) whose leaves bind the leaf-envelope digest; the verifier checks
   range completeness in the index, and ANY holder of any record can produce a compact fraud proof
   (record + its inclusion + the mislabelled index leaf) that `fa-verify fraud` checks. Witnesses who hold
   full prefixes sign an "index derived by recomputation through seq S" statement (fa-qtfd); the outsider
   accepts index-based scopes only under the configured witness policy, and the result is labelled
   `scope: index_witnessed` — never `recomputation`.
Until A or B lands for a proof kind, that kind's result is labelled
`premise: producer-derived envelope selection fields` and FA-INV-04.outsider-recomputation is demoted to
dormant with this bead as its activator.

## Acceptance
- Planted negatives (malicious producer generator): for each mislabel (class, account set, unit set,
  effective day, Finalize control kind, production scope) the verifier refuses with exit 8 under A, or
  reports the index-based label under B and `fa-verify fraud` accepts the fraud proof.
- Honest-producer differential (fa-fqi) stays green.
- invariants.toml clause text and status match the shipped behaviour.

## Tests & logging
Generator in fa-notary tests producing mislabelled envelopes over generated histories (≥ 8 seeds); each
verifier run logs the proof kind, scope label, selected/total leaves and the refusal code.
close_reason: Closed after verifying BALANCE_FORMAT_V3 payload-complete balance proofs, PREFIX_FORMAT_V2 payload-complete prefix proofs, legacy v1/v2 membership_only labeling, and fixing stale scope assertion in crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1534 (161 tests pass across fa-verify and fa-notary)

title: `fa period … --plan-out` silently truncates any existing file (including the book's own key file); every CLI/fad output path must create_new and refuse an existing path
description:
## Why (verified 2026-10-14 at 9e83c3f)
`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:2585` writes the period-transition plan with `std::fs::write(&target, bytes)`,
which truncates an existing file. Every other output path in the CLI uses `OpenOptions::create_new`
(cli.rs:3674, notary.rs:171, proof.rs:203) and verbs.toml promises "never overwrites" for plan outputs.
Failure: `fa period close FY26-P03 --plan-out <book>/book.keys` (or any existing certificate/plan/evidence
file) destroys it; with the key file gone the book cannot be opened and keys are never regenerated. Through
`fad`, the path resolves against the CLIENT-supplied `cwd`, so any process that can reach the socket can
clobber any file the daemon user can write. Same code on the integration line (wt-nlu cli.rs:2761).
AGENTS.md: "nothing an agent can type by accident may damage the books".

## What to build
1. Replace the write with the shared `create_new` helper used by `--plan-out` on post (one helper for every
   output path; no second implementation). Refuse an existing path with a catalog refusal naming the path
   and the fix (choose a new path), exit 2.
2. Audit every `std::fs::write`/`File::create`/`OpenOptions::truncate(true)` in fa-cli, fad, fa-mcp, fa:
   each output path either uses the helper or is documented as an intentional overwrite of a file the tool
   itself owns (none expected).
3. Add a tripwire test that greps the source tree (std-only, like the reference-boundary step) for
   `fs::write(` / `File::create(` in surface crates outside the helper and fails with the file:line.

## Acceptance
- Planted negative: `--plan-out` onto an existing file refuses, the file's bytes are unchanged (hash before
  and after), exit 2, robot `error` event names the path.
- Same through `fad` (socket request) and MCP (where plan_out is already refused — keep that).
- Tripwire test passes on the fixed tree and fails on the old line (prove by running it against a copy of
  the old cli.rs in the test's fixture).

## Tests & logging
Binary e2e in fa-cli/tests/cli.rs (real `fa` + tempdir book; logs the command, exit code, stderr and file
hashes); fad e2e in crates/fad/tests.
close_reason: Consolidated CLI output file creation (--plan-out, --review-out, --certificate-out) into write_new_output_file (OpenOptions::create_new(true) + 0600), replaced std::fs::write in period --plan-out, added source-scan tripwire and E2E existing-file/book.keys refusal tests directly and through fad.

title: fa-mcp lists only tools the launch authority can use and filters suggested_tool_calls by authority (6 tools can never succeed under any profile; 5 posting tools always refuse under the default Agent)
description:
## The defect
On main, tools/list advertises fa_book_create, fa_book_checkpoint, fa_chart_import_chart,
fa_time_create_periods, fa_time_approve and fa_evidence_import_document, which refuse under every launch
profile (admission matrix hard-coded in fa-cli cli.rs ~1157-1199), plus post/reverse/reserve/resolve/
commit_plan, which always refuse under the default Agent profile (FA-REF-013). suggested_tool_calls in
structured errors are not filtered by authority (fa-mcp registry.rs ~649-700, errors.rs ~72-86), so a
refusal can suggest another tool that will also refuse. Agents burn turns on dead ends.

## What to build
- Derive the admission matrix from verbs.toml (a per-verb `mcp_ops` / `profiles` field) instead of the
  hard-coded match in cli.rs; tools/list = tools whose required ops ⊆ launch ops.
- suggested_tool_calls and next_actions filtered by the same predicate; when nothing is admissible,
  the error says which operator action (outside MCP) is needed.
- Parity gate extended: every listed tool has at least one admissible call under the profile it is
  listed for (schema-level).

## Tests
e2e_stdio: default Agent launch → tools/list excludes the 11 dead tools; Preparer launch includes
posting tools; a refusal's suggested tools are all admissible.
acceptance_criteria: Tests green; MCP parity gate covers admissibility per profile.
close_reason: Added LaunchAuthority command/tool admission checker across fa-cli and fa-mcp; VerbTool descriptions append launch_admission_note when tools are unconditionally or partially refused under launch authority; Adapter::error_of and call_inner filter suggested_tool_calls and next_actions against launch authority and --files posture; verified with unit and integration tests.

comments.author: CobaltGull
comments.text: 2026-10-13 (CobaltGull): design tension found before implementing; needs an owner ruling. crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs (owner, ~1350) states "Valid accounting/evidence reaches Profile::Agent in the kernel; this must not be replaced by a blanket adapter write ban or an owner call" and asserts an Agent's fa_post_post (dry_run true and false) is refused FA-REF-013 by the kernel. Removing posting tools from an Agent session's tools/list is an adapter-level ban of exactly that kind, and a call to an unlisted tool becomes the framework's unknown-tool error instead of the structured kernel refusal. Proposed narrower slice that respects both: keep tools/list complete, but (1) filter suggested_tool_calls / next_actions by the launch authority (no refusal suggests a tool that must refuse), and (2) mark each tool's description with "requires: <ops>; refused under this launch: <reason>" derived from the bound-surface admission table, after moving that table out of fa-cli cli.rs admit_bound_command into one shared function. Hiding tools stays the owner's call.

title: One content-addressed chunked object layer for every durable object that can exceed the substrate's 16,384-byte row: Entries, Certificates, Documents, allocation bases, plan certificates, workpapers — boundary-tested at 16 KiB±1 for each
description:
## Why
The pinned substrate refuses any stored row over 16,384 bytes (fgdb-strata store.rs:123 at b323bd17). It has
now broken, one object kind at a time:
- Entries (fa-fdt): schema allows 8 MiB / 4,096 legs; native refuses ~500+ legs.
- Certificates (main): certificate_store.rs:182 writes one row; a TB with ~100 account×unit rows fails
  exit 5 (fixed on staging with an ad-hoc blob route c5f5b9c/b7b53e5/557c14d).
- Documents (main): inline bound is the 16 MiB policy; 16 KiB–16 MiB imports fail (fixed on staging bdcb490
  with a 12 KiB inline bound).
- Allocation bases: MAX_POSTING_TARGETS = 1024 but ~32 B/target + ~40 B/leg in one Entry row caps real
  allocations near 200 targets (by estimate, not measured).
- Plan certificates, scoped-production manifests and JSONL workpapers are next.
Each fix so far is local. The plan's doc_commit already defines a 4 KiB-chunk Merkle tree (§9.1).

## What to build
0. First check upstream FrankenGraphDB (fa-0mft re-pin) for a native large-object / chunked-value API; if
   one exists, adopt it through the pin (doctrine 10: consumed, never forked) and keep only the
   accounting-level ObjectRef contract here.
1. `fa-blob` (or a module in fa-model/fa-journal, per workspace_topology layering): one API
   `put_object(kind, bytes) -> ObjectRef{digest, len, chunk_root}` that stores bytes ≤ an inline threshold
   (registered in limits.toml, below 16 KiB minus row overhead, derived not guessed) inline and larger
   bytes as 4 KiB chunks keyed by content, with a chunk Merkle root identical to doc_commit's construction;
   `get_object(ref)` verifies the root. Writes ride the caller's transaction (no second publication).
2. Migrate every durable writer to it: Entry payload, Certificate, Document bytes (replacing both the
   staging blob store and the inline route), allocation basis, plan certificate, production manifests.
3. Every reader refuses a mismatched chunk root as corruption (exit 5) with the object ref.
4. operation_costs.toml rows updated (same-change law): chunked writes add k row writes per object.

## Acceptance
- For EACH object kind: fixtures at threshold−1, threshold, threshold+1, 16384±1 and 1 MiB round-trip
  through the real binary (post, certify+replay, document add+disclose, allocate 1,024 targets) with
  byte-identical reads; a planted chunk corruption refuses.
- fa-fdt closes on this mechanism (Entries up to the schema limit).
- No object kind writes a single unbounded property (tripwire: grep for set_vertex_property with a
  payload of unbounded length outside fa-blob).

## Tests & logging
Boundary matrix test per kind logging (kind, size, inline|chunked, chunks, root, read-back digest);
crash-point test between chunk writes and the referencing commit (all-or-nothing).

title: Admissibility three-way check: parse plan Appendix C from the plan's markdown (std-only) and diff it against registries/admissibility.toml and fa-reference's independent table; exhaustive class x state x kind cells
description:
## Why
The kernel and fa-reference both read admissibility.toml (and the oracle calls the kernel's own
`decide_disposition`), so a wrong registry row is invisible to the differential. The "exhaustive"
Appendix C test only counts cells (classes x 5) and spot-checks a few; admissibility.toml is never compared
to the plan's Appendix C text (invariants/topology/foundations are).

## What to build
- tools/ or fa-registry test: a std-only parser of COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN…md Appendix C table(s) into
  (class, state, kind, qualifier) → disposition.
- fa-reference gets its own hand-transcribed table (not read from the TOML) — coordinate with fa-vfu.
- A check.sh-run test that enumerates every cell and asserts plan == TOML == oracle == kernel decision
  (kernel via a pure decision entry point), printing the first mismatching cell with all four values.

## Tests & logging
Planted: flip one TOML cell → test fails naming the cell; flip one plan cell in a fixture copy → fails.
acceptance_criteria: Every cell agrees across the four sources; planted flips are caught.
close_reason: Implemented std-only Appendix C markdown parser (PlanAdmissibility::parse in fa-registry::admissibility_plan), replaced fa-reference Oracle's admissibility.toml reader with an independent hand-transcribed Appendix C matrix (fa_reference::admissibility::decide_cell), added pure kernel cell evaluator (fa_journal::decide_admissibility_cell), and wired the exhaustive 1,125-cell four-way cross-check (plan == toml == oracle == kernel + planted TOML/plan flip detection) into FA-INV-03.core.

title: fa-lantern first slice: procedures.toml registry, money-flow/preparer/document projections as verified folds, JET/duplicate/sequence-gap/cutoff/aging/digit procedures, graph procedures via fnx (tracing laws, related-party exposure, kiting, structuring) with CGSE determinism and complexity witnesses, Findings and workpapers as journaled objects with evidence rows, calibration corpus with measured precision/recall

The graph schema exists (symbols.toml labels/relations are written), so projections can be built. fa-fk5 (adopt-later graph algorithms) and fa-vpk (statistical lane with fsci-stats oracles) both presume this registry and these projections, so they depend on this bead.

WHAT (first slice):
1. `crates/fa-lantern` (analytics layer; procedures run under a Cx with no clock/entropy/net/fs): a `registries/procedures.toml` registry (id, inputs, output schema, evidence class = statistical | invariant, complexity witness, calibration status) and a `Procedure` trait returning `Findings` with evidence rows that cite entries/documents by ref, never by free text.
2. Projections: the money-flow projection (accounts × periods × units as a weighted graph of posted legs), the preparer/approver bipartite projection, the document-to-entry projection; each is a deterministic fold with a digest, rebuildable, never authoritative (FA-INV-04).
3. First procedures: JET (round amounts, period-end clustering, weekend/holiday posting by effective vs recorded date, same-preparer-approver), duplicate (exact and near on amount/date/counterparty), sequence gaps on document numbers, cutoff (document_date vs effective_date vs recorded_at across a boundary, plan §11.7), aging (open items from fa-registers' settlement folds), reconciliation (register vs bank lines once Teller exists; dormant until then), digit tests (first-digit distribution as a statistical score with the test statistic and sample size reported; fa-vpk adds the exact independent oracles).
4. Graph procedures via fnx (direct over projection graphs; Prism when live per Appendix H): tracing (follow value from a source account through settlements with a registered tracing law: FIFO, LIFO, pro-rata, lowest-intermediate-balance), related-party exposure (paths between flagged parties), kiting motif (round trips across cash accounts near period ends), structuring (sub-threshold clustering); each ranking carries a CGSE determinism witness (seed-free, order-independent) and a complexity witness checked by a test that the input size bound holds.
5. Findings and workpapers: `Finding` as a journaled, immutable object with `RESOLVES`/supersession lineage, severity as a statistical score (never a legal conclusion), the procedure version, inputs digest and the coordinate; `fa lantern run <procedure> --json`, `fa findings list`.
6. Calibration: synthetic planted-anomaly corpora with known labels; precision/recall reported per procedure in a manifest; G3 asks for "measured precision/recall".

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: on the planted corpus every procedure finds its planted anomalies with the reported precision/recall and a byte-identical ranking across two runs and two leg orders; a finding cites only refs that resolve; [ ] planted negatives: a procedure whose ranking depends on insertion order fails the determinism witness; a finding with a free-text citation is refused at commit; [ ] proof class: statistical (scores) with invariant-class determinism witnesses; [ ] consumers: forensic accountants and examiners, fa-vpk, fa-fk5, G3; [ ] no-claim boundary: a finding is a technical predicate with a score; it is never an accusation or a legal conclusion (AGENTS.md doctrine).

TESTS: fa-lantern unit tests per procedure on the planted corpus with per-finding logs, projection fold tests vs fa-reference naive procedures, CLI binary tests.

title: Polish Bar regression suite: verify-determinism, verify-stdout-stderr-split, verify-non-tty-discipline, and the first-try spellings agents actually type
description:
## WHY
Plan §15.1/§15.3 and Appendix D require named regression tests (`verify-determinism`, `verify-stdout-stderr-split`,
`verify-non-tty-discipline`) and G1 requires `fa triage|post|tb|explain balance|doctor` "at the Polish Bar". None of the
named tests exists; Polish Bar coverage is scattered across fa-cli/tests/cli.rs (853, 866, 888, 5151, 8306, 8335, 8591,
8633). First-try failures found: `--robot` is not accepted (only `--json`; verbs.toml:40), `fa gl` alias missing (only
`gl-detail`), `--for-period`/`--effective-at` absent, and `fa tb --jsno` exits 2 where the plan says read-class verbs run
with a warning (cli.rs:868).

## WHAT
`crates/fa-cli/tests/polish_bar.rs` driving the real binary: (1) determinism — every read verb twice under
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH yields byte-identical stdout; (2) stdout/stderr split — stdout parses as NDJSON envelopes only;
(3) non-TTY/NO_COLOR/CI/TERM=dumb — no ANSI, no prompts; (4) first-try matrix: `--robot` anywhere and first, `fa gl`,
`fa trial-balance`, `fa balance`, `fa journal`, `--for-period`, `--effective-at`, Levenshtein-1 typos on read verbs run
with a warning, on write verbs exit 2 with the corrected command; (5) every non-zero exit emits exactly one error event
with refusal_id/exit/class; (6) bare `fa` exits 0 and never opens a TUI. Add `--robot` and the aliases to verbs.toml.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: polish_bar.rs green; every row of the first-try matrix logged with argv, exit and event.
- [ ] planted negatives: injecting a timestamp read into a read verb fails determinism; a stray eprintln on stdout fails
  the split test.

```acceptance-tests
fa-cli::polish_bar::verify_determinism
fa-cli::polish_bar::verify_stdout_stderr_split
fa-cli::polish_bar::verify_non_tty_discipline
fa-cli::polish_bar::first_try_spellings_matrix
fa-cli::polish_bar::exactly_one_error_event_per_nonzero_exit
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: none needed beyond the suite. E2E: the suite itself drives the real binary. Logging: one JSONL record per matrix case {argv, env, exit, events, stdout_digest}.

title: Unit identity: reopening a book must reconcile the journaled Unit vertices with the binary's unit registry and refuse on mismatch; registry rows are id-stable; rendering never panics on an unknown unit
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §4.4 "A UnitId is immutable, scale included … historical payloads are never rewritten or reinterpreted". Genesis writes Unit vertices with their UNIT_ID (crates/fa-journal/src/genesis.rs:463-479), but `Book::open_dir` rebuilds the unit table from the binary's embedded registries/units.toml (crates/fa/src/book.rs:446 `fa_money::UnitRegistry::embedded()`) and never reads back or compares the journaled rows. Amounts store `unit_id: u32`; if a later binary inserts or reorders a row in units.toml, every stored mantissa is silently reinterpreted under a different unit/scale (e.g. 100 KWD read as 100 BTC), and `Amount::render` panics on an id it does not know (crates/fa-money/src/amount.rs:289). Nothing guards this today.

WHAT: (1) on open (dir and memory books), read every journaled Unit vertex and compare (id, code, kind, scale, rounding_default) with the binary's registry: equal ⇒ proceed; binary has extra later rows ⇒ proceed (additive-minor); any id whose code/scale differs, or a journaled id the binary lacks ⇒ refuse open with exit 5 and `fa doctor` guidance (never "best effort"). (2) fa-registry test: units.toml ids are explicit, unique, never reused, append-only against a pinned fixture (removing/reordering a row fails). (3) `render` returns a typed error for an unknown unit; the CLI maps it to exit 5. (4) The book's journaled unit table becomes the runtime source; the binary's table is only the admission set for NEW units (unit evolution itself is fa-thp).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: reopen with the same binary works; a binary with an added unit opens old books; [ ] planted negatives: a fixture book whose journaled USD id is re-mapped in a patched registry → open refused exit 5 naming the unit; render of an unknown id → typed error, no panic; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-02.unit-version activation precondition, FA-INV-06) ; [ ] consumers: fa-thp, every reader; [ ] no-claim boundary: does not implement redenomination or scale change (fa-thp).

TESTS: fa facade reopen tests over a persisted fixture book (real directory); fa-registry append-only test; fa-cli binary test for exit 5 with the error event logged.

title: fa-formats and external oracles: Beancount/hledger/ledger-cli balance differential on every fixture, TigerBeetle semantic corpus, AICPA ADS and SAF-T writers/readers with export-import identity and proofs, XBRL calculation-linkbase validation, published conformance matrices with documented divergences
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): The ladder's external oracles (Beancount/hledger/ledger-cli balance differential on every fixture, the TigerBeetle semantic corpus, AICPA ADS and SAF-T round trips, XBRL calculation-linkbase validation) and the W9 crate `fa-formats` have zero code at 96d1918 (0 hits). Gate G3 needs ADS/SAF-T exports with proofs; G4 needs the conformance matrices published with documented divergences. Export→import identity is also one of the metamorphic suites.

WHAT (ordered slices, one bead; split only if a slice needs its own owner):
1. `crates/fa-formats` (interop layer): a Beancount writer and a Beancount/hledger journal reader for the subset FrankenAccounting fixtures use (accounts, dated transactions, multi-unit postings, balance assertions); amounts exact (fa-money), no floats; every reader fuzzed (fa-fuzz bead).
2. Balance differential: for every fixture history (the genesis and differential corpora, later the §15.6 workflows), write Beancount, run `bean-check`/`bean-report balances` and hledger `balance` as external subprocess oracles (test-only, skipped as UNRUN when the tools are absent, never PASS), and compare per-account per-unit balances exactly with FrankenAccounting's trial balance at the same effective selector; divergences are recorded in `docs/conformance/beancount.md` with the reason.
3. TigerBeetle semantic corpus: the two-phase transfer semantics (pending/post/void/expire, per-leg sub-vector, reserved availability) replayed from a checked-in corpus of TigerBeetle-shaped scenarios with expected outcomes; divergences documented.
4. AICPA ADS (GL detail, TB, chart) and SAF-T (header, master files, GL entries) writers with round-trip readers; export→import identity test (byte-identical journal after re-import, FA-INV-04 refold equal) and a certificate naming the export's coordinate.
5. XBRL calculation-linkbase validation of statements (after fa-statements engine): the statement's calculation tree is emitted and validated against the linkbase; blocked on the statements bead.
6. Conformance matrices: one TOML per oracle with rows (fixture, expected, observed, divergence, reason) generated by the tests and rendered into docs; the gauntlet fails when a row changes without a documented reason.

title: Installer must refuse empty or unverifiable release artifacts before reporting success
description:
## Problem and current-source evidence
At source 32bed7d7 (unchanged through c7b5eb58), install.sh accepts an empty --artifact-dir. It conditionally checks SHA256SUMS only if present, conditionally installs each existing binary, then conditionally executes each existing binary. With --verify it prints "self-verification passed" even when all four binaries are absent. Fresh reproduction used new empty source/destination directories under /Users/jemanuel/.codex/artifacts/fa-reality-check-20261023.Nemi4F: bash install.sh --offline --artifact-dir SOURCE --dest DEST --verify exits 0, installs nothing. This is an actually executed shell counterexample, not an older Rust binary result. No open bead explicitly owns this defect; fa-eqk closed on release engineering and fa-ldfy does not list it.

## Required behavior and implementation
Repair install.sh and its real shell integration tests together. Determine the requested release binary set before writing. Under default verification, require a readable manifest and exactly matched checksum entries covering every installed release artifact; do not silently skip absent manifests, missing members or unsupported target artifacts. Preserve an explicit, clearly reported --no-verify choice if still admitted by owner policy, and never report that path as verified. Missing/corrupt/incomplete artifacts must fail before replacing any existing executable. Stage a complete validated candidate in a fresh location and use the existing installer contract for publication; do not invent unapproved destructive rollback or cleanup. Verification must execute all required probes, including the MCP posture as applicable, and report the actual checked set. An empty set can never succeed. Use the project's own honest User-Agent for any installer downloads.

## Acceptance and tests
Keep ordinary code and tests in this bead. Real-process shell tests use new temporary destinations, preserve test files and never touch HOME binaries. Cover empty source, no SHA256SUMS, omitted fa-verify, missing checksum row, wrong digest, non-executable/wrong-target member, successful complete synthetic release set, explicit opt-out labeling and preexisting destination preservation on each failure. Fixtures test installation mechanics only; they do not prove real release linkage or accounting.

```acceptance-tests
installer::missing_manifest_refuses_without_explicit_opt_out
installer::missing_member_or_bad_digest_preserves_destination
installer::success_requires_the_complete_executed_probe_set
```
These names are required future tests, not claims they already exist. Log exit code, required/verified members and content hashes without secrets. Full project checks and exact-tree proof remain required; UBS's unsupported shell verdict is not a pass. W10/G4, V36. Close only through the normal evidence-bound closure path.

comments.text:
## 2026-10-19 (claude-opus-5-5): adversarial audit of the agent surfaces, one defect class fixed; suite file not written. Status: still OPEN

### Audit method
Two read-only audits at 3da42f32 (one of the MCP surface, one of fad and issued tokens) went through the bead's ten attack classes. I re-read every claimed hole before acting on it.

### Refused today, and where
- **(1) Identity and authority override.** `as/grant/yes/keys/book/token/principal/profile/via` are refused as `forbidden_argument` (fa-mcp registry.rs). The same flags on an argv, including the `--x=v` form, are refused with usage exit 2 (entry.rs, cli.rs).
- **(2) Self-approval.** No launch ceiling or token profile holds `approve` (FA-REF-011, exit 7). The MCP `self_approval` detector fires first for a digest this session planned.
- **(3) Token replay or forgery.** A wrong or truncated secret, a holder that doesn't match the principal, or a never-issued token: exit 2 at decode, or FA-REF-156 at open.
- **(4) Revoked or expired mid-session.** FA-REF-023 / FA-REF-014 at book open for every command, reads included (3da42f32).
- **(5) Confused deputy.** `--as/--grant/--yes/--book/--keys/--token` beside a token: exit 2.
- **(6) Agent trunk writes.** post, commit, PostBatch, reserve, resolve, reverse, the typed documents, allocate/settle, event record, bank import and custody: FA-REF-013, raised by the kernel. Period transitions and schema changes: FA-REF-011.
- **(7) HumanUpload by an agent.** `import_document` with any `grade`: FA-REF-011. No grade: AgentUpload.
- **(8) Privileged documents.** A governed BankStatement reads redacted, or FA-REF-142.
- **(10) Placeholders.** `TODO/TBD/FIXME/YOUR_/<…>/…` are refused by the detector with exit 2.

### Fixed (216a93f2, landed on main at 2298d47a)
Five host-file inputs escaped both containment checks: `reverse --replace-with` and the positional object files of `chart open`, `party add`, `instrument add` and `entity add`. The checks are the launch `--files` root and fad's `--files-root`. Both checks now walk one shared list (`host_path_arguments`). Planted negatives are in the fad confinement test and in authority_cli. 2298d47a writes `--certificate-out` only after retention admission (fa-mg2j).

### Deliberately not changed
- **No route-level Agent trunk gate.** `bound_command_admissible`'s FA-REF-013 rule shapes tool descriptions and suggestions only; dispatch admits ops, and the kernel refuses. The e2e test says this is intended: "must not be replaced by a blanket adapter write ban". Side effects before that kernel refusal:
  - an Agent's `allocate --review` uploads its basis document (an Agent may upload documents anyway);
  - `--replace-with` was read first (now closed by containment).

### Needs an owner decision
1. **fad's tokenless route is owner authority for the daemon's uid** (fa-r3q). A same-uid holder can drop its token, or read another holder's 0600 token file.
2. **Sealed memo/description fields.** `entry show` and `party list` open them for any read holder. FA-THR-06 names "sealed Erasable<T> party/memo fields" as a protected asset with an unprivileged-agent actor, but its mitigation covers only documents.
3. **No broadcast-scope detector exists in fa-mcp.** Plan §15.x and AGENTS.md name one ("all accounts" on a write). `Verb.writes` is per verb, not per subcommand, and the open-items resource accepts `*`. A detector needs a definition of which arguments are scopes first, or it will refuse valid reads.
4. **Placeholder matching is uppercase-only.** Matching lowercase `todo` would misfire on ordinary text such as Spanish "todo", so I left it.
5. **Inconsistent result for the same token.** A token above its ceiling (System profile, or `approve`) gets exit 2 from fad and FA-REF-011 exit 7 from `fa --token`.
6. **Scope caveats.** doctor, triage and next ignore period/account caveats. This is latent, because CLI issuance cannot set caveats.
7. **Minor:**
   - fad's `status` frame needs no token (same uid only).
   - `stop` compares the owner token in non-constant time (same uid only).

### Where each live class is already a planted negative (so no duplicate suite file)
| Class | Test(s) |
|---|---|
| (1) Override arguments | e2e_stdio `the_server_over_stdio_matches_the_cli_byte_for_byte_on_data` loops every `FORBIDDEN_ARGUMENTS` entry; also `default_agent_authority_survives_stdio_and_cannot_be_changed_by_a_call` |
| (2) Self-approval | the same byte-for-byte test (the `self_approval` detector); authority_cli `handlers_cannot_add_operations_omitted_from_the_launch_grant` |
| (3), (4) Token replay and revocation | e2e_stdio `an_issued_token_binds_the_session_and_its_revocation_is_enforced`; fad.rs `token_sessions_through_fad_bind_each_request_to_its_holder`; authority_cli `revoked_report_and_evidence_authority_cannot_disclose_book_or_instant_metadata` (18 commands) |
| (5) Confused deputy | fad.rs token sessions (`--as` beside a token); fad.rs confinement, which now includes the five inputs fixed here |
| (6) Agent trunk writes | e2e_stdio default-authority test; authority_cli `an_agent_launch_rehearses_typed_documents_but_never_posts_them_to_trunk` |
| (7) HumanUpload grade | authority_cli `owner_mutations_are_refused_before_input_files_or_book_creation` |
| (8) Privileged reads | fa `book::tests::a_bank_statement_through_the_facade_reads_redacted_until_privileged`; fa-journal redaction tests (FA-THR-06 test_refs) |
| (10) Placeholders | fa-mcp detect `placeholders_positive_and_negative` |

Dormant:
- (9) Ceiling split across calls waits on daily_total (fa-llx).
- The broadcast-scope part of (10) waits on the missing detector.

title: One certificate contract for every report family: 14 format tags today, only ReportCertificate can be retained, replayed by `fa replay` or checked by `certificate status` — unify retention, replay, status and FA-INV-11 checkers across all families
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14)
Aging, aging reconciliation, portfolio, roll-forward, GL detail, cash flow ×4, statement diff/trace and summary
TB each define their own certificate format (14 tags across ~11 families). They are portable bytes that
embed whole-book native evidence and nest each other's outputs, but cannot be retained in the book, replayed
through `fa replay`, or checked by `fa certificate status`. Capability commitment is the constant
`"embedded-owner"` in most; there is no completeness grade or replay command (App A Certificate schema).

## What to build
1. One `Certificate` envelope (App A) with a `family` discriminator and family-specific inputs; every
   family's producer emits it; retention through the BLOB layer; `fa replay` and `certificate status`
   dispatch by family; nested sources referenced by certificate oid, not embedded copies.
2. Bind the real capability commitment, completeness grade and a replay command string.
3. FA-INV-11 clauses per family, live, with replay tests as checkers and a planted output-byte mutation as
   the negative (INVGATE).
4. fa-verify (offline) can check the envelope's self-digest and nested-oid structure (fa-70h4 extends it to
   full offline report verification).

## Acceptance
Every family: certify → retain → replay byte-identical → status Current; a later backdated entry → status
SupersededBy with the entry; envelope round-trips through fa-verify; certificates > 16 KiB retained.

## Tests & logging
Per-family binary e2e; logs family, oid, size, replay verdict.

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-25: a status audit against main deec8188. The description (10-14) is stale on item 1. No code changed.

**1. One envelope, retention, `fa replay`, `fa certificate status`: implemented.**
- `fa::ReportArtifact` (fa/src/report_artifact.rs) is the one family-discriminated envelope, over 18 families: native, summary, effective-date-aging, roll-forward, equity-roll-forward, external-feed, cash-flow, indirect-cash-flow, aging-reconciliation, procedure, statement-diff, statement-trace, aging-portfolio, split and policy cash flow, scenario-diff, draft-diff and query.
- `notary::retain_report_artifact` retains any of them; certificate_store chunks bodies above the row limit.
- `fa replay` and `fa certificate status` decode a ReportArtifact and dispatch by family (notary.rs `certificate_cmd`, with family-specific status for summary, query and scenario-diff and the shared path for the rest).

**2. Real capability commitment, completeness grade, replay command: open.**
- fa/src/certificate.rs:69 is still `pub const AUTHORITY: &str = "embedded-owner";`.
- I found no completeness grade or replay-command field in the envelope.

**3. FA-INV-11 per family: partial.**
- `FA-INV-11.core` is live (5 checkers, 4 negatives) and `FA-INV-11.finding-replay` is live (6, 3).
- `FA-INV-11.report-replay` ("every report, finding and bundle replays byte-for-byte from its certificate; erased closure elements downgrade the grade") is dormant with no checker. Its erasure half waits on the erasure machinery (FA-INV-12.erasure, fa-v74).

**4. fa-verify offline check of the envelope: open.**
- crates/fa-verify/src/report.rs knows only `fa:report-certificate:v1` and `v4`.
- It knows no other report-certificate version (v2, v3, v5 to v8) and no other family's format (fa-70h4 is the offline-verification bead).

So what remains is items 2 and 4, plus the report-replay clause's checker. The rest of the acceptance ("certify, retain, replay byte-identical, status Current; certificates over 16 KiB retained") needs a per-family run to confirm. I have not run one here.

description:

## Scope & Implementation Plan

title: FDIC Part 370 on the CLI: deposit instruments, account participants with ORC codes, and `fa export part370` (the last absent vision step, WF-FDIC-03)
description:
## WHY
Plan §15.6 workflow 3 ("Part 370 is a registered profile, not a trial balance"): deposit `Instrument { kind: Deposit }` liabilities carrying ownership-right-and-capacity codes, `Party` participants (owners, beneficiaries, agents) as role-typed edges, aggregation per owner across accounts and capacities, provisional holds as Pending entries, and fa-formats writers for the four output files at the end-of-day effective date. `fa_formats::part370::generate_part370_bundle` (customer, account, account-participant and pending files, owner aggregation, certificate digest, golden fixtures) is finished library code with no caller. fa-pbm closed on the library, but scoreboard WF-FDIC-03 (`fa export part370`) is the one vision step still `absent`, and it cites fa-pbm. The REA model cannot feed it today:
- `InstrumentKind` has no Deposit (BankAccount is a book's own account at another bank).
- There is no instrument–party participant edge with a role, ORC code, ownership share or beneficiary count.
- `PartySpec` has no tax-id type or address fields beyond free identifiers.

title: Make unit evolution, signs, overflow, and FX residual laws mutually consistent
description:
References: §§4.4, 5.2, 6.1/6.4/6.7, Appendix A/F (lines 325, 395, 443, 455, 467, 1131-1132, 1145-1146, 1328, 1333).
1. Amount stores only unit_id and i128 mantissa. §4.4 allows changing that unit's scale and rescaling every stored mantissa, contradicting immutable entries and digests. Example: mantissa 100 means 1 at scale 2 and 0.1 at scale 3. Use immutable unit-version identity with a named conversion/migration law; never silently reinterpret or rewrite historical payloads. Distinguish precision changes from economic redenomination.
2. Entry legs have both Debit/Credit and signed i128 without a nonnegative-leg rule. Reversal wording says exact negation without deciding side swap vs signed storno. Negative legs can undermine per-side amount limits and produce two representations of the same posting. Define one canonical sign convention and boundary behavior, including i128::MIN.
3. Bounded checked i128 amounts are not an unrestricted ordered abelian group: MAX+1 and -MIN fail. Proofs/metamorphics need representability hypotheses or an unbounded reference domain; summation policy must define intermediate overflow and register cumulative totals.
4. FX residual encoding is incomplete: EUR debit 1 minor unit + debit 1 = credit 2; at rate 1/2 under HalfUp, USD base debits 1+1 != credit 1. Adding one USD credit residual fixes base balance but violates USD per-unit balance. Define lawful base-only valuation/residual effects or a complete balanced construction, including remeasurement and historical-cost release, without inventing funds or weakening FA-INV-01.
Acceptance must include these exact examples, inverse/cross-rate scale boundaries, negative refunds/allocations and both per-unit/base validation. W1/W2/W7, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.4 immutable unit versions (USD@2 -> USD@4 via ScaleConversion law + Redenomination record; historical mantissas never reinterpreted), non-negative mantissas with side swap (no storno; i128::MIN unreachable), bounded register accumulators; §6.1 bounded abelian group with representability hypothesis and independent reference arithmetic; §5.2 valuation residual absorbed by a designated leg with the exact EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ 1/2 HalfUp counterexample, conversion-account pairing for realized FX, revaluation through Valuation contra leaves; §6.5 lot laws. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: fa-money valuation test realizes the EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ ½ HalfUp counterexample (designated-leg residual). WhiteCreek 2744: per-legal-entity base equality + residual selection is NOT implemented; the kernel does no base valuation yet, so the single-residual Option is the single-entity subset; multi-entity proposals must refuse until the residual-list schema/checker lands (awaiting the fa-p7r handoff patch).
close_reason: All four requirements now live and verified: immutable unit versions & conversion laws (fa-2ly), non-negative leg mantissas with side swap & bounded i128 accumulator checks (fa-money/fa-registers), and journal FX-law admission/base_totals/designated-leg base_residual with EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ 1/2 HalfUp end-to-end test (fa-s3c)

description:
## The defect
fa-journal `record_tick` (sweep.rs ~446-531) has no upper bound on `observed_utc_ns`, and `monotonic_ok`
is whatever the caller passes; TimeTick payload validation is empty (fa-model entry.rs ~1104-1136).
Anyone holding `witness` can journal `observed_utc_ns = u64::MAX`: every timed hold becomes due and no
later honest tick is admissible (ticks must increase), so the book's time axis is permanently stuck.

## Design
- Ticks enter only from fad's clock loop under System authority (plan §7.1a); the library/CLI path that
  records ticks for tests is lab-only (fa-sim) and cannot set corroboration.
- Corroboration: fad computes `monotonic_ok` from its own monotonic clock delta vs the UTC delta since
  its previous tick in the same process; first tick after restart is uncorroborated (already true).
- Bound: an instant beyond (last corroborated tick + measured monotonic elapsed + registered skew from
  limits.toml) is recorded `uncorroborated: true` and can never be the basis of automatic effects
  (expiry, scheduled reversals); later honest ticks remain admissible (monotonicity is enforced against
  the last corroborated tick, not the last recorded one).
- Refusal rows for malformed ticks; oracle mirrors the rule.

## Tests
Planted: tick u64::MAX via the library → refused or recorded uncorroborated; a subsequent honest tick
is admitted and expires due holds; differential over generated tick sequences with skew injections.
acceptance_criteria: Planted far-future tick cannot stop later honest ticks or trigger effects; differential green.
close_reason: Enforced MAX_TICK_UTC_NS (i64::MAX as u64) and MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_NS (366 days) in limits.toml, ControlPayload::validate, fa-journal, and fa-reference; downgraded skew-exceeding ticks to monotonic_ok = false; enforced tick monotonicity, hold anchors, and HOLD_DUE checks against latest_corroborated_tick so an uncorroborated forward jump never bricks subsequent honest ticks or sweeps; filtered superseded uncorroborated forward jumps from temporal instant resolution; added unit, differential, and fad virtual-time lab tests.

title: Multi-currency application law: open_base per open item, RemainingCarryingValue relief law, typed ApplyPayment differences, reachable realized-FX settlement through the conversion account
description:
## WHY
§5.7: each open item has open_native and open_base; relief uses a named law (RemainingCarryingValue: law-rounded
open_base·x/open_native, final application relieves all remaining base); reversing an application restores exactly the
recorded relief; Appendix B ApplyPayment carries typed differences (Discount, ShortPay, Writeoff, BankCharge, RealizedFx)
so no difference becomes a plug; §5.2 cross-unit settlement routes through the conversion account with a paired
realized-FX leg. At 0d338c0 OpenItem is native-only (open_items.rs:45-62); fa/src/settlement.rs:1-6 has the caller author
difference legs; `plan_realized_fx_settlement` (fa-registers fx.rs:551-660) is unreachable and needs a caller-supplied
carrying_base_amount — the plug risk §5.2 forbids.

## WHAT
open_base fold with recorded relief per application; law ids registered in fx_laws.toml; `fa receipt|payment
--difference kind=…` and MCP equivalents; realized-FX planner wired into application with carrying basis derived from the
journal; `fa verify fx-conversion` (with fa-3ock) checks the conversion account's functional balance is zero after
revaluation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: the plan §5.2 six-leg EUR invoice / USD receipt example posts exactly as written; reversal restores
  native and base relief exactly; reference oracle agrees.
- [ ] planted negatives: an application with an unexplained cash difference refused naming the open amount; a supplied
  base_amount that disagrees with the derived carrying basis refused.

```acceptance-tests
fa-registers::fx::cross_currency_settlement_matches_plan_example
fa-registers::differential::application_relief_agrees_with_reference
fa-cli::cli::receipt_difference_requires_kind
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: relief law arithmetic incl. final application; reversal restoration. E2E: real binary — EUR invoice, USD receipt with a RealizedFx difference, reversal of the receipt, `fa explain balance` and `fa tb` per unit; reference oracle comparison. Logging: plan output shows conversion-account legs and relief amounts.

title: Qualify actual DSR artifacts: distinct builders, truthful linkage, perturbation control and offline install
description:
## Why
Closed fa-eqk supplied .dsr/repos.yaml, install.sh, version reporting and scripts/check_reproducible_verify.sh. That is source availability, not G4 delivery. Current reproducibility script builds twice on the same host with direct rustc; its extra_cfg perturbation parameter is never exercised, --help is called proof that the binary executes, and no object/linkage check establishes static Linux linkage. Its rm -rf EXIT cleanup violates the local no-deletion contract, so this audit did not execute it. Plan 13.3/19 requires a released standalone verifier and golden proofs. No releases were established by this audit; README explicitly says none yet.

## Work and boundaries
Repair and test the release/reproducibility driver in place, routed through admitted RCH/DSR builders on the pinned toolchain; do not bypass canonical build controls or invent a second release service. Retain exact source/tree, complete flags, builder/target identities and artifacts from two genuinely distinct builder environments. Compare byte-identical outputs only within the stated target/toolchain/profile. A digest equality for two builds on one host is a narrower result, never a cross-worker claim. Execute a real controlled perturbation and require the comparator to reject it; source path remapping must not mask semantic differences. Preserve build artifacts and use owner-authorized cleanup only, without deletion traps.

Independently inspect the produced Linux binary's real linkage and platform metadata; std-only does not imply static. For Darwin/Windows state the actual runtime linkage/support instead of extending a Linux claim. Validate the DSR target matrix one target at a time, explicitly label unavailable targets UNRUN, and install a complete checksum-verified artifact set into a fresh destination through the repaired installer. Exercise fa/fad/fa-mcp version/discovery and fa-verify golden positive and tampered fixtures in the intended offline environment. Keep trust keys supplied independently from the proof. Publish checksums, build receipts, exact-tree PASS and supported-target/capability manifest together. An inactive SLO is not a measured pass: required performance criteria cannot be discharged by deactivating their rows. This bead prepares concrete release artifacts and evidence; it does not authorize an unreviewed public release.

## Acceptance and logging
```acceptance-tests
release_verify::distinct_builders_same_target_produce_identical_bytes
release_verify::controlled_build_perturbation_is_detected
release_verify::linkage_matches_the_target_claim
release_verify::fresh_offline_install_executes_all_required_goldens
```
Required future tests, not existing checker names. Real unit and end-to-end tests ship with the script repair. Log builder/target, resolved compiler, source closure, raw checksum/linkage results, installer exits and verifier predicates. Wrong builder identity, different source closure, omitted binary, tampered golden and absent manifest are negatives. Retain prior failed/unrun receipts. W10/G4 V36; depends on repaired installer, composed reader acceptance and the actual G4 domain results. Main publication and bead closure remain subject to exact-tree gates.

title: Evidence and memo full-text search via frankensearch Quill (native pure-Rust BM25, FSLX segments, delta-visible indexing) over Documents' derived text, entry descriptions and memos — pinned by git rev, default features only (no tantivy lane)
description:
WHY: investigators and agents need full-text search over evidence documents (derived text from fa-646), entry descriptions, memos and findings; the substrate's Beacon indexes cover structural lookups, not ranked text retrieval. The owner's frankensearch (/data/projects/frankensearch, last commit 2026-10-10) ships Quill (crates/frankensearch-quill v0.4.0): a native pure-Rust BM25 lexical engine with FSLX segments and delta-visible indexing, receipted at ~0.2 ms lexical search over 1K docs; tantivy remains only as an opt-in conformance oracle lane (features lexical-tantivy / tantivy-oracle) outside Quill's dependency graph, and frankensearch-fsfs's pdf-extract path is not needed. comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-23: WHAT (2)–(3) for documents and findings. Landed on main as 00c80016, f767cea0.

**`fa search <query> [--kind entry|document|finding|all]`** indexes all three kinds in one BM25 index under the default `--kind all`, rebuilt from the journal for each query. Their scores are comparable there.

**Documents:**
- Each document recorded at the frontier is read through the caller's capability. One the caller sees only redacted, may not read, or that is erased contributes nothing. The redacted-view governance this bead asked for is therefore the read path's own.
- A document that fails its own proof fails the search (exit 8). It never silently drops out.
- A derived document (`fa document extract`) is searched by its extracted text, and any other derivation never by its envelope. A plain document is searched by its own UTF-8 bytes.
- A PDF, image, audio or video document's raw bytes are never indexed: a text-layer PDF is ASCII and would decode. A PDF is found through its extraction.

**Findings:**
- Each finding of every run recorded at the frontier is indexed by its procedure and narrative.
- They are read through `finding_runs` and `read_findings_with_history`, the certified replays `fa finding runs|show` use, never a graph cache. A run that does not replay fails the search.
- Hits carry the finding's vid, for `fa finding show`.

**Interface:**
- `--kind` searches one kind only: just that kind is gathered and indexed, so `index_digest` names the index over the kinds searched. A finding-free search never replays a run. An unknown kind is usage (exit 2).
- The MCP `search` tool takes `kind`.
- `fa::Book::search` replaces `search_entries` and takes the caller's records.

**Found along the way, landed as ac266309:** derived text could escape its source's redaction contract through `extract --kind` (now FA-REF-083), and uploaded derivations had no `DERIVED_FROM` edges. Details are on fa-lzrn.

**Tests:**

title: Witnessed transparency checkpoints: WitnessPolicy quorum, `fa checkpoint witness` cosignatures, trust-anchor sets with rotation as journaled controls; fa-verify reports detection vs prevention
description:
## Why (plan §13.5; CPA workflow "the firm signs the checkpoint as a witness")
Staging's TransparencyCheckpoint is signed only by a key derived from the book's own key file: the book
holder can re-sign a rewritten history. Tamper evidence against the holder requires independent
witnesses (FA-INV-14.witnessed dormant).

## What to build
- WitnessPolicy control (quorum k of n external public keys), TrustAnchorSet with rotation
  (KeyRotation control, overlap windows).
- `fa checkpoint witness --checkpoint <oid> --key <witness key>`: produces a cosignature over the signed
  checkpoint body (CT cosignature style: "this root was observed at this time", never a statement about
  content); cosignatures journaled; fa-verify checks quorum against a supplied anchor set and reports
  `detection` (witnessed) vs `prevention` honestly.
- Consistency between witnessed checkpoints required (no fork without detection).

## Tests
Quorum met/unmet; rotated key; forked history detected by a witness's consistency check; golden vectors.
acceptance_criteria: Witnessed checkpoints verify offline with quorum; FA-INV-14.witnessed live.

comments.text:
2026-10-22 (claude-opus-5-5 / LavenderSwan): slice 1 (witnessed detection) LANDED on main and master (ae751134). Status stays open.

**What works** (plan §13.5, in the substrate's §5.8 detection vocabulary; never a prevention claim):
- **`fa checkpoint witness-key --out <new file>`**: a new Ed25519 witness key, a 64-hex seed in a 0600 file. No book is opened.
- **`fa checkpoint witness --key <file> [--state] [--previous <file>] [--onto <file>] --out <new file> --grant witness`**: cosigns the state's book-signed checkpoint, adding the witness's signature over the same body. No format change: the checkpoint already carries a sorted signature list.
  - With `--previous` (the cosigned file this key produced last, recognized by re-signing), the book must hold a consistency proof from that statement to the state. A rollback or a rewritten history has none and is refused: FA-REF-124, exit 8, nothing signed.
  - With `--onto`, the signature is added to another witness's cosigned file of the same state (its body must be exactly the book's), so one file carries a quorum.
  - The key file must be 0600 and the caller's (FA-REF-155).
  - Nothing is written to the book.
- **`fa-verify checkpoint <file> --key <book key> --witness <key>... [--quorum n]`**: adds a `witnesses` check, at least n of the named witnesses signed; claim witnessed_detection. A witness key equal to a --key is refused.
- **Host-only**: both commands are MCP exclusions and write-matrix HOST_ONLY rows (no launch template or token ceiling holds witness).

**Acceptance (the 2026-10-12 E2E):**
- [x] two witness key files; `fa checkpoint witness` from both; fa-verify quorum 2 passes; quorum 3 fails with a named predicate ("2 of the 3 named witnesses signed").
- [x] a forked checkpoint is detected: a second book with the same identity and signing key whose first posting differs is refused a cosignature over the history the witness signed (FA-REF-124). A rollback to an earlier state is refused the same way.
- [ ] WitnessPolicy (quorum k of n) and TrustAnchorSet with rotation as journaled controls.
- [ ] cosignatures journaled in the book.
- [ ] golden vectors for cosigned checkpoints.

**Invariant:** FA-INV-14.witnessed ("signed, witnessed transparency checkpoints detect rollback") stays dormant. The test above could be its checker, with the rewritten-history refusal as its negative, but whether this slice is enough to make it live is the owner's call. I am not changing the registry.

**Test:** fa-cli tests/proofs.rs witnesses_cosign_an_extending_history_and_refuse_a_rewritten_one; fa-notary checkpoint.rs a_witness_cosigns_the_same_body_as_a_new_object; fa-cli cli.rs every_declared_event_is_emitted_by_the_binary runs both commands.

title: Owner-line compile watch: every push to origin/main gets an rch keep-going clippy+test within the hour; a red result becomes a P0 repair bead with the exact compiler output, and a git note marks the commit RED
description:
## Why
The owner authors from an environment with no Rust toolchain ("cargo not installed") and pushes straight
to main: 50 of 57 commits since 2026-10-11 say UNRUN. b801003 broke the `fa` library build on 2026-10-13
18:48 and nobody noticed for ~21 hours while 20 commits stacked on it. The pre-push guard (fa-7dx) is the
end state but needs the owner's environment to change; a watch works today, with no change on the owner's
side, and shrinks "time to first compiler error" from days to minutes.

## What to build
1. `scripts/owner_watch.sh` (+ a systemd user timer or `fad`-independent loop documented in AGENTS.md):
   polls `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` every 5 minutes; for each new tip T not yet noted:
   a. checks T out into ONE permanent warm worktree (`/data/projects/franken_accounting-watch`, reused, so
      the rch pool stays warm — see fa-aj8);
   b. runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings` then `cargo test --workspace
      --no-fail-fast` through rch with `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1`, classifying PASS/FAIL/UNRUN with
      scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh (an rch refusal is UNRUN, never FAIL);
   c. writes a git note on T under `refs/notes/owner-watch` ({tree, verdict, steps, first error lines,
      worker, build ids, test totals}) and pushes the notes ref;
   d. on FAIL: creates (or updates, if one is open for the same first-error signature) a P0 bead
      "main red at <T>: <first error>" with the de-ANSI'd error block, the introducing commit found by
      `git log -L`/bisect over the new commits, and the staging-line fix if one exists
      (`git log -S'<snippet>' origin/staging`).
2. A one-line status in `fa doctor`/triage tooling for agents: "main@T: GREEN|RED|UNRUN since <time>".
2b. Tracker drift report in the same note: commits in the new range that cite no bead id (92 of 133 owner
   commits cite none today) and commits whose subject names a bead that is closed or assigned to another
   agent; appended as a comment to fa-ul9 so tracker truth is maintained continuously, not per reality check.
3. Never edits code, never pushes to main/staging, never resets anything; it only reads, builds, notes and
   files beads.

## Acceptance
- Planted: push a commit with a deliberate compile error to a scratch branch configured as the watched
  ref in a test mode; within one cycle a RED note and a bead exist with the exact error and the commit.
- A green commit produces a GREEN note with test totals; an rch refusal produces UNRUN and no bead.
- Runs for 24 h on the real main with a log showing every tip evaluated.

## Tests & logging
A self-test mode with a temp bare repo and stub rch (exit codes 0/101/103) covering GREEN/RED/UNRUN; every
cycle logs `=== <ts> tip=<sha> step=<s> verdict=<v> rc=<n> worker=<w>` to an append-only log.
close_reason: Implemented scripts/owner_watch.sh (--once, --loop, --status, --self-test) with warm watch worktree, rch clippy/test classification, refs/notes/owner-watch git notes, tracker drift report, and automatic P0 repair bead creation on RED; verified via scripts/tests/owner_watch_selftest.sh and shellcheck -S warning

title: Aggregate basis guard per plan §5.10: per-intent dependency_class, head-equality guard for fold-derived mutations, and the pinned-foundation conformance test that nothing publishes between comparison and marker
description:
## WHY
Plan §5.10: mutating plans whose effect amounts depend on a fold not covered by point witnesses must record the target
prefix and require `current_head == aggregate_basis_seq` immediately before publication; "Its atomicity is
source-supported but UNRUN: a pinned-foundation conformance test must establish that no internal path publishes between
comparison and the marker"; the intent registry carries a per-intent `dependency_class`. At 0d338c0 head equality is
applied case by case (fa-journal migration.rs:1337; plan.rs:574-593); there is no dependency_class column and no
conformance test. Fold-derived mutations (revaluation, close tasks, allocations over balances, migration Finalize
visibility) are exactly where a silent race would change an amount.

## WHAT
`dependency_class ∈ {point, aggregate}` per intent kind in the intent/verb registry; every aggregate-class plan records
its basis and the kernel enforces head equality under the exclusive &mut Database before publication, refusing
PlanInvalidated otherwise; fa-conformance substrate test proves no publication can interleave between the comparison and
the marker (both orders, plus a planted variant that drops the guard); fa-revaluation and closing paths migrated to the
shared guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: revaluation planned at seq s commits only if head is still s.
- [ ] planted negatives: a post committed between plan and commit of a revaluation yields PlanInvalidated; the guard
  removed in a planted variant lets the conformance test observe the race.

```acceptance-tests
fa-conformance::substrate::aggregate_guard_no_publication_between_compare_and_marker
fa-journal::plan::aggregate_plan_invalidated_by_intervening_post
fa-registry::tests::every_intent_has_dependency_class
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: guard helper. E2E: real-binary `fa fx revalue --dry-run --plan-out`, an intervening `fa post`, then `fa commit
--plan` refuses with exit 6 naming both sequences. Logging: refusals log basis seq, head seq and the intervening entry.

title: foundation_dependencies.toml: add an `unconsumed` state so upstream-live capabilities FrankenAccounting does not call (R-CERT, R-PRISM, most of R-API) are not reported `fa_status = "live" (consumed as-is)`

WHY (verified at e606b46): the legend defines `fa_status = live (consumed as-is) | interim` (registries/foundation_dependencies.toml:1-17), so every capability not on an interim posture is "live".
