description:
WHY: plan §15.3 has `fa` auto-route to `fad`, the daemon that owns the writer lease; §14.2 makes authority current-policy-at-commit. At e606b46 fad's `Server::handle` passes the client's raw argv into `cli::run` (crates/fad/src/lib.rs:194-216), so whatever `--as`/`--grant` the client typed becomes the capability; the Unix socket at `<dir>/fad.sock` is bound with no peer-credential check (crates/fad/src/main.rs:161-163). Anyone who can connect to the socket acts as any principal with any op. The `fa capabilities` text claims the opposite (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:1225).

WHAT:
1. Session handshake on connect: the client sends `{token_commitment, proof}` (from `--token <file>` or `FA_TOKEN`); fad checks SO_PEERCRED uid against the book directory owner policy (registry row: `daemon.allowed_uids = owner|group|list`), verifies the token against the journaled issuance (fa-v62) and binds `(principal, commitment)` for the connection's lifetime; every request on the connection runs under it. Revocation/expiry are re-checked at each commit (kernel witness), and at stream re-admission for long reads (§14.2 "Streams explicitly choose … re-admission").
2. On the daemon path `--as` and `--grant` are refused (exit 7, FA-REF code with fix "present a token: fa cap issue … then --token <file>"), never silently ignored.
3. Embedded posture (no daemon): `--as/--grant` remain for the book-key holder only, through fa-v62's explicit OwnerPosture; the robot envelope gains `authority: {posture: embedded-owner|session, principal, commitment|null}` on every event so no consumer mistakes a self-asserted identity for an authenticated one (robot-schema pin bump, additive-minor).
4. fa-mcp hosted by fad (fa-z5u) inherits this binding: an MCP session is a fad session with the server's launch token.
5. `fa doctor` (fa-12x) reports the posture and warns when an embedded-owner process writes to a book a daemon serves.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] positive: two clients of one fad with different tokens are attributed to different principals in the journal (PREPARED_BY / principal_ref), and SoD refuses the second only when it is the same principal;
[ ] planted negatives: a client presenting no token → refused at handshake; a client whose uid is not allowed → refused; a valid token for another book → refused; `--as` on the daemon path → refused exit 7; a token revoked mid-session → the next commit refuses FA-REF-023;
[ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core/current-policy) + lab test over the fad connection loop (crates/fad/src/lab_tests.rs pattern) with chaos;
[ ] consumers: fa-ohe, fa-z5u, every fad user;
[ ] no-claim boundary: Unix peer credentials authenticate a local uid, not a human; human-ness of approvals is a profile/key-custody property (fa-kae).

TESTS: crates/fad/tests/fad.rs (binary, real socket) for each case with frames logged; lab_tests for handshake under chaos; fa-cli tests for `--token`.
close_reason: fad authenticates token-bound CLI sessions (--token <file> and FA_TOKEN), binds each connection's session token for its lifetime, checks admit_current at the daemon boundary (FA-REF-156/023/014/011), refuses unauthenticated --as on the daemon path with FA-REF-011, and proves multi-holder attribution, SoD, and chaos session-binding

title: Explanation verbs: `fa explain entry|evidence|refusal|period|register` with robot events and MCP tools (evidence closure with supplements and sequences; refusal id → catalog row, law, fix)
description:

Only `fa explain balance` exists. Agents and auditors need: what is this entry (legs, class, origin,
lineage, approvals, evidence heads, plan certificate); what is its evidence closure (documents,
supplements, attestations, rate documents, with their recorded sequences — the auditor workflow's
`fa explain evidence E…`); what does refusal FA-REF-xxx mean (catalog row, law/policy row, exit code,
fix, alternatives — `fa explain refusal`); a period's state history; a register cell's fold proof.

## What to build
Five subcommands, each a verbs.toml row with a robot event shape, MCP tool, human table; read-only;
authorization before observation (fa-0x0 when it lands; today the session capability's read op);
evidence closure walk bounded and certified on request (`--certify`).

## Tests
CLI tests for each with planted data; schema pin; parity gate; `explain refusal` covers every
catalog row (generated test).
acceptance_criteria: Five verbs on CLI and MCP with tests; every catalog id explainable.

title: Prepare the four planned technical reports with source-bound evidence and explicit non-claims
description:
## Scope from the existing vision
Plan 16.10 explicitly targets four papers/tech reports: Palimpsest Ledger, Balance = Fold, Tracing as code, and Agent-operated books. Plan G4 requires published papers to match proven scope. No dedicated open publication acceptance owner was found in the 314-issue audit; a comment in the DSR recipe is not an executable completion condition. This is existing plan scope, not new product work.

## Work
Maintain one authoritative document per report using existing repository locations where available; do not create versioned duplicate plans. Explain the precise implemented semantics, reference/independent verification method, artifact/source cuts, exact bounds, external-oracle divergences, tested trust assumptions, measured costs and known failures. Cite the released artifact manifest and work-witness ledger per substantive claim. Distinguish theorem/model/fixture/statistical/benchmark classes. Detection via witnessed roots is not prevention or accounting truth, the solvency screen is not fair value, and current runtime evidence cannot be inferred from older source.

Do not withhold useful negative findings; place them beside supported claims. Drafting a paper does not close a missing capability. A release-required claim needs its domain evidence before publication; narrower research drafts remain plainly labeled. Public submission or external messaging requires the user's applicable authorization.

## Acceptance
All four drafts exist, every load-bearing claim resolves to machine-produced evidence for its stated cut/class or is explicitly unresolved, and an independent review catches an intentionally stale artifact and overstrong claim. Cross-reference actual release hashes and no-claim boundaries. Include validation in the existing claims-lint/evidence framework, not a parallel certificate bureaucracy.
```acceptance-tests
publication_claims::all_four_planned_reports_have_traceable_scope
publication_claims::stale_artifact_or_stronger_claim_is_refused
```
Future checks. W10/G4; no legal compliance/admissibility or universal performance claim is inferred.

The audit found: FA-INV-16.core live on a smoke checker (crates/fa-journal/tests/genesis.rs:545 checks only the side mirror and that some Decimal exists — fa-avx builds the real one); FA-INV-05.external-retained live with no implementing code (retention floors / ByReferenceOnly absent); FA-INV-04.outsider-recomputation live while fa-verify's balance proof has no migration predicate (crates/fa-verify/src/balance.rs:60; tracked by fa-e00); FA-INV-04.core's checker `fold_digest_is_a_function_of_cells_and_watermark` (crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:1046) tests the deviation from §5.3 (fa-i39); FA-INV-01.leaf-only's registered statement drops "effective at the entry's date" (invariants.toml:146; AccountRow has no effectivity dates). invariants_check.sh proves that named tests ran and passed (and says itself this is not sufficiency, lines 27-28); heavy reuse (one generated-history test backs 5 clauses). Live-on-weak-evidence is the "proof-class inflation" pattern the suite forbids.

WHAT: (1) schema: `checker_strength` per clause and `statement_matches_plan = true|false (reason)`; fa-registry enforces: live ⇒ strength ≥ unit and a planted negative that reaches only that clause; (2) demote the over-claimed clauses now (one commit, each with its reason and activating bead), re-promote as fa-avx/fa-i39/fa-e00/retention land; (3) restore the plan's leaf-only statement and mark the effectivity part dormant until account effectivity exists; (4) invariants_check.sh reports per-clause strength in its transcript; (5) the summary line printed by check.sh shows live/dormant counts by strength so the number is not mistaken for coverage; (6) negative-discrimination probe: registries/mutations/<clause>.patch holds, per live clause, a minimal source mutation that disables exactly that clause's check; `scripts/mutation_probe.sh` (run on a free worker, not every landing) applies each patch in a scratch clone and asserts that exactly that clause's registered negative test fails and no other clause's does — this turns "each planted negative reaches exactly one check" (the swarm's own M6 lesson) from a review convention into a measured property, and its report is attached to the verdict manifest (fa-u7u).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: registry validates; transcript lists strengths; [ ] planted negatives: a live clause with strength smoke fails fa-registry; a live clause whose negative is shared with another clause fails; [ ] proof class: registry gate; [ ] consumers: G1 (the Genesis clause set), every reviewer; [ ] no-claim boundary: strength labels describe the checker, not correctness.

TESTS: fa-registry tests with planted registry rows; invariants_check.sh shell tests.
close_reason: Enforced checker_strength honesty on invariants.toml: added checker_strength to all 45 live clauses, refused smoke checker_strength on live clauses, split sub-clauses (FA-INV-01.account-effective, FA-INV-05.by-reference-downgrade) so live clauses never over-claim dormant predicates, and enforced disjoint negative tests across all live clauses in fa-registry and scripts/invariants_check.sh.

Fix the tag (with a codec-compat note: tag 8 documents already written are Remittance-labelled; add a migration note in

title: Register maintainer must apply the migration visibility predicate exactly as the literal fold does (staged/abandoned runs and pre-opening FullDetail detail are invisible)
description:

For an Open or Abandoned MigrationRun, or FullDetail detail dated before the opening date (plan §8.6, FA-INV-07 migration-disjoint), `Book::advance_registers` publishes cells that include invisible entries, which `verify_period` then reports as drift (exit 8) — a false corruption signal, and a true divergence between maintained and literal folds. Visibility also CHANGES without a new posting to the cell: a Finalize control record makes a whole run visible at once, so the maintainer must treat Finalize/Abandon controls as cell-affecting deltas. No test exercises the maintainer on a Historical or Opening period while a run is open, finalized later, or abandoned. fa-vn4 (WhiteCreek) is landing maintainer changes now (candidate be73b36); coordinate the fix into that series or immediately after it.

WHAT: maintainer folds only entries visible at the delta's commit_seq under the same predicate; a MigrationControl Finalize in the delta re-folds the run's entries into their cells (bounded by the run's chunk manifest, never a full scan); Abandon is a no-op for cells; the metamorphic "rebuild = maintained" test gains migration histories (open → chunks → finalize; open → chunks → abandon; FullDetail with pre-opening detail).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: maintained cells equal the literal fold at every step of the three histories; [ ] planted negatives: removing the predicate (mutation) makes exactly the new test fail; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04.maintainer, FA-INV-07.migration-disjoint) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-vn4, fa-715, fa-e00; [ ] no-claim boundary: maintainer correctness for native period cells; other register families follow fa-715.

title: Drafts and promotion (A6, doctrine 10 interim posture): intent-log drafts, Agent-profile work lands on a draft, authorized promotion replays to trunk
description:
Background: plan bet A6 says agents work on drafts that cannot touch trunk without authorized promotion; doctrine 10 names the interim posture while substrate branches are not live: intent-log drafts (a DraftSet lifecycle object whose body is the ordered list of intents/proposals, journaled; nothing in it is a trunk entry). fa-llx (MistyPlateau, 2026-10-10) ships the Agent-profile trunk refusal FA-REF-013 whose fix text must cite this bead because the draft path does not exist yet.

Scope: (1) DraftSet lifecycle object (Appendix A): immutable body = book, branch-or-interim marker, owner principal, ordered intents with their dry-run plan certificates and proposal_digests; status projection by LifecycleTransition control entries (Open -> Submitted -> Promoted|Rejected|Abandoned). (2) fa draft new|add|show|submit|promote|abandon with --json and robot envelope events; Agent-profile capabilities may create/add/submit, never promote. (3) Promotion = an authorized Human/System principal replays every intent against trunk inside the normal posting kernel (period law, admissibility, SoD, evidence minimum all re-evaluated at promotion time); any intent whose proposal_digest differs from the draft's recorded digest (because trunk moved: period closed, chart changed, policy epoch changed) is refused with a typed refusal naming the drift, never silently re-approved (FA-INV-10 approval-binds-proposal). (4) Metamorphic test: draft promotion == trunk post (same entries, same digests, same register cells) for model-generated histories; property: a rejected/abandoned draft leaves trunk byte-identical. (5) Oracle: fa-reference models a draft as a list of intents replayed through its own post; differential with planted negatives: Agent promoting (refused), promotion after period close (refused per matrix), drift in proposal_digest (refused), valid promotion (admitted). (6) Switch-over rule registered: when substrate branches land, DraftSet body gains a branch id and promotion becomes a branch merge; the intent-log remains the lineage.

No-claim boundary: green proves promotion re-runs the kernel and refuses drift; it does not prove agents cannot post to trunk through some other surface (that is fa-llx's FA-REF-013 and its tests).

title: Specify public evidence commitments and scope-completeness proofs
description:
References: §§9.1/9.6, 11.11, 13.1-13.3, 15.6, Appendix A/F (lines 560, 580, 704, 745-755, 917, 1188-1194, 1217-1223, 1341).
The MMR is ordered by commit, whereas bundle scopes filter by effective period/account subtree, and retroactive entries make matching records noncontiguous. Inclusion proofs prove supplied leaves belong; they do not prove all matching leaves were supplied. Appendix A contains inclusion_paths but no range/selection-completeness proof, while the CPA workflow says fa-verify confirms a complete FY extract. A producer can omit one matching entry and all retained membership proofs still verify.
Define a sound supported proof mode (e.g. verify the full relevant prefix and selection or an authenticated predicate index bound to the same checkpoint), exact scope/known-at/auth intersection, missing-entry negative vectors, and accurate costs. Do not label membership_only as complete.
Document Oid uses the substrate's keyed identity (fgdb-crypto/src/lib.rs:80-97). A verifier with only public bundle/root cannot recompute it without K_oid. ImportReceipt.digest_at_receipt could provide a public binding, but its algorithm/domain and authenticated binding to Document Oid, kind, bytes and length are not specified. Require an explicit public body commitment chain without disclosing the storage key.
Whole-document hash alone also cannot verify arbitrary disclosed byte ranges against the original redacted document. Define chunk commitments or weaken the redaction proof scope honestly. Specify signature schemes, public trust anchors, key rotation and signed transcript; the std-only verifier budget must cover these implementations.
RFC scope reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html . W4/W9, G0/G1.
The canonical Entry deliberately excludes its creating MarkerRef/recorded time. An MMR leaf of only Entry bytes plus a checkpoint's aggregate commit_seq does not authenticate the per-entry commit sequence/HLC, especially when one commit has many leaves. Specify a domain-separated leaf envelope binding record kind, book/branch, creating marker/sequence, and within-commit ordinal, with canonical ordering and a proof of the sequence-to-prefix boundary used by historical selection.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §13.2 LeafEnvelope binding kind/coordinate/commit_seq/within-commit ordinal/selection fields; ScopeIndexComplete mode with scope_index_root in every checkpoint and boundary-neighbor proofs (missing-entry negative vectors); §9.1 public doc_commit over a 4 KiB chunk tree (substrate ObjectId is a locator only), redaction at chunk granularity labeled honestly; Ed25519 + TrustAnchorSet + KeyRotation in the std-only verifier budget; §13.1 completeness_scope labels; Appendix A LeafEnvelope/ScopeIndex/TransparencyCheckpoint/Bundle; FA-INV-14 clauses. Left open for re-review.
close_reason: Promoted FA-INV-03.witness-race, FA-INV-07.book-scoped, and FA-INV-16.recovery-rebuild to live (57/79 live clauses), reassigned remaining dormant clauses to their concrete implementation beads, and verified all round-1 G0 plan repairs and executable checks pass in CI

title: Remove approval and certificate hash cycles before freezing durable schemas
description:
References: §4.2/4.6, §10.1/10.4, Appendix A (plan lines 294-305, 333, 592, 645, 1128-1172, 1200-1223).
Entry BodyDigest excludes only entry_digest and includes approvals. ApprovalRef itself contains approved_digest. §4.6 requires that digest to equal the committed object's digest. Consequently d = H(entry containing approval.approved_digest = d), a cryptographic fixed point rather than a constructible approval flow. RestatementCase similarly embeds approvals and mutable lifecycle status. Attestation and checkpoint signature transcripts also lack explicit exclusions of the signatures and signed-digest fields.
Certificate/output references have a related missing contract: Finding contains certificate_oid and the certificate contains output_digest of the result; bundles contain report certificates; Origin::Intent contains plan_certificate_oid. Without a distinct semantic output body, hashing can become cyclic or depend on runtime IDs/approvals and make Canon's byte-for-byte replay claim impossible.
Required repair: an explicit acyclic identity/transcript graph separating immutable proposal digest, approvals/signatures, committed envelope digest, and certified semantic output. Bind approvals to complete effects, book, target coordinate and policy epoch; require reapproval if promotion replays materially different effects. Enumerate ordered construction and digest tags for every signed/certified type. Negative acceptance: change one leg after approval must fail, while adding the first valid approval must be constructible without finding a hash fixed point. W1/W3/W4, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.6 acyclic identity graph (EntryProposal -> proposal_digest -> plan certificate -> Approvals binding proposal_digest+effects_digest+coordinate+policy epoch -> envelope entry_digest); Appendix A Entry/Approval/Attestation/Checkpoint transcripts exclude signatures/self-digests; normative construction order added; RestatementCase split into immutable body + projection with Approval objects; negative acceptance stated (leg change after approval => digest mismatch refusal; first approval needs no fixed point). Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: code consequences landed in fa-model/fa-journal: (1) plan_certificate_oid moved out of the proposal into the envelope (entry_digest = H(domain ‖ proposal_digest ‖ opt(plan_cert) ‖ approvals)); test envelope_fields_change_the_entry_digest_but_not_the_proposal_digest. (2) Idempotency: same key + different content refuses FA-REF-032 exit 6 on both the retry and race-recovery paths (RubyMoose 2739 / WhiteCreek 2730); tests identical_retry_is_recorded_and_a_changed_retry_is_a_conflict + CLI test. (3) Erasable sealing is deterministic under the key (salt/nonce KDF-derived) so identical retries compare equal; WhiteCreek carries the Appendix A row in their patch. (4) fa:entry:v1 is positional schema 1.0: the first additive field needs a minor bump + length-delimited extension block (WhiteCreek 2734) — not yet implemented; lands with the first schema patch that needs it.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: schema-review.patch (RubyMoose/WhiteCreek) APPLIED to the plan text; code parity, row by row — NOT YET ADMITTED by fa:entry:v1 as encoded: effective_date: Option<DateDay> (code: DateDay on every entry incl. controls); Disposition::Posts { source_ordinals } (code: posted_legs); settles.target_leg: EntryTarget (code: EntryRef); ControlPayload::ReservationRelease (absent); ProposalRef/EffectManifest/IntentOutcome objects (absent; no vid(IntentOutcome) yet, refusals are not durable); Certificate resolved_sequence/resolution_frontier/instant_resolution and DocumentStub proof grammar (no certificate/document code yet). ADMITTED: FA-INV-09 semantic-request equivalence (EntryPayload::semantic_digest, FA-REF-032/033). Each row lands with its slice via the minor-version + extension-block mechanism (msg 2734); the live codec is positional schema 1.0.

title: Bind commit authorization and audit delivery to explicit current policy
description:
References: §§5.1/5.10, 9.7, 14.2-14.4, Appendix A/G/H (lines 375-386, 435, 584, 779-787, 1224-1225, 1365-1375, 1399).
Plan has initial admission and commit-time SoD but no explicit current-policy witness for revocation/expiry between dry run and commit, or for reads pinned before revocation. known_at should select accounting history without resurrecting revoked access. Define security epoch, current authority evaluation, approval authority expiry/revocation policy and fail-closed boundaries.
daily_total and per-entry amount ceilings require a precise measure (gross debit, credit, absolute per-leg, per-unit), day/time-zone source, shared principal/token scope and serializable budget debit. Net of balanced entries is always zero. Attenuation/issuance must not reset a principal ceiling. No operation-cost row prices those stateful checks.
Every external-profile read must be completely logged, but Appendix G declares balance/report/bundle reads 0 writes. Define durable access recording before protected bytes escape, stream/cancellation/failure semantics, daemon authority for read-only callers, and avoidance of recursive log reads. Price the real transaction/barrier or name a distinct admitted audit path.
Account-subtree/dimension caveats and full immutable Entry payloads conflict when one entry crosses an authorized and unauthorized account: define whole-entry admission, redacted/partial-view representation and proof scope, or refuse before fetching; do not return the full other-account leg or silently describe a partial fold as whole-book.
Acceptance: revoke after plan, historical read using revoked token, two simultaneous daily-budget posts, token attenuation, crash before/after first protected output byte, and split-scope balanced entry. W2/Steward/W5, G0/G1.
The ordering of ADMIT→RESOLVE→CANON also needs explicit post-evaluation authorization: a typed event does not yet have its generated accounts/dimensions/amounts at step 1. Safely admit explicit inputs, run under restricted capabilities, then validate every generated effect and current caveat before commit. Initial authorization of the verb alone is insufficient.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.1 step 5 post-evaluation authorization of rule-generated legs; §14.2 closed ops vocabulary, current-policy witness at commit (PlanInvalidated{CapabilityRevoked}), historical selectors never resurrect authority, ceiling measure (per-leg mantissa; daily gross debits per root issuance; day from TimeEvidence) via a UsageCell, whole-entry visibility with partial_view; §9.7 AccessEvent committed before the first protected byte and priced as an Appendix G row; FA-INV-10 clauses. Left open for re-review.

title: Report certificates bind raw registry text: a comment-only registry edit changes every certificate digest and makes every retained certificate refuse replay (FA-INV-11)
description:
## Why
Report certificates commit to the registries they were computed under (`registry_digest`, crates/fa/src/certificate.rs ~391-431), but they hash each registry's RAW TEXT, comments included.

Observed on 2026-10-16:
- Two edits moved the cross-target trial-balance certificate pin:
  - a comment-only rewrite of registries/account_types.toml (6893ac3d, fa-a57x);
  - an additive symbols.toml row (1ecc2507, fa-yyl3).
- b1a4f34d's account_types/units changes moved it again.

The same mechanism has two consequences:
1. **Every retained certificate refuses replay** after any registry edit, comment typos included. certificate.rs ~987 compares the registry digest. That breaks FA-INV-11 ("`fa replay <certificate>` ⇒ byte-identical re-execution") for every book whose binary is upgraded, even when no accounting rule changed.
2. **Pins churn on cosmetic edits.** Every cross-target and golden pin over certificates moves on cosmetic edits, which trains everyone to regenerate goldens reflexively (a named reward-hacking pattern).

## What to build
1. Commit to the **parsed, canonical registry content** each report depends on, not file bytes. Use a versioned canonical encoding per registry, with comments and whitespace excluded. Tag it with the registry `schema_version` so a semantic change still changes the digest.
2. A certificate binds only the registries its computation reads, by name plus canonical digest. Today all hashed registries are bound.
3. Replay of a certificate produced under an older registry digest:
   - If the binary still carries a registry whose canonical digest equals the recorded one, replay proceeds.
   - Otherwise it is a typed refusal naming the registry and both digests, never an opaque mismatch.
4. Migration note for already-retained certificates: they bind raw-text digests. Keep a v-tagged verifier for them, or document the one-time break. Do not silently reinterpret.

## Acceptance
- Planted: a comment-only edit to account_types.toml leaves the TB/BS/IS certificate digests and replay unchanged.
- Planted: changing an account type's normal side changes the digest, and replay is refused with the typed refusal.
- Cross-target pins re-measured once under the new encoding, with the commit naming why.
- FA-INV-11 clause updated with these negatives.
close_reason: Narrowed ReportCertificate bound registry closure to the registries each report's computation reads (account_types, entry_classes, units, foundations; plus reason_codes for ExplainBalance only), preserved replay compatibility for both v1 raw-text and pre-narrowing v2 canonical closures, re-measured cross_target_determinism TB/BS/IS certificate pins once, and registered FA-INV-11.core checkers/negatives.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Landed on main at 923e929d (2026-10-18, claude-opus-5-5) in commit f704b85e (fix(certificates)). Gates: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` exit 0 at 923e929d (2157 passed, 0 failed, 168 test binaries; vmi1149989, 2026-10-18T16:37Z); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0 at fda5f40f (vmi1153651, 0 warnings), and on the crates changed since (fa, fa-cli, fa-registry) exit 0 (hz2, 0 warnings) at 923e929d.

**What works:**
- **Canonical encoding:** fa-registry Document::canonical_bytes (fa:registry-document:v1) is an injective encoding of the parsed content. Comments, blank lines, spacing, key order and integer separators do not reach it; every key, value, table name and array row (in order) does, schema_version included.
- **v2 closures:** report and procedure certificates bind a v2 closure over each bound registry's canonical digest.
- **Comment edits:** a comment-only or layout-only edit to account_types.toml leaves the closure unchanged, as do the TB/BS/IS certificates and their replay (planted test). A flipped normal side moves the closure.
- **Retained certificates:** a certificate retained before this change carries the v1 raw-text closure, and replay still accepts it (tested for the trial balance and open items), so nothing retained breaks. New certificates never carry v1.
- **Typed refusal:** a closure this executable does not carry is FA-REF-159 CERTIFICATE_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE (exit environment). It names the recorded closure, this executable's closure and the registries it covers, instead of the old opaque FA-REF-150 text.
- **Pins:** the cross-target pins were re-measured once (tb/bs/is certificates only; the fold, statement bytes and bundle are unchanged). They no longer move on cosmetic edits.

**Not done (the bead stays open):**
- Naming the one registry that differs: the certificate holds a single closure digest, so this needs per-registry digests in the format. That belongs with fa-oimc's unified certificate contract.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## 2026-10-20 (StormyLion, claude-opus-5-5): design findings, read-only at origin/main de229bf3. Not started; still open

These are the five decisions that make this bead multi-day:

1. **A book's unit table is sealed at genesis.**
   - genesis journals the binary registry's units as Unit vertices.
   - It pins `Book.unit_table_digest` on the root.
   - `fa_journal::genesis::read_units` refuses any journaled unit that the binary registry (units.toml) lacks.
   - A version added later therefore needs a second source, verified by its own control rather than by the root digest. That control is `SchemaChange` kind 14 (kinds 1-13 are taken: chart 1-4, REA 5-11, closing routes 12, period births 13).
   - `fa/src/certificate.rs` compares the root digest with `unit_table_digest(&book.units)`, so certificates must bind the genesis table plus the version controls, not a recomputed whole table.

2. **The successor must not enter units.toml.**
   - Adding `USD@v1` there would put it in every new book's genesis table.
   - Unversioned parsing ("1.23 USD") resolves to the highest registered version (fa-money `rendering_preserves_historical_unit_versions`), so every fixture would silently switch scale.
   - The version is therefore book-local: the next dense UnitId after the book's table.

3. **Parsing becomes date-dependent.**
   - "USD" must mean the version in force at the entry's effective date.
   - Every intent and typed-document parser needs the date: fa-cli intents, typed verbs, allocation, bank and migration imports, and MCP.
   - Otherwise backdated entries must spell `USD@v0`.

4. **Account unit policy.**
   - `UnitPolicy::Single(UnitId)` pins one version.
   - Either the redenomination control re-points accounts, or policies match by code.
   - Pick one before the kernel check "posting into a superseded version after the successor's date is refused, naming the successor".

5. **Cross-version folds.**
   - TB, statements and certificates must convert old-version cells by the ×10^k law at read time and name the law.
   - Report rows are keyed by `unit_id` today.

Suggested first slice: items 1 and 4, plus `fa unit list`, plus the posting refusal. Leave parsing (item 3) and folds (item 5) to later slices.

title: Docket slice 2: custody chains, ImportRun control records with receipt hashes, external document storage behind public commitments with verified reads, redaction contracts as derived objects, retention holds blocking erasure and expiry
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Docket's first slice (fa-lp6) delivers content-addressed documents, chunk-Merkle commitments, evidence minimums and `EVIDENCED_BY`; fa-journal/src/evidence.rs lists custody, import receipts, bank lines, external storage and redaction as "later slices". Plan §9 and W4 require them before Gate G2 ("documents, custody, attestations, balance assertions"). fa-v74 (subject keys) and fa-646 (intake pipeline) touch adjacent ground; fa-j9t is the spec-side contract bead. This bead is the code.

WHAT:
1. Custody chain: every document carries an immutable `Custody` lineage (received-from principal/system, received-at CommitSeq, transfer events as journaled objects), queryable as `fa document custody <oid>`; a document cannot be cited by an entry unless its custody chain is complete to a registered intake source.
2. Import receipts: `ImportRun` as a control record (legs = []) with the source descriptor, byte count, document count, the Merkle root over the imported documents' oids, and a receipt hash the external party can keep; `fa import receipt <run>`; receipts are what fa-ff6 and fa-646 must produce.
3. External document storage: documents above the inline threshold store bytes outside the journal under a registered store descriptor with the public commitment (chunk-tree root) inline; reads verify the commitment on every access; a missing external blob is a typed refusal (exit 5, foundation/I-O) and never a silent null; the plan's "public commitments" let a bundle prove a document without shipping it.
4. Redaction contracts: `redaction = <contract>` capability caveat; a redacted view of a document is a derived object with its own commitment and lineage to the original; redaction never changes an amount or an entry (erasure-leaves-amounts-intact oracle); subject-key erasure (fa-v74) composes with this.
5. Retention holds: `RetentionHold` control records that block erasure cuts and expiry sweeps for the held subjects; releases are journaled.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an import run of N documents produces a receipt whose root recomputes from the oids; an external document reads back byte-identically with the commitment verified; a redacted view omits the field and keeps the entry's amounts; a hold blocks an erasure cut with a refusal naming the hold; [ ] planted negatives: a tampered external blob is refused on read (exit 8); a document without custody cannot be cited (refusal names the missing link); an erasure cut under a hold is refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (commitments, lineage) + differential (fa-reference naive custody/receipt model); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, fa-646, fa-v74, bundles (A3), G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: receipts prove what was imported, not that the source was truthful.

title: Accumulator maintained in commit order off the write path: an MMR advanced by fad from delta_since (O(log n) append, RFC 9162-style O(log n) inclusion/consistency proofs) replacing whole-prefix rescans
description:
## Why (plan §13.2)
Today `checkpoint` (fa-notary state.rs ~308) and every proof re-read the whole prefix with
`db.vertices_at(seq)` and rebuild the tree; `verify_accumulator` rebuilds every state on the chain
(O(states x vertices)). Plan: a journal-level accumulator maintained in commit order, off the write path.

## What to build
- Merkle Mountain Range over entry leaves in commit order: peaks persisted as AccumulatorState control
  records at each checkpoint; fad advances it from delta_since after commits (supervised, cancellable);
  append O(log n).
- Inclusion proofs (leaf → peak → bagged root) and consistency proofs between checkpoints of O(log n)
  size; fa-verify verifies them with its own BLAKE3; golden vectors.
- Equivalence campaign: MMR roots/proofs vs the current rebuild implementation over generated histories
  (existing proofs must remain verifiable or carry a format version bump with both verifiers).

## Tests
Golden vectors; equivalence campaign >= 8 seeds; checkpoint cost scaling test (log-shaped).
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint and proof generation no longer rescan the prefix; formats pinned; campaign green.

title: Bind every verdict to an exact tree: per-step verdict manifests keyed by tree hash (a split run is one verdict iff every step PASSed on that tree), scripts/local_proof.sh + merge_train.sh + br_sync.sh adopted from the substrate, verdicts as git notes; bead closes cite a manifest id
description:
WHY: AGENTS.md "A green scripts/check.sh in a dirty tree is not a verdict"; local_proof.sh "runs scripts/check.sh against the exact committed tree, refuses a dirty worktree, and writes a manifest binding the verdict to that commit and tree hash"; merge_train.sh is "the only path from staging to main". At e606b46 none of local_proof.sh, merge_train.sh, br_sync.sh, check-forbidden-deps.sh exist, there are no git notes refs, and the last literal single check.sh exit 0 is a7203b82 (2026-10-10 22:24), 45 commits before the tip; the tip has clippy + tests on an equivalent tree but no check.sh run. Because rch's daemon queue cap (300 s) and 1800/3600/7200 s kill limits routinely leave steps UNRUN, the swarm has closed beads on stitched runs (a full run with 13 PASS / 2 UNRUN plus a separate `--quick` run at the same tree, e.g. 3a4349f; commit 5de0c4b itself notes "their concatenation is not a new all-fifteen-step verdict"). The doctrine is right; the tooling to satisfy it honestly under a saturated fleet is missing, which is what pushes people into stitching.

WHAT (the ambitious, honest fix): (1) check.sh writes a per-step verdict record `{step, status PASS|FAIL|UNRUN, tree_hash, toolchain, worker, started, finished, log_digest}` to a manifest; (2) `scripts/local_proof.sh <commit>` refuses a dirty tree, runs only the steps not already PASSed for that exact tree hash and toolchain, and emits a final verdict manifest iff every registered step has a PASS record for that tree — so a split run IS one verdict by construction, with no human stitching; any FAIL for that tree invalidates the manifest; (3) manifests stored as git notes under refs/notes/fa-verdict keyed by commit, and mirrored to origin; (4) `scripts/merge_train.sh run` merges staging into a private clone, requires a verdict manifest for the exact resulting tree, and fast-forwards main only then (gives the owner a verdict to merge PRs by); (5) `scripts/br_sync.sh <ids…>` flushes and verifies the exact bead set before staging JSONL (AGENTS.md landing step 4); (6) bead-close helper refuses to close without citing a manifest id whose tree contains the bead's landing commit; (7) check.sh's registry step stops being a grep (fa-szi replaces it) and forbidden-deps gains the cargo tree --invert posture-confinement check (§18.4).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: a run split across two workers (one step UNRUN on the first) completes on the second and produces one manifest for that tree; [ ] planted negatives: a FAIL recorded for the tree blocks the manifest; a dirty tree is refused; a manifest for tree A cannot close a bead landed in tree B; [ ] proof class: gate (verdict contract) ; [ ] consumers: every landing, the owner's staging→main merges, bead closes; [ ] no-claim boundary: binds verdicts to trees; does not make a weak step strong.

TESTS: scripts/tests/ shell tests with fixture repos for each case; shellcheck clean.

title: fad performs file reads and writes for unauthenticated socket clients relative to an unvalidated client `cwd`: confine host paths to a declared files root and refuse everything else
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14)
`fad` forwards the client's argv and `request.cwd` (fad/src/lib.rs:398-407) to the owner dispatcher; the
cwd is never validated. `document add`, `chart import`, `--intent`, `--plan` read any file the daemon user
can read into the book; `--plan-out`, `--certificate-out`, `--out` create files anywhere it can write
(combined with the --plan-out clobber, any file). The socket on main is bound with the default mode and no
peer-credential check (fad/src/main.rs:184); 5de90c6 (0600 socket) exists only on the unpushed nlu line.
fa-yha confines MCP host paths only; fa-ohe tests the `--as` variant only.

## What to build
1. `fad serve --files-root <dir>` (required for any file-reading or file-writing verb over the socket;
   absent ⇒ those verbs refuse over fad with a fix naming the flag). Paths are resolved against the root,
   canonicalized, and refused if they escape it (.., symlinks out, absolute paths elsewhere).
2. The client cwd is used only to make a relative path absolute on the CLIENT side; the daemon never trusts
   it.
3. Socket 0600 + SO_PEERCRED uid check (land 5de90c6 via RECON-3, then add the peer check).

## Acceptance
- Planted: socket request reading `/etc/passwd` as a document, writing `--out ../escape`, a symlink in the
  root pointing outside → all refused, nothing read or written (strace-free check: file hashes/mtimes
  unchanged; the book frontier unchanged).
- A request from a different uid is refused before any parsing.

## Tests & logging
fad integration tests with a tempdir root, logging request argv, resolved path, decision, refusal id.
close_reason: Implemented launch-time --files-root <dir> confinement for fad serve (resolve_in_daemon_files_root, admit_daemon_files, BookSource::locate Held --keys rejection, --receipt-out output path admission), refused host-file reads/writes when --files-root is omitted or escaped (via .., symlinks, book_dir overlap, or foreign request.cwd), and moved foreign-UID peer refusal to Ready::Accepted before any frame reading or parsing.

title: Exercise corrected forensic semantics through CLI, MCP, retained findings and replay
description:
## Why
Companion integration acceptance for unequal multi-party attribution and explicit solvency valuation/maturity inputs. Calibration or byte-identical replay can faithfully certify the wrong calculation. Existing same-party fixtures and command/event probes do not prove these semantics.
## What to test
One small labeled synthetic corpus with A100/B200 batched versus separate payments/investments, distribution pool90, old register assertion followed by spending, explicit valuation applicability, and long-term versus inside-horizon debts. Independent literal expected schedules, never production collector reused as oracle. Run library, real fa CLI, bound fa-mcp, persisted findings/workpapers and retained replay at identical coordinates. Keep missing infrastructure UNRUN. Preserve semantic versions and old certificate meaning; no silently regenerated goldens.
## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact party/unit/entity source and recipient margins and due-date/valuation predicates agree across every intended surface.
- Wrong-subject/scope/late-recorded inputs refuse before unauthorized observation. Refused accounting calls mutate no accounting/intent outcome or other guarded domain state; independently mandated audit/time publications are separately identified and test-pinned.
- Empty/no-party/duplicate-party/unrelated-dimension/mixed-unit cases, partial settlement, reverse/replace, staged migration and effective cutoff boundaries have explicit expected outcomes.
- A closure exceeding its bound refuses or has an explicit partial claim; never drops citations silently and returns a complete computation. Mutating one due date, attribution, valuation input or omitted citation fails its own independent expected predicate.
```acceptance-tests
fa-cli::forensic_semantics::creditor_and_investor_margins_survive_public_workflow
fa-mcp::forensic_semantics::solvency_inputs_and_refusals_match_cli

```
## Logging
Retain exact fixture/entry/leg ids, source prefix, method/parameter/input digests, per-party schedules, certificate bytes and per-surface outcomes. Bind canonical exact-tree pass to all tests. Block calibration and the complete reader-workflow claim until these semantic examples pass; harness authoring can proceed independently of final green certification.

Audit basis: source tree 3c964f1f07a91c3ad9b72eebcd1a95e7809f02c8 / ba83ac090e82779518a335691fc92ab2e5704278, 2026-10-21 local. Existing binary observations are SHA256-bound in /private/tmp/fa-reality-check-20261021.d9HmEI/manifest.json; those binaries predate HEAD and are not an exact-tree gate. All fixes require normal canonical Rust gates and published proof. No implementation was changed by the audit. Preserve all accounting features, authorization-before-observation, exact arithmetic, journal immutability and independent oracles. Never weaken a gate or regenerate a golden to accommodate incorrect output.

## Refinement: scope, time and independent evidence
Public corpus also includes contra-asset net assets20/liabilities50/deficit30, maturity schedule omission/duplication, per-target invoice dates, counterleg-only party evidence and mixed attributed/unattributed legs. Distinguish invalid duplicate dimensions from valid repeated party references. For every finding, label source-derived versus older-binary-reproduced versus exact-source-proved evidence independently. This campaign shares one bounded corpus rather than multiplying superficial event-name tests.

title: Capability issuance as journaled control + holder-bound capability tokens + kernel verification of the presented token; profiles and caveats registry (capability_caveats.toml)
description:
WHY: plan §14.2 says caveats are conjunctive and attenuable only and "issuance and revocation are journaled control entries"; §14.4 registers ten profile templates (Agent, Preparer, Approver, Controller, Auditor, Regulator/Examiner, Investigator, Receiver/Trustee, Production, Witness); Appendix A has `ControlPayload::CapabilityEvent { commitment, kind: Issue | Revoke | Attenuate, caveats_digest }`. At e606b46 revocation is journaled (fa-llx e97746b, FA-REF-023) and witnessed on writes (fa-bcd), but there is no issuance: every capability is constructed in-process from argv by `Capability::embedded` (crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247) and the kernel checks only that the presented value is not revoked (crates/fa-journal/src/policy.rs:714). Profiles implemented: Human/Agent/System only (capability.rs:56). `registries/capability_caveats.toml` does not exist. So there is nothing an operator can hand an agent that the kernel will verify, and nothing that makes "the holder of this token is principal P with ops O" true by construction. WHAT: 0. Consume before building (doctrine 10, AGENTS.md "Never a copy of substrate code"): first evaluate FrankenGraphDB's live Warden permit/policy types (`fgdb-warden`, `fgdb-policy`; plan §2.1 "Policy/permit types live") and asupersync's macaroons/authenticated types (plan §2.2) as the token format and attenuation algebra; record the decision (adopt, or why not) as an Appendix H row update (R-WARDEN) in the same change. Build an FA-level token only for what those types cannot express, and keep the accounting caveat vocabulary owned here. 1. `registries/capability_caveats.toml`: the closed `ops` vocabulary (21 names, already `fa-policy/src/op.rs:11-59` — the registry becomes the source and the code is checked against it), the caveat vocabulary of §14.2 with per-caveat status live|dormant (live today: ops, per-leg ceilings, books, expires_at; others dormant naming their bead), and the ten profile templates as data (ops ceilings, required caveats such as Agent ⇒ branch-confined + requires_dry_run once fa-we7/fa-s7x land). fa-registry reader + parity test vs op.rs. 2. `IssueCapability` control (Appendix A CapabilityEvent{Issue}): issued by a principal holding `issue_capability`, under SoD for `IssueCapability(ops ∋ restate)` (sod_policy.toml row), body = {holder principal, profile, caveats (sorted, tag-coded like Capability v2), expires_at, parent commitment for attenuation}, commitment = BLAKE3 over the canonical body; journaled, immutable; a Capability metadata vertex keyed by commitment (identity-derived vid) is the point-read witness the kernel checks at commit (exists, not revoked, not expired, holder matches session principal). 3. Capability token = the canonical body + a holder key binding (the holder's public key, Ed25519 via fa-l3c's signer once landed; until then a 32-byte secret whose hash is in the body), stored in a 0600 token file like DatabaseKeys. Attenuation produces a child body whose caveats ⊆ parent's and whose daily_total root is the parent's root issuance (§14.2 "attenuation never resets a ceiling"). 4. Kernel: `admit` takes a `PresentedCapability { commitment, proof }`, point-reads the Capability vertex, verifies proof-of-possession, and derives the effective caveats from the JOURNALED body — never from a caller-built struct. The embedded owner posture keeps `Capability::embedded` but only behind an explicit `OwnerPosture` constructor that requires the book key file and is labelled in every outcome (`authority.posture = "embedded-owner"`), so tests and single-user CLI keep working and the label makes the trust boundary visible. 5. CLI: `fa cap issue --holder

--profile [--caveat k=v]... --out `, `fa cap list|show [--json]`, (revoke is fa-1d6 and reuses the commitment); robot events `capability_issued`, `capability`; verbs.toml + MCP parity (issue is NOT exposed to Agent-profile MCP sessions). 6. fa-reference: naive issuance/attenuation/expiry/revocation model; differential over generated issue/attenuate/revoke/use histories. ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: a Controller issues an Agent token; a post presented with it on trunk is refused FA-REF-013; a read with it succeeds; an attenuated child with a smaller per-leg ceiling refuses a leg above it; issuance is visible in `fa cap list --json` with the issuing control entry's EntryRef; [ ] planted negatives (one check each): forged body (caveats edited after issuance) → commitment mismatch refusal; valid body, wrong proof-of-possession → refused; attenuation widening an op → refused at issuance; issuance by a principal lacking issue_capability → FA-REF-012; IssueCapability with ops ∋ restate without the SoD approval → FA-REF-008; expired token → refused at the admission point (expires_at against TimeEvidence per §14.2 "Expiry admission"); [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-10.core/current-policy over journaled issuance) + differential vs fa-reference; [ ] consumers: fa-r3q, fa-0x0, fa-7dw, fa-ohe, fa-1d6, fa-s7x, fa-z5u, fa-zgn (Auditor profile); [ ] no-claim boundary: tokens prove possession of a journaled grant; key custody of the holder's secret is the operator's responsibility (R-KEY interim). TESTS: fa-policy unit tests for attenuation algebra (property tests: caveats only narrow, ceilings never reset); fa-journal kernel tests for every negative; fa-cli binary tests for issue/list/show with robot transcripts logged; fa-reference differential with the seed printed.
close_reason: Added registries/capability_caveats.toml and fa_registry::CapabilityCaveats (21 ops, active/dormant caveats, 10 profile templates) wired into registry-check and fa-policy parity tests; implemented cascading issuer-to-child revocation in fa-journal/src/policy.rs; added resource://fa/capabilities/{token} and capability_caveats.toml in LAWS in fa-mcp.

**What works:**
- **Issuance:** issuance is a journaled control entry: PolicyControl with CapabilityEvent{Issue}, control kind 10. The issued capability's canonical body is in extension 7, at issuance_vid(book, commitment). It is idempotent by identity.
- **Widening refused:** the issuer can never widen its own authority: ops, units/ceilings, books and expiry are each bounded by the issuer's.
- **Possession caveat (tag 8):** a holder-bound capability carries H(secret). The kernel admits it only against its journaled issuance (FA-REF-156 otherwise). Revocation (FA-REF-023) applies as before.
- **CLI:** `fa capability issue --holder … --profile agent|human --op … [--ceiling …] [--expires-at …] --out <new 0600 file>`, plus `fa capability list` and `fa capability show --commitment`.
- **Token file:** holds the principal, the capability and the secret. The secret is never printed or journaled. The file is written only after the issuance commits, and an existing `--out` is refused before anything is journaled.
- **Bound sessions:** `fa-mcp --token <file>` binds the session to the token's journaled capability, posture `issued-token`, within the agent or preparer launch ceiling. `fa --token` and fad sessions are fa-r3q slice 1.

title: Subject keys: per-Party erasable-field keys held outside the journal (R-KEY), managed by fad, with Party objects; ErasureCut switch-over from the typed refusal
description:
Background: fa-lp6 (TopazOsprey, 2026-10-10) ships Erasable<T> fields with subject_ref but every key is the book key, and ErasureCut is a typed refusal (FA-REF-088) citing plan 8.5 / Appendix H R-ERASE: an FA-level tombstone that leaves plaintext reachable is a prohibited shortcut, so erasure waits for destroyable per-subject keys. The invariant 'redaction or key loss never changes an amount' is proven in fa-lp6 on the real substrate.

Scope: (1) Party objects (vertices, content-addressed, immutable body) as the subjects of erasable fields; (2) a subject-key store OUTSIDE the append-only journal: a keys file owned by fad (writer lease) with per-Party keys, key ids referenced from Erasable<T>.subject_ref, key creation journaled as a control entry naming the key id (never the key), destruction journaled as a typed tombstone naming the key id and the legal basis; (3) fold/read behaviour with a destroyed key: amounts, digests, registers, trial balance unchanged; erased fields render as a typed absence naming the tombstone; retry equivalence per FA-REF-033; (4) ErasureCut control entry (plan 8.5) admitted only with a destroyable key present, SoD row for erasure, refusal rows updated; (5) oracle in fa-reference models key presence; differential plants: erasure with the book key (refused), erasure of a subject with live legal hold (refused), valid erasure (admitted, amounts unchanged), read after destruction (typed absence); (6) CLI: fa party add, fa erase <subject> --basis <code> --yes, fa keys status; MCP parity later.

Depends on fa-lp6 (Erasable fields, SupplementalEvidence) and fa-i8j (fad owns the keys file). No-claim boundary: green proves key destruction removes plaintext reachability through FA's own readers and never changes an amount; it does not claim substrate-level erasure (R-ERASE) or storage-media guarantees.

Testing: real-substrate kernel tests, CLI binary tests with detailed logs, differential floors for each planted negative.

title: The accumulator covers every journaled evidence object, not only ENTRY vertices: attestations, document and import receipts, custody transfers, supplemental evidence, legal holds and period/policy controls get leaf envelopes in commit order
description:
## Why (verified by reading 2026-10-14)
Only `ENTRY` vertices are accumulator leaves (fa-notary/src/journal.rs:232). Attestations, receipts, custody
transfers, supplemental evidence and legal-hold cells are outside the tamper-evident chain, though §13.2
lists them; a key holder can rewrite an attestation without any proof exposing it.

## What to build
Leaf envelope kinds for every journaled object class (record kind, coordinate, commit seq, ordinal); the
scope index covers them; fa-verify inclusion/consistency handle the new kinds; existing books get the new
leaves from the next checkpoint (append-only: no rewrite), with the boundary recorded in the state.

## Acceptance
Rewriting an attestation, a receipt or a hold under the keys is detected by `fa verify accumulator` (exit 8)
and by an outsider inclusion check; fa-70o's red-team matrix rows for these objects go green.

## Tests & logging
fa-notary tests + fa-verify fixtures; logs leaf kind counts per checkpoint.

title: Certificates that replay across binary upgrades: journaled RegistryEpoch objects, selector-scoped certified closures, certified reads that feed the fold, typed refusal above the row budget
description:
## Why (A5: "a damages schedule computed in 2026 replays in 2029")
Today (fa/src/certificate.rs): `registry_digest` hashes the include_str! text of 7 registries plus
franken-stack.lock (~391-431) and replay refuses on any mismatch (~990-994): any registry edit or pin bump
orphans every earlier certificate unless the old binary is kept. The certified closure is `MATCH
(n:Entry)` over the whole book (~449-453 policy: result_rows 1,000,000), so any report on a book with >1M
entries cannot be certified, and the report is recomputed via `db.vertices_at` beside the certified reads
rather than from them (plan §13.6 wants the closure's reads to be the fold input).

## What to build
1. RegistryEpoch control object: the exact texts of every registry a certificate depends on, stored
   content-addressed in the book (through the blob store when large) at genesis and whenever the running
   binary's registry set differs from the latest epoch (journaled, authorized). Certificates bind epoch
   digests. Replay loads registries from the book's epoch; a binary refuses only when it cannot interpret
   the epoch's format major (typed refusal naming the epoch and the needed major).
2. Selector-scoped closures: certified reads restricted to what the report needs (period/effective range,
   account set) where the substrate's query surface allows; otherwise a typed refusal with a pagination
   plan when the row budget would be exceeded (no silent truncation).
3. The fold consumes the certified read results (single computation path), so the certificate proves
   what was actually folded.

## Tests
Replay of a certificate after editing a non-format-breaking registry row in a newer binary build →
byte-identical; after a format-major change → typed refusal; >budget book → typed refusal; mutation of a
certified read input → replay detects.
acceptance_criteria: All four tests green; README's replay claim updated to the proven scope.

title: Make fa-reference independent where it matters: its own period resolution, period state machine and admissibility table (no calls into fa-time/fa-registry decision code), its own unbounded arithmetic in the application law, an exhaustive Appendix C cell test, and multi-seed differential campaigns
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §16.2 — "a mismatch is triaged against the spec and never resolved by making the reference imitate the engine"; AGENTS.md — the oracle has "its own limb arithmetic … so a shared arithmetic bug cannot make the differential green". fa-reference calls the kernel's own `periods_for_year`, `resolve_period`, `transition` (fa-time) and `Admissibility::decide` (fa-registry) (crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:55-60, :978, :1127, :1562-1567), and its docs say it "mirrors the kernel's law order exactly" (lib.rs:6-11). For period law and admissibility, therefore, the differential proves the kernel is wired to those functions, not that the laws are right — fa-zxm's reversal-period bug survived precisely because both sides omit it. Its application law uses raw i128 (lib.rs:1752-1764, :2608-2618, :2629), contradicting the own-limbs design (it would panic, not refuse, on overflow). The "exhaustive" admissibility test checks the cell count plus about a dozen spot cells (crates/fa-registry/src/lib.rs:1230), not every cell against Appendix C. Each differential runs one fixed seed with 420–700 steps, USD only, amounts ≤ ~91k (crates/fa-registers/tests/differential.rs).

WHAT: (1) fa-reference gets naive, obviously-correct implementations: period generation by day-walking the calendar definition, resolution by linear search, a state machine as an explicit transition table, admissibility as a literal table transcribed from Appendix C (a second transcription, reviewed against the plan, not generated from admissibility.toml) — the kernel's registry and the oracle's transcription are then compared cell-by-cell in a test, so a registry typo is caught; (2) the application/open-item law on the oracle's limb arithmetic; (3) the topology gate forbids fa-reference from calling fa-time's resolution/transition functions and fa-registry's decide (allowlist only data types and parsing); (4) differential campaigns: N seeds per test in check.sh (e.g. 32, time-boxed), 10k seeds nightly-equivalent on a free worker, multi-unit histories (USD, JPY scale 0, BTC scale 8, ETH scale 18) and amounts near register bounds; the failing seed and a replay command printed; generated histories include the envelope fields fa-cw1 refuses; (5) a planted-negative audit: each planted negative must reach exactly one check (the M6 lesson recorded by the swarm: a mutation survived because every negative also tripped a sibling check).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: differential green across the seed campaign; Appendix C transcription equals admissibility.toml on all cells; [ ] planted negatives: deliberately wrong kernel admissibility cell is caught by the oracle (it was not before); the fa-zxm reversal-period bug is caught by the new oracle before fa-zxm's fix lands (record the old-code negative); [ ] proof class: differential (strengthened) ; [ ] consumers: every kernel bead, G1 ("the reference differential over model-generated histories"); [ ] no-claim boundary: differential agreement, not proof.

TESTS: fa-reference unit tests, differential campaigns with seeds/crashpack-style replay lines logged.
close_reason: Removed the last remaining fa_time::period::transition call from fa-reference in favor of admissibility::oracle_transition with an exhaustive 45-pair parity test, and converted open-item/settlement calculations (step 1e, step 7a, applied_to, open_items) to use fa-reference's independent Int limb arithmetic.

title: Lantern semantics defects: FIFO/LIFO/pro-rata tracing ignores supersession, Benford counts both legs and mixes units, duplicates flag Replace corrections, cutoff false positives in adjustment periods, round_trips not one-to-one, self_approved never fires
description:
## Why (found by reading the integration line 7ec4895, 2026-10-14)
- trace.rs:176 takes every posting entry including reversed originals and their reversals: tainted 500 day 1,
  erroneous clean 1,000 day 2, its Reverse day 3 → FIFO consumes the tainted 500 as part of the "1,000
  withdrawal" and traces 0 (LIBR correctly 500). Graph procedures exclude only REVERSAL-class entries,
  not the originals they reverse (graph.rs:90, 333).
- digits.rs:117-131 counts every leg of every unit: both sides of a two-leg entry (N ≈ 2×, chi-square ≈ 2×
  overstated) and USD/JPY/share counts in one distribution.
- duplicates.rs:66-73 flags a Replace that keeps the legs as a duplicate of the still-present original.
- cutoff.rs:43-44 resolves the document date without the effective-period hint → FYxx-P13 adjusting
  entries dated year-end flagged "0 days apart".
- graph.rs:105-163 round_trips: one outbound matches every same-amount return; quadratic without budget.
- jet.self_approved: the kernel refuses self-approval, so the planted set is empty; no positive test.
- The complexity witness allows n² on a 30-entry corpus — a tautology.

## What to build
Supersession-aware projections (net effects by lineage per §8.2 netting laws) as the input to every
procedure; Benford population rule (one side per entry, one unit, registered eligibility) recorded in the
procedure's evidence row; duplicates exclude supersession pairs; cutoff uses the entry's period
resolution; one-to-one matching with a budget; self_approved fed by approval records on drafts/imports or
removed from the registry; a real complexity witness (operation counts on corpora of 10², 10³, 10⁴ with a
registered bound).

## Acceptance
Each item gets a planted fixture that fails before and passes after; the fa-reference naïve versions are
written independently (not mirrors; see fa-vfu/fa-jt7p defect 9).

## Tests & logging
crates/fa-lantern/tests; each procedure run logs population size, parameters digest, findings count.
close_reason: Fixed all 7 Lantern semantics defects across fa-lantern, fa-reference, and registries/procedures.toml with planted regression tests (supersession netting, single-side single-currency Benford population, duplicate correction-lineage exclusion, adjustment-period cutoff discriminator, O(L log L) 1-to-1 RoundTrips matching, migrated self-approval detection, and registered complexity bounds verified across 10^2, 10^3, and 10^4 corpora).

title: fa-registers maintainer: incremental delta_since folds with a CAS watermark, RegisterCheckpoint control records with checkpoint cadence as a decision card, rebuild = maintained metamorphic, recovery discards and rebuilds, read paths never serve stale cells, Ripple switch-over rule registered
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A1 says balances are "materialized incrementally and verifiable by recomputation", W2 names "the fa-registers maintainer over delta_since", and Appendix H registers the interim posture for Ripple views as a FrankenAccounting-level `delta_since` register maintainer. At 96d1918 every fold is a full rescan of the entry stream at a known-at seq (fa-registers/src/lib.rs `fold_period`, `trial_balance_at`); `materialize` writes register vertices and `verify_period` compares, but there is no incremental maintainer, no watermark advance from `delta_since`, no checkpoints, and `delta_since` has 0 hits. This is correct but will not scale, and the recovery rule ("recovery discards and rebuilds") has no code path to exercise.

WHAT:
1. The maintainer: `Registers::advance(&cx, book)` reads the substrate's `delta_since(watermark)` entry stream, folds only the new entries into the register cells (period × account × unit, plus the pending, open-item, availability and per-entity cells as they exist), moves the watermark under CAS inside the same transaction, and is idempotent under crash (re-running from a stale watermark yields identical cells).
2. Checkpoints: a journaled `RegisterCheckpoint` control record (legs = []) naming the watermark and the fold digest per register family; verify-by-fold runs from the last checkpoint or from genesis on demand; the checkpoint cadence is an adaptive decision with a decision card and a pinned fallback (every N entries), per the adaptive-decision contract.
3. Recovery: `fa registers rebuild` discards every register vertex and refolds from genesis (or from a checkpoint whose digest verifies); the rebuilt cells equal the maintained ones (metamorphic `rebuild = maintained`); `fa verify registers` stays green across the rebuild.
4. Reads: the report paths use maintained cells only when their watermark covers the requested known-at and the cells' verify digest matches; otherwise they fold (never a stale answer; the envelope reports which path answered).
5. Switch-over rule: when the substrate's Ripple views land, the maintainer becomes the registered interim's replacement per Appendix H; the rule is recorded in foundation_dependencies.toml.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: after N posts, `advance` moves the watermark by N and the maintained trial balance equals the full fold byte-for-byte; a crash between fold and watermark move (fa-sim crash point) leaves cells that re-advance to the same result; `rebuild` reproduces every cell; [ ] planted negatives: a maintainer mutation that skips one entry class is caught by verify-by-fold; a checkpoint with a forged digest is refused on rebuild; reading maintained cells past their watermark is refused by the read path test; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04 register-never-more-authoritative, live) + metamorphic; [ ] consumers: every report path, G1 register verification, fa-sim campaigns; [ ] no-claim boundary: incremental equality is proven on the covered register families only.

TESTS: fa-registers integration tests with watermark and digests logged, fa-sim crash-point campaign for the maintainer, metamorphic rebuild test, CLI binary tests.
close_reason: Incremental delta_since register maintainer (crates/fa-registers/src/maintainer.rs), DecisionCard cadence, retired-cursor rebuild, migration visibility tracking, CLI/MCP registers advance/materialize/verify, and FA-INV-04.maintainer live in registries/invariants.toml.

title: Statistical audit lane with independent oracles: in-house exact Benford/KS/chi-square procedures checked against frankenscipy fsci-stats (test-only), NumPy-reproducible sampling via franken_numpy fnp-random-core (PCG64DXSM), property suites on frankensim fs-propcheck
description:
WHY: doctrine 12 — a detector's score is `statistical` evidence, never an invariant; an examiner must be able to re-run the numbers in Python. frankenscipy (/data/projects/frankenscipy) has chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest and Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared distributions — all f64, so it cannot produce the certified statistic but is an ideal TEST-ONLY checker (fa-lantern dev-dependency; 4 MB lib.rs compile cost noted). franken_numpy's fnp-random-core (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe)) gives SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM, so a sample drawn from a declared seed is reproducible in Python; the seed is a declared input (no entropy capability, doctrine 3). frankensim's fs-propcheck (zero deps: deterministic property testing with shrinking and seed replay) and fs-rand (seeded streams independent of scheduling) serve the §16.6 property/metamorphic suites and fa-gen.
WHAT: (1) crates/fa-lantern first slice: exact-integer Benford first/second-digit expected counts (rational expectation × n, law-rounded), chi-square and KS statistics over register legs with a certificate; (2) `fa sample random|mus --seed <declared> --size n` over open items/legs using fnp-random-core, output reproducible by a documented NumPy snippet; (3) dev-dependencies: fsci-stats pinned by git rev as the differential oracle for the statistics (tolerance stated as an f64 oracle bound, never applied to amounts); fs-propcheck for property suites; (4) registry rows for the procedures' claim classes.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] oracle differential passes on fixtures and generated histories; [ ] sample reproducibility test vectors (seed → indices) pinned; [ ] no float in any amount path; [ ] `fa capabilities --json` lists the procedures with claim class statistical. UPSTREAM: frankenscipy — integer/exact-rational entry points for expected counts, or document f64 as oracle-only.
notes:
Upstream issue filed 2026-10-10: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenscipy/issues/16 (oracle numerical contract; exact entry points; split lib.rs).
TESTING (idea-wizard pass 1): every slice lands unit tests in the owning crate AND an end-to-end script-level test (binary test in crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs where a verb is involved) with detailed, greppable logging of inputs, digests, and verdicts; external tools absent => UNRUN, never a fake pass; gate stays rch-only.
close_reason: Landed exact-integer Benford expected counts, KS and chi-square statistics with naive and pinned fsci-stats differential oracles, NumPy-reproducible SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm sampling with pinned vectors, and deterministic property/shrinking suites in fa-lantern (57 unit + 25 integration + 22 reference tests passing, 0 clippy warnings, 6/6 doctrine checks green).

title: Work-witness evidence schema and claim–artifact ledger: every benchmark/proof/model/oracle/calibration claim cites a machine-produced artifact carrying a witness only the real computation can produce
description:
## WHY
Every fabrication found on 10-20 shares one shape: a claim with no witness of the work. A timing of corpus generation
labelled "10M-leg rebuild"; `Verified` from `--version`; `Pass{23}` from a byte prefix; an "incumbent" that is the same
closure. Rather than policing each instance, make the artifact itself carry proof of work, and make registry-check refuse
claims without it.

## WHAT
1. `registries/evidence_artifacts.toml` + `evidence/` content-addressed store (BLAKE3 digests; large raw files kept out of
   git under a registered path with the digest in git). Artifact kinds and their mandatory witnesses:
   - benchmark: engine operation counters (legs_folded, entries_posted, fsyncs, substrate_reads, bytes_allocated) read
     from the engine's own instrumentation, raw samples, host fingerprint (CPU, kernel/OS, filesystem, measured fsync
     distribution), commit, toolchain; counters must meet the manifest's declared scale.
   - external-oracle: tool name+version+sha256 of the binary, the evaluated journal digest, compared-cells count ≥ 1 and
     their digest, divergences.
   - lean: `lake build` log digest, theorem inventory (names + statement hashes), toolchain.
   - tlc: spec digest, cfg digest, distinct states, depth, result, TLC version.
   - lab-campaign: seed list, crash-point coverage matrix, oracle verdict counts.
   - calibration: corpus digest, scenario labels, confusion counts per procedure, interval method.
2. registry-check: any row in slo.toml, invariants.toml (checker_strength proof/model/bounded_model), proof_lanes.toml,
   formats.toml oracle rows, evidence.toml calibrated rows, or procedures.toml `calibration = "planted"` must cite an
   artifact id whose witness satisfies its kind's rule; otherwise the row is refused.
3. claims_lint extends to docs/** and README: sentences asserting "proof", "external oracle", "measured", "calibrated",
   "constant-time", "agreement across" must cite an artifact id or be flagged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: a real artifact produced by fa-ykbp/fa-09q8/fa-dj6j/fa-sa4w passes; a doc citing it passes claims_lint.
- [ ] planted negatives (one per kind): benchmark with legs_folded below scale; oracle with zero cells; lean inventory
  missing a theorem the row names; tlc artifact with 0 states; calibration row without confusion counts → each refused.
- [ ] proof class: invariant of the registry.
- [ ] no-claim boundary: witnesses raise the cost of fabrication; they do not prove the instrumented counters themselves
  are correct (those are covered by unit tests of the counters).

```acceptance-tests
tools/registry-check::tests::benchmark_artifact_requires_scale_witness
tools/registry-check::tests::oracle_artifact_requires_compared_cells
tools/registry-check::tests::lean_artifact_requires_theorem_inventory
tools/registry-check::tests::tlc_artifact_requires_state_count
tools/registry-check::tests::calibration_artifact_requires_confusion_counts
tools/registry-check::tests::claims_lint_covers_docs
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: one test per artifact kind and witness rule, positive and planted negative. E2E: a real tier-2 artifact (e.g. from fa-sa4w or fa-ykbp once landed) resolves through registry-check end to end. Logging: registry-check prints, per evidence row, artifact id, kind, witness fields checked and the verdict.

title: Decide whether an empty (zero-byte) document may be recorded for disclosure; intake refuses it today (FA-REF-083)
description: WHY: the owner's document-disclosure test (b3ebf30, external_document_storage_and_empty_documents_use_the_same_public_export) recorded a zero-byte document and exported a disclosure over chunk 0. title: Document intake requires a capability and derives the provenance grade from the intake source and principal profile; the caller can never declare `HumanUpload`
description:
WHY: plan §9.3 — every document carries a provenance grade derived from its receipt chain (ThirdPartySigned, Connector, HumanUpload, AgentUpload, Generated); an entry whose only evidence is AgentUpload/Generated is self-sourced and needs a human Reviewed attestation before promotion (FA-INV-05; AGENTS.md "a document you uploaded yourself is graded AgentUpload"). At e606b46 `add_document` (crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:651) takes no capability; the CLI sets the grade from `--grade` (crates/fa-cli/src/document.rs:97, default AgentUpload) and the uploader from `--as` (cli.rs:1477). An agent can label its own upload HumanUpload and skip the review gate; the reviewer-≠-uploader check compares against the caller-supplied identity.

WHAT: `add_document` takes the session capability; the grade is a pure function of (intake source registry row in registries/intake_sources.toml, principal profile, connector transcript if any): Agent profile ⇒ AgentUpload always; Human upload only from a Human-profile authenticated principal (fa-r3q) or the explicit embedded-owner posture (labelled); ThirdPartySigned only when a registered signature verifies; `--grade` is removed (or retained only as an assertion that must equal the derived grade, refused otherwise); the ImportReceipt records the authenticated principal and commitment.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an Agent session's upload is AgentUpload and the self-sourced gate fires on its entry until a Human Reviewed attestation exists; [ ] planted negatives: `--grade HumanUpload` from an Agent session refused; a reviewer equal to the uploader refused using the authenticated identity; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-05 evidence-minimum over honest grades) + evidence oracle differential update (crates/fa-registers/tests/evidence_oracle.rs); [ ] consumers: fa-g21, fa-646, Lantern jet.self_sourced_evidence; [ ] no-claim boundary: a grade states custody provenance, not document authenticity.

TESTS: evidence_oracle updates with seeds; CLI binary tests; fa-mcp e2e upload as Agent.

comments.author: MaroonCat
comments.text:
MaroonCat 2026-10-25: implemented; landed on main as 67664fdfb. Closure is an independent verifier's call.

**The test** is `fa-formats::tests/tigerbeetle.rs::corpus_runs_through_kernel`, the id this bead's acceptance-tests block names.
- Each corpus scenario runs on a fresh in-memory book over the real posting kernel (fa-journal; fa-formats already depends on it).
- Each account is a debit-normal Asset, and max_debit_net > 0 becomes its upper BalanceLimit.
- How each step maps:
  - a transfer is an Original;
  - a pending transfer is a Pending hold whose timeout is anchored to a daemon-clock tick journaled at its day;
  - post_pending is a Resolution(Posts) of both legs;
  - void_pending is a Resolution(Voids);
  - an expiry is a tick past the deadline, then the System sweep's Resolution(Expires).
- Refusals map by catalog code: FA-REF-062 to already_resolved, FA-REF-091 to exceeds_limit, FA-REF-061 to exceeds_pending.
- Checked for every scenario: its outcomes, and each account's four sub-vectors from the trial-balance fold. A limited account's LimitCell must carry the same four fields.

**Result:** all 9 scenarios agree. That includes expiry through the sweep (tb_05), the reserved-availability refusal (tb_07), and over-capture (tb_08). Each scenario logs expected and observed.
