title: fa-intents first slice: typed intents with canonical bytes, Book::plan dry-run returning a Plan with a PlanCertificate, Book::commit(plan) re-validating the bound fields (PlanInvalidated refusals), confirm_plan gating, non-null certificate in the robot envelope
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A6 says agents work through typed intents with dry-run plans, and plan §19 says the Genesis slice takes "real PostEntry, IntentHeader and Plan types from fa-intents". At 96d1918 `fa::Book` has `post` but no `session/plan/commit`; `plan_certificate` is always `None` (fa-cli main.rs ~1750, fa book.rs ~849); the robot envelope's `certificate` field is emitted as `null`; `confirm_plan` has zero hits. An Agent-profile capability is refused on trunk with a pointer to drafts (fa-s7x), so today an agent cannot post at all. Intents are the laws-layer abstraction (crate layer "laws": pure, stripped Cx) that both drafts (fa-s7x) and Canon (W6) build on, so this slice must exist before either.

WHAT (first real slice, not a prototype):
1. `crates/fa-intents` (laws layer; no I/O, no Cx with capabilities): `IntentHeader { book, branch, principal, capability_ref, idempotency_key, known_at? }`, the intent union for the classes the kernel admits today (PostEntry, Reverse, Reserve, Resolve, Settle, PeriodTransition, DocumentAdd) with Appendix B field names, a canonical byte form (versioned, additive-minor, tag-coded like fa:entry:v1) and `proposal_digest` (which already exists in the kernel; move the single source here).
2. `Book::plan(&cap, intent) -> Plan`: a dry run that runs the full posting pipeline up to but excluding commit (admission, period law, evidence minimum, balance law, limits, SoD) against a snapshot, returning the effects (legs, mirrors it would move, approvals it needs, refusal it would raise) and a `PlanCertificate { proposal_digest, effects_commitment, snapshot_seq, security_policy_epoch, expires_at_seq }`; nothing is written.
3. `Book::commit(&cap, plan)`: re-validates the certificate's bound fields (plan §4.6 line 371: proposal digest, effects commitment, coordinate, policy epoch, current SoD, execution authority) inside the serializable transaction and refuses `PlanInvalidated { reason }` (new FA-REF codes with catalog rows) when any changed; otherwise commits with `plan_certificate` recorded on the entry and emitted in the robot envelope (`certificate` non-null).
4. `confirm_plan`: dangerous verbs (post with post_closed, period close/lock/reopen, resolve voids) require `--yes` or a `--confirm-plan <certificate>` whose digest matches; the refusal names the safe alternative (`--dry-run`).
5. CLI: `fa post --dry-run` emits the plan with its certificate (Agent-profile capabilities imply dry-run once per session, §15); `fa commit --plan <file|digest>`; robot events `plan`, `plan_invalidated`.
6. Oracle: fa-reference models plan = pure evaluation and commit = re-evaluation under the current state; differential plants: a plan invalidated by a concurrent close, by an epoch change, by a revoked capability, by changed legs; a valid plan commits byte-identically to a direct post.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa post --dry-run --json` returns a certificate and writes nothing (journal head unchanged, proven by `fa verify registers` and an entry count); the same plan committed produces the same entry bytes as a direct post (metamorphic test); [ ] planted negatives: each `PlanInvalidated` reason is exercised by a test that changes exactly that bound field between plan and commit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-11.core: certificates replayable) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-s7x drafts (intent-log), fa-canon (intents bound to rule families), fa-cli/fa-mcp dry-run macros, FA-INV-11; [ ] no-claim boundary: a certificate proves what the plan bound, not that the intent was economically correct.

TESTS: fa-intents unit tests for canonical bytes (golden vectors per minor), kernel tests in fa-journal/tests, CLI binary tests for dry-run/commit/confirm_plan, differential floors ≥ 3 per planted reason, all with the proposal digest logged.

**What works** (plan §10.4: refused "with PlanInvalidated {changed: [...]} and a fresh plan, never silently re-planned"):
- `Book::replan`, `replan_replacement` and `replan_batch` rehearse the stale plan's own intent(s) again at the current head under the caller's capability.

**Now works:**
- **Record:** `IssuanceControl` (class 28, control kind 15). It carries the period, ordinal, statement definition, the retained statement certificate and its known-at (`certified_at`), the audience and an optional transmittal document.
- **Numbering:** a period's issuances are numbered from 1 in commit order, so the first issuance is one point read.
- **Authority:** `close` plus one Human approver who is not the preparer (`sod_policy` `statement-issuance`). Appendix C has no IssuanceControl row. I gave it the authority of the Lock whose pin it supersedes: period-lock is W(close, 1).
- **Flow (CLI):**
  1. The preparer plans: `fa statement issue --certificate C:<oid> [--for P] --issued-to <audience> --dry-run`.
  2. Another principal runs `fa approve --proposal <digest>`.
  3. The preparer runs `fa statement issue --plan <bytes> --approval <vid>`.

  Listing: `fa statement issuances [--for P]`.
- **The plan carries the sealed description**, like the period Lock's plan, because sealing is randomized. Its ordinal is part of the approved proposal. A rival issuance that commits first makes the plan stale (exit 6); it is never renumbered.
- **Pin:** `originally_reported` reads the first issuance's `certified_at`, else the first Lock. A later issuance never moves it.
- **Refusals:** FA-REF-172 NOT_ISSUABLE for a certificate that is not retained, not a trunk statement certificate, or not one reporting the period. A plan whose issuance its certificate does not state is refused at commit.

title: Qualify all six reader workflows together on the exact release candidate
description:
## Why and current boundary
Plan sections 15.6, 16.9 and 19 require the composition of all six bets, not isolated command samples. At inspected 32bed7d7/c7b5eb58 the generated scoreboard samples 33 workflow commands and 18 gate criteria; it omits important Genesis/lab/Canon/consolidation/caveat obligations. Retained full workspace at 836009e9 is RED (3075 passed,31 failed); later repaired campaigns are UNRUN. Existing beads cover components, but none explicitly owns final composed acceptance at the release candidate. fa-y6eu owns the fresh-agent campaign, fa-0fl simulation and fa-ubl0 criterion transcription; reuse their outputs, do not replace them.

## Deliver
Build and test one bounded release-acceptance driver under the existing check/proof architecture. Consume the complete criterion transcription, supported-capability manifest, per-domain work-witness artifacts, named test inventory and exact candidate source/target hashes. Execute the plan's complete reader workflows through real CLI, fad-hosted MCP and embedded APIs where their contract applies: agent closes month with draft/review/promotion; CPA freezes and checks a real exported population; examiner reproduces positions and Part370 output; trustee preserves appointment-prefix history and estate branch; expert replays a counterfactual production independently; investigator replays cited graph findings and its own access trail. The plan calls these the five readers although section 15.6 contains six workflows; retain all six. Do not use stub tools or synthetic captures as live integration proof. Synthetic books with planted truth are explicitly labeled.

## Independent falsification
Per reader exercise the actual negative contract: unauthorized observation/trunk mutation, self/shared-lineage approval, revoked/expired capability, bad evidence, stale aggregate basis, omitted out-of-scope/within-scope records, altered assumption/report and partial/cancelled stream. Report state/frontier and artifact digests before/after. Run independent verifier without book keys/network and compare exact report bytes; membership or producer-index attestation cannot stand in for recomputed scope. Missing inputs/tools/worker capacity are UNRUN and cannot aggregate to PASS. Retain a named original-bug or planted negative showing the driver rejects one wrong candidate.

## Acceptance
```acceptance-tests
release_acceptance::all_six_reader_workflows_use_real_registered_surfaces
release_acceptance::missing_or_stale_domain_evidence_cannot_pass
release_acceptance::stronger_criterion_rejects_a_proxy_probe
release_acceptance::unauthorized_or_tampered_reader_workflow_fails
```
Future required tests. Code and its unit/e2e tests land together. The campaign is a distinct integration obligation, not a companion micro-closure that lets implementation land without tests. Log exact candidate tree, binary hashes, seed, selected subjects, coordinate, authority commitment, per-step exit, independent predicates and domain artifact links. No verdict unions across different trees or unpublished overlays. Criterion omissions, unexpected ignores and accounting result mismatches are RED. Existing allowed upstream absences keep their registered correct interim posture; do not drop required 1.0 features to obtain a green. W10/G3-G4, all V01-V36.

title: Content-addressed per-crate verdicts: whole-tree verdict as a Merkle root over workspace steps and per-crate verdicts keyed by exact input-closure hashes (incremental exact-tree proof)
description:
## Why
A Lantern-only landing re-runs fa-money, fa-time and every other unaffected crate's tests. The
exact-tree doctrine does not require that: it requires every verdict to bind its exact inputs.

## Design
- Workspace steps (fmt, deny, forbidden-deps, foundations, topology, registry checks, invariants,
  robot-schema pin, ubs, shellcheck) always run on the whole tree.
- Per crate: input hash = BLAKE3 over (crate source tree, transitive path-dependency crate trees,
  Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, franken-stack.lock, deny.toml, every registry file the crate
  embeds via include_str!/include_bytes!, feature set, test-target list). A crate whose input hash
  has a stored green verdict (git notes ref refs/notes/crate-verdicts, keyed by input hash) is not
  re-tested; its verdict is reused.
- Conservative invalidation: any change to Cargo.lock, toolchain, franken-stack.lock, deny.toml, or any
  registries/*.toml invalidates all crates.
- Tree verdict = Merkle root over (workspace step verdicts, per-crate verdict leaves); the manifest
  lists which leaves were reused and from which trees.

## Tests & logging
Planted change in a leaf crate → >= 50% of crate verdicts reused; planted registry change → 0 reused;
a composed root's per-crate results equal a cold full run on the same tree (equivalence test run once
per week as a lane).
acceptance_criteria: The three tests pass; a real landing reuses verdicts and the manifest lists reused leaves.
close_reason: Implemented per-crate input-hash closure, conservative include_str!/include_bytes! scanning, and Merkle tree verdict composition in scripts/crate_verdicts.py and scripts/crate_verdicts.sh; verified with scripts/tests/crate_verdicts_selftest.sh.

title: Resolve special periods, carry-forward folds, and report cutoffs
description:
References: §§4.8, 7.1-7.5, 8.6, 12.1/12.5, 15.6, Appendix A/C/F (lines 349, 475-491, 552, 717, 733, 919, 1181, 1265-1279, 1330).
A date must resolve to exactly one Period, but normal December, adjustment period 13 and closing/opening periods can share civil dates. There is no target-period field on Entry/PostEntry or registered routing rule to disambiguate. Shared calendar identity also needs separation from per-book period state.
The fold boundary is not defined for stock vs flow: FOR PERIOD filters effective dates, while balance-sheet/TB positions require opening balances; §7.5 additionally posts next-year opening balances despite an all-time append-only fold. Simple cash 100 at year end plus a new opening 100 becomes 200 under All unless openings are anchors or an explicit selection law excludes double counting. Closing entries likewise must not zero the income-statement activity reported for the closed year.
§8.6 imports opening trial balance plus optional full legacy history; specify a cut so both cannot be counted twice.
§7.4 defines originally reported as first Closed, while close can include further adjusting entries before publication/lock. Either label this view as first close or persist a ReportPublication fact/certificate; retain AS REPORTED IN for actual filings.
Required examples: Dec 31 normal/adjustment/closing, FY aggregate, Jan opening, pre/post-close P&L and BS, known-at retrospective correction, multi-book shared calendar with independent status, migration opening+detail. Special-period reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/651d8af3ea974ad1a4d74449122c620e/2252d7531a4d424de10000000a174cb4.html . W1/W3/W7/W9, G0.
Appendix C refuses PriorPeriodAdjustment in Open/SoftClosed, although §8.1 defines it as an opening-retained-earnings adjustment. Decide whether it posts into the current open period while referring to historical error periods, or whether its class name means a different operation; do not force a current-period correction into a closed/locked target.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §7.3 effective_period discriminator (special periods must be named; class-restricted); §4.1 Period key per book with shared calendar; §7.5 stock-vs-flow rule (flow lines filter by period, stock lines fold EFFECTIVE <= end), income statements exclude Closing, no opening-balance entries, incremental reclose + nominal-zero; §8.6 migration-disjoint modes; §7.4/§12.5 AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED anchored to StatementIssuance; Appendix C PriorPeriodAdjustment row posts in the current open period with relates_to. comments.text:
## 2026-10-19 (claude-opus-5-5): the aging portfolio (d6b01a46) and rule-policy cash flow (e6beb110) are surfaced on the CLI. Status: still OPEN

**What was unwired.** Three owner report families exist only in the library, about 3.7k lines with library tests: aging portfolio, split cash flow and policy cash flow. No CLI, fad or MCP path reached them; the sync `Book` had no wrapper for the portfolio. These two commits wire the first two.

**Aging portfolio (d6b01a46):**
- **Selections:**
  - `fa gl aging --reconcile --account 1200,2100 …` reconciles exactly those leaves.
  - `--all-posting` reconciles every posting leaf.
  - Both run from one chart, one aging fold and one control trial balance at ONE coordinate.
  - One code (`--account 1200`) is unchanged and still emits `aging_reconciled`.
- **A missing selection is still a usage refusal.** It is never read as the whole book (broadcast-scope doctrine). The two owner tests that assert exit 2 for it are unchanged.
- **New event and shapes:** event `aging_portfolio_reconciled`, shapes `aging_portfolio_account` and `aging_portfolio_uncovered`. Unselected leaves are `uncovered`, never zero. `complete`, `reconciled` and `pending_reservations` are separate verdicts. This is an additive row in robot-schema v1.
- **Certification:** `--certify` / `--certificate-out` retain the `fa:aging-portfolio:v1` artifact.
  - The new `--expect` kind `aging-portfolio` takes scope (all-posting, or selected with accounts), through, fixed known_at and buckets.
  - `fa replay C:<oid> --expect …` reproduces the original. Without `--expect` it exits 8, and the fix names `--expect`.
- **Sync wrappers:** `Book::reconcile_aging_portfolio` and `Book::certify_aging_portfolio`.

**Test:** `aging_portfolio_equals_each_single_leaf_reconciliation_and_replays_only_against_its_request` (crates/fa-cli/tests/retained_report_storage.rs).
- Differential: each whole-book portfolio account equals that account's own `aging_reconciled` at the same known_at.
- Event and shape keys equal the pinned schema.
- Six planted usage refusals publish nothing.
- Certify -> replay works. A changed cutoff or scope exits 8; a HEAD prefix exits 2.

**Rule-policy cash flow (e6beb110, library fa-i9yn):**
- A `gl cash-flow --policy` file with `account_rules` ([{account, activity}] for non-cash counterparts) and optional `overrides` (whole cash legs) is a rule policy.
- It emits the new event `policy_cash_flow`: `cash_flow`'s units plus `decisions` (each leg's activity and basis: account_rules, override or internal_transfer).
- Direct and indirect formats still refuse `account_rules`. A rule policy refuses `assignments` and `--indirect`.
- `--certify` retains `fa:policy-cash-flow:v1`, with the new `--expect` kind `policy-cash-flow`.
- Sync wrappers: `Book::cash_flow_with_policy` and `Book::certify_cash_flow_with_policy`.
- Test: `rule_policy_cash_flow_equals_its_explicit_leg_assignments_and_replays_only_against_its_policy`.
  - Differential: the 64 derived decisions, fed back as explicit assignments, give an identical `cash_flow`.
  - One override moves exactly 1.00 USD from operating to financing.
  - Seven planted usage refusals publish nothing.
  - Replay: a changed rule or a dropped override exits 8; an omitted `--expect` exits 8 with a fix naming `--expect`.
- A rule policy is a handful of rows instead of one assignment per cash leg, which also keeps the replay_command far below the argv limit recorded on fa-lzrn.

**Also:**
- README "Reporting available now" now lists six gl lines (ca790fdf), each registry-checked by the README test. They are not executed by that test; the surfaces they name are exercised by binary tests.
- Event coverage: `every_declared_event_is_emitted_by_the_binary` (cli.rs) now also runs `gl aging --all-posting --reconcile` and a rule-policy `gl cash-flow`. Gate k17 caught that the first version of d6b01a46 had omitted this; the fix is folded into d6b01a46 and e6beb110 so every commit stays green.

**Still open on this bead:**
- Split cash flow (`Book::split_cash_flow` / certificate: exact principal/interest portions of one cash leg) has no surface. I did not wire it because of a format question for the owner.
  - `CashFlowPortion.amount` is a bare i128 mantissa "in the SAME unit … as its source cash leg"; the definition carries no unit.
  - A CLI that parses portions as exact strings ("0.40 USD") and passes only the mantissa would silently accept "0.40 EUR" against a USD leg, because both have scale 2.
  - A safe surface must either check each portion's unit against the cited leg's unit before retention (the CLI has the source lines after the read), or the library definition should carry the unit.
  - The `--expect` replay path needs the same check.
- The portfolio JSONL workpaper (`aging_portfolio_jsonl`, read+produce, recipient-bound) has no surface.
- MCP: `gl` has no MCP tool at all, so none of the gl families are on MCP. The cluster has to be chosen first (see fa-i7e on full clusters).

title: Solvency, lookback and distribution procedures (plan §11.5–11.6): solvency.balance_sheet_test/cash_flow_test, lookback.preferences with computed §547(c) defenses, lookback.fraudulent_transfer, ponzi.net_investment, distribution.rising_tide/pro_rata, damages.but_for over scenario scratch books
description:
WHY: plan §11.6 and the second half of §11.5 (distribution methods "registered beside tracing, because the receiver's work product is the investor-level schedule"), §0.1 readers 3–4, §15.6 workflows 4–5 ("The trustee or receiver takes over", "The litigation consultant computes but-for damages"). fa-nlu covers tracing laws (FIFO/LIFO/pro-rata/LIBR) and JET; nothing covers solvency, preferences, fraudulent transfer, Ponzi net-investment/rising-tide/pro-rata distributions or but-for damages.

WHAT: registered procedures (procedures.toml rows, fa-nlu's registry) with typed parameters and evidence rows: solvency tests at a coordinate (AS KNOWN AT pinnable to what management knew) with fair-value adjustments supplied as documents; lookback.preferences (90-day/1-year insider windows via RELATED_TO closure, defenses computed: subsequent new value §547(c)(4), ordinary course §547(c)(2) statistics vs a baseline window, contemporaneous exchange §547(c)(1)) → net exposure per creditor; lookback.fraudulent_transfer (§548 2-year, UVTA 4-year windows; badges as findings); ponzi.net_investment (Madoff net-equity), distribution.rising_tide (SEC v. Huber), distribution.pro_rata (Cunningham v. Brown) with investor cohorts and clawback schedules; damages.but_for = statements on a scenario scratch book (fa-s7x) minus trunk, certified (fa-cqk).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: golden fixtures from published worked examples (cite the source in the fixture) reproduce exactly; reruns byte-identical with certificates; [ ] planted negatives: a preference inside the window offset by subsequent new value nets correctly; a parameter change changes the certificate; [ ] proof class: statistical/exact per procedure as registered (never invariant for scores) ; [ ] consumers: receivers, trustees, experts; [ ] no-claim boundary: technical predicates; legal conclusions are counsel's (§13.4).

TESTS: procedure golden fixtures, CLI tests, determinism tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the 8 solvency, lookback, Ponzi, distribution, and damages procedures (solvency.balance_sheet_test, solvency.cash_flow_test, lookback.preferences with 11 U.S.C. 547(c)(1)/(2)/(4) defenses, lookback.fraudulent_transfer, ponzi.net_investment, distribution.rising_tide, distribution.pro_rata, damages.but_for + compute_scenario_but_for_damages) in fa-lantern and registries/procedures.toml (FA-EVID-L52..L59); verified cargo test & cargo clippy on worker hz4, doctrine_check (6/6), and ubs (0 critical).

title: Fresh-context agent campaign (G3.2): scenario cards for every §15.6 workflow run by fresh agents given only in-tool docs; transcripts graded for useless_error; regressions pinned as tests
description:
## Why
G3 requires "fresh-context simulated agents complete every §15.6 workflow with zero useless_error
outcomes". fa-12x covers scripted Polish Bar tests, not model-driven agents.

## What to build
- scenarios/agent-cards/*.md: one card per workflow (agent closes a month; CPA audit; examiner; receiver;
  litigation; investigator) with the goal, the sandbox book (fa demo), and success predicates.
- A harness (NTM or plain subprocess) launching fresh agents with only `fa robot-docs` / MCP tool docs
  and the card; every tool call and result logged; a grader classifies each refusal/error as
  useful (taught the next step) or useless_error.
- Metrics per run: first-try success per command, useless_error count, turns to completion. Each
  useless_error becomes a regression test (refusal text/fix change) before the next run.

## Tests & logging

title: fad can miss a queued connection's readiness under load and park forever; the fa client then blocks without a deadline
description:
## WHY
An `fa` request through a serving fad can hang forever. Observed 2026-10-21 (MaroonRaven, macOS, under build/test load):
- In a full workspace run, fad tests every_registered_verb_and_subcommand_is_served_by_both_hosts sat for 15+ minutes; the same target normally finishes in about 10 s.
- Looping that test alone while the machine was loaded reproduced the hang twice: in 8 iterations, then in 7.

Evidence:
- Client stack (macOS `sample`): fa_cli::entry::through_daemon -> client::call -> block_on -> kqueue wait. The client connected and wrote its request. client::call reads under Budget::INFINITE, so it never gives up.
- Daemon stack: every thread idle (main parked in block_on; workers in kqueue wait or condvar).
- With a temporary eprintln at Ready::Accepted and Ready::Timer in serve_with: connection #155 was accepted and closed; #156 was never accepted; no timer fired afterwards.
- With no connections, Untimed::deadline() is None. The listener's readiness is then the only wake source, and that event was lost.
- asupersync UnixListener::poll_accept (rev 78b6463) calls accept() on every poll and closes the re-arm race. The lost event is below fad, in the readiness and waker path; the root cause is not identified.

## WHAT
1. fad: never wait on listener readiness alone. Cap each serve-loop wait with a short re-poll deadline, so a lost wakeup costs bounded latency instead of a hang.
2. Root cause upstream in asupersync's reactor or accept-waker path: reproduce with a minimal listener loop under load and report it there.
3. Consider a client-side bound in client::call (no response within N) that returns a typed error naming fad status, instead of blocking forever.

## Acceptance
- The parity test looped at least 20 times under load with no hang. A re-poll timer is seen to recover a queued connection (diagnostic run).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
MaroonRaven, 2026-10-21: WHAT 1 landed in 17c03d73. serve_with caps every wait at 1 s, so a lost readiness event costs at most a second.
Evidence (load average about 26): before the fix, 2 hangs in 15 looped parity runs; after it, 54 of 54 passed. A diagnostic build saw the re-poll recover three times in 30 runs: two queued connections accepted right after a zero-connection timer, and one connection's request read (1008 ms).
Full workspace on main ab772d61 plus the fix: 218/2964/0/7.
Stays OPEN for WHAT 2, the root cause in asupersync's readiness or waker path (not reproduced minimally yet; reads are affected too, not only accept), and WHAT 3 (a client-side bound in client::call). Self-verified on macOS only.

title: Never-silent-fail on panic: install a panic hook in fa, fad and fa-mcp that emits exactly one robot `error` event (exit 5, refusal_id, class "internal") instead of exit 101 with no event
description:
WHY: plan §15.3 "every non-zero exit emits exactly one error event carrying refusal_id, exit, and class, which is what the never-silent-fail regression test asserts"; exit code 1 is never emitted and Rust's panic exit is 101. At e606b46 there is no panic hook (Teller audit): a panic in the substrate or a dependency exits 101 with no error event, breaking the robot contract and the exit-code dictionary. Surface code has no unwrap/expect, but the substrate and foundations can still panic.

WHAT: a panic hook (std::panic::set_hook) in each binary's main that writes one `error` event (stdout when --json, stderr text otherwise), maps to exit 5 with class "internal" and refusal_id, and includes the panic location; fad keeps serving other connections where the region model allows (a panic inside one request's region is that request's error, not the daemon's death) — verify with asupersync's region semantics; a test binary feature `fa-test-panic` (dev-only, compiled out of release) triggers a panic to test it.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: forced panic → exit 5 + one error event; [ ] planted negative: removing the hook fails the test; [ ] proof class: e2e; [ ] consumers: agents, fa-fs0; [ ] no-claim boundary: process-level reporting; aborts (OOM kill) cannot be reported.

TESTS: fa-cli/fad/fa-mcp binary tests.

title: fa-mcp containment: tool arguments that name host filesystem paths (document/intent/plan/chart inputs, plan_out output) require an explicit launch filesystem root or are refused; inline/forwarded-stdin forms are the MCP path
description:
WHY (TopazOsprey 4185, WhiteCreek 4184, 2026-10-11): after fa-23r a launch-bound fa-mcp fixes identity, authority, the book and its keys, but path arguments still resolve against the server process's working directory on the host: fa_evidence_import_document.file, fa_post_post/reserve/resolve.intent_file and fa_chart_import_chart.file read any file the server's OS user can read; fa_time_period_transition.plan reads a plan file; plan_out writes one anywhere the user can write. An agent holding read+post can therefore import arbitrary host files as documents or write files outside the book. fa-23r explicitly does NOT claim filesystem confinement.

WHAT:
1. In the MCP posture the inline / forwarded-stdin forms (intent, text, chart) are the positive path.
2. A path argument is refused with a structured error whose fix names the inline form, unless the launch configuration grants an explicit filesystem root (--files <dir>); paths are then resolved under that root with no .., symlink or absolute escape.
3. plan_out and plan work only under that root.
4. Audit every tool, resource and macro (fa-z5u's macros included) that accepts a path.
5. Planted negatives: absolute path, .. escape, symlink escape, and a path given without the root; positive: inline forms and an in-root path.

ACCEPTANCE: positive observable = an e2e stdio session launched with --files <dir> imports a document from under the root and the same call with a path outside it is refused with the structured error; planted negatives as in WHAT 5 each reaching exactly one check; proof class = e2e + unit on the resolver; consumers = every MCP host, fa-z5u, fa-ohe; no-claim boundary = this confines path arguments only; it is not a sandbox for the server process and does not authenticate the operator (fa-v62/fa-r3q).
close_reason: Added --files <dir> launch-confined directory root to fa-mcp and LaunchAuthority in fa-cli; resolve_in_files_root rejects relative escapes, absolute paths, directories, and symlink components along path; document add/import/export and plan file paths work inside root when --files is provided; verified with unit and integration tests.

comments.author: CobaltGull
comments.text: 2026-10-13 (CobaltGull, fa-ul9 tracker truth): the containment half is on the integrated trunk. fa-mcp never exposes a host-path property in a tool schema (registry.rs is_host_path_property / forbidden_path_argument, pinned by tests/parity.rs), and the bound CLI surface refuses --plan-out/--certificate-out/--out and any non-stdin --intent/--plan/file input (fa-cli cli.rs admit_bound_files: "MCP accepts no output paths", "forward the complete content on stdin with -"). Inline/forwarded-stdin forms are the positive path. NOT done: the optional `--files <dir>` launch root (resolver with no ..,symlink or absolute escape) and its e2e positive/negatives, which this bead's acceptance names. Until a host needs in-root files, "every path refused" is the safe posture; keep open for the root, or re-scope the acceptance to "paths refused" by ruling.

title: Owner-project survey and adoption decisions (2026-10-10): what each of the owner's 47 Rust projects can contribute to FrankenAccounting, the rulings that govern adoption, and the upstream issues filed
description:
PURPOSE: the durable record of the 2026-10-10 survey of every Rust project written by the owner (47 projects, local checkouts under /data/projects and GitHub Dicklesworthstone), evaluated for applicability, utility and accretion to FrankenAccounting, plus the owner rulings that govern adoption. Read this before proposing any dependency; do not re-survey.

OWNER RULINGS (binding, recorded in AGENTS.md doctrine 1 and README):
1. The closed dependency universe excludes THIRD-PARTY crates only. Every Rust project written by the owner — Franken-named or not (e.g. fastapi_rust) — is an admissible foundation, pinned by git rev, with its transitive closure confined by deny.toml wrapper allowlists exactly like asupersync/frankengraphdb/fnx/fastmcp-rust. First-party code still never imports serde, tokio, chrono, decimal crates, arrow or SQLite bindings directly.
2. Upstream changes are fine: file GitHub issues with the requests (nine filed, listed below).
3. Adoption follows a concrete consumer slice (plan rule): each adoption bead lands the pin in the same change as the first consuming code.

METHOD: four read-only explorer passes (no builds), each reading README/plan/architecture headers, root Cargo manifests, crate counts, .rs counts, #[test] counts, status notes and last commit dates; verdicts are tied to file paths. Present-tense READMEs about planned systems were not accepted as evidence.

ADOPT NOW (beads): franken_markdown → fa-cet (deterministic PDF/A-2b, HTML, SVG statements; std-only engine fmd-font/fmd-math with clap/wasm/asupersync optional; ~4.5k tests; src/pdfa.rs, src/diff.rs semantic diff, src/diagrams.rs flowcharts; crates.io v0.5.0; numeric table alignment/footing to be verified by fixture first). frankensympy → fa-pri (fsym-bigint/fsym-rational: normalised exact rationals, cross-cancelled composition, metered arithmetic; local snapshot has no .git — pin upstream f449ab0; its own plan calls the exact substrate an open decision; today it wraps num-bigint/num-rational with serde derives — allowlisted as foundation transitives).

ADOPT LATER OR TEST-ONLY (beads): frankenscipy fsci-stats → fa-vpk (chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest, Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared; f64 only, so test-only oracle; 4 MB lib.rs; nightly CI not green per its README). franken_numpy fnp-random-core → fa-vpk (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe); SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM for seed-declared reproducible audit sampling; bit-exactness is the README's claim, 5 tests in the core crate). frankensim fs-propcheck / fs-rand / fs-blake3 → fa-vpk (zero-dep property testing with shrinking and seed replay; seeded streams; a test-time BLAKE3 cross-check; frankensim has no local .git — pin upstream; its README says not yet an integrated end-user application; skip fs-eproc (asupersync covers it), fs-ledger (frankensqlite), fs-qty (no money)). frankengit fgit-deflate → fa-646 (std-only bounded streaming zlib/DEFLATE, 3,865 LOC, 41 tests, for PDF FlateDecode and ZIP-based XBRL/SAF-T packages; the rest of frankengit (234 third-party packages, fgit-crypto with ed25519-dalek) is not needed; its constellation.lock pattern is already plan §2.6). franken_lean fln check-olean → fa-uqq (zero external crates; elaborator accepts only 25 of 2,961 upstream elab tests so it cannot compile our .lean, but check-olean accepted all 2,433 stdlib modules — a second kernel over anchors compiled by upstream Lean; fln-bignum uses Lean number semantics, wrong for money). franken_ocr focr and franken_whisper fw robot → fa-646 (external processes only: both link frankensqlite and other closures; OCR has 19.3% character error rate on its own corpus so output is advisory, never an amount source; whisper NDJSON transcripts with diarization; models download separately 1.6 GB + 0.49 GB). hedge_fund_data_tool → fa-646 after upstream extraction (deterministic PDF text-layer extraction crates/hfdt-sources/src/extract.rs pdf_text_to_text, no OCR; hfdt-pdf-crypto AES-256 empty-password PDFs with deps aes+sha2 only; hfdt-tables cells-as-evidence; hfdt-accounting-quality statement-level procedures; inline-XBRL reader only; no Benford; proprietary license; carries chrono/serde today). flywheel_connectors → fa-ff6 (separate supervised process: fwc → fcp-host → connector subprocesses over stdio/JSON-RPC; connectors/plaid transactions_sync and accounts_balance_get, snowflake sql.write/sql.query, bigquery, s3, stripe, postgresql; cannot be linked: tokio/hyper/reqwest/chrono in fcp-async-core). franken_alignment → fa-s30 (GitHub only; reference model, zero external crates, nightly-2026-09-07; one-shot permits bound to immutable payloads, conserved rights, authority-graph dominators/min-cuts for separation of duties, judgment caching with emptiness witnesses, DecisionClosure; crate names collide with ours (fa-reference, fa-policy, fa-verify, fa, fa-cli) so linking needs package renames; port invariants as fa-policy tests first). eidetic_engine_cli → fa-i8j design reference (daemon over a local Unix socket with 4-byte length-prefixed JSON frames and size limits, src/daemon/protocol.rs; uses std::os::unix::net — we use asupersync Unix sockets src/net/unix/listener.rs). fastapi_rust → fa-i8j later HTTP posture only (v0.5.0, not production-ready per README:784, TCP-only server crates/fastapi-http/src/server.rs; asupersync-native; inatd uses it for a daemon status endpoint). toon_rust → fa-1gb (TOON spec v3.0, 289 tests; every dep always on incl. unused chrono, f64 numbers; in-house encoder validated against its tests/fixtures/spec and the tru binary until the lib/cli split lands). mcp_agent_mail_rust and coding_agent_session_search → fa-xex design/behavioural references (error envelope with recoverable/fix_hint; robot mode triage next_command, capabilities, robot-docs schemas); mortgage_processing_data_tool → design reference for dual control and one command catalog driving CLI and daemon (private, serde/num-bigint/pdf-extract). franken_surveillance_system fss-graph-algorithms and franken_overlap → fa-fk5 blocked on upstream (fss: exact-integer Hungarian/max-flow/SCC/temporal reachability with proof witnesses, 17.4k LOC, 108 tests, but tied to fss-core and u64 weights, no local .git; NOT APPLICABLE (do not revisit without a new reason): frankenpandas (fp-types already carries chrono/chrono-tz/serde, amounts parse to f64, fp-io drags arrow/parquet/calamine/csv/quick-xml; only a post-1.0 fa-frames adapter outside every posture closure), franken_snowflake (alpha, writes pending; 641 packages incl. fsqlite/frankenpandas; its MCP crate is a pattern for fastmcp+asupersync only), frankenfs (FUSE ext4/btrfs; one storage engine rule), frankenredis (mature Redis clone; no cache/KV server needed), franken_engine and franken_node (JS/TS runtimes; Canon is total and I/O-free; node requires tokio), frankenlibc (LD_PRELOAD glibc replacement, unsafe allowed; a deployment choice at most), frankenterm (terminal hypervisor for swarms), frankentui/charmed_rust/opentui_rust/rich_rust (TUI/terminal styling; no TUI in 1.0; human mode is plain text; rich_rust arrives transitively via fastmcp-console), frankentts (text to speech), franken_manim (animation engine; SVG writer far too heavy for exhibits), frankenjax/frankentorch (ML; learned scores only advisory by doctrine, no consumer before 1.0), franken_agent_detection, franken_trends (fragment, missing crate in workspace), franken_code_browser (planning), franken_nlp (no model inference yet; rules-only redaction CLI maybe later for erasable fields), meta_skill/pi_agent_rust/mcp_agent_mail_rust as dependencies (tooling), injective_network_automated_threat_detector, building_trades_data_tool, copulattice, mechanism_interferometry_causality (research), franken_remote/frankensonos/franken_threed/franken_drone_geometry/franken_native_capsule (unrelated domains).

title: Real §17 measurement harness: each domain's bench executes the named workload at stated scale with work witnesses, raw samples, measured fsync, side-by-side previous-release incumbent, statistical regression detection
description:
## WHY
After fa-e75k retracts the fabricated evidence, §17 needs real numbers. Plan §17: every gate is an EmpiricalGate with a
pinned manifest; "no balance read number without watermark/tail disclosure"; derivability from the barrier chain using
the measured fsync distribution.

## WHAT
Per domain (single post, batched post, bulk migration [fa-zddh], balance read at watermark, 100k-account TB, 10M-leg register
rebuild, watermark lag, known-at TB, close dry-run, restatement diff, bundle production + fa-verify, JET/Benford over 10M
legs, layering over 1M parties, accumulator checkpoint, CLI/MCP latency, bytes per leg, endurance): a bench that runs the
real operation on an fa-gen book of the stated scale; work witnesses from engine counters (fa-vtzt); all raw samples kept;
exact quantiles and bootstrap 95% CIs; regression = Mann–Whitney U with Cliff's δ against the previous release binary
built in the same invocation; fsync distribution measured by a probe on the target filesystem; dev-class hosts labelled
as such; gates activate only on the reference machine class. Memory per leg measured from allocator counters.

Sequencing: domains land independently. Balance-read-at-watermark, 100k-account TB, known-at TB and watermark-lag
benches measure the register read path and are meaningful only after fa-715 (reports read registers) and fa-9xf9
(RegisterCheckpoints); until then they report the literal-fold path and say so in the artifact. Bulk migration waits on
fa-zddh. Everything else can be built now.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: register_rebuild_10m reports legs_folded = 10,000,000 and digest equality with maintained registers.
- [ ] planted negatives: a bench whose counter is below scale emits no artifact; a candidate 20% slower with δ large is
  reported as a regression.

```acceptance-tests
fa-bench::tests::rebuild_10m_witness_counts_legs
```

title: Agent-safe authority on every surface: authenticated principals, issued capabilities, Agent-profile defaults, read-path authorization (reality check 2026-10-11)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-11 at origin/staging e606b46): the plan's agent-safety story (§14.2 caveats, §14.4 profiles, doctrine 7 "SoD enforced at commit", doctrine 8 "authorization precedes observation", AGENTS.md "Do not write to trunk from an Agent-profile capability") is implemented correctly INSIDE the kernel (fa-policy admit/SoD, FA-REF-013 Agent-on-trunk, revocation witnesses) but every surface constructs the capability it presents from caller-supplied argv. `Capability::embedded(holder, op_names)` (crates/fa-policy/src/capability.rs:237-247) self-issues a Human-profile capability; fa-cli reads the principal from `--as` (crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:1476-1478) and ops from `--grant` (cli.rs:2104-2106, :2591-2595); fad forwards the client's argv unchanged into `cli::run` (crates/fad/src/lib.rs:194-216); fa-mcp exposes `as`, `grant`, `yes` and `keys` as tool arguments and turns them into argv (crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:1381-1388; its own unit test at :1775-1800 pins `grant: post_closed, yes: true` → `--grant post_closed --yes`). Consequences, all verified in source: an MCP agent can act as any principal, grant itself post_closed/approve/migrate/witness, approve its own proposal as a second invented principal, and is never issued an Agent-profile capability, so FA-REF-013 and the Agent profile never fire outside tests. The MCP self-approval mistake detector even tells the agent to retry "with `as` set to a different, admissible principal" (crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:484-488) — coaching impersonation. `fa capabilities` claims "The daemon/MCP posture binds the capability from an authenticated session" (cli.rs:1225), which is false today. Reads take no capability at all (crates/fa/src/book.rs:1162-1212), and `Book::read_document` returns privileged bytes without one (book.rs:982).

This epic makes the authority model real on the postures agents actually use (fad, fa-mcp), keeps the embedded owner posture explicit and labelled, and adds the adversarial tests that prove it. It does NOT weaken any kernel check; the kernel already does the right thing given an honest capability.

Children: fa-23r (MCP containment, ship first), fa-v62 (journaled issuance + holder-bound tokens + profiles registry), fa-r3q (fad session binding), fa-0x0 (read-path authorization), fa-087 (ungated privileged read), fa-vwf (intake authorization + derived provenance grade), fa-7dw (AccessEvent), fa-kae (signed approvals/attestations), fa-ohe (agent-safety red-team acceptance suite). Related existing beads: fa-llx (caveats in the kernel), fa-1d6 (revocation surface), fa-s30 (permit model), fa-t6m (current-policy spec), fa-kuu (redaction caveat), fa-s7x (drafts: the only legal place for Agent-profile writes).

Epic acceptance: fa-ohe's suite green on the exact landing tree; `fa capabilities --json` reports the binding posture truthfully; no surface accepts a principal or op from an untrusted caller.

title: Prove capacity admission across prepared races, batches, pending releases and migration activation
description:
## Why
Companion integration work for the newly reproduced cumulative-register admission defect, not a duplicate of single-entry money tests. Two individually balanced entries can currently commit and make later literal folds unrepresentable. The repair must survive every activation path and both publication orders.
## What to test
Use a retained synthetic corpus with exact native/functional gross columns, period and stock scopes and independent limb arithmetic. Cover cap-1/cap/cap+1; gross overflow with small net; two prepared transactions each individually fitting, both commit orders; a batch whose members fit separately but aggregate does not; exact uncertain-ack retries; cancellation/crash before and after guard/publication; released pending amounts crossing periods with final representability; draft and case atomic promotion; scheduled effects; staged migration remaining invisible until Finalize, with over-cap Finalize refused atomically. Every positive path must still work and report certificates/refolds agree.
## Acceptance Criteria
- Bad accounting mutations preserve the original intent outcome and capacity/draft/case/run state at the guarded basis; independently required AccessEvents/TimeEvidence are explicitly accounted for. The owner CLI reproduction leaves its exact head unchanged. Corrected retry does not duplicate anything.
- Real CLI MAX then +0.01 now returns a named refusal while tb/verify work; independent engine/reference outcomes agree.
- Negative campaign with capacity guard disabled catches the original defect and each alternate bypass; no implementation-mirroring expected values.
```acceptance-tests
fa-conformance::register_capacity::every_activation_path_preserves_representable_cells
fa-journal::register_capacity::pending_release_uses_final_state_without_intermediate_false_refusal
fa-journal::register_capacity::migration_finalize_capacity_failure_is_atomic
```
## Tests and logging
Bounded existing prepared-transaction/lab APIs first; full seeded campaign integrates with fa-0fl when available. Retain seeds, crash points, commit order, exact expected columns, observed head and refusal. Missing lab/fleet is UNRUN, never a pass. This campaign closes only with a canonical exact-tree proof listing its tests.

Audit basis: source tree 3c964f1f07a91c3ad9b72eebcd1a95e7809f02c8 / ba83ac090e82779518a335691fc92ab2e5704278, 2026-10-21 local. Existing binary observations are SHA256-bound in /private/tmp/fa-reality-check-20261021.d9HmEI/manifest.json; those binaries predate HEAD and are not an exact-tree gate. All fixes require normal canonical Rust gates and published proof. No implementation was changed by the audit. Preserve all accounting features, authorization-before-observation, exact arithmetic, journal immutability and independent oracles. Never weaken a gate or regenerate a golden to accommodate incorrect output.

## Refinement: scope, time and independent evidence
Add already-over-cap immutable-history diagnosis and gross-small-net counterexamples. Do not invent an unsupported reversal-based repair. Full lab campaign absence is UNRUN; the bounded prepared-order regression must still be executable in the existing integration suite. Record input and final expected columns independently, not merely the same fold on both sides.

title: [cases] Public-record forensic case studies as end-to-end tests of franken_accounting
description:
## Why
The owner asked for elaborate case studies built from public forensic-accounting records (WorldCom,
Enron, and complex public-company restatements and mergers). They are to serve as end-to-end
integration tests that exercise franken_accounting's deep functionality and show where it would have
raised alarms, refused entries, or matched the published reconciliations.

Research (Brenner session RS-20261024-fa-forensic-cases; modes-of-reasoning run 20261024T205000Z) and
four plan review rounds settled what can honestly be claimed. A public record gives *documented
entries*, *published tie-outs* and *trustee ledgers*. It never gives a whole general ledger. So every
case is a provenance-typed reconstruction:
- each fact is sourced, an interpretation, derived, or synthetic;
- each claim is typed:
  - D: a named procedure reports;
  - P: the first kernel refusal, with its catalog exit;
  - T: an exact tie-out, an observation and never `proof`;
  - C: consistency within a display band;
  - R: a read-back;
  - N: a negative result with a mutation twin;
  - CF: a counterfactual row;
- every attribute the record leaves open is a branch, never a silent choice.

The rendered write-ups use technical predicates only ("given the documented entry at Beresford p.111,
SoD refuses it with FA-REF-008"). They never say "would have stopped the fraud" or "matches the
auditors" (doctrine: no accusations; a statistic is never an invariant).

## What to build
The normative plan is `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md`. Its §15 work items are this epic's
children, one bead per item:
- **Phase A, the harness.** Walking skeleton first:
  - the `fa-oracles` case model, with provenance, derivation, tier, branch and status checks (K-*);
  - the CLI runner `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, which prints PASS/FAIL/UNRUN;
  - the reference differential, filler, cell evaluation and the witnesses (filler/identifier
    invariance, contributing entry, mutation twins, outsider verification);
  - the coverage gate, the renderer and the MCP walkthrough;
  - the CLI approval surface A0;
  - the WorldCom pilot A8.
- **Phase W, WorldCom.** Line-cost capitalization:
  - `expense.capitalization`, `jet.round_amounts`, `cutoff.period_boundary` and `jet.self_approved`;
  - FA-REF-008/010/080/185 first refusals;
  - a restated FY2000 bridge, the $818M 2002Q1 diff, and F6's allocation.
- **Phase X, XBRL restatements.** SunPower's 122 tagged A+Δ=B triples and Microsoft's ASC 606/842
  recast.
- **Phase E, Enron.** Branch tables, the two restatement vintages, and the entry-derived Raptor
  equity Δ.
- **Phase L, Lehman.** Statement footing, the Repo 105 scenario diff, and the no-derecognition-law N.
- **Phase M, BLMIS.** Exhibit B footing on 7 accounts, C rows on 6, the ponzi.net_investment transfer
  gap, and the record-silent program sweep.
- **Phase C, mergers.** The LinkedIn purchase-price-allocation footing, and research into an Article
  11 consolidation T.
- **Phase H, product findings.** Each is a franken_accounting fix the research surfaced (H1–H18; H18, `events.subsequent`'s period selection, was added after polish round 2).

**Where things live** (the children name their files; this is the map):
- `crates/fa-oracles/` (verification layer, `publish = false`, A1a): `src/cases/` (loaders, K-checks,
  derivations, branch enumeration, statuses, filler, reference adapter, renderer), `src/sha256.rs`,
  `src/json.rs`; case data in `cases/<dir>/` and harness tables in `data/`, all embedded with
  `include_str!` through `src/cases/embedded.rs`; loader fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`.
- **Names (plan §3.2b).** Case directories `worldcom` (W), `xbrl` (X), `enron` (E), `lehman` (L),
  `blmis` (M), `mergers` (C) and `_selftest`; a case's `id` is its directory name and `case.toml`
  `letter` prefixes every expectation and generated row id (`W-D-01`, `W-SELF-native`,
  `W-CASE-<case id>`, `W-N-90`; the self-test, which has no letter, uses its id: `_selftest-T-01`).
  Book variants are `books/<kind>[-<suffix>].toml`. One runner `#[test]` per case, named after its
  directory (`cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact worldcom`); run-time planted negatives are
  permanent `<dir>_neg_<slug>` tests over a temp copy of the case, never an edit of committed files.
- The CLI runner `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs` (A7a), with helpers in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/`;
  the MCP runner `crates/fa-mcp/tests/cases_mcp.rs` (A15).
- The authoring tool `tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py` and its unittests (A9), run by a fa-oracles
  `#[test]`.
- Generated docs: `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<id>/README.md` and `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`, and
  `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` (A14, A14b, A15).
- Registry edits in the whole program are few and each invalidates every crate verdict
  (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`): A1a and A15 (topology), A10b (claims lint), A0, H3, H12, H16
  (verbs.toml text or rows; A0 also the robot-schema pin), H1/H2/H18 (procedures.toml version bumps,
  each also invalidating that procedure's A4 tier row; H1 also adds its transfer role to
  account_roles.toml), H4 (refusal catalog), H14 (reason codes).
  Harness tables under `crates/fa-oracles/data/` are not registries and invalidate only fa-oracles and
  its dependants.
- **Verdict reuse.** fa-cli's crate verdict is never reused, because `crates/fa-cli/tests/readme.rs:31` includes
  `README.md` from outside the crate (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:16-19`, `:152-179`, `:231`), so the CLI runner and the
  drift test re-run on every gate. A9 and A13 make fa-oracles the same on purpose (they `include_str!` the fetch tool and
  a `covered_by` file), so its checks of files outside the crate are never skipped by a stale green verdict; each landing
  states that cost.

## Tests & logging
Every child lands real code and real tests together, with a positive observable, a planted negative and
a no-claim line. The runner prints one line per evaluated (expectation, variant, target, cell):
`PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection> [reason=…]`; an expectation's
verdict is the worst of its lines (FAIL, then UNRUN, then PASS). On failure it prints the reproducing
`fa` argv (`REPRODUCE fa --book <dir> …`), and it always prints the JSONL log path (`LOG <path>`). The
log holds one step record per `fa` invocation (plan §3.5 fields plus the placeholder bindings) and one
verdict record per line (A7a). UNRUN is never PASS; an UNRUN on a claimed expectation (`case.toml`
`claims`) makes the case's `#[test]` fail. An expectation with a `pending` branch cell (one awaiting
another item's probe, printed UNRUN with its observed outcome) cannot be claimed: the loader refuses
it (`PendingClaimed`, A1c), and a claim never excludes a cell. Load-time checks print
`CHECK <K-ID> PASS|FAIL|UNRUN examined=<n>` (A3a, A10a). Planted negatives are named so the gate-evidence
ratchet counts them (`scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`; `neg` is not one of its name tokens, so a
`<dir>_neg_<slug>` test calls `.expect_err(…)` on the planted run, which its body rule counts, A7a).

**Landing gates (every child that lands code; AGENTS.md).** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` (`cargo fmt --all
--check` plus `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`) passes before anything lands on main, or the work
goes to a `train/<bead>-<agent>` branch and lands through `scripts/merge_train.sh`; `cargo test` for the
touched crates through rch; `bash scripts/check.sh` whenever a non-`.rs` file changes (registries,
harness tables, case data, `tools/`, docs). Read the exit code, never a grep. Removing a test needs a
`Retired-tests:` trailer and lowering a crate's negative-test or assert count a `Weakened-tests:` trailer;
removing or weakening an expectation follows §16 the same way. fa-oracles stays engine-independent
(`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, on `scripts/doctrine_check.sh`'s no-float list, checked i128 at each unit's
scale, its topology allowlist `["fa-registry", "fa-reference", "fa-time"]`, no third-party crate).

## Notes
- Owner decisions gate sub-steps only (plan §14); see the owner-decision bead.
- **A0 at landing.** The repository tracker already holds A0 as fa-6f3g (filed from the landed plan); at landing the operator replaces fa-yugf.2 with fa-6f3g and posts A0's extra scope there (the `attest manual` sealed-proposal route), so the children that wait on A0 wait on fa-6f3g.
- **Priorities follow plan §18** (checked in polish round 4 with `bv --robot-insights`/`--robot-plan`). P1 is the walking skeleton and its pilot: A0, A1a–A7c with A7m, A8a, A8, A8b, and every item they wait on (A9, A10a, A11a–c, A12, and W1's SRC-WC-001 slice); OD is P1 because OD 1 and OD 5 touch the pilot's path (OD 1 decides whether W1's receipts can compare EDGAR originals; OD 5's reason code has the recorded `InternalTransfer` fallback, so it does not block A8). A10b, A13–A16 and most case-phase and product-finding beads are P2; R-TRACE, H4–H8, H14, H15 and the research or later-phase case items (C2, C3, E5, E6, M6, X6) are P3. H17 is research but P2, because it concerns false positives of shipped procedures on any restated book. No P1 bead waits on a P2 bead, the graph has no cycle, and A1a is the top unblocker.
- **Coordination with the rest of the tracker** (polish round 4; each child names its related beads in its Notes and as `related` links). No non-case bead already plans an H item's product change, except that fa-qh60 plans H8's user-loaded statement definitions (H8 narrows to ratio lines). The links of the A and H children (the case-phase children name theirs):
  - A0: fa-z46b (signed approvals), fa-651f (principals), fa-ohe (red-team self-approval cases);
  - A3b: fa-wrrw; A3c, A4, A8: fa-4psc; A4: fa-b6xs; A5a: fa-xvba;
  - A4r: fa-xvba (`Oracle::reclassify`), fa-2ihd (the generated-history differential over the same oracle);
  - A7a: fa-81lu (`jet.self_sourced_evidence`, grades), fa-z46b (`approve_as` is the switch-over point); A7b: fa-75j4, fa-wrrw, fa-651f, fa-z46b, fa-k07b; A7m: fa-z46b, fa-zddh;
  - A8a: fa-75j4, fa-wrrw; A8b: fa-z46b, fa-s7x (drafts), fa-xvba;
  - A10a: fa-vz7e (marker resolution); A12: fa-70h4, fa-kkxl, fa-sa4w, fa-ipom, fa-qtfd, fa-2q91, fa-0m9r; A13: fa-kkxl;
  - A14, A14b: fa-rdid; A15: fa-y6eu, fa-z5u; A16: fa-g8em, H16;
  - H1, H2: fa-6l8g, fa-v0m2; H3: fa-v6j, fa-ldfy; H6, H7: fa-c34 (and L4, E3 inside the epic; H18's flip partner L4 holds its link to H18); H8: fa-qh60; H9: fa-4psc; H10: fa-y6eu (blocking); H12: fa-75j4, fa-vz7e; H13: fa-75j4; H15: fa-ipom; H16: fa-g8em, fa-zgn.
- The plan's mechanical lint (ids defined once and delivered by an item; references resolve; edges
  topologically sort) passed at landing, but the lint script is not in the repository: the plan's landing
  commit (8e0d4306e) adds only `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` and one COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN bullet.
  So the epic's negative is the runner's completeness rule (an UNRUN on a completeness-claiming case fails
  `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases`), which the repository can check; the plan lint is not a criterion
  here (PLAN_DELTA after polish round 2).
- **OD 2b at run time.** Tests never read the fetch cache, so until OD 2b allows committing whole tables,
  every expectation built on the BLMIS Exhibit B rows or the Valukas dated series (case M, L-D-01,
