acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: every child bead is closed on cited evidence bound to its landing commit (scripts/close_bead.sh); every case README is generated from a green run, renders its Limits section, and its markers resolve (A10a)
- [ ] negative: `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases` exits non-zero while any case that claims completeness still prints an UNRUN row (plan §16), so the epic cannot be closed on a partially witnessed case
- [ ] no-claim: green cases show what registered procedures and laws do on our encodings of documented entries; nothing about what any control would have prevented

title: [cases] Owner decisions for the forensic case studies (plan §14, OD 1–6)
description:
## Why
Six decisions in `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §14 belong to the owner (RULE 0). Each one gates only a sub-step of the forensic case-study work, never the harness ("each blocks only what it gates", §14). Hash-first vendoring lets every case proceed without quote text (§1.3, §4.2), so no child bead waits on this one as a blocker. The items it gates link to it as `related`.

## What to build
No product code. Record each decision as a comment on this bead (`br comments add <this bead> …`), quoting the owner, together with what it unblocks and the one repository change it licenses. The comment's first line is `OD <n> DECIDED <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the owner's words verbatim, then `unblocks: <bead ids>` and `repo change: <file / constant / row>`. A decision is never inferred from silence or from another agent's message.

The six decisions, what each gates (§14), and the switch each one flips:
1. **SEC EDGAR contact address.** sec.gov and data.sec.gov refuse a User-Agent without a contact address. The SEC's "Accessing EDGAR Data" page asks for the form "Sample Company Name AdminContact@<sample company domain>.com" (§1.2).
   - Options: a project contact address, the owner's address, or archive-only. Archive-only is not neutral: Internet Archive captures are granted "for scholarship and research purposes only" and cannot settle byte equality with the EDGAR originals.
   - Gates: direct sec.gov fetches by `tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py` (item A9), and therefore verification of archive bytes against the EDGAR originals: until OD 1, every EDGAR row's `original_hash_compared` is false, and receipts copy it from `sources.toml` (A9, §4.4).
   - Switch: none in the repository. The address lives only in the `FA_SEC_CONTACT` environment variable of whoever runs `case_fetch.py fetch`, and never lands in a committed file, receipt, log or fixture (A9's leak test). The owner's personal address is never put in a header without explicit permission (§1.2).
2. **Redistribution of excerpts** (the facts it rests on are in §1.3).
   - (a) Quote text, at most 60 words per fact. Gates committing quote text, not the harness (§14 item 2a): the `quote` field of any facts file (W1 states it: "quote text only after (OD 2a)") and the quote column of a README's "What the record says" section (§12.3 item 2). Switch: `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED` in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/policy.rs` (A10a), false until this decision; A10a's offline test fails any committed quote text while it is false, and any quote over 60 words once it is true.
   - (b) Whole numeric exhibits. Gates committing whole tables beyond the values a case cites (the cited facts' literal values are committed like every case's, §1.3):
     - all BLMIS Exhibit B rows: M2t's generated `exhibit_b_rows.toml` ("committing it requires OD 2b"), M1, and M2a–M2c;
     - the Valukas dated series, in L1's committed form ("(OD 2b) for the dated series");
     - SunPower's (X1) and Microsoft's (X1m) whole tagged tables beyond the facts the cases cite; the cited facts' values are committed like any case's literal values, which replaces the earlier "hashes only" wording;
     - `jet.thin_descriptions` on the BLMIS rows runs "only if OD 2b vendors the row descriptions" (§9.4, M7).

     Switch: the gated items' own committed tables; the decision comment names which.

     Run-time effect until it is decided: tests never read the fetch cache (§4.3), so every expectation built on the BLMIS Exhibit B rows or the Valukas dated series (case M, L-D-01, L-N-02, L-R-03) prints UNRUN with the reason "rows file not committed (OD 2b)" (§3.2b), and those cases cannot claim completeness. The extractor (M2t) and the harness are built and tested on fixtures meanwhile. The product findings whose case oracle is one of those rows observe it only after OD 2b: H1's BLMIS equality (M-N-01's flip), H2's and H9's M5 rows, and H18's L-N-02 re-check; each states its interim evidence.
3. **Real names.** Gates committing quote *text* that contains names (a sub-item of OD 2a). Under hash-first vendoring no quote text is committed, so OD 3 gates neither the pilot nor W1, E1 or M1. It gates the post-OD-2a quote text of the F6 quote (Beresford p.111), the BLMIS account holders, and most WorldCom quotes (§14 item 3). The recommendation is role labels, the SEC's "the DPA" precedent, and a hashed deny list (§2.8; A3c's K-NAMES keeps names out of every committed field either way).
4. **Public claim wording.** The request's phrases "prevented the fraud" and "match the final work of the Big4 auditors" conflict with project doctrine (no accusations; a statistic is never an invariant). The second is also factually false for Enron, whose restated figures were never audited or reviewed. The recommendation is the §0.3 templates and assertion-status phrases, with N results given equal prominence. Gates rendering `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` (A14: "(OD 4) for `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`"), and through it A10b. Switch: `OVERVIEW_WORDING_APPROVED` in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/policy.rs` (A14); a wording other than the recommended templates is a template change in A14's `render/templates.rs`, reviewed with the decision.
5. **The `NotInPublicRecord` ManualAssertion reason code** (product finding H14), an additive registry row. Until it is decided, cases use `InternalTransfer` as the recorded placeholder code (§2.7(a); A8: "(OD 5 or the recorded `InternalTransfer` choice)"). Switch: H14's one `[[reason]]` row in `registries/reason_codes.toml` (a registry edit, global crate-verdict invalidation), then the W, E and L case-data cells that use the code (W2, W3, W5, W5b, E3, E3b, L4; H14 names them).
6. **WorldCom-labelled synthetic artifacts** (§12.4). Two exist:
   - fa-gen's `WorldComCapitalization` scenario ("WorldCom-Style Operating Line-Cost Capitalization", `crates/fa-gen/src/lib.rs:202`);
   - fa-demo's `worldcom` scenario ("WorldTel Line Systems Demo Corp.", `crates/fa-demo/src/lib.rs:115,129`; a Sunday 50,000.00 entry).

   Both plant attributes the sourced record contradicts (weekend booking and self-approved capitalization). The decision is whether their hedged labels are enough. Switch: if not, a follow-on bead relabels or re-documents them; nothing in the case program waits on it.

## Tests & logging
- Each decision is recorded as one comment in the format above; the bead's own check is that every `OD <n> DECIDED` line quotes the owner and names its unblocked items and repo change.
- OD 1's invariant is enforced in code by A9's `FA_SEC_CONTACT` leak test: a sentinel contact value appears in no file the tool writes.
- OD 2a's invariant is enforced by A10a's offline validator, which reports the excerpt volume per case (§4.2) and fails committed quote text while `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED` is false: until OD 2a is recorded, every case's committed quote volume is zero.
- OD 4's invariant is enforced by A14's renderer, which writes `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` only while `OVERVIEW_WORDING_APPROVED` is true and otherwise prints `RENDER overview UNRUN docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md reason=awaiting OD 4` (A14's logging line).

## Notes
- The bead closes when all six decisions are recorded.
- Items that cite an OD link here as `related` (checked in the beads database in polish round 5): A8 (OD 5), A14 (OD 4), W1 (OD 2a), X1 (OD 2b), L1, L3 and L4 (OD 2b: the Valukas series), M1, M2t, M2a, M2b, M2c, M3, M4, M5, M6 and M7 (OD 2b: the Exhibit B rows; §14 item 2b names M2a–M2c, and polish round 4 linked the items that run on them), and H14 (OD 5, §14 item 5). X1m's tagged tables follow X1's rule by analogy, and the plan gives it no OD link.
- Recording a decision changes no expectation by itself. Its consequences land in the gated items, each as the one repo change named above (for OD 5, H14's registry row, then the W/L case-data cells that use the code).
- The two policy switches (`QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED`, `OVERVIEW_WORDING_APPROVED`) are introduced by A10a and A14; flipping one is a one-line landing that cites the decision comment, never a side effect of a case landing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: each of the six decisions is recorded as a comment (`OD <n> DECIDED <date>`) quoting the owner and naming the items it unblocks and the one repository change it licenses
- [ ] negative: no committed file carries an EDGAR contact address (OD 1; A9's `FA_SEC_CONTACT` leak test)
- [ ] negative: until OD 2a is recorded, A10a's excerpt-volume report shows no committed quote text in any case, and committed quote text fails while `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED` is false
- [ ] negative: until OD 4 is recorded, `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` is not rendered (A14 reports UNRUN for it)
- [ ] negative: until OD 2b is recorded, no whole Exhibit B or Valukas table is committed, and every expectation resting on one prints UNRUN, never PASS (§3.2b)
- [ ] no-claim: recording a decision changes no case result by itself

title: [cases] A4: two-reader procedure tier table case_procedure_tiers.toml keyed by (id, version, row digest) and check K-TIER
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A4, §2.5, §3.6 (K-TIER), §0.4 (refuted hypotheses).

A D verdict on a reconstructed book is admissible only if the procedure's verdict on the target does not depend on data the record does not give (§2.5). The research refuted two shortcuts:
- reading dependence from the registry: H-001's registry-level classification agreed with code on only 54/68 = 79.4%;
- one reader of code: H-040's independent second reader disagreed on 4 of 12 sampled procedures, and `expense.capitalization`'s statistic depends on account VId order (§0.4).

So each claimed procedure gets a tier row that two readers classify independently from code, with the conservative tier on disagreement (§2.5). Rows are keyed by (id, version, row digest) so that an upstream change invalidates them ("Upstream change silently changes a case", §17). A per-crate code-closure hash is deliberately not used: `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` closures include every transitive workspace crate and every registry, so such a hash would invalidate the row on almost every landing and leave a gate that is permanently red, or pressure to weaken it (§2.5). The table gates D (tiers P and A cannot carry D unless the comparison population is itself sourced and complete) and, through `reads_evidence`, K-EVID on `statement` and `ledger` variants (A3c ← A4).

## What to build
**Files and public API** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_procedure_tiers.toml`, a harness table embedded with `include_str!` and listed in the embedded index (§2.4 conventions: `schema_version = 1`, a Consumer (K-TIER; K-EVID through `reads_evidence`; A5a's `reader` rows; A6's discipline; A11a's extremal variants) / Gate (`every_seeded_row_matches_procedures_toml`) / Retire (with the program) header).
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/tiers.rs`: `pub enum Tier { L, C, SRel, SAcct, SParty, G, O, P, A }` (written `L`, `C`, `S-rel`, `S-acct`, `S-party`, `G`, `O`, `P`, `A`), `pub struct TierRow`, `pub fn tiers() -> Result<Tiers, LoadError>` (`from_text` for test copies), and `pub fn row_digest(procedures_toml: &str, id: &str) -> Result<String, LoadError>`.
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/check/tier.rs`: K-TIER, added to `run_load_checks`.
- `procedures.toml` is read with `include_str!("../../../../registries/procedures.toml")` (a declared input under `registries/`, which `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` admits) and with `fa_registry::procedures::Procedures` for versions; tests pass edited copies to `from_text`.

**Row schema** (one `[[tier]]` per claimed procedure):
- `procedure`, `version`, `row_digest`;
- `tier`, the row's tier; `code_location`, the file:line at the pinned commit that justifies it;
- `reader`, `reader_tier`, `second_reader`, `second_reader_tier` (agent or human ids, each classifying independently from code with the §2.5 definitions in hand), and `disagreement` (true iff the two tiers differ). On disagreement `tier` is the more conservative (higher-dependence) of the two. The plan gives no total order, so A4 adopts the §2.5 table order L < C < S-rel < S-acct < S-party < G < O < P < A;
- `reads_evidence` with `reader_reads_evidence` and `second_reader_reads_evidence` (two readers): whether the procedure reads an entry's evidence, documents or attestations. `reads_evidence` is true if either reader says true (the conservative reading). It is required for any expectation on a `ledger` or `statement` variant.

**Row digest.** SHA-256 (A1a) of the canonical bytes (`fa_registry::toml::Document::canonical_bytes`, `crates/fa-registry/src/toml.rs:56-95`) of a document holding the procedure's `[[procedure]]` row and, in file order, its `[[parameter]]` rows and its `[[input]]` rows. Hashing the parsed rows rather than the text means comments and whitespace do not invalidate a row, while any semantic edit (version, summary, calibration, a parameter default, an input) does.

**K-TIER (§3.6).**
- Every procedure a case claims (every D's `procedure`, every N's procedure, every procedure named by a `finding_record` step, and the runner-generated `jet.self_sourced_evidence` row) has a two-reader row whose (id, version, row digest) matches the tree. A version or row change invalidates the row and requires a fresh two-reader classification.
- `reader` and `second_reader` are present and differ; `tier` equals the conservative choice of the two reader tiers.
- Tiers P and A cannot carry D unless the comparison population is itself sourced and complete (§2.5; the §9.4 `ledger` rows, M-D-10…, `record_label = "silent"`, over the complete BLMIS Exhibit B population). The plan does not say how a case marks that; A4 adds two expectation fields to A1c's schema, `population = "sourced_complete"` and `population_basis` (the fact ids, such as the exhibit's footing facts, that establish completeness), and K-TIER refuses a P- or A-tier D without them.

**Seed rows, one for every procedure any case claims (§15 A4).** Versions as checked at 8196f5e40 in `registries/procedures.toml`:
- `expense.capitalization` (v2), `jet.round_amounts` (v1), `jet.self_approved` (v1), `jet.period_end_timing` (v1), `jet.post_closing` (v1), `jet.weekend` (v1), `jet.self_sourced_evidence` (v1);
- `cutoff.period_boundary` (v1), `events.subsequent` (v1), `ponzi.net_investment` (v3);
- `recon.assertion_drift` (v1), `damages.attested_baseline` (v1);
- for §9.4: `duplicates.same_same_same` (v1), `duplicates.same_same_different` (v1), `numbers.relative_size_factor` (v1), `numbers.round_amount_density` (v1), `benford.first_digit` (v2);
- for E6: `graph.related_party_exposure` (v2), `graph.party_circular_flows` (v1).

**The plan's readings, which the readers check but must not copy.**
- `expense.capitalization` C; `jet.round_amounts` L; `jet.self_approved` L; `jet.period_end_timing` C; `jet.weekend` L; `cutoff.period_boundary` C (§6.4, §9.4).
- `jet.post_closing` P: "its commit gap depends on the population of commits" (§6.4).
- `ponzi.net_investment` S-party by the research's code reading, which "the two-reader row must confirm" (§2.5; `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:2712-2725`, `:2626`; no findings cap; its only parameter is `cohort_window_days`).
- `duplicates.*` S-rel; `numbers.relative_size_factor` S-party (one party per account) (§9.4).
- `numbers.round_amount_density` and `benford.first_digit` P. They are admissible for D only over a sourced, complete population (§2.5, §9.4).
- `graph.related_party_exposure` G (§7.2).
- The plan states no tier for `jet.self_sourced_evidence`, `events.subsequent`, `recon.assertion_drift`, `damages.attested_baseline` or `graph.party_circular_flows`.

## Tests & logging
Unit tests in `tiers.rs` and `check/tier.rs`, run by `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; negative names follow `scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`.
- **Positive.** `every_seeded_row_matches_procedures_toml`: each of the 19 rows' (id, version, digest) equals the tree's, every row has two distinct readers and `reads_evidence` recorded, and K-TIER passes over the pilot's D rows (`expense.capitalization`, `jet.round_amounts`). `comment_only_edit_keeps_every_row_valid`: a copy of `procedures.toml` with an added comment line and re-indented whitespace gives the same 19 digests.
- **Negative (§15).** `version_bump_in_a_test_copy_invalidates_the_row`: a copy with `jet.round_amounts` at `version = 2` → `FAIL K-TIER case_procedure_tiers.toml:<line> jet.round_amounts@1: registry is at version 2, row digest <old> != <new>`.
- **Derived negatives** (from §2.5, §3.6):
  - `parameter_default_change_invalidates_the_row` (`round_power` default 3 → 4 in a copy);
  - `input_row_change_invalidates_the_row` (one of `procedures.toml`'s 18 `[[input]]` rows edited);
  - `p_tier_d_without_a_sourced_complete_population_is_refused`, and `p_tier_d_marked_sourced_complete_is_admitted` (a fixture `ledger` D on `benford.first_digit` carrying `population = "sourced_complete"`, the §9.4 exception);
  - `single_reader_row_is_refused` and `same_reader_twice_is_refused`;
  - `disagreement_not_resolved_to_the_conservative_tier_is_refused` (readers L and P, row tier L);
  - `claimed_procedure_without_a_tier_row_is_refused` (a D on `jet.weekend` with its row removed in a test copy).
- **Logging.** `CHECK K-TIER PASS|FAIL|UNRUN examined=<n>`; one `FAIL K-TIER` line per invalidated row with the procedure, the versions and the old and new digest.

## Notes
- **Dependency.** A4 ← A1a: the crate, the TOML loader, `LoadError`, the embedded index and the SHA-256.
- **Digest canonicalization.** The plan does not fix it; the canonical-bytes form above is A4's choice. Checked at 8196f5e40: `procedures.toml` has 68 `[[procedure]]` rows and 18 `[[input]]` rows keyed by procedure; the plan's digest names the row and its `[[parameter]]` rows, and including the procedure's `[[input]]` rows is the conservative reading.
- **The §9.4 exception.** K-TIER's text now carries it (§3.6), so M7 is not blocked. The `population`/`population_basis` marker is A4's; the §9.4 `ledger` rows are its only use today, and A1c's loader accepts the two fields once A4 lands.
- **Two readers.** The second reader must be a different agent or human from the first, classifying before seeing the first's answer. Coordinate through Agent Mail with the bead id as thread. A reader's id is recorded, never a model's self-report of agreement; code can check only that the ids differ, so the process is part of the review.
- **Runtime backstop.** Undeclared behaviour drift is caught at runtime by A11a's filler-invariance witness with extremal variants, which fails and names the procedure (§2.5).
- **fa-b6xs.** It re-points the graph procedures to the PAID projection. A version or row change there invalidates the `graph.*` rows, and E6 then needs a fresh classification.
- **fa-4psc.** Edits to calibration fields in `procedures.toml` change the row digest and invalidate the row, even when the code is unchanged.
- **Product beads that bump a claimed procedure.** H1 and H2 (`ponzi.net_investment`, and the distribution procedures if they bump) and H18 (`events.subsequent`) change version and row digest, so K-TIER fails those rows until a fresh two-reader classification lands; each such landing re-seeds its rows here (a harness-table edit, not a registry edit) and re-pins the case rows that name the old version (M5's M-D-01/M-N-01, L4's L-N-02).
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the data file.
- **No registry edit.** The table lives in `crates/fa-oracles/data/`, so re-seeding it invalidates only fa-oracles' and its dependants' verdicts; a `procedures.toml` edit by another bead is a registry edit (global invalidation) that also turns K-TIER red until the row is re-read.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: every one of the 19 seeded procedures has a two-reader row whose (id, version, row digest) matches `registries/procedures.toml`, with distinct readers and `reads_evidence` recorded, and K-TIER passes over the pilot's D rows; a comment-only edit of a `procedures.toml` copy leaves every digest unchanged.
- [ ] negative: a version bump in a test copy invalidates the row, and K-TIER fails naming the procedure, both versions and both digests.
- [ ] negative (derived): a `[[parameter]]` or `[[input]]` change in a test copy invalidates the row; a D on a tier-P or tier-A procedure is refused unless it carries the sourced-and-complete population marker (the §2.5 / §9.4 `ledger` exception), and a fixture carrying that marker is admitted; a single-reader row, a row whose two readers are the same id, and a disagreement not resolved to the conservative tier are refused.
- [ ] no-claim: a tier row records two readers' classification of the code at the pinned commit. It does not show that a verdict is filler-invariant at runtime; that is A11a's witness.

title: [cases] A4r: fa-reference differential adapter comparing P first refusals, D cite sets and T folds with the CLI run's
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A4r, §2.6 rule 6, §5.2 (P `reference_verdict`), Appendix Z.4, Z.6.

A P verdict is a first-refusal verdict, and its premises are every attribute the encoding sets (§2.6 rule 6). The plan replaced a hand-maintained kernel-step table (A4k) with this differential, for its lower maintenance cost and its robustness to concurrent edits of `post.rs` (Appendix Z.4). Where `fa-reference`'s `Oracle` models the deciding law, the same intent is also posted to the oracle, and its verdict must equal the kernel's first refusal. The oracle mirrors the kernel's law order with independent constants (`crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1-20`). Dedicated modules model SoD with approver identity, the evidence minimum, naive Lantern procedures and statement rendering, "A4r uses all of them" (§2.6 rule 6; Appendix Z.6 item 5). This serves P (first refusals), D (cite sets) and T (folds) as a second implementation, and it answers the risk "Upstream change silently changes a case" (§17).

## What to build
An adapter in fa-oracles. From a book variant it builds the oracle's inputs and compares the oracle's verdicts, findings and folds with the CLI run's observations (A7a).

**Files and public API** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/Cargo.toml` gains `fa-reference = { path = "../fa-reference", version = "=0.0.1" }` and `fa-time = { path = "../fa-time", version = "=0.0.1" }` (both already in the allowlist A1a writes; fa-reference's API takes `fa_time::DateDay` and `FiscalCalendar`).
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/reference.rs`: `pub struct ReferenceAdapter`, `pub fn ReferenceAdapter::new(case: &Case, variant: &BookVariant) -> Result<Self, LoadError>`, `pub fn p_cell(&mut self, intent: &IntentDef, cell: &Cell, kernel: &Observed) -> RefVerdict`, `pub fn d_cites(&self, procedure: &str, version: u16, live: &[LiveEntry], kernel: &[Cite]) -> RefVerdict`, `pub fn t_fold(&self, read: &TRead, explained: &[ExplainedBalance], kernel: i128) -> RefVerdict`, and `pub enum RefVerdict { Agree, Disagree { reference, kernel }, NotModelled { reason } }`.
- `LiveEntry` is built by the runner from its own run log: every admitted entry (its intent, entry vid, legs, preparer and approvers as recorded), minus Reversal-class entries, entries a live Reversal reverses and entries a live Replacement replaces, which is `snapshot.live_postings()`'s rule (`crates/fa-lantern/src/snapshot.rs:505-513`).

**Oracle set-up.** `fa_reference::Oracle::new(calendar)` (`crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1037`) with a `fa_time::FiscalCalendar` built from the variant's `[book]` and `[[period]]` rows (`FiscalCalendar::custom`, `crates/fa-time/src/calendar.rs:227`); `set_opening_date` (`:1437`), `create_periods` (`:1444`), `add_account` (`:1270`) and `set_account_type` (`:1184`) from `[[account]]`; and the variant's period steps replayed through `Oracle::transition` (`:1532`) in `[[step]]` order, so the oracle's period states at each P cell equal the book's. Unit ids come from `fa_registry::units_embedded()` (`UnitRow.id`). Principals map to the oracle's `u128` identities by the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(`fa:case-principal:v1` ‖ label): any injective map serves, because the oracle compares identities only.

**Field map** (`[[intent]]` → `fa_reference::Intent`, `crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:429-447`):
- `class` → `class`;
- `effective_date` → `date` (`fa_time::DateDay::parse`, `crates/fa-time/src/date.rs:249`);
- `[[leg]]` rows → `legs` (`side`, `account`, `unit` id, `entity`, `mantissa` from `amount_literal` at the unit's scale);
- `idempotency_key` → `key` (for a branch cell, the cell's own key, A7c's `cell_key`, so the oracle's identity law sees the same keys the kernel did and a committed earlier cell never turns a later cell into a replay in either implementation);
- the acting principal's grants → `ops`;
- the count of approvals the intent cites → `approvals`;
- a `target_kind = reverses` target → `reverses` (its journal index);
- a `target_kind = reclassifies` target → the `target` argument of `Oracle::reclassify` (its journal index; below);
- `reason` → `supersession_reason` (the registered code).

`Intent` has no restates or revises target, no allocation and no evidence field; it also has `discriminator`, `resolves` and `settles`, which the map leaves empty. Reclassification, batches, drafts and migration runs are not `Intent` fields but separate `Oracle` entry points (next paragraph).

**Oracle entry points by step** (plan §15 A4r since polish round 4: Reclassification, batches, drafts and migration runs are compared through the oracle's own entry points; the adapter uses each where the case's step maps to it):
- an ordinary intent → `Oracle::post` (`lib.rs:1713`);
- a `reclassifies` intent → `Oracle::reclassify(&intent, target)` (`:2303`; fa-xvba), whose shape refusal is `RECLASSIFICATION_SHAPE` = `FA-REF-185` (`:577`), the refusal W-P-04 expects;
- a filler `PostBatch` chunk (A6, A7c) → `Oracle::post_batch(key, members)` (`:1723`), all or nothing;
- a draft step (W-P-01(a), A8b) → `Oracle::open_draft(name, owner)` (`:1783`), `plan_into_draft(name, planner, &intent)` (`:1811`, which rehearses through `post` only, so the adapter composes `evidence::verdict` for step 1's evidence outcome as in item 3 below) and `promote_draft(name, promoter, ops)` (`:1845`). `promote_draft` checks `approve` (`CAPABILITY` = `FA-REF-011`), then the owner (`SOD` = `FA-REF-008`), then the draft's state, then its contents, which is the kernel's order (`crates/fa-journal/src/draft.rs:990`, `:996-1001`, `:1016-1024`). Its empty-draft refusal is `STRUCTURE` = `FA-REF-100`, where the kernel's is a usage refusal (exit 2, `draft.rs:1022-1024`); the adapter maps that one pair as equivalent and logs both ids. The promoter's `ops` are the route's: the embedded `--as` route implies `approve` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:6090`);
- a `migration` book's steps (A7m) → `Oracle::open_run(&spec, control_key, ops)` (`:3386`, with `RunSpec { key, opening_date, lines, periods, full_detail }`, `:685-691`, built from the derived legacy trial balances), `post_migration(run, &intent)` (`:3510`) per staged chunk, and `finalize_run(run, planned_chunks, control_key, ops, approvals)` (`:3515`). Plan vs code: §15 A4r cites `:3510-3515` for all three; `open_run` is at `:3386`, and only `post_migration` and `finalize_run` sit at `:3510`/`:3515` (checked in the current tree, as in polish round 4).

**Composition, in kernel order.** On a clone of the oracle:
1. The step's entry point above (`Oracle::post` for an ordinary intent) decides the steps it models: balance, period, identity, and period law with its approval count.
2. If it admits, `fa_reference::sod::verdict` (`crates/fa-reference/src/sod.rs:28`) runs over the intent's approvals (`sod::Approval { principal, profile, op }`).
3. Then `fa_reference::evidence::verdict` (`crates/fa-reference/src/evidence.rs:236`) runs over its citations and attestations: the cell's `evidence_attached` value mapped to a document (citation stub, `placeholder:<fact>` reviewed or not) or a ManualAssertion with its reason code.

The first refusal is the reference verdict. The clone replaces the oracle only if all three admit, so the oracle's journal follows the book's admitted history. A `PostBatch` chunk is decided member by member in order on the clone (steps 1–3 with `Oracle::post` for each member), as the kernel admits a batch: the first member's refusal is the chunk's, logged with its member index, and when every member admits, the oracle records the chunk with `post_batch` under the chunk's key, so its identity law sees the batch.

**`not_modelled`** (plan §15 A4r; the list is closed).
- A P cell is `not_modelled` for exactly three reasons: its intent is a case Δ (`restates`/`revises`: the oracle has no case functions; it refuses those classes outside a case, `CASE_MEMBERSHIP` = `FA-REF-178`, but cannot post them inside one), reason `case_delta`; or an allocation (the oracle posts given legs and computes no allocation law), reason `allocation`; or the kernel's order puts an unmodelled first step (an event citation) before the first modelled refusal, reason `unmodelled_first_step`. Every other P cell maps to one of the entry points above; a cell that maps to none is an adapter defect, which fails the row (`disagree`, reference verdict `unmapped`), never a silent `not_modelled`.
- A D target is `not_modelled` when its procedure has no `fa_reference::lantern` function (for example `expense.capitalization`, `ponzi.net_investment`, `events.subsequent` and the graph procedures), reason `no_lantern_function`.
- The runner line prints `ref=not_modelled` (A7a's token); the reason goes into the step record's `reference.reason` and the verdict record.

**D comparison.** Otherwise D cite sets are compared with `fa_reference::lantern::{round_amounts, period_end_timing, post_closing, weekend, self_approved, cutoff, same_same_same, same_same_different, first_digit_counts, relative_size_factor_by_account}` over `lantern::Row` slices (`crates/fa-reference/src/lantern.rs:22-46`) built from the `LiveEntry` list, with each procedure's registered parameter defaults (`round_power`, `window_days`, …) read from `procedures.toml`. For `benford.first_digit` the statistic is compared too: the reference's MAD `benford_mad_1e9` (`lantern.rs:336`, its own literal table) over its digit counts against the procedure's MAD (`mad_1e9`, `crates/fa-lantern/src/digits.rs:48-69`, over `BENFORD_1E9`, `:21-31`, whose last entry FA lowers by one unit so the table sums to 10^9). §9.4's `jet.thin_descriptions`, if OD 2b vendors the row descriptions, compares through `lantern::thin_descriptions` (`lantern.rs:148`). The kernel's cites are projected to (fact, leg ordinal) through A7a's fact↔vid map before comparison.

**T comparison.** T folds are compared with `fa_reference::statements::render` (`crates/fa-reference/src/statements.rs:148`) over the leaf balances the runner read with `fa explain balance --certify` (A11b), so the reference recomputes the line in its own limb arithmetic.

**Verdict per row.** Each row logs `agree`, `disagree` or `not_modelled`. `disagree` is FAIL. `not_modelled` is printed with its reason, never skipped silently and never counted as PASS. A P row passes only when the reference verdict, where modelled, agrees with the kernel's first refusal and with the row's declared `reference_verdict` (§5.2).

## Tests & logging
- **Adapter unit tests** (`crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/reference.rs`, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`), with no binary: on the pilot fixture's native book,
  - `original_into_a_closed_period_is_fa_ref_010_in_the_reference` (W-P-03's cell → `Oracle::post` refuses `FA-REF-010`);
  - `no_evidence_cell_is_fa_ref_080_in_the_reference` and `unreviewed_placeholder_cell_is_fa_ref_086_in_the_reference` (`evidence::verdict`);
  - `reclassification_cell_is_compared_through_oracle_reclassify` (a move back to where the amount came from → `FA-REF-185` in the reference, the kernel's refusal for that shape, `crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:4609` via `fa_palimpsest::validate_reclassification`; a valid move admitted). The binary-level comparison runs where a case carries a Reclassification cell (W5's W-P-04);
  - `owner_promotion_of_a_planned_draft_is_fa_ref_008_in_the_reference` (`open_draft`, `plan_into_draft`, `promote_draft` with the owner as promoter and `approve` in `ops`) and `promotion_without_approve_is_fa_ref_011_in_the_reference`;
  - `migration_chunks_and_finalize_agree_through_the_run_entry_points` (a synthetic one-chunk run: `open_run`, `post_migration`, `finalize_run` admit, and a Migration-class intent sent through `Oracle::post`, outside any run, is `MIGRATION_OUTSIDE_RUN` = `FA-REF-132`, the kernel's code for the same case, `crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1739` at 8196f5e40, catalog row `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:918`). The binary-level comparison runs on A8b's migration book;
  - `benford_statistic_is_compared_through_benford_mad_1e9` (labelled synthetic digit counts; the reference's MAD equals `mad_1e9`'s).
- **Runner-level tests** (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, the `_selftest` case or a runner micro-book, through the real `fa`):
  - P cells decided by `Oracle::post` (`FA-REF-010`) and by `evidence::verdict` (`FA-REF-080`, `FA-REF-086`) log `agree`;
  - a D on `jet.round_amounts` compares cite sets through `fa_reference::lantern::round_amounts`;
  - an `expense.capitalization` target prints `ref=not_modelled` and its verdict record carries `reference.reason = "no_lantern_function"`.
- **Negative from §15.** `planted_wrong_period_state_in_the_adapter_fails`: a test-only hook skips the 2001Q2 `period_close` replay in the oracle. The history soft-closes the period before it closes it, so the oracle decides W-P-03's Original-in-Closed cell in SoftClosed, where Original is `with:post_softclosed` (`registries/admissibility.toml:63-66`): it refuses `FA-REF-011` (`CAPABILITY`, `crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs` refusal constants `:528-585`) when the cell's principal lacks `post_softclosed`, and admits when it holds it. Either differs from the kernel's `FA-REF-010` → `FAIL W-P-03 P native F4/entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Closed refusal=FA-REF-010 exit=7 law=admissibility.toml#Original/Closed ref=disagree … reason=expected ref=agree observed ref=disagree (reference FA-REF-011)` on the pilot's default grants {read, post}; the test asserts the FAIL and logs which verdict the reference gave. E3's `enron_neg_adapter_wrong_state` reuses the hook.
- **Derived negative.** `p_cell_with_no_entry_point_fails_as_unmapped`: a test-only P cell on an intent outside the field map (a settlement, whose `settles` the map leaves empty) → `ref=disagree` with reference verdict `unmapped`, never `not_modelled`.
- **Derived negative.** `not_modelled_is_printed_and_never_counted_as_pass`: a case whose only P row is an allocation cell prints `not_modelled`, and its expectation's verdict is decided by the kernel-side conditions alone, never upgraded by the reference.
- **Logging.** The JSONL step record (§3.5) carries `reference = {verdict, reason?, reference_refusal?}`, with `reason` one of `case_delta`, `allocation`, `unmodelled_first_step`, `no_lantern_function` for `not_modelled` and `unmapped` for an adapter gap. The runner line `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection>` includes the reference component (`ref=agree|disagree|not_modelled`). On FAIL the runner prints the reproduce argv of the kernel side and the reference's verdict.

## Notes
- **Dependencies.** A1b (the book-variant intents, legs, principals and grants the field map reads) and A7a (the run's observations, live postings and kernel refusals to compare against, and the fact↔vid map).
- **Code check at 8196f5e40.** The anchors hold. `Intent` is at `lib.rs:429-447`; it also has `discriminator`, `resolves` and `settles` fields, which the plan's map does not use. `Oracle::post` is at `:1713`, `Oracle::new` at `:1037`, `transition` at `:1532`, `sod::verdict` at `sod.rs:28`, `evidence::verdict` at `evidence.rs:236`, `statements::render` at `statements.rs:148`. All ten `lantern` functions exist, beside others the adapter does not need for the claimed procedures (`sequence_gaps`, `round_trips`, `structuring`, `trace`, `unusual_accounts`, …). Checked in polish round 4: `Oracle::reclassify` `:2303`, `post_batch` `:1723`, `open_draft` `:1783`, `plan_into_draft` `:1811`, `promote_draft` `:1845`, `open_run` `:3386`, `post_migration` `:3510`, `finalize_run` `:3515`, `RunSpec` `:685-691`, the refusal constants `:528-585`; `lantern::benford_mad_1e9` `lantern.rs:336`, `thin_descriptions` `:148`.
- **The allowlist.** These inputs are fa-time types, so fa-oracles' allowlist is `["fa-registry", "fa-reference", "fa-time"]` (plan §3.1 since polish round 2; A1a's topology edit). fa-oracles uses fa-time only at this boundary.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main (the new dependency lines change `Cargo.lock`, a global verdict input), `cargo test -p fa-oracles` and the runner tests.
- **Draft promotion (A8b), settled in polish round 4.** The adapter models it through the oracle's own draft law (`Oracle::promote_draft`, `lib.rs:1845`), not through `sod::verdict`, because the oracle checks the owner directly (`d.owner == promoter` → `SOD`) in the kernel's order. A8b's W-P-01(a) rows therefore expect `ref=agree`.
- **Related beads.** fa-xvba (Reclassification, open, P1) added `Oracle::reclassify` with the kernel's Reclassifies law; a change to either side moves this adapter's Reclassification rows. fa-2ihd (in progress, MaroonCat) is the generated-history differential over the same oracle (fa-registers tests); it shares no code with this adapter (fa-oracles may not import fa-registers), but an oracle fix it lands moves rows here, which are re-observed, never regenerated.
- **Independence.** fa-reference stays independent: the adapter depends on it, never the reverse, and nothing here touches fa-reference's allowlist (`["fa-time", "fa-registry"]`). The reference-boundary step of `scripts/check.sh` (`:536-551`) still passes, because fa-reference's own closure is unchanged.
- **No registry edit** (the allowlist edit is A1a's).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: on the `_selftest` or micro-book cells, every modelled P cell's reference verdict equals the kernel's first refusal and logs `agree` (`FA-REF-010` through `Oracle::post`, `FA-REF-080`/`FA-REF-086` through `evidence::verdict`, `FA-REF-185` through `Oracle::reclassify`, a draft owner's `FA-REF-008` through `Oracle::promote_draft`, and a migration run through `open_run`/`post_migration`/`finalize_run`). A modelled D's cite set equals the run's, and `benford.first_digit`'s MAD equals the reference's `benford_mad_1e9`. Unmodelled targets print `not_modelled` with their reason.
- [ ] negative: a planted disagreement (a wrong period state in the adapter: one `period_close` not replayed into the oracle, so the oracle decides the cell in SoftClosed and gives `FA-REF-011` or admit against the kernel's `FA-REF-010`) fails with `ref=disagree`, printing both verdicts.
- [ ] negative: a `not_modelled` row is printed with one of the closed reasons (`case_delta`, `allocation`, `unmodelled_first_step`, `no_lantern_function`), and is never counted as PASS or skipped silently; a P cell the adapter cannot map fails as `unmapped`, never `not_modelled`.
