title: [cases] A8: WorldCom pilot on the native book (F2, F4, F9, F12): W-D-01, W-D-03, W-N-01, W-P-02 no-evidence cell, W-P-03 Closed cell
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A8, §6.2–§6.4, §18 item 1, §17 ("The program becoming ceremony").

"Phase A ends with a real, reachable pilot (A8) before more machinery" (§17). The harness is the product, and the pilot exercises it on a slice the binary can reach at 8196f5e40 (§18 item 1). WorldCom comes first because it has the densest entry-level record, with D and P together (§18 item 2). The pilot takes four documented entries:
- F4 (2001-07-17, line costs → CIP, $560,000,000 exact at p.26);
- F9 (2001-10-19, line costs → PP&E, $742,725,000);
- F12 (2002-04-12, $718M);
- F2 (2001-04-23/24, OLTA → CIP $402M, asset→asset).

It carries five expectation rows that span the claim types:
- D: W-D-01 `expense.capitalization`, W-D-03 `jet.round_amounts`;
- N: W-N-01;
- P: W-P-02 no-evidence (`FA-REF-080`), W-P-03 Original-in-Closed (`FA-REF-010`).

W-D-01 also exercises the observed-covariate (Rel) path, through F9's minimum-VId fixed-asset leg.

## What to build
**Files.** The pilot case `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/` (case id `worldcom`, `letter = "W"`, the prefix of every WorldCom expectation id, §3.2b and A1a), authored from the A1a–A1c fixture (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/pilot/`) once W1's receipts exist:
- `case.toml` (`kind = "case"`, `claims` = the five rows plus the generated `W-SELF-native`, the declared capabilities, the pinned commit);
- `sources.toml` (SRC-WC-001, with `anchor_scheme = ["page", "line"]`);
- `receipts.toml`, generated by `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify worldcom` from the SRC-WC-001 slice of W1 (receipts for pp.26, 105–116), never hand-edited;
- `facts.toml` for F2, F4, F9 and F12, one sourced fact per sentence, with interpretations joining sentences (F4 joins p.108's description with p.26's exact amount, §6.2), plus their `[[value]]` rows. Fact ids follow W2's scheme (`F<n>` is the fact an intent encodes, `F<n>-p<page>` its other sentences), so W1–W3 extend these files without renaming, and W2 keeps the pilot's rows byte-stable;
- `roles.toml` (role labels such as `gen-acct-manager-1`, the harness roles, and the hashed deny list);
- `books/native.toml`;
- `expectations.toml`;
- the filler variants A11a needs (declared `9…` filler accounts and `filler_batch` steps; the content is A6's).

Each file gets its line in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/embedded.rs`; the runner test is `fn worldcom()` in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs` (named after the directory, §3.2b; `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact worldcom`). All of this is hash-first: no quote text (OD 2a).
- **The native book (§6.3).**
  - Opening date before 2001-01-01, calendar quarters from 2001Q1 (labels mapped to reported codes by A7a).
  - Chart by `role_map` (interpretive): CIP / PP&E / Transmission Equipment / Communications Equipment → `fixed_asset`; line costs → Expense; OLTA → an `Asset`-type account with no role; SG&A → Expense; accruals → `accrued_expense`.
  - Principals are the role labels (F4: `gen-acct-manager-1`).
  - Reporting periods are sourced facts: F2 1Q01, F4 2Q01, F9 3Q01, F12 1Q02.
- **Expectations.**
  - **W-D-01** `expense.capitalization`@2 (tier C):
    - **F4:** cite Sd (sourced account names + `role_map`): the entry, its CIP account and its line-cost credit accounts, the procedure's cite shape (`Cite::Entry`, the capitalizing account, then each credited cost account, `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:1103-1107`); severity S (constant High); statistic Sd `capitalized_expense_amount` = 560,000,000.00 (`statistic_value = 56000000000`, `statistic_scale = 2`) under `one_leg_per_named_account` (one CIP account named; single-source, Beresford pp.26, 108).
    - **F9:** cite Sd for the entry and Rel(account VId order) for the cited fixed-asset account (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:1103-1104`), `rel_rule = min_vid_debit_leg{fixed_asset}` (A5b); severity S; statistic B(leg_split) plus Rel. The value is the debit leg on the minimum-VId fixed-asset account of the entry (`cutoff.rs:1100-1122`), checked on every run from the logged book id, and rendered as the set of documented leg amounts it can take. F9's proposed split is Transmission Equipment $300M + Communications Equipment $442M (= $742M, not the booked amount).
  - **W-D-03** `jet.round_amounts`@1 (tier L, `round_power` 3) on F4, one line per feasible `leg_split` cell (`mmm`, `nnm`, `nmn`, `mnn`, `nnn`, A5a): cite Sd for the entry and its leg 0 (the 560,000,000.00 CIP debit is a multiple of 10^3 units under `one_leg_per_named_account`) and B(leg_split) for the three credit legs 1–3; severity B(leg_split); statistic B(leg_split). Leg ordinals are 0-based: the procedure cites the entry and each round leg by its index in the posted entry (`crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:40-42`, `:105`, `:129-132`), and the runner renders legs in `[[leg]] ordinal` order (A7a), so `(F4,0)` is the CIP debit (W4's spelling).
  - **W-N-01** on F2 (`kind = no_finding`): not cited. Asset→asset moves are outside the predicate (mechanism `cutoff.rs:1066-1124`), with its mutation twin (A11c): F2's credit account retyped Expense, which the procedure must then cite.
  - **W-P-02**, the no-evidence branch on F4: first refusal `FA-REF-080`, exit 3. It is evaluated only in a cell that passes period law and SoD. F4's record-consistent evidence cell is "none named" (§6.4).
  - **W-P-03**, the Original-in-Closed cell (no recorded approvals): `FA-REF-010`, exit 7. The rendering shows "the system's stated remedy" from the catalog's `fix` template (`registries/refusal_catalog.toml:103-108`).
- **D runs.** D procedures read `live_postings`, so they see only admitted cells. Every D target names its admitted cell (K-JOINT, §2.6 rule 7). F4 with no evidence is refused (W-P-02), so W-D-01 and W-D-03 on F4 run on a declared admitted evidence cell. That cell is a reconstruction placeholder: `manual_assertion(InternalTransfer, reconstruction placeholder)` until OD 5 (posted through `fa document attest manual --plan-out`, then `fa commit --plan`, A7a), or `placeholder_reviewed`. Each D renders with that cell named.

## Tests & logging
- **`worldcom`** (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`) evaluates every row through all required witnesses:
  - filler invariance over 5 seeded + empty + extremal variants and ≥ 2 runs (A11a);
  - the mutation twin for W-N-01 (A11c);
  - the dry-run sweep and committed representatives for the P cells (A7c);
  - the reference differential: `fa_reference::lantern::round_amounts` for W-D-03, `Oracle::post` for W-P-03, `evidence::verdict` for W-P-02; W-D-01 is `not_modelled` (A4r);
  - finding export/replay for D reads, and `fa verify book` (A12).
- **The offline gate.** `ledgers_validate_offline` (A10a) runs the load-time checks on the pilot's real receipts; every check prints PASS with `examined > 0` except those whose input kind the pilot lacks (K-TAUT, K-ORACLE, K-VINTAGE: no T rows), which print UNRUN.
- **Negatives (§15).** Each must FAIL. §15's "must FAIL, then be restored before landing" is kept as a stronger, permanent form: each is a `worldcom_neg_<slug>` test over a `run_planted` temp copy of `cases/worldcom/` (A7a), which calls `.expect_err(…)` and asserts the line; the committed files are never edited, so the negative is observed on every run (`cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- worldcom_neg_`):
  - `worldcom_neg_w_d_01_fails_when_f4_debit_moves_one_minor_unit`, two planted copies in one test (A7a's "Where a plant stops"):
    1. **Run time (§15's observable).** F4's CIP debit and its first line-cost credit, both re-ruled `amount_rule = "synthetic"` with their literals moved +0.01 (still balanced; one `run_planted` call with two edits). No load check recomputes a synthetic leg, so the copy loads and runs, the kernel posts 560,000,000.01, and the procedure's statistic moves: `FAIL W-D-01 D native F4/<admitted cell> … statistic=Sd:capitalized_expense_amount=560000000.01 reason=expected 560000000.00 observed 560000000.01`;
    2. **Load time.** The same +0.01 under the CIP debit's own `value:F4#…` rule (W3). K-DERIVE recomputes the rule against the literal at load (A3a), so no book is built and every line reads FAIL with the load failure, which names K-DERIVE and F4's CIP leg: the edit a hand-moved amount would make is caught before the binary runs.

    W4 adds a third copy to the same test (W-D-01/F4's expected `statistic_value` moved one minor unit, a run-time exactness check on the expectation side);
  - `worldcom_neg_w_n_01_fails_when_f2_credit_account_is_retyped_expense` → the procedure cites F2, `FAIL W-N-01`;
  - `worldcom_neg_w_p_03_fails_without_the_period_close_step`: the 2001Q2 `period_close` step removed, together with that period's `period_soft_close` step (two edits in one copy). With only the close removed, the period stays SoftClosed and the cell is decided there (`registries/admissibility.toml:63-66`, Original/SoftClosed `with:post_softclosed`): `FA-REF-011` without that op, admit with it, which would make the observable depend on the cell's grants. With both removed the period stays Open, so the post is admitted, as §15 states → `FAIL W-P-03 P native F4/entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Closed … reason=expected FA-REF-010 observed admit`. The later rows that need 2001Q2 closed fail too; the test asserts the W-P-03 line.
- **Expected lines** (A7a's notation, one line per (expectation, target, cell)): `PASS W-D-01 D native F4/<admitted cell> expense.capitalization@2 cite=Sd:[F4,<CIP code>,<line-cost codes>] severity=S:High statistic=Sd:capitalized_expense_amount=560000000.00 ref=not_modelled`; `PASS W-D-01 D native F9/leg_split=… … cite=Sd:[F9]+Rel:min_vid_debit_leg{fixed_asset} statistic=B+Rel:<debit on the min-VId fixed-asset account>` (one line per `leg_split` cell); one line per A5a `leg_split` cell over the credit ordinals 1–3 (`m` a multiple of 10^3 units, `n` not): `PASS W-D-03 D native F4/leg_split=mmm jet.round_amounts@1 cite=Sd:[F4,(F4,0)]+B:[(F4,1),(F4,2),(F4,3)] severity=B:Medium statistic=B:round_legs=4 ref=agree`; `PASS W-D-03 D native F4/leg_split=nnm … cite=Sd:[F4,(F4,0)]+B:[(F4,3)] severity=B:Low statistic=B:round_legs=2`, likewise `nmn` (`B:[(F4,2)]`) and `mnn` (`B:[(F4,1)]`); and `PASS W-D-03 D native F4/leg_split=nnn … cite=Sd:[F4,(F4,0)] severity=B:Low statistic=B:round_legs=1`. A single non-multiple credit is infeasible (A5a), and the count classes (`all_multiples`, `two_non_multiples`, `three_non_multiples`) appear only in A5a's `ENUM` log, never as cell keys; `PASS W-N-01 N native F2/default expense.capitalization@2 kind=no_finding twin=reported`; `PASS W-P-02 P native F4/evidence_attached=none refusal=FA-REF-080 exit=3 law=evidence_policy.toml#Original ref=agree matrix=n/a fix_argv=n/a alternatives=n/a`; `PASS W-P-03 P native F4/entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Closed refusal=FA-REF-010 exit=7 law=admissibility.toml#Original/Closed ref=agree matrix=ok fix_argv=ok alternatives=ok`; and the generated `PASS W-SELF-native …`. The structured-remedy tokens follow A7a's rule: `FA-REF-010`'s site sets the {Closed, Original} matrix and its fix ends with the placeholder-free `fa period list --json` (`crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2844`, `:2860-2863` at 8196f5e40), so all three checks run; `FA-REF-080`'s site sets no matrix and its fix names only `fa document add <file> --kind <Kind> --json`, whose placeholders keep `fix.argv` null (`crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:1191-1195`; `crates/fa-cli/src/refusal_object.rs:19-22`), so all three print `n/a`.
- **Logging.** Per row, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses>`; on FAIL the `REPRODUCE` argv; the JSONL log (§3.5) with each run's `book_id`, from which W-D-01/F9's Rel component is recomputed with `fa_model::account_vid`; `LOG <path>` at the end. With `FA_CASES_LOG_DIR` set, the log is copied as `worldcom.jsonl` for the renderer (A14).

## Notes
- **Dependencies.**
  - A8a: the harness passes its own self-test first.
  - A2, A3a, A3b, A3c: derivations and load-time checks.
  - A4r: the reference differential.
  - A5b: statuses, K-BRANCH, K-PRED and K-JOINT.
  - A7c: the dry-run cell sweep.
  - A9: `case_fetch.py` produces the receipts.
  - A10a: the offline ledger test.
  - A11a, A11c: the filler-invariance witness and mutation twins.
  - A12: outsider verification of D reads.
  - W1: the SRC-WC-001 slice, receipts for pp.26, 105–116, verified by the author and re-verified by a second agent with a second cache (§4.5).
- **Owner decisions.**
  - The pilot also waits on OD 5 (`NotInPublicRecord`, H14) or the recorded `InternalTransfer` choice, which is not a work item and so not in `deps`.
  - OD 2a (quote text) does not gate the pilot, which is hash-first.
  - OD 3 gates neither the pilot nor W1 (§14 item 3).
  - OD 4 gates rendered wording (A14), not this item.
- **Rows the pilot carries beyond §15's list.**
  - The runner (A7a) generates the self-disclosure row `W-SELF-native` for the pilot's book (§2.7): `jet.self_sourced_evidence` cites every posting that cites a reviewed citation stub, at severity Medium (`about = "reconstruction"`). It renders first in "How this book was built".
  - A16's probe generates the guidance N `W-N-90` for the case (§12.5).
  - §2.7 also makes the finding → source review normative after each D run (`fa finding review F:<vid> --action acknowledge --note <template> --evidence D:<fact stub>` by `case-second-reader`; R row: each such finding carries exactly one review, whose evidence is its entry's stub; no finding that cites only filler carries one). If the pilot's book does not declare those R rows, they arrive with W4.
- **fa-4psc.** W-D-01's rendered clause is `planted` (`expense.capitalization`) and W-D-03's is `corpus` (`jet.round_amounts`). If fa-4psc recalibrates either procedure, the clause and the A4 tier row change (§12.4).
- **Trailers.** After landing, removing a pilot expectation needs a `Retired-tests:` trailer, and weakening one (fewer cites, a branch where there was a single verdict) needs a `Weakened-tests:` trailer (§16).
- **README.** `_selftest` is never rendered, so the pilot's `cases/worldcom/README.md` is the first rendered README; whichever of A8 and A14 lands second renders and commits it.
- **Shared files.** W1–W9 extend the same `cases/worldcom/` files; the pilot's book uses W3's harness labels (`case-second-reader`, `case-closer-1` for period steps) so W3 extends rather than replaces it.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases -- worldcom`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the case data. Removing or weakening a pilot row needs the §16 trailers.
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: W-D-01 PASS on F4 (cite Sd, severity S High, statistic Sd = 560,000,000.00 under `one_leg_per_named_account`) and on F9 (cite Sd; the cited fixed-asset account Rel, equal on every run to the debit leg on the minimum-VId fixed-asset account computed from the logged book id; statistic per its B(leg_split) cells). This holds on every filler variant (5 seeded + empty + extremal) across ≥ 2 runs.
- [ ] positive: W-D-03 PASS on F4 (cite Sd; severity and statistic match their B(leg_split) branch cells); W-N-01 PASS on F2 (no finding from a run with no refusal and no error, and its mutation twin reports).
- [ ] positive: W-P-02's no-evidence cell on F4 has first refusal `FA-REF-080` (exit 3) in a cell that passes period law and SoD, and W-P-03's Original-in-Closed cell has first refusal `FA-REF-010` (exit 7). Each matches the catalog exit, the structured remedy and the reference verdict.
- [ ] positive: `cases/worldcom/receipts.toml` is the output of `case_fetch.py verify worldcom` (pp.26, 105–116), and `ledgers_validate_offline` passes on it; the case's `#[test]` is `worldcom`.
- [ ] negative: moving F4's debit by one minor unit fails W-D-01's statistic (a synthetic-ruled copy that runs, `observed 560000000.01`; the same move under its `value:` rule is refused at load by K-DERIVE); retyping F2's credit account as Expense fails W-N-01; removing the 2001Q2 `period_close` step (with its `period_soft_close`, so the cell is decided in Open, not in SoftClosed where the grants would decide) makes W-P-03 fail with an admitted post. Each is observed as FAIL by a permanent `worldcom_neg_<slug>` test over a temp copy of the case (A7a's `run_planted`); the committed case is never edited.
- [ ] no-claim: the pilot shows that registered predicates hold, and named refusals occur, on our encoding of four documented entries over N variants. It shows nothing about WorldCom's actual ledger, false-positive rates on real books, or what any control would have prevented.

title: [cases] A8b: F6 pilot: W-P-01(a) draft self-promotion FA-REF-008 with W-P-01-CF-01 on native, and W-D-02 on the migration book
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A8b, §6.2 (F6), §6.4 (W-P-01, W-D-02), §0.4 (H-011), Appendix Z.6 item 1.

F6 (2001-08-22, CIP $544M → asset clearing → "10 assets in the amount of exactly $54.4 million each" under Fiber Optic Cable, Beresford p.111) is the record's one documented approval, and the program's model case for an Si component. Under the natural reading of p.111, "Abide rarely entered and approved entries himself so his involvement in these transfers was unusual", the director both entered and approved the transfers. On that reading the 2001-08-22 transfers have a `FA-REF-008` branch, which is why H-011 ("WorldCom P collapses to forced attribution") was refuted (§0.4). The P claim is reachable at 8196f5e40 through draft self-promotion (W-P-01(a)), with no A0 needed. Promotion attaches no Approval to the promoted entries, so the detection side (W-D-02, `jet.self_approved`) needs the migration book (A7m). This item delivers one P with its CF row and one D. Both are conditional on the interpretation, and the rendering says so.

## What to build
- **F6 facts.**
  - The sourced p.111 sentences.
  - The `interpretation` that the director both entered and approved the 2001-08-22 transfers: `from` the sourced facts, with `reader`, `second_reader` and `rationale` (§2.1). Two independent readers are required for Si.
  - F6 is encoded as two intents (§6.2):
    - **F6a**: CIP → clearing, $544M. Class branch Original / Adjusting / Reclassification split per target.
    - **F6b**: clearing → ten items; class `Allocation` via `fa allocate`.
- **Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/` gains the F6 facts and values (W2's ids: the encoded fact `F6`, intents `F6a` and `F6b`), the interpretation row, the W-P-01, W-P-01-CF-01 and W-D-02 expectations, and `books/migration.toml` (the A7m fixture shape with the real F6 facts and the F6 chunks' legacy attribution: a sole-source FullDetail run, its derived per-period legacy trial balances filed as one `stub_of = "legacy_tb"` document that every chunk cites, A7m; shared with W3, Notes), each with its line in `src/cases/embedded.rs`; `cases/worldcom/case.toml` adds W-P-01-CF-01 and W-D-02 to `claims`; W-P-01 joins `claims` with W5, once W5's probe settles its `manual_assertion` cell and W5 deletes that cell's `pending` field (below), because a claimed row that prints UNRUN fails the case (A7a) and the loader refuses a `pending` cell on a claimed expectation (`PendingClaimed`, A1c). A claim never excludes a cell (§5.1), so deleting `pending` is the only way W-P-01 becomes claimable. The runner rows run inside `fn worldcom()` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`), the draft steps in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/drafts.rs`.
- **W-P-01(a)** on the native book: `approval_encoding = draft_self_promotion`, F6a only (drafts refuse Allocation, `crates/fa-journal/src/draft.rs:759-767`). It is the sequence `fa draft new <d> --as property-accounting-director-1`, then `fa post --intent <F6a cell>.json --draft <d> --as property-accounting-director-1 [--grant <op>]… [--evidence <oid>]` (the `--grant` ops are the cell's `capability_grants`, §2.6), then `fa draft promote <d> --as property-accounting-director-1 --yes` by the director (the draft's owner). No `--grant` is passed (next paragraph).
  - **The promoter's op.** `draft-promote`'s `preparer_op` is `approve` (`registries/sod_policy.toml:564-573`), checked before any read (`draft.rs:394-422`, called at `:990`). On the embedded `--as` route the CLI implies it: the promote handler asks for `ctx.capability(args, &["approve"])` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:6090`), and `capability` adds the handler's implied ops on the explicit embedded-owner route only (`cli.rs:1173-1185`; a launch-bound session reuses its launch capability verbatim). So the director's promotion reaches the owner check with no `--grant`, and `FA-REF-011` arises only under an issued token that lacks `approve` (§6.4, PLAN_DELTA after polish round 3; this replaces the earlier `--grant approve` requirement). The rendering names the route (embedded `--as`, which implies `approve`).
  - **Step 1** (`plan_into_draft`) accepts only batchable classes: Original, Adjusting, Reversal, Pending and Resolution (`draft.rs:759-767`; `crates/fa-journal/src/batch.rs:389-399`). On the Reclassification branch step 1 refuses with a usage error (exit 2).
  - Step 1 rehearses the intent, with no approvals, through the whole posting pipeline (`draft.rs:863-870`). So period law and the evidence minimum decide it first:
    - in Closed or Locked, an Original is refused `FA-REF-010`;
    - with no admitting evidence the refusal is `FA-REF-080` or `FA-REF-086`;
    - where period law requires an op, the cell's `capability_grants` decide (`registries/admissibility.toml:64-66`, Original in SoftClosed `with:post_softclosed`; `:238-240`, Adjusting in Closed `with:post_closed,1`): without the op the refusal is `FA-REF-011` (exit 7); an Original in SoftClosed with `post_softclosed` is admitted; an Adjusting in Closed with `post_closed` is refused `FA-REF-012` (exit 7), because the rehearsal carries no approval (the request builder's empty approvals, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:8230`; `crates/fa-journal/src/plan.rs:105-122`). So no Closed cell is an admitted cell of this encoding.

    On these cells the entry's first refusal is step 1's, and that is the cell's verdict.
  - **Step 2, the owner check.** The owner check (`draft.rs:996-1001`) runs before the empty-draft check (`:1016-1024`), so the owner's promotion is refused `FA-REF-008` (exit 7) under `sod_policy.toml#draft-promote` (`crates/fa-policy/src/denial.rs:167-181`) on every cell, whether or not step 1 put anything in the draft. Only on an admitted cell (Original or Adjusting in an admitting state, with `placeholder_reviewed` evidence; the `manual_assertion` cell waits on W5's probe, below) is that refusal about the documented entry. On a cell step 1 refused, the runner logs the empty draft's `FA-REF-008` as a step outcome but does not count it as the entry's verdict.
  - **Plan and code agree (polish round 2).** §6.4 now states the code's order: step 2 admits the capability (`draft.rs:990`; on the embedded `--as` route the CLI implies `approve`, so `FA-REF-011` arises only under an issued token without `approve`), then checks the owner (`draft.rs:996-1001`) before the draft's contents (`:1002-1024`, the empty-draft usage refusal at `:1022-1024`). So the owner's promotion of even an empty draft is `FA-REF-008`, counted as the transfer's refusal only on admitted cells and logged elsewhere; a promoter who is not the owner reaches the usage refusal.
  - **Locked is record-inconsistent, not excluded.** The sourced booking-before-filing facts exclude Locked at commit (§6.3), so the Locked cells (step 1 refuses an Original or Adjusting there with `FA-REF-010`) carry `record_consistent = false`: they are evaluated and rendered as such, never summarized, and they only constrain the branch set (§6.4; A5a, A5b, A7c).
  - **ManualAssertion under a draft (W5's probe).** A ManualAssertion is bound to the proposal digest it was recorded over (`crates/fa-journal/src/attestation.rs:433`; the kernel point-reads it by the posted proposal's digest, `crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:1367-1381`), and `fa document attest manual` takes only `--intent` at 8196f5e40, planning for trunk with `--plan-out` (§3.3). `fa draft plan <name> --intent <file> [--evidence <oid>]…` and `fa post --draft` re-parse the intent, which reseals it (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:8137`), and neither takes an assertion (`registries/verbs.toml`, `draft plan` usage). Whether an assertion can cover an intent planned into a draft is probed by W5 (§15 W5). Until that probe passes, W-P-01(a)'s admitted evidence cell is `placeholder_reviewed` only, and the `manual_assertion` cell is authored with `pending = "W5: ManualAssertion over a draft-planned intent"` (A1c's pending-cell field), so it prints `UNRUN … step1=<observed refusal> reason=needs:W5 (ManualAssertion over a draft-planned intent)` (A7a's serialization puts `reason=` last), its step 1 still run and its observed refusal logged, while it keeps its authored expected verdict for W5 to compare (PLAN_DELTA after polish round 3). That UNRUN line, and the loader's `PendingClaimed` refusal, are why W-P-01 is not in `claims` until W5 deletes the field; every other W-P-01 cell is evaluated, and a FAIL in any of them fails the case even unclaimed (A7a). A0's review form of `attest manual` serves trunk posts (W5b, E3b), not drafts.
- **W-P-01-CF-01.** The same transfer with no approval attached passes SoD. Step 5b then decides on `evidence_attached`: `FA-REF-080` with none; admitted with a document or a ManualAssertion (a reconstruction placeholder, §2.7). That holds on the cells period law admits without an approval; in a Closed or Locked cell period law decides first (`FA-REF-010`, `-011` or `-012`, as in step 1 above), and that is the cell's line. It renders as "if ⟨attribute⟩ were ⟨value⟩ …", and it is also the weaker reading ("entered only") rendered beside the Si component.
- **Reading and scope.**
  - The claim is conditional on the `interpretation` that the director approved these transfers (p.111's "so" clause, the natural reading), rendered "under the reading ⟨rationale⟩".
  - On the weaker reading, `approvals_recorded` is a branch, and the no-approval cell is CF-01.
  - Scope: the director's transfers only (F6a, F6b).
- **W-D-02** on the migration book (A7m fixture shape, real F6 facts): `jet.self_approved` (tier L) on F6's entries attributed to the property-accounting director, one `[[target]]` per F6 chunk entry (`F6a` and `F6b`, intent ids as D subjects, A1c), since the procedure reports one finding per entry (`crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:360-410`). It does not cover the specialist's $0.2M entry (F7). The cell is `approval_encoding = migration_legacy_pair`, `approvals_recorded = {approved_by = entered_by = property-accounting-director-1}`. Statuses:
  - cite **B(approvals_recorded)**. The record states the approval only as a habit (p.111), pp.260–261 credit the ten entries to "Abide and his staff", and the procedure fires only on the branch "legacy entered-by = approved-by", a declared encoding resting on an `interpretation`;
  - severity S (constant High) on that branch;
  - statistic Sd on that branch: `own_approvals` = 1, the legacy self-pair counted once (`jet.rs:360-410`: a legacy pair whose entered-by equals its approved-by adds 1, and the chunks carry no recorded Approval).

## Tests & logging
- **Runner rows** in `worldcom` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`):
  - W-P-01(a) per branch cell. Step 1 is a real `fa post --draft` per cell (a draft plan journals into the draft, so A7c's dry-run rule does not apply), one fresh draft per cell (`W-P-01-<cell key>`), with the promotion attempted on each;
  - W-P-01-CF-01 (the same F6a cells posted to trunk with no approval, by A7c's dry-run sweep);
  - W-D-02 on the finalized migration book, through filler invariance (A11a) on the L-tier discipline;
  - the reference differential (A4r): W-P-01(a)'s cells through the oracle's draft entry points, `Oracle::open_draft` / `plan_into_draft` / `promote_draft` (`crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1783`, `:1811`, `:1845`; `promote_draft` checks `approve`, then the owner (`FA-REF-008`), then the draft's state and contents, the kernel's order), with `evidence::verdict` composed for step 1's evidence outcome because `plan_into_draft` rehearses through `Oracle::post` only; W-P-01-CF-01 through `Oracle::post`, `sod::verdict` and `evidence::verdict`; `fa_reference::lantern::self_approved` for W-D-02's cite set over the finalized migration book's live rows. A cell the adapter cannot map prints `not_modelled` with its reason, never skipped.
- **Derived negatives**, permanent `worldcom_neg_<slug>` tests over `run_planted` temp copies of `cases/worldcom/` (as A8's are; each calls `.expect_err(…)`, A7a):
  - `worldcom_neg_w_p_01a_fails_when_a_non_owner_promotes`: the promoter set to `case-approver-1` → the admitted cell promotes, no `FA-REF-008`, `FAIL W-P-01`;
  - `worldcom_neg_w_d_02_fails_when_approved_by_differs_from_entered_by` → no finding, `FAIL W-D-02`;
  - `worldcom_neg_w_d_02_fails_before_migrate_finalize` (the `migrate_finalize` step removed) → no finding (A7m's negative), `FAIL W-D-02`;
- **Companion CLI test for the promoter's route** (in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/drafts.rs`, beside the draft steps; not a case row): `draft_promote_under_a_token_without_approve_is_refused_fa_ref_011`: the director opens and plans a draft on the embedded route, an issuer issues the director a token without `approve` (`fa capability issue --holder property-accounting-director-1 --profile human --op post --out <tok> --as <issuer> --grant issue_capability`, `registries/verbs.toml:203`), and `fa --token <tok> --book <dir> draft promote <d>` is refused `FA-REF-011` (exit 7) before the owner check. On the CLI no token session can hold `approve`: `LaunchAuthority::from_token` refuses a token granting any op beyond the Agent or Preparer launch ceiling (`crates/fa-cli/src/authority.rs:167-179`; its unit test refuses a token granting `approve`, `:693-695`; lines read in the working tree, whose copy of the file was last written 2026-10-20, before 8196f5e40), so the token route always reaches `FA-REF-011` at `draft.rs:990`, and an issued Human token carrying `approve` is refused at launch, not at promotion; the same promotion on the embedded `--as` route with no `--grant` reaches `FA-REF-008`. The test records the observed refusal and exit of both calls. It documents why the encoding names the embedded route (§6.4), replacing the earlier planted negative that removed `--grant approve`.
- **Logging.** Per row, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses>` (one line per (expectation, target, cell), A7a), including the step-1 outcome and the promotion outcome of each cell (`step1=<id|admit> promote=<id>`). The JSONL log (§3.5) has the draft name, the promotion step and the migration steps.

## Notes
- **Dependencies.** A7m (the migration fixture and its finalize visibility), A8 (the WorldCom pilot case, its native book, sources and receipts; the W1 slice covers p.111 within pp.105–116), A11a (filler invariance for W-D-02).
- **No A0 here.** W-P-01(b), the `entry_approval` encoding, is W5 (on F6b, probing `fa allocate --approval <self vid>`) and W5b (on F6a, ← A0). W-P-04 (F6a as one Reclassification → `FA-REF-185`) is W5's.
- **Interpretation readers.** The `interpretation` needs two independent readers, coordinated through Agent Mail. Each records their id; neither copies the other's rationale.
- **Owner decisions.** OD 3 gates the post-OD-2a quote text of the F6 quote (Beresford p.111), because it contains a name. Under hash-first vendoring no quote text is committed, so OD 3 does not gate this item (§14 item 3). The record-consistent placeholder cell uses `InternalTransfer` until OD 5 (H14).
- **fa-z46b.** The director's own promotion is a single-principal act, and fa-z46b keeps single-principal operations working under the embedded posture. The migration stage's two approvals (A7m) must come from distinct key holders once it lands.
- **fa-s7x (drafts and promotion, open, P1)** owns the draft life cycle W-P-01(a) runs on. Its plan text has states Open → Submitted → Promoted|Rejected|Abandoned and "Agent-profile capabilities may create/add/submit, never promote"; the code at 8196f5e40 promotes from Open with the owner check first (`draft.rs:986-1024`; FA-INV-10.self-promotion is live, per fa-s7x's 2026-10-22 comment). If fa-s7x lands a Submitted state or another promotion precondition, step 2's first refusal can move, and W-P-01(a)'s expected lines are re-observed then, never regenerated. No other bead plans the F6 encodings; A8b and W5 carry them.
- **fa-xvba (Reclassification, open, P1)** made Reclassification postable on trunk (`fa reclass`); drafts still refuse it at step 1 (`draft.rs:759-767`), which is the Reclassification branch's usage refusal here. If drafts start accepting Reclassification, that branch's expected line changes.
- **Shared `books/migration.toml` with W3.** A8b and W3 both author this file, and plan §15 names no edge between them (A8b ← A7m, A8, A11a; W3 ← W2, A1b, A5a, A7m), so either may land first. A8b's version holds what W-D-02 needs: the `[book]`, the Historical periods and principals the F6 chunks name, the accounts of F6a's and F6b's legs, the run intent and its `legacy_tb` document (A7m), F6a's and F6b's chunks with their legacy attribution, and the open, stage and finalize steps. W3's holds every F1–F13 chunk. As W3's Notes say, whichever lands second extends the other's file: it keeps the ids `F6a` and `F6b`, the attribution `source_entered_by = source_approved_by = property-accounting-director-1` on the `migration_legacy_pair` cell, and the existing step order, and it re-derives the legacy trial balances with `legacy_tb_from_chunks` over every chunk then in the file (never hand-merging the declared lines), so finalize's tie-out still holds; W-D-02's lines stay byte-identical across the merge.
- **Rendering.** The rendering names the Si reading and shows CF-01 beside W-P-01. It never says WorldCom's controls would have prevented anything (§0.3 wording rules).
- **Expected lines** (A7a's notation): `PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=draft_self_promotion,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Open,evidence_attached=placeholder_reviewed refusal=FA-REF-008 exit=7 law=sod_policy.toml#draft-promote ref=agree matrix=n/a fix_argv=n/a alternatives=n/a step1=admit promote=FA-REF-008` (the SoD denial cites `sod_policy.toml#draft-promote`, sets no matrix, and its fix names only `fa approve --proposal <digest> --as <approver> --json`, whose placeholders keep `fix.argv` null: `crates/fa-policy/src/denial.rs:343-351`, `:390-392`, current tree; A7a's rule); on a step-1 cell, `… refusal=FA-REF-010 … step1=FA-REF-010 promote=FA-REF-008`; on the assertion cell, `UNRUN W-P-01 P native F6a/…,evidence_attached=manual_assertion(InternalTransfer) step1=<observed> reason=needs:W5 (ManualAssertion over a draft-planned intent)`; `PASS W-D-02 D migration F6a/approval_encoding=migration_legacy_pair,approvals_recorded=entered_by=approved_by jet.self_approved@1 cite=B:[F6a] severity=S:High statistic=Sd:own_approvals=1` and the same line for `F6b` (W4's spelling); the cells `approved_by ≠ entered_by` and no legacy approver print `no finding`.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- worldcom`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the case data.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: W-P-01(a): on every cell that step 1 admits (F6a as Original or Adjusting in an admitting state with `placeholder_reviewed` evidence), the owner's `fa draft promote` on the embedded `--as` route (which implies `approve`; no `--grant`) is refused `FA-REF-008` (exit 7) citing `sod_policy.toml#draft-promote`, and the reference differential agrees. The other cells give their first refusals at step 1: Reclassification → usage (exit 2); Original in Closed → `FA-REF-010`; no admitting evidence → `FA-REF-080`/`FA-REF-086`. On those cells the owner's promotion of the empty draft is also refused `FA-REF-008` (the owner check precedes the empty-draft check, `draft.rs:996-1001` before `:1016-1024`), and the runner logs it without counting it as the entry's verdict. title: [cases] A9: tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py (fetch, extract, xbrl-facts, verify into receipts.toml) and the fa-oracles #[test] running its unittests
description:
## Why

A facts file is accepted only with a receipt from `case_fetch.py verify` run by its author, and its review re-runs `verify` independently: a second agent, with a second cache (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §4.5). That rule exists because the research workspace is not a source: the research record contained quotes that occur in no stored source (EV-040: 0 hits in 22 stored texts), account ids not in the texts, a procedure name that does not exist (`cutoff.late_posting`) and a misattributed scope (SEC ¶29) (§4.5, Appendix Z.3). The tool is Python and lives outside the Rust workspace for the plan's three reasons (§4.4): it needs an HTTP client, which would be a new third-party dependency in a closed universe; it runs only at authoring time; and its outputs, the receipts, are reviewable data that the offline Rust validator checks, so nothing in a test depends on the network or on the tool's code. Under hash-first vendoring (§1.3) the receipt, not committed quote text, is what binds a vendored fact to source bytes before owner decision 2a. Every claim type (D/P/T/C/R/N/CF, §0.3) rests on it, because every expectation's basis must contain at least one sourced fact (K-BASIS) and every sourced fact needs a receipt (A10a).

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here):
- `tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py`: Python 3 standard library only (≥ 3.11, for `tomllib`, as `scripts/foundation_check.py` already requires), run with `python3 -B`, following `scripts/foundation_check.py:1-20` (§4.4). Subcommands below; `--help` prints usage.
- `tools/case-fetch/test_case_fetch.py`: the stdlib `unittest` suite.
- `tools/case-fetch/fixtures/`: the fixture documents the tests verify against (a small text extraction, a small HTML page, a small XBRL instance), each written for the test, with a matching fixture `sources.toml`/`facts.toml`. Their sentences are synthetic or quote only phrases the plan itself quotes, and contain no real names (OD 3).
- `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_fetch.rs`: the gate `#[test]` (below).
- `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_fetch.sha256`: one `<sha256>  <path>` line per file under `tools/case-fetch/` (the pin, below).

**Inputs.** `<case>` on the command line is a case directory name under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/` (§3.2b: `worldcom`, `xbrl`, `enron`, `lehman`, `blmis`, `mergers`), or a path to a case directory (any argument containing `/`), so an author's authoring-time negatives can run `verify <temp copy>` on an edited copy (W2) without touching the committed case. The tool reads and writes only inside that directory; the cache and the contact rules are the same either way. `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<case>/sources.toml` rows (§4.1: `id`, `title`, `publisher`, `original_url`, `archive_url?`, `retrieval_route` ∈ {`original`, `archive_capture`, `third_party_copy`, `re_render`}, `original_hash_compared`, `retrieved_utc`, `sha256`, `format`, `extraction`, `redistribution_basis`, `assertion_status`, `assurance`, `anchor_scheme` naming the anchor kinds its facts use (`page{printed page, line range}`, `line{range}`, `table_cell{table, row label, column label}`, `xbrl{concept, context id}`, `paragraph{¶ number}`, and A1a's `exhibit{label, page range}` for a whole table of rows, which M2t's `verify` extension handles), `status` = `OK` | `BLOCKED`, `notes`) and the case's `facts.toml` sourced facts with their `[[value]]` rows (§2.1, A1a's field names and anchor grammar), read with `tomllib`. Each case's facts may cite only `OK` rows.

**Subcommands (§4.4).** (`exhibit-b` is item M2t's, not this one.)
- `fetch <case> [--source <id>]`: downloads each `OK` source by its `retrieval_route` with `urllib.request`, and prints `SKIP <id> BLOCKED <status_reason>` for each `BLOCKED` row; with `--source <id>` it fetches that one row whatever its status, so an author can read a `BLOCKED` candidate (W1's SEC v. Abide row) under the tool's own rules instead of by hand. A row with no recorded `sha256` (an unread candidate) is stored in the cache and printed as `FETCHED <id> sha256=<hex> fetched_utc=<t> unverified`, for the author to record in `sources.toml`; it is never reported as a verified match and never gets a receipt. In every mode it sends the project's User-Agent `franken_accounting-agent (+https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_accounting)`; keeps to at most 1 request per second; verifies each SHA-256; stores the bytes in the cache `$FA_CASES_CACHE` (default `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/franken_accounting/cases/<sha256>`, §4.3) with a sidecar recording the fetch time. Direct sec.gov requests are made only when `FA_SEC_CONTACT` is set, which is then appended to the User-Agent; the variable is read from the environment only and is never written to any committed file, receipt, log or fixture (§1.2, OD 1).
- `extract <case>`: PDF via `pdftotext -layout` when installed (a system tool used only by this authoring tool, never by shipped code); HTML/XML via a stdlib tag-stripper (`html.parser`) whose algorithm version (`case-fetch-strip-v1`) is recorded. The `extraction` field records tool + version + SHA-256 of the extracted text.
- `xbrl-facts <case>`: from an XBRL instance, extracts (concept, context id, period, unit, decimals, dimension members, value) rows for the facts a case cites, each anchored by instance line. `verify` uses the same rows: an `xbrl` fact binds only if its value, its `precision` (A1a: the power of ten of the stated precision, so `decimals="-3"` is precision 3, and `decimals="INF"` matches only the unit's minor unit) and its `cell`'s `:<member>` suffix (A1a: the member in `cell` is the pairing key, X1's and C0's form; no suffix means an undimensioned context) all equal the instance fact's value, `decimals` and explicit dimension member. A difference in any of the three sets `values_in_quote = false` and prints a `FAIL ` line naming which (C0's authoring-time negatives: wrong `decimals`, missing member). Lines come from `xml.parsers.expat`'s `CurrentLineNumber` (ElementTree keeps none). The instance (or the HTML table) is the T oracle, never the companyfacts API, which drops dimensional facts (§1.2).
- `verify <case>`: for every sourced fact (a fact citing a `BLOCKED` source fails, since facts may cite only `OK` rows, §4.1):
  - **Locating the quote.** Until OD 2a allows committed quote text, a fact carries only `quote_sha256` and its anchor. `verify` enumerates the sentence-aligned spans at the anchor in the normalized extraction and selects the one span whose SHA-256 matches; zero or several matches is a FAIL (§4.4). When the quote text is present it is searched directly.
  - **Prose anchors** (`page`, `line`, `paragraph`): the quote occurs **sentence-aligned** and **exactly once** in the extraction at the anchor, after normalization; its literal values occur in it after the literal rule; and `about_scope` passes the K-SCOPE word check (the same rules as A3a's Rust check).
  - **Value-bound anchors** (`table_cell`, `xbrl`): the fact binds by exact cell or fact value instead of sentence alignment (§4.1). The receipt records `alignment = "value"` for them and `alignment = "sentence"` for prose anchors (§4.4 after polish round 2), and `aligned` then means whole-unit binding: the quote is the whole cell text or fact value, never a fragment of it (A3a reads it the same way).
  - It then writes `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<case>/receipts.toml`, one `[[receipt]]` row per sourced fact: `source`, `fact`, `anchor` (the page or line range the quote was found at, in A1a's grammar, which K-ANCHOR checks), `verified_utc`, `tool_version`, `extraction_sha256`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (the SHA-256 of A1a's canonical values bytes, `fa:case-values:v1` then `about_scope` then one TAB-joined line per `[[value]]` row in ordinal order, so K-BIND detects offline a value or scope edited after `verify`), `alignment` (`sentence` | `value`), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok`, and the source's `original_hash_compared`, copied from its `sources.toml` row (false for an archive capture until OD 1 allows an original fetch) (§4.4). `verified_utc` is the cache entry's fetch time, not the run's clock, so re-running on an unchanged cache is byte-identical. Rows are written in a fixed order (by fact id), in the fa-registry TOML subset (one-line arrays, basic strings with only the `\n \t \" \\` escapes), with a generated-file header. The file is regenerated whole and never edited by hand (Python's stdlib has no TOML writer, and a rewrite of `sources.toml` would lose its comments).

**Normalization (identical in Python and Rust; the Rust side is A3a).** Decode UTF-8; replace every run of U+0009, U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020 and U+00A0 with one U+0020; trim; no case folding, no Unicode normalization, typographic quotes kept. `quote_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the normalized bytes. Neither Python's `str.split()` nor Rust's `char::is_whitespace` is used: they disagree on U+001C–U+001F. Both suites test it on the shared rows of `crates/fa-oracles/data/binding_fixtures.toml` (`[[normalize]]`, `[[sentence]]`, `[[scope]]`; hex-encoded where the TOML subset cannot spell a code point). A1a creates that file with its `[[values]]` rows; A9 adds its Python suite over every section, so the values bytes are also tested in both languages.

**Sentence alignment.** A quote starts at the extraction's start, or after `[.?!]` plus an optional closing `"` or `)` plus whitespace. It ends with `[.?!]` plus an optional closing `"` or `)`, followed by whitespace or the end. A boundary preceded by a registered abbreviation (`p`, `pp`, `Inc`, `Co`, `No`, `U.S`, `Mr`, `Ms`, `Dr`) is not a boundary. A heading-only line (SRC-ENR-002's "UNAUDITED", E1) is one whole sentence: a quote is aligned when it is the whole normalized text of exactly the lines its anchor names and those lines contain no `[.?!]` (A3a's rule; `verify` checks it on the extraction's lines before normalization joins them), and any part of such a line is a fragment.

**Gate (§15 A9).** `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_fetch.rs` has two `#[test]`s, run by check.sh's existing `test` step:
- `case_fetch_unittests_pass`: runs `python3 -B -m unittest discover tools/case-fetch` from the repository root (`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../..`) and fails, never skips, if `python3` is absent (`FAIL case_fetch gate: python3 not found on PATH (this is not a pass)`) or any unittest fails (the unittest output is printed);
- `case_fetch_sources_match_their_pin`: recomputes the SHA-256 of every file under `tools/case-fetch/` and compares it with `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_fetch.sha256`, so a green run names the exact tool bytes it tested.
- **Input closure (fail closed).** `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` builds a crate's input hash from the global inputs and the trees of the crate and its workspace dependencies (`:216-228`); a runtime read of `tools/case-fetch` is in none of them. So an edit to the tool alone, with the pin untouched, would leave fa-oracles' input hash unchanged and reuse a stale green verdict (`:231`): the pin by itself closes nothing under reuse. `case_fetch.rs` therefore also embeds the tool's two Python files (`include_str!("../../../tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py")`, `include_str!("../../../tools/case-fetch/test_case_fetch.py")`; the unittests still run the files on disk). An `include_str!` target outside the crate marks the crate `undeclared_external_read`, and such a crate never reuses a cached verdict (`:16-19`, `:152-179`, `:231`), as `crates/fa-cli/tests/readme.rs:31` already does with `README.md`. Every gate then re-runs the unittests and the pin test; the cost, stated in the landing, is that fa-oracles' verdict is never reused while the tool lives outside the crate.

**Exit codes (gate vocabulary).** 0 when everything is verified; 1 with `FAIL ` lines on failure; 4 with `UNRUN ` lines when a required system tool or the network is unavailable (an environment exit, as fa's exit 4), never reported as success; 2 on a usage error.

## Tests & logging

- **stdlib `unittest`** (`tools/case-fetch/test_case_fetch.py`) over the fixture documents, with the five planted failures of §4.4, each asserting a `FAIL ` line on stdout and exit 1: `test_quote_not_found_fails`; `test_quote_found_twice_fails`; `test_value_not_in_quote_fails`; `test_scope_conflict_fails`; `test_sentence_fragment_fails` (the shape of the "entered and approved" fragment, in a synthetic carrier sentence).
- **Positive fixture:** `test_verify_writes_receipts_with_all_four_booleans_true`: `verify` on the fixture writes receipts with `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok` all true, `alignment` set by anchor kind, `values_sha256` equal to the shared fixture row's, `anchor` set to the range the quote was found at, and `original_hash_compared` equal to the fixture source row's; `test_rerun_on_unchanged_cache_is_byte_identical`.
- **Derived tests (§4.1, §4.4):** `test_find_by_hash_selects_the_one_matching_span` and `test_find_by_hash_with_zero_or_two_matches_fails` (the pre-OD-2a lookup); `test_table_cell_and_xbrl_facts_bind_by_exact_value` (and a cell fragment fails); `test_paragraph_anchor_is_prose`; `test_receipts_parse_with_the_registry_toml_subset` (the written file round-trips through `tomllib` with only one-line arrays and the four escapes); `test_xbrl_facts_rows_carry_instance_lines`; `test_values_sha256_matches_the_shared_fixture_rows` (Python builds A1a's canonical values bytes for each `[[values]]` row and gets its `canonical_hex` and `values_sha256`); `test_value_bound_fact_gets_alignment_value_and_prose_fact_sentence`.
- **`FA_SEC_CONTACT` leak test:** `test_sec_contact_is_never_written`: with the variable set to a sentinel, every file the tool writes (receipts, cache sidecars, logs) is grepped for it; any hit fails.
- **Derived tests (round 4's cross-half list):** `test_verify_accepts_a_case_directory_path` (a temp copy of the fixture case: receipts are written into the copy, and the committed fixture's bytes are unchanged); `test_fetch_single_blocked_source_prints_an_unverified_sha256` (against the local server: `fetch <case> --source <id>` on a `BLOCKED` row with no `sha256` prints `FETCHED <id> sha256=<hex> … unverified`, exits 0, writes no receipt, and plain `fetch` prints `SKIP <id> BLOCKED …`); `test_fact_citing_a_blocked_source_fails`; `test_xbrl_fact_with_wrong_decimals_fails` and `test_xbrl_fact_missing_a_dimension_member_fails` (each prints `FAIL ` naming the field and exits 1), with the matching fact passing; `test_heading_only_line_is_one_sentence` (a fixture page with a heading line "UNAUDITED" anchored on its own line: aligned, `quote_found_once` true) and `test_part_of_a_heading_line_fails` (one word of a two-word heading → `FAIL `, not sentence-aligned).
- **UNRUN path (derived from §4.4's exit codes):** `test_missing_pdftotext_reports_unrun`: with `pdftotext` absent from `PATH`, extracting a PDF prints `UNRUN ` and exits 4, never 0.
- **Normalization fixture:** `test_normalization_matches_the_shared_fixtures` over `binding_fixtures.toml`; A3a's Rust test reads the same rows.
- **No network:** `fetch` is tested against a local `http.server` bound to 127.0.0.1 serving fixture bytes; a test-wide guard makes any other connection raise. No test reaches a remote network (§0.5); hash verification is tested on local bytes.
- **Gate tests (Rust):** `case_fetch_unittests_pass` passes under `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; a test-only copy of the suite with one planted failing unittest makes the runner function report the failure; `case_fetch_sources_match_their_pin` fails, naming the file, when a tool file changes without its pin line.
- **Logging:** stdout follows the gate vocabulary: one `VERIFY <fact> PASS` line per verified fact, `SKIP <id> BLOCKED <reason>` and `FETCHED <id> sha256=<hex> … unverified` lines from `fetch`, `FAIL `/`UNRUN ` lines at column 0 with the fact, source and reason; diagnostics go to stderr. The receipts file is the durable record. The case runner's log (§3.5) does not involve this tool, because tests never read the cache (§4.3).

## Notes

- **← A1a:** A1a defines the `Receipt` type, the anchor grammar and the loader in `fa-oracles`; this tool writes the file that loader reads, so it follows A1a's schema (§15: "← A1a (schema)").
- **Consumers:** W1, X1, X1m, X6, E1, L1, M1, M2t and C0 depend on A9, and so does the pilot A8 (its receipts are `case_fetch.py verify worldcom`'s output); A10a's offline test checks the receipts it writes.
- **OD 1 (SEC contact address)** gates direct sec.gov fetches, and so `original_hash_compared = true` for EDGAR rows. Until then retrieval is archive-only, which is not neutral: the Internet Archive grants access "for scholarship and research purposes only", and archive captures cannot settle byte equality with the EDGAR originals (§1.2, §14). The address lives only in `FA_SEC_CONTACT`.
- **OD 2a (quote text)** gates committing quote text, not this tool (hash-first vendoring, §1.3, §4.2).
- **Round 4's cross-half items (settled here in polish round 5):** the case-directory path (W2), the single-row fetch of a `BLOCKED` candidate (W1), and the `decimals` and member comparison for `xbrl` facts (C0, X1). M2t extends `verify` with the `rows_file` case (the complaint's block hash and its per-row booleans); this item's `verify` locates one quote per fact.
- **Independent re-verify (§4.5):** the reviewer runs `verify` with a second `FA_CASES_CACHE`; the two receipts files must be byte-identical except for `verified_utc` (each cache's own fetch time).
- **Settled by the plan (§4.4):** the receipt's `anchor` field carries the range K-ANCHOR checks; `values_sha256` binds the fact's values and scope; `alignment` names the binding mode; the four booleans are named (`aligned` replaces round 2's `sentence_aligned`), with `original_hash_compared` copied from the source row; `verified_utc` is the cache fetch time, which makes the byte-identical re-run consistent; before OD 2a, `verify` finds the quote by hash among the sentence-aligned spans at the anchor.
- **Observed at 8196f5e40 (code check):** `scripts/foundation_check.py` imports the stdlib `tomllib`, which can read the fa-registry TOML subset the case files use. `scripts/check.sh` has no Python unittest step for `tools/` (its one Python test step is `scripts/tests/foundation_negative.py`, `scripts/check.sh:527`); the fa-oracles gate test above is how check.sh's existing `test` step runs this tool's tests, with no new check.sh step.
- **Risk: worker environment.** `cargo test` runs on the rch workers (`scripts/gate_workers.conf`: hz2, vmi1152480), so each needs `python3` ≥ 3.11 on `PATH`; on a worker without it the gate test fails, as the plan requires. The landing records the workers' `python3 --version`.
- **Risk:** a `pdftotext` version change alters the extraction bytes and so `extraction_sha256`. Receipts record `tool_version` for that reason.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main (the new fa-oracles test file), `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_fetch`, and `bash scripts/check.sh` (non-`.rs` files: the tool, its fixtures, the pin).
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: on the fixture document, `verify` writes `receipts.toml` with all four binding booleans true (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`), `alignment` matching each fact's anchor kind, `values_sha256` equal to A1a's canonical values bytes' hash (the shared `[[values]]` rows reproduce in Python), `original_hash_compared` copied from the fixture source row, and the found `anchor`; re-running on an unchanged cache is byte-identical (`verified_utc` is the cache fetch time).
- [ ] positive: with no quote text committed, `verify` locates each quote as the one sentence-aligned span at the anchor whose SHA-256 matches; `table_cell` and `xbrl` facts bind by exact value; `paragraph` anchors are prose.
- [ ] positive: the fa-oracles `#[test]` running `python3 -B -m unittest discover tools/case-fetch` passes under `cargo test`, and `case_fetch_sources_match_their_pin` passes; `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` reports fa-oracles with `undeclared_external_read = true` (the tool's files are `include_str!` targets), so a tool-only edit is never covered by a reused verdict.
- [ ] positive: the normalization fixture rows are committed in `crates/fa-oracles/data/binding_fixtures.toml`, and the Python implementation reproduces them (A3a's Rust test reads the same rows).
- [ ] negative: each of the five planted failures of §4.4 (quote not found; quote found twice; value not in the quote; scope conflict; sentence fragment) prints a `FAIL ` line and exits non-zero; a hash lookup with zero or two matching spans fails.
- [ ] negative: the `FA_SEC_CONTACT` leak test: a sentinel contact value appears in no file, receipt, log or fixture the tool writes.
- [ ] negative: with `pdftotext` unavailable, a PDF extraction reports `UNRUN` with a non-zero exit, never success.
- [ ] negative (derived): an `xbrl` fact whose `precision` disagrees with the instance's `decimals`, or whose `cell` member suffix differs from the context's member, or part of a heading-only line quoted as a fact, fails `verify`; a fact citing a `BLOCKED` source fails; `fetch --source <id>` on an unread `BLOCKED` row prints its SHA-256 as unverified and writes no receipt.
- [ ] positive (derived): `verify` accepts a path to a case directory and writes its receipts there, leaving the committed case unchanged; a heading-only line quoted whole is one aligned sentence.
- [ ] negative: the gate test fails when `python3` is absent, when any unittest fails, and when a tool file changes without its pin line.
- [ ] no-claim: a receipt shows that the quote occurs in bytes with that SHA-256 at that anchor. It does not show that the bytes are the publisher's unless `original_hash_compared = true`.

title: [cases] A10a: ledgers_validate_offline #[test] in fa-oracles (receipts, K-PROV…K-JOINT) and a marker test over renderer templates and case READMEs
description:
## Why

This is the offline gate of docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §4.6. There is no new `scripts/check.sh` step: the validator is a `#[test]` of `fa-oracles`, which check.sh's existing `test` step already runs and counts in its gate evidence. It never touches the network; source fidelity is established by the receipt, which is reviewable evidence bound to a SHA-256. Because case data is embedded with `include_str!` from inside `fa-oracles`, `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` hashes it into the crate's tree, so editing a facts file invalidates exactly the verdicts it can affect (§3.1). The second test exists because registry-check's claims lint skips a missing file (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:830-837`): until the rendered files exist (A14, then A10b), nothing would check the markers the renderer emits, so this test checks them independently of whether any rendered file exists. It also scans every committed case README, so per-case READMEs never need a `claims_lint.toml` edit, each of which would invalidate every crate verdict (§15 A10a; Appendix Z.7 split A10a from A10b for this reason). It serves every claim type by refusing malformed provenance, tautological ties and inadmissible branches before any book is built.

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here): `crates/fa-oracles/tests/ledgers.rs` with the two `#[test]`s below, and `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/policy.rs` (`pub const QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED: bool = false`, the OD 2a switch, and `pub const MAX_QUOTE_WORDS: usize = 60`).

**1. `ledgers_validate_offline`** (§4.6). For every case in `fa_oracles::cases::embedded::CASES` (every committed case, `_selftest` included) and every harness table under `crates/fa-oracles/data/`:
- ledger well-formedness: the case loads through the A1a–A1c loaders (and A2/A4/A5a's table loaders);
- receipts present and consistent with the facts: every sourced fact has exactly one `[[receipt]]` whose `source`, `fact` and `quote_sha256` match the fact and whose `anchor` passes K-ANCHOR; `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok` are true, its `alignment` is `sentence` for a prose anchor and `value` for a `table_cell` or `xbrl` one (where `aligned` is whole-unit binding, A3a/A9), and its `values_sha256` equals the hash of the fact's current canonical values bytes (A1a), so a value or scope edited after `verify` fails here, offline; `original_hash_compared` equals the source row's and is reported per source (`SOURCE <id> original_hash_compared=<bool> route=<retrieval_route>`), never required; and no receipt names a fact that is not sourced;
- the load-time checks of §3.6 from K-PROV through K-JOINT, through `run_load_checks`: K-PROV, K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR, K-DERIVE (A3a); K-BASIS, K-TAUT, K-ORACLE, K-VINTAGE (A3b); K-ASSERT, K-ERRRATE, K-NAMES, K-EVID, K-REASON (A3c); K-TIER (A4); K-BRANCH, K-PRED, K-JOINT (A5b); and the case-scoped checks registered in A3a's `CASE_CHECKS` (X5's group check), each on its own case;
- the excerpt volume per case (§4.2): `EXCERPTS <case> facts_with_quote=<n> words=<n>`. While `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED` is false (OD 2a undecided), any committed `quote` field fails; once the OD 2a landing flips it (citing the owner's recorded decision), a quote over `MAX_QUOTE_WORDS` words fails.

**Verdict rule.** The test fails on any FAIL. A check reports UNRUN, and does not fail the test, only when the case has no rows of the check's input kind (a case with no T rows has nothing for K-TAUT); a check whose input rows exist must examine every one of them, and an `examined` count below the input count is a FAIL (a check that skipped rows), so UNRUN can never hide a skipped row. The one exception the plan makes is data that may not be committed yet: a `rows_file` fact whose file is absent (whole tables wait on OD 2b, §3.2b), every fact derived from it, and every leg whose `amount_rule` names one (A3a's `pending_facts`: M2a's six row-derived facts, M2c's drift facts, M6's declared trial balances) count as unrun inputs, reported `examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, never as examined and never as a FAIL; `examined + unrun` must still equal `inputs`, and any other shortfall still fails. The test never reads the network or the fetch cache (§4.3).

**2. `renderer_and_readme_markers_resolve`** (a second `#[test]` in `tests/ledgers.rs`).
- Every marker the renderer can emit must resolve against the registries, independent of whether any rendered file exists: the markers in its template vocabulary (A14's templates, once they exist) and every marker in any string field of committed case data (the `refusal`, `twin_expect` and `reference_verdict` fields among them), because the renderer prints those fields.
- The same test scans every committed case `README.md` under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/` (read from `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`, inside the crate's hashed tree) and requires every marker in it to resolve. That covers the READMEs without a `registries/claims_lint.toml` edit per case, since each registry edit invalidates every crate verdict (§15 A10a).
- **Marker grammar and resolution follow registry-check exactly:** the extraction rule of `extract_markers` (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:514-544`: a family prefix, at least two digits, not followed by a letter or `_`), over every `[[marker_family]]` of `registries/claims_lint.toml` (12 families, `FA-CON-` … `FA-BENCH-`), each resolved against its `registry`/`table`/`key`, plus the reserved refusal codes registry-check also admits (`main.rs:808-813`). The plan names only `FA-REF-*`/`FA-INV-*`; using the full family list means a renderer that ever emits another family is covered without a change here. The registries are read with `include_str!` from `registries/`, which `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` admits as a declared input, and parsed with `fa_registry::toml::parse`. fa-oracles stays within its allowlist.

## Tests & logging

- Both run under `cargo test -p fa-oracles` (through rch), so check.sh's `test` step, completion markers and test-inventory witness count them.
- **Planted negative (§15):** `unresolved_marker_fails_the_marker_test`, in two forms: a test-only copy of a case data file naming `FA-REF-999` (absent from `refusal_catalog.toml`), and a test-only copy of a case `README.md` carrying it; each fails with `FAIL markers <file>:<line> FA-REF-999 has no row in refusal_catalog.toml`.
- **Derived positive:** with no case README committed yet, the README half reports `UNRUN markers readmes examined=0`, never PASS; the case-data half still runs.
- **Derived negatives:**
  - `planted_k_check_violation_fails_through_ledgers_validate_offline`: for each K-check, the planted fixture its item lands (A3a/A3b/A3c/A4/A5b) fails through this test's entry point, naming the check, the file and the line;
  - `sourced_fact_without_a_receipt_fails`, `receipt_whose_quote_sha256_disagrees_fails`, `fact_value_edited_after_verify_fails_through_values_sha256`, `receipt_for_a_non_sourced_fact_fails`;
  - `uncommitted_rows_file_and_its_derived_facts_are_unrun_never_examined` (a ledger-row fact whose rows file is absent and one `difference` fact derived from it: `CHECK <case> K-BIND … unrun=1 (OD 2b)` and `CHECK <case> K-DERIVE … unrun=1 (OD 2b)`, and the test does not fail on them), and `missing_rows_for_any_other_reason_fails` (a check that skips a committed rows file's fact, or a derived fact whose input is committed, still FAILs);
  - `check_examining_fewer_rows_than_its_input_fails` (a test-only check that skips one row);
  - `committed_quote_text_fails_while_od_2a_is_undecided`.
- **Output:** one line per (case, check), `CHECK <case> <K-ID> PASS|FAIL|UNRUN examined=<n>/<inputs>[ unrun=<k> (OD 2b)]` (A3a's line with the case id), one `FAIL` line per failing row (case, file, line, check id, reason), the `SOURCE` and `EXCERPTS` lines, and a final `LEDGERS cases=<n> pass=<n> fail=<n> unrun=<n>`. No book is built, so there is no run-log JSONL here.

## Notes

- **Pending inputs (polish round 5).** Round 4's exception named only the rows fact, so the facts derived from it (M2a, M2c, M6, M0's rule) would have read as an examined count below the input count, a FAIL; the exception now covers A3a's `pending_facts`, which is the same set the runner prints UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` for (A7a).
- **Why each edge:** A3a, A3b, A3c, A4 and A5b supply the checks this test aggregates; A9 defines and generates `receipts.toml`, which "receipts present and consistent" reads.
- **A10b** adds only `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` to `registries/claims_lint.toml` `scanned_docs` (one registry edit in total), once A14 renders it. The case READMEs stay covered by this marker test, permanently, with no per-case registry edit.
- **Observed at 8196f5e40 (code check):** registry-check's known-marker set includes constitution constraints, evidence gates, threats, trust boundaries, tamper vectors, proof lanes and SLO rows as well as refusals and invariants (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:797-827`), from the families of `registries/claims_lint.toml:12-83`. This test resolves the same families.
- **fa-vz7e (registry and documentation truth, open, P1)** plans a std-only README/AGENTS sync check whose first rule is that every `FA-*` marker in `README.md`/`AGENTS.md` resolves. That is the same marker grammar this test resolves for the case READMEs and the renderer's markers, but in two places: fa-vz7e's check lives in registry-check itself (its acceptance tests are `tools/registry-check::tests::…`), while this test mirrors registry-check's `extract_markers` rule and claims-lint families inside fa-oracles, which cannot import the tool crate (its allowlist is `["fa-registry", "fa-reference", "fa-time"]`). So a change fa-vz7e makes to `extract_markers` or the families is mirrored here in the same landing, or the two resolutions drift. A10a covers the case READMEs and renderer markers, fa-vz7e the repository's README and AGENTS.md.
- **OD 2a enforcement.** The OD bead's negative ("until OD 2a is recorded, every case's committed quote volume is zero") is enforced here by `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED`. Flipping it is the OD 2a landing's one-line change, never a side effect of a case landing.
- **Gate evidence:** check.sh counts tests per crate, so a later removal of a check test needs a `Retired-tests:` trailer, and reducing negative-test or assert counts needs `Weakened-tests:` (AGENTS.md gate rules; §16; `scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155` counts the negatives by name).
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test ledgers`; `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `ledgers_validate_offline` passes on every committed case and harness table, with a per-check report of the rows each K-check examined from K-PROV through K-JOINT (`examined=<n>/<inputs>`); a check reports UNRUN only when the case has no rows of its input kind, and the excerpt volume per case is reported.
- [ ] positive: `renderer_and_readme_markers_resolve` resolves every marker the renderer can emit against the registries with no rendered file present, using registry-check's extraction rule and all `registries/claims_lint.toml` families, and every marker in every committed case `README.md`.
- [ ] negative: a planted unresolved marker fails the marker test (in a case-data copy, and in a case README copy).
- [ ] negative: a sourced fact with no receipt row, or with a receipt whose `quote_sha256` or `values_sha256` disagrees (a value edited after `verify`), fails `ledgers_validate_offline`, naming the fact; a rows file absent under OD 2b, and every fact derived from it, is reported `unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, never examined and never PASS; a check that examines fewer rows than its input fails; committed quote text fails while OD 2a is undecided.
- [ ] no-claim: green shows the vendored data is well-formed, consistent with its receipts and passes K-PROV…K-JOINT; it says nothing about whether a fact is true of the historical record beyond what each receipt binds, and it touches no network.

title: [cases] A10b: add docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md (only) to registries/claims_lint.toml scanned_docs once A14 renders it
description:
## Why

docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §4.6: `registries/claims_lint.toml` `scanned_docs` gains `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`, so every `FA-REF-*` and `FA-INV-*` marker the renderer emits must resolve against the registries (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:797-843`). Round 4 split this item from A10a (Appendix Z.7) because registry-check skips a missing file (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:830-837`), so the scan lands only once A14 renders the document. The case READMEs are covered by A10a's marker test instead, which avoids a registry edit (and a global crate-verdict invalidation) per case (§15 A10a). It protects every claim sentence of the program overview (D/P/T/C/R/N/CF) whose wording names a refusal or an invariant.

## What to build

- Edit `registries/claims_lint.toml` `scanned_docs` to add `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`, and nothing else: one registry edit in total. At 8196f5e40 the line reads `scanned_docs = ["COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENACCOUNTING.md", "README.md", "AGENTS.md"]` (`registries/claims_lint.toml:8`), a one-line array in the TOML subset; after the edit it ends `…, "AGENTS.md", "docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md"]`. The case READMEs are covered by A10a's marker test, not by this list.
- No new check.sh step: registry-check's existing claims-lint pass (check.sh step `registry-check`) reads the list and resolves every marker family of `claims_lint.toml` with `extract_markers` (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:514-544`).

## Tests & logging

- **Planted negative (§15):** a planted unresolved marker (`FA-REF-999`) in the rendered `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`, in the gate worktree, makes `scripts/check.sh` exit non-zero with a `FAIL ` line for the `registry-check` step, and registry-check's own output (the step's log) names the document and the marker: ``claims_lint: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` cites `FA-REF-999`, which has no row in its owning registry`` (`main.rs:561-563`). The plant is observed and restored before landing; the landing records the observed line and exit code.
- **Positive:** with the file present, registry-check's summary event (`"event":"registry_check"`, `main.rs:970-977`) reports a `markers_checked` count that rises, relative to the run before the edit, by exactly the number of distinct markers the document contains (A10a's marker test can compute that number from the same file).
- Read the gate's exit code, never a grep of its output (AGENTS.md).

## Notes

- **← A14:** the file must exist. registry-check silently skips a listed path whose file is missing (`tools/registry-check/src/main.rs:830-837`), so a path added before A14 renders it would check nothing.
- **Global invalidation:** this is a `registries/*.toml` edit, which invalidates every crate verdict (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`). The landing states it.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/check.sh` (the `registry-check` step carries the scan) and `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; a registry edit with no `.rs` change still needs both, since the global digest invalidates every crate's cached verdict.
- **Per-case READMEs.** They need no `scanned_docs` row and no further registry edit: A10a's marker test scans every committed case README (§15 A10a, A10b).
- The plan does not name `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md` (A15) for either scan; extending A10a's README scan to it would need no registry edit. Flagged for the owner.
- A10a's marker test checks the renderer's marker vocabulary in the meantime; the two are complementary.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: with A14's rendered `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` present, registry-check scans it and every marker in it resolves; `scanned_docs` gains exactly that one path (one registry edit), and registry-check's `markers_checked` rises by the document's distinct markers.
- [ ] negative: a planted unresolved marker in the rendered `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` fails `scripts/check.sh` (non-zero exit, a `FAIL ` line for the `registry-check` step, and registry-check's log naming the document and the marker), observed before the plant is restored.
- [ ] no-claim: marker resolution shows that each cited id exists in the registries; it does not show that the sentence citing it is true or that the refusal fires as described (that is the runner's job).

title: [cases] A11a: filler and identifier invariance witness: 5 seeded + empty + extremal filler variants and at least 2 runs per D/P/N
description:
## Why

docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §3.7 item 1. A filler- or identifier-dependent D is a named risk (§17). The research refuted two shortcuts (§0.4): H-001 ("filler never matters": registry-level classification of procedure dependence agreed with code on only 54/68 = 79.4%) and H-040 (one reader can read tiers reliably from code: an independent second reader disagreed on 4 of 12, and `expense.capitalization`'s statistic depends on account VId order, which hashes the random book id). Tier rows (A4) are declarations; this witness executes them, so undeclared behaviour drift is caught at runtime and names the procedure (§2.5). Book ids come from production entropy with no seed flag (§3.4), so at least two runs sample different VId orders without making a test nondeterministic. It serves D, P and N verdicts and their S, Sd, Si and Rel components; its wording is "shown on N variants", never "proved".

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here): `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/invariance.rs` (pure: `pub fn compare(observations: &[VariantObservation], statuses: &Statuses) -> InvarianceVerdict`, where a `VariantObservation` is (filler variant id, book id, projection) and the verdict is `Agree`, or `Disagree { procedure, component, a, b }` naming the two observations) and `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/invariance.rs` (builds and runs every variant through A7c's `runs` plan and feeds `compare`).

For every D, P and N expectation it applies to, the runner executes and compares:
- **K = 5 seeded discipline-obeying filler variants** from the A6 generator (seeds 1–5). Content is a pure function of SHA-256(case id ‖ variant id ‖ seed); each variant is posted as `PostBatch` chunks of at most 8,190 entries (`registries/verbs.toml:263`; `registries/limits.toml:99-101`; on a `migration` book, as migration chunks staged before finalize, A6) and cites one `fa:case-filler:v1` document (§2.7).
- **The empty variant.**
- **One extremal variant per tier**, maximizing what its discipline leaves free (A6):
  - L and C: 10^3 × the target's leg count of filler entries on the filler accounts, dated in every period the history opens;
  - S-rel: one filler duplicate pair per target key shape, under disjoint keys;
  - S-acct: 10^3 entries on a sibling account of the same type and role;
  - G and S-party: same-scope volume of at least 10^3 × the target. This is where truncation by `max_findings` shows;
  - O: 10^3 commits interleaved before the first target.
- **At least 2 runs**, so at least 2 book ids. Every variant builds its own book, and the empty variant is run twice: two books with byte-identical content and different book ids, which isolates identifier dependence from filler dependence.

Every S, Sd, Si and Rel component must agree across all of them; a disagreement fails and names the procedure. A Rel component (§2.6 rule 9) agrees when its relational rule (A5b's `rel.rs`) holds on every run, with the account order computed from the logged book id by `fa_model::account_vid` (`crates/fa-model/src/ids.rs:294-298`) or read from `fa explain balance --json`; its value may differ between runs. A B component is compared across the filler variants on its default cell, where every variant runs; its other cells run on the empty variant only (the combination rule, below).

The combination rule (§3.3, implemented by A7c) applies: filler variants run on the default branch cell only; branch cells run on the empty-filler variant only.

## Tests & logging

- **Positive (§15):** `w_d_01_f4_agrees_across_filler_variants_and_book_ids`: W-D-01 on F4 (cite Sd, severity S constant High, statistic Sd 560,000,000.00 under `one_leg_per_named_account`, §6.4) agrees across 5 seeded + empty + extremal variants and 2 runs of the empty variant, on the §3.2a pilot fixture (`fa_oracles::cases::fixtures::pilot()`).
- **Negative (§15):** `tier_l_row_for_round_amount_density_fails_naming_the_row`: a test-only tier table declaring `numbers.round_amount_density` tier L, with a fixture D on that procedure (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/invariance_negative/`), fails: the procedure is population-relative (its `min_legs` and `z_squared` gate move with filler volume), so the L-discipline extremal variant changes its projection; the line reads `FAIL <id> … invariance=disagree(numbers.round_amount_density@1,statistic,empty,extremal-L) reason=tier row case_procedure_tiers.toml:<line> declares L` (A7a's trailing `reason=`).
