- **Derived negative:** `expectation_needing_invariance_with_one_book_id_is_unrun`: a run plan with a single book prints UNRUN, never PASS (§3.7: the runner prints UNRUN for any expectation whose witness is not implemented, never PASS).
- **Unit tests** (`invariance.rs`, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`): `compare_names_the_procedure_component_and_both_variants`; `rel_component_with_different_values_across_book_ids_agrees_when_its_rule_holds`; `rel_component_whose_rule_fails_on_one_run_disagrees`.
- **Runner output:** one line per (expectation, variant, target, cell) in A7a's notation, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses>`, with `invariance=agree(variants=<n>,book_ids=<m>)` in the projection (no space inside the field); it is printed on the lines of the cells the variants ran (the default cell, under the combination rule). A disagreement names the procedure and the two variants (filler variant ids, book ids) that disagree, and prints the exact `fa` argv to reproduce each; the JSONL log path is printed at the end (§16).
- **Run log (§3.5):** one JSONL record per step: `case`, `book_variant`, `branch_class`, `filler_variant`, `book_id`, `step`, `verb`, `argv_redacted`, `exit`, `refusal_id?`, `finding_procedure?`, `certificate_kind?`, `elapsed_ms`; the verdict record lists the variants and book ids in `witnesses`.
- **Budget (§16):** each case completes in under 60 s on a warm worker; A7c records invocation counts and wall time per book. A case above budget fails; it never silently caps.

## Notes

- **← A6:** the seeded, empty and extremal variants come from the filler generator. **← A7c:** cell evaluation, co-residence, `PostBatch` filler, budget logging and the combination rule.
- **"At least 2 runs" (§3.7).** The plan does not say which content runs twice; running the empty variant twice is A11a's reading, because two books with identical content isolate the book id (VId order) from filler, at the cost of one extra book rather than a second full variant set.
- **Consumers:** A8 (the pilot needs A11a), A8b (W-D-02 on the migration book), W4, W8, E3, E6, L4, M5, M7, and A13 (the coverage gate depends on it).
- **Ledger variants:** §3.2 says ledger variants carry no filler, but §9.3 requires M-D-01's extremal variant on the ledger book (thousands of same-scope investor parties must still give 1ZR176 the same flag, severity and value). Both hold this way (M5's reading, adopted here): the declared ledger book has no filler (A1b refuses a `filler_batch` there, A6's `specs` gives only the empty spec), and for a G- or S-party D on a ledger stem this witness builds a harness-only copy of the book plus A6's extremal content (synthetic parties and accounts disjoint from every exhibit account), runs it beside the real book, and compares. The copy is never a declared variant, never rendered, and logged with `filler_variant = extremal-<tier>@copy`. If the copy cannot be built, the row prints UNRUN `reason=filler_invariance`, never PASS.
- **Projection form.** The runner prints this witness as `invariance=agree(variants=<n>,book_ids=<m>)` or `invariance=disagree(<procedure>,<component>,<variant a>,<variant b>)` (A7a's `<name>=<status>:<value>` notation has no spaces inside a field); a case bead's `variants=empty,extremal runs=2` gives the same contents.
- **Risks:** the 10^3 × extremal volumes press on the 60 s budget; an extremal variant above the 8,190-entry batch limit (`registries/limits.toml:99-101`) posts as several chunks (§3.3), each an invocation in A7c's budget log. The plan meets the budget through the §3.3 rules, not by capping (§16).
- Co-resident D cells of tier L and C are each other's filler (§3.3), so the witness also shows that co-residents do not interact.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the `invariance_negative` fixture.
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: W-D-01/F4's single components agree across 5 seeded + empty + extremal variants and 2 runs (2 distinct logged book ids, the empty variant run twice).
- [ ] negative: a test-only tier row declaring `numbers.round_amount_density` tier L fails, naming the row and the two disagreeing variants.
- [ ] negative: an expectation requiring this witness that ran with only one book id prints UNRUN, never PASS.
- [ ] positive (derived, §9.3): on a ledger stem, a G- or S-party D's extremal comparison runs on a harness-only copy (never a declared filler variant), and a copy whose synthetic parties share the target's party fails, naming the procedure (M5's `blmis_neg_ponzi_extremal_moves_target` uses this path).
- [ ] no-claim: agreement is shown on the variants and book ids that ran; it does not establish that a component is independent of every possible filler or every VId order.

title: [cases] A11b: contributing-entry witness for T: certified explain-balance and statement-trace contributions are exactly the named inputs
description:
## Why docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §3.7 item 2. A tautological T is a named risk (§17). K-TAUT (A3b) is its static half; this witness is the dynamic half: a T passes only if the certified value folds exactly the postings its predicate names as inputs, and none of them carries the published comparison value B. Round 2 adopted it to replace fold sensitivity, which was vacuous on all-published bridges (Appendix Z.4). Any failure re-types the T as R, so the witness decides which rows may be rendered as T at all. It also supplies the dependency through which a T's read verbs count as exercised in the coverage gate (§12.2). ## What to build **Files** (introduced here): `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/contrib.rs` (pure: `pub fn witness(t: &Expectation, contributions: &[Contribution], named_inputs: &BTreeSet, certified: i128, trace: &TraceIndex) -> ContribVerdict`, with `ContribVerdict::{Holds, Retype { condition }, Disagree { trace, explained }}`) and `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/contrib.rs` (the reads below). `TraceIndex` is A3b's `posted_from`, used to tell whether a contribution's amount traces to B. - **Named inputs ("the postings the predicate names as inputs", §3.7 item 2).** The plan does not say which field carries them; `inputs_named` alone cannot (§5.3 gives it to K-ORACLE's `oracle_output` inputs, and C1's C-T-01 lists only goodwill there, while its contributions are every posted component). So `named_inputs(t, book)` is computed, never authored, as the union of: - every `[[intent]]` whose `fact` is in the T's `basis`, other than its `published` fact (§3.2b makes a documented entry's intent id its fact id); on a `ledger` stem, every intent rendered from a `[[ledger_map]]` whose `source` is in the `basis` (M0); - every fact or `[[intent]]` id the T lists in `inputs_named` (A1c accepts intent ids there, D10; W7's W-T-03 names `delta-F12` and `delta-F13`); - every Δ intent (`target_kind = restates | revises`) whose `target` is in the set: the predicate's ΣΔ. For a read of a Δ (the `delta` column of `fa case diff --statements`, `fa statement trace --from-diff`, a `delta`-kind T), the named inputs are the Δ intents of that set only, since an A posting does not move a Δ. Each id maps to its entry vid(s) through A7a's fact↔vid map; an id that maps to no posted entry is a `missing named input` (re-type R). A derived leg inside an input intent (a `remainder` or `difference` leg, E4) is part of its intent; it is never a separate input. - **Stock reads span every period.** `fa explain balance --period

` explains one period's register cells: it skips every entry whose period is not `

` (`crates/fa-registers/src/explain.rs:230-233`, `entry_period(book, entry)? != period_code`, checked in the current tree), so on a book whose stock is posted period by period it explains only the T period's activity. The witness therefore takes the fold from the read, never from authoring and never per account: - a **stock** read explains every declared `[[period]]` of the variant whose end is on or before the T period's end, at the T's known-at, and takes the union of the contributions. Stock reads are: a balance-sheet line (the definition's `basis = "stock"`, `registries/statements/balance-sheet.toml:10`, which also maps the Revenue and Expense accounts as unclosed earnings of all years, `:33-62`, so `total_equity` and `liabilities_and_equity` union those accounts too); a `tb` read without `--activity`; and a per-account read of an account whose type has `kind = "stock"` (`registries/account_types.toml`: Asset, Liability, Equity at `:34`, `:40`, `:46`); - a **flow** read explains the periods of the read's own coordinate only (one quarter, or every period of a fiscal-year or year-to-date read, §10.1's duration rule). Flow reads are: an income-statement line (`basis = "activity"`, `registries/statements/income-statement.toml:9`, Closing entries excluded, `:11`); a `tb --activity` read; and a per-account read of a `kind = "flow"` account (Revenue, Expense at `:52`, `:58`). The three conditions below apply to that union (E4's bridge book: total assets, debt and equity from FY1997 through the T's year, net income in its year alone). `fa explain balance` reads an account, not a statement definition, so on an income-statement line, whose definition excludes Closing entries (`registries/statements/income-statement.toml:11`), a Closing entry's legs are set aside before the comparison and logged (`excluded_by_definition`); on every other read a Closing entry, like any entry that contributes and is not a named input, is an unnamed contribution. - **Leaf-account T.** Read `fa explain balance --period --certify --json` at the T's coordinate, for each period q the fold above selects. Its `balance_explained` event (`registries/verbs.toml:2443-2446`) lists `contributions` (`entry`, `ordinal`, `side`, `amount`, `class`, `effective_date`, `recorded_at`, …). The T passes only if all three hold: - the set of contributing entries (`contribution.entry`) is exactly the set of named inputs; - no contributing posting carries the published comparison value B, directly (a leg amount equal to B) or through a derivation (its intent's `amount_rule` traces to B through `TraceIndex`): the dynamic half of K-TAUT; - the contributions re-add to the certified value, which the command itself enforces per period (the event's doc: "The legs re-add to the cells exactly or the command fails"); the witness re-adds the union again in fa-oracles' own arithmetic and compares it with the T's certified value (for a stock read, the sum of the per-period explained balances). - **Type-level line.** The check runs over each account the line selects, all with the line's fold above (its definition's `basis`), whatever each account's own type. When a line selects more than 8 accounts, the harness reads `fa statement trace --certify` instead (`registries/verbs.toml:543`, event `statement_trace` `:2053-2056`): `--from-diff C:` for bridges, and `--definition … --before --after ` for footing. - Every publication that changes the line must be a posting the predicate names as an input, and none may carry B. - In addition, `fa explain balance --certify` runs over every leaf account the line selects (case books have tens of accounts, not thousands), and `fa_reference::statements::render` (`crates/fa-reference/src/statements.rs:148`, through A4r's `t_fold`) recomputes the line from those explained balances in its own arithmetic. - The trace and explained-balance witnesses must agree (A8a and W6 run both). - **No scenario-fork probe.** `fa scenario diff` reports per-account rows, not statement lines (`crates/fa-cli/src/scenario.rs:6-9`, `:515-530`), and posting probe intents into Closed or Locked periods is itself refused. - **Outcomes.** Any failure or disagreement re-types the T as R (the verdict record's `reason` names the failed condition). An `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` read on a line where Δ = 0 is flagged "selector not exercised". - Applies to every T kind of §5.3: `bridge`, `footing`, `per_account`, `allocation`, `delta`, and A1c's `rule` kind (M-T-02: the contributions are the originating account's postings up to the transfer, and none may carry the published credit). ## Tests & logging - **Unit tests** (`contrib.rs`, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`): `witness_holds_when_contributions_are_exactly_the_named_inputs`; `extra_contributing_entry_retypes_r`; `missing_named_input_retypes_r`; `contribution_equal_to_b_retypes_r`; `contribution_tracing_to_b_through_a_derivation_retypes_r`; `contributions_that_do_not_re_add_fail`; `trace_and_explained_balance_disagreeing_fails`. - Named inputs: `named_inputs_are_basis_intents_their_deltas_and_inputs_named` (a C-T-01-shaped footing: every component intent is named although `inputs_named` lists only the `oracle_output` one; a W-T-03-shaped T: the Δ ids it lists are named); `delta_read_names_only_the_delta_intents` (the A intents of the same basis are not inputs of a `delta` read, so an A contribution there re-types R). - Stock and flow: `stock_read_unions_every_period_through_the_t_period` (A posted in P1, Δ in P2, a stock T read in P2 holds on the union and re-adds to the stock); `stock_witness_missing_an_earlier_periods_explanation_fails` (the runner omits P1's explanation: FAIL `reason=missing explanation of `, never a pass on P2 alone); `flow_read_explains_only_its_coordinates_periods` (a quarterly income line's earlier-period postings are not contributions; a fiscal-year line reads each of its quarters); `closing_entry_is_set_aside_on_an_income_line_only` (a Closing entry on a Revenue account is logged `excluded_by_definition` on the income line, and is an unnamed contribution on a `tb` per-account read of the same account); `balance_sheet_total_equity_unions_its_unclosed_earnings_accounts` (a Revenue posting of an earlier period contributes to the `total_equity` line, read as stock). - **Runner tests** (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`): - **Positive (§15):** `selftest_bridge_contributions_are_exactly_a_and_delta`: the `_selftest` bridge's contributions on `1100` are exactly A's and Δ's entries and re-add to the certified 900.00. - **Negative (§15):** `_selftest_neg_read_back_t_never_passes_as_t`: a `run_planted` copy of `_selftest` that posts B directly (A7a) → the row prints with type R and `contrib=retyped(contribution carries B)`, never `PASS _selftest-T-01 T`. Before A12 claims the T this leaves the case green, so the test uses `.expect(…)` and its slug carries `never` for the ratchet; once A12 claims the T, a claimed row re-typed R fails the case and the test switches to `.expect_err(…)` in A12's landing. - **Derived negatives (§3.7 item 2):** `_selftest_neg_unnamed_contribution_never_passes_as_t` (an extra posting on `1100` in Q1 → re-typed R); `as_originally_reported_on_a_zero_delta_line_is_flagged_selector_not_exercised`. - **Runner output:** one line per (expectation, variant, target, cell) in A7a's notation, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN / ` (`-` for a T with no target), with `contrib=holds|retyped()` in the projection; the condition is `extra contribution `, `missing named input `, `contribution carries B` or `does not re-add`, and a trace/explained-balance disagreement prints `contrib=disagree(trace,explained)`. A re-typed row prints the exact `fa` argv to reproduce; the JSONL log path is printed at the end (§16). Each witness read is a logged step (§3.5) carrying its `certificate_kind` and the period it explains, and the verdict record lists the named-input ids and the periods read in `witnesses`. ## Notes - **← A7b:** the restatement lifecycle, issuance, case diff and bitemporal reads produce the certified reads this witness inspects. **← A8a:** the `_selftest` bridge is its fixture. - **First green T:** A8a's T row prints UNRUN until both A11b and A12 land (§15 A8a); A12 runs the outsider check of the T's read kind. - **Second half elsewhere:** `fa certificate status C:` reporting SupersededBy with `later_entries` equal to the case's Δ entries is "an independent second half of the contributing-entry witness" (§12.7); it lands with A12. - **Consumers:** A12 (the first green T needs this witness), W6, W7, W9, X3, X5, E4, L2, M3, C1, C3, and A13. - **Polish round 5.** E4 (a stock line posted period over period) needed the per-period union, and C1 and W7 read "named inputs" two ways (C1: the intents of the basis facts; W7: the ids in `inputs_named`); the computed set above serves both and keeps `inputs_named` K-ORACLE's field (§5.3). - **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases -- _selftest`. - **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the `_selftest` bridge's contributions are exactly A and Δ and re-add to the certified value.
- [ ] negative: a planted read-back T (B posted directly) is re-typed R, the line naming the failed condition.
- [ ] negative: an extra contributing posting the predicate does not name re-types the T as R, and an `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` read on a line where Δ = 0 is flagged "selector not exercised".
- [ ] positive (derived): the named inputs are computed from the T's `basis` intents, the ids in `inputs_named` and their Δ intents (only the Δs for a Δ read), and a stock read unions the explanations of every period through the T's, while a flow read explains only the periods of its own coordinate; the fold is the read's, not the account's, so a balance-sheet equity line unions its unclosed-earnings (Revenue and Expense) accounts as stock.
- [ ] negative (derived): a stock witness missing an earlier period's explanation fails, never passing on the T's period alone.
- [ ] no-claim: the witness shows which posted entries a certified value folds; it does not show the inputs are true of the history. A T that passes it is an exact observation on the constructed book, never a proof.

title: [cases] A11c: mutation twins for N rows (no_finding / no_refusal): a one-attribute harness-only twin must report; N barred on tier P
description:
## Why

A vacuous N is a named risk (§17): an N that "passes" because nothing could ever fire. docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §3.7 item 3 gives every N a harness-only mutation twin, and §5.2 makes an N "a regression lock in both directions". N results are published with the same prominence as D, P and T (§0.3); the twin is what makes them evidence rather than silence. N is barred on tier-P procedures because, for example, Benford below its 500-leg minimum returns a finding that cites nothing (§3.7). This item serves N rows, including A16's guidance N, and supplies the mutation-twin dependency through which a capability counts as exercised (§12.2).

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here): `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/twin.rs` (`pub fn twin_of(case: &Case, n: &Expectation) -> Result<TwinSpec, LoadError>`: the target's book variant with exactly the one attribute the N's `twin_attribute` names set to `twin_value`, plus the expected report `twin_expect`; and the load-time tier-P bar) and `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/twins.rs` (runs the target and its twin). The twin runs on its own book, built from the twin spec, so it never adds a posting to the target's book; it is logged like any step and never rendered.

For each N (§5.2 fields, A1c: `kind` = `no_refusal` | `no_finding` | `exact_gap`, the target, `mechanism` as file:line at the pinned commit, `twin_kind`, `twin_attribute`, `twin_value`, `twin_expect`, for `exact_gap` `gap_amount`, `gap_unit`, `twin_target`, and, for `no_finding` and `exact_gap`, the `procedure` and `version` whose run the N reads; E6's E-N-03 and the tier-P bar below need them, and §5.2's N field list omits them):
- **Target run.** An N `no_finding` must come from a run with no refusal and no error, in which the procedure reports no finding on the target. An N `no_refusal` requires the documented intent to be admitted. An N `exact_gap` (§5.2; M-N-01) requires the procedure's value on the target to differ from the sourced value by exactly `gap_amount`, the amount the mechanism explains.
- **Twin.** Harness-only. It flips the one attribute that the N's mechanism names, and the procedure must then report the target (`twin_expect = reports`); for `no_refusal`, the system must refuse it (`refuses <FA-REF-NNN>`); for `exact_gap`, the twin is `twin_target`, a target without the mechanism's input, where the gap must be 0 (`gap_zero`; e.g. M-N-01's 1ZR176).
- **Harness-observability twins** (`twin_kind = harness_observability`). Where no law-level twin exists at the pinned commit, the plan names a harness-observability twin instead: for E-N-01 and L-N-01, the same intent posted into a Closed period must be refused `FA-REF-010` (§7.2, §8.3a). It shows the harness observes refusals of that exact intent shape on that book, not that any law reacts to the documented attribute, and the rendering says so.
- **Matcher twins** (`twin_kind = matcher`, A16's guidance N): the twin is recorded input fed to the probe's matcher, not a book; A16 owns it, and this item's evaluation treats it as any twin.
- **Verdict.** The N passes when the documented intent is admitted, or the procedure reports no finding on it (or the gap equals `gap_amount`), **and** the twin reports. A twin whose run errors is FAIL, never UNRUN.
- **Tier-P bar (load time).** An N on a tier-P procedure (tier rows from A4's `case_procedure_tiers.toml`) is refused, except where the expectation carries A4's `population = "sourced_complete"` marker (§2.5, §9.4); there a tier-P N is admissible with a planted digit-skew or residue twin.

## Tests & logging

- **Negative (§15):** `benford_below_its_minimum_as_an_n_fails_its_twin`: a fixture N on `benford.first_digit`@2, marked `population = "sourced_complete"` so it passes the load bar, over 120 legs; its digit-skew twin cannot report, because below `min_population` (default 500, `registries/procedures.toml:199-203`) the finding cites nothing, so the line reads `FAIL <id> N … twin did not report (population 120 < min_population 500)`.
- **Derived positive:** `n_with_a_reporting_twin_passes`: on a micro-book, `jet.round_amounts` reports nothing on 1,234.56 legs and its twin (1,000.00 legs) reports the target. A8a's "one N with its twin" is the first consumer.
- **Derived positives (§5.2, §7.2):** `exact_gap_n_passes_when_the_gap_equals_the_mechanism_amount` (and its twin's gap is 0) on a micro-book; `harness_observability_twin_is_refused_fa_ref_010_in_a_closed_period`.
- **Derived negatives:** `n_whose_target_run_was_refused_reports_fail` and `n_whose_target_run_errored_reports_fail`, never PASS; `n_on_a_tier_p_procedure_without_the_sourced_complete_marker_is_refused_at_load`; `twin_flipping_two_attributes_is_refused` (A1c's shape rule, re-checked when the twin is built); `no_finding_n_without_a_procedure_is_refused` (`twin_of` returns `MissingField` for a `no_finding` or `exact_gap` N with no `procedure`@`version`, whether or not A1c's loader already refused it: the tier-P bar cannot key an N that names no procedure).
- **Runner output:** one line per (expectation, variant, target, cell) in A7a's notation, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses>`, with `twin=<twin_kind>:reported|did_not_report|refused:<FA-REF-NNN>|gap:<amount>` in the projection (no space inside the field, so A7a's whitespace-separated line stays parseable). Twin steps are logged in the JSONL run log (§3.5) with `book_variant = <variant>~twin`, like any other step but never rendered; a failure prints the exact `fa` argv of both the target and the twin.

## Notes

- **← A7a:** the runner core executes the target and the twin. **← A4:** the tier-P bar reads the tier table and its `population` marker. §15 lists only A7a; the bar cannot be implemented without A4's table, so the edge A11c ← A4 is added (no cycle: A4 ← A1a only), and A8a, which needs A11c, already waits on A4 through A7c → A5a.
- **Consumers:** A8a; A8 (W-N-01: the pilot's planted negative "retyping F2's credit account as Expense fails W-N-01" is that N's twin direction); W4; E3; E6 (E-N-03's twin moves the repurchase inside the window); L4; M5 (M-N-01); M7; A16; A13.
- **E-N-01 and L-N-01.** No law-level twin exists at 8196f5e40: Canon rules map a recorded REA event to candidate legs (`crates/fa-canon/src/lib.rs:1-3`), and "Rule families bound to intents are not in this build" (`registries/verbs.toml:664`), so no planted rule can refuse a posted intent. Both use the harness-observability twin above (§7.2, §8.3a). H7 and H6 research a kernel law, an intent-bound Canon rule family or (H6) a Lantern detector; whichever lands flips the N and gives it a law-level twin. E3 and L4 no longer wait on H7/H6.
- The tier-P exception rests on §9.4's sourced, complete population (BLMIS Exhibit B; Glantz alone exceeds Benford's 500-leg minimum). Until OD 2b commits those rows, an N resting on them prints UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` (A7a), never PASS.
- **Projection form.** `twin=<twin_kind>:reported|did_not_report|refused:<FA-REF-NNN>|gap:<amount>` is the serialization of this component; a case bead's `twin=reported (entry_class=Adjusting)`, `twin=harness_observability:refuses …`, `twin=refused FA-REF-010 exit=7` or `twin=1ZR176:gap=0.00` gives the same contents (the twin's attribute and target are in the verdict record's `witnesses`).
- **N procedure field (polish round 5).** The target run, the twin and the tier-P bar read the N's `procedure`@`version`; A1c carries the two fields on `no_finding` and `exact_gap` N rows (E6's E-N-03 required them), and a `no_refusal` N names none (its "procedure" is the kernel's admission).
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases`.
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: an N row passes only when its target run has no refusal, no error and no finding on the target (or, for `no_refusal`, the intent is admitted; for `exact_gap`, the gap equals the mechanism's amount) and its harness-only twin, built on its own book, reports the target (for `exact_gap`, shows gap 0; for a harness-observability twin, is refused `FA-REF-010` in a Closed period).
- [ ] negative: Benford below its minimum, used as an N (admitted under the sourced-and-complete marker), fails its twin.
- [ ] negative: an N declared on a tier-P procedure over a population that is not marked sourced and complete is refused at load; an N whose target run was refused or errored reports FAIL; a `no_finding` N that names no `procedure`@`version` is refused at load.
- [ ] no-claim: a passing N with its twin shows the procedure or law reacts on this encoding when the named attribute flips; it does not show that no other law, procedure or encoding would catch the documented entry.

title: [cases] A12: outsider verification (checkpoint, bundle, literal fa-verify argv incl. report, replay, ADS, kit) and the §12.7 witnesses
description:
## Why This item carries plan bet A3 (evidence-native and outsider-verifiable) into the case program: "A case whose bundle fails verification fails, whatever its expectations say" (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.1). A T passes only with the outsider check of its read kind (§5.3), so the program's first green T run happens here (moved from A8a to A12 in round 4, Appendix Z.7). The outsider kit's consumer is an examiner or opposing expert re-checking a case; the append-only witness renders as "an examiner who witnessed the as-filed root can verify offline that the restated book extends it; the as-filed entry is still included" (§12.7). It serves T (outsider check per read kind), D (finding export and replay), T and R (the GQL second read path, an R-class cross-check), and every case (book integrity and interop identity). ## What to build **Files** (introduced here): `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/outsider.rs` (extending A8a's checkpoint/bundle/replay steps), `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/witness.rs` (the append-only witness), `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/interop.rs` (second read path and interop identity); in fa-oracles, `src/cases/kit.rs` (renders `VERIFY.txt` from the run log's step records, pure), `src/cases/gql.rs` (the GQL statement for each T/R read, and the netting of its rows by unit and side), and `src/cases/verify_report.rs` (reads fa-verify's `report` JSON and compares the recomputed line or row with B). `crates/fa-oracles/cases/_selftest/books/statement.toml` is added: a minimal `statement` variant (two synthetic balance-sheet postings citing their stubs, no filler), so the ADS and interop checks, which run only on `statement` and `ledger` variants, have a self-test book. `fa-verify` runs in-process through `fa_verify::cli::run(&argv, read) -> Output { exit, stdout, stderr }` (`crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700`), where `read` reads the runner's files; fa-verify is already a dev-dependency of fa-cli. **1. TB / balance-sheet / income-statement certificates (§12.1), on any book variant:** - `fa checkpoint create --grant witness`, covering the read's known-at; - `fa bundle produce --certificate --out --receipt-out ` (`crates/fa-cli/src/proof.rs:804`; `registries/verbs.toml:784`); - `fa-verify bundle --key K --receipt R --json` and `fa-verify report --key K --checkpoint C --receipt R --json` (C from `fa proof signed-checkpoint --out `), both run as the literal argv through `fa_verify::cli::run`; both must exit 0, and the `report` recomputation of the T's line or row must equal B (fa-oracles compares it on fa-verify's report; `report` also accepts `--expect`, which the harness does not use, so the comparison stays independent of the tool under test); - `fa replay --output `, whose bytes must equal the original report bytes within the run (FA-INV-11). **2. Other read kinds replay their own way (§12.1):** D reads through `fa finding export --certificate C: --export-format canonical --out ` then `fa finding replay --certificate C: --known-at `; scenario expectations through their `fa scenario diff` certificate (`fa replay C:`); BLMIS footing (and any other `fa gl detail --certify` read, E4's debt cells) through `gl detail` certificates and account bundles (`fa bundle produce --account --from … --to … --balance :USD:`, verified in-process by `fa_verify::verify_bundle`; precedents `crates/fa-cli/tests/proofs.rs:335`, `crates/fa-cli/tests/production.rs:1014`). **2a. The read-kind table** (`src/cases/outsider_kind.rs`, pure): every T and R read verb (A1c's `read_verb`, A7b's reads) maps to exactly one outsider route, and the projection prints `outsider=:verified|failed`, several checks joined by `+`: - `report`: TB, balance-sheet and income-statement certificates, step 1 (`fa-verify bundle` and `report`, recomputed line = B, plus `fa replay`); - `replay`: certificates `fa bundle produce` does not take (its usage refuses "Other scopes", `registries/verbs.toml:784` at 8196f5e40), replayed byte for byte with `fa replay C:`: the scenario-diff and statement-diff certificates (`fa case diff --statements --certify`), and the consolidation report certificate of `fa consolidate --period --certify` (`registries/verbs.toml:632-640` at 8196f5e40: format `fa:report-certificate:v6`, "fa replay C: re-executes it byte for byte"; C3). fa-verify has no consolidation or diff recomputation (no `consolidat` in `crates/fa-verify/src`, current tree), so a `replay` check renders as "replayed in the book; no offline recomputation exists", never as an offline outsider verification (the same rule as the scenario note, fa-0m9r); - `gl detail` reads print `replay:<…>+bundle:<…>`: the certificate's `fa replay` and the account bundle's refold (the bundle's `--balance` equal to the read value); - `round_trip` (X-T-02, A1c's case-local kind, plan §10.1): `fa export xbrl` selects what the trial balance folds at its coordinate ("Refolding the exported legs gives the stock trial balance at that coordinate", `registries/verbs.toml:917` at 8196f5e40), so its outsider route is the balance-sheet certificate of the period ending at the export's instant (`fa statement balance-sheet --for

--certify`, which X3 already produces), through step 1: `outsider=report:verified` only when `fa-verify report`'s recomputed line for the concept's binding equals both the exported value and B. `fa verify export xbrl ` (`registries/verbs.toml:929` at 8196f5e40) is logged beside it as the §12.7 interop self-check. There is no `outsider=not_applicable`: §5.3 requires an outsider check for every T. A read verb with no row in the table prints its T UNRUN `reason=outsider`, never PASS. **3. ADS extract:** for every `statement` and `ledger` variant, `fa export ads --period

--out

--with-proofs`, then `fa-verify ads --key K` (`registries/verbs.toml:917`). Rendered as "an ADS-shaped GL extract (column set not yet the published standard, fa-ipom), verified complete by `fa-verify ads`". **4. Outsider kit:** with `FA_CASES_OUT=`, per case under `//`: the book directory and public key; signed and witnessed checkpoints; bundles with receipts and proofs; the ADS extract; canonical finding workpapers; and `VERIFY.txt`, generated by `kit.rs` from the run log, listing exactly the `fa-verify` and `fa replay` argv the runner executed with their exit codes. Never committed (ids vary per run, §3.4). Gate: every listed command was executed in the run that wrote it (`kit.rs` renders only from executed step records, and the kit test re-checks the file against the log). **5. Book integrity (§12.7):** after step 8 of §3.3, `fa verify book --json` must exit 0 on every book variant (`registries/verbs.toml:929`); exit 8 fails the case whatever its expectations say. **6. Append-only witness (§12.7)**, for every restatement case (W-T-02, W-T-03, E-T-01/03/04, X-T-01, X-T-03), landed here on the `_selftest` bridge: - role `examiner-witness` makes a key (`fa checkpoint witness-key --out k`) and cosigns the checkpoint before the case (`fa checkpoint witness --key k --out w1 --grant witness`); - after the case, `fa checkpoint witness --key k --previous w1 --out w2 --grant witness` must succeed, and `fa-verify checkpoint w2 --key --witness --quorum 1` must exit 0 (`registries/verbs.toml:760`: "a rollback or rewritten history is refused (FA-REF-124, exit 8)"); - `fa proof consistency --state --next-state ` and `fa proof inclusion --entry ` (at the after state) must verify with `fa-verify` (`registries/verbs.toml:772`); - `fa certificate status C:` must report `SupersededBy`, with `later_entries` equal as a set to the case's posted Δ entries (`registries/verbs.toml:567`), an independent second half of the contributing-entry witness; - harness-only twin: `--previous` set to another book's witness statement must be refused `FA-REF-124`. **7. Second read path (§12.7):** every T and R value is also read with `fa query ""` under the FA GQL profile (`registries/verbs.toml:652`), as a `MATCH` aggregate of legs grouped by unit and side (`(e:Entry)-[:HAS_LEG]->(l:Leg)-[:POSTS_TO]->(a:Account {code: ''})`, `(l)-[:IN_UNIT]->(u:Unit)`, `RETURN u.code, l.side, SUM(l.amount)`) and netted by `gql.rs`. It must equal the fold-path value. Which reads can be certified follows the profile, not §12.7's blanket `--certify`: - stock: `EFFECTIVE BETWEEN '' AND '' AS KNOWN AT `, with `--certify`; activity: `FOR PERIOD ''`, with `--certify`; - R rows with `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED`: the view read itself is uncertified (the usage at `registries/verbs.toml:652` at 8196f5e40: "a native read there is not certified: certify it AS KNOWN AT that sequence"; the current tree refuses `--certify` beside a view, `crates/fa-cli/src/query.rs:186-194`). So the harness runs the uncertified view read and a certified `AS KNOWN AT ` read at the sequence the fold path's `--as-originally-reported` read resolved (logged from its time selection); both must equal the fold value; - Lehman's scenario: `AT BRANCH 'scenario:'` (or `--branch scenario:`) "read at the replay's head, uncertified … no AS KNOWN AT and no certification beside it" (`registries/verbs.toml:652` at 8196f5e40; `crates/fa-cli/src/query.rs:64-73` refuses either); the values are compared, nothing is certified. This is an R-class cross-check of two FA read paths, never independent evidence. The projection prints `gql=ok|fail`; `fail` makes the row FAIL. A book with pending holds refuses the check, because GQL rows include them: it is not run and prints `gql=not_run(pending holds)`, which never turns a row UNRUN, since the check is not a T witness. **8. Interop identity (§12.7):** every `statement` and `ledger` book's ADS extract must re-import byte-identically (`registries/formats.toml:65-71`, `round_trip_identity = true`). `fa export beancount` and `fa export ads` are each checked with the native `fa verify export beancount|ads ` (`registries/verbs.toml:929`; `crates/fa-cli/src/export.rs:401-412`), which re-reads the file with the format's own reader and requires the balances to refold (beancount) or the journal to be re-read identically (ads), byte for byte; exit 8 names the first difference. There is no `--format` flag on `fa migrate import`; the format is a field of its `--intent` JSON. Once fa-sa4w's harness exists, the same books join its bean-check/hledger differential, reported UNRUN when the binaries are absent. **9. Claims.** When this lands, `_selftest`'s `case.toml` adds the bridge T to `claims`: the first claimed green T. A claimed T that is re-typed now fails the case (A7a), so A11b's `_selftest_neg_read_back_t_never_passes_as_t` and `_selftest_neg_unnamed_contribution_never_passes_as_t` switch from `.expect(…)` to `.expect_err(…)` in this landing (a stronger assertion, not a weakening). ## Tests & logging - **Positive (§15):** `selftest_bridge_t_passes_with_the_outsider_check`: with A11b, the `_selftest` bridge T prints PASS. This is the first green run of a T. - **Negative (§15):** `witness_with_another_books_previous_is_refused_fa_ref_124` (exit 8). - **Derived (read kinds and the second read path):** `every_t_read_verb_maps_to_one_outsider_kind` (unit, fa-oracles: every A1c read verb and A7b read is in the table; a test-only verb outside it leaves its T UNRUN `reason=outsider`); `gql_view_read_is_certified_at_its_resolved_sequence` and `gql_branch_read_is_compared_uncertified` (runner, on the `_selftest` R row and the scenario the case lifecycle forks: no `--certify` beside the view or the branch, values equal to the fold path); `consolidation_certificate_replays_byte_identically` (runner micro-book `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/consolidation_min/`, two entities, one OWNS edge, one member posting: `outsider=replay:verified`, rendered as replayed in the book). - **Derived negatives (§12.1, §12.7):** - `one_changed_byte_in_a_bundle_fails_fa_verify_and_the_case` (exit non-zero from `fa-verify bundle`; the case outcome is not ok whatever its expectations say); - `verify_book_exit_8_fails_the_case` (through the observation layer, as A8a); - `verify_txt_listing_an_unexecuted_command_fails_the_kit_gate`; - `gql_read_differing_from_the_fold_fails` (a test-only netting bug in `gql.rs` flips one side); - `_selftest_neg_report_recomputation_differing_from_b_fails` (a `run_planted` copy whose published B is B + 1 minor unit → `FAIL _selftest-T-01 … outsider=report:failed reason=expected observed `; the test calls `.expect_err(…)`); - `certificate_status_later_entries_missing_a_delta_fails`. - **Positives (derived):** `append_only_witness_holds_on_the_selftest_bridge`; `ads_extract_verifies_and_reimports_byte_identically` (on a `statement` variant of `_selftest`); `beancount_export_refolds_through_fa_verify_export`; `finding_export_replays_for_d_reads`. - **Runner output:** one line per (expectation, variant, target, cell) in A7a's notation, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN / `, where a T's projection includes `outsider=:verified|failed` (2a), every T and R row `gql=ok|fail|not_run(pending holds)`, and a restatement-case T `append_only=ok|fail` (step 6). Every `fa-verify`, `fa replay` and `fa verify` invocation is a JSONL step (§3.5) with `argv_redacted`, `exit` and `certificate_kind`; `VERIFY.txt` is generated from those records. Failures print the exact argv; the JSONL log path is printed at the end (§16). ## Notes - **← A7b:** issuance, the restatement lifecycle, case diff and bitemporal reads produce the certificates checked here. **← A8a:** the `_selftest` bridge, with its checkpoint, bundle, `fa_verify`, replay and `fa verify book`, is the fixture. - **← A11b:** the positive (the first green T) needs the contributing-entry witness, so A12 waits on A11b (§15: A12 ← A7b, A8a, A11b). - **External edges (§15 Phase H):** "§12.7's differential ← fa-sa4w; §12.1's ADS wording ← fa-ipom". They gate those sub-steps only: the differential reports UNRUN until fa-sa4w's harness exists, and the ADS wording names fa-ipom. They are listed under related, not deps, so that the walking skeleton's first green T does not wait on them. - **Scope:** §15's A12 scope list does not repeat §12.7's second read path and interop identity, but A12 is the only item that cites §12.7, so this bead carries them. §12.6 litigation production is optional and is not part of A12. - **fa-70h4** ("outsider-verifiable certified reports") is open at 8196f5e40, yet `fa bundle produce --certificate` (`registries/verbs.toml:784`) and `fa-verify report` (`crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:151`, `:1294`) already exist. A12 uses those surfaces and relates to fa-70h4 without waiting on it. **fa-kkxl** applies the same honesty rule (UNRUN unless cells were compared). - **More related beads (tracker search, polish round 4).** None plans A12's work, which composes their surfaces; each one's change moves the step that uses it. - **fa-qtfd** (witnessed checkpoints, open; FA-INV-14.witnessed live per its 2026-10-24 comment) owns `fa checkpoint witness` and fa-verify's quorum check, which step 6 runs. - **fa-2q91** (`fa export ads --with-proofs`, open; slice 1 landed per its 2026-10-22 comment, the account-month positive not done) owns the ADS proof sidecar step 3 verifies; step 3 uses the period scope only. - **fa-0m9r** (offline scenario-diff verification, open) is what an outsider needs to verify a scenario expectation without the source book. Until it lands, step 2's scenario check is an in-book `fa replay C:` of the `fa scenario diff` certificate, reported as such and never as an outsider verification. - **Plan vs code (polish round 5).** §12.7 says every second read is `fa query --certify`, including R rows `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` and Lehman's `AT BRANCH`; at 8196f5e40 the profile certifies neither (verbs.toml:652's usage, above), so step 7 certifies the view's resolved sequence and compares the branch read uncertified. §12.1 names no outsider route for an export or a consolidation; step 2a gives `round_trip` the balance-sheet certificate's route (X4 proposed `outsider=not_applicable`) and the consolidation certificate an in-book replay (C3). - **Code check at 8196f5e40:** `pub fn run(args: &[String], read: Read<'_>) -> Output` is at `crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700`, as §12.1 cites; `report` takes `--key`, `--receipt`, `--checkpoint`, `--expect`, `--units` (`cli.rs:207`). The witness usage at `registries/verbs.toml:760` is `checkpoint witness --key [--state ] [--previous …] [--onto …] --out --grant witness`, matching §12.7's `--key k … --grant witness`. - **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases -- _selftest`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the `_selftest` statement book. - **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: with A11b present, the `_selftest` bridge T row prints PASS (the program's first green T run, now claimed in `_selftest/case.toml`): `fa-verify bundle` and `fa-verify report` exit 0 as literal argv through `fa_verify::cli::run`, the report's recomputed line equals B, and `fa replay` reproduces the report bytes.
- [ ] positive: on the `_selftest` bridge the append-only witness holds: w2 cosigns with `--previous w1`, `fa-verify checkpoint --quorum 1` exits 0, the consistency and inclusion proofs verify, and `fa certificate status` reports SupersededBy with `later_entries` equal to the case's Δ entries; the GQL second read equals the fold; the ADS extract verifies and re-imports byte-identically.
- [ ] negative: the FA-REF-124 twin (`--previous` set to another book's witness statement) is observed, exit 8.
- [ ] negative: a corrupted bundle fails the case whatever its expectations say, `fa verify book` exiting 8 fails the case, and a `VERIFY.txt` listing a command the run did not execute fails the kit gate.
- [ ] positive (derived): every T read verb maps to one outsider route (`report`, `replay`, `replay+bundle` for `gl detail`; `round_trip` through the balance-sheet certificate at the export's instant; a consolidation certificate replayed byte for byte), and a verb outside the table leaves its T UNRUN, never PASS; the GQL second read certifies stock, activity and a view's resolved sequence, and compares a scenario branch read uncertified.
- [ ] no-claim: the outsider checks show that the produced artifacts verify offline and replay byte for byte within the run; they do not show that the book reflects the historical record. The GQL cross-check is two FA read paths agreeing, never independent evidence.

title: [cases] A13: capability coverage gate (declared ⊆ exercised per case) and registry closure over case_coverage.toml: 68 procedures, 81 verbs
description:
## Why

The owner asked for case studies "showing off ALL the deep functionality" (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §0.1). §12.2 answers that honestly: a capability counts as exercised only if some passing expectation's verdict depends on its output, so a verb that merely ran does not count. This answers the project's own precedent, "the registry check proves names, not behavior" (`crates/fa-cli/tests/readme.rs:19`). The dependency comes from the contributing-entry, mutation-twin and kernel-twin witnesses (§3.7 items 2–4) and from the outsider checks (§12.1), which is why A11a, A11b, A11c and A12 are dependencies. Registry closure makes the docs render both what the cases exercise and what they cannot, with equal prominence, and where it is exercised instead. It covers the capabilities behind every claim type; the table retires with the program.

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_coverage.toml`, a harness table embedded like those of §2.4 (`schema_version = 1`, a Consumer (A14's coverage table, A14b's Limits) / Gate (the two tests below) / Retire (with the program) header, `include_str!`).
- `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_coverage_tests.sha256`: one `<sha256>  <path>` line per test file a `covered_by` names (the pin, below).
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/coverage.rs`: the loader, `pub fn closure(rows, procedures, verbs) -> CheckReport` (structural), and `pub fn exercised(rows, verdicts: &[VerdictRecord]) -> Vec<RowVerdict>` (the "passed in the last run" half). Procedures come from `fa_registry::procedures::Procedures::embedded()`; verbs from `registries/verbs.toml`'s `[[verb]]` rows, read raw with `fa_registry::toml::parse` (fa-oracles cannot link fa-cli's verb registry).
- Tests: `coverage_rows_close_over_procedures_and_verbs` (unit, fa-oracles) and `coverage_declared_subset_of_exercised` plus `coverage_exercised_rows_passed` (cross-cutting, `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`).

**Per case.** Each `case.toml` declares the capabilities it exercises (A1a's token grammar `<kind>:<name>[@<version>]`: verbs, procedures with versions, refusal ids, laws, bitemporal selectors, case kinds, statement kinds and export formats). The cross-cutting test asserts *declared ⊆ exercised* per case, where a capability is exercised when an expectation of that case whose verdict is PASS lists it in the `witnesses` of one of its verdict records (the runner records, per line, the capabilities whose output its witnesses read: the read verb and selector for a T via its contributing-entry and outsider checks, the procedure for a D or N via the finding projection and twin, the refusal and law row for a P).
- **Expectation verdicts.** A7a writes one verdict record per (expectation, variant, target, cell) line, and an expectation's verdict is the worst of its lines (FAIL > UNRUN > PASS). Every "passed" in this item means that expectation verdict, never one line's: an expectation with one PASS cell and one UNRUN cell (a `pending` cell, A1c, or a missing witness) is UNRUN, so none of its capabilities counts as exercised.

**Registry closure.** One row per `[[procedure]]` in `registries/procedures.toml` (68) and one per verb or verb subcommand in `registries/verbs.toml` (81 verbs; 206 subcommands, so 243 verb rows, one per subcommand of a verb that has them and one per verb that has none). Row fields: `kind` (`procedure` | `verb`), `id` (`<procedure id>` or `<verb>[ <subcommand>]`), `status`, `expectations` (one-line array), `reason`, `covered_by`, `bead`. Each row is exactly one of:
- `exercised`: the expectation ids whose verdicts depend on it. The row passes only if each passed in the last run (its expectation verdict, above); an UNRUN expectation makes the row UNRUN.
- `not_exercisable`: a `reason` from a closed set, plus `covered_by` naming the fa-gen scenario or motif (`crates/fa-gen/src/lib.rs:130-136`, `:412-425`), the fa-demo scenario (one of the seven `fa_demo::SCENARIO_NAMES`), or the existing test that does exercise it, as `<path>::<test fn>`. Reasons:
  - `no_public_data`: the public record holds no population of the kind the predicate reads;
  - `population_relative`: tier P or A over a population the record does not give completely;
  - `needs_judgment`: an input the auditor states and the record does not, such as tolerable misstatement (`registries/verbs.toml:724`);
  - `law_absent`: no law or procedure exists; the row names its §13 bead in `bead`;
  - `adds_no_claim`: it runs in setup, but no expectation could depend on it;
  - `research`: the row names its bead in `bead`.

The closure test fails on: a registry row without a coverage row; a coverage row naming no registry row; a row with both statuses' fields or neither; an `exercised` row whose expectations did not pass.

**Seed.** Appendix Z.5.1, by procedure family. Every `covered_by` must name an existing test that actually runs the procedure, found in the fa-lantern and fa-gen tests: the closure test checks that the named file exists, contains `fn <test fn>`, and mentions the procedure id.

**Verdict soundness of the `covered_by` check.** That check reads other crates' test sources at runtime. `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` builds fa-oracles' input hash from the global inputs and the trees of fa-oracles and its workspace dependencies (`:216-228`), and fa-lantern and fa-gen are not among them, so a renamed test in fa-lantern alone would leave the input hash unchanged and reuse a stale green verdict (`:231`); a pin file by itself changes nothing until fa-oracles' tests run. So the closure test also embeds a `covered_by` file with a literal `include_str!` (for example the fa-lantern test file most rows name): an `include_str!` target outside the crate marks fa-oracles `undeclared_external_read`, which never reuses a cached verdict (`:16-19`, `:152-179`, `:231`), as A9 does for the fetch tool and `crates/fa-cli/tests/readme.rs:31` for `README.md`. Every gate then re-runs the check. `case_coverage_tests.sha256` holds the SHA-256 of every file a `covered_by` names, and the closure test fails when a file's hash differs, naming the file to re-check, so a green run records the exact test bytes it checked.

**"The last run".** The cross-cutting tests take the verdicts from A7a's memoized `outcome(case)` for every committed case, so they read the verdicts of the same `cargo test` invocation, never a stale log. An expectation absent from those verdicts counts as UNRUN.

**Consumer, gate, retire.** Consumer: the coverage table of `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` (rendered by A14). Gates: the per-case assertion and the closure test. It retires with the program.

## Tests & logging

- **Negative (§15):** `procedures_copy_with_a_new_row_fails_the_closure`: a test-only `procedures.toml` copy (through `Procedures::from_text`) with one added `[[procedure]]` → `FAIL coverage procedure <id>: registry row without a coverage row`.
- **Derived negatives (§12.2):** `coverage_row_naming_no_registry_row_fails`; `exercised_row_citing_an_unrun_expectation_is_unrun`; `expectation_with_one_unrun_cell_exercises_nothing` (a fixture expectation whose lines are PASS on one cell and UNRUN on another: its expectation verdict is UNRUN, and an `exercised` row citing it prints UNRUN); `covered_by_naming_a_missing_test_fails`; `covered_by_file_changed_without_its_pin_fails`; `_selftest_neg_declared_capability_without_a_passing_dependent_fails` (a `run_planted` copy of `_selftest` whose `case.toml` declares `procedure:benford.first_digit@2`, which no passing expectation depends on → `FAIL coverage _selftest procedure:benford.first_digit@2: declared but not exercised`; the test calls `.expect_err(…)`, A7a); `verb_subcommand_without_a_row_fails` (a verbs.toml copy with an added subcommand).
- **Placement:** the structural closure (registry rows ↔ coverage rows, the `covered_by` existence and pin checks) is the unit test in `fa-oracles`. The "passed in the last run" half and declared ⊆ exercised run with the runner as cross-cutting `#[test]`s in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs` (§3.1: one test per cross-cutting check).
- **Output:** one line per coverage row, `COVERAGE <kind> <id> PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <status> [<expectation ids>|<reason> covered_by=<…>]`; failures name the registry row; a final `COVERAGE rows=<n> exercised=<n> not_exercisable=<n> unrun=<n>`.

## Notes

- **Why each edge:** A7a (the runner, its verdict records and `outcome`); A11a, A11b, A11c and A12 supply the witnesses through which a verdict "depends on" a capability.
- **Counts checked at 8196f5e40:** 68 `[[procedure]]` rows; 81 `[[verb]]` rows with 206 subcommands. Appendix Z.5.1's "other singletons (7)" row lists events.subsequent, expense.capitalization, completeness.unrecorded_liabilities, party.master_changes, payroll.ghost, reversal.patterns and confirm.coverage, which matches the seven singleton families in the registry; the family counts sum to 68.
- **Risk: the gate binds every future registry edit.** Once closure lands, any bead that adds a procedure, verb or subcommand fails this test until a coverage row is added. That is the intended gate, but landers of unrelated beads must know it; the failure line names the missing row.
- **fa-kkxl** (retract false oracle claims) is the precedent for this honesty rule: names are not behaviour.
- **H3.** A `covered_by` naming a fa-demo scenario must name one of the seven that `Scenario::parse` accepts (H3 corrects the usage text that lists more).
- Rendering of the coverage table is A14's; the Limits section's not_exercisable rows are A14b's.
- **Version bumps.** H1, H2 and H18 bump procedure versions without adding rows, so the closure stays green; but a case's declared `procedure:<id>@<version>` token names the version, so their landings update the declaring `case.toml` (M5, L4) in the same change.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the data and pin files.
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `case_coverage.toml` holds exactly one row for each of the 68 procedures and each of the 243 verb/subcommand pairs of the 81 verbs, each `exercised` (with expectation ids that passed in the same `cargo test` invocation) or `not_exercisable` (with a closed-set reason and a `covered_by` naming an existing test, fa-gen motif/scenario or fa-demo scenario, the named test files pinned by hash); every case passes declared ⊆ exercised.
- [ ] negative: a test-only `procedures.toml` copy with a new row fails the closure test.
- [ ] negative: an `exercised` row citing an UNRUN expectation reports UNRUN, where an expectation's verdict is the worst of its per-cell lines (one UNRUN cell makes it UNRUN); a `covered_by` naming a nonexistent test fails; a `covered_by` test file changed without its pin fails, and fa-oracles is reported `undeclared_external_read` by `scripts/crate_verdicts.py`, so that check is never skipped by a reused verdict.
- [ ] no-claim: a `not_exercisable` row records a reason; it does not prove that no public source exists.

title: [cases] A1a: crates/fa-oracles crate (topology flip, allowlist, SHA-256 + FIPS vectors), Source/Fact/Value/Receipt and case.toml/roles.toml loaders
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A1a, §3.1, §3.2, §3.2a, §2.1–§2.3, §2.8, §4.1, §4.4.

This is the first slice of the harness crate. The case model (schema, loader, validators, derivation engine, filler, branch enumeration, expectation evaluation, citation stubs, README renderer) lives in `crates/fa-oracles`, module `cases` (§3.1). The plan gives four reasons:
- `fa-oracles` is already a planned row of the verification layer (`registries/workspace_topology.toml:202-206`, `planned = true`), and COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN §18.1 names it.
- Public-record tie-outs are exactly the external oracles of COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN §16.
- The topology pin test (`crates/fa-registry/src/topology.rs:160-235`) pins names and layers to §18.1, so a new crate name would need a plan edit.
- `fa-conformance` (the substrate behaviour suite) and `fa-reference` (the independent oracle, which must stay independent) are the wrong homes.

The Source / Fact / Value / Receipt types carry the provenance model (§2.1); the `case.toml` header and `roles.toml` carry the case's identity, kind and role labels (§3.2, §2.8). The first rule that makes the harness honest is "every expectation is tied to sourced facts" (§0.2), so every claim type (D/P/T/C/R/N/CF, §0.3) rests on these types. Engine independence follows `fa-reference`'s reasoning (`crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:3-14`): a bug shared with the engine must not be able to make a tie-out agree. The data format is the registries' TOML subset, not JSON. Its parser is public, std-only and gives canonical bytes; it allows comments, where JSON would push every rationale into string fields; and every other hand-authored data file in the repository already uses it (§3.1).

## What to build
1. **Create the crate** (§3.1 "Creating the crate"):
   - `crates/fa-oracles/Cargo.toml`: `name = "fa-oracles"`, `version = "0.0.1"`, `edition`/`license-file`/`repository` from the workspace, `publish = false`, `[lints] workspace = true`, and one dependency, `fa-registry = { path = "../fa-registry", version = "=0.0.1" }`. `fa-reference` and `fa-time` are added by A4r, their first user; the allowlist below already admits them.
   - add `"crates/fa-oracles"` to the root `Cargo.toml` `members` (and the resulting `Cargo.lock` entry);
   - in `registries/workspace_topology.toml`, flip the row's `planned = true` to `planned = false` and add `allowlist = ["fa-registry", "fa-reference", "fa-time"]`. The existing `topology` step of `scripts/check.sh` (`scripts/topology_check.sh`) enforces both. This is the plan's allowlist (§3.1, which added `fa-time` after polish round 2), because fa-reference's public API takes fa-time types (`Oracle::new(calendar: FiscalCalendar)`, `crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1037`; `Intent.date: DateDay`, `:429-447`; `lantern::Row.date`, `crates/fa-reference/src/lantern.rs:22-46`), so A4r cannot build the oracle's inputs without naming fa-time. fa-time is a foundation crate (dates and calendars), the one fa-reference itself is allowlisted to, not an engine crate, so the independence argument of §3.1 is unchanged. Adding it now keeps the program to one topology edit and one global invalidation, instead of a second one in A4r;
   - `src/lib.rs` starts with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` (AGENTS.md doctrine 2; `scripts/doctrine_check.sh` rule 5 checks every crate root);
   - add `"fa-oracles"` to the no-float crate list of `scripts/doctrine_check.sh` (`amount_crates`, `:93-108`), so doctrine 4 is enforced on the harness's own arithmetic. That is a script edit, not a registry edit.
2. **Engine independence (§3.1).**
   - fa-oracles does its own exact integer arithmetic: checked i128 at each unit's declared scale, the scale read from `fa_registry::units_embedded()` (`crates/fa-registry/src/lib.rs:1107-1121`, `UnitRow.scale`).
   - It has its own minimal JSON reader (A7a, its first user), its own SHA-256 (here) and its own canonical renderers.
   - It never links `fa-money`, `fa-model`, `fa-cli` or the substrate; the topology allowlist refuses any such edge. Its first-party closure is fa-registry, fa-time and fa-reference (fa-reference depends only on fa-time and fa-registry). fa-oracles uses fa-time types only at the fa-reference boundary (A4r); its own derivations keep their own date arithmetic (A2), so a shared date bug cannot make a derived date agree with the engine.
   - **Own SHA-256.** It is std-only and tested against the FIPS 180-4 vectors. fa-oracles needs its own because the only workspace implementation is private (`crates/fa-docket/src/intake.rs:566`). It lands here because A3a, A3c, A4 and A6 all hash (§15 A1a).
3. **Files and public API** (all introduced here; every public type is reachable by a `pub` path, because the workspace denies `unnameable_types`, `Cargo.toml:58`):
   - `src/lib.rs`: `pub mod sha256; pub mod cases;`.
   - `src/sha256.rs`: `pub fn digest(bytes: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32]`, `pub fn hex(digest: &[u8; 32]) -> String` (lower-case), and the FIPS 180-4 vector table as data (`pub const FIPS_180_4_VECTORS`) with `pub fn check_vectors(table) -> Result<(), String>`, which names the first vector whose computed digest differs.
   - `src/cases/mod.rs`: `pub struct Case { header, sources, facts, values, receipts, roles, … }` and `pub fn load(files: &CaseFiles) -> Result<Case, Vec<LoadError>>`, where `CaseFiles { id, files: &[(relative path, text)] }` lets a test load an edited copy. Later items add `books` (A1b) and `expectations` (A1c) to `Case`.
   - `src/cases/error.rs`: `pub struct LoadError { file, line: Option<usize>, kind: LoadErrorKind, row: Option<String>, detail }`, displayed as `<file>:<line>: <kind>: <detail>`. Kinds introduced here: `Toml` (wraps `fa_registry::toml::TomlError`, keeping its line), `MissingField`, `UnknownField`, `WrongType`, `UnknownValue` (outside a closed set), `TwoProvenanceKinds`, `DanglingKey`, `NotSha256Hex`, `ReceiptMismatch`, `DuplicateId`. Every error is collected, sorted by (file, line), never only the first.
   - `src/cases/rows.rs`: `pub fn row_line(text: &str, array: &str, index: usize) -> Option<usize>`, the 1-based line of the `index`-th `[[array]]` header. `fa_registry::toml::Document` keeps no line numbers (`crates/fa-registry/src/toml.rs:56-60`), so every semantic error (a dangling key, two provenance kinds) gets its line from this helper; the parser's own `TomlError.line` covers syntax errors.
   - `src/cases/source.rs` (`Source`, `RetrievalRoute`, `AssertionStatus`, `AnchorKind`, `SourceStatus`), `src/cases/fact.rs` (`Fact`, `Provenance` = `Sourced | Interpretation | Derived | Synthetic`, `Granularity`, `Value`), `src/cases/receipt.rs` (`Receipt`), `src/cases/header.rs` (`CaseHeader`, `CaseKind`), `src/cases/roles.rs` (`Roles`, `Role`, the hashed deny list).
   - Each typed file has `fn to_document(&self) -> fa_registry::toml::Document`, used by the canonical-bytes round trip below.
   - `src/cases/embedded.rs`: the embedded index, `pub const CASES: &[EmbeddedCase]`, one `include_str!` literal per committed file under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<dir>/`, generated files included (`receipts.toml`, M2t's `exhibit_b_rows.toml`, the rendered `README.md` and `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`) (`include_str!` needs literal paths, so every later item that commits a case file adds its line here). It is empty at A1a; `_selftest` (A7a) is its first entry.
4. **Types and loaders** over `fa_registry::toml::parse` (`crates/fa-registry/src/lib.rs:29`, `toml.rs:155`). Unknown keys in any row are refused (`UnknownField`), so a misspelled field is never silently ignored.
   - **Source** (`sources.toml`, §4.1): `id`, `title`, `publisher`, `original_url`, `archive_url?`, `retrieval_route` (`original` / `archive_capture` / `third_party_copy` / `re_render`), `original_hash_compared`, `retrieved_utc`, `sha256`, `format`, `extraction` (a one-line array: tool, version, SHA-256 of the extracted text), `redistribution_basis`, `assertion_status` (the closed set of §2.2), `assurance` (filer statements only: `audited`, `reviewed`, `unaudited` or `not-from-audited`, §4.1; empty on a row that is not a filer statement) with `assurance_fact` (the sourced fact whose sentence establishes it), `anchor_scheme` (a one-line array of the anchor kinds its facts use: `page{printed page, line range}`, `line{range}`, `table_cell{table, row label, column label}`, `xbrl{concept, context id}`, `paragraph{¶ number}` for complaints and indictments, and `exhibit{label, page range}` for a whole table of rows, below), `status` (`OK` / `BLOCKED`, with `status_reason` for BLOCKED), `notes`. Facts may cite only `OK` rows (§4.1). §4.1 also lists, for K-VINTAGE (§3.6, A3b), `filed_on` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the filing or publication date; empty for a source that is not a filing) and `restates` (a one-line array of the source ids whose figures this filing restates; each must resolve to a source row of the case, `DanglingKey`). Sentence alignment applies to the prose kinds (`page`, `line`, `paragraph`); a `table_cell` or `xbrl` fact binds by exact cell or fact value instead (§4.1), and an `exhibit` fact binds its rows by the rows-block hash (below) and each row by value (M2a's receipt booleans).
   - **Anchor strings.** A1a fixes one grammar per kind, which A9 writes and A3a parses: `page` = `p<printed page>:l<first>-<last>`; `line` = `l<first>-<last>`; `paragraph` = `para<n>`; `table_cell` = `<table>|<row label>|<column label>`; `xbrl` = `<concept>|<context id>`; `exhibit` = `<exhibit or table label>|p<first page>-<last page>` (the printed pages the rows span, for example the Glantz Exhibits B-1 … B-6, M2a). A string that does not parse under its kind is refused (`WrongType`). `exhibit` is accepted only on a fact that carries `rows_file`, and a fact that carries `rows_file` must use it (`WrongType` either way): neither `page` (one printed page) nor `table_cell` (one cell) spells a page range (M2a).
   - **Fact** (`facts.toml` `[[fact]]`, §2.1): `id`, `provenance`, and exactly that kind's flattened fields:
     - `sourced`: `source`, `anchor_kind`, `anchor`, `quote_sha256`, `quote` (optional until owner decision 2a), `about_scope`, `granularity` (§2.3: `journal_entry`, `dated_aggregate`, `period_total`, `statement_line`, `xbrl_fact`, `ledger_row`), optional `role = "oracle_output"` (§2.1), and, for `statement_line`, `xbrl_fact` and `period_total` facts, `cell`: a vintage-independent key `<key>@<date or period label>`, so K-VINTAGE can compare the same published cell across vintages (§3.6 needs it; §2.1 does not list it). `<key>` is one or more segments of letters, digits, `_` and `-` joined by `.` (a line, or a line and a sub-line: E2d's Δ form `<line>.<adjustment slug>` and EX-27 form `equity.<tag>`), optionally followed by `:<member>`, an XBRL dimension member's local name (X1 and C0: `<concept local name>[:<member local name>]`, which keeps the previously-reported A and the adjustment Δ apart from the undimensioned B) or a printed column's slug (C2: `<line>:<column>`). Examples: `total_assets@2000-12-31`, `NetIncomeLoss:RestatementAdjustmentMember@<period label>`. A `cell` that does not parse is refused (`WrongType`), and two facts of one source with the same `cell` are refused (`DuplicateId`), because K-VINTAGE pairs one fact per (source, cell). The member in `cell` is the pairing key only; `verify` checks it against the fact's XBRL context (A9). And, for a fact that stands for a whole table of rows, `rows_file` (the generated rows file under the case directory, for example `exhibit_b_rows.toml`) and `complaint` (the source id whose rows block it holds; the name is M2t's per-row field, and on a series fact it equals the fact's `source`). Two granularities admit them: `ledger_row` (a complaint's Exhibit B rows, M2a–M2c, M2t) and `dated_aggregate` (a dated series committed as one series fact, L1's `V874-FN3365` and `A17E`; §3.2 names entries derived from a `dated_aggregate` series as the other `ledger` source). Such a fact's `quote_sha256` is M2t's `rows_sha256`: the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of that source's contiguous `[[row]]` block in `rows_file`, from its first `[[row]]` header line through the newline ending its last field line, so `verify` (Python) and K-BIND (Rust) hash the same slice and neither ports the other's TOML canonicalization (round 2's "canonical `[[row]]` bytes" is replaced; M2t pins one digest in both languages). The two fields are refused on any other granularity (`UnknownField`). A rows file absent from the tree (whole tables wait on OD 2b, §3.2b) is not a load error: the fact loads with `rows_committed = false`, the checks that read its rows report UNRUN for it, and the runner prints every expectation whose basis reaches it UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` (A7a);
     - `interpretation`: `from`, `reader`, `second_reader`, `rationale`;
     - `derived`: `from`, `rule`, `params`;
     - `synthetic`: `reason`, `discipline`.

     A row carrying a field of a second kind is refused at load (`TwoProvenanceKinds`), because the typed `Provenance` cannot hold it. Required fields and value sets per kind are K-PROV's (A3a), which reports the rows it examined.
   - **Assurance per fact.** §2.2 determines assurance "from the filing itself … from its audit report, review report or legend", and one filing can carry several: SRC-ENR-008's selected-data cells beside its audited statements (E1, E2d), a 10-Q's comparative year-end column beside its reviewed interim column (L1, which determines that column's assurance from the filing). So a `sourced` fact of a filer-statement source may carry its own `assurance` (the source row's value set) with its own `assurance_fact`, a sourced fact of the same source whose sentence or legend establishes it; a fact `assurance` without its `assurance_fact`, with an `assurance_fact` of another source, or on a source row whose `assurance` is empty is refused (`MissingField`, `DanglingKey`, `UnknownValue`). The rendered precedence is K-ASSERT's (A3c), three levels: a T's own `assurance` (A1c; X1's per-line rule writes it), then its published fact's `assurance`, then the source row's. The vocabularies differ: a T's `assurance` uses §2.2's statuses (`filer_audited`, `filer_unaudited`, …; §10.1 writes X-T-01's per-line values so), while the fact and source fields use §4.1's `audited`, `reviewed`, `unaudited` and `not-from-audited`, which K-ASSERT maps to `filer_audited`, `filer_reviewed`, `filer_unaudited` and `filer_not_from_audited_statements`.
   - **Assurance facts.** A fact named by an `assurance_fact` is an ordinary `sourced` fact and carries the granularity of the facts its sentence governs (a statements legend: `statement_line`; a tagged instance's HTML heading: `xbrl_fact`), M1's rule for header and footnote facts; §2.3's six tags are not extended. A heading-only legend (SRC-ENR-002's "UNAUDITED", E1) is anchored `page` or `line` on the heading's own line(s), and its quote is the whole heading line; whether the sentence splitter treats such a line as one sentence is A3a's and A9's rule.
   - **Value** (`[[value]]` rows, foreign keys to their fact): `fact`, `ordinal` (1-based within the fact, the `<ordinal>` of A1b's `value:<fact>#<ordinal>`; a numbering separate from A1b's 0-based leg ordinals), `literal` (the text as it appears in the quote), `rule` (the literal rule it is read under: `scale`, `date_literal`, `date_range_literal`, `month_literal`, `number_word`, `period_literal`; §2.4), `param` (the rule's integer parameter, for example the power k of `scale`), `value` (the canonical result: an integer string at the unit's scale, a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, a closed day range `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD`, a month `YYYY-MM`, or a period label), `unit` (empty for dates and periods), and `precision` (the power of ten of the stated precision, for example 6 for "stated to $1M"). A2's rules consume these fields; K-BIND (A3a) checks them against the quote or receipt.
     - **Unitless values** (a printed count before a caption's multiplier applies, a multiplier, a ratio, a percentage) have `unit = ""` and `value` an integer string in units of 10^`precision`: a $M table cell printed `327,774` is `value = "327774"`, `precision = 0` (its dollar amount is a separate `derived` fact under A2's two-input `scale`, L1); a ratio printed `13.9x` is `value = "139"`, `precision = -1` (tenths; L1, L3's L-C-01); an EX-27 MULTIPLIER printed `1,000,000` is `value = "1000000"`, `precision = 0` (W2). `precision` may be negative only on a unitless value (`WrongType`). A date or period value also has `unit = ""`; its `rule` (a date or period rule, never `scale` or `number_word`) tells the two apart, and a unitless `value` that is not an integer string is refused (`WrongType`).
   - **Receipt** (`receipts.toml`, GENERATED by `case_fetch.py verify`, never hand-edited, §4.4): one `[[receipt]]` per sourced fact, with `source`, `fact`, `anchor` (the page or line range the quote was found at, which K-ANCHOR checks), `verified_utc` (a string: the cache entry's fetch time, not the run's clock), `tool_version`, `extraction_sha256`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (SHA-256 of the fact's canonical values bytes, below, so K-BIND detects offline a value or scope edited after `verify`), `alignment` (`sentence` for prose anchors, `value` for `table_cell`, `xbrl` and `exhibit` facts), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok`, and `original_hash_compared`, copied from the source's `sources.toml` row (false for an archive capture until OD 1) (§4.4 after polish round 2). The loader cross-checks: the receipt's `fact` exists and is `sourced`; its `source` is that fact's source; its `alignment` is the one its fact's `anchor_kind` implies; its `original_hash_compared` equals the source row's (else `ReceiptMismatch`); `quote_sha256` and `values_sha256` are 64-hex (`NotSha256Hex`). Recomputing `values_sha256` against the facts is K-BIND's (A3a).
   - **Canonical values bytes** (`src/cases/fact.rs`, `pub fn values_canonical(fact, values) -> Vec<u8>`, shared with A9's writer): `fa:case-values:v1`, a newline, `about_scope=<about_scope>`, a newline, then one line per `[[value]]` row of the fact in `ordinal` order, the fields `ordinal`, `literal`, `rule`, `param`, `value`, `unit`, `precision` joined by one U+0009 TAB, each line ending in a newline. `values_sha256` is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of those bytes. A1a creates `crates/fa-oracles/data/binding_fixtures.toml` (embedded, `schema_version = 1`, Consumer/Gate/Retire header) with its `[[values]]` rows (`id`, `about_scope`, `value_lines` as a one-line array of the TAB-joined lines, `canonical_hex`, `values_sha256`); A3a and A9 add their `[[normalize]]`, `[[sentence]]` and `[[scope]]` suites to the same file and test both implementations on identical bytes.
   - **Case header** (`case.toml`, §3.2): `id`, `letter`, `title`, `version`, `kind` (`case` | `harness_selftest`), `scope`, `claims` (one-line array of expectation ids), `capabilities` (one-line array of tokens `<kind>:<name>[@<version>]`, kinds `verb`, `procedure`, `refusal`, `law`, `selector`, `case_kind`, `statement`, `export`; read by A13), `pinned_commit`, `variants` (the book-variant stems). All of these are required (`MissingField`), `letter` only for `kind = "case"`; `claims`, `capabilities` and `variants` may be empty one-line arrays, so a case's first item writes the header with `[]` (E1, M1) and later items fill them (X1's "X3 and X5 add" fills X1's empty arrays). `kind = "harness_selftest"` is what exempts `_selftest` from K-BASIS (A3b, A8a). Optional fields added by later items, which the loader accepts once their item lands (each item extends the header's field table in `header.rs`): `reader`, `no_claims`, `expected_limits`, `raised` (A14b).
   - **Case ids and letters (§3.2b).** A case's `id` is its directory name: `worldcom`, `xbrl`, `enron`, `lehman`, `blmis`, `mergers`, `_selftest`. Its `letter` (W, X, E, L, M, C) prefixes every expectation id and every runner-generated row id (`W-D-01`, `W-NOTE-01`, `W-SELF-native`, `W-CASE-<case id>`, `W-N-90`). `letter` is required and unique for `kind = "case"`. The plan names no letter for the self-test; this round fixes that a `harness_selftest` case carries no `letter` and its id is its prefix (`_selftest-T-01`, `_selftest-SELF-native`), the spelling A7a, A8a and M0 already use. The loader refuses a `case.toml` whose `id` differs from the `CaseFiles` id it was loaded under (the directory name for a committed case, the declared id for a fixture: the pilot is `worldcom`), a `case` without a letter or with one outside {W, X, E, L, M, C}, and a letter on a `harness_selftest` case (`UnknownValue`).

E4's vintage decision, E5's candidate and `E5-outcome` rows (`runs_E-N-02`, `runs_E-D-02`, `runs_E-N-03` booleans and `native_calendar_from`) and X3's two-book decision use it.

A key neither in the header table nor in its case's extension row is refused (`UnknownField`), naming the case.
     The checks on those values (counts recomputed, flags consistent) are the case items' own load-time tests.

A1b's `[[principal]] label`, `[[party]] label` and step principals resolve against these labels; A3c's K-NAMES reads the hashes.

Also a two-block message whose length crosses the 55/56-byte padding boundary.
