title: [cases] R-TRACE: research a free public tracing computation (LIBR, FIFO or pro rata) for a trace.<law> T, else a decision record
description:
## Why

The trace family is otherwise not honestly exercisable on public records: "No public source gives a commingled-account series together with a court's computed traceable amount. Forcing the trustee's transfer rule through `trace.libr` would mislabel the law, which is the reasoning of H5. → research R-TRACE (§12.2), else fa-gen tests" (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md Appendix Z.5.1). A court- or receiver-computed traceable amount would be an externally labelled result of the kind fa-gen cannot supply (§12.4). The claim type at stake is T, an exact tie-out against a published, separately sourced figure. The item is bounded: it either finds such a source or closes with a decision record.

## What to build

- Find a free, public court opinion or receiver report (not PACER) that states a deposit/withdrawal series and the traceable amount computed under LIBR, FIFO or pro rata (§15 R-TRACE).
- Acceptable sources follow §0.5 (no paywalled, login-gated, leaked or sealed material) and §4.1 (an `OK` sources row with `original_url`, `retrieval_route`, `sha256`, `redistribution_basis`, `assertion_status` such as `court_ruling` or `trustee_computation`).
- **If one exists:** record it as a sources row, with anchors for the series and the computed amount, and name the `trace.<law>` procedure the T would run against it.
  - At 8196f5e40 the family is `trace.libr`, `trace.fifo`, `trace.lifo`, `trace.pro_rata`, `trace.network_fifo`, `trace.network_lifo`, `trace.network_libr`, `trace.network_pro_rata`, `trace.restitution_order` (`registries/procedures.toml`, id rows `:372`–`:735`).
  - The court's or receiver's method must map to a law row of `registries/tracing_laws.toml` (codes `libr` `:17`, `fifo` `:28`, `lifo` `:39`, `pro_rata` `:50` and `restitution_order` `:61`, each with its citation, presumption and rounding law; checked at 8196f5e40). The record states the mapping and whether the source's intraday ordering and replenishment treatment match the row's; a mismatch is a reason to reject, not to adapt.
  - The published traceable amount is never posted (K-TAUT).
- **Otherwise:** close with a decision record listing the candidates examined and why each fails.

**Search protocol.**
- Free, public routes only: court websites, government sites, receivership websites, and opinion texts republished by a court-run or government site. Never PACER, a login or a paywall (§0.5).
- Every web request uses the project User-Agent `franken_accounting-agent (+https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_accounting)` (AGENTS.md). Each document read is hashed (SHA-256) and the hash recorded.

**Where the record lives.** As one comment on this bead (`br comments add <id> …`), the tracker's record, as the owner-decision bead records decisions. It has one row per candidate examined:
- title and court or receiver;
- URL and access route;
- SHA-256;
- whether it gives a deposit/withdrawal series;
- whether it gives a computed traceable amount;
- the named method and its `tracing_laws.toml` mapping;
- verdict and reason.

The comment ends with the decision (found / not found) and the follow-on bead id if found. The close reason cites the comment. No `docs/` file is created: the repository has no research-record convention under `docs/`.

## Tests & logging

- Research item: it closes on a decision record, not on code. If a source is found, the T and its runner rows (the `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN …` line of §16, contributing-entry and outsider witnesses) land in a follow-on case bead; R-TRACE carries none of the T machinery's edges (A3b, A7b, A11b, A12), so a T cannot be green inside it.
- The source row, if any, gets its receipt through `case_fetch.py verify` (A9) in that follow-on. The follow-on bead's acceptance names its case directory under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/` (an existing one if the source belongs to a case, such as `blmis`; otherwise a new directory and case letter, which §3.2b does not list and so needs a plan edit), the T's `trace.<law>` procedure and version, its tier row (A4), and the A13 coverage row it moves from `research` to `exercised`.

## Notes

- **No dependencies** (§15: "← none").
- **Interaction with A13:** until R-TRACE closes, the trace rows of `case_coverage.toml` are `not_exercisable` with reason `research` naming this bead; a negative decision moves them to `no_public_data` with fa-gen tests as `covered_by`.
- **Mislabelling risk:** BLMIS's `trustee_transfer_credit` (§2.4, interpretive) is a trustee's credit rule, not a tracing law; it must not be presented as LIBR, FIFO or pro rata (Appendix Z.5.1; H5's reasoning).
- `trace.network_fifo` is `uncalibrated` (§5.6). The calibration clause belongs to D sentences (§5.6; A14 renders it for D only), so a follow-on T against a court's computed amount carries the source's assertion status ("the court held", `court_ruling`, §2.2) and its own assurance, and the clause appears only if that follow-on also adds a D on the procedure.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: a decision record, recorded as a comment on this bead, has one row per candidate source examined (court opinion or receiver report, URL, access route, SHA-256) stating whether it gives both a deposit/withdrawal series and a traceable amount computed under a named method (LIBR, FIFO or pro rata) and that method's `registries/tracing_laws.toml` mapping, and ends with the decision.
- [ ] positive (only if a source is found): an `OK` sources row with SHA-256 and anchors for the series and the amount, and a follow-on bead for the `trace.<law>` T whose acceptance names its case directory, procedure and version, tier row and A13 coverage-row move.
- [ ] negative: a candidate that gives only the amount, only the series, no named method, a method that maps to no `tracing_laws.toml` row, or sits behind PACER or a login is rejected and recorded as such; mapping the trustee's transfer rule onto `trace.libr` is rejected as mislabelling the law.
- [ ] no-claim: a negative decision records what was searched; it does not show that no such source exists.

title: [cases] A14: fa-oracles renderer for case README.md and docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md from the last green run, template-only, byte drift test
description:
## Why

Overclaiming in docs is the first risk the plan names (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §17); its answer is template-only rendering, assertion-status phrases, the calibration clause, owner review, and N and CF rows rendered. §12.3 generates every write-up from the last green run and the data files, so "the docs cannot drift from the evidence". Every sentence comes from an expectation template, and there is no free-text path. Only record-consistent branch rows appear in summaries, which is the FRE 702 "sufficient facts or data" point. The write-ups are the demonstration to forensic accountants, examiners and expert witnesses (§0.1 goal 1); they are how every claim type (D/P/T/C/R/N/CF) reaches a reader.

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/render/mod.rs`: `pub fn render_readme(case: &Case, run: &RunRecords) -> Result<String, RenderError>` and `pub fn render_overview(cases: &[(&Case, &RunRecords)], coverage: &Coverage) -> Result<String, RenderError>`, where `RunRecords` holds a run's step and verdict records (A7a's `cases::log`). Pure functions: the same inputs give the same bytes.
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/render/templates.rs`: one fixed template text per A1c template id, with typed slots (fact ids, values, phrases from A3c's `phrases.rs`, statuses, refusal ids); a slot can take only data-file or run-invariant values, never free text.
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/render/lint.rs`: the wording lint over every template text and every rendered sentence (below).
- The drift test `rendered_docs_do_not_drift` in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, and the outputs it writes: `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<dir>/README.md` and `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`, plus the overview's hash pin `crates/fa-oracles/data/overview.sha256` (below).
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/policy.rs` gains `pub const OVERVIEW_WORDING_APPROVED: bool = false` (OD 4); the OD 4 landing flips it, citing the owner's recorded decision.

**Inputs.** The run's step and verdict records come from A7a's memoized `outcome(case)`, so the renderer and its drift test read the run of the same `cargo test` invocation, never a stale file; `FA_CASES_LOG_DIR`, when set, also receives the JSONL copy for an outsider (§3.5). A case is rendered only when its outcome is green (every claimed expectation PASS, A7a); otherwise the drift test fails, printing `RENDER <case> FAIL <path> reason=run not green; README not rendered` (the logging line below).

**Outputs:**
- each case's `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<dir>/README.md` (GENERATED from the last green run; never hand-edited, §3.2), with a generated-file header naming the renderer and the case version;
- the program overview `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`, including the §0.4 summary table generated from the case chapters' expectation rows, and the §12.2 coverage table (A13's rows), which renders `exercised` and `not_exercisable` rows with equal prominence. It is written only while `OVERVIEW_WORDING_APPROVED` is true (OD 4); until then its drift check prints `RENDER overview UNRUN docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md reason=awaiting OD 4` and the drift test still passes on the READMEs, because the overview is the one output §15 gates on an owner decision ("(OD 4) for `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md`").

`AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md` is A15's; the Limits section, normative section order, transcript mode and `--present-in` tables are A14b's.

**Rendering rules (§12.3, §0.3):**
- Every sentence comes from an expectation template (`statement_template`, §5.1); there is no free-text path.
- Each claim sentence carries the assertion status of every source in its basis (A3c's phrase list per expectation: "the SEC alleges"; "the indictment charges"; "the committee found" / "the examiner reported"; "the trustee computed"; "reported (audited)"; "reported (reviewed; a review is not an audit)"; "reported (unaudited)"; "reported (selected data; not derived from audited statements)"; "the court held"); for D, the claim class and the calibration clause of §5.6 (`planted`, `corpus`, `uncalibrated`), taken from the registries; the encoding and premises; and the named interpretive rules. A claim states its granularity (§2.3).
- **Assurance phrases come from `phrases()` only.** Every claim sentence's assertion and assurance phrases are A3c's `Expectation::phrases(case)` (`crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/phrases.rs`), rendered as given; the renderer has no precedence rule of its own. A3c fixes the order (a T's own `assurance`, then a sourced fact's own assurance, then the source row's `assertion_status`, never stronger than the status it replaces), so X-T-01's quarterly lines inside an audited 10-K/A render "reported (unaudited)" and "reproduces audited figures" is said only of lines whose phrase is "reported (audited)" (§10.1, §2.2). The test below checks that the renderer passes `phrases()` through unchanged.
- Branch tables render as tables; each row is marked *record-consistent* or *unconstrained*, and only record-consistent rows appear in summaries. A cell with `record_consistent = false` that the record excludes (W-P-03's Locked column, W-P-04's single-Reclassification cell; §6.3, §6.4) renders in its table without the record-consistent mark and never in a summary.
- The runner-generated rows render like authored ones: `<case>-SELF-<variant>` first in "How this book was built" (below), `<case>-CASE-<case id>` among the restatement's read-backs, and `<case>-N-90` in Limits (A14b).
- Rows with `record_label = "silent"` (§9.4) render only as counts per procedure, under "What the analytics report on data the record does not characterize"; never in summaries, never a rate.
- N results and CF rows render with the same prominence as D/P/T.
- **Verdicts are expectation verdicts.** A7a writes one verdict record per (expectation, variant, target, cell); an expectation's verdict is the worst of its lines (FAIL > UNRUN > PASS), and only a PASS expectation renders as a result. A green run can still hold unclaimed UNRUN rows (a walking-skeleton row whose witness has not landed, or one with a `pending` cell, which A1c keeps out of `claims`). Such a row renders in its section only as "not yet evaluated: <reason>" (the line's `reason=`, for a pending cell its `pending` text), never with its authored expected verdict as an outcome and never in a summary; Limits lists it (A14b). A pending cell's observed outcome is logged, not rendered.
- Only run-invariant fields are rendered (§3.4): fact ids, expectation ids, refusal ids, procedure ids and versions, component statuses and values; never VIds, certificate ids, finding ids, book ids or digests.
- An `owner_review = true` expectation renders only when its row also carries `owner_approved = "<reference to the owner's recorded approval>"` (a field A14 adds to A1c's schema); otherwise it renders as "wording awaiting owner review" and is never summarized.
- Wording (§0.3): never "would have caught/stopped/prevented ⟨company⟩"; never "matches the Big-4 auditors", but "reproduces the published bridge ⟨source⟩" with the source's assurance status; never "proves", "proven" or "proof" for any T, C, R, D, P or N row, and the templates contain no such word; a D finding is "a finding"; a P refusal names the documented attribute it rests on, with its avoidability CF row next to it, and prints "the system's stated remedy" from the catalog `fix` template filled with the cell's values (§5.2).
- Fixed phrases from §2.7: a citation stub renders as "a citation of ⟨source⟩ (bytes: the reference, not the document)"; a placeholder as "a placeholder the reconstruction attached"; a finding review as "acknowledged, citing ⟨source, anchor⟩", never "confirmed"; the runner-generated `jet.self_sourced_evidence` self-disclosure row (`<case>-SELF-<variant>`, one per book variant, A7a) comes first in "How this book was built": "franken_accounting's own `jet.self_sourced_evidence` reports that every posting here rests on documents this reconstruction uploaded itself".

**Drift test (§12.3).** `rendered_docs_do_not_drift` re-renders every committed README (and the overview, once OD 4 allows) from the same run and the data files and compares bytes with the committed file; a difference fails with the first differing line. With `FA_CASES_RENDER=write` (an authoring mode, never set by `scripts/check.sh`) it writes the rendered files instead and reports `WROTE <path>`, so the committed docs are always the renderer's output.

**The overview sits outside every crate's input closure, and the drift test still runs on every gate.** A case README lives in fa-oracles' tree, so a hand edit changes fa-oracles' input hash. `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` does not: `scripts/crate_verdicts.py` hashes a crate's own tree, `registries/` and its workspace dependencies' trees (`:216-228`). But fa-cli's verdict is never reused in any case: `crates/fa-cli/tests/readme.rs:31` already does `include_str!("../../../README.md")`, an include outside the crate, which marks fa-cli `undeclared_external_read`, and such a crate never reuses a cached verdict (`:16-19`, `:152-179`, `:231`; checked in polish round 4). So the drift test, in fa-cli's `cases` target, re-runs on every gate and reads the overview at run time; a hand edit of the overview fails the next gate. The test also compares the overview's SHA-256 with a pin, `crates/fa-oracles/data/overview.sha256`, which `FA_CASES_RENDER=write` rewrites with the document, so a regeneration is a visible change in fa-oracles' tree and the run log records the rendered bytes' hash. (Polish round 4: the earlier text said a reused green verdict could not see a docs-only edit, which is not so while fa-cli includes README.md; A9 and A13 now use the same fail-closed include for fa-oracles.)

## Tests & logging

- **Drift test (§12.3):** `rendered_docs_do_not_drift`: re-rendering from the same run and data is byte-identical to the committed file; and two renders of two runs (different book ids) are byte-identical (`render_is_identical_across_two_runs`).
- **Derived negatives (§15 gives none for A14; derived from §12.3 and §0.3):**
  - `hand_edit_to_a_rendered_readme_fails_the_drift_test` (a test-only copy with one changed word);
  - `template_containing_proves_is_refused` (and "proven", "proof", "would have prevented", "fraud detected", "matches the Big-4"), by `lint.rs` over a test-only template table;
  - `claim_sentence_without_its_assertion_phrase_fails` and `d_sentence_without_its_calibration_clause_fails` (K-ASSERT and K-ERRRATE from A3c, enforced at render time as well);
  - `run_variant_field_in_rendered_output_fails` (a test-only template slot fed a VId, certificate id, finding id or digest);
  - `owner_review_row_without_approval_is_not_rendered`;
  - `non_green_case_is_not_rendered`;
  - `overview_differing_from_its_pin_fails_the_drift_test` (a test-only copy of the overview with one changed byte and the old pin);
  - `record_inconsistent_row_never_in_a_summary_fails_if_summarized` (a test-only summary template fed a `record_consistent = false` cell is refused);
  - `unrun_row_renders_only_as_not_yet_evaluated` (a fixture's unclaimed row with a `pending` cell renders "not yet evaluated: <pending>", and a test-only template that renders its authored verdict as an outcome is refused);
  - `t_sentence_renders_the_phrases_a3c_gives` (a fixture T with `assurance = "filer_unaudited"` over a `filer_audited` source row renders exactly `phrases()`'s "reported (unaudited)", and a template slot that renders "reproduces audited figures" on it is refused).
- **Unit tests** (`render/`, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`): `every_template_id_has_one_text_and_only_typed_slots`; `branch_table_marks_record_consistent_rows`; `silent_rows_render_only_as_counts`.
- **Logging:** the drift test prints `RENDER <case> PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <path>` per document, with the run's log path; the runner prints the JSONL log path at the end of each run (§16).

## Notes

- **← A7a:** the runner's records (through `outcome`) are the renderer's input. **← A13:** the overview renders the coverage table, and the Limits section (A14b) draws its not_exercisable rows.
- **OD 4 (public claim wording)** gates `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` (§15: "(OD 4) for docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md"), through `OVERVIEW_WORDING_APPROVED`; the recommended defaults are the §0.3 templates. OD 4 is an owner decision, not a bead, so it is not in deps. A10b waits for the overview file.
- **OD 2a** gates quote text in "What the record says" (§12.3 item 2; A10a's `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED`); **OD 3** gates quote text containing names.
- **First real README:** `_selftest` is never rendered (A8a), and the A8 pilot does not depend on A14, so whichever of A8 and A14 lands second renders and commits the pilot's README with `FA_CASES_RENDER=write`.
- **Settled here:** the drift test re-runs the case through the memoized runner rather than consuming a log file, so it never compares against a stale run (round 1 left this open).
- **Marker checks.** A10b adds only `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` to the claims-lint scan (one registry edit), once this item renders it. The case READMEs are covered by A10a's marker test, which scans every committed case README, so a rendered README needs no registry edit.
- **fa-rdid** (technical reports with source-bound evidence and explicit non-claims) can cite these generated documents.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases`; `bash scripts/check.sh` (rendered files and the pin are non-`.rs`; A10b's claims-lint scan of the overview runs there).
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: for a fixture case with a green run, the renderer produces a README whose every sentence comes from a template and carries its sources' assertion status, the D calibration clause, the encoding, the premises and the named interpretive rules; re-rendering from the same inputs, and from a second run with a different book id, is byte-identical, and the drift test passes.
- [ ] positive: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES.md` renders the §0.4 summary from expectation rows and the coverage table with `exercised` and `not_exercisable` rows at equal prominence (rendered only after OD 4; until then its drift check reports UNRUN).
- [ ] negative: a hand edit to a rendered README fails the drift test; a template containing "proves", "proven" or "proof" is refused; a run-variant field (VId, certificate id, finding id, digest) in rendered output fails; a case whose run is not green is not rendered.
- [ ] negative: an `owner_review = true` expectation without recorded owner approval is not rendered.
- [ ] negative (derived): an overview whose bytes differ from `crates/fa-oracles/data/overview.sha256` fails the drift test; a `record_consistent = false` branch row never appears in a summary; an unclaimed UNRUN row (including one with a `pending` cell) renders only as "not yet evaluated", never with its authored verdict; a T's assurance phrase is the one A3c's `phrases()` gives (its own `assurance` over its source row's), passed through unchanged.
- [ ] no-claim: a rendered sentence restates an expectation's verdict under its encoding and premises; it adds no evidence beyond the run it was rendered from, and it is never a legal conclusion.

title: [cases] A14b: README Limits section, normative 8-section order, transcript mode (FA_CASES_TRANSCRIPT=1) and --present-in statement tables
description:
## Why "A case study that shows only what fires is marketing. One that shows what does not fire, and why, is evidence an expert witness can use" (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §0.3). The Limits section is generated from the case's own N, X and CF rows and is never shortened in summaries (§12.3). The normative section order follows the COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN §15.6 reader workflows, so each README reads as a CPA's, examiner's, investigator's, litigation consultant's or receiver's workflow. The Reproduce section is re-executed in transcript mode, so the rendered commands are known to regenerate the projections. Statement tables are franken_accounting's own presentation, never renderer arithmetic. It serves N, X and CF rows directly and the reproduce path of every claim type. ## What to build **Files** (introduced here): `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/render/{sections,limits,reproduce,statements}.rs`, the no-claim templates in `render/templates.rs`, and the runner test `transcript_reproduces_every_projection` in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs` (helper `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/transcript.rs`). **Normative section order of a case README (§12.3)**, checked by `sections.rs` on every render (a README whose headings are out of this order is refused): 1. Reader and workflow: the COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN §15.6 reader, with a step table in which each step is either executed, citing its expectation id, or not executable here, with the reason. Readers: W and X, CPA audit and examiner; E, investigator; L, litigation consultant's but-for; M, receiver or trustee; C, CPA audit (business combination). The reader comes from `case.toml` (`reader`, a closed set of these five). 2. What the record says: the sourced facts table (value, anchor, assertion status, granularity; quote text only after OD 2a). 3. How this book was built: book variants, declared defaults, interpretive rules, branch attributes, and the self-disclosure rows (§2.7). 4. Findings, refusals with the system's stated remedy (§5.2), and tie-outs with their assurance status. 5. What franken_accounting does not catch here, and why (Limits). 6. Verify it yourself: the §12.1 kit commands and the §12.7 witness. 7. Reproduce. 8. What green does not show: the work items' no-claim lines. The plan does not say where they are stored; because the renderer has no free-text path (§12.3), each is a fixed template `NOCLAIM.` in `render/templates.rs` holding that item's no-claim text, and `case.toml` lists the ones that apply (`no_claims = ["NOCLAIM.A8", …]`, a field A14b adds to A1a's schema). **Limits (item 5)** is generated by `limits.rs` from: the case's N rows, each with its mechanism (file:line) and twin status; its X components, each with the rule that makes it inadmissible; the CF rows that show what a D or P depends on; the `not_exercisable` coverage rows for procedures a reader would expect for this scheme (for example the population JET tests for WorldCom and `graph.ponzi_motif` for BLMIS; `case.toml` lists them as `expected_limits`); and the §13 beads the case raised (`case.toml` `raised = [...]`); plus, under "not yet evaluated", every unclaimed expectation whose verdict in the green run is UNRUN, with its `reason=` (a `pending` cell's text, A1c; a witness or prerequisite not yet landed), never with its authored verdict (A14's rule). `[[note]]` rows (§5.1, for example W-NOTE-01) render only in Limits, have no verdict and are never counted as expectations. Limits is never shortened in summaries. **Reproduce (transcript mode).** `reproduce.rs` renders the section from the run log's `argv_redacted`, with symbolic placeholders (`$BOOK`, `$C_IS_2002Q1`, `$F4`) bound to the event fields that produced them (A7a's `binds`), one command per line, each followed by a comment naming the placeholders it binds. With `FA_CASES_TRANSCRIPT=1`, `transcript_reproduces_every_projection` parses the rendered Reproduce text (no shell: commands are split into argv by the renderer's own quoting rule), runs each command against a fresh book directory, rebinds every placeholder from the event the comment names, and recomputes the projection (§5.4) of every runner line, one per (expectation, variant, target, cell) (A7a), which must equal the run's. Without the variable the test prints `TRANSCRIPT UNRUN commands=0 reason=FA_CASES_TRANSCRIPT not set` (the logging line below) and passes. A README is not rendered otherwise: A14's `FA_CASES_RENDER=write` refuses to write a README unless the transcript test passed for that case in the same invocation (so writing needs both variables), and the landing that commits a README records that run. **Statement tables** (`statements.rs`): franken_accounting's own presentation in the filing's unit (`fa statement balance-sheet|income-statement --for

--present-in thousands|millions`, `registries/verbs.toml:543`; its `statement_presented` event), recorded as a runner step and printed from that event, never renderer arithmetic. ## Tests & logging - **Negative (§15):** `transcript_that_does_not_reproduce_a_projection_blocks_rendering`: an edited `_selftest`-shaped fixture whose rendered Reproduce text drops one step (so a later projection differs) makes the transcript test fail with `TRANSCRIPT FAIL commands= reason= projection differs at command `, and `FA_CASES_RENDER=write` then refuses to write the README. - **Derived negatives (§12.3, §5.1):** `readme_with_sections_out_of_order_is_refused`; `limits_missing_an_n_row_x_component_or_cf_row_fails` (and one missing an unclaimed UNRUN row); `note_rendered_outside_limits_or_with_a_verdict_fails`; `statement_table_not_taken_from_present_in_output_fails` (a test-only renderer path that divides amounts itself is refused by `statements.rs`). - **Positive:** `fixture_readme_renders_in_the_eight_section_order_with_complete_limits`: a fixture case renders in the eight-section order with a complete Limits section, and its statement tables match `fa statement … --present-in` output byte for byte. - **Logging:** the transcript test logs each re-executed command and its projection comparison as JSONL steps (§3.5, `book_variant = ~transcript`); a failure prints the first command whose projection did not reproduce, and `TRANSCRIPT PASS|FAIL|UNRUN commands=`. ## Notes - **← A14:** the renderer, its templates and the drift test. - Limits uses A13's `not_exercisable` rows (A14 already depends on A13). - **Settled here:** the no-claim lines' home (fixed `NOCLAIM.` templates listed in `case.toml`), which round 1 left open; and the reader, expected-limits and raised-bead lists as `case.toml` fields. - **Known Limits content from the chapters:** W-P-03-CF-01 ("the period law protects closed periods, but it cannot know an entry's true effective date"); the note W-NOTE-02 (`jet.post_closing`, all X, and the population-tier row with it; §6.4, which replaced the expectation W-D-05 after polish round 2, since an all-X row can neither PASS nor FAIL); the W-D-08 / `jet.post_closing` sentence "a correction looks like the entry it corrects to these predicates" (H17); E-N-03's "a related-party round trip spread over two years escapes a windowed cycle detector"; the guidance N `-N-90` of A16 (`` = the case letter, `W-N-90`). - **Risk:** the transcript test is the guarantee behind every rendered Reproduce section, but `scripts/check.sh` does not set `FA_CASES_TRANSCRIPT`, so under the gate the test prints its `TRANSCRIPT UNRUN` line and passes rather than re-executing; the guarantee holds at render time (writing requires it). Transcript re-execution runs the real binary and counts toward the per-case runtime budget (§16) when it runs. - A15's `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md` is drift-tested like the README. - **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the templates' data and any rendered file. - **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: a fixture case README renders in the eight-section normative order; its Limits section lists every N row (mechanism file:line, twin status), every X component with its rule, every CF row, the expected `not_exercisable` coverage rows, the §13 beads raised and, as "not yet evaluated", each unclaimed UNRUN expectation with its reason; its "What green does not show" section prints the listed `NOCLAIM.<item>` templates; its statement tables come from `fa statement … --present-in`.
- [ ] positive: with `FA_CASES_TRANSCRIPT=1`, the transcript test re-executes the rendered Reproduce text and reproduces every projection; `FA_CASES_RENDER=write` writes a README only after that test passed in the same invocation.
- [ ] negative: a rendered transcript that does not reproduce a projection blocks rendering.
- [ ] negative: a `[[note]]` row rendered outside Limits, or carrying a verdict, fails; a README with sections out of order is refused.
- [ ] no-claim: a reproducing transcript shows the rendered commands regenerate the run's projections on a fresh book; it shows nothing beyond the expectations themselves.

title: [cases] A15: MCP case runner crates/fa-mcp/tests/cases_mcp.rs: CLI projection parity, case-shaped mistakes, generated AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md
description:
## Why

AI agents are franken_accounting's primary day-to-day operators (AGENTS.md, Agent Ergonomics). docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.5 runs a deterministic MCP walkthrough on every case now: the case's audit program replayed as tool calls, with every D/T/R projection equal to the CLI runner's (parity), and the case-shaped mistakes agents make exercised against fa-mcp's own detectors. Its output, `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`, is consumed by agents learning the forensic workflow and by fa-y6eu card authors. It serves D, T and R parity, and the CF row W-P-03-CF-01 (the re-dated retry that only fa-mcp refuses).

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-mcp/Cargo.toml`: a new `[dev-dependencies]` section (fa-mcp has none at 8196f5e40) with `fa-oracles = { path = "../fa-oracles", version = "=0.0.1" }`.
- `crates/fa-mcp/tests/cases_mcp.rs` (one `#[test]` per case, named after its directory as in the CLI runner, `_selftest` first, plus `walkthrough_does_not_drift`), with helpers in `crates/fa-mcp/tests/cases_mcp/*.rs` via `#[path]`. There is no shared e2e crate (§3.1), so it defines its own versions of the e2e helpers: the in-process CLI front door `cli(args)` (`crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs:48-60`, `fa_cli::entry::fa`), the server spawn `Mcp::start_with` (`:110-140`), `call_tool` (`:252`) and `structured_error` (`:265`). `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fa-mcp` is available only to fa-mcp's own tests.
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/render/walkthrough.rs`: `pub fn render_walkthrough(case, calls: &[ToolCallRecord]) -> String`, on A14's template machinery; output `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<dir>/AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md` (inside fa-oracles' tree, so a hand edit invalidates its verdict and the drift test re-runs).
- **Topology edit:** in `registries/workspace_topology.toml:187` (the fa-mcp row, `:182-187`), `allowlist = ["fa-cli", "fa", "fa-registry"]` becomes `allowlist = ["fa-cli", "fa", "fa-registry", "fa-oracles"]`. `edge_allowed` rejects any edge outside a present allowlist, dev edges included (`crates/fa-registry/src/topology.rs:141-149`). That is one registry edit, so one global crate-verdict invalidation (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`), which the landing states.

**Book construction:** in-process, through `fa_cli::entry::fa`, replaying the case's setup and history exactly as A7a's runner does (the same `fa_oracles` renderers produce the same argv). Then spawn fa-mcp with an Agent template: `--cluster fa.forensics --cluster fa.findings --cluster fa.case --cluster fa.query --cluster fa.notary --cluster fa.draft --grant read --grant produce`. `fa.post`, `fa.time`, `fa.read` and `fa.orient` are default clusters; `fa.draft` is on-demand (its `[[mcp.cluster]]` row has `on_demand = true`), and planning into a draft needs it, as the e2e precedent does (`e2e_stdio.rs:3115-3117`: "fa.draft is an on-demand cluster"). §12.5's Agent template now lists it (polish round 2).

**Parity.** Replay the case's audit program as tool calls (`fa_forensics_procedure`, `fa_forensics_jet`, `fa_findings_record`, `fa_findings_list`, `fa_query_gql`, the `fa_read_*` reads), and issue the same reads through the in-process CLI on the same book; every D/T/R projection (§5.4), computed by `fa_oracles::cases` from each transport's output, must be equal. The two transports read one book, so a difference is a transport difference, never a book difference.

**Case-shaped mistakes (§12.5):**
- an Agent trunk post (`fa_post_post`) is refused `FA-REF-013` (AGENT_TRUNK), then planned into a draft (`fa_draft_manage` new, then `fa_post_post` with `draft`);
- F4 as Original into the Closed 2Q01 is refused `FA-REF-010`; the same legs re-dated to the 2001-07-17 booking date are then refused *before dispatch* by fa-mcp's `redated_intent` detector (`crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:677-712`), observed as a structured error naming the detector with no book change, while the CLI and the kernel admit that re-dated intent because 3Q01 is Open. This is CF row W-P-03-CF-01, rendered in Limits: the period law protects closed periods, but it cannot know an entry's true effective date;
- `self_approval` on the session's own lock or issuance proposal (`detect.rs:715-739`): `fa_time_period_transition` lock with a plan, then `fa_time_approve` of its own digest;
- the `investigate_account` and `certify_period_reports` macros (`crates/fa-mcp/src/registry.rs:154-184`).

**Output:** `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md` (§12.5 writes `cases/<id>/AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`), generated from the green run (tools, arguments with placeholders, projections) and drift-tested like the README: `walkthrough_does_not_drift` compares bytes, and `FA_CASES_RENDER=write` writes it (A14's authoring mode).

## Tests & logging

- **Positive (§15):** `selftest_projections_over_mcp_equal_the_cli`: the `_selftest` projections over MCP equal the CLI's.
- **Negatives (§15):** `redated_retry_is_refused_by_redated_intent_before_dispatch` (on `_selftest`'s `FA-REF-010` cell: the structured error names `redated_intent`, the book head is unchanged, and the in-process CLI admits the same intent); `divergent_projection_fails_parity` (a test-only projection transform on the MCP side → `FAIL parity <id>: cli=<…> mcp=<…>`).
- **Derived negatives (§12.5):** `agent_trunk_post_is_refused_fa_ref_013` before being planned into a draft; `self_approval_of_the_sessions_own_lock_is_refused_by_the_detector`.
- **WorldCom form:** `worldcom_redated_f4_is_refused_by_redated_intent` runs on the WorldCom `native` book through the same code once W3/W5 land; A15 has no W edge, so until then the row prints UNRUN, never PASS.
- **Output:** one line per (expectation, variant, target, cell) in A7a's notation, `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> <variant> <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses>`, with `transport=cli|mcp` and `parity=equal|differs`, the parity compared line by line; a parity failure prints both projections and the tool call. Each tool call is a JSONL step (§3.5) with `verb = "mcp:<tool>"`, the arguments with placeholders, and the exit or refusal id; the log path is printed at the end.
- The walkthrough drift test compares re-rendered bytes with the committed `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`.

## Notes

- **Why each edge:** A7a (the CLI runner whose projections are the parity reference, and its argv renderers); A12 (the outsider read kinds, such as finding export/replay and certificates, which the MCP replay also exercises); A14 (the walkthrough is rendered and drift-tested by the renderer).
- **W-P-03-CF-01's two halves (§6.4).** W5 delivers the CLI half (the kernel admits the re-dated intent because 3Q01 is Open); this item's `redated_intent` negative is the fa-mcp half.
- `_selftest` already contains an `FA-REF-010` cell (A8a), so the `redated_intent` negative runs there before the WorldCom books exist, and A15 closes on that form.
- **The cluster list.** §12.5's Agent template includes `fa.draft` since polish round 2, which the "then planned into a draft" step needs (on-demand cluster; `e2e_stdio.rs:3115-3117`); plan and bead agree.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main (the new `[dev-dependencies]` section changes `Cargo.lock`), `cargo test -p fa-mcp --test cases_mcp`, and `bash scripts/check.sh` for the topology edit; a targeted `-p fa-registry -p fa-mcp` probe first, since the allowlist line gates every fa-mcp edge.
- **Downstream:** A16 (← A15) probes MCP `fa_orient_next`; H10 (← A15) runs the fresh-agent campaign over this harness.
- **fa-z5u (fa-mcp 1.0 posture, open, P1)** plans a fad-hosted server (`fad serve --mcp stdio|socket`), profile-gated cluster discovery and the Appendix D error shape. When it lands, this harness's launch (the stdio `fa-mcp` binary with `--cluster` flags) and the walkthrough's tool list are re-observed, and a parity difference it introduces is a FAIL to explain, not a pin to regenerate. fa-y6eu (related) is the fresh-agent campaign H10 builds on. No bead plans the case runner over MCP.
- **H12 interaction:** MCP tool docs are generated from `registries/verbs.toml`, so until H12 lands the fa.case tool's usage text says a Restatement case's entries are refused with FA-REF-178 (`registries/verbs.toml:251`), which a walkthrough reader would see.
- **Registry edit:** the one allowlist line above (global invalidation, stated in the landing). No verbs.toml, robot-pin or write-authority change: A15 adds no tool, flag or event.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the `_selftest` projections over MCP equal the CLI's on the same book; fa-mcp's topology allowlist gains `fa-oracles` (one registry edit) and the `topology` step passes.
- [ ] negative: a re-dated retry is refused by `redated_intent` before dispatch (structured error, book head unchanged), while the CLI admits the same intent (on `_selftest`'s `FA-REF-010` cell): the fa-mcp half of W-P-03-CF-01, whose CLI half is W5's.
- [ ] negative: a deliberately divergent projection fails parity, printing both projections.
- [ ] positive: the same check is wired for the WorldCom `native` book: F4 as Original into the Closed 2Q01 is refused `FA-REF-010`, and the same legs re-dated to 2001-07-17 are refused before dispatch by `redated_intent` while the CLI admits them. Until W3/W5 build that book the row prints UNRUN, never PASS; A15 closes on the `_selftest` form above.
- [ ] negative: an Agent trunk post is refused `FA-REF-013`, and the Agent then plans it into a draft (with `--cluster fa.draft`).
- [ ] no-claim: fa-mcp's behaviour on a reconstruction; nothing about any agent's ability to find fraud.

title: [cases] A16: guidance-reachability probe: a per-case ergonomics N that triage, next and fa_orient_next offer no audit program before findings
description:
## Why

docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.5. At 8196f5e40, no procedure is offered before a finding run exists (`crates/fa-cli/src/triage.rs:798-890`). On an all-Closed book the first step offered is `fa period open <code> --json` (`:809-815`): a write step with a placeholder, which fa-mcp's own detector refuses (`crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:251`). An agent that follows the product's guidance never reaches the audit program. That is an ergonomics N row per case, rendered in Limits and locked in both directions; it is the reason for H16, and when H16 lands the N flips and is retired with a trailer. It serves the N claim type for agent ergonomics.

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/guidance.rs` (pure): `pub struct VerbRows` (verb name → `writes`, subcommands, flags and switches, from `registries/verbs.toml`'s `[[verb]]` rows read raw), `pub struct BoundRules` (the `[[bound]]` rows read raw, in file order: `verbs`, `subcommands`, `args`, `when_all`, `when_any`, `unless_any`, `flag`/`values`, `ops`; the header at `registries/verbs.toml:5636-5653` defines each), `pub fn bound_ops(command, verbs, bound) -> Option<Vec<String>>` (the first rule that decides the command, as `fa_cli::cli::bound_command_rule` does, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:2173-2195`; fa-oracles cannot link fa-cli, so this is its own reading), `pub fn classify(command: &str, verbs: &VerbRows, bound: &BoundRules) -> Offer { verb, subcommand, writes, bound_ops, read_only: bool, placeholder: bool, audit: bool }`, `pub fn placeholders(command) -> Vec<String>` (every `<…>` token), and `pub fn guidance_n(case) -> Expectation`, which generates the case's guidance N with the reserved id `<case>-N-90` (§12.5; `<case>` is the case letter, `W-N-90`, or the self-test's id, `_selftest-N-90`), `kind = no_finding`, `twin_kind = matcher`, for every case, as A7a generates the SELF rows; authors never write it (A1c refuses the id).
- `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases/guidance.rs` (the CLI walk) and `crates/fa-mcp/tests/cases_mcp/guidance.rs` (the MCP walk through `fa_orient_next`, A15's harness).
- `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/guidance/triage_with_jet.jsonl`: the twin, one recorded `book_triage` envelope whose `next_actions` carries one planted read-only `fa jet --json` entry, plus entries with `<chart.json>` and `<resolution.json>` tokens and a `fa period open FY2002-P04 --json` write entry.

**Walk:** from each built case book, follow only read-only `next_actions` of `fa triage --json` and `fa next --json`, and of MCP `fa_orient_next`, to depth 6: at each depth, collect the offered (command, why) pairs, classify each, execute each read-only offer not executed before (a read leaves the book unchanged, so the walk terminates), and repeat. Record whether a Lantern procedure (`fa procedure …`) or `fa jet` is ever offered, and whether an offered command contains a placeholder.

**Read-only entry (§15 A16).** `next_actions` entries are (command, why) pairs (`crates/fa-cli/src/triage.rs:1003-1007`); the internal `writes` flag (`:671-686`) is not emitted. An entry is read-only when its command's verb row in `registries/verbs.toml` has `writes = false` (for example `fa procedure` and `fa jet`, `registries/verbs.toml:668-670`, `:680-683`), or when the first `[[bound]]` rule that matches its verb, subcommand and flags has `ops = ["read"]` (§12.5 and §15 A16 since polish round 2; for example `fa period list` and `fa chart list`, `registries/verbs.toml:5738-5741`, although the `period` row is `writes = true`, `:148`). The probe resolves the verb (and subcommand) from the offered command against `VerbRows` and the deciding rule against `BoundRules`.
- **Cross-check against the code.** The CLI walk parses each offered command with `fa_cli::args::parse` (`crates/fa-cli/src/args.rs:22`) and compares fa-oracles' `bound_ops` with `fa_cli::cli::bound_command_ops` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:2173`, public); a disagreement FAILs the probe, naming the command, so the harness's reading of the rule set cannot drift from the binary's.
- **Empty ops.** The write-authority test treats bound ops ⊆ {read}, an empty list included, as read-only (`crates/fa-cli/tests/write_authority.rs:1532-1551`); the plan says `ops = ["read"]`. The probe follows the plan and logs `ops_subset_read` beside `read_only`, so an offered command with an empty-ops rule (none is offered at 8196f5e40) would be visible.

**Placeholder (§12.5).** Any `<…>` token in an offered command. fa-mcp's detector (`crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:251`) flags only some forms; triage also emits `<N>`, `<chart.json>` and `<resolution.json>`, so the probe uses the any-token rule, not the detector's.

**When:** twice per case book, before the case's first `finding_record` step and after its last (the runner inserts the two probe steps). The N is asserted on the first run: no read-only entry offers `fa jet`, `fa procedure list` or an MCP `fa.audit` tool. The second run is logged, not asserted. A book variant with no `finding_record` step (a `statement` book that only reads, for example) is probed once, after its history's last step, and that run is the asserted one; the plan names only the two-step form. `<case>-N-90` prints one line per probed book variant (A7a's per-variant lines), and the case's N passes only if every variant's line does.

**Per-case expected value:** computed from the book's state at the probe. A book with a `Future` period and none Open expects the concrete `fa period open <code>` with that period's code (`triage.rs:810-816`), never a placeholder; a book with no Future period and none Open expects the placeholder form `fa period open <code>`, which is the defect H16 removes. The expected command is part of the N's projection.

**Twin (§15 A16).** The probe's matcher is fed `triage_with_jet.jsonl` and must report the planted `fa jet` offer. This twin covers the matcher; the binary-level flip comes when H16 lands. It lives in the probe's test data, never in a product path (§3.4).

**Rows:** one N per case, `<case>-N-90`, rendered in Limits (A14b).

## Tests & logging

- **Positive:** `guidance_n_holds_on_every_case_book`: on every case book, the first probe run asserts the N and it holds (no read-only offer of `fa jet`, `fa procedure list` or an `fa.audit` tool within depth 6, over both triage and next and over MCP `fa_orient_next`), and the per-case expected value is observed.
- **Negative (§15):** `matcher_twin_reports_the_planted_jet_offer`: fed the recorded envelope, the matcher reports the planted read-only `fa jet --json` entry, and the N evaluated over it fails.
- **Derived (timing):** `book_without_finding_steps_is_probed_once_after_its_history` (a `_selftest` statement variant: one asserted probe, logged with `probe = "only"`).
- **Derived negatives (§12.5):** `write_entry_is_not_followed` (the recorded `fa period open FY2002-P04 --json` has a `writes = true` verb row, and the walk does not execute it); `chart_json_and_resolution_json_tokens_are_placeholders` (flagged although `detect.rs:251` does not flag them); `authored_n_90_is_refused` (A1c's reserved id).
- **Unit tests** (`guidance.rs`, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`): `classify_resolves_verb_and_subcommand_from_an_offered_command`; `placeholders_finds_every_angle_bracket_token`; `bound_rule_makes_period_list_read_only` (`fa period list --json` → the `["chart", "period"]`/`["list"]` rule, `ops = ["read"]`, read-only) and `unmatched_period_open_is_a_write` (no read rule decides it, and the verb row writes); `first_deciding_rule_wins_over_a_later_one` (a test-only rule table where two rules match: the first decides, as the binary's lookup does).
- **Output:** `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <case>-N-90 N <stem> -/default <projection-with-statuses>` for each case's guidance N (A7a's notation), the projection carrying `audit_offered=false`, `placeholder_offered=<bool>`, `expected=<command>` and `twin=matcher:reported`. JSONL steps (§3.5) for every followed entry: depth, command, verb row and its `writes` value, the deciding `[[bound]]` rule's index and ops, `read_only`, `ops_subset_read`, and the placeholder flag; the second run's observations are logged with the same fields (`probe = "after"`) but not asserted.

## Notes

- **Why each edge:** A7a (runner, books and the verb table); A11c (the N needs its twin; here a matcher twin, `twin_kind = matcher`); A15 (the MCP harness that reaches `fa_orient_next`).
- **Code check at 8196f5e40.** `writes` is a field of the internal `NextStep` struct (`crates/fa-cli/src/triage.rs:30-40`) and is not emitted. `fa triage` and `fa next` build `next_actions` as (command, why) pairs (`triage.rs:1003`, `:1124`), and the `next_step` event carries only `command` and `why` (`registries/verbs.toml:2334-2337`). That is why §15 A16 defines read-only from the offered command's verb row.
- Under a launch capability, `rank_for` (`triage.rs:919`) drops trunk writes for an Agent profile, so the MCP probe under the Agent template sees a filtered list.
- **H16 flip:** when H16 lands, each case's guidance N fails on the real binary as designed (case books open an `investigation` engagement, §2.7, so triage then offers `fa jet`) and is retired with a `Retired-tests:` trailer (§12.5, §16).
- **fa-g8em (triage, next and bare `fa`, open, P2)** keeps adding triage steps (drafts, findings, pending approvals, capability ranking; its open item is `unmatched_bank_lines`). Each case's expected value is computed at the probe from the book's state, so a new fa-g8em step changes the logged second run and the walk's input; only an offer of `fa jet`, `fa procedure list` or an MCP `fa.audit` tool flips the asserted N. H16 is the planned flip (related link).
- **`fa period list` under H16.** H16's all-Closed fallback offers the read-only `fa period list`; under the bound-rule reading the walk now follows it (round 2 had to log it instead).
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases -p fa-mcp --test cases_mcp`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the twin fixture.
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: on every case book, the first probe run (before the first `finding_record` step) finds no read-only `next_actions` entry (verb row `writes = false` in `registries/verbs.toml`, or a deciding `[[bound]]` rule with `ops = ["read"]`) offering `fa jet`, `fa procedure list` or an MCP `fa.audit` tool within depth 6, reported as the generated row `<case>-N-90`, and the per-case expected value holds (a book with a `Future` period and none Open offers the concrete `fa period open <code>`, never a placeholder, where a placeholder is any `<…>` token).
- [ ] negative: the twin, a recorded triage envelope with one planted read-only `fa jet …` entry, is reported by the probe's matcher, and the N evaluated over it fails.
- [ ] negative (derived): fa-oracles' `[[bound]]` reading disagreeing with `fa_cli::cli::bound_command_ops` on an offered command fails the probe, naming the command; `fa period list` classifies as read-only and `fa period open FY2002-P04` as a write.
- [ ] negative (derived): a planted `<chart.json>` token is flagged as a placeholder, a planted entry whose verb row has `writes = true` is not followed, and an authored `<case>-N-90` expectation is refused.
- [ ] no-claim: the probe shows what triage offers on these books, not what an agent would do. The twin covers the matcher only; the binary-level flip comes with H16.

title: [cases] W1: WorldCom sources ledger and receipts (SRC-WC-001..004, -401, -406, -EX27-1999, SEC v. Abide candidate), hash-first
description:
## Why
WorldCom's line-cost capitalization (2001 – 1Q02) is the program's densest entry-level record: 13 entry facts at `journal_entry` granularity from Beresford pp.105–116, which carry the case's D, P, N, T, R and CF rows (plan §0.4, §6). Every one of those rows rests on facts, and a fact may cite only an `OK` row of the case's sources ledger (§4.1). The research record itself contained anchor errors (Appendix Z.3: EV-040's quotes occur in no stored text; the SEC ¶29 scope was misapplied to 1Q02), so the plan rules that "the research workspace is not a source" (§4.5): a fact is accepted only with a receipt from `case_fetch.py verify` run by its author, and its review re-runs `verify` independently with a second cache. This item lands that ledger and those receipts for WorldCom. It serves every claim type of the case indirectly: K-ASSERT renders each source's assertion status into every sentence (§2.2), and K-VINTAGE needs the accessions named (§3.6). Vendoring is hash-first (§1.3): anchors, literal values and `quote_sha256` now, quote text only after owner decision 2a.

## What to build
**Files** (case directory `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/`, letter `W`, §3.2b):
- `sources.toml` (hand-authored, comments allowed);
- `receipts.toml` (GENERATED by `case_fetch.py verify`, regenerated whole, never hand-edited, §4.4);
- the pilot slice's sourced `[[fact]]` rows in `facts.toml` (see "Pilot slice" below);
- one `include_str!` line per committed file in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/embedded.rs` (A1a's index; `embedded_index_lists_every_committed_file` fails on an unlisted file);
- if `case.toml` does not exist yet when W1 lands (A8 authors it, with `claims`), the minimal header the loader needs: `id = "worldcom"`, `letter = "W"`, `kind = "case"`, `claims = []`; A8 extends it and W3 adds `variants`;
- `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`: the load-time negatives below (W2 and W3 add theirs to the same file).

**`sources.toml` rows.** One `[[source]]` row per source with every §4.1 field: `id`, `title`, `publisher`, `original_url`, `archive_url` (when archived), `retrieval_route` (`original` | `archive_capture` | `third_party_copy` | `re_render`), `original_hash_compared`, `retrieved_utc`, `filed_on` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the filing or publication date), `restates` (one-line array of the source ids whose figures this filing restates; `[]` otherwise), `sha256` (of the bytes as retrieved), `format` (pdf / htm / txt / xml / json), `extraction` (tool + version + SHA-256 of the extracted text), `redistribution_basis`, `assertion_status` (§2.2), `assurance` (filer statements only, with A1a's `assurance_fact`, the fact whose sentence establishes it), `anchor_scheme`, `status` (`OK` | `BLOCKED`, with A1a's `status_reason` for BLOCKED), `notes`. Values copied from §6.1 and §15 W1; every URL, accession not listed here, byte count, hash and filing date the plan does not state is recorded at fetch from the filing itself, never guessed:

| `id` | source | `assertion_status` | `redistribution_basis` | `anchor_scheme` (§4.1 kinds) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRC-WC-001 | Report of Investigation by the Special Investigative Committee of the Board of Directors of WorldCom, Inc. (Beresford, 2003-03-31), EDGAR `0000931763-03-001862`, `dex991.htm` | `investigative_finding` | `company-commissioned/edgar-exhibit` | `page{printed page, line range}` (the printed page plus the extraction line range, §6.1) |
| SRC-WC-002 | SEC v. Betty L. Vinson and Troy M. Normand, complaint (`comp17783`) | `allegation` | `government-work (§105)` | `paragraph{¶ number}` |
| SRC-WC-003 | SEC complaint against Yates (`comp17771`) | `allegation` | `government-work (§105)` | `paragraph{¶ number}` |
| SRC-WC-004 | SEC complaint against Myers (`comp17753`) | `allegation` | `government-work (§105)` | `paragraph{¶ number}` |
| SRC-WC-401 | WorldCom 10-K405 FY2000 (originally filed; total assets 98,903 $M) | `filer_audited` | `public-record/sec-filing` | `table_cell{table, row label, column label}` for the balance sheet; `page{…}` or `line{range}` for the audit-report sentence its `assurance_fact` names |
| SRC-WC-406 | WorldCom (MCI) 10-K FY2002 (restating), EDGAR `0001193125-04-039709` | `filer_not_from_audited_statements` (one value: A1a's field holds one, and K-ASSERT renders it into every sentence resting on the source, A3c). The audit opinion covers only the balance sheets at 2002-12-31 and 2001-12-31, which no fact cites; Item 6 excludes the 2000-12-31 summarized balance-sheet data, and every SRC-WC-406 figure the case cites is that excluded or selected data (W2); `notes` records the split. Written `filer_audited`, it would render W-T-02 "reported (audited)", which §6.4 forbids | `public-record/sec-filing` | `table_cell{…}` for the restatement and selected-data tables; `page{…}` or `line{range}` for prose (the $176M reclassification footnote, the Item 6 sentence) |
| SRC-WC-EX27-1999 | WorldCom 10-K FY1999, EX-27 (TOTAL-ASSETS 91,072 at MULTIPLIER 1,000,000) | `filer_audited` (FDS of audited statements) | `public-record/sec-filing` | `table_cell{EX-27, tag, column}`: the Financial Data Schedule is a tag/value table, so its values bind by value; a `line` anchor would subject a tag line to sentence alignment, which it cannot satisfy |
| SRC-WC-ABIDE | SEC v. Mark P. Abide, 06 Civ. 5660 (S.D.N.Y.), Litigation Release 19776, 2006-07-27 (§2.8, §6.6) | `allegation` | `government-work (§105)` | `paragraph{¶ number}` (complaint) or `line{range}` (release text) |

(`SRC-WC-ABIDE` is a proposed id; the plan names the source but gives it no id. Its `status` stays `"BLOCKED"` with `status_reason = "unread candidate"` until sub-task 1 below reads it, so no fact can cite it.)

- **Vintage fields (`filed_on`, `restates`; §4.1, K-VINTAGE orders vintages by them, A3b).**
  - SRC-WC-406 (the restating FY2002 10-K): `filed_on` = its EDGAR filing date, recorded at fetch from the filing header; `restates = ["SRC-WC-401", "SRC-WC-EX27-1999"]`: its restatement tables restate the FY2000 balance sheet that SRC-WC-401 filed (98,903 filed; 98,727 "as previously reported"; 44,188 restated, W-T-02) and its selected data mark FY1999 "(Restated)" (85,280 against the EX-27's 91,072, W-NOTE-01). K-VINTAGE therefore sees SRC-WC-406 as the later vintage of every W-T-02 cell, and the bridge names both vintages (§10.4).
  - SRC-WC-401 and SRC-WC-EX27-1999: `filed_on` recorded at fetch; `restates = []`.
  - SRC-WC-001: `filed_on` = the date of the EDGAR filing that carries `dex991.htm`, recorded at fetch (the report itself is dated 2003-03-31, §1.1); `restates = []`.
  - SRC-WC-002/-003/-004 and SRC-WC-ABIDE: `filed_on` = the complaint's (or, for the release, 2006-07-27, §2.8) date as the document states it, recorded at fetch; `restates = []`. A complaint is not a vintage of any figure.
  - A non-reliance 8-K row (sub-task 2), if found: `filed_on` from its header; `restates = []` (it announces non-reliance; the restating figures are SRC-WC-406's).
- **Anchor kinds and binding (§4.1).** The five kinds are `page`, `line`, `table_cell`, `xbrl`, `paragraph`; K-ANCHOR checks each fact's kind against its source's `anchor_scheme`. Anchor strings use A1a's grammar: `page` = `p<printed page>:l<first>-<last>` (for example `p111:l12-14`), `line` = `l<first>-<last>`, `paragraph` = `para<n>`, `table_cell` = `<table>|<row label>|<column label>`. Sentence alignment applies to prose anchors (`page`, `line`, `paragraph`); their receipts carry `alignment = "sentence"`. A `table_cell` fact (SRC-WC-401, SRC-WC-406 tables, the EX-27) binds by exact cell value instead; its receipt carries `alignment = "value"`.
- **Assurance from the filing itself** (audit report, review report or legend; never assumed, §2.2). A1a flattens it as `assurance` (the §4.1 value: audited, reviewed, unaudited or not-from-audited) plus `assurance_fact`, the sourced fact whose sentence establishes it; under hash-first that sentence is a receipted fact (anchor and `quote_sha256`), never text in `sources.toml`. SRC-WC-406: not-from-audited, `assurance_fact` = its Item 6 sentence excluding the 2000-12-31 summarized data (W-T-02 renders `filer_not_from_audited_statements` from it and must never be called audited). SRC-WC-401: audited, `assurance_fact` = its audit-report sentence covering the FY2000 balance sheet. W1 lands these two sourced facts with the pilot slice (proposed ids `W-ST-406-item6` and `W-ST-401-opinion`, in W2's `W-ST-<topic>` scheme), so both rows load; W2 keeps them.
- **Retrieval** (§1.2, OD 1). Direct sec.gov requests only when `FA_SEC_CONTACT` is set (the address lives only in that variable). Otherwise Internet Archive captures, recording the original URL, the archive URL and the SHA-256 of the captured bytes, with `retrieval_route = "archive_capture"` and `original_hash_compared = false`.
- **Extraction** (§4.4): PDF via `pdftotext -layout` (authoring tool only); HTML via the stdlib tag-stripper, with its algorithm version recorded in `extraction`.

**Pilot slice (`facts.toml`, sourced rows only).** `verify` writes one receipt per sourced fact, so the "SRC-WC-001 slice of W1 (receipts for pp.26, 105–116)" that A8 waits on needs the sourced `[[fact]]` rows of the pilot sentences to exist. W1 lands exactly those rows (plus the two assurance facts above): the sentences on Beresford pp.26 and 105–116 that state F2 (p.106), F4 (p.108 and p.26), F9 (p.113) and F12 (p.116), and each pilot entry's reporting period (W2's rule: a `period_literal` `[[value]]` on the sentence that names the quarter, or its own `F<n>-period` fact if another sentence names it; A8 treats the reporting periods as sourced facts, and K-SCOPE checks an `entry:` scope against the entry's sourced reporting period, A3a), each with `provenance = "sourced"` (A1a's field name), `source = "SRC-WC-001"`, `anchor_kind = "page"`, `anchor`, `quote_sha256`, `about_scope`, `granularity = "journal_entry"` and its `[[value]]` rows (§2.1). Ids follow W2's scheme (W2 owns the rest of `facts.toml` and keeps these ids and values; A8's pilot adds the F4 join interpretation).
- **Quote lookup before OD 2a (§4.4).** A fact carries only `quote_sha256` and its anchor, no quote text. The author selects the sentence-aligned span at the anchor in the normalized extraction (§4.4 normalization: whitespace runs of U+0009–U+000D, U+0020, U+00A0 → one U+0020, trimmed, no case folding) and commits its SHA-256. `verify` enumerates the sentence-aligned spans at the anchor and selects the one span whose SHA-256 matches; zero or several matches is a FAIL.

**`receipts.toml`** (§4.4). One `[[receipt]]` per sourced fact, in fact-id order: `source`, `fact`, `anchor` (the page or line range the quote was found at, which K-ANCHOR checks), `verified_utc`, `tool_version`, `extraction_sha256`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the fact's canonical literal values and `about_scope`, so K-BIND detects offline a `[[value]]` or scope edited after `verify`; the serialization is A9's/A1a's), `alignment` (`sentence` for the `page` and `paragraph` facts, `value` for the `table_cell` facts), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok`, and the source's `original_hash_compared`, copied from its `sources.toml` row (false for an archive capture until OD 1; it is not a fifth binding boolean). `verified_utc` is the cache entry's fetch time, not the run's clock, so re-running `verify` on an unchanged cache is byte-identical.

**Two research sub-tasks**, each recorded in the row's `notes`:
1. Fetch and read SEC v. Abide (LR-19776) and record which control-layer facts it carries, if any, such as who approved the 2001-08-22 transfers (§6.6). Until then the row is `BLOCKED{unread candidate}` and no fact cites it. `case_fetch.py fetch` downloads only `OK` rows (§4.4, A9), so `fetch worldcom` skips the candidate while it is `BLOCKED`: the author retrieves it under the same rules (the project User-Agent, at most 1 request per second, sec.gov only with `FA_SEC_CONTACT`, else an Internet Archive capture) and records `original_url`, `archive_url`, `retrieval_route`, `sha256` and `retrieved_utc` from that retrieval; once the row is `OK`, `fetch worldcom` downloads it and must reproduce the recorded `sha256`. If it is read and useful, the row becomes `OK` and W2 decides which facts it supports.
2. Look for a WorldCom non-reliance (Item 4.02) 8-K (§6.3: "W1 looks for one"). If one exists, add its row (it is the native and statement cases' authority and the sourced `case_determination_date`). If none exists, record "none found" here; the cases keep the declared-default determination date, the restating filing's date (§2.6), which is SRC-WC-406's `filed_on`.

## Tests & logging
**Run (authoring; network only here, never in tests).**
```
export FA_CASES_CACHE=<author cache dir>          # default $XDG_CACHE_HOME/franken_accounting/cases
python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch worldcom;   rc=$?   # 0; 4 with `UNRUN ` lines when the network is missing (never 0)
python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py extract worldcom; rc=$?   # 0; 4 with `UNRUN ` when pdftotext is absent
python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify worldcom;  rc=$?   # 0, one `VERIFY <fact> PASS` line per sourced fact, no `FAIL ` line (1 with `FAIL ` lines otherwise)
cp crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/receipts.toml <scratch>/receipts.1
python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify worldcom;  rc=$?
cmp <scratch>/receipts.1 crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/receipts.toml   # byte-identical
```
- **Second reader (§4.5).** A second agent, in its own checkout with a second `FA_CASES_CACHE`, runs the same `fetch`, `extract`, `verify worldcom`. Its receipts must equal the author's on every field except `verified_utc` (its own cache's fetch time). A difference in `extraction_sha256` is a FAIL unless both runs record different extractor versions in `extraction`, in which case the reviewer records the version pair and re-runs on the author's version. That principal is the one the books label `case-second-reader`; its receipt is what lets it record the Reviewed attestation on each citation stub (§2.7).
- **Leak check (OD 1).** If OD 1 grants a contact and the author fetches with `FA_SEC_CONTACT` set, `grep -rF "$FA_SEC_CONTACT" crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/` must find nothing before landing (A9's leak test covers the tool's own outputs).

**Offline check** (`cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline`, A10a). Expected report lines once W1's rows exist (A3a/A10a own the line format; the values below are what each field must contain; `<n>` is the number of sourced facts W1 lands):
```
SOURCE SRC-WC-001 original_hash_compared=false route=archive_capture   # one line per source row, values as recorded
CHECK worldcom K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>
CHECK worldcom K-BIND PASS examined=<n>/<n>
CHECK worldcom K-SCOPE PASS examined=<n>/<n>
CHECK worldcom K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<n>/<n>
CHECK worldcom K-DERIVE UNRUN examined=0/0     # no derived fact until W2/A8; never PASS on zero rows
EXCERPTS worldcom facts_with_quote=0 words=0   # before OD 2a
```
Receipts consistency (one receipt per sourced fact, matching `source`/`fact`/`quote_sha256`/`values_sha256`, `alignment` matching the anchor kind, the four booleans true, `original_hash_compared` equal to the source row's) prints no line of its own; a violation prints `FAIL` lines. Every other §3.6 check reports `UNRUN examined=0/0` until its input rows land (W2–W9), never PASS.

**Load-time planted negatives** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`, `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_worldcom`). Each edits an in-memory copy of the embedded case text and asserts the named refusal; the committed files are never edited:
- `wc_fact_citing_blocked_source_is_refused`: a pilot fact's `source` set to `SRC-WC-ABIDE` (status `BLOCKED`) → refused by the ledger well-formedness check, naming the fact id, the source id, its status and the line.
- `wc_receipt_flipped_binding_fails`: `scope_ok = false` on F4's p.26 receipt → "receipts consistent" FAIL naming the receipt's fact and field.
- `wc_receipt_hash_mismatch_fails`: one hex digit of a receipt's `quote_sha256` changed → FAIL naming the fact and both digests.
- `wc_complaint_fact_with_page_anchor_fails_k_anchor`: W1 lands no SRC-WC-002 fact (the ¶ facts are W2's), so the copy adds one: a sourced fact citing SRC-WC-002 with a `page` anchor `p<n>:l<first>-<last>`, plus a matching receipt (`alignment = "sentence"`, its `values_sha256`), so that only the anchor kind is wrong, while the source's `anchor_scheme` lists only `paragraph` → K-ANCHOR FAIL naming the fact and the kind.
- `wc_original_hash_compared_mismatch_fails`: a receipt whose `original_hash_compared` differs from its source row's value → FAIL (the receipt copies it; it is never independently set).
- `wc_value_edited_after_verify_fails_k_bind`: F4's p.26 `[[value]]` changed from `56000000000` to `56000000001` in the copy (560,000,000.00 → 560,000,000.01 USD: A1a's `value` is an integer string at the unit's scale; its receipt untouched) → `FAIL K-BIND facts.toml:<line> <F4 p.26 fact id>: values_sha256 mismatch`, naming both digests. The same test with only `about_scope` changed (`entry:F4` → `entry:F5`) fails the same way. This is the offline lock that a value or scope cannot drift from what `verify` checked.
- `wc_receipt_alignment_kind_mismatch_fails`: a `page`-anchored fact's receipt with `alignment = "value"` → FAIL naming the fact, its anchor kind and the receipt's `alignment` (prose anchors bind by sentence, §4.1).
- `wc_source_row_without_filed_on_fails` (`MissingField`, naming SRC-WC-406 and the line), and `wc_restates_naming_an_unknown_source_fails` (`restates = ["SRC-WC-499"]` → `DanglingKey`).

There is no book and no run-log JSONL in this item.

## Notes
- **← A9.** `case_fetch.py` (fetch, extract, verify and the receipts writer) must exist before any receipt can be produced. A9 ← A1a, so the loaders exist; A3a and A10a are not edges of W1. If A10a has not landed when W1 does, the offline lines above and the `case_worldcom.rs` negatives arrive with whichever of W1/A10a lands second, and W1's own gate is `verify worldcom` exit 0 plus the `cmp` re-run.
- **OD 1** gates direct sec.gov fetches, and so `original_hash_compared = true`. Archive-only is not neutral: the Internet Archive grants access "for scholarship and research purposes only". The contact address lives only in `FA_SEC_CONTACT` and never lands in a committed file.
- **OD 2a** gates committing quote text (at most 60 words per fact). **OD 3** gates committed quote text that contains names: most WorldCom quotes, including the F6 quote at Beresford p.111. Under hash-first vendoring neither gates this item (§14 item 3).
- **A8 edge.** A8 (the WorldCom pilot) depends on "the SRC-WC-001 slice of W1 (receipts for pp.26, 105–116)", so land that slice first. A8's bead also lists `facts.toml` for F2, F4, F9, F12: the sourced rows land here, A8 adds the pilot's interpretation rows, and ids and values must agree.
- **W1/W2 split.** W1 fetches and extracts all seven sources with `case_fetch.py` (the Abide candidate is retrieved and read outside `fetch` while it is `BLOCKED`, sub-task 1), and lands the pilot slice's sourced rows and receipts; W2 adds F1–F13 and the statement-level facts W-T-02 and W-NOTE-01 read (SRC-WC-401, SRC-WC-406, SRC-WC-EX27-1999; §15 W2) and regenerates `receipts.toml` whole. Those three filings are fetched here so their rows are `OK` before W2 cites them.
- **Settled: the `paragraph` kind.** Round 1 flagged that §6.1's "anchor = paragraph" was not a §4.1 kind. §4.1 now has `paragraph{¶ number}` for complaints and indictments, so SRC-WC-002/-003/-004 facts use it.
- **Settled: alignment of value-bound facts.** §4.4 now gives every receipt `alignment` (`sentence` for prose anchors, `value` for `table_cell`/`xbrl`) and renames the boolean `sentence_aligned` to `aligned`, which for a value-bound fact records that the quote is the whole cell text, never a fragment. So every W1 receipt, prose or table cell, must carry all four booleans true. The round-1/2 open question is closed.
- **Requires (foundation beads at r2b):** A1a (Receipt type), A9 (writer), A3a and A10a (K-BIND, receipts consistency) to carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned`, and A3a/A10a to check `alignment` against the anchor kind; A1a to load `letter` from `case.toml` and take the id prefix from it, with `id = "worldcom"` = the directory name (A1a at r2b derives the prefix from the id and spells the directory `cases/W/`).
- K-NAMES covers principal, party, memo and assertion text (§3.6). Source titles that contain names are outside it; they matter for OD 3 only when quote text lands.

Abide (LR-19776) candidate row, with every §4.1 field including `filed_on` and `restates` (SRC-WC-406 `restates = ["SRC-WC-401", "SRC-WC-EX27-1999"]`; every other row `[]`; dates recorded at fetch unless the plan states them); each `anchor_scheme` names its §4.1 kinds (`paragraph` for the SEC complaints, `page` for Beresford, `table_cell` for the filings' tables and the EX-27, `page` or `line` for the filings' prose sentences); SRC-WC-406's `assertion_status` is `filer_not_from_audited_statements` and its `assurance_fact` names the receipted Item 6 sentence that excludes the 2000-12-31 summarized data (SRC-WC-401's names its audit-report sentence); no quote text is committed.
