title: [cases] W2: WorldCom facts F1–F13 (F6a/F6b, F8 decomposition), interpretations, reporting periods, derived dates, AN-100 quarantine, roles, and the W-T-02/W-NOTE-01 statement-level facts
description:
## Why
Every WorldCom D, P, T and N row names the documented entries it rests on (plan §6.4). This item turns §6.2's table into `facts.toml` rows with exactly one provenance each (§2.1), so that K-BIND, K-SCOPE and K-DERIVE can check every value against a receipted quote, and so that every inference is labelled as an `interpretation` or a `derived` fact. The plan's rules are what keep the claims narrow. There is one fact per sentence. Facts from different sentences are joined only by an `interpretation` row that two readers read. A value that is not literally in its quote cannot be `sourced`. The case's single verdicts depend on exactly these distinctions:
- W-P-01's Si status rests on the p.111 interpretation;
- W-D-06 rests on F10's draft journal entry being the only dated instruction document;
- W-T-03 rests on F12 and F13 being stated in the same sentence as the $818M;
- W-P-02's record-consistent cell and W-D-06's B(document_date) for F12/F13 rest on the Post-it reading being an `interpretation`, not a sourced or derived fact;
- W-T-02 and W-NOTE-01 rest on statement-level facts with their own vintages and assurance (SRC-WC-401, SRC-WC-406, SRC-WC-EX27-1999), which this item also owns (§15 W2).

The research's own scope error, SEC ¶29 applied to the 1Q02 entries, is why K-SCOPE exists, so the real facts must bind ¶29 to 1Q01 only (§2.1). Claim types served: D, P, N, T, R and CF on every WorldCom variant.

## What to build
**Files** (`crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/`): `facts.toml` (`[[fact]]` + `[[value]]` rows), `roles.toml` (with its line in `src/cases/embedded.rs`, A1a), `receipts.toml` regenerated whole by `case_fetch.py verify worldcom`, and W2's tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`. Every field is a scalar or a one-line array, for the `fa_registry::toml` subset: no inline tables, dotted keys, multi-line strings, floats or TOML dates (`crates/fa-registry/src/toml.rs:1-9`). Sourced facts carry `source`, `anchor_kind`, `anchor`, `quote_sha256`, `quote` (absent until OD 2a: A10a fails any committed `quote` field while `QUOTE_TEXT_ALLOWED` is false), `about_scope`, `granularity` and their `[[value]]` rows; interpretations carry `from`, `reader`, `second_reader`, `rationale`; derived facts carry `from`, `rule`, `params` (§2.1, §2.3). The `[[value]]` row shape is A1a's Value type: `fact`, `ordinal`, `literal` (as printed), `rule` (`scale`, `date_literal`, `number_word`, `period_literal`, and §2.4's `date_range_literal` and `month_literal`), `param`, `value` (an amount as A1a's integer string at the unit's scale, for example `56000000000` for 560,000,000.00 USD; a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, a `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD` day range, a `YYYY-MM` month or a period label), `unit`, `precision` (for example 6 for "stated to $1M"). Anchors use A1a's grammar: Beresford `p<page>:l<first>-<last>`, the complaints `para<n>`, table cells `<table>|<row label>|<column label>`.

**Authoring rule (§4.4, before OD 2a).** For each sourced fact the author selects the sentence-aligned span at the anchor in the normalized extraction (`case_fetch.py extract`), commits only its `quote_sha256` and anchor, and runs `verify`, which re-finds the one span with that SHA-256 (zero or several matches is a FAIL) and writes the fact's receipt with `alignment = "sentence"`. `table_cell` facts (the filings' tables and the EX-27) bind by exact cell value instead of sentence alignment (§4.1); their receipts carry `alignment = "value"`. Every receipt also carries `values_sha256` over the fact's committed values and `about_scope` (§4.4), so after `verify` no value or scope can change without an offline K-BIND FAIL. Every value below is re-verified against the receipted extraction at authoring (SRC-WC-001 §IV.C.3–4); the research workspace is not a source (§4.5).

**Conventions (§6.2).** "A → B" means credit A, debit B. "Date" is the booking date: it fixes commit order relative to period transitions, releases and filings, and nothing else (recorded time is the CommitSeq, doctrine 6). The effective date is W3's declared default (the reporting period's last day) or the `effective_date` branch. One fact per sentence.

**Fact ids (this round's proposal; W3, W4–W9 and the A1a–A1c pilot fixture use the same ids).** `F<n>` is the fact an intent's `fact` field names: the one sourced sentence that states the entry, or the `interpretation` joining the entry's sentences when more than one states it. Its other sentences are `F<n>-p<page>[a|b…]`. Context facts are `W-CTX-<topic>`, statement-level facts `W-ST-<topic>`, and the quarantined pair `AN100-<n>`. F6 is one documented entry encoded as two intents, `F6a` (CIP → clearing) and `F6b` (clearing → ten items); both intents name `fact = "F6"`, and their cites project to (intent id, leg ordinal).

**Entry facts** (`granularity = "journal_entry"`; `source = "SRC-WC-001"`, `anchor_kind = "page"`, `about_scope = "entry:F<n>"` unless noted; the plan's §6.2 values):

| Fact | kind | page | booking date `[[value]]` | amount `[[value]]` (literal → rule → exact) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | sourced | 106 | 2001-04-20 (`date_literal`) | legs as documented: Dr Other Long Term Assets 629M, Dr Construction in Progress 142M / Cr line costs 771M ("$771 million" → `scale{multiplier}` 10^6, precision "stated to $1M") | `F1-p105`: "not effected through a single, round-dollar entry" (`about_scope = "period:2001Q1"`), the documented R-QUAL exception |
| F2 | sourced | 106 | 2001-04-23/24: if the re-verified sentence states one span over both days ("April 23 and 24, 2001"), one `date_range_literal` value `2001-04-23..2001-04-24` (a branch over its two days, Monday and Tuesday); if it dates two entries, one `date_literal` per entry | OLTA → CIP 402,000,000.00 ("$402 million", 10^6) | asset→asset; "parking" in OLTA (p.106) |
| F3 | sourced | 106 | none (1Q01, no day) | OLTA 227M offset by an Ocean Cable Liability accrual release (10^6) | leg sides from the re-verified sentence |
| F4 | interpretation of `F4-p108` + `F4-p26` (two readers) | 108, 26 | 2001-07-17 | `F4-p108`: line costs → CIP "$560 million", credits over "three separate line cost accounts"; `F4-p26`: "$560,000,000 on … July 17, 2001" → 560,000,000.00 exact (`scale{multiplier}` 1) | preparer gen-acct-manager-1; split of the three credits unsourced |
| F5 | sourced | 108 | 2001-07-17 | line costs → SG&A 50M (10^6) | expense→expense |
| F6 | sourced (one row per p.111 sentence; an interpretation joins them if more than one) | 111 | 2001-08-22 | CIP 544M → asset clearing → "10 assets in the amount of exactly $54.4 million each in Property Accounting's sub-ledger under the Fiber Optic Cable account" (544 at 10^6; 54.4 at 10^6 → 54,400,000.00; "10" via `number_word` if spelled) | the ten items are ten leaf accounts under Fiber Optic Cable (W3) |
| F7 | sourced (`F7`, the p.111 sentence "the $0.2 million that remained", likewise; by the id rule above the one sentence that states the entry is `F7`, the fact intent `F7` names) | 111 | derived `F7-date` | 0.2 at 10^6 → 200,000.00 | the specialist's entry, not the director's |
| F8 | sourced | 111, 261 | 2001-09-20 (`date_literal`, from the p.111 sentence) | CIP 560M → Ocean Cable 250M / Computer Equipment 150M / Fiber Optic Cable 160M (10^6) | `F8-p261`: "12 entries in similar, round-dollar amounts" (the `entry_decomposition` basis: `one_entry` / `twelve_entries`). If the p.261 sentence dates the entries only by month ("In September 2001"), that value is `month_literal` → `2001-09` on `F8-p261`; the booking day stays p.111's |
| F9 | sourced | 113 | 2001-10-19 | line costs → PP&E "in the amount of $742,725,000" → 742,725,000.00 exact | `F9-p113b`: the proposed split Transmission Equipment $300M + Communications Equipment $442M (= $742M, not the booked amount); credit accounts changed, amounts not stated |
| F10 | sourced | 114 | 2002-01-23 | line cost expense → PP&E 941M (10^6), into "furniture and fixture accounts" (plural; split unsourced) | |
| F11 | sourced | 114–115 | derived `F11-date` | 100M out of an asset account, offset by a release from a corporate accrual account (10^6) | accrual offset |
| F12 | sourced (`F12-p116`), or an interpretation (see F13) | 116 | 2002-04-12 | line cost expense → capital 718M (10^6) | W-T-03's input; "stated in the same sentence as the $818M" (§6.4) |
| F13 | as F12 | 116 | 2002-04-17 | line cost expense → capital 100M (10^6) | §6.4 says F12 and F13 are stated in the same sentence as the $818M. If the extraction confirms one sentence, it is one sourced fact `F12F13-p116` (values 718M, 100M, 818M; `about_scope = "period:2002Q1"`), and `F12` and `F13` are two-reader interpretations of it, one per entry (one fact per sentence, §6.2) |

**Reporting periods** (§6.2; a `[[value]]` with rule `period_literal` on whichever sentence names the quarter, its own `F<n>-period` sourced fact if that is a different sentence): F1–F3 `2001Q1`, F4–F5 `2001Q2`, F6–F9 `2001Q3`, F10–F11 `2001Q4`, F12–F13 `2002Q1`.

**Derived facts** (rules from `case_derivations.toml`, A2; K-DERIVE recomputes each at load):
- `F7-date`: `from = ["F6", "F7"]`, `rule = "date_offset"`, `params = ["days=3"]` → `2001-08-25` (rendered weekday Saturday);
- `F11-date`: `from = ["F10", "F11"]`, `rule = "date_offset"`, `params = ["days=2"]` → `2002-01-25` (Friday);
- every `scale{multiplier}`, `date_literal`, `period_literal` and `number_word` application is a literal rule on a `[[value]]`, not a separate fact, unless its inputs sit in two facts (the EX-27 below).

**Interpretations** (two readers each, `reader` and `second_reader` are role/agent ids; `rationale` carries the reading and, where the plan names one, the weaker reading):
- `F4` (above): p.108's description joined with p.26's exact amount.
- `F6-approval`: `from = ["F6"]` (the p.111 sentence "Abide rarely entered and approved entries himself so his involvement in these transfers was unusual"); reading: the director both entered and approved the 2001-08-22 transfers (the "so" clause, the natural reading; H-011). `rationale` records the weaker reading "entered only", the basis of W-P-01-CF-01.
- `F12F13-doc`: `from` = the p.116 sentence (possibly `F12F13-p116` itself) that says the preparer "handed him [Capital Reporting] a Post-it Note that had the $818 million adjustment on it"; reading: the Post-it is F12's and F13's instruction document. It is an `interpretation` (§5.5 H-013 note, §6.2, §6.4 W-D-06 and W-P-02), never `derived`: no registered rule produces it. `rationale` records the weaker reading "the record gives F12 no instruction document"; W-P-02 and W-D-06 keep `evidence_attached` and `document_date` as branches either way.
- F6's decomposition is not a fact: it is the interpretive rule `subledger_to_gl_legs` (A2), with "creating 10 assets" (p.111) and "making 10 different entries" (pp.260–261, `F6-p260`, sourced) as its basis.

**Instruction-document facts (§6.2):** `F1-doc` (sourced, p.106: the one-page "March 2001 Adjustments" document; existence, no date: "March 2001" is the title's subject month, not a document date, so it gets no `month_literal` value and F1 stays B(document_date) in W-D-06); `F9-doc` (sourced, p.113: the e-mail; undated; "Vinson sent it to Renfroe to have the entry booked"); `F10-doc` (sourced, p.114: "On January 23, 2002, Howard in Abide's group prepared a draft journal entry"; date value 2002-01-23 — the only dated one, W8's anchor); `F12F13-doc` (the interpretation above, undated).

**Second-source facts (§6.4 confirmed scope).** The SEC v. Vinson & Normand ¶¶30–35 sentences that give "approximately" amounts with the PP&E capital-expenditure accounts named: `source = "SRC-WC-002"`, `anchor_kind = "paragraph"`, `about_scope` the period each paragraph names. A ¶ sentence is joined to its Beresford entry only through an `interpretation` (scheme- or period-level → entry-level, §2.1), and W4 names these in W-D-01's basis. ¶34's sentences carrying the disputed 4Q01 JE values are the AN-100 facts below, not second sources.

**Context facts** (§6.2):
- `W-CTX-afe` (p.103): corporate-level general-ledger adjustments without an Authorization for Expenditure.
- `W-CTX-round` (p.90, `about_scope = "scheme:capitalization-2001Q1-2002Q1"`): "The capitalization entries were made in large, round-dollar amounts after the close of the quarter and only a few days before the Company announced its earnings."; `W-CTX-round-usage` (p.21): "in the tens, and often hundreds, of millions" (the R-QUAL basis for `round_dollar_lower_bound`).
- Earnings releases `W-CTX-er-2001Q1` 2001-04-26 (p.107), `W-CTX-er-2001Q2` 2001-07-26 (p.110), `W-CTX-er-2001Q3` 2001-10-25 (p.114).
- Filing dates: SRC-WC-002 ¶¶48–50, "on or about", 2001-05-15, 2001-08-14, 2002-03-31, 2002-05-15 (one fact per sentence, `W-CTX-filed-<period>`); `W-CTX-filed-2001Q3`: the 3Q01 10-Q was "filed on November 14, 2001" (SRC-WC-001 p.301).
- Oral instructions: `W-CTX-oral-ppe` ("NORMAND telephoned", ¶30); `W-CTX-oral-1q02` (p.116: "Yates, with Normand and Vinson on the phone, called and asked Abide to book the entry").
- Support: `W-CTX-support-p7` ("these accounting entries were made without supporting documentation", SRC-WC-002 ¶7; `about_scope = "scheme:capitalization-2001Q1-2002Q1"`, scope from ¶6: 1Q01–1Q02), a characterization of support, not a statement that no document existed, so it supports entry facts only through an `interpretation`; `W-CTX-support-p29` (¶29: "without any supporting documentation or proper business rationale"), `about_scope = "period:2001Q1"` only.
- **AN-100, quarantined** (§6.2): ¶34 gives a $941M line-cost reduction (agreeing with Beresford) and $560M of journal entries "in or around February 2002", while Beresford p.114 dates F10's draft JE 2002-01-23. Every ¶34 fact that carries the $560M JE amount or the "in or around February 2002" date gets an `AN100-<n>` id (if the $941M is in the same sentence, that fact is quarantined too and F10 rests on Beresford alone). The date is a bare month: its `[[value]]` is `month_literal`, literal "February 2002" → `2002-02` (§2.4); the "in or around" hedge is wider than the month; it is recorded as a comment on the fact row and not modelled, because no expectation may read it. No expectation's basis may contain an `AN100-*` fact (W4's test). Beresford's 2002-01-23 (`F10-doc`) is not quarantined: §6.4 W-D-06 rests on it by name.

**Statement-level facts** (`granularity = "statement_line"`; they feed only the `statement` variant and the W-NOTE-01 note, never an entry-level book, §3.2; `anchor_kind = "table_cell"` binds by value unless noted; table, row and column labels are read from the filing at authoring). Each carries A1a's vintage-independent `cell` key so K-VINTAGE (A3b) can compare one published cell across vintages: `W-ST-ta2000-prev`, `W-ST-ta2000-restated` and `W-ST-ta2000-filed` share `cell = "total_assets@2000-12-31"` (SRC-WC-406 `restates` SRC-WC-401, W1, so K-VINTAGE treats SRC-WC-406 as the later vintage and the bridge uses its A); `W-ST-ta1999-restated` and `W-ST-ex27-1999-ta` share `total_assets@1999-12-31`; the two Δ facts carry their own row-label keys `<Δ row label>@2000-12-31` as the table prints them:

| Fact | source | value (literal → rule → exact) | assurance (from W1's row) | used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `W-ST-ta2000-prev` | SRC-WC-406 | 98,727 → `scale{multiplier}` 10^6 (the table's "in millions" caption) → 98,727,000,000.00 | `filer_not_from_audited_statements` (Item 6) | W-T-02's A |
| `W-ST-ta2000-adj1` | SRC-WC-406 | −745 → −745,000,000.00 | same | W-T-02's Δ |
| `W-ST-ta2000-adj2` | SRC-WC-406 | −53,794 → −53,794,000,000.00 | same | W-T-02's Δ |
| `W-ST-ta2000-restated` | SRC-WC-406 | 44,188 → 44,188,000,000.00 | same | W-T-02's B (never posted) |
| `W-ST-ta2000-reclass` | SRC-WC-406 (prose footnote; `anchor_kind = "page"` or `"line"`, sentence-aligned) | the $176M reclassification between the filed and the "previously reported" value | same | K-VINTAGE naming both vintages |
| `W-ST-ta2000-filed` | SRC-WC-401 | 98,903 → 98,903,000,000.00 | `filer_audited` | W-T-02's second vintage (named, never posted) |
| `W-ST-ta1999-restated` | SRC-WC-406 (selected data, "(Restated)") | 85,280 → 85,280,000,000.00 | `filer_not_from_audited_statements` | W-NOTE-01 |
| `W-ST-ex27-1999-ta` | SRC-WC-EX27-1999 (`table_cell{EX-27, TOTAL-ASSETS, …}`) | literal 91,072 | `filer_audited` | W-NOTE-01 |
| `W-ST-ex27-1999-mult` | SRC-WC-EX27-1999 (`table_cell{EX-27, MULTIPLIER, …}`) | literal 1,000,000 | same | the scale of the above |
| `W-ST-ta1999-ex27` | derived: `from = ["W-ST-ex27-1999-ta", "W-ST-ex27-1999-mult"]`, `rule = "scale"`, `params = ["multiplier=from:W-ST-ex27-1999-mult"]` | 91,072,000,000.00 | — | W-NOTE-01 |

A + ΣΔ = B (98,727 − 745 − 53,794 = 44,188) is observed by W6 on the book, never computed here. W-NOTE-01 is a `[[note]]` (§5.1), not an expectation; W2 only supplies its basis facts.

**`roles.toml`** (§2.8; row shape is A1a's loader):
- one `[[role]]` per person the record names as a preparer, booker, sender, instructor or approver, with a label in the plan's style and the report's role words as its description: `property-accounting-director-1` (F6, p.111), `gen-acct-manager-1` (F4, §6.2), `gen-acct-director-1`, and one label each for F7's specialist, F9's booker (p.113), F10's draft-JE preparer (p.114) and F12/F13's preparer (p.116), as the re-verified sentences name them;
- the harness labels the books use: `case-second-reader`, `case-approver-1`, `case-approver-2`, `examiner-witness` (named by the plan), plus `case-poster-1` (the non-approver who posts a case) and `case-closer-1` (plans period closes, locks and issuances) — the last two are this round's proposed names;
- the K-NAMES deny list: SHA-256 of each normalized name token of every person the record names, never in clear (normalization is A3c's).

Keep the A8 pilot's facts (F2, F4, F9, F12) consistent with the full set: same ids and values (the shared A1a–A1c fixture, §3.2a). W1 landed the pilot slice's sourced rows; W2 keeps them byte-stable.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
```
python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify worldcom; rc=$?      # 0, no `FAIL ` line; regenerates receipts.toml whole
cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline         # A10a
cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_worldcom                          # W1/W2/W3 load-time tests
```
The second reader re-runs `verify worldcom` with a second `FA_CASES_CACHE` (W1) and must agree on every receipt field except `verified_utc` (`values_sha256` and `alignment` included).

**Expected check-report lines** (A3a/A10a own the format; the values below are what each field must contain; `<n>` counts the rows of this case):
```
CHECK worldcom K-PROV PASS examined=<all facts>/<all facts>
CHECK worldcom K-BIND PASS examined=<sourced facts>/<sourced facts>
CHECK worldcom K-SCOPE PASS examined=<sourced facts>/<sourced facts>
CHECK worldcom K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<sourced facts>/<sourced facts>
CHECK worldcom K-DERIVE PASS examined=3/3     # F7-date, F11-date, W-ST-ta1999-ex27 at W2; W3's leg amount_rules raise it
EXCERPTS worldcom facts_with_quote=0 words=0
```
Receipts consistency prints no line of its own: one receipt per sourced fact, `alignment` = `sentence` for every `page`/`paragraph` fact and `value` for every `table_cell` fact, the four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) true, `values_sha256` matching the committed values and scope, `original_hash_compared` as copied; any violation prints a `FAIL` line.

**Unit tests** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`):
- `wc_derived_dates_recompute`: `F7-date` = 2001-08-22 + 3 = `2001-08-25`, weekday Saturday; `F11-date` = 2002-01-23 + 2 = `2002-01-25`, weekday Friday.
- `wc_scaled_amounts_are_exact`: F4 560,000,000.00 (`scale` 1 on "$560,000,000"), F9 742,725,000.00, `W-ST-ta2000-prev` 98,727,000,000.00, `W-ST-ta1999-ex27` 91,072,000,000.00; each as a checked i128 at scale 2 with no float.
- `wc_statement_bridge_inputs_are_three_separate_facts`: A, both Δs and B are four distinct facts with distinct anchors, so no B value feeds an A or Δ (the K-TAUT precondition W6 relies on).
- `wc_roles_hold_no_clear_names`: every `[deny] hashes` entry of `roles.toml` is a 64-hex digest (A1a), and no label or description contains a deny-listed token.
- `wc_month_literal_values_recompute`: the `AN100-*` date value "February 2002" → `2002-02`, whose days are 2002-02-01 … 2002-02-28 (2002 is not a leap year); a planted member `2002-02-29` is refused; if F2 uses `date_range_literal`, `2001-04-23..2001-04-24` has exactly two days and a planted `2001-04-24..2001-04-23` (reversed) is refused.

**Planted negatives** (each edits one row of an in-memory or temp copy; the committed files are never edited). With `values_sha256` in every receipt (§4.4), an edit to a sourced fact's values or `about_scope` made after `verify` fails offline as K-BIND; an edit to its `source` or `quote_sha256` fails offline as a receipt mismatch. The authoring-time run on the author's cache additionally names the semantic reason (`scope_ok`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`), so each such edit is locked twice:
- Offline (`cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_worldcom`):
  - `wc_p29_rescoped_to_f12_fails_k_bind_offline`: `W-CTX-support-p29` with `about_scope = "entry:F12"` → `FAIL K-BIND facts.toml:<line> W-CTX-support-p29: values_sha256 mismatch` (the research's own ¶29 error, §2.1);
  - `wc_f4_p108_exact_dollar_value_fails_k_bind_offline`: `F4-p108`'s value rewritten as the exact 560,000,000.00 under `scale` 1 (p.108 states only "$560 million") → K-BIND `values_sha256` mismatch naming `F4-p108`;
  - `wc_ta2000_prev_value_edited_fails_k_bind_offline`: `W-ST-ta2000-prev` set to 98,903 (the filed vintage) → K-BIND `values_sha256` mismatch;
  - `wc_ta2000_prev_repointed_to_401_fails_receipt_mismatch`: `W-ST-ta2000-prev` with `source = "SRC-WC-401"` → `ReceiptMismatch` (the receipt's `source` is SRC-WC-406, A1a);
  - `wc_f6_fragment_hash_fails_receipt_mismatch`: the "entered and approved" fragment's SHA-256 written as `F6`'s `quote_sha256` → receipt `quote_sha256` mismatch naming `F6` and both digests;
  - `wc_postit_typed_derived_fails_k_prov`: `F12F13-doc` retyped `provenance = "derived"` (A1a's field), its interpretation fields (`reader`, `second_reader`, `rationale`) replaced by `rule` = a name absent from `case_derivations.toml` and `params = []` → K-PROV (no registered rule) / K-DERIVE FAIL naming `F12F13-doc` and its line (changing only the `provenance` value is refused earlier, at load, as `TwoProvenanceKinds`, A1a);

  - `wc_ex27_fact_anchored_line_fails_k_anchor`: `W-ST-ex27-1999-ta` re-anchored `line{…}` (anchor `l<first>-<last>`, and its receipt's `alignment` set to `sentence`, so A1a's loader does not refuse the copy first with `WrongType` or `ReceiptMismatch`) while its source's `anchor_scheme` lists `table_cell` → K-ANCHOR FAIL naming the fact;
  - `wc_fragment_quote_fails_k_bind_shape`: a copy whose `F6` carries `quote = "entered and approved"` (quote present, as after OD 2a) → K-BIND FAIL: the quote is not sentence-shaped and its SHA-256 differs from the receipt's.
- Authoring-time (a temp copy of the case directory, `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify <copy>` on the author's cache; each prints a `FAIL ` line naming the fact and exits non-zero):
  - `W-CTX-support-p29` re-scoped `about_scope = "entry:F12"` → `scope_ok = false` (¶29 is about "the first quarter of 2001"; F12's reporting period is 2002Q1);
  - the "entered and approved" fragment's SHA-256 used as `F6`'s `quote_sha256` → no sentence-aligned span matches (`aligned = false` / not found);
  - `F4-p108` typed `sourced` with the value 560,000,000.00 → `values_in_quote = false` (p.108 states only "$560 million"; which is why F4 is an interpretation);
  - `W-ST-ta2000-prev` re-pointed at SRC-WC-401's total-assets cell → `values_in_quote = false` (that cell prints 98,903).
  Each authoring-time negative is recorded in the landing with its `FAIL ` line (exit 1); its offline twin above is the permanent regression lock.

No book is built, so there is no run-log JSONL here.

## Notes
- **← W1** supplies the `OK` source rows, the pilot slice and the fetch/extract records. **← A3a** supplies K-PROV, K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR and K-DERIVE, the std-only SHA-256 and the normalization these facts are checked with.
- **Owner decisions.** Under hash-first vendoring `quote` stays absent (A10a) and `quote_sha256` binds. Quote text waits for OD 2a; quotes containing names (the p.111 F6 quote, and most others) also wait for OD 3.
- **The research workspace is not a source** (§4.5). A §6.2 value that fails to bind on re-verification is committed as the source states it. Any §6.4 expectation resting on it is then reopened in its own item, with a `Weakened-tests:` trailer if a single verdict becomes a branch (§16).
- **Settled: Post-it reading.** The plan types the F12/F13 Post-it reading an `interpretation` (§6.2's F12 row, §6.4 W-D-06 and W-P-02, §5.5's H-013 note), so no rule is registered for it in `case_derivations.toml`. W-P-02's record-consistent cell for F12/F13 stays `manual_assertion(InternalTransfer, reconstruction placeholder)` and W-D-06 stays B(document_date) for F12.
- **Settled: statement-level facts and §2.7.** W-T-02's A posting cites the restating filing's "as previously reported" column (SRC-WC-406), because the bridge uses the restater's A (§2.7, K-VINTAGE); the filed 98,903 (SRC-WC-401) is named as the other vintage and never posted. Table cells bind by value (§4.1 after round 1), so these facts need no sentence alignment.
- **AN-100 reading.** §6.2 records both ¶34's values and Beresford's 2002-01-23 "as separate sourced facts" and bars any expectation from resting on "the disputed JE amount or date"; since §6.4 W-D-06 rests on Beresford's 2002-01-23 by name, the quarantined set is ¶34's conflicting values (`AN100-*`). W4 enforces it.
- **Settled: receipts bind the fact row.** Round 2 recorded that a receipt carried no values, so a value or scope edit after `verify` passed offline. §4.4 now gives every receipt `values_sha256` (the fact's canonical literal values and `about_scope`) and `alignment`, and renames `sentence_aligned` to `aligned`; the offline twins above replace that gap. The anchor is bound by the receipt's own `anchor` (K-ANCHOR). Requires A1a/A9/A3a/A10a to carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned`, and A1a/A2 to accept the `month_literal` / `date_range_literal` value forms `YYYY-MM` and `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD` (neither rule is in A1a's or A2's list at r2b).
- **Fact ids** are this round's proposal; the A1a–A1c pilot fixture and A8 must use the same ids for F2, F4, F9 and F12.
- **Requires (foundation beads at r3):** A9 to accept a case-directory path as `<case>`, because the authoring-time negatives run `verify <copy>` on a temp copy and A9 reads `<case>` as a directory name under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/`; and A2 to accept `scale` as a two-input derived rule that reads its multiplier from its second input fact (`W-ST-ta1999-ex27`'s `params = ["multiplier=from:W-ST-ex27-1999-mult"]` is this bead's proposal), since A2 lists `scale{multiplier}` only as a literal rule over one `[[value]]`, its power k in `param`.
- W8 depends on this item for F10's draft-JE date anchor (`F10-doc`), and W3 for every fact the books encode.

description:
## Why One documented entry can need several books (§3.2), and entry-level facts and statement-level aggregates must never share one. If they did, a $98,727M total-assets posting would enter `jet.round_amounts`' population and add findings no source supports. WorldCom needs three variants (§6.3): - `native` carries the D, P, N, CF rows and the native restatement (W-T-03, W-R-02..04, W-D-07/08), plus W-T-04; - `migration` exists only for `jet.self_approved` on F6, the one documented approval; - `statement` carries W-T-02 and W-R-01, because the native calendar starts at 2001Q1 and a Historical period admits only Migration. Every input the kernel or a procedure reads that the record does not state must be a declared default or an enumerated branch class (§2.6). This item writes those declarations once, so that W4–W9 assert against one encoding. The shape follows the plan's §3.2a schema exactly: the TOML subset cannot nest rows or keep the relative order of arrays, so the documented history is one ordered `[[step]]` array and every leg, target and cell is a foreign-key row. ## What to build **Files** (`crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/`): `books/native.toml`, `books/migration.toml`, `books/statement.toml` (§3.2a tables `[book]`, `[[period]]`, `[[principal]]`, `[[account]]`, `[[document]]`, `[[intent]]`, `[[case]]`, `[[leg]]`, `[[step]]`, `[[branch_class]]`, `[[default]]`), each with its line in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/embedded.rs` (A1a's index), and W3's tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs` (load-time) and `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs` (the `worldcom_neg_*` build negatives). `case.toml` is A8's (with `letter = "W"`; W1 may land its minimal header first); W3 adds `variants = ["native", "migration", "statement"]`. Ids follow W2's fact ids and §3.2b: a documented entry's intent id is its fact id (`F1` … `F13`, with F6 as intents `F6a` and `F6b`, both `fact = "F6"`); a case Δ is `delta-`, and when one book has several Δs against the same target they are `delta--`, n = 1, 2, … in step order (only the statement book's W-T-02 needs it; this round's extension of §3.2b); a statement-book posting uses the fact id of the figure it posts. Field spellings are A1b's: `allocation_law`, `allocation_total`, `allocation_targets` for an allocation; `[[leg]] amount_literal` (the canonical decimal at the unit's scale) with `amount_rule` = `value:#` | `derived:` | `branch:` | `synthetic`; step `ref`s per A1b's per-kind grammar. Account codes, step `seq` numbers and branch-class ids below are this bead's proposals (only their order and uniqueness matter; filler codes start with `9`, A6). Every authored `idempotency_key` is a stable per-intent key of at most 51 bytes (A1b's limit: A7c's per-cell key `.<12 hex>` adds 13 bytes and must fit `max_idempotency_key_bytes = 64`, `registries/limits.toml:33-35`). ### `books/native.toml` (§6.3) - **`[book]`**: `variant = "native"`, `opening_date` before 2001-01-01 (proposal `2000-12-31`), `calendar = "custom"`, `base_unit = "USD"`, `posture` per A1b. The native book extends the A8 pilot's `books/native.toml` (the shared A1a–A1c fixture, §3.2a): same ids for F2, F4, F9 and F12. - **`[[period]]`** (`kind = "Normal"`): `2001Q1` 2001-01-01..2001-03-31, `2001Q2` ..06-30, `2001Q3` ..09-30, `2001Q4` ..12-31 (`fiscal_year = 2001`); `2002Q1` 2002-01-01..03-31, `2002Q2` ..06-30 (`fiscal_year = 2002`). `fa period create --fiscal-year 2001|2002` creates them (and any calendar periods the case does not use, which stay `Future`); the runner maps each label to the code the command reports and logs the map (§3.2a, A7a). Every `[[step]]` and branch cell names the label, never a CLI code. - **`[[principal]]`** (`profile = "Human"`): the record's role labels from `roles.toml` (W2), each with `grants = ["read", "post"]` (the `capability_grants` default, below; `property-accounting-director-1`'s W-P-01 cells add `approve`, §6.4's spelling: `fa draft promote` admits the capability (`crates/fa-journal/src/draft.rs:990`) before it checks the owner (`:996-1001`), but on the CLI's embedded `--as` route the promote handler implies `approve` itself (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:6090`, `ctx.capability(args, &["approve"])`, `:1173-1185`), so the grant is harmless there and `FA-REF-011` at `:990` arises only under an issued token lacking `approve`, which no case cell uses; plan §6.4 says "else `FA-REF-011`", the code implies the op, as W5 records), and the harness labels: `case-second-reader` (`read`, `approve`; reviews stubs and findings), `case-approver-1`, `case-approver-2` (`read`, `approve`, `restate`), `case-poster-1` (`read`, `post`, `restate`; posts the case, never approves it), `case-closer-1` (`read`, `close`; plans soft-close, close, lock and issuance), `examiner-witness` (`witness`). `case-poster-1` and `case-closer-1` are this round's proposed labels (W2's `roles.toml`). - **`[[account]]`** (`role_map` interpretive, `role_map_rule` set on every row; title: [cases] W4: WorldCom D rows W-D-01/-03/-04 and W-N-01 on native, W-D-02 on migration; W-NOTE-02 (jet.post_closing, all X) in Limits
description:
## Why
This item lands WorldCom's detection rows: the "externally labelled positives" that case books add beside fa-gen (entries the investigators documented, not entries we planted), and the predicate-level negatives from documented scheme entries that fall outside a predicate (§12.4). The claim types are D and N (§0.3).

The shape is DEBATE-002's single-verdict table as re-verified by the H-010 final-state review (§6.4). Each target carries per-component statuses (S/Sd/Si/B/Rel/X). Branch tables appear wherever the record leaves an attribute open, and X wherever a procedure's tier makes a verdict inadmissible (§2.5). The confirmed scope is that `expense.capitalization`@2 cites each of F1, F4, F9, F10, F12 and F13 at severity High, on two independent sources: Beresford pp.106–116, and SEC v. Vinson & Normand ¶¶30–35 ("approximately" amounts, with the PP&E capital expenditure accounts named). Every other single verdict rests on Beresford alone.

A8's pilot lands a subset (W-D-01 on F4 and F9, W-D-03 on F4, W-N-01 on F2). W4 completes the native table, and carries W-D-02 (A8b's pilot) on W3's full migration variant. `jet.post_closing` is all X on this record, and a row whose components are all X is not an expectation (it can neither PASS nor FAIL), so it lands as the Limits note W-NOTE-02 (§5.1, §6.4; the former W-D-05).

## What to build
**File.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml` (§5.1–§5.2): the `[[expectation]]`, `[[target]]` and `[[branch_cell]]` rows below, and the `[[note]]` row W-NOTE-02. Its claimed ids (every row below except the note) are added to `case.toml` `claims` (A8 authors the WorldCom `case.toml`, with `letter = "W"`). It reads W3's `books/native.toml` and `books/migration.toml` and W2's `facts.toml`; it adds no intent or step except one `finding_record` (and `finding_review`, `engagement_file`) step per claimed procedure in each book's `[[step]]` array, at `known_at = pre_case` on `native` (`finding_review` and `engagement_file` only where a finding cites a documented entry with an S, Sd or Si cite, so none on `migration`, whose W-D-02 cite is B). On `migration`, which carries no restatement case, W-D-02's `finding_record` step follows `migrate_finalize` (staged chunks are invisible to every Lantern procedure until finalize, §6.6) and records at the head after it (see Notes). Each `finding_record` and `engagement_file` step names its `principal` (A1b refuses either without one, `MissingField`): a label holding `read` and `produce` (`registries/verbs.toml:881`: "Recording and exporting require read and produce"; `:736`: `engagement file` journals "under produce"), never `case-second-reader`, because the review "requires a Human with read and approve who is independent of the run producer" (`:881`). The `engagement_file` step's `ref` is `finding:<expectation id>` (W3's spelling).
- Each D row has `type = "D"`, `book_variant`, `statement_template = "D.detection"`, `basis`, generated `premises`, `granularity = "journal_entry"`, `capabilities`, `procedure`, `version`, `about = "history"` and `known_at = "pre_case"`: the §5.1 default for D on `native`, so that the case's own Restatement entries never enter these populations (§6.3). W-N-01 has `statement_template = "N.no_finding"`.
- Each `[[target]]` row names its fact, its `branch_scope`, `branch_attrs`, its `admitted_cell` (K-JOINT) and the component fields of A1c (`cite`, `cite_status`, `severity`, `severity_status`, `statistic_name`, `statistic_value`, `statistic_scale`, `statistic_status`; statuses `S`, `Sd`, `Si`, `B(<attr>,…)`, `Rel(account_vid_order)`, `X`). Cited accounts project to account codes, and cited legs to (fact, leg ordinal); ordinals are 0-based, as `jet.rs` enumerates legs (`crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:40-42`, `:105`).
- Each `[[branch_cell]]` row carries `expectation`, `target`, `cell`, the expected verdict, `record_consistent` and `default`.

**Rows authored** (values copied from §6.4; statistic names from the code at 8196f5e40: `capitalized_expense_amount` `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:1121`, `round_legs` `jet.rs:142`, `days_to_period_end` `jet.rs:200`, `own_approvals` `jet.rs:404`):

| `[[expectation]]` | type | variant | procedure@version (params) | targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W-D-01 | D | native | `expense.capitalization`@2 (tier C) | F1, F4, F9, F10, F12, F13 |
| W-N-01 | N, `kind = "no_finding"`, `mechanism = "crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:1066-1124"` | native | `expense.capitalization`@2 | F2, F3, F5, F6a, F6b, F7, F8, F11 |
| W-D-03 | D | native | `jet.round_amounts`@1 (L, `round_power` 3) | F4, F6a, F6b, F1, F9, F10, F12, F13 |
| W-D-04 | D | native | `jet.period_end_timing`@1 (C, `window_days` default 3, `registries/procedures.toml:61-64`) | F1, F4, F9, F10, F12, F13 |
| W-D-02 | D | migration | `jet.self_approved`@1 (L) | F6a, F6b (the director's entries; never F7) |

| `[[note]]` | case | basis | template |
|---|---|---|---|
| W-NOTE-02 (`jet.post_closing`@1, tier P, every component X; the former W-D-05) | `worldcom` | F1, F4, F9, F10, F12, F13, `W-CTX-round` (p.90: "… after the close of the quarter …") | `NOTE.observation` |

**`[[target]]` and `[[branch_cell]]` values.**
- **W-D-01 / F4**: cite Sd `[F4, CIP account, the three line-cost accounts]`; severity S `High`; statistic Sd `capitalized_expense_amount = 560000000.00` (scale 2) under `one_leg_per_named_account` (one CIP account named; single-source, Beresford pp.26, 108).
- **W-D-01 / F1**: cite Sd; severity S High; statistic B(amount_precision): "$142 million" is presentation-rounded, so each residue cell's expected value is the CIP debit leg of that cell's witness (F1's OLTA debit has no `fixed_asset` role and is never the capex leg).
- **W-D-01 / F12, F13**: cite Sd; severity S High; statistic B(amount_precision, leg_split).
- **W-D-01 / F9, F10**: cite Sd for the entry and Rel(account VId order) for the cited fixed-asset account (`cutoff.rs:1103-1104`), with A5b's `rel_rule = "min_vid_debit_leg{fixed_asset}"` (the closed list in `rel.rs`; A8's F9 row); severity S; statistic B(leg_split) and Rel: the value is the debit leg on the minimum-VId fixed-asset account of the entry (`cutoff.rs:1100-1122`: `capex_debits` sorted by account VId, `[0]` taken), checked on every run from the logged book id with `fa_model::account_vid(book, code)` (`crates/fa-model/src/ids.rs:296-298`), or by reading `account_vid` from `fa explain balance --json` (§2.6 rule 9). The book id is random per `fa book create` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:3879-3883`). The rendering lists the values the documented legs allow and says the selection depends on a random identifier.
- **W-N-01** per target: not cited; each target carries its twin as A1c's `twin_kind = "mutation"`, `twin_attribute`, `twin_value` and `twin_expect = "reports"` (§3.7 item 3), the flip being the one account attribute that puts the entry inside the predicate (a `fixed_asset`-role debit against an Expense or `accrued_expense` credit, `cutoff.rs:1066-1097`): F2, the credited OLTA account retyped `Expense`; F5, the debited SG&A account retyped `Asset` with role `fixed_asset` (the role admits only `Asset`, `registries/account_roles.toml:46-48`); F8, the credited CIP account retyped `Expense` (its debits are already `fixed_asset`), dropping CIP's `fixed_asset` role with it, since the role admits only `Asset`; F6a (Dr asset clearing / Cr CIP, W3), the credited CIP account retyped `Expense` (its role dropped as for F8) and the debited asset clearing account mapped to `fixed_asset`, because a CIP flip alone leaves no `fixed_asset` debit; F7, by its re-verified legs: as F6a if it debits clearing and credits CIP, as F6b if it credits clearing into `fixed_asset` items; F6b, the credited clearing account retyped `Expense`; F3 and F11, see Notes. Every twin flips one §2.6 attribute, `chart_role_mapping` (the `role_map` output for the entry's accounts), which the `[[target]]` row states account by account. The twin is never rendered. These entries are documented parts of the scheme ("parking"; transfers designed to keep the auditor from detecting the capitalized amounts, pp.106, 111). They are never "legitimate look-alikes" and never enter a near-miss denominator (§12.4).
- **W-D-03 / F4** (`leg_split`; one `[[branch_cell]]` per feasible cell from A5a; "exactly one non-multiple" is infeasible and is named, not authored). Expected values follow `jet.rs:130-142` (legs cited as `Cite::Leg`; Medium iff every leg is round, else Low):
  - `leg_split=all_multiples`: cite `[F4, (F4,debit), (F4,credit×3)]`, Medium, `round_legs = 4`;
  - `leg_split=two_non_multiples`: cite `[F4, (F4,debit), (F4,the round credit)]`, Low, `round_legs = 2`;
  - `leg_split=three_non_multiples`: cite `[F4, (F4,debit)]`, Low, `round_legs = 1`.
  The cite of the 560,000,000.00 CIP debit leg is Sd in every cell.
- **W-D-03 / F6a, F6b**: Sd on the fact; B(entry_decomposition) on the cited (fact, leg ordinal) set under `subledger_to_gl_legs` ("exactly $54.4 million each", p.111; "10 different entries", pp.260–261); severity Sd Medium (every leg is a multiple of 10^3 units under either decomposition, `jet.rs:134-138`); statistic B(entry_decomposition): `one_allocation_entry` → `round_legs = 11` on one compound entry (10 × 54.4M Dr + 544M Cr); `ten_two_leg_entries` → `round_legs = 2` on each of ten entries. F6a (CIP → clearing, 544M, two legs) gives `round_legs = 2`, Medium, on its default class cell; that value is computed here from `jet.rs:130-142`, not a §6.4 figure.
- **W-D-03 / F1, F9, F10, F12, F13**: B(amount_precision, leg_split) on every component; F1 has a documented exception to R-QUAL ("not effected through a single, round-dollar entry", p.105).
- **W-D-04** per capitalization entry: cite B(effective_date), severity S `Low`, statistic B: `effective_date=inside_window` → finding, `days_to_period_end` = the cell's distance to the period's last day (0, 1 or 2; the period `end` is exclusive, `jet.rs:187-189`); `effective_date=outside_window` → no finding. The declared default (the reporting period's last day) is the inside cell with `days_to_period_end = 0`, marked `default = true`.
- **W-NOTE-02** (`[[note]]`, §5.1): `id = "W-NOTE-02"`, `case = "worldcom"`, `basis` as tabled, `template = "NOTE.observation"`, and no other field. It has no `[[target]]`, no component, no verdict and no `procedure`/`version` field (A1c refuses a note naming a verdict field, `NoteWithVerdict`), it is never PASS or FAIL and never counted as an expectation, and it renders only in Limits (§12.3, A14b) as a limit of what a reconstruction can show: the corrected code-tier table classes `jet.post_closing` as tier P (its commit gap depends on the population of commits; its verdict would only mirror where the harness places the period close), and "a correction looks like the entry it corrects to these predicates" (H17). No N row: N is barred on tier P (§3.7). The population-tier procedures (`jet.unusual_*`, `numbers.round_amount_density`, `benford.*`) are part of the same note; they get no expectation row and reach Limits through A13's `not_exercisable` (`population_relative`) coverage rows.
- **W-D-02** (B(approvals_recorded); the record states the approval only as a habit, the p.111 sentence quoted in W2, and pp.260–261 credit the ten entries to the director "and his staff"). Cells, from `jet.rs:360-404`:
  - `approval_encoding=migration_legacy_pair,approvals_recorded=entered_by=approved_by=property-accounting-director-1`: finding; cite B `[F6x entry]` (a legacy pair adds no `Cite::Approval`); severity S High; statistic Sd `own_approvals = 1`. This is the cell §15 A7m/A8b name;
  - `approvals_recorded=approved_by≠entered_by`: no finding (`total_own = 0`);
  - `approvals_recorded=none`: no finding (the entry is outside the population).
  The procedure fires only on the branch "legacy entered-by = approved-by", a declared encoding resting on an `interpretation`, not a sourced fact.

**Admitted cells (K-JOINT, §2.6 rule 7).** A refused branch removes the entry from every D population on that branch, so every D target names the admitted cell it runs on, its evidence cell at least.
- Capitalization targets run on `entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Open,evidence_attached=manual_assertion(InternalTransfer)` (A8's recorded choice, or OD 5's `NotInPublicRecord`), or the Adjusting/Open cell where a row says so.
- F4's record-consistent evidence cell is "none named" (W-P-02 → `FA-REF-080`). Its D targets therefore run on a named admitted cell that is not record-consistent, and the rendering says so.

**Claim class and calibration (K-ERRRATE, §5.6),** rendered verbatim from the registries:
- `expense.capitalization`@2: `claim = "statistical"`, `calibration = "planted"` (`procedures.toml:1482`) → "exercised only on planted anomalies in tests; its false-positive rate on real books has not been estimated".
- `jet.round_amounts`@1, `jet.period_end_timing`@1, `jet.self_approved`@1: `corpus` → "measured on fa-gen's labelled synthetic corpora, where precision is 100% by the generator's construction (`lantern_calibration.toml:22-33`); its false-positive rate on real books has not been estimated".

**Runs and reads** (§3.3 steps 6 and 8):
- `fa procedure run <id>` / `fa jet …`, then `fa finding record <id> --known-at <seq>` at the pre-case frontier (`registries/verbs.toml` `finding record <procedure-id> [--param <name=integer>]… [--known-at HEAD|<seq>]`). Components are read with `fa finding list --certificate C:<run>`.
- The D outsider read: `fa finding export --certificate C:<run> --export-format canonical --out <f>`, then `fa finding replay <f> --certificate C:<run> --known-at <seq>` (§12.1).

**Finding → source traversal (§2.7).** After each D run, `case-second-reader` records `fa finding review F:<vid> --action acknowledge --note <template> --evidence D:<fact stub>` for every finding that cites a documented entry with an S, Sd or Si cite. Then `fa engagement file <id> --finding <vid>`, and `fa finding export --include-reviews --export-format canonical` replays it.
- R check: each such finding carries exactly one review, whose evidence is its entry's stub, and no finding that cites only filler carries one. It is reported inside the D line's projection (`review=acknowledge:<fact>-stub`); a missing or extra review FAILs that line.
- It renders as "acknowledged, citing ⟨source, anchor⟩", never "confirmed"; `dismiss` is never used.

**Witnesses** (§3.7), all executed:
- Filler and identifier invariance (A11a): K = 5 seeded discipline-obeying filler variants, the empty variant, one extremal variant per tier, and ≥ 2 runs (≥ 2 book ids). Native filler posts as `PostBatch` chunks of at most 8,190 entries; migration filler is migration chunks staged before finalize (A6). Every S, Sd, Si and Rel component must agree across all of them; a disagreement fails and names the procedure.
- The mutation twin for each W-N-01 target (A11c).
- The reference differential (A4r, present through A8). Cite sets of `jet.round_amounts`, `jet.period_end_timing` and `jet.self_approved` are compared with `fa_reference::lantern::{round_amounts, period_end_timing, self_approved}`. `expense.capitalization` has no reference function and is printed `not_modelled`, never skipped silently.
- Combination rule (§3.3): filler variants run on the default branch cell only, and branch cells on the empty-filler variant only. L and C cells are co-resident targets in one book.

title: [cases] W5: WorldCom P rows W-P-01(a)+CF-01, W-P-01(b) on F6b (allocate probe), W-P-02, W-P-03+CF-01, W-P-04
description:
## Why This item lands WorldCom's prevention-at-commit rows (P, with CF rows; §0.3). A P row is a first-refusal observation that is conditional on its encoding. It cites the invariant its refusal exercises but never inherits `invariant` class, and it names the documented attribute it rests on, with its avoidability CF row beside it (§0.3 wording rules). The record fixes almost none of the attributes the kernel reads: entry class, period state at commit, evidence and approvals. So most rows are branch tables over the §2.6 closed enum, evaluated by dry run and checked against the fa-reference differential (§2.6 rule 6, §3.3). The one single verdict is W-P-01. It is Si: conditional on the two-reader interpretation of p.111 that the property-accounting director both entered and approved the 2001-08-22 transfers. H-011 was refuted because, on that natural reading, those transfers have a `FA-REF-008` branch (§0.4). Rounds 3b and 4 established which encodings reach it today: draft self-promotion of F6a, but only on admitted cells (Z.6), and possibly the allocation self-approval of F6b, since `fa allocate` already takes `--approval` (Z.7). ## What to build **File.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml`: the P and CF rows below, on `native` (W3's `books/native.toml`). It adds no documented intent; the branch-cell copies of F1, F4, F6a, F6b, F9, F10, F12 and F13 are generated by the runner from W3's intents and `[[branch_class]]` rows (A7c), never authored.
