title: [cases] A1b: book-variant schema (§3.2a) loader for books/<variant>.toml with foreign-key resolution and per-unit balance checks
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A1b, §3.2, §3.2a, §2.6.

Book variants are first-class (§3.2). One documented entry can need several books (`native`, `migration`, `statement`, `ledger`), and every expectation names the variant it runs on. A P claim's premises are "every attribute the intent's encoding sets" (§2.6 rule 6). The encoding must therefore be explicit, checkable data (§3.2a) that the runner replays, not choices buried in runner code. The schema is shaped by the TOML subset: tables cannot nest, so legs, steps and branch classes are foreign-key rows; and the parser loses the relative order of arrays with different names, so the documented history is one ordered `[[step]]` array (§3.1; `crates/fa-registry/src/toml.rs:56-60`). The variant split serves D/P/N/CF (entry-level `native`/`migration`) and T/C/R (`statement`/`ledger`). Entry-level facts and statement-level aggregates never share a book: if they did, a 98,727,000,000.00 total-assets posting would enter `jet.round_amounts`' population (§3.2).

## What to build
A loader and validator for `crates/fa-oracles/cases/<dir>/books/<stem>.toml`, with the tables of §3.2a (all scalars or one-line arrays). A stem is `<kind>` or `<kind>-<suffix>` (§3.2b): the kind (`native`, `migration`, `statement`, `ledger`) is the prefix, so `statement-bridge`, `statement-sunpower` and `ledger` are stems and every rule that names a variant kind (K-EVID, A6's no-filler rule) reads the prefix.

**Files and public API** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/book.rs`: `pub struct BookVariant { book, periods, principals, accounts, parties, documents, intents, cases, legs, steps, branch_classes, defaults, ledger_maps, events, migration_imports }` with one struct per table (`BookHeader`, `PeriodDef`, `PrincipalDef`, `AccountDef`, `PartyDef` with its parsed `Relation`s, `DocumentDef`, `IntentDef`, `CaseDef`, `LegDef`, `StepDef` with `pub enum StepKind`, `BranchClassDef`, `DefaultDef`, `LedgerMapDef`, `EventDef`, `MigrationImportDef`, `EntityRelation`), `pub enum VariantKind { Native, Migration, Statement, Ledger }` parsed from the stem, `pub fn load_book(case: &Case, path: &str, text: &str) -> Result<BookVariant, Vec<LoadError>>`, and `to_document()` for the canonical-bytes round trip. `Case` gains `books: BTreeMap<variant, BookVariant>`.
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/amount.rs`: `pub fn parse_amount(text: &str, scale: u8) -> Result<i128, AmountError>` (an optional `-`, digits, and exactly `scale` fractional digits; no exponent, no separators) and checked per-unit sums (`checked_add`, never wrapping). The scale of each unit comes from `fa_registry::units_embedded()` (`crates/fa-registry/src/lib.rs:1107-1121`). This is fa-oracles' own arithmetic (§3.1), never fa-money.
- New `LoadErrorKind`s: `Unbalanced`, `UnknownPeriod`, `DuplicateLabel`, `TargetRequired`, `TooLong`, `BadStem`, `BadId`.

**Tables (§3.2a).**
- `[book]`: `variant` (equal to the file's stem, else `BadStem`), `opening_date`, `calendar` (`custom`), `base_unit`, `posture`, and optional `entities` (a one-line array of `<code>[:<name>]`, the `fa book create --entity` members of a multi-entity book; C3's pro forma book is the one user, a case-local extension the plan does not list), with, beside it, optional `entity_relations`: a one-line array of `<from entity code>|<kind>:<to entity code>;basis=<code>;valid_from=<date>[;valid_to=<date>][;pct=<num>/<den>]`, the relations between two of the book's legal entities, posted as `fa party relate <from> <to> --kind … --basis … --valid-from … [--pct …]` (C3's OWNS edge, `<acquirer>|owns:<target>;basis=<code>;valid_from=<date>;pct=<bps>/10000`). They cannot be `[[party]] relations`: `fa consolidate` keeps only OWNS edges whose two ends are the book's legal entities (`crates/fa/src/consolidation.rs:316-334`), and `fa party relate` resolves a code to a party before a legal entity (`crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:183-206`), so no `[[party]] id` may equal an entity code.
- `[[period]]`: `code` (the case's label, for example `2001Q1`; `fa period create` assigns its own codes, so the runner maps each label to the code the command reports and logs the map, A7a), `start`, `end`, `fiscal_year`, `kind`. The runner creates every declared period (`fa period create --fiscal-year N` per fiscal year, A7a) and opens none: a period is opened only by a `period_open` step of the history, which the case beads author for every period they post into. Periods are born `Future`, which admits nothing (`registries/admissibility.toml:55`), so a post into a period no earlier `period_open` step opened is observed as the kernel's refusal, never opened silently. Migration pre-opening periods are born in the state admissibility's `[[pre_opening]]` rows give them (A7m).
- `[[principal]]`: `label` (from `roles.toml`), `profile`, `grants` (a one-line array of ops).
- `[[account]]`: `code`, `name_fact`, `type`, `role` (may be empty), `opened`, `closed`, `role_map_rule`.
- `[[document]]`: `id`, `stub_of` (a source id, or a fact id for a fact stub), `grade` (`AgentUpload`), `reviewed_by`.
- `[[intent]]`: `id`, `fact` (the documented entry it encodes, `derived:<rule>` for a Δ, or `synthetic`), `class`, `principal`, `effective_date`, `document_date`, `memo`, `evidence` (a document id, `manual_assertion:<code>`, or empty), `idempotency_key`, `target`, `target_kind` (`reverses` / `restates` / `revises` / `reclassifies`), `reason`, `scenario`, `allocation` (flattened as `allocation_law`, `allocation_total`, `allocation_targets` (a one-line array of account codes; §5.3), `allocation_source` (an `[[account]]` code) and `allocation_source_side` (`debit` | `credit`)). An allocation intent names its `source` account and, beside an explicit `total`, the `source_side` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:10142`, `:10306` at 8196f5e40; the usage, `registries/verbs.toml:459`, "`total` + `source_side` … or `source_period`"), so `allocation_source` is required on every allocation intent and `allocation_source_side` with `allocation_total` (`MissingField`); these are W9's names for W3's F6b. The period-balance form (`source_period`) has no field here; no case uses it.
  - On an intent that a `migrate_stage` step stages (a `migration` stem only; elsewhere `UnknownField`), the optional legacy attribution `source_entered_by` and `source_approved_by`: `roles.toml` labels (so K-NAMES reads them), rendered into the chunk JSON, whose two fields `fa migrate stage` seals as text (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:21397-21404` at 8196f5e40). W-D-02's cell `entered_by = approved_by = property-accounting-director-1` (W3, A7m) is their first user; A7m's "chunks carry legacy `source_entered_by` and `source_approved_by`" had no case-file field until now. `source_recorded_at_ns` is never authored, because recorded time is never user-supplied (doctrine 6); it is not in this table (`UnknownField`).
- `[[case]]`: `id`, `kind`, `periods`, `determined_on`, `authority`, `disclosure`, `approvers` (a one-line array of two role labels with no shared session lineage, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:3450`), `poster`.
- `[[leg]]`: `intent`, `ordinal` (0-based and dense within its intent: the leg's index in the rendered intent, which the runner renders in ordinal order, A7a; the kernel numbers a cited leg by its index in the entry's legs, `crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:40-42`, `:117-133`, so A1c's cite `F4#0` names the leg with `ordinal = 0`), `account`, `side` (`Dr`/`Cr`), `amount_literal`, `amount_rule`, `unit`.
  - `amount_literal` is the leg's amount in canonical form: a decimal string with exactly the unit's scale (`"560000000.00"` for USD).
  - `amount_rule` says where that amount comes from:
    - `value:<fact>#<ordinal>`: a `[[value]]` row (1-based ordinal, A1a) read under its literal rule;
    - `derived:<fact id>`: the computed value of a `derived` fact (L1's `scale{multiplier}` dollar facts, which L2's legs post; E4's remainder facts `REM-A-<period>`; W6's planted `plant-rem`);
    - `derived:negate`: on a case Δ only, the target intent's leg with the same ordinal, with the same account and unit and the opposite side (A2's `negate`);
    - `branch:<class id>`: the declared representative of a branch class;
    - `synthetic`: filler, and the planted run-time edits that must load (A7a).

    A bare rule name other than `negate` (`derived:difference`, `derived:remainder`) names no inputs, so K-DERIVE could not recompute it: it is refused (`DanglingKey`), a computed amount always names its derived fact, and no `derived` fact may take the id `negate`. Legs carry no sign: `amount_literal` is the magnitude of the computed value and `side` the direction (W6's `plant-rem` computes −53,794 $M and its leg's literal stays 53,794,000,000.00). A1b checks the form; K-DERIVE and K-BIND (A3a) recompute each non-literal rule and refuse a leg whose `amount_literal` differs. That is how "after each leg's literal rule" (§15 A1b) is checked without A1b depending on A2.
- `[[step]]`: `seq`, `kind`, `ref`, `known_at` (`head` / `pre_case`, for `finding_record`), `branch_class` (empty means all), and two optional fields this bead adds, because §3.2a names no actor for a step that runs no intent: `principal` (the role label that runs the step) and `approvers` (a one-line array of the labels whose `fa approve` vids the step cites). Defaults follow the plan's named roles: `finding_review` and stub reviews → `case-second-reader` (§2.7); `checkpoint_witness` → `examiner-witness` (§12.7); `case_approve` → the `[[case]]` row's `approvers`; `case_post` → its `poster`. Every other step that runs no intent (`period_*`, `issue`, `assert_balance`, `checkpoint`, `finding_record`, `engagement_file`, `scenario_*`, `case_open` … `case_close` except the two above, `migrate_*`, `filler_batch`, `event_record`, `rule_*`) must name its `principal` (`MissingField`), and `period_lock`, `issue`, `migrate_stage`, `migrate_finalize` and a `migrate_import` stage step must name `approvers` (two for the migration steps, `admissibility.toml:350`; `--approval <vid> --approval <vid>` on an import stage, `crates/fa-cli/src/migration_import.rs:41`), none of them the step's own principal. W3's `case-closer-1` (period transitions and issuances) is this field's first user. `kind` is one of §3.2a's kinds plus four this bead adds for L3's optional L-R-03 (`event_record`, `rule_check`, `rule_propose`, `rule_backtest`): `intent`, `batch`, `allocate`, `period_open`, `period_soft_close`, `period_close`, `period_lock`, `issue`, `assert_balance`, `scenario_fork`, `scenario_run`, `scenario_diff`, `case_open`, `case_determine`, `case_rehearse`, `case_approve`, `case_post`, `case_disclose`, `case_close`, `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_witness`, `finding_record`, `finding_review`, `engagement_file`, `filler_batch`, `migrate_open`, `migrate_stage`, `migrate_finalize`, `migrate_import`, `event_record`, `rule_check`, `rule_propose`, `rule_backtest`.
  - Four per-kind fields, also this bead's:
    - `params`, a one-line array of `<name>=<value>`. On `finding_record`, each name is a registered parameter of the step's procedure (`fa_registry::procedures::Procedure::parameter`) and each value an integer, passed as `fa finding record <id> --param <name>=<integer>` (`registries/verbs.toml:881` at 8196f5e40; L4's `window_days=4`). On `rule_backtest`: `compare=<seq of an earlier rule_propose step>` (its IR digest is the `--compare` baseline), `from=<YYYY-MM-DD>`, `to=<YYYY-MM-DD>`. On any other kind it is refused (`UnknownField`); an unregistered parameter name or a non-integer value is `UnknownValue`.
    - `evidence`, on `assert_balance` only and required there: the `[[document]]` id of the filing stub its `fa assert-balance --evidence` cites (A7b; W6's SRC-WC-406 stub, never SRC-WC-401's).
    - `asserts`, on `assert_balance` only and optional: the fact id whose value the step asserts; by default the row's published value (an R's `posted`). W6 asserts W-T-02's A fact before the case and its published B after it.
    - `document`, on `issue` only and required there: the `[[document]]` id of the filing stub the issuance cites (`fa statement issue … --document <filing stub oid>`, A7b), whose `stub_of` must be a source id (`MissingField`, `DanglingKey`). It records which filing each issuance carries, so A3b's K-VINTAGE can check the filing an A1c `read_selector = reported_in:<period label>[#<n>]` (the n-th `issue` step of that period in step order) names; E4 issues FY1999 twice, once per filing.
- `[[party]]` (§3.2a since polish round 2): `id` (the party code `fa party add` receives), `label` (a `roles.toml` role label, or the id of a sourced fact naming an entity such as LJM1; both checked by K-NAMES), `kind` (as `fa party add` accepts: `fa_model::PartyKind`, `crates/fa-model/src/rea.rs:48-57`: Customer, Vendor, Employee, Bank, RelatedEntity, BeneficialOwner, Regulator, Counterparty), and `relations` (a one-line array, posted with `fa party relate`, `crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:23`; verb row `registries/verbs.toml:824-833`). §3.2a spells a relation `kind:party`; `fa party relate <from> <to> --kind owns|controls|related --basis <code> --valid-from YYYY-MM-DD [--valid-to …] [--pct <num>/<den>]` requires a basis and a valid-from (`rea.rs` `PARTY_EXAMPLE`), so each token is `<kind>:<party id>` followed by `;basis=<code>;valid_from=<date>` and optionally `;valid_to=<date>`, `;pct=<num>/<den>` (E6's CFO→LJM1 edge, C3's ownership). The party-scoped procedures (`ponzi.net_investment`, the `graph.*` procedures, §9.3, §7.2) read the party a leg names. `[[leg]] party` (§3.2a) is a `[[party]]` id or empty; `[[leg]] entity` (C3's extension) is a code of `[book] entities` or empty.
- `[[branch_class]]`: `id`, `attribute` (the §2.6 closed enum), `rule` (from `case_branch_rules.toml`), `values`.
- `[[default]]`: `attribute`, `rule`, `rationale`. These are the declared default encodings (§2.6 rule 2).
- `[[ledger_map]]` (M0's case-local extension for `ledger` stems; §3.2a has no ledger table): `source` (the complaint rows `[[fact]]` id), `account` (the trustee account id), `book_account`, `party`, `cash_account`, `transfer_account`, `amount_columns` (one-line array of printed headers). The runner renders one two-leg intent per row, id `<account>:<page>:<line>`; A1b checks every code and the party resolve, that `transfer_account` holds neither the `cash` nor the `investor_capital` role, and that `[[ledger_map]]` appears only on a `ledger` stem.
- `[[event]]` (L3's case-local extension for L-R-03's optional Canon backtest; §3.2a has no event table): `id` (the `--code`), `kind` (one `fa event record --kind` accepts: sale, purchase, receipt, payment, shipment, return, accrual, depreciation), `occurred_on`, `evidence` (a one-line array of `[[document]]` ids, at least one: "Every recorded Event requires at least one non-empty evidence citation"), `participants` (a one-line array of `[[party]]` ids or `[book] entities` codes), and one resource as `resource_label`, `resource_amount_literal`, `resource_amount_rule` (the leg forms above, so K-DERIVE recomputes it) and `resource_unit` (`registries/verbs.toml:507` usage at 8196f5e40: `event record --code <CODE> --kind … --occurred-on … --evidence <oid>[:<role>]… [--participant …]… [--resource <label>:<amount>[:<instrument>]]…`). L3's `sale` events, one per positive difference of consecutive §E observations, are authored with OD 2b's observation facts (their `resource_amount_rule` names L4's derived change facts); until then the table is empty and L-R-03 prints its OD 2b UNRUN (A7a). Events are records, not postings: no population reads them.
- `[[migration_import]]` (M6's case-local extension for `fa migrate import`): `id`, `run` (the `seq` of the `migrate_open` step whose run it binds), `source` (a `[[document]]` id, distinct from every trial-balance document, `registries/verbs.toml:519`), `format` (one of the usage's formats: quickbooks-iif, quickbooks-csv, xero-csv, netsuite-csv, csv, beancount, hledger), `account_map` (a one-line array of `<legacy account>=<[[account]] code>`), optional `column_map` (a case file path, required for `csv`), `default_unit` and `entry_periods` (a one-line array of `<source id>=<[[period]] label>`, FullDetail only). These are the import intent's fields (`registries/verbs.toml:519` at 8196f5e40: "run, source (D:<oid>), format …, account_map, optional default_unit, and column_map TOML for generic csv"; `crates/fa-cli/src/migration_import.rs` field list :294-303), rendered by the runner (A7a, A7m) with the run and document vids it observed; the import JSON is derived, never committed.

**What each step `ref` names** (the plan says only "an intent, period, case or procedure id, etc."; A1b fixes the grammar):

| `kind` | `ref` |
|---|---|
| `intent`, `allocate` | an `[[intent]]` id |
| `migrate_import` | `<import id>` (a `[[migration_import]]` row: `fa migrate import --action prepare --intent <rendered import.json>`), or `<import id>#<chunk>` (`--action stage --package D:<the package the prepare step reported> --chunk <zero-based index> --approval <vid> --approval <vid>`, `crates/fa-cli/src/migration_import.rs:41`, `:94-103`); an import's stage steps follow its prepare step, chunks in order from 0 |
| `batch`, `migrate_stage` | an intent range `<first id>..<last id>`, in file order, of one principal; on a `ledger` stem `batch` may instead name a `[[ledger_map]] account` (one batch per account, M0) |
| `filler_batch` | a filler variant id (A6) |
| `period_open`, `period_soft_close`, `period_close`, `period_lock`, `issue` | a `[[period]]` label |
| `case_open` … `case_close` | a `[[case]]` id |
| `scenario_fork`, `scenario_run`, `scenario_diff` | a scenario name that some `[[intent]] scenario` names |
| `checkpoint` | a new checkpoint label, unique in the variant |
| `checkpoint_witness` | an earlier `checkpoint` label |
| `finding_record` | `<procedure id>@<version>`, a row of `registries/procedures.toml` |
| `assert_balance` | `<expectation id>[#<target fact>]`: the T or R whose read fields give the account and period; with `#<target fact>`, one `[[target]]` of a multi-read row (W7's W-R-04, one per (account, quarter) cell). The value is `asserts`, or the row's published value (resolved by A1c's loader, which loads after the books) |
| `finding_review` | an expectation id (resolved by A1c's loader) |
| `engagement_file` | a `[[document]]` id (`fa engagement file <id> --document <oid>`), or `finding:<expectation id>` (W3, W4, W8): every finding the runner matched to that D expectation's targets in this run, each filed with `fa engagement file <id> --finding <vid>` (`registries/verbs.toml:736` at 8196f5e40); the expectation must be a D whose `procedure@version` has an earlier `finding_record` step in the variant (A1c resolves the id) |
| `event_record` | an `[[event]]` id |
| `rule_check`, `rule_propose`, `rule_backtest` | a rule source file `rules/<name>.rule` of the case (each listed in A1a's embedded index); `fa rule check <file>`, `fa rule propose <file>`, `fa rule backtest <file> --compare <digest> --from … --to …` (`registries/verbs.toml:664` at 8196f5e40), whose IR digest binds from the `rule_proposed` event |
| `migrate_open` | the `[[document]]` id of the declared legacy trial balance |
| `migrate_finalize` | the `seq` of its `migrate_open` step |

**Validation.**
- **Foreign keys.** Every foreign key resolves:
  - leg → intent, and leg → account;
  - intent, document `reviewed_by`, and case approvers/poster → principal label → a `roles.toml` label (A1a);
  - intent `evidence` → a document id, or `manual_assertion:<name>` with a name in scope `manual_assertion` (`registries/reason_codes.toml:29-53`, read with `fa_registry::reason_codes::ReasonCodes::embedded()`);
  - intent `reason` → a reason in scope `supersession`;
  - intent `class` → a row of `registries/entry_classes.toml` (`fa_registry::EntryClasses::embedded()`);
  - intent `target` → an intent id. It is required, together with `target_kind`, for the classes that reverse, restate, revise or reclassify (`TargetRequired`);
  - intent `fact` → a fact id, `derived:<rule>`, or `synthetic`;
  - document `stub_of` → a source id or a fact id (a citation stub, §2.7), `placeholder:<fact id>` (a `fa:case-placeholder:v1` reconstruction placeholder of a documented entry, §2.6 `evidence_attached`), `filler:<variant id>` (the variant's `fa:case-filler:v1` document, A6), `rows:<rows fact id>` (M6: a source file the runner renders from a committed `rows_file` for `fa migrate import`, as the generic csv its `column_map` reads; derived, never committed; while the rows file is uncommitted, OD 2b, every step that needs it prints UNRUN, A7a), or `legacy_tb` (A7m: the migration run's legacy trial balances derived by A2's `legacy_tb_from_chunks`, rendered `fa:case-legacy-tb:v1`; accepted on a `migration` stem only, at most one per variant, `UnknownValue` elsewhere; a case-derived `migrate_open` ref names it, while M6's printed trial balances are source stubs). K-EVID (A3c) tells the five apart by this field;
  - step `ref` → per the table above;
  - account `type` → `registries/account_types.toml` (`fa_registry::account_types_embedded()`), and `role` → `registries/account_roles.toml` (15 roles, `fa_registry::account_roles::AccountRoles::embedded()`) or empty; a role must admit the account's type (`AccountRole::admits`, `crates/fa-registry/src/account_roles.rs:169`; for example `fixed_asset` admits only `Asset`, `registries/account_roles.toml:46-47`), so `fa chart` never refuses the case's chart;
  - leg `unit` → a code of `registries/units.toml`;
  - leg `party` → a `[[party]]` id; each `relations` token's party → a `[[party]]` id, with `valid_from` present and `basis` a code of `registries/relationship_bases.toml` (read with `fa_registry::g0::RelationshipBases::embedded()`, `crates/fa-registry/src/g0.rs:632-637`; the CLI refuses any other, `crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:390-395`); a relation token's other end may also be a `[book] entities` code; `[[party]] label` → a `roles.toml` label or a sourced fact id; leg `entity` → a `[book] entities` code; each `entity_relations` token's two ends → two distinct `[book] entities` codes, with `basis` and `valid_from` as above and, for `owns`, a `pct` of whole basis points (`<bps>/10000`; `fa consolidate` refuses any other stake with FA-REF-194, `registries/verbs.toml:640` at 8196f5e40); a `[[party]] id` equal to an entity code → `DuplicateLabel`;
  - intent `allocation_source` → an `[[account]]` code; `source_entered_by`/`source_approved_by` → `roles.toml` labels; `[[event]] evidence` → document ids and `participants` → party ids or entity codes; `[[migration_import]] run` → a `migrate_open` step's `seq`, `source` → a document id, `account_map` values → account codes, `entry_periods` values → period labels;
  - step `evidence`/`asserts` (`assert_balance`) → a document id / a fact id; step `document` (`issue`) → a document whose `stub_of` is a source id; `params` names → registered parameters (`finding_record`) or `compare` → an earlier `rule_propose` step;
  - step `principal`/`approvers` → `[[principal]]` labels;
  - branch-class `attribute` → the §2.6 enum; default `attribute` → the §2.6 enum, `reason` (a correction reason is "a declared default with its rationale", §3.2a and K-REASON, but `reason` is not in §2.6's branch-attribute enum), or a book-context default of a `ledger` stem (`sign`, M0; `period_grain`, M3).
- **Balance.** Every intent balances per unit: ΣDr = ΣCr per unit, in exact integers at the unit's scale, over the legs as declared. Where a `[[branch_class]]` varies a leg's amount (`amount_precision`, `leg_split`), the declared legs are the default cell's representative; every other cell's balance feasibility (Σ rᵢ ≡ total mod 10^p, total ≥ the number of legs) is A5a's enumerator's. So "under every amount class" is delivered by A1b for the declared cell and by A5a for the rest.
- **Legs.** Each intent's leg `ordinal`s are 0, 1, …, n − 1 (dense and unique, else `WrongType`); a `value:<fact>#<n>` rule names an existing `[[value]]` row of that fact; a `derived:<x>` rule names `negate` on a case Δ or the id of a `derived` fact (`DanglingKey` otherwise).
- **Periods.** Every period an intent or step uses is declared in `[[period]]`; an intent's `effective_date` falls inside a declared period; `[[period]] code` labels are unique within the variant (they key the runner's label → reported-code map).
- **Ids (§3.2b).** An intent whose `fact` names a sourced or interpretation fact has that fact id as its `id`, or the fact id plus a one-letter suffix where one fact is encoded as several intents (`F6a`, `F6b`); a case Δ (an intent whose `target_kind` is `restates` or `revises`, §3.2b) has id `delta-<target intent id>`, or, where one variant has several Δs against the same target, every one of them `delta-<target intent id>-<n>`, n = 1, 2, … in step order (W3/W6's `delta-W-ST-ta2000-prev-1` and `-2`; E4's two FY1999 Δs); a Δ of a Δ prefixes again (E4's `delta-delta-10K-TA-A-FY1999-1`). The check reads the intent's `target` field, so the suffix is never parsed out of an id, and this rule takes precedence over the fact-id rule for a Δ whose `fact` names a sourced Δ value; `synthetic` intents and other `derived:<rule>` intents (a remainder posting, L4's derived net-change series) need only a unique id. Branch-cell copies are the runner's (A7c) and never authored. A breach is `BadId`.
- **Cases.** A `[[case]]` names two distinct `approvers`, and its `poster` is neither of them (`fa case post` by a non-approver, §3.3 step 5).
- **No filler on statement or ledger stems.** A `filler_batch` step on a `statement` or `ledger` stem is refused (§3.2: those variants carry no filler; a ledger D's extremal witness is A11a's harness-only copy, not a declared variant).
- **Limits.** Every authored `idempotency_key` fits in 51 bytes, so A7c's per-cell key (`<key>.<12 hex>`, 13 more bytes) stays inside the 64-byte limit (`registries/limits.toml:33-35`, `max_idempotency_key_bytes`); derived batch keys (M0, A6) are checked against 64 bytes; and every `memo` fits in 512 bytes (`:30-32`, `max_memo_bytes`), read with `fa_registry::limits_embedded()` (`crates/fa-registry/src/lib.rs:2087`), so the kernel never refuses a case intent for its length.
- **Step order.** `seq` values are unique and strictly increasing in file order, because the `[[step]]` array is the documented history.

## Tests & logging
Unit tests in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/book.rs` and `amount.rs`, run by `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; negative names follow the gate-evidence ratchet (`scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`).
- **Positive.** `pilot_native_book_loads_and_every_intent_balances`: `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/pilot/books/native.toml` (WorldCom F2, F4, F9, F12; A1b authors it) loads, every foreign key resolves, every declared intent balances per unit, and its canonical bytes round-trip.
- **Negatives (§15),** each a one-line planted edit of the pilot book, each asserting the kind and the planted line:
  - `leg_with_unknown_intent_is_refused`: a `[[leg]]` with `intent = "F99"` → `books/native.toml:<line>: DanglingKey: leg 1 names intent F99`;
  - `unbalanced_intent_is_refused`: F4's CIP debit changed to `"559999999.99"` → `Unbalanced: intent F4 USD Dr 559999999.99 Cr 560000000.00 gap 0.01`, naming the unit and the gap;
  - `step_with_unknown_period_is_refused`: a `period_close` step with `ref = "2001Q9"` → `UnknownPeriod`.
- **Derived negatives** (from §3.2a and the limits registry):
  - `duplicate_period_label_is_refused` (two `[[period]] code = "2001Q2"` → `DuplicateLabel`);
  - `amount_with_wrong_scale_is_refused` (`"560000000.0"` for USD → `WrongType`), and `amount_sum_overflow_is_refused` (two legs of `i128::MAX` minor units → `AmountError::Overflow`, never a wrapped sum);
  - `reclassification_without_target_is_refused` (`TargetRequired`);
  - `unknown_step_kind_is_refused` (`kind = "post"` → `UnknownValue`);
  - `manual_assertion_with_unregistered_reason_is_refused` (`evidence = "manual_assertion:NotARealCode"` → `DanglingKey`);
  - `role_that_does_not_admit_the_account_type_is_refused` (`role = "fixed_asset"` on an `Expense` account → `UnknownValue`);
  - `stem_with_an_unknown_kind_prefix_is_refused` (`books/statment-bridge.toml` → `BadStem`) and `variant_differing_from_its_stem_is_refused`;
  - `documented_entry_intent_not_named_after_its_fact_is_refused` (F4 encoded as intent `f4-cap` → `BadId`) and `negate_delta_not_named_delta_target_is_refused`;
  - `case_poster_who_is_an_approver_is_refused`;
  - `period_close_step_without_a_principal_is_refused` (`MissingField`) and `period_lock_step_approved_by_its_own_principal_is_refused`;
  - `party_relation_without_basis_or_valid_from_is_refused` and `leg_naming_an_unknown_party_is_refused`;
  - `filler_batch_on_a_statement_stem_is_refused`;
  - `authored_key_over_51_bytes_is_refused` (52 bytes → `TooLong`; 51 bytes loads: the boundary);
  - `ledger_map_on_a_native_stem_is_refused` and `ledger_map_transfer_account_with_the_cash_role_is_refused`;
  - (polish round 5) `legacy_tb_stub_on_a_native_stem_is_refused` (`stub_of = "legacy_tb"` in `books/native.toml` → `UnknownValue`); `leg_ordinals_not_dense_from_zero_are_refused` (ordinals 1, 2 → `WrongType`); `bare_derived_rule_name_amount_is_refused` (`amount_rule = "derived:difference"` → `DanglingKey`) and `derived_negate_outside_a_delta_is_refused`; `second_delta_on_one_target_without_its_ordinal_is_refused` (`delta-F4` beside `delta-F4-2` → `BadId`); `allocation_without_its_source_or_source_side_is_refused` (`MissingField`); `legacy_attribution_on_a_native_intent_is_refused` (`source_entered_by` on `books/native.toml` → `UnknownField`) and `authored_source_recorded_at_ns_is_refused`; `entity_relation_naming_a_non_entity_is_refused`, `owns_entity_relation_with_a_fractional_basis_point_stake_is_refused` and `party_id_equal_to_an_entity_code_is_refused`; `params_on_a_period_step_is_refused`, `finding_record_param_not_registered_for_its_procedure_is_refused` and `finding_record_param_that_is_not_an_integer_is_refused`; `assert_balance_without_evidence_is_refused`; `issue_step_without_its_filing_document_is_refused` (`MissingField`) and `issue_document_that_is_not_a_source_stub_is_refused` (a `placeholder:` stub → `DanglingKey`); `engagement_file_finding_ref_without_a_finding_record_step_is_refused`; `migrate_import_stage_before_its_prepare_is_refused` and `migrate_import_stage_with_one_approver_is_refused`; `event_without_evidence_is_refused`; `rule_step_naming_a_file_outside_rules_is_refused`.
- **Derived positives.** `statement_and_ledger_stems_load_with_their_kind`: `books/statement-bridge.toml` loads as `VariantKind::Statement`, `books/ledger.toml` with two `[[ledger_map]]` rows loads, and a `[[party]]` with `relations = ["owns:P2;basis=equity_voting;valid_from=1999-06-30;pct=1/2"]` parses into one relation. `migration_fixture_loads_with_migrate_step_kinds`: a minimal fixture `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/migration_min/books/migration.toml` whose steps use `migrate_open`, `migrate_stage` (an intent range, its intents carrying `source_entered_by`/`source_approved_by`) and `migrate_finalize` loads, and each step's `ref` resolves; a second copy with one `[[migration_import]]` row, a prepare step and two stage steps (`<import id>#0`, `#1`) loads. `extension_tables_load`: an `entity_relations` OWNS token between two `[book] entities` codes, an allocation intent with its source fields, an `assert_balance` step with `evidence`, `asserts` and a `#<target>` ref, two `issue` steps of one period each naming its filing stub's `document`, an `engagement_file` step with `ref = "finding:<D id>"`, a `finding_record` step with `params = ["window_days=4"]`, and an `[[event]]` row with its `event_record` and the three `rule_*` steps each load, with every reference resolved.
- **Logging.** Loader errors print `<file>:<line>: <kind>: <detail>`, naming the table and the foreign key. There are no runner lines.

## Notes
- **Dependency.** A1b ← A1a: the TOML loader plumbing, `row_line`, the `roles.toml` labels that `[[principal]] label` resolves against, and the shared four-file pilot fixture (the §3.2a worked example, authored as the A1a–A1c acceptance fixture under `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/pilot/`; A1b owns `books/native.toml`).
- **Period codes.** Checked at 8196f5e40: `fa period create --fiscal-year N` assigns the period codes itself. For a 13-period custom year these are `FY2026-P01`…`FY2026-P13` plus `FY2026-OPEN`, `FY2026-A1` and `FY2026-CLOSE` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs:15494-15530`). A `[[period]] code` such as `2001Q1` (the §2.4 `period_literal` form) is therefore a harness label, as §3.2a now states; the runner (A7a) maps it to the code the `period create` event reports and logs the map.
- **Flattening.** `allocation` (law, total, targets, source, source side), an `[[event]]`'s one resource, `entity_relations` and step `params`, `[[case]] approvers` and `[[branch_class]] values` must be scalars or one-line arrays, because the parser has no inline tables; the field names above are A1b's choice.
- **Parties.** §3.2a now lists `[[party]]` and the leg `party` field (polish round 2), with `relations` as `kind:party` tokens; the `;basis=…;valid_from=…` suffix is this bead's, because `fa party relate` requires both. Round 2's separate `[[party_relation]]` table is folded into `relations`.
- **Case-local names this bead accepts** (from the case beads; the plan does not spell them): `<kind>-<suffix>` stems (§3.2b now), `[[ledger_map]]` and the `sign`/`period_grain` defaults (M0, M3), `[book] entities`, `entity_relations` and leg `entity` (C3), the step `principal`/`approvers` fields with W3's `case-closer-1`, W3's statement-posting intent ids (the fact id of the figure posted, such as `W-ST-ta2000-prev`), and since polish round 5 the allocation source fields (W9), the legacy attribution fields (W3, A7m), `derived:<fact id>` amounts (L2, E4, W6), several-Δ ids (W3, W6, E4), step `params` (L4), `evidence`/`asserts` and `#<target>` refs on `assert_balance` (W6, W7), `document` on `issue` (A7b, A3b), `finding:` refs (W3, W4, W8), `[[event]]` with the `event_record`/`rule_*` kinds (L3), and `[[migration_import]]` with `rows:` stubs (M6).
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the fixture files.
- **Migration step kinds.** §3.2a lists `migrate_open`, `migrate_stage`, `migrate_finalize` and `migrate_import`; the `migration` variant replays through `fa migrate open|stage|finalize` (§3.3 step 3, §6.6, A7m), and `migrate_import` drives `fa migrate import --action prepare|stage` (M6's M-T-03).
- **Approvers and fa-z46b.** The two `[[case]] approvers` are role labels approved today with `--as` from the runner's process. Under fa-z46b they become distinct key holders (see A7b).
- **No `[[branch_class]] rule` check yet.** The `rule` field resolves against `case_branch_rules.toml`, which A5a creates. Until then the loader records the name and A5b's K-BRANCH resolves it.
- **Polish round 5 (cross-half items, checked against the case beads and the code at 8196f5e40).** The Δ-id rule rejected the several-Δ ids W3, W6 and E4 author (`delta-<target>-<n>`); the allocation fields lacked the `source`/`source_side` `fa allocate` reads (W3, W9); relation tokens named only `[[party]]` ids, while C3's OWNS edge must join two legal entities; no `amount_rule` named a derived fact (L2's dollar facts, E4's remainders, W6's plant), and `derived:<rule>` named no inputs; steps had no parameter field (L4's `window_days`), no event or rule kinds (L3's L-R-03; the verbs exist at 8196f5e40, `registries/verbs.toml:499-507`, `:656-664`, so the kinds are added rather than leaving L-R-03 hand-run), no `migrate_import` form for prepare and stage (M6), no `finding:` ref for `engagement_file` (W3, W4, W8), no way for `assert_balance` to say which value or target it asserts or which stub it cites (W6, W7), no field naming the filing stub an `issue` step cites (A7b's `--document`; K-VINTAGE's check of `reported_in:<period>[#<n>]`, E4's two FY1999 issuances), and migration intents had no field for the legacy attribution A7m says chunks carry (W3). Each now has a field, a resolution rule and a test above. Also: leg ordinals are 0-based (they are the kernel's cited-leg indices, `jet.rs:40-42`: W4 cites `(F4,0)` for F4's CIP debit, and A8's leg references follow the same numbering), and only `period_open` steps open periods (the runner creates them; the plan's "created … and then opened", §3.2a, is read that way, so A7a's book creation and the authored `period_open` steps never both open one).
- **Registries read, none edited.** A1b reads `entry_classes`, `account_types`, `account_roles`, `reason_codes`, `relationship_bases`, `units` and `limits` through fa-registry; it changes no registry, so no global crate-verdict invalidation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the A8 pilot `books/native.toml` (WorldCom F2, F4, F9, F12; `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/pilot/`) loads, every foreign key resolves, and every declared intent balances per unit in exact integers at the unit's scale (`pilot_native_book_loads_and_every_intent_balances`); a `statement-bridge` stem loads as a `statement` variant and a `ledger` stem with `[[ledger_map]]` rows loads.
- [ ] negative: a `[[leg]]` whose intent does not exist is refused with a named error and its line.
- [ ] negative: an unbalanced intent is refused, naming the unit and the gap.
- [ ] negative: a `[[step]]` referencing an unknown period is refused.
- [ ] negative (derived): two `[[period]]` rows with the same `code` label are refused (the label keys the runner's label → reported-code map); an amount with the wrong scale, an overflowing per-unit sum, an authored idempotency key over 51 bytes, a reversing/restating/revising/reclassifying intent without `target`, an unknown step kind, a stem whose kind prefix is not one of the four (or whose `[book] variant` differs from it), a documented-entry intent whose id is not its fact id, a `[[case]]` whose poster is an approver, a non-intent step with no principal, a party relation without a basis or valid-from, a `filler_batch` on a `statement` or `ledger` stem, and a `stub_of = "legacy_tb"` document outside a `migration` stem are each refused with a named error and its line.
- [ ] positive: the four migration step kinds (`migrate_open`, `migrate_stage`, `migrate_finalize`, `migrate_import`) are accepted kinds, and a fixture migration variant using them loads with every step `ref` resolved under the per-kind grammar (a `migrate_import` prepare step and its `#<chunk>` stage steps; staged intents carrying `source_entered_by`/`source_approved_by`).
- [ ] positive (polish round 5): `entity_relations` between two `[book] entities`, an allocation intent with `allocation_source`/`allocation_source_side`, `amount_rule = "derived:<fact id>"`, several-Δ ids `delta-<target>-<n>`, an `assert_balance` step with `evidence`, `asserts` and a `#<target>` ref, `issue` steps naming their filing stub's `document`, `engagement_file` with `finding:<expectation id>`, `finding_record` `params`, and an `[[event]]` row with the `event_record` and `rule_*` steps all load with every reference resolved; leg ordinals are 0-based.
- [ ] negative (polish round 5): non-dense or 1-based leg ordinals, a bare `derived:<rule>` amount, `derived:negate` outside a Δ, an unsuffixed Δ beside a suffixed one on the same target, an allocation without its source fields, legacy attribution outside a `migration` stem, an entity relation naming a non-entity or a fractional basis-point stake, a party id equal to an entity code, `params` on a kind that takes none or naming an unregistered parameter, an `assert_balance` step without `evidence`, an `issue` step without its filing `document` (or naming a non-source stub), a `finding:` ref with no earlier `finding_record` step, an import stage step before its prepare or with one approver, and an event without evidence are each refused with a named error and its line.
- [ ] no-claim: well-formedness only, nothing about whether a fact is true (as A1a). Nor does it show that the encoding is how the entry was booked; declared defaults and branches are A5a/A5b's, and the balance of cells other than the declared one is A5a's.

title: [cases] W5b: W-P-01(b) on F6a — fa post carrying the director's self-approval, FA-REF-008 first refusal (needs A0)
description:
## Why W-P-01(b) on F6a is the `entry_approval` encoding of the 2001-08-22 CIP → clearing transfer: the director's own Approval, cited at commit by `fa post` / `fa commit`. It is the most direct encoding of the p.111 reading that he both entered and approved the transfers (Si; §6.4). At 8196f5e40 it cannot be expressed through the CLI. `fa post` and `fa commit` take no `--approval` (`registries/verbs.toml:259`, `:395`), and the request builder hard-codes `approvals: Vec::new()` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:8230`). The plan therefore makes A0 a prerequisite: until it lands these cells are UNRUN, "never faked through the library" (§3.3 step 3). The item was split from W5 in round 4 so that A0 is a formal edge (Appendix Z.7). Claim type: P. Its avoidability row W-P-01-CF-01 lands with W5. ## What to build **File.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml`: the F6a `[[target]]` of W5's `W-P-01` expectation with `approval_encoding = entry_approval`, and its `[[branch_cell]]` rows, on `native` (W3's `books/native.toml`). No new intent: the cells are runner-generated copies of W3's F6a intent (A7c). Each cell sets `approvals_recorded = {approved_by = property-accounting-director-1}` (the preparer) and `acting_principal = property-accounting-director-1`. **Posting sequence** (A0's surface, spelled as A0's bead fa-yugf.2 now states it; A0 fixes the exact flag spellings; A0 is the repo bead fa-6f3g, see Notes). A0 follows the year-end close review pattern (`registries/verbs.toml:179`), per cell (each cell its own intent key, A7c `cell_key`): 1. `fa post --intent --review-out --as property-accounting-director-1 [--grant ]…` seals the F6a proposal once and emits its portable sealed bytes, `review_digest` and `proposal_digest`, writing nothing to the book; 2. `fa approve --proposal --as property-accounting-director-1`, the preparing principal approving his own entry, which prints the approval vid (the generic approval of a digest records it without reading the preparer, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:5217-5247`); 3. on a `manual_assertion` cell, in place of step 4: `fa document attest manual --review --digest --reason InternalTransfer --statement "" --approval --plan-out

--as property-accounting-director-1 [--grant ]…`, A0's review form of `attest manual` (plan §15 A0: "let `fa document attest manual` take the same retained sealed proposal … Then one proposal can carry both an approval and a ManualAssertion"), which records the assertion over the retained sealed proposal and plans it with the cited approval. This is the route A7a's runner runs for an approval-plus-assertion cell; A0's equivalent route (attest with `--review … --digest …` and no `--plan-out`, then step 4) is A0's own test, not used here. The preparer records the assertion, so the review must be the one he sealed in step 1 (`crates/fa-journal/src/attestation.rs:1502-1510`, A0); 4. on every other cell: `fa post --review --digest --approval --dry-run --plan-out

--as property-accounting-director-1 [--grant ]…` restores the exact sealed proposal and plans it with the cited approval. Then `fa commit --plan

` commits the representative of each distinct outcome. **Design constraints at 8196f5e40**, which the harness must respect (§15 A0): - `fa approve` is a publication, and any intervening publication invalidates a plan (`registries/verbs.toml:399`). - The builder seals with fresh entropy on every JSON parse (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:8137`), so re-parsing the intent after `fa approve` changes the digest and invalidates the approval (`crates/fa-cli/tests/bank.rs:887-888`; checked at `crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2923-2928`). The runner keeps the sealed bytes from step 1 and never re-renders the intent JSON between step 1 and step 4. - An entry that requires an approval (Adjusting in Closed) is refused `FA-REF-012` during planning, before any PostPlan exists (`crates/fa-journal/src/plan.rs:105-122`). The plan certificate binds the intent's digest, approvals included (`plan.rs:112`). **Cells and expected first refusals (§6.4).** Period law (step 5) checks the matrix op and carries the approval count forward (`crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2737-2766`); SoD (step 5'', `:2866`) runs before the evidence minimum (step 5b), so `FA-REF-008` (exit 7) is the first refusal in every cell that period law admits, whatever `evidence_attached` is: | class \ state | Open | SoftClosed | Closed | Locked | |---|---|---|---|---| | Original (`admissibility.toml:55-74`) | `FA-REF-008` | with `post_softclosed` → `FA-REF-008`; without → `FA-REF-011` | `FA-REF-010` | `FA-REF-010` (record-inconsistent) | | Adjusting (`:225-244`) | `FA-REF-008` | `FA-REF-008` | with `post_closed` → `FA-REF-008` (`adjusting-closed`); without → `FA-REF-011` | `FA-REF-010` (record-inconsistent) | | Reclassification, split per target (F1's $142M CIP leg; F2's $402M; `:203-222`) | `FA-REF-008` | `FA-REF-008` | with `post_closed` → `FA-REF-008` (`reclassification-closed`); without → `FA-REF-011` | `FA-REF-010` (record-inconsistent) | **SoD rule of each `FA-REF-008` cell** (settled from code; the refusal cites `sod_policy.toml#{rule}`, `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:94-100`). SoD's key is (class, state) (`crates/fa-policy/src/sod.rs:94-101`), and a key no `[[rule]]` names falls back to `[default]`, named `"default"` (`crates/fa-registry/src/sod_policy.rs:464-471`; `registries/sod_policy.toml:59-65`). So `law_row` is `sod_policy.toml#adjusting-closed` (`:118-127`) on Adjusting/Closed, `sod_policy.toml#reclassification-closed` (`:140-149`) on Reclassification/Closed, and `sod_policy.toml#default` on every Open and SoftClosed cell. The preparer exclusion refuses the self-approval in SoD's approver loop (`sod.rs:183-188`) before the approval count is checked (`:237`), so a Closed cell with `post_closed` gives `FA-REF-008`, never `FA-REF-012`. Each row is crossed with `evidence_attached` ∈ {none, placeholder_unreviewed, placeholder_reviewed, manual_assertion(InternalTransfer)}; the expected refusal is the same in every evidence cell, which is what this table shows (SoD precedes 5b). The single-$544M Reclassification is W-P-04, refused `FA-REF-185` before SoD (W5). The grant-reading cells are B(`capability_grants`) with W3's default marked. `record_consistent` follows W5's W-P-01 rule (the Si reading); every Locked cell is record-inconsistent (`record_consistent = false`: the sourced booking-before-filing facts exclude Locked), evaluated and rendered as such (§6.4). - **`manual_assertion` evidence cells.** A ManualAssertion binds the proposal digest it was recorded over (`crates/fa-journal/src/evidence.rs:1340-1377`), and at 8196f5e40 `fa document attest manual --intent … [--plan-out]` seals and plans its own proposal with no approvals (`crates/fa-cli/src/document.rs:1711-1765`; usage `registries/verbs.toml:483`), so no CLI route records the assertion over A0's reviewed proposal. Plan §15 A0 makes that route part of A0 (step 3 above), and A0's bead (fa-yugf.2) now carries it; the repo bead fa-6f3g does not yet, and the operator posts it there at landing (Notes). So these cells are built like the others once A0 lands and are expected `FA-REF-008` (SoD precedes 5b) on every cell period law admits. The runner detects the route from the `document` verb row listing `--review` (A7a). On a tree whose A0 lacks it, every `manual_assertion` cell (one per class × state × grant cell of the table, each Reclassification target separately) prints `UNRUN W-P-01 P native F6a/…,evidence_attached=manual_assertion(InternalTransfer) reason=needs:A0 (attest manual --review)` (A7a's text), never PASS and never built through the library, and W5b cannot close. These cells never carry `pending`: their prerequisite is detected at run time, not a probe. **Verdict checks** (as W5, §5.2): - the first refusal id, its exit read from the catalog (`registries/refusal_catalog.toml:94`, `:102`, `:110`), and the envelope naming the row; - `refusal.why.matrix`, `fix.argv` and `alternatives` checked structurally where the refusal carries them: the period-law `FA-REF-010`/`-011` carry `why.matrix` (and `FA-REF-010` a `fix.argv`), while SoD's `FA-REF-008` is a bare refusal with no Appendix D detail and no placeholder-free `fa` command in its fix (`crates/fa-journal/src/policy.rs:70-81`; `crates/fa-policy/src/denial.rs:390-391`), so its lines print `matrix=n/a fix_argv=n/a alternatives=n/a` (W5's token rule and its plan-vs-code note); - `fa explain refusal ` echoing the instance; - the stated remedy rendered from the catalog's `fix` template. For `FA-REF-008` at 8196f5e40 (`refusal_catalog.toml:94-100`): "collect the approval from a different, admissible principal over the same proposal digest". **Reference verdict** (A4r, via W5): `Oracle::post`, then `fa_reference::sod::verdict` with approver identity (`crates/fa-reference/src/sod.rs:28`), then `fa_reference::evidence::verdict`. The split-per-target Reclassification cells enter through `Oracle::reclassify(intent, target)` in place of `Oracle::post` (`crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:2303`; A4r), with the same SoD and evidence steps after it, so they are compared too (`ref=agree`). **Rendering.** W-P-01(b) renders "under the reading ⟨rationale⟩", beside W-P-01(a), W-P-01-CF-01 and W-P-04. ## Tests & logging **Run.** `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact worldcom`; negatives `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval`; unit tests `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_worldcom -- f6a_entry_approval_cells`. **Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; the values below are what each field must contain; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `/`; an UNRUN or FAIL carries its reason in A7a's trailing `reason=` field): ```text PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Open,evidence_attached=none refusal=FA-REF-008 exit=7 law=sod_policy.toml#default ref=agree matrix=n/a fix_argv=n/a alternatives=n/a commit_agrees=ok PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Adjusting,period_state_at_commit=Closed,capability_grants=+post_closed,evidence_attached=none refusal=FA-REF-008 exit=7 law=sod_policy.toml#adjusting-closed ref=agree PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Closed,… refusal=FA-REF-010 exit=7 law=admissibility.toml#Original/Closed ref=agree PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Locked,… refusal=FA-REF-010 exit=7 law=admissibility.toml#Original/Locked ref=agree record_consistent=false PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Adjusting,period_state_at_commit=Closed,capability_grants=-post_closed,… refusal=FA-REF-011 exit=7 law=admissibility.toml#Adjusting/Closed PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Reclassification,period_state_at_commit=Closed,capability_grants=+post_closed,… refusal=FA-REF-008 exit=7 law=sod_policy.toml#reclassification-closed ref=agree PASS W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Open,evidence_attached=manual_assertion(InternalTransfer) refusal=FA-REF-008 exit=7 law=sod_policy.toml#default ref=agree (sealed, approved, then attested and planned in one `fa document attest manual --review … --approval --plan-out`) … one line per cell of the table × evidence cell ``` Without A0 (on 8196f5e40 and any tree where the `post` verb row lists no `--approval`), every F6a entry-approval cell prints ```text UNRUN W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,… reason=needs:A0 (fa post --approval) ``` and, on a tree whose A0 has `--approval` but no review form of `attest manual`, each `manual_assertion` cell prints `UNRUN … reason=needs:A0 (attest manual --review)`. No library call stands in for the CLI approval. The runner detects A0 from the verb table as A7a does (`fa_cli::verbs::registry()`: `post` lists `--approval`; `document` lists `--review`), not from a build flag. Whether a tree that loses A0 fails the case test depends on W-P-01's claim (below): while W-P-01 is claimed these UNRUN lines exit non-zero; while it is unclaimed they are the observable and do not fail the test. **Planted negatives** (permanent tests on a temp copy; the committed case is never edited; each asserts the observable and a non-zero case verdict): - `worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval_by_other`: step 2 run `--as gen-acct-director-1`. Observable: `FAIL W-P-01 P native F6a/approval_encoding=entry_approval,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Open,… refusal` with the observed outcome `admit` on the evidence-admitting cells (and `FA-REF-080`/`-086` on the others): the cell depends on `approvals_recorded` and `acting_principal`. - `worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval_no_close`: the `period_close` step before the Original sweep removed. The sweep soft-closes the period before it closes it (A7c runs the cells through the history's own transition steps, and the table has a SoftClosed column), so the Closed cell is evaluated in SoftClosed, where an Original needs `post_softclosed` (`admissibility.toml:64-66`), which the cell's default grants lack, and period law refuses before SoD. Observable: `FAIL W-P-01 P native F6a/…,entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Closed,… reason=expected FA-REF-010 observed FA-REF-011`. - `worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval_reparsed`: the runner posts `fa post --intent --approval --dry-run` (a fresh seal) in place of `fa post --review --digest …`. Observable: the cited approval does not bind the new proposal digest (`post.rs:2923-2928`), so the dry run does not reach `FA-REF-008`; the observed refusal id or usage exit is recorded (as A0's own `approval_over_a_resealed_intent_does_not_admit` records it) and the cell prints `FAIL`. This locks the "never re-parse" constraint. - On a tree without A0: the UNRUN line above, and, once W-P-01 is claimed, a non-zero exit (asserted by the case test itself, not a separate test; A7a's `_selftest_neg_approval_row_without_a0_is_unrun_and_fails_the_claimed_case` is the runner's own lock). **Unit tests** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`, pure): - `f6a_entry_approval_cells` derives every authored cell's expected refusal from `registries/admissibility.toml` (Original `:55-74`, Adjusting `:225-244`, Reclassification `:203-222`) with SoD ordered after the op check and before evidence, and compares with the `[[branch_cell]]` rows; a planted copy expecting `FA-REF-080` on Original × Open × `none` (evidence before SoD) fails naming the cell. - `f6a_entry_approval_sod_rules` reads `registries/sod_policy.toml` raw and derives each `FA-REF-008` cell's rule by (class, state): `adjusting-closed` on Adjusting/Closed, `reclassification-closed` on Reclassification/Closed, `default` elsewhere; a planted `law_row = "sod_policy.toml#adjusting-closed"` on Adjusting/Open fails, naming the cell. **JSONL records** (§3.5): `verb = "post"` (`--intent … --review-out`, the seal), `verb = "approve"` (`--proposal`; the approval vid bound as `$APPROVAL_`), `verb = "document"` (`attest manual --review … --approval … --plan-out` over the sealed proposal, `manual_assertion` cells only, with `exit` and `refusal_id`), `verb = "post"` (`--review … --approval … --dry-run --plan-out` on the other cells, with `exit` and `refusal_id`), `verb = "commit"` (`--plan`, the representative, naming its dry-run step), `verb = "period"` for the sweep transitions, `verb = "explain"` (`explain refusal`); `branch_class` = the cell. On failure `REPRODUCE fa --book

` prints the `fa post --review-out`, `fa approve`, `fa post --review … --dry-run --plan-out` (on a `manual_assertion` cell, `fa document attest manual --review … --plan-out`) and `fa commit --plan` sequence, and `LOG ` ends the run. **Claims (the strict `pending` rule, plan §5.1).** `claims` holds expectation ids and a claim never excludes a cell, so W5b's cells, `manual_assertion` cells included, are claimed only as part of W-P-01. W-P-01 can be in `claims` only when none of its cells carries `pending` (A1c `PendingClaimed`). W5's F6a draft `manual_assertion` probe cells, and its F6b route-B cells if route B did not reach `FA-REF-008`, may still carry `pending` when W5b lands; then W-P-01 stays unclaimed, W5b's cells print their verdicts unclaimed, and a FAIL on any of them still fails the case test (A7a). If W5b's landing is the one that leaves no W-P-01 cell pending, it adds W-P-01 to `claims`; otherwise the landing that removes the last field does. Any UNRUN or FAIL on a claimed row exits non-zero; no `#[ignore]`. ## Notes - **← W5** supplies the W-P-01 rows, the probe outcome on F6b, the reference adapter use and the cell-evaluation sweep. **← A0** supplies `--approval ` on `fa commit` and `fa post --dry-run` and the review form of `fa document attest manual`, with verbs.toml and MCP parity. - **Settled from code: the self-approval count in Closed.** In Closed the matrix decision is `with:post_closed,1`; period law checks the op and carries the count to SoD (`post.rs:2737-2766`), and SoD refuses an approver equal to the preparer inside its approver loop (`crates/fa-policy/src/sod.rs:183-188`) before it checks the count (`:237`, `TooFewApprovals` → `FA-REF-012`). So the Closed cells give `FA-REF-008`. A0 changes no kernel code; if its landing still shows `FA-REF-012`, the cell's observed refusal is logged and the row is reopened, never relabelled to pass. - **Settled: the Locked column.** Locked cells are record-inconsistent (`record_consistent = false`), evaluated and rendered as such (§6.4; W5's note, and the requirement on A5b's K-BRANCH stated there). - **A0 is the repo bead fa-6f3g** (PLAN_DELTA after polish round 4). `fa-6f3g` ("Case studies [A0]: CLI approval surface for fa post (seal once, approve, post or plan with --approval)", open, P1) was filed from the landed plan; at landing the operator replaces fa-yugf.2 with fa-6f3g and posts A0's extra scope (the `attest manual` sealed-proposal route, the fa-z46b note) as a comment there, so W5b's A0 edge then means fa-6f3g. Besides `--approval`, the `manual_assertion` evidence cells need that extra scope; if fa-6f3g lands without it, those cells print `UNRUN … reason=needs:A0 (attest manual --review)` and W5b cannot close. - **fa-651f** (Principal objects and complete SoD rows, in progress; related link): a `session_lineage` or model-family exclusion would refuse an approver who shares the preparer's CLI session, which every `--as` label of one runner process does; re-check the cells when it lands. - **fa-z46b.** Principals here are `--as` labels from one process, so this is SoD's identity rule over labels, not cryptographic segregation of duties. If fa-z46b requires principal keys for approvals, the harness must create the director's key before step 2. - **K-JOINT.** The refused cells remove F6a from every D population on those cells; W-D-03's F6a target names an admitted cell outside this scope. - **H14** (related link added in round 4): the `manual_assertion(InternalTransfer)` cells switch to `NotInPublicRecord` when H14's registry row lands (OD 5).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: with A0 present, on every cell period law admits (Original/Open, Original/SoftClosed with `post_softclosed`, Adjusting and split-per-target Reclassification in Open, SoftClosed and Closed-with-`post_closed`), the F6a intent carrying the director's own approval vid is refused `FA-REF-008` (exit 7) as its first refusal, whatever `evidence_attached` is, citing `sod_policy.toml#adjusting-closed` / `#reclassification-closed` on the Closed cells and `sod_policy.toml#default` on the Open and SoftClosed cells. On Original-in-Closed/Locked and Adjusting/Reclassification-in-Locked cells the first refusal is `FA-REF-010` (exit 7), every Locked cell evaluated with `record_consistent = false`; on the grant-missing cells `FA-REF-011` (exit 7). Each modelled cell's reference verdict agrees (the Reclassification cells through `Oracle::reclassify`), and the structured-remedy checks pass on the period-law cells (`FA-REF-010`/`-011`), while the `FA-REF-008` cells, whose SoD refusal carries no Appendix D detail, print them `n/a`, never `ok`.
- [ ] positive: with A0 present, the `manual_assertion` cells are built by recording the assertion over the same sealed proposal (A0's `attest manual` route) and give the same first refusal as the other evidence cells of their class × state cell (SoD precedes 5b). Each cell is sealed once (`fa post --intent … --review-out`), approved (`fa approve --proposal <proposal_digest>`), planned from the retained review (`fa post --review … --digest … --approval <vid> --dry-run --plan-out`, or on a `manual_assertion` cell `fa document attest manual --review … --digest … --approval <vid> --plan-out`), and the dry run and the committed representative (`fa commit --plan`) agree on every distinct outcome; the intent JSON is never re-parsed between the seal and the plan. `f6a_entry_approval_cells` and `f6a_entry_approval_sod_rules` pass and fail on their planted copies.
- [ ] negative: `worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval_by_other` → `FAIL W-P-01 … F6a …` (no `FA-REF-008`); `worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval_no_close` → `FAIL W-P-01 … Original … Closed` (`FA-REF-011` in place of `FA-REF-010`: the period left SoftClosed); `worldcom_neg_f6a_entry_approval_reparsed` → `FAIL` (the cited approval does not bind the resealed proposal; the observed refusal recorded, never `FA-REF-008`). Each runs on a temp copy; the committed case is unchanged.
- [ ] negative: on a tree without A0 every F6a entry-approval cell prints `UNRUN W-P-01 … reason=needs:A0 (fa post --approval)`, and no library call stands in for the CLI approval; once W-P-01 is claimed, the run then exits non-zero. With A0's `--approval` but without the review form of `attest manual`, every `manual_assertion` cell prints `UNRUN … reason=needs:A0 (attest manual --review)`, never PASS, and W5b cannot close.
- [ ] negative (strict `pending` rule, plan §5.1): W-P-01 is in `case.toml` `claims` only if none of its cells carries `pending` (`PendingClaimed`); no cell is excluded from a claim, and W5b's cells are never authored `pending`.
- [ ] no-claim: this shows the kernel's first refusal for one encoding of F6a, under the p.111 reading (Si) and the listed premises. It says nothing about what WorldCom's controls did, and nothing about cryptographic SoD (fa-z46b). A0 shows that the CLI can carry an approval, nothing about any case.

title: [cases] W6: W-T-02 FY2000 total-assets bridge + W-R-01 on the WorldCom statement variant; Limits note W-NOTE-01
description:
## Why
W-T-02 is WorldCom's published-bridge tie-out (T, with its read-back W-R-01; §0.3). franken_accounting posts the restater's "previously reported" Dec-31-2000 total assets (A) and the restater's two adjustments (Δ) through a real Restatement case, and its certified fold must equal the restated value (B) exactly. All three numbers come from one restating filing, so the T reproduces that filing's bridge; it does not independently re-derive the restatement. The plan shapes it around three honesty constraints:
- **Assurance is stated, not assumed.** The audit opinion of SRC-WC-406 covers only the 2002 and 2001 balance sheets, and Item 6 excludes the 2000-12-31 summarized data, so the rendering never calls W-T-02 audited (§6.4, §2.2).
- **Vintages are named.** The restater's A (98,727) differs from the originally filed 98,903 (SRC-WC-401) by a $176M reclassification the restater footnotes; K-VINTAGE and §10.4 require both, with the bridge stating which it uses.
- **It needs its own book.** It runs on the `statement` variant, because the native calendar starts at 2001Q1 and a Historical period admits only Migration (§6.3).

The FY1999 comparison has no published Δ and no franken_accounting computation, so it is a Limits note (W-NOTE-01), never a T.

## What to build
**Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml` (the rows below) and the `[[step]]` array of `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/books/statement.toml` (W3 owns the book's accounts, intents and case row; this item adds the steps and documents its rows need). Facts read (all owned by W2; this item adds none): A = 98,727, Δ = −745 and −53,794, B = 44,188 (SRC-WC-406, `scale{multiplier}` to dollars), the as-filed 98,903 (SRC-WC-401), 91,072 (SRC-WC-EX27-1999, `scale{multiplier}` at MULTIPLIER 1,000,000), and 85,280 "(Restated)" (SRC-WC-406 selected data).

**Rows authored.**
- `[[expectation]]` **W-T-02**: `type = "T"`, `kind = "bridge"`, `book_variant = "statement"`, `basis` = the A, Δ and B facts, `published` = the B fact, `vintages = ["A:SRC-WC-406", "D:SRC-WC-406", "B:SRC-WC-406"]` (A1c's `<role>:<source id>` form), with SRC-WC-401 named as the filed A (§10.4) through W2's `W-ST-ta2000-filed` fact: it and the A fact `W-ST-ta2000-prev` carry the same `cell` key (`total_assets@2000-12-31`, A1a), so K-VINTAGE (A3b) finds the two vintages of that cell, orders them by W1's source rows (SRC-WC-406's `filed_on` later than SRC-WC-401's, and SRC-WC-406 `restates = ["SRC-WC-401"]`), and accepts the bridge because it uses the latest vintage's A (98,727, the restater's "previously reported"; the filed 98,903 differs by the footnoted $176M reclassification, `W-ST-ta2000-reclass`). A1c's roles have no slot for a named-but-unused vintage, so SRC-WC-401 is not listed in `vintages`; the rendering names both from K-VINTAGE's ordering, `assurance = "filer_not_from_audited_statements"`, `read` = the certified balance-sheet total-assets line at the 2000Q4 label, and the leaf account's certified balance for the kernel attestation. B = 44,188,000,000.00 USD at declared precision $M (scale 10^6 after the literal rule). A = 98,727,000,000.00; ΣΔ = −54,539,000,000.00.
- `[[expectation]]` **W-R-01**: `type = "R"`, `book_variant = "statement"`, `read` = `fa statement balance-sheet --for <2000Q4> --as-originally-reported --certify`, total-assets line, expected the posted A, 98,727,000,000.00.
- **Generated, never authored: `W-CASE-wc-statement-restatement`** (§3.3 step 5; A7b generates it for every restatement case, id `<letter>-CASE-<case id>` with W3's statement `[[case]] id = "wc-statement-restatement"`): `fa case show wc-statement-restatement --json` reports state Closed and the declared determination day, the restating filing's date (SRC-WC-406's `filed_on`, recorded by W1 at fetch; or the Item 4.02 8-K's date if W1 found one). Like `W-SELF-statement`, it joins `case.toml` `claims` with this item.
- The two §5.3 read-backs on this book (**as filed** and **drift**) have no id in §6.4; they are reported as fields of the W-T-02 line (`asfiled_R`, `drift_R`), not as new ids (a new id would be a plan edit).
- `[[note]]` **W-NOTE-01**: `id = "W-NOTE-01"`, `case = "worldcom"`, `basis` = [the EX-27 91,072 fact, the 85,280 "(Restated)" fact], `template` = the two-point-comparison note template. No verdict field (A1c refuses one). It renders only in Limits and is never counted.

**`books/statement.toml` steps this item adds** (one ordered `[[step]]` array; `ref` names intent, period, case or procedure ids; period refs are case labels, which the runner maps to the codes `fa period create` reports, A7a):
1. `period_open` 2000Q4; `intent` `W-ST-ta2000-prev` (A, W3's intent, citing SRC-WC-406's stub, §2.7);
2. `assert_balance` (`ref = "W-T-02"`, the as-filed read-back), as filed: A = 98,727,000,000.00 on the total-assets leaf, `--evidence` SRC-WC-406's stub, never SRC-WC-401's (whose figure is 98,903);
3. `period_soft_close`, `period_close`; `issue` 2000Q4 (§3.3 step 4: `fa statement balance-sheet --for 2000Q4 --certify`; `fa statement issue --certificate C:<oid> --for 2000Q4 --issued-to sec --document <SRC-WC-406 stub> --dry-run`; `fa approve --proposal <digest> --as <non-planner>`; `fa statement issue --plan <file> --approval <vid>`); `period_lock` (`--plan … --approval <vid>`);
4. `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_witness` (w1, by `examiner-witness`);
5. `case_open` (`fa case open --kind Restatement --periods <2000Q4> --determined-on <declared default> --authority <SRC-WC-406 stub>`; no WorldCom non-reliance 8-K row exists unless W1 found one, §6.3); `scenario_fork`, `scenario_run` (W3's Δ intents `delta-W-ST-ta2000-prev-1` (`fact = "W-ST-ta2000-adj1"`, −745,000,000.00) and `delta-W-ST-ta2000-prev-2` (`fact = "W-ST-ta2000-adj2"`, −53,794,000,000.00) on the leaf, each `class = "Restatement"`, `target = "W-ST-ta2000-prev"`, `target_kind = "restates"`, `reason` = W3's declared default; their remainder legs take only the A or Δ fact as input, never `W-ST-ta2000-restated`), `scenario_diff` (`--certificate-out`);
6. `case_rehearse`, `case_approve` (`--dry-run`; two `fa approve --proposal <digest>` by the two `case-approver-*` labels with no shared session lineage, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:3450`; `fa case approve <case> --approval <vid> --approval <vid>`), `case_post` (by a non-approver), `case_disclose` (D = the `Disclosure`-kind SRC-WC-406 stub reviewed by `case-second-reader`; its unreviewed twin first), `case_close`;
7. `assert_balance` (`ref = "W-T-02"`, the kernel-attested B) B = 44,188,000,000.00 (and its B ± 0.01 twins), `finding_record` `ref = "recon.assertion_drift@1"` (`known_at = head`);
8. `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_witness` (w2 `--previous w1`, and the `--previous` twin).

Restatement is admitted only in Closed or Locked (`with:restate,2`; the Restatement cells are `registries/admissibility.toml:380-401`, Closed and Locked at `:392-401`, checked at 8196f5e40); each Δ `restates` the A posting (`post.rs:2503-2512`).

**Kernel-attested bridge (§5.3).** A and Δ sit on one leaf account in one period, so B is also recorded with `fa assert-balance --account <TA leaf> --period <2000Q4> --balance "44188000000.00 USD" --evidence <SRC-WC-406 stub>` (`registries/verbs.toml:487-497`; needs `reconcile`). The kernel records a RegisterEquals attestation only if B equals the fold, and refuses any other amount with `FA-REF-140` (exit 3). The T requires the attestation recorded and its twin (B ± 1 minor unit) refused. The two read-backs:
- **as filed**: before the case, A is asserted (step 2);
- **drift**: after the case, `recon.assertion_drift`@1 (`claim = "invariant"`, `registries/procedures.toml:1401-1409`, the whole row, checked at 8196f5e40) reports exactly the A assertion, citing the case's two Restatement entries (one finding citing the Attestation, the leaf account, 2000Q4 and every entry recorded after the attestation that moves the cell, `crates/fa-lantern/src/assertion_drift.rs:123-126`, `:150`), with drift = ΣΔ = −54,539,000,000.00. Its projected statistic is `assertion_drift` = 54,539,000,000.00: the procedure reports the drift's magnitude (`:118-122`, `:160-163`) and prints the sign only in the finding's text, which the projection excludes (§5.4). B's own attestation (step 7) still equals the fold, so it yields no finding (`:115-117`).

**After the post** (§3.3 step 5): `fa case diff <case> --statements --certify` (lines carry `before`, `after`, `delta`; `after` is the T and `before` an R); `fa explain lineage <A>` names the Restates edge; `fa case show` reports Closed and the determination day (the generated row `W-CASE-wc-statement-restatement`).

**Witnesses** (§3.7, §12.1, §12.7), executed in the run:
- **Contributing-entry witness (A11b).** `fa explain balance <account> --period <2000Q4> --certify --json` at the T's coordinate: the `balance_explained` contributions (`registries/verbs.toml:2443-2446`) are exactly A and the two Δs; none carries 44,188,000,000.00, directly or through a derivation; they re-add to the certified value. For the type-level assets line it runs over each account the line selects. `fa statement trace --certify --from-diff C:<case statement-diff>` (`registries/verbs.toml:543`, event `:2053-2056`) also runs, and `fa_reference::statements::render` recomputes the line from the explained balances. §3.7 requires W6 to run both the trace and the explained-balance witness, and they must agree. Any failure or disagreement re-types the T as R.

A and B are also read with `fa query --certify` under the FA GQL profile (stock with `EFFECTIVE BETWEEN '<opening>' AND '<end>' AS KNOWN AT <seq>`; W-R-01 with `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED`), netted by the harness, equal to the fold-path value (an R-class cross-check, never independent evidence).
