title: [cases] W7: WorldCom native restatement — W-T-03 ($818M 2002Q1 IS diff), W-R-02..04, W-D-07/W-D-08, D pinning at pre_case
description:
## Why
This item runs the correction of the documented capitalization entries as a real Restatement case on the `native` book, and publishes what the system then shows. W-T-03 is the program's entry-level income-statement tie-out. The certified 2002Q1 statement diff of the case moves expenses by exactly the committee's "$818 million adjustment" (p.116), computed from F12 and F13, the two entries the same sentence names. The diff isolates the correction's own effect, so filler cancels (§6.4).

W-R-02..04 are read-backs of the selector and attestation paths (R). W-R-04 includes the "but-for" view an expert witness uses (`damages.attested_baseline`).

W-D-07 and W-D-08 publish franken_accounting's own false positives on a real-shaped book. After the correction, the findings persist on the corrected entries, and `jet.round_amounts` fires on the correction's own entries, because the journal is append-only and Lantern populations keep Restatement entries (doctrine 5; §6.4). An examiner should see that, and it is the evidence behind H17.

D pinning is part of this item. Every other D on `native` must be evaluated at the frontier before the case's Post, or the case's own entries enter their populations (§6.3). Claim types: T, R, D (two rows `about = "reconstruction"` or post-correction), and the Limits note W-NOTE-02 for `jet.post_closing` (all X; a note, never an expectation, §5.1, §6.4).

## What to build
**Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml` (the rows below) and `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/books/native.toml`. W3 authors the native `[[case]]`, its Δ intents and the issue / lock / case steps; this item adds the `assert_balance` steps at each issuance (`ref = "W-R-04"`, A1b's expectation-id ref), the `finding_record` steps for W-D-07/W-D-08 (`ref = "expense.capitalization@2"` and `"jet.round_amounts@1"`, `known_at = head`), `recon.assertion_drift@1` and `damages.attested_baseline@1`, and the checkpoint-witness steps, and adds any of W3's case steps that are missing when it lands. It adds its rows (and the generated `W-CASE-wc-restatement`) to `case.toml` `claims`.

**The native Restatement case** (W3's `[[case]]`; default branch cell only; §6.3):
- One case of kind Restatement negates F1, F4, F9, F10, F12 and F13: Δ intents `delta-F1`, `delta-F4`, `delta-F9`, `delta-F10`, `delta-F12`, `delta-F13`, each `fact = "derived:negate"` (non-interpretive: the exact additive inverse of the entry's legs, same accounts and units), `target = "F<n>"`, `target_kind = "restates"` (`crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2503-2512`), `reason = "WrongAccount"` (`registries/reason_codes.toml:63-66`), a declared default, never `Fraud` (K-REASON), and `scenario` = the case's scenario.
- It runs after each quarter is issued at its sourced filing date (2001-05-15, 2001-08-14, 2001-11-14, 2002-03-31, 2002-05-15; SRC-WC-002 ¶¶48–50, SRC-WC-001 p.301) and locked.
- **Steps** (`[[step]]`, in order; period refs are case labels mapped to CLI codes by the runner, A7a):
  1. per quarter: `issue` (§3.3 step 4), then `assert_balance` on every line-cost account (`fa assert-balance --account <code> --period <q> --balance "<fold> USD" --evidence <that quarter's filing stub>`), then `period_lock`;
  2. `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_witness` (w1 by `examiner-witness`);
  3. `case_open` (`fa case open --kind Restatement --periods <2001Q1>,…,<2002Q1> --determined-on <declared default> --authority <restating filing stub>`), `scenario_fork`, `scenario_run` (the six Δ intents), `scenario_diff` (`--period <each> --certificate-out <file>`);
  4. `case_rehearse` (`--certificate <scenario-diff-certificate>`), `case_approve` (`--dry-run`; two `fa approve --proposal <digest>` by two `case-approver-*` roles with no shared session lineage, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:3450`; `fa case approve <case> --approval <vid> --approval <vid>`), `case_post` (by a non-approver);
  5. `case_disclose` (the unreviewed `Disclosure` twin first, refused `FA-REF-179`; then the reviewed one), `case_close`;
  6. `finding_record` for `expense.capitalization@2` and `jet.round_amounts@1` at `known_at = head` (W-D-07, W-D-08), `finding_record recon.assertion_drift@1`, `finding_record damages.attested_baseline@1`;
  7. `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_witness` (w2 `--previous w1`, and the `--previous` twin).
- After the post: `fa case diff <case> --statements --certify` (one statement-diff certificate per affected period and definition; lines carry `before`, `after`, `delta`), and `fa explain lineage <F12>` (and each target) naming the Restates edge. `fa case show` reports Closed and the determination day (§6.5 lists disclose and close for the native book): that read-back is the generated row `W-CASE-wc-restatement` below.

**Rows authored** (`[[expectation]]`; values copied from §6.4):
- **W-T-03**: `type = "T"`, `kind = "footing"`, `book_variant = "native"`, `basis` = F12, F13 and the p.116 "$818 million" fact, `published` = the $818M fact (818,000,000.00 at declared precision $1M), `read` = the 2002Q1 income-statement certificate of `fa case diff --statements --certify`, expense line `delta`, `inputs_named` = [`delta-F12`, `delta-F13`], `vintages = ["exhibit:SRC-WC-001"]` (A1c's footing role; the committee report is EDGAR exhibit `dex991.htm`), assertion status "the committee found", assurance none. Expected: the expense line's `delta` = 818,000,000.00 in magnitude, an increase in expenses (each Δ debits the line-cost account its target credited); the sign convention is the certificate's. 818 is never posted (K-TAUT). Rendering: "reproduces the committee's own total of the two entries it names", never "independently".
- **W-R-02**: `type = "R"`, one `[[target]]` per other quarter (`fact` = the restated entry, `posted` = its Δ intent), `read` = that quarter's income-statement diff, expected = the posted Δ on the expense lines: 2001Q1 771,000,000.00 (`delta-F1`), 2001Q2 560,000,000.00 (`delta-F4`), 2001Q3 742,725,000.00 (`delta-F9`), 2001Q4 941,000,000.00 (`delta-F10`) (read-backs, unless W2 sources a separate quarterly total).
- **W-R-03**: `type = "R"`, `read` = `fa statement income-statement --for <2002Q1> --as-originally-reported --certify`; expected = the pre-case frontier's certified value, recorded in the same run from the pre-case income-statement certificate (filler-dependent, so never authored as a literal). The selector is exercised, because Δ ≠ 0.
- **W-R-04**: `type = "R"`, one `[[target]]` per (line-cost account, quarter) cell asserted at issuance that a Δ moves; expected statistic `assertion_drift` = |ΣΔ| on that cell, the magnitude of fold − attested that `recon.assertion_drift` reports (`crates/fa-lantern/src/assertion_drift.rs:118-122`, `:160-163`; the sign appears only in the finding's text, which the projection excludes, §5.4), with ΣΔ computed at load from the Δ intents' signed legs on the cell (filler-independent). Every Δ here is the negation of a credit to a line-cost account (W2, §6.2: "line costs → …"), so it debits that account, ΣΔ > 0 and |ΣΔ| = ΣΔ; `w_r_04_expected_drift` derives the magnitude and never assumes the sign. An asserted cell that no Δ moves still folds to its attestation and yields no finding (`:115-117`), so it is not a target. The 2002Q1 line-costs-a cell is one attestation moved by both `delta-F12` and `delta-F13`: one target (proposal `fact = "F12"`, `basis = ["F12", "F13"]`) whose one finding cites both, drift 818,000,000.00. `recon.assertion_drift`@1 (`claim = "invariant"`, `registries/procedures.toml:1401-1409`, checked at 8196f5e40) must report exactly those assertions, citing the case's Restatement entries. `damages.attested_baseline`@1 (`claim = "statistical"`, calibration `planted`, `registries/procedures.toml:1702-1711`) is run and its per-account, per-period delta logged beside the drift, but only the drift is asserted (§6.4).

The rendering names the Restates edge from `fa explain lineage`, and says "the finding persists because the corrected entry stays in the journal (append-only, doctrine 5)".
- **W-D-08**: `type = "D"`, `procedure = "jet.round_amounts"`, `version = 1`, `known_at = "head"`, `about = "reconstruction"`; targets = W-D-03's targets plus each `delta-F<n>` on its target's default branch cell only (the case runs on the default cell, §6.3, and W3's Δs negate the default cell's legs), whose components are W-D-03's components for its target on that cell with the cited legs projected to (`delta-F<n>`, ordinal): each Δ is the exact `negate` of its target's legs, so its legs fall in the same residue classes. `live_postings` keeps every class except Reversal (`snapshot.rs:505-512`), and the procedure does not filter by class (`crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:102`).

**D pinning on `native`.** Every D row on `native` except W-D-07/W-D-08 (which declare `known_at = "head"`) is evaluated at `known_at = pre_case` (A1c's default for a D on `native`), the frontier before the case's Post, via `fa finding record <id> --known-at <seq>`. **JSONL records** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord`, `record = "step"`, with `binds` mapping `$F12`, `$delta-F12`, … to their `posted` vids and A7b's `$C_IS_<quarter>`, `$C_ISSUE_<quarter>`, `$C_SDIFF_wc-restatement_<quarter>` and `$C_SCEN_<scenario>` to their certificates): `verb = "statement"` (`issue --dry-run`, `issue --plan`, `income-statement --certify`, `--as-originally-reported`, `trace`), `verb = "assert-balance"` per asserted cell, `verb = "period"` (lock), `verb = "case"` (open, rehearse, approve, post, diff with the statement-diff `certificate_kind`, disclose with the twin's `refusal_id = "FA-REF-179"`, close, show for `W-CASE-wc-restatement`), `verb = "scenario"`, `verb = "approve"`, `verb = "finding"` (`record` with `known_at` and `finding_procedure` ∈ {`expense.capitalization`, `jet.round_amounts`, `recon.assertion_drift`, `damages.attested_baseline`}), `verb = "explain"` (lineage, balance), `verb = "checkpoint"` (the twin with `refusal_id = "FA-REF-124"`, exit 8), `verb = "proof"`, `"certificate"`, `"replay"`, `"query"`, `"verify"`. On failure `REPRODUCE fa --book <dir> <argv>` is printed, and `LOG <path>` at the end. No `#[ignore]`; the rows join `case.toml` `claims`, so an UNRUN on any of them fails the `worldcom` test. ## Notes

title: [cases] W8: W-D-06 cutoff.period_boundary on F10's dated draft JE (2002-01-23); F1, F9, F12 as B(document_date)
description:
## Why
`cutoff.period_boundary` reports an entry whose document's period differs from the entry's period. WorldCom's record dates exactly one instruction document: the draft journal entry for F10, prepared 2002-01-23 (p.114), for an entry whose sourced reporting period is 4Q01 (§6.2). That makes W-D-06 the case's one D on a dated document: a cut-off finding resting on a sourced date rather than on our encoding.

Round 4 narrowed it to F10 alone (Appendix Z.7):
- F9's e-mail is undated;
- F12's Post-it was handed on by the preparer, and reading it as F12's document is an `interpretation` (§5.5, §6.2), which gives no date;
- F1's one-page document is undated.

So those three are branch rows over `document_date`. The row also carries the plan's caveat. A legitimately documented post-closing adjustment satisfies the same predicate, and the procedure's claim class is statistical with `corpus` calibration, so the sentence says so (§6.4). Claim type: D. The coverage review added it to exercise the cutoff family on WorldCom, not only on Enron (Appendix Z.5.1).

## What to build
**Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml` (the rows below). It reads W2's facts `F10-doc` (sourced, p.114, its `[[value]]` 2002-01-23 under `date_literal`), the undated `F1-doc` (p.106) and `F9-doc` (p.113), and the Post-it `interpretation` `F12F13-doc` (two readers; no date), and W3's `books/native.toml` (F10's intent carries `document_date = "2002-01-23"`; F1, F9 and F12 carry W3's `bc-<F1|F9|F12>-document_date` class). It adds one `finding_record` step (`ref = "cutoff.period_boundary@1"`) at `known_at = pre_case`, and the `finding_review` / `engagement_file` steps for the F10 finding (`engagement_file` `ref = "finding:W-D-06"`, W3's spelling). The `finding_record` and `engagement_file` steps name their `principal` (A1b refuses either without one, `MissingField`): a label holding `read` and `produce` (`registries/verbs.toml:881`: "Recording and exporting require read and produce"; `:736`: `engagement file` journals "under produce"), never `case-second-reader`, whose review must come from a Human "independent of the run producer" (`:881`); `finding_review` defaults to `case-second-reader` (A1b). W-D-06 joins `case.toml` `claims`.

**Rows authored.** `[[expectation]]` **W-D-06**: `type = "D"`, `book_variant = "native"`, `statement_template = "D.detection"`, `procedure = "cutoff.period_boundary"`, `version = 1` (`registries/procedures.toml:243-251`: `claim = "statistical"`, `calibration = "corpus"`), `known_at = "pre_case"`, `granularity = "journal_entry"`, `basis` = `F10`, `F10-doc` (and per target its entry and document facts). Each `[[target]]` carries A1c's component fields (`cite`/`cite_status`, `severity`/`severity_status`, `statistic_name`/`statistic_value`/`statistic_scale`/`statistic_status`), `branch_attrs` and `admitted_cell`. Targets, copied from §6.4:

| target | cite | severity | statistic.value |
|---|---|---|---|
| F10 (draft JE dated 2002-01-23, p.114) | Sd: the document's period (1Q02) ≠ the sourced reporting period (4Q01). The effective day is not read for the cite (`cutoff.rs:52-67`) | S (constant Medium, `cutoff.rs:83`) | B(effective_date), default cell marked: `days_between_dates` reads the effective day (`cutoff.rs:68`) |
| F1, F9, F12 | B(document_date): F9's e-mail is undated; F12's Post-it was *handed on* by the preparer (p.116), an interpretation; F1's document is undated | B | B |

- **F10's encoding.** `document_date = 2002-01-23`, the sourced fact anchored at W2. The effective date is the declared default (2001-12-31, the reporting period's last day) or an `effective_date` cell inside 4Q01.
- **Cite components at 8196f5e40** (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:75-80`): `Cite::Entry`, `Cite::Period(effective period)`, and `Cite::Period(document period)` when the calendar has generated that period. The native calendar includes 2002Q1. The cited period codes project back to the case labels (`2001Q4`, `2002Q1`) through the runner's label map (A7a).
- **Statistic.** `Statistic::count("days_between_dates", |document_date − effective_date|, population)` (`cutoff.rs:68`, `:84`). Over 4Q01 (2001-10-01 … 2001-12-31) the value runs from 114 (effective 2001-10-01) to 23 (the default cell, effective 2001-12-31); both endpoints are computed here, not plan figures. `[[branch_cell]]` rows follow A5a's `effective_date` class rule for this reader; the expected value of each cell is `2002-01-23 − effective_date` in days, never one claimed value, and the default cell (23) is marked `default = true`.
- **F1, F9, F12 `[[branch_cell]]` rows** (W3's `document_date` class, §6.3), each on the default effective date (the reporting period's last day): `document_date=absent` → not evaluated (`cutoff.rs:54-56`: the field is optional, and no commit law requires it), no finding; `document_date=inside_reporting_period` → no finding; `document_date=after_reporting_period` (a day in the next quarter) → finding, cite `[F<n>, period:<reporting>, period:<next>]`, severity Medium, `days_between_dates` = the cell's day count. `record_consistent = false` on every F1, F9 and F12 cell: no sourced or derived fact dates their documents. For F12 the only basis is the Post-it `interpretation` (W2), which supports the document's existence but no date; the interpretation is named in the rendering. On F10 the sourced-date cell is `record_consistent = true`.
- **Admitted cell (K-JOINT).** Each target names its admitted evidence cell: `entry_class=Original,period_state_at_commit=Open,evidence_attached=manual_assertion(InternalTransfer)`, which for F10 is also the record-consistent W-P-02 cell.
- **K-ERRRATE** (§5.6): claim `statistical`, calibration `corpus` → "measured on fa-gen's labelled synthetic corpora, where precision is 100% by the generator's construction (`lantern_calibration.toml:22-33`); its false-positive rate on real books has not been estimated", followed by the caveat sentence: a legitimately documented post-closing adjustment satisfies the same predicate.
- **Tier C context.** Every context fact the procedure reads (the calendar, period codes, the document date) is sourced, declared-derived or a listed branch attribute (§2.5). The filler discipline fixes context facts by the case, never by filler.
- **Finding → source review** (§2.7). The F10 finding (an Sd cite) gets one `case-second-reader` review, `fa finding review F:<vid> --action acknowledge --note <template> --evidence D:<F10 fact stub>`, and is filed with `fa engagement file <id> --finding <vid>`.

## Tests & logging
**Run.** `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact worldcom`; negatives `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- worldcom_neg_w8_` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_worldcom -- w8_ w_d_06`.

**Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the in-field serialization; the values below are what each field must contain):
```text
PASS W-D-06 D native F10/effective_date=2001-12-31 cutoff.period_boundary@1 cite=Sd:[F10,period:2001Q4,period:2002Q1] severity=S:Medium statistic=B:days_between_dates=23 default review=acknowledge:F10-stub
PASS W-D-06 D native F10/effective_date=<cell> … statistic=B:days_between_dates=<2002-01-23 − cell day>      (one line per A5a cell; 114 on 2001-10-01)
PASS W-D-06 D native F1/document_date=absent … no finding
PASS W-D-06 D native F1/document_date=inside_reporting_period … no finding
PASS W-D-06 D native F1/document_date=after_reporting_period … cite=B:[F1,period:2001Q1,period:2001Q2] severity=B:Medium statistic=B:days_between_dates=<n>    (and F9: 2001Q3/2001Q4; F12: 2002Q1/2002Q2)
```
A row whose witness is missing prints `UNRUN W-D-06 D native <target>/<cell> reason=<witness>`, never PASS. Field order is §16's and A7a owns the serialization; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `<target>/<cell>`.

**Witnesses.**
- Filler and identifier invariance (A11a): 5 seeded + empty + extremal (tier C) variants and ≥ 2 runs; the F10 cite and severity must agree on all of them.
- Branch classes (A5a property tests): 64 seeded witnesses per `document_date` and `effective_date` class through the real binary on micro-books give the class's verdict.
- Reference differential: where A4r is present (it is not an edge of W8), the cite set is compared with `fa_reference::lantern::cutoff`; a `disagree` is FAIL. The D outsider replay (`fa finding export` → `fa finding replay`, §12.1) runs where A12 is present.

**Planted negatives** (permanent; the committed case is never edited):
- `worldcom_neg_w8_f10_date_inside` (run-time): F10's `document_date` set to 2001-12-28 (inside 4Q01). Observable: `FAIL W-D-06 D native F10/effective_date=2001-12-31 … cite` (no finding).
- `worldcom_neg_w8_f10_date_removed` (run-time): F10's `document_date` removed. Observable: `FAIL W-D-06 D native F10/… cite` (the entry is outside the population, no finding).
- `w8_f12_date_sourced_from_postit_refused` (load-time, `case_worldcom.rs`): a copy adding a date `[[value]]` to the sourced p.116 sentence fact behind `F12F13-doc`, so F12's `document_date` would read as sourced. Observable: K-BIND FAIL naming that fact and its line, offline: the fact's committed values no longer hash to its receipt's `values_sha256` (§4.4; the date was never in the verified quote); a copy that sets F12's `document_date` to a single declared value with no sourced basis is refused by K-BRANCH instead (an unanchored attribute that is neither sourced nor a branch class).
- `w8_f12_postit_typed_derived_refused` (load-time): a copy typing the F12 Post-it reading `derived` (no registered rule produces it). Observable: refusal naming K-PROV / K-DERIVE and the fact.

**Unit tests the item adds** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`, pure):
- `w_d_06_days_between`: fa-oracles' own day arithmetic over `date_literal` values: 2002-01-23 − 2001-12-31 = 23; 2002-01-23 − 2001-10-01 = 114 (the 4Q01 boundary day); a planted expected 22 for the default cell fails.
- `w_d_06_period_of_date`: period resolution against the case's custom calendar labels: 2001-12-31 → 2001Q4, 2002-01-01 → 2002Q1 (the boundary), 2002-01-23 → 2002Q1; a planted calendar that ends 2001Q4 on 2002-01-31 makes the F10 cite cell fail.

**JSONL records** (§3.5): `verb = "finding"` (`record` with `finding_procedure = "cutoff.period_boundary"` and the pre-case `known_at` seq, `certificate_kind` of the run certificate; `list`; `review` for F10; `export`/`replay` where A12 is present), `verb = "engagement"` (`file --finding`); each record carries `branch_class` (the cell) and `filler_variant`. On failure `REPRODUCE fa --book <dir> <argv>` is printed, and `LOG <path>` at the end. No `#[ignore]`; any UNRUN or FAIL on the claimed W-D-06 rows exits non-zero (A7a `claims`).

## Notes
- **Edges.**
  - ← W2: F10's 2002-01-23 date anchored as a sourced fact, the undated F1/F9 documents, and F12's Post-it `interpretation` (two readers).
  - ← W3: the native book and the `document_date` / `effective_date` classes.
  - ← A4: the two-reader tier row for `cutoff.period_boundary` (C) and K-TIER.
  - ← A5b: the status model, K-BRANCH, K-PRED and K-JOINT.
  - ← A11a: the invariance witness.
- **Risk.** B(effective_date) for the statistic is not a two-class split: `days_between_dates` takes a distinct value for each effective day in 4Q01 (92 days, 23…114). The class rule must render the statistic as a function of the effective day within A5a's 256-cell cap, or as the default cell plus that function. It must never claim a single value.
- E-D-01 (Enron) uses the same procedure with three `document_date` cells (§7.2); keep the two rows' rule ids aligned.
- **Names.** §3.2b fixes the case directory `worldcom` (`letter = "W"`) and the test names (`worldcom`, `worldcom_neg_<slug>`); A7a names the case test after the directory (`fn worldcom()`), settled at r4a (at r2b it was `case_w`).
- **Filing the finding.** Requires A1b to accept an `engagement_file` step that files a row's reviewed finding (`fa engagement file <id> --finding <vid>`, `registries/verbs.toml:736`): A1b's step-ref grammar names only a `[[document]]` id for `engagement_file`, so this step's `ref` is `finding:W-D-06` (W3's spelling, which W4 also uses). W3's `[[principal]]` rows (r4a) give no label `produce`; requires W3 to declare one, distinct from `case-second-reader`, for the `finding_record` and `engagement_file` steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `PASS W-D-06 D native F10/…`: `cutoff.period_boundary`@1 cites F10 (with periods `2001Q4` and `2002Q1`) at severity Medium, Sd, on all filler variants and ≥ 2 runs. Its `days_between_dates` statistic matches the B(effective_date) cells (23 on the default 2001-12-31 cell, marked; 114 on 2001-10-01), and the K-ERRRATE clause and the legitimate-adjustment caveat render with it. The F10 finding carries exactly one `case-second-reader` acknowledge review citing its stub.
- [ ] positive: F1, F9 and F12 PASS as B(document_date) tables: absent → no finding; inside the reporting period → no finding; after it → finding. Every F1/F9/F12 cell is `record_consistent = false`; F10's sourced-date cell is `record_consistent = true`. `w_d_06_days_between` and `w_d_06_period_of_date` pass and fail on their planted values.
- [ ] negative: `worldcom_neg_w8_f10_date_inside` and `worldcom_neg_w8_f10_date_removed` each print `FAIL W-D-06 … F10 … cite` on a temp copy. `w8_f12_date_sourced_from_postit_refused` (K-BIND offline through the receipt's `values_sha256`, or K-BRANCH for an unanchored single value) and `w8_f12_postit_typed_derived_refused` (K-PROV/K-DERIVE) are refused at load, naming the fact and line.
- [ ] negative: a row whose witness is missing prints `UNRUN W-D-06 … reason=<witness>`, never PASS, and, W-D-06 being claimed, the test exits non-zero.
- [ ] no-claim: the predicate holds on our encoding of F10 with its sourced draft-JE date. A legitimately documented post-closing adjustment satisfies the same predicate, and the procedure's false-positive rate on real books has not been estimated. Nothing here speaks to intent, or to what a cut-off review would have concluded; a finding is not an accusation.

title: [cases] W9: W-T-04 — F6b through fa allocate under EqualSplitResidualFirst, ten legs of exactly 54,400,000.00, residual 0
description:
## Why
The committee reports that the $544M left CIP and went into "10 assets in the amount of exactly $54.4 million each in Property Accounting's sub-ledger under the Fiber Optic Cable account" (p.111). W-T-04 makes that sentence an `allocation` tie-out (T; §5.3). `fa allocate` under a registered allocation law, applied to the posted 544,000,000.00 and ten declared targets, must compute ten legs of exactly 54,400,000.00 with residual 0. The sourced "$54.4 million" is never posted: the law computes the parts from the sourced total.

Round 3's coverage review, which targeted under-delivery against the owner's "ALL the deep functionality", added it (Appendix Z.5: "the F6 allocation through a registered law (W-T-04)"). It also exercises the `Allocation` class whose period-law cells W5 tabulates (`admissibility.toml:270-289`). The T exists only on the `one_allocation_entry` cell of F6b's `entry_decomposition` branch. On `ten_two_leg_entries`, F6b is ten Original or Adjusting entries and there is no allocation to tie out (§6.2, §6.3).

## What to build
**Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/expectations.toml` (the row below) and, in `crates/fa-oracles/cases/worldcom/books/native.toml`, F6b's `allocation` field and its `[[step]] kind = "allocate"` (W3 authors F6a, F6b and the ten leaf accounts; this item fixes the allocation fields the T reads, if W3 has not).

**Encoding** (W3's intents, §3.2a `[[intent]] allocation` = law, total, targets, flattened by A1b as `allocation_law`, `allocation_total`, `allocation_targets`):
- F6a posts CIP → asset clearing, 544,000,000.00 (2001-08-22, 2001Q3).
- F6b, `class = "Allocation"` (`crates/fa-journal/src/allocation.rs:263`): `allocation_law = "EqualSplitResidualFirst"`, `allocation_total = "544000000.00"` (USD, the book's base unit), `allocation_targets` = the ten declared leaf accounts under Fiber Optic Cable, in input order, plus the explicit form's two source fields (proposed names `allocation_source` = the clearing account's code and `allocation_source_side = "credit"`, the side posted to the clearing account, which F6a debited). This is the explicit form of the `fa allocate` usage (`registries/verbs.toml:459`: "either `total` + `source_side` … or `source_period` … to fold `source_account`'s net period balance"). The explicit total is used because `source_period` would fold every posting to the clearing account in 2001Q3, and §6.2 does not say whether F7's "$0.2 million that remained, likewise" passed through it.
- **Rendered intent JSON** (A7a's `intent_json.rs`; keys checked at 8196f5e40 in `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs`): `source` (the clearing code, `:10142`), `effective_date` (`:10144`), `idempotency_key` (`:10158`), `method` = `"EqualSplitResidualFirst"` (`:9773-9786`; the parser also reads `law`), `total` = `"544000000.00 USD"` and `source_side` = `"credit"` (`:10295-10320`), and `targets` = `[{"account": <leaf>}, …]` with no `basis` (an equal split defaults each basis to 1, `:9883`). The law is always named: with no `method`/`law` key the CLI defaults to `largest_remainder` (`:9778`), and 544,000,000.00 over ten targets splits exactly under that law too, so the T alone could not notice the default. `source_period` is never rendered beside `total` (the CLI refuses both together with a usage error, `:10176-10182`).
- `[[step]] kind = "allocate"`, `ref = "F6b"`: `fa allocate --intent <F6b.json> --as property-accounting-director-1`, with the effective date in the intent; no `--period`, which the usage reads as the fold form. Evidence: the canonical driver Workpaper that `fa allocate` content-addresses and auto-imports (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:9730-9751`; `evidence_policy.toml:221-224`), not the `evidence_attached` branch.
- Posted on the default cell: Open 2001Q3, `entry_decomposition = one_allocation_entry`, `approval_encoding = none`.
- The ten leaves are touched by nothing but F6b: F8's "Fiber Optic Cable 160M" debit posts to a Fiber Optic Cable account that is none of the ten leaves (W3's chart), and A6 keeps filler off any account a target names.

**Rows authored.** `[[expectation]]` **W-T-04**: `type = "T"`, `kind = "allocation"`, `book_variant = "native"`, `branch_scope = entry_decomposition=one_allocation_entry`, `law` = `EqualSplitResidualFirst` (`registries/allocation_laws.toml:35-42`, the whole `[[law]]` row, checked at 8196f5e40: id 5, version 1, `basis = "one-per-target"`, `ordering = "input-order; entire-residual-to-first"`, `rounding = "truncate-magnitude"`, `signed = "magnitude-then-restore-sign"`; the plan's `:36-38` is the row's id…name lines), `basis` = the p.111 facts, `published` = the "$54.4 million each" fact (scale 10^6, declared precision $0.1M) and the ten-count fact (`number_word`), `vintages` = SRC-WC-001, assurance none (an investigative finding). Expected: ten legs of exactly 54,400,000.00 and residual 0.00, the sourced remainder.
- `read` (this round's choice; the plan names no read verb for W-T-04): the ten leaves' rows of `fa tb --period <2001Q3> --certify` (a TB certificate, so §12.1's outsider check applies), with `fa explain balance <leaf> --period <2001Q3> --certify --json` per leaf for the contributing-entry witness.
- The legs are computed by the law and posted (F6b); the intent holds only the total and the targets, never 54,400,000.00.

**Pass** (§5.3, §3.7): each of the ten legs equals 54,400,000.00 by exact integer equality at the unit's scale, and the residual is 0. The contributing-entry witness holds: each leaf's contributions are exactly F6b's leg; no contributing posting carries B through the authored intent; the contributions re-add to the certified value. The outsider check: `fa checkpoint create --grant witness` → `fa bundle produce --certificate <tb cert>` → `fa-verify bundle` and `fa-verify report` as literal argv through `fa_verify::cli::run` (`crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700`; the recomputed rows equal 54,400,000.00) → `fa replay` byte-identical (§12.1).

**Reference.** `fa_reference::statements::render` (`crates/fa-reference/src/statements.rs:148`) recomputes the folds where A4r is present. Allocation intents are `not_modelled` for P (§15 A4r); for this T only the fold comparison applies.

## Tests & logging
**Run.** `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact worldcom`; negatives `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- worldcom_neg_w9_`; unit test `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_worldcom -- w_t_04`.

**Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `<target>/<cell>`, and an UNRUN or FAIL reason in its trailing `reason=` field; the values below are what each field must contain):
```text
PASS W-T-04 T native -/entry_decomposition=one_allocation_entry kind=allocation law=EqualSplitResidualFirst@1(id 5) read=tb(2001Q3,certify)[leaf-1..leaf-10] value=10×54400000.00,residual=0.00 published=54400000.00×10 contrib=holds(each leaf: F6b leg only) outsider=report:verified(rows=54400000.00,replay=identical) ref=agree
```
On the `ten_two_leg_entries` cell the runner prints no W-T-04 line: the T is out of scope there. A missing contributing-entry or outsider witness prints `UNRUN W-T-04 … reason=<witness>` (`contributing_entry` or `outsider`, A7a's witness names), never PASS. The `law=` component is the law the runner rendered into F6b's `method`, checked against `allocation_law`; the posted entry's allocation basis binds the law id and version (`law_digest`, `crates/fa-journal/src/allocation.rs:124-132`), so a robot field that exposes it is compared too, and where none does the runner says so in the line rather than inferring it.

**Planted negatives** (permanent; the committed case is never edited):
- `worldcom_neg_w9_parts_posted` (run-time): the copy replaces F6b with an intent that carries 54,400,000.00 on each of the ten leaves (B posted). Observable: W-T-04 is re-typed R (K-TAUT names the "$54.4 million" fact as posted; the contributing-entry witness agrees). W-T-04 is claimed, so under A7a's completeness rule the line is `FAIL W-T-04 R native -/entry_decomposition=one_allocation_entry … reason=retyped T→R K-TAUT` and the case fails: the test calls `.expect_err` and asserts that line, never `PASS W-T-04 T`.
- `worldcom_neg_w9_eleventh_target` (run-time): an eleventh leaf target. Observable: `FAIL W-T-04 T native … reason=expected 10×54400000.00 observed …` (the `value` component) with the observed legs 49,454,545.45 on ten targets and 49,454,545.50 on the first (residual 0.05 to the first under `entire-residual-to-first` with `truncate-magnitude`). These exact legs also pin the law: a largest-remainder split (the CLI's default when `method` is absent) would give five targets one extra minor unit each, never one target the whole 0.05.
- `worldcom_neg_w9_total_plus_one` (run-time): `total = 544000000.01`. Observable: `FAIL W-T-04 T native … reason=expected residual=0.00 observed residual=0.01` with the first leg 54,400,000.01 and residual 0.01 ≠ 0.

**Unit tests the item adds** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_worldcom.rs`, pure):
- `w_t_04_f6b_intent_json_names_the_law_and_the_explicit_total`: the rendered F6b JSON carries `"method": "EqualSplitResidualFirst"`, `"total": "544000000.00 USD"`, `"source_side": "credit"`, the clearing code as `source` and the ten leaf codes in input order, and no `source_period`; a planted copy without `allocation_law` is refused at render (`allocation_law missing: the CLI would default to largest_remainder`), never rendered without a `method`.
- `w_t_04_equal_split_residual_first` recomputes `EqualSplitResidualFirst` in fa-oracles' own checked i128 arithmetic at scale 2: 54,400,000,000 minor units over 10 targets → 5,440,000,000 each, residual 0; 54,400,000,001 over 10 → first 5,440,000,001, the rest 5,440,000,000; 54,400,000,000 over 11 → 4,945,454,545 each and the first 4,945,454,550 (residual 5 to the first). A planted copy that sends the residual to the last target fails. The runner compares the posted legs with this independent recomputation as well as with the published value.

**JSONL records** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord`, `record = "step"`): `verb = "allocate"` (events `posted`/`recorded`; `argv_redacted` with the intent path; the driver workpaper's digest; `binds` maps `$F6b` to the `posted` event's vid), `verb = "tb"` (with the TB `certificate_kind`, bound as `$C_TB_2001Q3`), `verb = "explain"` (one `explain balance` per leaf), `verb = "checkpoint"`, `"bundle"`, `"replay"`, and one record per in-process `fa_verify::cli::run` argv with its exit; `branch_class = "entry_decomposition=one_allocation_entry"`; one `VerdictRecord` (`record = "verdict"`) for W-T-04 with its projection and witnesses. The period label → code map is logged once for the book (A7a). On failure `REPRODUCE fa --book <dir> allocate --intent …` is printed, and `LOG <path>` at the end. No `#[ignore]`; W-T-04 joins `case.toml` `claims` when it lands, so an UNRUN on it fails the `worldcom` test.

## Notes
- **Edges.**
  - ← W3: F6a, F6b and the ten leaf accounts.
  - ← A1b: the `allocation` field of `[[intent]]` (law, total, targets) and its loader.
  - ← A7a: the runner core that drives `fa allocate`.
  - ← A11b: the contributing-entry witness.
  - ← A12: the outsider check of the certified read.
- W-D-03 cites F6b's legs on the same cell (Medium; `round_legs` = 11). W-P-01(b)'s probe of `fa allocate --approval <self vid>` (W5) uses the same intent with a self-approval.
- The equal split of 544,000,000.00 into ten is exact under any equal-split law. The T shows that the registered law reproduces the sentence; it does not tell `EqualSplitResidualFirst` apart from other equal-split laws, which differ only on residuals.
- **Names.** Case directory `worldcom` (`case.toml` `letter = "W"`), the TB read choice and the test names are this round's fixed choices.
- **Requires A1b** to accept the explicit form's source fields beside `allocation_law`/`allocation_total`/`allocation_targets` (proposed `allocation_source`, `allocation_source_side`; `fa allocate` reads `source` and `source_side`, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:10142`, `:10306`). **Requires A7a** to render `allocation_law` into `method` and to refuse rendering without it.
- **Related tracker bead fa-joq** (allocation laws registry and the Allocate intent with law id and basis digest on every leg; open; related link added this round). Its registry, laws and kernel posting landed on main per its notes (2026-10-14), and it is still open; W-T-04 exercises its `EqualSplitResidualFirst` row and the `law_digest` on F6b's legs, so a change to the law's id, version or residual rule under fa-joq moves this T and its eleventh-target negative.
- **Doc nit (no edge).** The `allocate` verb row's summary names ExactProRata, LargestRemainder and SequentialWaterfall (`registries/verbs.toml:452`), while the CLI parses `equal_split_residual_first`/`EqualSplitResidualFirst` (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:9784-9785`) and the law is registered (`allocation_laws.toml:35-42`). The case follows the code.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `PASS W-T-04 T native -/entry_decomposition=one_allocation_entry`. `fa allocate` under `EqualSplitResidualFirst` (law id 5), applied to the explicit total 544,000,000.00 (`total` + `source_side = credit`, never `source_period`) and ten declared targets in input order, with the law named explicitly in the rendered intent (`method = EqualSplitResidualFirst`, never the CLI default `largest_remainder`), yields ten legs of exactly 54,400,000.00 and residual 0, equal to "exactly $54.4 million each" (p.111) and to fa-oracles' independent recomputation. Each leaf's certified balance has F6b's leg as its only contribution, and the certified TB read passes the outsider check (`fa-verify` argv exit 0, report rows 54,400,000.00; `fa replay` byte-identical). No W-T-04 line prints on the `ten_two_leg_entries` cell.
- [ ] positive: `w_t_04_f6b_intent_json_names_the_law_and_the_explicit_total` passes, and its planted copy without `allocation_law` is refused at render. `w_t_04_equal_split_residual_first` passes (10 targets: residual 0; total + 0.01: first leg + 0.01; 11 targets: residual 0.05 to the first) and fails on its planted residual-to-last copy.
- [ ] negative: on temp copies, `worldcom_neg_w9_parts_posted` re-types the claimed W-T-04 as R, printed `FAIL W-T-04 R … reason=retyped T→R K-TAUT` (never `PASS … T`), and fails the case; `worldcom_neg_w9_eleventh_target` prints `FAIL W-T-04 … value` (49,454,545.45 on ten legs and 49,454,545.50 on the first, the law's residual-to-first rule); `worldcom_neg_w9_total_plus_one` prints `FAIL W-T-04 … residual` (residual 0.01).
- [ ] negative: if the outsider or contributing-entry witness is missing, the row prints UNRUN, never PASS, and the test exits non-zero.
- [ ] no-claim: the registered law's equal split reproduces the committee's "exactly $54.4 million each" on our encoding of F6b as one allocation entry. It says nothing about how WorldCom's sub-ledger was built, it does not tell this law apart from other equal-split laws, and it is not a claim on the `ten_two_leg_entries` cell.

title: [cases] X1: SunPower 10-K/A and filed FY2022 10-K sources, cited xbrl-facts values and receipts; per-line assurance; census and duration rules
description:
## Why
SunPower's 10-K/A FY2022 is the program's flagship T case: "the cleanest exact T", and the "reproduces the published bridge" leg of the owner's request (plan §10.1, §18). Its XBRL instance tags, for the same concept, period and unit, the as-previously-reported value A (`srt:ScenarioPreviouslyReportedMember`), the adjustment Δ (`srt:RestatementAdjustmentMember`) and the as-restated value B (undimensioned) (§1.1). The research found 122 complete (concept, period) triples that close: A + Δ = B.

This item lands the sources, the extracted `xbrl-facts` rows and their receipts, so that X3 can post A and Δ and compare franken_accounting's certified B. Four findings shape it:
- **The oracle is the instance, never companyfacts.** The companyfacts JSON API drops dimensional facts, so it carries no RestatementAxis adjustment members (§1.2).
- **Assurance is per line.** E&Y audits the annual statements; the quarterly figures, including the worked example, come from "SELECTED UNAUDITED QUARTERLY FINANCIAL DATA" (§10.1).
- **The duration rule needs a census.** A and Δ may be posted only for the finest non-overlapping durations the instance tags, so whether durations overlap must be settled here (§15 X1).
- **Vintages are named.** K-VINTAGE needs the originally filed FY2022 10-K wherever the 10-K/A's "as previously reported" A differs from the filed A (§10.4, §15 X1), so this item fetches it too.

Claim types served: T and R (X-T-01, X-R-01) and the X7 lifecycle.

## What to build
**Files** (one case directory holds SunPower and Microsoft, `crates/fa-oracles/cases/xbrl/`, because X-T-01…X-T-04 share one numbering, one README and one examiner card, §12.3, §12.5):
- `sources.toml` (SunPower rows; X1m adds Microsoft's, X6 RH's);
- `facts.toml` (`[[fact]]` + `[[value]]` rows, A1a's schema);
- `receipts.toml` (GENERATED by `case_fetch.py verify`, never hand-edited);
- `case.toml`: X1 authors the XBRL case's header (`id = "xbrl"`, `letter = "X"`, `title`, `version`, `kind = "case"`, `scope`, `pinned_commit`; X3 and X5 add `claims`, `capabilities` and `variants`), the per-line assurance rule and the census fields (below);
- `roles.toml`: the harness labels the X books use (`kind = harness`): `case-preparer-1` (posts A), `case-closer-1` (plans issuances, closes and locks, as on WorldCom's books), `case-approver-1`, `case-approver-2`, `case-poster-1`, `case-second-reader`, `examiner-witness`; the `[deny] hashes` list holds the hashed tokens of any person a cited sentence names (none is expected: the instances name no individual), never names in clear;
- `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_xbrl.rs` (this item's load-time negatives and the census/coverage unit tests);
- the census/coverage functions in fa-oracles' `cases` module, and the matching counting in `tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py xbrl-facts` with stdlib `unittest` cases.

**Sources (§10.1, copied).** Proposed ids (the plan fixes none): `SRC-SPWR-10KA-2022`, `SRC-SPWR-10KA-2022-HTML`, `SRC-SPWR-8K-ITEM402`, `SRC-SPWR-10K-2022`.
- the 10-K/A, EDGAR `0000867773-23-000117` (`AmendmentFlag true`), as two rows: its XBRL instance (`SRC-SPWR-10KA-2022`, format `xml`, the row every `spwr.*` value fact, vintage role and citation stub names) and its HTML document (proposed `SRC-SPWR-10KA-2022-HTML`, format `htm`), where the assurance sentences are anchored. A §4.1 row carries one `original_url`, one `sha256` and one `format`, and K-ANCHOR checks each fact's anchor kind against its row's format (A3a), so one row cannot hold both files; both rows carry the same accession, `filed_on` and `restates`;
- the 8-K that selected it, from the EDGAR full-text-search index of 8-K Item 4.02 filings: accession `0000867773-23-000089`, items 4.02 / 5.02 / 9.01, filed 2023-10-24 (the determination-date source for X7);
- the originally filed FY2022 10-K's XBRL instance (`SRC-SPWR-10K-2022`, format `xml`, the row the `spwr10k.*` facts and X3's issuance stub cite; the plan gives no accession; it is recorded at fetch from EDGAR's filing index, never guessed), for K-VINTAGE (§15 X1).

Every §4.1 field is filled, including the two K-VINTAGE orders by (§4.1, A3b): `filed_on` and `restates`. Both 10-K/A rows have `restates = ["SRC-SPWR-10K-2022"]` (the 10-K/A restates the filed FY2022 10-K) and the filed 10-K row `restates = []`; both `filed_on` dates are recorded at fetch from the filings' EDGAR headers, never guessed. The 8-K row has `filed_on = "2023-10-24"` (§10.1) and `restates = []`. `assertion_status` is a sources-row field (§4.1): both 10-K/A rows are `filer_audited`, and their `assurance` names both establishing texts, each a sourced fact on the HTML row (the auditor named for the annual statements, which is A1a's single `assurance_fact`; the "SELECTED UNAUDITED QUARTERLY FINANCIAL DATA" heading, on which the per-line rule below rests). Per-line assurance is not a source field: it is the `assurance` field each X-T-01 row carries (§5.3, §10.1), computed by one declared rule recorded in `case.toml`: a fiscal-year duration or a fiscal-year-end instant inside the audited statements → `filer_audited`; every other context (a quarterly or year-to-date duration, or an instant that is not a fiscal-year end: the quarterly data) → `filer_unaudited`, so every X-T row, X4's instant rows included, gets exactly one status. `redistribution_basis` is `public-record/sec-filing`. `anchor_scheme` names `xbrl{concept, context id}` on the instance rows and `page`/`line` on the HTML rows (the 10-K/A's HTML and the 8-K). `status` is `OK`, or `BLOCKED{reason}` for anything not retrieved, never silently substituted.

**Retrieval** (A9). `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch xbrl`, `… xbrl-facts xbrl`, `… verify xbrl`, under the project User-Agent at ≤ 1 request per second. Direct sec.gov only with `FA_SEC_CONTACT` (OD 1), else archive captures (`retrieval_route = archive_capture`, `original_hash_compared = false`).

**`xbrl-facts` rows → `[[fact]]` rows** (§4.4). Each extracted row is (concept, context id, period, unit, decimals, dimension members, value), anchored by instance line. Each cited row becomes a `sourced` fact with `granularity = xbrl_fact`, `source`, `anchor_kind = xbrl`, `anchor` in A1a's grammar `<concept>|<context id>` (for example `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss|c-441`), `quote_sha256`, `about_scope = period:<label>`, A1a's `cell` key `<concept local name>[:<member local name>]@<period label>` (the member separates the previously-reported A and the adjustment Δ from the undimensioned B; the filed 10-K's undimensioned fact shares the B's cell, so K-VINTAGE can compare the two vintages), and one `[[value]]` row (A1a: `literal` = the fact's text as written in the instance, `rule = scale`, `param = 0` because an instance value is already in units, `precision` from `decimals` (3 for `decimals="-3"`), `unit = USD`, `value` in A1a's canonical form at USD's registered scale 2, `registries/units.toml:15-17`). Proposed fact ids: `spwr.<concept local name>.<context id>` (10-K/A) and `spwr10k.<concept local name>.<context id>` (filed 10-K).
- **Which facts are cited, and so committed.** Every fact of each of the 122 strict triples (A, Δ and B, so the strict coverage count recomputes offline), the coarser-duration B facts X3's fold rows compare, and the filed 10-K values for the same (concept, period) cells. The values of cited facts are committed like every case's literal values (§1.3). OD 2b governs only committing whole tables beyond them: the full instance row set behind the instance-wide census.
- **Worked example**, verbatim from §10.1: Q4 FY2022 (2022-10-03 … 2023-01-01) `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss`, A 7,613,000 (c-441) + Δ −4,188,000 (c-442) = B 3,425,000 (c-443), `decimals="-3"`, USD → facts `spwr.NetIncomeLoss.c-441` (value 7613000), `spwr.NetIncomeLoss.c-442` (−4188000), `spwr.NetIncomeLoss.c-443` (3425000).
- **Binding (§4.1, §4.4 as they now read).** An `xbrl` fact binds by exact fact value, not sentence alignment. Before OD 2a the fact carries only `quote_sha256` and its anchor; `verify` selects the one span at the anchor whose SHA-256 matches (zero or several matches is a FAIL). Each receipt carries `source`, `fact`, `anchor`, `verified_utc`, `tool_version`, `extraction_sha256`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the fact's canonical literal values and `about_scope`, so K-BIND detects offline a value or scope edited after `verify`), `alignment` (`value` for every `xbrl` fact; `sentence` for the HTML prose facts that anchor assurance), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok` (all true; for an xbrl fact `aligned` records value alignment: the quote is the whole fact value, never a fragment of it), and the source's `original_hash_compared`, copied from its source row (false for an archive capture until OD 1).

**Census and coverage: three fa-oracles functions** (exact, checked integer arithmetic; the Python tool implements the same rules for the instance-wide run):
- `census(rows) -> u64`: distinct (concept, context id, value) rows, dimensional members included (the rule the case states; the research found 506 / 524, the review 508 / 526 raw).
- `strict_triples(rows) -> (closing, complete, incomplete: Vec<(concept, period)>)`: a (concept, period, unit) group is a strict triple when it has exactly one A, one Δ and one B fact; it closes when A + Δ = B exactly. Expected over the 10-K/A: 122 complete, 122 closing.
- `closing_groups(rows) -> (closing, total)`: groups with one A, one B and one or more Δ members (or several restated facts) close when A + ΣΔ = B. The research's count is 486 (MOR audit AUD02).
- **Where the numbers live.** `case.toml` records `census_rule`, `census_count`, `strict_triples_closing`, `closing_groups`, and the instance SHA-256 they were computed over (field names are this round's proposal; X1 declares them, with the instance SHA-256 key (proposed `instance_sha256`) and the per-line assurance rule's key (proposed `assurance_rule`), in the `xbrl` row of A1a's `CASE_EXTENSIONS` table in `header.rs`; an undeclared key is refused `UnknownField`). The instance-wide numbers (census, groups) are computed at authoring by `xbrl-facts` over every instance row in the cache. The offline test recomputes `strict_triples` over the committed cited facts and must equal the recorded 122; the instance-wide numbers are offline-checked only for presence and rule text (their rows are OD 2b's), and the check report says so.

**Duration census** (§10.1 duration rule, §15 X1). A fa-oracles function `finest_non_overlapping(periods_by_concept)` returns, per concept, the durations tagged, whether they overlap, and the finest non-overlapping set on which X3 posts A and Δ. A finer value only implied (FY − 9M YTD) is returned flagged `difference` (K-TAUT bars a T on the line it came from). Two tagged durations of one concept that overlap without nesting are an error naming both contexts. The custom-calendar periods X3 needs (for example Q4 FY2022 = 2022-10-03 … 2023-01-01) come from the instance's contexts.

**Filed-vintage comparison** (§10.4, K-VINTAGE). For each cited (concept, period) that the filed 10-K also tags, a `derived` fact `rule = difference`, `from = [spwr10k.…, spwr.… (the A fact)]`, id `spwr.vintage.<concept>.<period label>`, whose value is 0 exactly when the filed value equals the 10-K/A's previously-reported A. K-DERIVE recomputes it at load. Where it is non-zero, X3 names both vintages and states which one the bridge uses. A cell the filed 10-K does not tag has no such fact, and X3 renders it "filed vintage not compared" (the plan names no 10-Q source), never assumed equal.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
- Authoring: `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch xbrl`, `… xbrl-facts xbrl`, `… verify xbrl`; read `rc=$?` after each. Each exits 0 (`verify` prints `VERIFY <fact> PASS` per fact), or exits 1 with `FAIL ` lines at column 0, or exits 4 with `UNRUN ` lines when the network or a tool is unavailable (A9's exit codes; never reported as success). Byte identity: copy `receipts.toml`, re-run `verify` on the unchanged cache, `cmp` the two (identical, because `verified_utc` is the cache fetch time). A second agent with a second cache re-runs `verify` independently (§4.5).
- Tool tests: `python3 -B -m unittest discover tools/case-fetch` (run by A9's fa-oracles gate test).
- Offline: `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_xbrl`.

**Expected lines** (A3a/A10a own the check-report format; the values are what it must contain):
- `CHECK xbrl K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, and the same for K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR and K-DERIVE (K-DERIVE examines the vintage `difference` facts), each n > 0. A check reports UNRUN only when the case has no rows of its input kind (K-DERIVE, if the filed 10-K tags none of the cited cells), and an `examined` count below its input count is a FAIL;
- `SOURCE SRC-SPWR-10KA-2022 original_hash_compared=<bool> route=<retrieval_route>` per source (false / `archive_capture` until OD 1), and `EXCERPTS xbrl facts_with_quote=0 words=0` (no quote text before OD 2a);
- `case_xbrl.rs` prints, from the census functions over the committed facts: `strict_triples complete=122 closing=122 recorded=122` (the instance-wide census and group counts print `recorded_only` with their rule).

**Unit tests** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_xbrl.rs`, fixture rows written in the test):
- `census_counts_distinct_concept_context_value`: rows (NetIncomeLoss, c-441, 7613000), (NetIncomeLoss, c-442, −4188000), (NetIncomeLoss, c-443, 3425000) → 3. Boundary: the c-443 row repeated at a second instance line (a duplicate fact) → still 3; the same concept and value under a different context → 4.
- `strict_triple_closes_worked_example`: the three rows above → complete 1, closing 1.
- `strict_triple_planted_wrong_delta`: Δ edited to −4,187,000 (one display unit at `decimals="-3"`) → complete 1, closing 0, and the failing group is named.
- `group_with_two_delta_members`: A 100, Δ 30 and Δ 0 under two members, B 130 → not a strict triple; `closing_groups` counts it closing.
- `incomplete_pair_listed`: A and B with no Δ → in neither closing count; listed in `incomplete`.
- `recorded_count_mismatch_fails`: `case.toml` records 122 while the committed facts give 121 → the test fails naming `strict_triples_closing`, 122 and 121.
- `finest_durations_prefer_quarters`: four quarters + FY + 9M YTD of one concept → the four quarters; `implied_q4_is_difference`: 9M YTD + FY with no Q4 context → Q4 flagged `difference`; `overlapping_unnested_durations_error`: two contexts overlapping without nesting → error naming both.
- `assurance_rule`: an FY-duration fact → `filer_audited`; a quarter → `filer_unaudited`; a fiscal-year-end instant → `filer_audited`; a quarter-end instant → `filer_unaudited`.

**Planted negatives** (load-time ones in `case_xbrl.rs`, each editing one row of an in-memory copy of the embedded case and asserting the named check, row id and line; tool ones as `unittest` cases on a fixture instance):
- a fact whose `anchor` disagrees with its receipt's `anchor` fails K-ANCHOR; at authoring, a context id that does not occur at its anchored instance line makes `verify` print a `FAIL` line and exit non-zero;
- a committed Δ value edited by 1,000 makes the recomputed `strict_triples` closing count 121 ≠ the recorded 122 (FAIL naming the triple), K-BIND FAILs that fact offline (its `values_sha256` no longer matches its receipt), and at authoring `verify` prints `FAIL` for that fact (`values_in_quote = false`);
- `x_fold_b_value_edited_after_verify_fails_k_bind`: a cited value outside every strict triple and vintage fact (a coarser-duration B that X3's fold rows compare) edited by one unit → `FAIL K-BIND … <fact>: values_sha256 mismatch`, naming the fact and its line. Before `values_sha256`, only the second reader's independent `verify` could catch this edit;
- `x_receipt_alignment_sentence_on_xbrl_fact_fails`: a receipt with `alignment = "sentence"` on an `xbrl` fact → refused at load as A1a's `ReceiptMismatch` (A1a's own `receipt_alignment_not_matching_its_anchor_kind_is_refused`; A10a's receipts-consistency check reports it too), naming the receipt and the anchor kind;
- a fact citing a `BLOCKED` row is refused;
- a fact anchored `xbrl` on a companyfacts-API source row (`format = json`) fails K-ANCHOR (the anchor kind does not match the source format), so companyfacts can never be the oracle;
- the vintage fact `spwr.vintage.…` recorded 0 while the filed and previously-reported values differ fails K-DERIVE.

**Logging.** This item has no runner rows. The tool's stdout carries the census per rule beside the plan's numbers (122 strict; 486 groups; 506/524 vs 508/526), the duration census per concept, and the filed-vintage result per cited cell (equal, differs with both values, or not compared). A difference from the plan's counts is reported and explained in the case, never hidden.

## Notes
- **← A9:** `case_fetch.py`, including `xbrl-facts`.
- **OD 1** gates direct EDGAR fetches. **OD 2a** gates quote text only. **OD 2b** gates committing whole tables beyond the cited facts (here, the full instance row set behind the instance-wide census). The cited facts' values are committed now (§1.3, §15 X1). This replaces the earlier hashes-only reading, and its row-set-hash negative is replaced by the committed-value and recorded-count negatives above.
- **Settled: the as-filed vintage.** §15 X1 has this item fetch the originally filed FY2022 10-K for K-VINTAGE. The plan names no 10-Q, so quarterly filed values are compared only where the original 10-K tags them.
- **Offline value guard (settled by `values_sha256`).** Round 2 noted that a receipt bound a value only at `verify` time, so a value outside every triple and vintage fact was guarded only by the second reader. The receipt's `values_sha256` now binds every cited fact's values and scope, so K-BIND catches such an edit offline (`x_fold_b_value_edited_after_verify_fails_k_bind`); the recomputed closure counts and the second reader's `verify` remain as further guards.
- **Receipt fields and header (settled).** A1a (Receipt type), A9 (writer), A3a (K-BIND reads `values_sha256`) and A10a (receipts consistency reads `alignment`) all carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned` now (§4.4 after round 2; `aligned` replaces round 2's `sentence_aligned`). A1a loads `case.toml` with `id = "xbrl"` (the directory name) and the required `letter = "X"`, which prefixes every expectation and generated row id (§3.2b; the prefix is the letter, not derived from the id). The census and assurance-rule keys load through the `CASE_EXTENSIONS` row above.
- **Naming** (this round's choices): the case directory `xbrl`, source ids and fact ids above. Book variant stems are X3's and X5's (`statement-sunpower`, `statement-sunpower-is`, `statement-microsoft`); the case letter is `X` (§3.2b).
- **Cross-bead.** K-ASSERT (A3c) renders a source's single `assertion_status`; for X rows it must render each row's per-line `assurance` instead, or quarterly lines would read "audited".
- X7 depends on this item for the Item 4.02 8-K row. X3 depends on it for every A, Δ and B fact.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `crates/fa-oracles/cases/xbrl/sources.toml` carries the 10-K/A (`0000867773-23-000117`) as two rows (its XBRL instance and its HTML), the Item 4.02 8-K (`0000867773-23-000089`, `filed_on = "2023-10-24"`) and the originally filed FY2022 10-K (accession as recorded at fetch) with every §4.1 field, including `filed_on` (recorded at fetch where the plan gives none) and `restates` (both 10-K/A rows restate the filed 10-K's row); `case.toml` carries `id = "xbrl"`, `letter = "X"` and the per-line assurance rule (fiscal-year durations and fiscal-year-end instants `filer_audited`, every other context `filer_unaudited`); `roles.toml` carries the X books' harness labels and a hashed (possibly empty) deny list.
- [ ] positive: `facts.toml` commits the value of every cited fact (all 122 strict triples' A, Δ and B facts, the fold B facts and the filed-10-K values) as `[[value]]` rows, each fact with an A1a `xbrl` anchor (`<concept>|<context id>`) and `cell` key, including `spwr.NetIncomeLoss.c-441` = 7613000, `c-442` = −4188000 and `c-443` = 3425000 (Q4 FY2022, `decimals="-3"`, USD). `receipts.toml` has one row per sourced fact with `alignment = "value"` on every xbrl fact (`sentence` on the HTML prose facts), all four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) true, `values_sha256` equal to the hash of the fact's committed values and scope, and `original_hash_compared` as copied from its source row; a re-run of `verify` on the unchanged cache is byte-identical, and a second reader's independent `verify` agrees.
- [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` prints `CHECK xbrl <K-ID> PASS examined=<n>/<n>` with n > 0 for K-PROV, K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR and K-DERIVE; `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_xbrl` recomputes `strict_triples` = 122 complete / 122 closing from the committed facts, equal to `case.toml`'s record; the instance-wide census (rule: distinct (concept, context, value), members included) and the 486-group count are recorded with the instance SHA-256 and reported beside the plan's figures; every concept has its duration census and finest non-overlapping set; every cited cell the filed 10-K tags has a K-DERIVE-checked vintage `difference` fact.
- [ ] negative: each is observed: a fact anchor that disagrees with its receipt fails K-ANCHOR (and a context id absent at its instance line makes `verify` print `FAIL`); a committed Δ edited by one display unit drops the recomputed closing count to 121 ≠ 122 and FAILs naming the triple, and FAILs K-BIND offline on `values_sha256`; a fold B value edited after `verify` FAILs K-BIND offline (`values_sha256` mismatch); a receipt with `alignment = "sentence"` on an xbrl fact is refused; a fact citing a `BLOCKED` row is refused; an `xbrl` anchor on a companyfacts (`json`) source fails K-ANCHOR; a vintage fact recorded 0 over differing values fails K-DERIVE; each census unit test's planted wrong count fails.
- [ ] no-claim: the rows reproduce the instance's tagged facts in bytes with a recorded SHA-256. They say nothing about whether SunPower's restated figures are correct, and the bytes equal the EDGAR originals only if `original_hash_compared = true`. Quarterly lines are unaudited.

title: [cases] X1m: Microsoft FY2018 10-K sources and xbrl-facts rows (16 complete A+Δ=B triples; 3 incomplete pairs)
description:
## Why
Microsoft's FY2018 10-K recast its prior-year statements for ASC 606 and ASC 842 under the full retrospective method. Its XBRL instance tags the previously reported, adjustment and recast values, and the research found 16 complete triples that close (§10.2). It feeds X-T-03, the program's first exercise of a PolicyChangeRetrospective case. This is a change in accounting principle, not an error correction, and the case must say so. PolicyChangeRetrospective posting has never been tested anywhere (H13). This item lands the sources and the extracted `xbrl-facts` rows that X5 posts and compares. As with SunPower, the oracle is the XBRL instance, never the companyfacts API, which drops dimensional adjustment members (§1.2). Claim types served: T and R (X-T-03, X-R-02).

## What to build
**Files**, in the shared XBRL case directory `crates/fa-oracles/cases/xbrl/` (one case with SunPower, X1): the Microsoft rows of `sources.toml`, its `[[fact]]` + `[[value]]` rows in `facts.toml` (`granularity = xbrl_fact`), its receipts in the regenerated `receipts.toml`, its census fields in `case.toml`, and its tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_xbrl.rs`. It reuses X1's census, strict-triple, group and duration functions; it adds none.

**Source (§10.2).** The FY2018 10-K, EDGAR `0001564590-18-019062`, as two rows: proposed `SRC-MSFT-10K-2018`, its XBRL instance (format `xml`, anchor scheme `xbrl`; the row every `msft.*` value fact, vintage role and citation stub names), and proposed `SRC-MSFT-10K-2018-HTML`, its HTML document (format `htm`, anchor scheme `page`/`line`), where the audit-report sentence is anchored. A §4.1 row carries one `original_url`, `sha256` and `format`, and K-ANCHOR checks each anchor kind against its row's format (A3a), as in X1; both rows carry the same accession, `filed_on` and `restates`. Every §4.1 field is filled, including `filed_on` (recorded at fetch from the filing's EDGAR header; the plan gives none) and `restates`: `["SRC-MSFT-10K-2017"]` if the FY2017 10-K is fetched as a row (proposed id; see Vintage), else `[]` with the reason in `notes` (K-VINTAGE then has no earlier Microsoft vintage to compare). `assurance` is determined from the filing's own audit report (§2.2: "never assumed"); the plan states no assurance for these lines. Per-line assurance on X-T-03 rows uses X1's declared rule (fiscal-year facts inside the audited statements `filer_audited`; other durations `filer_unaudited`), and the rows record whatever the filing establishes. `redistribution_basis` is `public-record/sec-filing`. Retrieval: `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch|xbrl-facts|verify xbrl` (A9), under OD 1's rule.

**`xbrl-facts` rows → `[[fact]]` rows** (§4.4), each (concept, context id, period, unit, decimals, dimension members, value), anchored by instance line, proposed id `msft.<concept local name>.<context id>`, `anchor_kind = xbrl`, `anchor = <concept>|<context id>` (A1a's grammar), A1a's `cell` key `<concept local name>[:<member local name>]@<period label>` (as X1), and its value committed as a `[[value]]` row (`literal` as written in the instance, `rule = scale`, `param = 0`, `precision` from `decimals`, `unit = USD`). The values of the facts the case cites are committed like every case's literal values (§1.3, by analogy with §15 X1); OD 2b governs only whole tables beyond them. Cited: every fact of the 16 complete triples, the facts of the 3 incomplete pairs (so they can be listed as not modelled), and any coarser-duration B facts X5's fold rows compare. The research's figures, copied from §10.2 and re-verified at authoring, for FY2017:
- `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss`: 21,204M + 4,285M = 25,489M;
- revenue (concept as tagged): 89,950M + 6,621M = 96,571M;
- `us-gaap:StockholdersEquity` at 2017-06-30: 72,394M + 15,317M + 0 (the ASU 2016-02 member) = 87,711M.

The equity group has two adjustment members (the ASC 606 adjustment and the ASU 2016-02 member, tagged 0), so it is A + ΣΔ = B. Each member's QName is recorded as tagged, and the zero member is a committed fact of its own (one `[[value]]` row with `literal = "0"`), never omitted. Binding is by exact fact value (§4.1). Receipts carry X1's shape: `anchor`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (values and scope, so an edit after `verify` fails K-BIND offline), `alignment = "value"` on every xbrl fact (`sentence` on HTML prose facts), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote` and `scope_ok`, all true, and `original_hash_compared` copied from the source row.

**Coverage per line** (§10.2). 16 complete triples close; three pairs are incomplete, listed as not modelled with their (concept, period). The census rule is X1's: distinct (concept, context, value), dimensional members included. The equity group has two Δ members, so X1's `strict_triples` (exactly one Δ) does not count it, yet §10.2 lists it among the 16; the 16 is therefore counted with X1's `closing_groups` (one A, one B, one or more Δ members) over the Microsoft facts, and the test prints the strict count beside it with its rule. A difference from the plan's 16 is reported and explained, never hidden. `case.toml` records `msft_complete_closing = 16` and `msft_incomplete = 3` beside Microsoft's instance SHA-256 (proposed key `msft_instance_sha256`; X1's key holds SunPower's), all three declared in the `xbrl` row of A1a's `CASE_EXTENSIONS` (A1a lists the first two; field names are this round's proposal, as in X1).

**Duration census.** X1's `finest_non_overlapping` per concept (the §10.1 rule applies to X-T-03 "as X-T-01"), plus the fiscal-year periods and instants (for example 2017-06-30) the X5 book needs.

**Vintage.** §15 X1m lists no FY2017 10-K. If it is fetched (proposed row `SRC-MSFT-10K-2017`, `filed_on` recorded at fetch, `restates = []`), each cited cell it tags gets a `derived` vintage fact (`rule = difference`, filed value − previously-reported A, 0 when equal), as in X1; if it is not fetched, X5 renders A as the FY2018 filing's "previously reported" vintage and says the filed vintage was not compared. Record which in the source row's `notes`.

## Tests & logging
**Run.** Authoring as X1 (`fetch`, `xbrl-facts`, `verify`; byte-identical re-run checked with `cmp`; second reader with a second cache). Offline: `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_xbrl`.

**Expected lines.** `CHECK xbrl K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, and the same for K-BIND, K-SCOPE and K-ANCHOR (and K-DERIVE where vintage facts exist), the Microsoft rows included in the counts (A3a/A10a own the format; a check is UNRUN only when the case has no rows of its input kind), `SOURCE SRC-MSFT-10K-2018 original_hash_compared=<bool> route=<retrieval_route>`, and from `case_xbrl.rs`: `msft complete=16 closing=16 incomplete=3 recorded=16/3 rule=closing_groups strict=<n>`. Authoring: `verify` prints `VERIFY <fact> PASS` per fact and exits 0 (1 with `FAIL ` lines; 4 with `UNRUN ` lines when a tool or the network is missing, A9).

**Unit tests** (in `case_xbrl.rs`, on the committed Microsoft facts):
- `msft_counts_match_record`: `closing_groups` over the committed Microsoft facts gives 16 closing (the two-Δ equity group included) and `strict_triples` lists the 3 incomplete pairs, equal to `case.toml`; the strict closing count is printed beside them.
- `msft_equity_group_keeps_zero_member`: the StockholdersEquity 2017-06-30 group holds A 72,394M, the ASC 606 Δ 15,317M, the ASU 2016-02 Δ 0 and B 87,711M, and closes A + ΣΔ = B.

**Planted negatives** (load-time, each on an in-memory copy, asserting the check or test name, the row id and its line):
- the equity group copied with the ASU 2016-02 member fact removed still closes arithmetically (the member is 0), so `msft_equity_group_keeps_zero_member` must FAIL naming the missing member; it never passes silently;
- a committed Δ edited by one display unit makes the closing count 15 ≠ the recorded 16 (FAIL naming the triple), K-BIND FAILs that fact offline (`values_sha256` mismatch), and at authoring `verify` prints `FAIL` for that fact;
- `msft_incomplete_pair_value_edited_after_verify_fails_k_bind`: a value of one of the 3 incomplete pairs (outside every closing triple, so no count moves) edited by one unit → `FAIL K-BIND … values_sha256 mismatch`, naming the fact and its line;
- a fact `anchor` that disagrees with its receipt fails K-ANCHOR;
- a recorded `msft_complete_closing` that disagrees with the recomputation fails, naming both numbers.

**Logging.** No runner rows. The tool's stdout carries the counts with their rule beside the plan's (16; 3), the duration census per concept, and the vintage outcome. A difference from the plan's counts is reported and explained in the case.

## Notes
- **← A9:** `case_fetch.py` with `xbrl-facts`.
- **OD 1** gates direct EDGAR fetches. **OD 2b** governs only whole tables beyond the cited facts (§1.3, §15 X1, by analogy); the cited values are committed now. This replaces the earlier hashes-only reading, and its row-set-hash negative is replaced by the committed-value and recorded-count negatives above.
- **Vintage (§10.4).** If the FY2017 10-K's as-filed values differ from the recast's previously-reported member, the case carries both and states which one the bridge uses.
- X5 depends on this item (with X2, A7b, A11b, A12 and H13).
- **Receipt fields (settled).** A1a, A9, A3a and A10a now carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned` (`aligned` replaces round 2's `sentence_aligned`), as X1 notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `crates/fa-oracles/cases/xbrl/sources.toml` carries the FY2018 10-K (`0001564590-18-019062`) as two rows (its XBRL instance and its HTML), each with every §4.1 field (`filed_on` recorded at fetch; `restates` naming the FY2017 10-K's row if it is fetched, else `[]` with the reason) and assurance read from the filing. `facts.toml` commits the value of every cited fact as `[[value]]` rows, each fact with an A1a `xbrl` anchor and `cell` key, including FY2017 NetIncomeLoss (21,204M + 4,285M = 25,489M), revenue (89,950M + 6,621M = 96,571M) and StockholdersEquity at 2017-06-30 (72,394M + 15,317M + 0 = 87,711M, the zero ASU 2016-02 member a fact of its own). Receipts bind every cited fact with `alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) true, `values_sha256` equal to the hash of the fact's committed values and scope, and `original_hash_compared` copied from the source row; a re-run is byte-identical and a second reader's `verify` agrees.
- [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_xbrl` recomputes 16 closing groups (X1's `closing_groups`, which counts the two-Δ equity group; the strict count is printed beside it) and 3 incomplete pairs from the committed facts, equal to `case.toml`'s record and the stated counting rule; `ledgers_validate_offline` prints `CHECK xbrl <K-ID> PASS examined=<n>/<n>` with the Microsoft rows counted; each concept carries its duration census; the vintage outcome (compared, or "filed vintage not compared") is recorded.
- [ ] negative: a silently omitted zero-valued ASU 2016-02 member FAILs `msft_equity_group_keeps_zero_member`; a Δ edited by one display unit drops the closing count to 15 ≠ 16 and FAILs naming the triple, and FAILs K-BIND offline on `values_sha256`; an incomplete-pair value edited after `verify` FAILs K-BIND offline; a fact anchor that disagrees with its receipt fails K-ANCHOR; a recorded count that disagrees with the recomputation fails.
- [ ] no-claim: the rows reproduce the instance's tagged facts in bytes with a recorded SHA-256. They say nothing about ASC 606 / ASC 842 compliance or the correctness of the recast, and the bytes equal EDGAR's only if `original_hash_compared = true`.

title: [cases] X2: us-gaap → FA role_map for the modelled XBRL concepts (type, role, certifiable read or not-modelled)
description:
## Why
X-T-01, X-T-03 and C-T-01 compare franken_accounting's certified reads with tagged XBRL values. A tagged us-gaap concept has a certifiable read only if it maps onto one of the two certified statement definitions' whole-type lines, or onto a per-account balance (§3.8, §10.1). `role_map{chart_rule}` is the plan's interpretive derivation rule for that mapping: sourced account name → account type (`registries/account_types.toml`) and optional role (the closed set of 15, `registries/account_roles.toml`) (§2.4).

Because the mapping is a judgment, every claim that uses it names it in its rendered sentence. A T through `role_map` holds under our mapping (§2.4). Concepts with no certifiable read are listed as not modelled, and coverage is reported per line, never as "the statements" (§10.1).

This item lands that mapping once, for the concepts X3, X5 and C1 model. Claim types served: T, R and C on the XBRL and merger books.

## What to build
**Files.**
- `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_derivations.toml` (A2's table, `schema_version = 1`, Consumer/Gate/Retire header): one chart rule, proposed id `us-gaap-xbrl-v1`, used as `role_map{chart_rule = "us-gaap-xbrl-v1"}`, `interpretive = true`, with one row per mapped concept. The plan names no separate file. Proposed row table `[[chart_rule_row]]` with scalar fields `chart_rule`, `concept` (QName as tagged), `type` (an `account_types.toml` name, or empty for a line-only total), `role` (one of the 15, or empty), `balance_side` (`debit` | `credit`), `read` (`bs:<line code>`, `is:<line code>`, `account`, or `not_modelled`), `reason` (required when `read = not_modelled`), `example`. A2 owns the table's schema and has accepted this proposal (A2's Notes, "Chart rules for `role_map{chart_rule}`"); its loader refuses an unknown `type` or `role`, a role that does not admit its type, a duplicate (`chart_rule`, `concept`) and a `not_modelled` row with no reason.
- The X and C books' `[[account]]` rows carry the result in their `type`, `role` and `role_map_rule = "us-gaap-xbrl-v1"` fields (§3.2a); X3, X5 and C1 author those rows.
- Loader, validation and tests in fa-oracles' `cases` module and `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_xbrl.rs` (the merger rows are tested there too, since the rule is shared).

**The certifiable reads at 8196f5e40.** The two definitions are the only certified reports (`crates/fa-statements/src/definition.rs:116-127`). Their lines select whole account types (`registries/statements/balance-sheet.toml`: `assets` :16, `liabilities` :22, `equity` "Posted equity" :28, `unclosed_revenue` :34, `unclosed_expense` :40, `unclosed_earnings` :46, `total_equity` "Equity including unclosed earnings" :52, `liabilities_and_equity` :58, `balance_check` :64; `income-statement.toml`: `revenue` :15, `expense` :21, `net_income` :27). Formula lines are add/subtract only (`crates/fa-statements/src/custom.rs:214-223`), and `StatementDefinition::from_toml` is wired to no verb (§3.8). So a below-type-level concept is modelled only as a per-account balance, and a ratio is never modelled.

**Rows (proposed; each consumer confirms the QName as tagged before relying on it):**

| concept | type | role | side | read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `us-gaap:Assets` | Asset | — | debit | `bs:assets` |
| `us-gaap:Liabilities` | Liability | — | credit | `bs:liabilities` |
| `us-gaap:StockholdersEquity` | Equity | — | credit | `bs:equity` on a book with no unclosed Revenue/Expense balance at that instant (X3's `statement-sunpower`); `account` (the concept's own leaf account) on a book that also carries flows (X5), because there the "Posted equity" line excludes the unclosed earnings |
| `us-gaap:LiabilitiesAndStockholdersEquity` | — (a line total) | — | credit | `bs:liabilities_and_equity` |
| `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss` | Revenue | — | credit | `account` (one leaf account per (concept, finest period), X3) |
| Microsoft's revenue concept (as tagged) | Revenue | — | credit | `account` |
| LinkedIn: cash | Asset | `cash` | debit | `account` |
| LinkedIn: PP&E | Asset | `fixed_asset` | debit | `account` |
| LinkedIn: short-term investments, other current assets, the intangible components, goodwill | Asset | — | debit | `account` |
| LinkedIn: short-term debt, other current liabilities, deferred tax, other | Liability | — | credit | `account` |
| LinkedIn: "Total purchase price" (as tagged) | — (a line total) | — | credit | `bs:equity` of the merger book's consideration account (C1's encoding) |
| LinkedIn: consideration transferred (as tagged, `decimals="-8"`) | — (compared, never posted) | — | credit | `bs:equity` (the same read, compared by C1's C-C-01 within its declared precision, never as T) |
| any other cited concept | — | — | — | `not_modelled`, with its reason |

- **Flow concepts read per account.** On a book holding several flow concepts, the `is:revenue`, `is:expense` and `is:net_income` lines sum every concept of the type, so a flow concept's read is `account`, never a type-level IS line.
