title: [cases] E4: Enron tie-outs: E-T-01/E-T-04 bridges per vintage, E-T-02 footing, E-T-03 delta from Powers entries, E-R-01/02; case-vs-revision decision
description:
## Why E4 lands every Enron T and R (claim types T and R). It is the "reproduces the published bridge" leg of the owner's request (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §0.1 goal 2), on a company whose restated figures were never audited: "No audited restated statements exist" (§7.1). Its shape follows the plan: - **Vintages.** The 8-K and the 10-Q restate the same periods differently in 20 of 30 cells (H-021). So each vintage is its own T, and the earlier one is read with an explicit `AS REPORTED IN` (K-VINTAGE). - **E-T-03.** It is the only T in the program whose Δ is computed from documented entries rather than replayed from a published bridge. - **Evidence class.** A T is an exact observation, replayable by `fa replay` and refolded by `fa-verify`, never `proof` (§5.3). It needs its contributing-entry witness and the outsider check of its read kind. - **Wording.** "reproduces the published bridge ⟨source⟩", with the assurance status. Never "matches the auditors" (§0.3). ## What to build **Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/enron/books/statement-bridge.toml`, `books/statement-10k2000.toml`, `books/statement-10q2001q3.toml`; E-T-03's additions to `books/native.toml`; E4's rows in `expectations.toml`; the posting derivations (`difference`, `sum`, `negate` rows over E2d's and E2b's facts) in `facts.toml`; the vintage decision and E4's expectation ids (added to `claims`) in `case.toml` (`id = "enron"`, `letter = "E"`, as E3 creates it); E4's tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_enron.rs` and `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`. (Variant stems are §3.2b's `-` form; requires A1b's loader to accept it.) **Ids (§3.2b).** A statement posting's intent id is the fact id of the figure it posts. On the bridge book each period's A entry posts several A cells in one balanced intent, so its id is the total-assets A fact its debit leg posts (`10K-TA-A-`, or `EX27-TA-A-FY1999` where the FY1999 posting uses the EX-27 vintage, K-VINTAGE), and its other legs name their facts through `amount_rule` (`value:10K-DEBT-A-#1`, `derived:difference`, `derived:remainder` over `REM-A-`, …; A1b's forms). A case Δ intent is `delta-`; where one book has more than one Δ intent against the same target (FY1999's A is restated by both the 8-K case and the 10-Q case), they are `delta--`, n = 1, 2, … in step order across the book (the `-` suffix is this round's extension of §3.2b for several Δs on one target), and a negation of case 1's Δ, if the decision takes that route, targets that Δ intent (`delta-delta-10K-TA-A-FY1999-1`). On the native book the Δs are `delta-NFS1` and `delta-NFS2e` (`fact = "derived:negate"`). The `[[case]]` ids are proposals: `enr-8k` (8-K Table 1 vintage, bridge book), `enr-10q` (Q3-2001 10-Q Note 3 vintage, bridge book; a Revision case if the decision says so) and `enr-raptor` (E-T-03, native book). The runner generates one R row per `[[case]]` row (`E-CASE-`, A7b, §3.3 step 5): `E-CASE-enr-8k`, `E-CASE-enr-10q`, `E-CASE-enr-raptor`; authors never write them. **Common to the three `statement` books** (§3.2, §7.2a): each has its own calendar and chart; citation-stub evidence from the publishing filings (§2.7: an A posting cites the filing whose figure it posts, the FY2000 10-K or the FY1999 EX-27; a Restatement/Revision Δ cites its restating filing, the 8-K, then the 10-Q; a footing line cites the filing that prints it); no filler; no D/P/N/CF except `about = "reconstruction"` rows; the runner-generated `E-SELF-statement-bridge`, `E-SELF-statement-10k2000` and `E-SELF-statement-10q2001q3` rows (A7a). **`books/statement-bridge.toml`** (E-T-01, E-T-04, E-R-01, E-R-02): - `[[period]]` labels `FY1997` … `FY2000` (annual, `kind` year); opening date before 1997-01-01. - `[[account]]`: one asset account (total assets), one debt account, one equity account, one liability-type remainder account (`remainder{line, of_total}`, §3.8), and one revenue-type net-income account; the type/role choices are the declared `role_map`. - **A intents** (one per period, `fact` = the A cells it posts, evidence the FY2000 10-K stub or, for FY1999 figures that come from it, the EX-27 stub). Stock lines are posted as period-over-period changes, so each certified year-end balance equals the printed A: `FY1997` posts the 1997-12-31 stock; each later year posts `difference` rows of consecutive A values (`10K-TA-A-FY` − `10K-TA-A-FY`, likewise DEBT and the remainder `REM-A`). Net income is posted as activity on the revenue-type account, and the equity leg is (EQ_y − EQ_{y−1}) − NI_y, so the balance sheet's `total_equity` ("Equity including unclosed earnings", `registries/statements/balance-sheet.toml`) certifies the printed equity and the income statement's `net_income` the printed net income. Every leg amount is an A value or a `difference`/`sum` of A values. A negative difference puts the leg on the other side. - **Δ intents** (`fact = "derived:"`, class Restatement, `target_kind = "restates"`, `target` = that period's A intent, `reason` a declared default with its rationale, never `Fraud` (K-REASON)): per period, the published Δ cells of the vintage, posted the same way (period-over-period `difference` of published Δs; equity Δ excluding the year's net-income Δ; the remainder from `REM-D` on Note 3's case. E2d's 8-K Δ cells for the bridge lines are FY1999's net income, total assets and equity only (its other 8-K cells are the B values and the Raptor line), with no debt Δ and no 8-K remainder, so the 8-K case posts FY1999 alone and its remainder Δ is a `difference` row E4 adds over those published Δs, ΔTA − ΔEQ (this round's proposal), which leaves the 8-K vintage's debt line unrestated and unread). No amount derives from a B value. - **Remainders** (§3.8, §7.2): the remainder's A side is `REM-A` (A values) and its Δ is `REM-D` (published Δs), never from a B value, so K-TAUT holds for the TA, debt and equity bridges. The restated remainder `REM-B` = 10,650 / 14,924 / 15,711 / 43,780 ($M) for FY1997–FY2000 is a logged consistency check of the certified remainder, not a T (the 2001Q1/2001Q2 values 42,751 / 39,230 are Note 3's own footing only, since those periods have no A). - **Two vintages, in order.** Issue FY1997–FY2000 as originally filed (citing the FY2000 10-K stub) and lock; case 1 posts the 8-K Table 1 Δ (citing SRC-ENR-002's stub); issue the restated statements to `sec` citing the 8-K stub; then the Q3-2001 10-Q Note 3 Δ. Note 3's Δ is stated against A, not against the 8-K's B, so the second step must leave the certified value at A + ΣΔ(Note 3) with every posted amount a published A or Δ: either a second Restatement case whose Δ intents reverse case 1's (`negate`) and post Note 3's, or a case plus a Revision (§7.3, §15 E4). **Decision record:** `case.toml` states the choice and its reason as a `[[decision]]` row (A1a's form: `id`, `outcome`, `reason`, `sources`), and the landing repeats it. K-VINTAGE holds either way. **`books/statement-10k2000.toml` and `books/statement-10q2001q3.toml`** (E-T-02): one period `FY2000`; one `Original` intent per book, effective 2000-12-31, with one leg per printed line of the 2000-12-31 balance sheet (`BS10K-*` / `BS10Q-*`, E2d): assets debit, liabilities and equity credit, contra lines on the side the filing prints them; amounts at $M under `scale{10^6}`; evidence the filing's stub. If the printed lines do not balance per unit, A1b's loader refuses the intent and E1's notes record the missing line. The printed totals are never posted. **`books/native.toml` additions for E-T-03** (E3's book): a Restatement `[[case]]` with Δ intents `delta-NFS1` and `delta-NFS2e`, derived by `negate` from E3's `NFS1` and `NFS2e` (Dr shareholders' equity / Cr notes receivable, 172,000,000.00 and 828,000,000.00; Powers p.126: "a reduction of $1 billion ($172 million plus $828 million)"), each `restates` its target, `reason = "WrongAccount"` (`registries/reason_codes.toml:65-66`; this round's proposed default, with its rationale), evidence the restating filing's stub. The case's `--periods` must cover every period whose Δ the T reads (2000Q4, 2001Q1, 2001Q2) and the periods the Δs post into (2000Q2, 2001Q1), each Closed or Locked; confirm at authoring that `fa case diff --statements` emits a diff for a case period with no Δ entry. **`[[case]]` rows** (all books): `kind = "Restatement"` (or Revision per the decision), `periods`, `determined_on` = the declared default, the restating filing's date (§2.6; §7.1 has no Item 4.02 8-K row), read from E1's `filed_on`: 2001-11-08 for `enr-8k` (SRC-ENR-002) and 2001-11-19 for `enr-10q` (SRC-ENR-003); `enr-raptor`'s restating filing is the 10-Q (this round's declared default, with its rationale: E-T-03's `published` cells are Note 3's `N3-RAPTOR-*`, and the 10-Q is the later vintage that prints the line, with the 8-K's equal cells named in `vintages`), so its `determined_on` is 2001-11-19; `authority` = the restating filing's stub, `disclosure` = a `Disclosure`-kind stub of it (reviewed by `case-second-reader`; its unreviewed twin is refused `FA-REF-179`), `approvers` = two `case-approver-*` labels with no shared session lineage (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:3450`), `poster` = a non-approver. **Expectations (§7.2; `[[expectation]]` + one `[[target]]` per cell, target = the published fact):** | id | variant | cells (target facts, E2d/E2b) | read | published (examples from the plan) | assurance | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | E-T-01 `bridge` (10-Q vintage) | statement-bridge | 15: net income FY1998, FY1999, FY2000; total assets, debt, equity FY1997–FY2000 (`N3--B-`) | `fa case diff --statements --certify` after column (NI on `net_income`, TA on `assets`, equity on `total_equity`); debt by `fa gl detail --account --from --to --certify`, its closing stock (`fa explain balance --period` reads one period's cells, Notes) | FY1999: NI 635, TA 33,272, equity 8,724 ($M) | `filer_unaudited` | | E-T-04 `bridge` (8-K vintage) | statement-bridge | 3: FY1999 NI, TA, equity (`8K--B-FY1999`) | the same lines with `--as-reported-in C:<8-K issuance certificate>` | 643 / 33,199 / 8,736 | `filer_unaudited`; rendered "AS REPORTED IN the 8-K of 2001-11-08", explicitly superseded 11 days later | | E-T-02 `footing` | statement-10k2000, statement-10q2001q3 | per book, the printed totals (`BS10K-TOTAL-ASSETS`, `BS10K-TOTAL-LE`, and `-TOTAL-LIAB` if printed; likewise `BS10Q-*`) | `fa statement balance-sheet --for FY2000 --certify`: `assets`, `liabilities`, `liabilities_and_equity` | the printed totals | per vintage: `filer_audited` (10-K), `filer_unaudited` (10-Q pp.5–6) | | E-T-03 `delta` | native | 6: the "Raptor equity adjustment" on `assets` and `total_equity` at 2000Q4, 2001Q1, 2001Q2 (`N3-RAPTOR-*`, with `8K-RAPTOR-*` named in `vintages`) | `fa case diff --statements --certify`, the `delta` column | −172 / −1,000 / −1,000 ($M) | `filer_unaudited` | | E-R-01 (10-Q vintage), E-R-02 (8-K vintage) | statement-bridge | each E-T-01 / E-T-04 cell whose Δ ≠ 0 | `--as-originally-reported` after each case | the posted A | R, never T | - **Not T** (recorded with reasons, no row): 1997 net income (the FY2000 10-K gives only "income before cumulative effect"); every 2001Q1 and 2001Q2 cell of Note 3 (their A needs the Q1/Q2-2001 10-Qs, E5). - **E-T-02.** T on the totals only. A per-line A→B bridge is T only where the 10-Q prints Δ separately; a Δ derived as B − A is a derivation tautology and renders R. - **E-T-03.** K-VINTAGE names the Δ accessions `0000950129-01-503835` and `0000950129-01-504218`; there is no A or B (§5.3). The equity/contra-equity mapping is the interpretive `role_map` rule, named in the claim. The published Δ line is compared, never posted. - **K-VINTAGE (§10.4).** FY1999 A has two printed vintages (the FY2000 10-K comparatives and the FY1999 EX-27); each T names the one its A posting uses, and the 8-K's A (893) is the EX-27's. K-VINTAGE orders the restating vintages by E1's source rows: SRC-ENR-002 (`filed_on = "2001-11-08"`) and SRC-ENR-003 (`filed_on = "2001-11-19"`) each `restates` SRC-ENR-008 and SRC-ENR-402, and the 10-Q is the later one. So E-T-01 reads the latest vintage on the bridge book's current state, and E-T-04, whose 8-K cells differ from the 10-Q's on asserted cells (H-021: 20 of 30), must read with the explicit `AS REPORTED IN` selector (`--as-reported-in C:<8-K issuance certificate>`). - A read on a line where Δ = 0 is flagged "selector not exercised" (§3.7). **Pipeline (§3.3 steps 4, 5, 7):** issue before bitemporal reads (`fa statement balance-sheet --for

--certify`; `fa statement issue --certificate C: --for

--issued-to sec --document --dry-run`; `fa approve --proposal --as `; `fa statement issue --plan --approval `; then close or lock — `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` reads the first StatementIssuance, else the first Lock, else refuses `FA-REF-161`); the Restatement lifecycle (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs:4524-4733`): `fa case open` with the verified authority stub and `--determined-on`, the Δs planned in a scenario (`fa scenario run`, `fa scenario diff --certificate-out`), `fa case rehearse`, `fa case approve --dry-run`, two Human approvals by non-planners, `fa case approve`, `fa case post` by a non-approver; each Δ names the posting it `restates` (`crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2503-2512`), and Restatement is admitted only in Closed or Locked periods, as `with:restate,2` (`registries/admissibility.toml:380-401`: Closed at `:392-396`, Locked at `:397-401`; the plan cites `:381-397`, which stops before the Locked cell); after the post, `fa case diff --statements --certify`, `fa explain lineage ` naming the Restates edge, `fa case disclose --document `, `fa case close`, and `fa case show --json` reporting Closed with the determination day: the runner-generated R row `E-CASE-` for each of `enr-8k`, `enr-10q` and `enr-raptor` (A7b; requires A7b to generate the `-CASE-` row, which §3.3 step 5 assigns to it). Its harness-only twin `fa case disclose` with the unreviewed Disclosure stub is refused `FA-REF-179` (exit 3, `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:1112`). **Witnesses and outsider checks.** - **Contributing-entry witness (A11b, §3.7 item 2).** `fa explain balance --period --certify --json` reads one period's register cells, so a stock line (total assets, debt, equity) is explained in every period q from FY1997 through the T's period and a flow line (net income) in that period alone: the union of the contributions is exactly the predicate's input postings (the A and Δ intents of those periods), none carries B, and they re-add to the certified value. Requires A11b's leaf-account path to read every period up to the T's for a stock read (it reads the T's period only). A line that selects more than 8 accounts uses `fa statement trace --certify` (`--from-diff C:` for bridges, `--definition … --before --after ` for footing), with `fa explain balance --certify` over every leaf account and `fa_reference::statements::render` recomputing the line. Any failure re-types the T as R. - **Kernel-attested bridges** (§5.3, §3.7 item 4; §5.3 admits bridges "whose A and Δ sit on one leaf account in one period"): on the bridge book, total assets and debt at FY1997 only. `fa assert-balance --period

` evaluates the (account, unit, period, entity) register cell, the net of that period's entries (`crates/fa-registers/src/entity.rs:237-240`, `:596-616`), and FY1998–FY2000 post period-over-period differences, so their cells hold the year's change, not B. `fa assert-balance --account --period

--balance " USD" --evidence ` (`registries/verbs.toml:487-497`) records a RegisterEquals attestation, and its twin, B ± 0.01, is refused `FA-REF-140` (exit 3). The equity and net-income lines span several accounts and are not kernel-attested. - **Outsider check (A12, §12.1)**, for each T read from a BS or IS certificate: `fa checkpoint create --grant witness`; `fa bundle produce --certificate `; `fa-verify bundle --key K --receipt R --json` and `fa-verify report --key K --checkpoint C --receipt R --json`, as literal argv through `fa_verify::cli::run` (`crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700`), both exit 0, and `report`'s recomputation of the line equals B; `fa replay ` is byte-identical (FA-INV-11). E-T-01's total-assets, net-income and equity cells are read from the case diff's `after` column, a statement-diff certificate, so their `report` check runs on the balance-sheet or income-statement certificate of the same line and period read after the case (`fa statement balance-sheet|income-statement --for

--certify`, whose line must equal the `after` column, a logged equality); without that read, `outsider=report:verified` on their lines would name a check that never ran on them. E-T-03's statement-diff certificate replays its own way (as E-T-01's case-diff certificates also do, `fa replay`), and so do the debt cells' `gl detail` certificates (A12's item 2: `fa replay`, plus an account bundle `fa bundle produce --account --from … --to … --balance :USD:` verified by `fa_verify::verify_bundle`). - **ADS extract**, per `statement` variant: `fa export ads --period

--out

--with-proofs`, then `fa-verify ads --key K`, rendered "an ADS-shaped GL extract (column set not yet the published standard, fa-ipom), verified complete by `fa-verify ads`". - **Append-only witness title: [cases] E5: Research: sourced Enron deal-level party postings (CFO-LJM1 edge, Cuiaba, Talon) and the Q1/Q2-2001 10-Qs; decision record if insufficient
description:
## Why
"A graph D on Enron exists only if the case sources deal-level postings with party legs" (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §7.2). The graph procedures need posted party flows, not bare ownership edges. E5 is the bounded research that decides whether the public record supports them; E6 (E-N-02, E-D-02, E-N-03) runs only if it does.

E5 also looks for the Q1/Q2-2001 10-Qs, the A side that E-T-01's 1Q01 and 2Q01 cells lack: "1Q/2Q-2001 A needs the Q1/Q2-2001 10-Qs" (§7.2).

Claim types served: D and N (E6), and T (a possible extension of E-T-01). It closes with a decision record if the record is insufficient (§15), so that no expectation rests on an unanchored deal.

## What to build
**For each candidate (§7.2), decide "anchored" or "not anchored"** at the precision the code reads, with SRC-ENR-005 page anchors and receipts (`python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify enron`):
- **The CFO→LJM1 edge.** A `CONTROLS` or `RELATED_TO` edge from the role-labelled CFO party to LJM1, with its valid-from date (Powers).
  - It is posted with `party relate <from> <to> --kind controls|related --basis <code> --valid-from YYYY-MM-DD` (`registries/verbs.toml:832`; `crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:23`); the basis is a `registries/relationship_bases.toml` code.
  - `graph.related_party_exposure` evaluates relationships at each posting's effective date (`related_as_of(root_vid, eff, max_depth)`, `crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:1549`, `:1555` at 8196f5e40), from every registered legal entity and party root. `related_as_of` (`crates/fa-journal/src/rea.rs:180-238`) walks active `[valid_from, valid_to)` edges in both directions and never returns the root itself, so LJM1 is "related" only through the CFO edge: the valid-from must be on or before the posting it would cite.
  - What an anchored edge licenses (E6 authors the rows): the §3.2a `[[party]]` rows `P-CFO` (`label = "enron-cfo-1"`, E2c's `roles.toml` role label, K-NAMES) and `P-LJM1` (`label = "LJM1-ENT"`, E2c's entity-name fact), `relations = ["<controls|related>:P-LJM1;basis=<code>;valid_from=<YYYY-MM-DD>"]` on `P-CFO` (A1b's token: the kind as Powers's words support it, `basis` E6's declared interpretive choice, `valid_from` the fact value). The decision row records the relation kind and the fact that carries the valid-from.
- **The Cuiaba sale** (1999-09-30, $11.3M; E2c's `CUI1`) with an LJM1 party leg (the leg `party = "P-LJM1"`; LJM1 is the sale's counterparty, so no separate counterparty party exists), plus the repurchase if Powers states its date and amount. E-N-03 needs the repurchase's date relative to `graph.party_circular_flows`' `window_days` (default 14, `registries/procedures.toml:1167` at 8196f5e40) and its amount relative to `min_retention_bps` (7000: the twin can report only if the repurchase retains at least 70% of the sale).
- **Talon** ($172M) and the other deal-level party postings Powers names.
- **Optional: `lookback.preferences`' 365-day insider window** (`procedures.toml:1564-1604`), only if the payment and the petition date are sourced, and then as a branch over the obligation date.
- **The Q1/Q2-2001 10-Qs.** Find their EDGAR accessions and captures, and record whether they print the A values Note 3's 1Q01/2Q01 cells need. If they exist, add `sources.toml` rows (`OK`, or `BLOCKED` with A1a's `status_reason`) with every §4.1 field, including `filed_on` (recorded at fetch from the filing's header, never guessed), `restates = []` (each is an as-filed vintage; SRC-ENR-002 and SRC-ENR-003, which both restate 1Q01 and 2Q01 among §7.2's six periods, would then list them in their own `restates`, E1's rows, and E1's `enron_sources_vintage_order` lock is updated to the new lists in the same landing) and, on an `OK` row, `assurance` with its receipted `assurance_fact` (the filing's own review report or legend, as for E1's filer rows; never assumed, §2.2), and record the follow-up that would turn those cells into E-T-01 bridges.

**Output: the decision record**, as `[[decision]]` rows in `crates/fa-oracles/cases/enron/case.toml` (the same file that holds E4's vintage decision; this round's proposal for a checkable record, which A1a's `case.toml` loader accepts once E5 declares its extra keys in `CASE_EXTENSIONS`, Notes):
- one row per candidate: `id` (`E5-cfo-ljm1`, `E5-cuiaba-sale`, `E5-cuiaba-repurchase`, `E5-talon`, `E5-other-deals`, `E5-preference-window`, `E5-10q-2001q1`, `E5-10q-2001q2`), `outcome` (`anchored` | `not_anchored`), `facts` (the receipted fact ids, when anchored) or `reason` (why not, when not), and `sources` (the source rows it read; A1a's `[[decision]]` fields);
- one summary row `E5-outcome` with one flag per E6 expectation, each conditional on its own anchoring (§7.2: "Its candidate facts and expectations, each conditional on anchoring"): `runs_E-N-02` (the Cuiaba sale is anchored), `runs_E-D-02` (the sale with an LJM1 party leg and the CFO→LJM1 edge with a valid-from on or before 1999-09-30), `runs_E-N-03` (the sale and the repurchase anchored with dates and amounts, LJM1 the counterparty of both, the repurchase dated after 1999-10-14 and of at least 7,910,000.00 USD, below; the CFO edge is not needed, because `graph.party_circular_flows` walks the party-level PAID projection, `crates/fa-lantern/src/projection.rs:185`, not REA relationships); and `native_calendar_from` (`1999Q3` if the Cuiaba postings are sourced, else `2000Q1`, §7.2a). E6 runs if any flag is true. The two `runs_E-N-03` thresholds are `graph.party_circular_flows`' registered defaults (`registries/procedures.toml:1164-1180` at 8196f5e40): a closing transfer counts only within `window_days` (14) civil days of the cycle's first transfer, so a repurchase on or before 1999-10-14 would be reported and there would be no N; and the cycle's bottleneck must retain `min_retention_bps` (7000) of the first hop, so a repurchase below 7,910,000.00 USD (70% of 11,300,000.00) leaves the twin unable to report, a vacuous N (E6).

Anchored candidates become `[[fact]]` rows in `facts.toml` with receipts (`alignment = "sentence"` for Powers's page anchors, `"value"` for a 10-Q table cell; the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok` true; `values_sha256` binding the date, amount and scope; `original_hash_compared` copied from the source row); the bead records the same outcome in a comment. If every flag is false, E6 does not run and closes with this record.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
```
python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify enron; rc=$?
cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_enron -- enron_e5_
```
**Expected output.** `verify` exits 0 with one `VERIFY <fact> PASS` line per adopted fact and no `FAIL ` line (author plus independent second reader with a second cache, §4.5); exit 1 with `FAIL ` lines on a failure, exit 4 with `UNRUN ` lines when `pdftotext` or the network is missing (A9), never read as success. Once A10a runs: `CHECK enron K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>` and likewise K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR, with every E5 fact among the examined rows.

**Load-time tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_enron.rs`:**
- `enron_e5_decision_record_complete`: every candidate above has exactly one `[[decision]]` row with an `outcome`; an `anchored` row's `facts` all exist in `facts.toml` as `sourced` facts with receipts; a `not_anchored` row has a non-empty `reason` and no synthetic fact stands in for it. A copy that deletes one row, or marks a candidate `anchored` whose fact has no receipt, fails naming the row.
- `enron_e5_flags_follow_the_facts`: each `E5-outcome` value equals its condition recomputed from the anchored facts: `runs_E-N-02` iff `E5-cuiaba-sale` is anchored; `runs_E-D-02` iff the sale and `E5-cfo-ljm1` are anchored and `CFO-LJM1`'s valid-from value is on or before 1999-09-30 (an edge is active on a day when `day >= valid_from`, `crates/fa-model/src/rea.rs:588-590`); `runs_E-N-03` iff the sale and `E5-cuiaba-repurchase` are anchored, `CUI2`'s date is after 1999-10-14 and its amount is at least 7,910,000.00 USD; `native_calendar_from` is `1999Q3` iff the sale is anchored, else `2000Q1`. A `month_literal` value counts by its last day for the valid-from and by its first day for the repurchase, so every day of the month meets the condition. ISO dates compare as strings and amounts as i128 at USD's scale 2, so the test needs only A1a's loader. A copy that flips one flag fails, naming it.
- `enron_e5_calendar_matches_decision` (lands with E6, Notes): `native_calendar_from` equals the first `[[period]]` label of `books/native.toml`; a copy that disagrees fails.
- `enron_e5_e6_rows_match_decision` (lands with E6, Notes): each of E-N-02, E-D-02 and E-N-03 exists in `expectations.toml` (and in `case.toml` `claims`) if and only if its `runs_<id>` flag is true, and `books/native.toml` carries the `[[party]]` rows `P-CFO`/`P-LJM1`, the CFO relation and the `party = "P-LJM1"` legs only where a true flag needs them (E-D-02: both parties and the relation; E-N-03: `P-LJM1` on `CUI1` and `CUI2`); a copy with a row or a party whose flag is false fails, naming it.

**Authoring-time negative** (needs the cache): a candidate whose amount or date is not literal in its quote, tried as a sourced fact on a test copy, makes `verify` print a `FAIL ` line and exit non-zero; it is recorded `not_anchored` with that reason, never admitted as a fact or filled with a synthetic value. The author records the output in the landing.

**Logging.** The decision record is a reviewable artifact; it adds no runner row and no JSONL record.

## Notes
- **Edge.** ← E2c: the SPE relationship and deal facts already anchored.
- **Owner decisions.** OD 2a and OD 3 gate quote text.
- **Calendar (§7.2a).** The `native` calendar is quarters 2000Q1–2001Q3, "extended back to 1999Q3 if E5 sources the Cuiaba postings (1999-09-30)". So this item's decision record states whether the Cuiaba postings are sourced and, therefore, whether the native book extends to 1999Q3; E6 applies the extension as declared book context. No E3 row waits on Cuiaba since E-N-02 moved to E6 (§7.2).

They are specified here and land with E6 (E6 ← E5), whether E6 adds rows or closes with this record, never as `#[ignore]`.
- **Precedent.** The research record has contained anchor errors (Appendix Z.3). No candidate becomes a fact without a receipt.

A1a's loader accepts `[[decision]]` rows (`id`, `outcome`, `facts`, `sources`, `reason`) but refuses an undeclared key (`UnknownField`), so E5 declares its decision keys (`runs_E-N-02`, `runs_E-D-02`, `runs_E-N-03`, `native_calendar_from`) in the `enron` row of `CASE_EXTENSIONS` (`crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/header.rs`; A1a: the item that introduces a key declares it). A1b's `[[party]]` row (`id`, `label`, `kind`, `relations`) carries each relation's details in its token, `<kind>:<party id>;basis=<code>;valid_from=<date>` (A1b folded round 2's `[[party_relation]]` table into it).

title: [cases] E6: E-N-02 SPE-posting N, E-D-02 graph.related_party_exposure on Cuiaba, E-N-03 windowed graph.party_circular_flows N (if E5 succeeds)
description:
## Why
This item is the graph half and the N result of the Enron SPE strand (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §7.2), with claim types D and N. It is conditional: each row runs only if E5 sources the postings it needs.

- **E-N-02** is the SPE-strand N: the strand's defects are "concealed side deals and backdated documents attached to booked, documented transactions, for example Cuiaba, $11.3M, 1999-09-30. No refusal or named D procedure applies". Its target is a sourced SPE posting such as the Cuiaba sale, which needs E5's sourcing and the calendar extension to 1999Q3, so it is delivered here, not in E3 (§7.2).
- **E-D-02** is a D on a graph procedure (tier G).
- **E-N-03** is an N that renders in Limits as "a related-party round trip spread over two years escapes a windowed cycle detector". A case study that shows only what fires is marketing; showing what does not fire is evidence (§0.3).

Both graph procedures are registered and implemented at 8196f5e40 (`graph.party_circular_flows`: `registries/procedures.toml:1155`, `crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:646`; `graph.related_party_exposure`: `:1295`, `graph.rs:1470`; §15 E6 cites only the first pair).

## What to build
**Files.** Additions to `crates/fa-oracles/cases/enron/books/native.toml` and `expectations.toml`, E6's tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_enron.rs`, and `enron_neg_e6_*` in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`. E5's two cross-file tests, `enron_e5_calendar_matches_decision` and `enron_e5_e6_rows_match_decision` (specified in E5), also land here: they compare E5's record with this item's native extension and rows through A1b's and A1c's loaders, which are not upstream of E5, so they land with E6 whether it adds rows or closes with E5's record and none. Each expectation lands only if its E5 flag (`runs_E-N-02`, `runs_E-D-02`, `runs_E-N-03` in `case.toml`'s `E5-outcome` row) is true.

**`books/native.toml` additions** (§7.2a: "(if E5 succeeds) the Cuiaba postings with party legs"):
- `[[period]]` labels `1999Q3` and `1999Q4` before `2000Q1` (the calendar "extended back to 1999Q3", as declared book context following E5's `native_calendar_from`), `fiscal_year = 1999`, each created (`fa period create --fiscal-year 1999`) and opened, with the opening date moved before 1999-07-01.
- `[[party]]` rows (§3.2a: `id`, `label`, `kind`, `relations`), created by the runner with `fa party add <party.json>` and `fa party relate` (`crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:23`; usage `registries/verbs.toml:832`):
  - `P-CFO`: `label = "enron-cfo-1"`, the CFO's `roles.toml` role label that E2c's `[[role]]` row fixes (style `<role>-<n>`, K-NAMES), `kind = "Employee"` (a declared default: an officer of the company), `relations = ["<controls|related>:P-LJM1;basis=<code>;valid_from=<CFO-LJM1's date>"]` (A1b's token) with the kind E5's `E5-cfo-ljm1` row records;
  - `P-LJM1`: `label = "LJM1-ENT"`, E2c's sourced entity-name fact for LJM1 (the counterparty `CUI1`'s quote names), `kind = "Counterparty"` (a declared default chosen so the kind does not presuppose the relatedness E-D-02 tests: the procedure reads REA relationships and leg party dimensions, never the party kind, `crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:1525-1559`), `relations = []`. LJM1 is also Cuiaba's counterparty, so no third party exists;
  - the relation's dated details, carried in its `relations` token (A1b: `<kind>:<party id>;basis=<code>;valid_from=<YYYY-MM-DD>`, optional `;valid_to=` and `;pct=`): `basis` (a `registries/relationship_bases.toml` code, e.g. `contractual_management` or `executive_officer_or_director`: E6's declared interpretive choice, named in E-D-02's claim), `valid_from` = the value of `CFO-LJM1` (E2c), `valid_to` empty, no `pct`; posted as `fa party relate P-CFO P-LJM1 --kind <controls|related> --basis <code> --valid-from <date>`. A1b's loader checks the token's party, its `basis` against `registries/relationship_bases.toml` and the presence of `valid_from`;
- `[[intent]] CUI1` (fact `CUI1`): class Original, effective 1999-09-30 (the sourced sale date, also 1999Q3's last day), evidence a reviewed reconstruction placeholder (`placeholder_reviewed`; K-EVID), legs under `one_leg_per_named_account` (declared accounts): `[[leg]]` 1 Dr receivable 11,300,000.00 USD with `party = "P-LJM1"` (`party_and_dimension_values`, a declared encoding; `amount_rule = "value:CUI1#<ordinal>"`, sourced, stated to $0.1M) / `[[leg]]` 2 Cr the Cuiaba interest 11,300,000.00 USD with `party` empty. In the PAID projection a flow runs from the credit leg's node to the debit leg's (`crates/fa-lantern/src/projection.rs:175-184`), so the sale is book → LJM1;
- `[[intent]] CUI2` (fact `CUI2`), the repurchase, only if E5 anchors its date and amount: Dr the Cuiaba interest / Cr payable with `party = "P-LJM1"`, so its flow is LJM1 → book and the pair is a two-node cycle.

**E-N-02** (`type = "N"`, `kind = "no_refusal"`, target `CUI1`, `basis = ["CUI1", "SPE-DEF<n>"]`).
- The plan fixes the target only; this round proposes the kind and twin, mirroring E-N-01, and the author fixes them at authoring (§5.2 requires kind, mechanism and twin). `CUI1` is admitted in an Open 1999Q3.
- **Mechanism.** The kernel reads legs, class, period, approvals and the presence and kind of evidence, never a side agreement or a document's true date: the evidence minimum checks presence and kind, not content (`registries/evidence_policy.toml:166-212`; H4). The author confirms the anchor at the pinned commit.
- **Twin: harness-observability**, as E-N-01 (A1c: `twin_kind = "harness_observability"`, `twin_attribute = "period_state_at_commit"`, `twin_value = "Closed"`, `twin_expect = "refuses FA-REF-010"`): the same intent posted on a twin book where 1999Q3 has been soft-closed and closed must be refused `FA-REF-010` (exit 7, `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:102`, `safety`). It shows the harness observes refusals of this intent shape; it does not show a law would fire on concealment. The rendering says so.

**E-D-02** (`type = "D"`, `procedure = "graph.related_party_exposure"`, `version = 2`, target `CUI1`, `basis = ["CUI1", "CFO-LJM1"]`, `known_at = "pre_case"`).
- Tier G; claim `statistical`; calibration `planted`; `max_depth` default 4 (`registries/procedures.toml:1295-1307` at 8196f5e40).
- Predicate: a valid-time traversal of OWNS, CONTROLS and RELATED_TO edges (`ReaSnapshot::related_as_of`, called from every legal-entity and party root at the posting's effective date, `crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:1549`, `:1555`; it walks active `[valid_from, valid_to)` edges in both directions and never returns its root, `crates/fa-journal/src/rea.rs:180-238`, so `P-LJM1` is reached only from `P-CFO` through the relation, which is what `enron_neg_e6_valid_from_after_sale` turns off; fnx `bfs_layers_directed` with a CGSE witness), intersected with live postings carrying a reached party or legal-entity dimension. Each affected posting is cited with the reached party (`Cite::Entry`, `Cite::Principal`, `graph.rs:1589-1591`), at constant severity High (`:1595`), with statistic `related_party_exposure_mantissa` = the posting's debit volume in its entity and unit (`:1597`).
- Components: cite Sd (the sourced counterparty under the declared party-leg encoding), severity S (High), statistic Sd = 11,300,000.00 under the declared one-debit-leg encoding.
- Each tier-G D cell gets its own book (§3.3). Filler is component-disjoint (A6); the extremal variant carries same-scope volume of at least 10^3 × the target (§3.7); at least 2 runs.
- K-ERRRATE renders the `planted` clause: "exercised only on planted anomalies in tests; its false-positive rate on real books has not been estimated" (§5.6).
- After the run, `case-second-reader` records `fa finding review F:<vid> --action acknowledge --note <template> --evidence D:<CUI1 stub>` (the cite is Sd), then `fa engagement file <id> --finding <vid>`; R check: the finding carries exactly one review, whose evidence is `CUI1`'s stub (§2.7).

**E-N-03** (`type = "N"`, `kind = "no_finding"`, target the pair `CUI1` + `CUI2`, `procedure = "graph.party_circular_flows"`, `version = 1`; defaults `window_days` 14 (`procedures.toml:1165-1168`), `max_hops` 6, `min_retention_bps` 7000).
- The procedure does not report the sale/repurchase pair, because the closing transfer lies further from the first than `window_days`.
- **Mechanism:** the cycle search admits a closing transfer only when `(l.effective_date.0 - first.effective_date.0) <= window_days` (`crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:955`, and `:978` for intermediate hops). The procedure reads the party-level PAID projection, `crate::projection::party_flow_legs` (`crates/fa-lantern/src/projection.rs:185`), in which a leg naming no party is the book node (`BOOK_NODE`, `:156`), so the sale (book → LJM1) and the repurchase (LJM1 → book) form a two-node cycle.
- **Twin:** the repurchase's effective date moved to within 14 days after 1999-09-30 (a day from 1999-09-30 through 1999-10-14, in a period the twin book has open); the procedure must then report the pair (§3.7 item 3). A1c: `twin_kind = "mutation"`, `twin_attribute = "effective_date"` (on `CUI2`), `twin_value` = the moved date, `twin_expect = "reports"`; `[[target]]` rows `CUI1` and `CUI2`. The twin also needs the repurchase to retain at least `min_retention_bps` (7000) of the sale's 11,300,000.00 (`crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:959-961`, the closing transfer's retention test; `:978-983` tests intermediate hops, which a two-node cycle does not use). E5's `runs_E-N-03` flag already requires the sourced repurchase to be dated after 1999-10-14 (outside `window_days`, so the N holds on the sourced dates) and to be at least 7,910,000.00 USD (70% of 11,300,000.00, so the moved twin passes the retention test), recomputed by E5's `enron_e5_flags_follow_the_facts`. The twin's own run still checks feasibility: if it cannot report, E-N-03 is not admissible and E5's decision record is corrected.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
```
cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_enron -- enron_e6_
cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact enron
cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- enron_neg_e6_
```
**Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; the values below are what each field must contain; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `<target>/<cell>`; FAIL/UNRUN reasons in A7a's trailing `reason=` field):
```
PASS E-N-02 N native CUI1/default kind=no_refusal twin=harness_observability:refuses FA-REF-010 exit=7
PASS E-D-02 D native CUI1/default graph.related_party_exposure@2 cite=Sd:[CUI1,party:P-LJM1] severity=S:High statistic=Sd:related_party_exposure_mantissa=11300000.00
PASS E-N-03 N native CUI1/default graph.party_circular_flows@1 kind=no_finding twin=mutation:reports
PASS E-N-03 N native CUI2/default graph.party_circular_flows@1 kind=no_finding twin=mutation:reports
```
E-D-02's line repeats per filler variant (5 seeded, empty, extremal) and per run (≥ 2 book ids), all equal. Each row joins `case.toml` `claims` only when its E5 flag is true (`enron_e5_e6_rows_match_decision`); a claimed row whose witness is missing prints UNRUN and the `enron` test exits non-zero (A7a).

**Load-time tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_enron.rs`:**
- `enron_e6_native_extension_loads`: the extended `books/native.toml` loads, its first period equals E5's `native_calendar_from` (the equality E5's `enron_e5_calendar_matches_decision` owns, landed with this item, so this test reuses it rather than restating it), `CUI1` balances per unit, and the relationship's `--valid-from` equals `CFO-LJM1`'s sourced date.
- `enron_e6_valid_from_not_after_posting`: the sourced valid-from of `CFO-LJM1` is on or before `CUI1`'s 1999-09-30, so the edge is live at the posting's effective date; a copy with a later date fails the test, naming `CFO-LJM1`.

**Run-time planted negatives in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`** (case directory copied, one named edit, observable and non-zero case verdict asserted; committed files never edited):
- `enron_neg_e6_valid_from_after_sale`: the `P-CFO` → `P-LJM1` relation's `valid_from` moved after 1999-09-30 (a plain `run_planted` edit of the relation token, Notes) → `FAIL E-D-02 D native CUI1/default … reason=expected cite observed no_finding` (the edge is inactive at the posting's effective date and `related_as_of` never returns its root, so nothing else makes LJM1 related).
- `enron_neg_e6_party_leg_dropped`: `CUI1`'s `party = "P-LJM1"` removed → `FAIL E-D-02 D native CUI1/default … reason=expected cite observed no_finding` (no reached party dimension on the posting, `crates/fa-lantern/src/graph.rs:1539-1546`).
- `enron_neg_e6_twin_outside_window`: E-N-03's twin left outside `window_days` → `FAIL E-N-03 N native CUI1/default … reason=expected twin reported observed twin no_finding (vacuous N)`.
- `enron_neg_e6_twin_open_period`: E-N-02's twin posted with 1999Q3 still Open → `FAIL E-N-02 N native CUI1/default … reason=expected twin refused observed twin admitted (vacuous N)`.
- `enron_neg_e6_filler_reverses_target`: a test-only filler variant that breaks the discipline by reversing `CUI1` → the filler-invariance witness FAILs naming `graph.related_party_exposure` and the variant.

**JSONL run log (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord`/`VerdictRecord`).** Each record carries `record`, `case = "enron"`, `book_variant = "native"` and `binds` (`$CUI1`, `$CUI2` entry vids, `$DOC_<document id>`); `period create --fiscal-year 1999` and `period open` for 1999Q3/1999Q4 (the label → code map logged once per book); `party add` and `party relate` steps with their exits; the `CUI1`/`CUI2` posts; `procedure run` and `finding record` with `finding_procedure = "graph.related_party_exposure"` or `"graph.party_circular_flows"` and their `certificate_kind`; the `finding review` and `engagement file --finding` steps; twin steps with `book_variant = "native~twin"` (A11c's marker; never rendered); `filler_batch` steps per variant. D reads replay with `fa finding export --certificate C:<run> --export-format canonical --out <f>` then `fa finding replay <f> --certificate C:<run> --known-at <seq>` (§12.1, A12), each logged with its exit.

## Notes
- **Edges.**

  - ← A11a: filler invariance with the extremal variant.
