title: [cases] L1: Lehman sources, facts and receipts: Valukas p.889, fn 3365, App. 17; 10-Q Q2 2008 with review legend; Q1-2008 10-Q; FY2007 10-Qs BLOCKED
description:
## Why
Lehman Repo 105 (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §8) is the program's litigation-consultant but-for case (§12.3). It contributes statement footing, scenarios and dated aggregates (§18 item 4). Its facts are `dated_aggregate` granularity on irregular dates (§0.4, §2.3).

L1 lands the sources ledger and receipts that every Lehman row rests on:
- T: L-T-01;
- R: L-R-01, L-R-02 (the scenario diff's ±e, a read-back) and L-R-03 (the optional Canon backtest on `ledger`);
- C: L-C-01 (adjusted net leverage within Valukas's 0.1x display unit);
- N: L-N-01, L-N-02;
- D: L-D-01.

(An earlier draft had a scenario T "L-T-02" and a CF "L-T-02-CF-01"; the plan retypes them as L-R-02 + L-C-01 and L-R-03, §8.3.)

§15 has no separate Lehman facts item, and receipts are per sourced fact (§4.4). So L1 also authors the §8.2 sourced facts and the case's `roles.toml`. The source conflicts are carried as separate facts, not resolved, so that no expectation rests on a contested attribute (§17).

## What to build
Files, all under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/lehman/`: `sources.toml`, `facts.toml`, `roles.toml`, `receipts.toml` (generated), plus the load-time tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`. L2 creates `case.toml`; L2–L4 create the `books/` and `expectations.toml` files.

**`sources.toml`** (every §4.1 field: `id`, `title`, `publisher`, `original_url`, `archive_url?`, `retrieval_route`, `original_hash_compared`, `retrieved_utc`, `filed_on`, `restates`, `sha256`, `format`, `extraction`, `redistribution_basis`, `assertion_status`, `assurance` (with A1a's `assurance_fact`), `anchor_scheme`, `status` (A1a's `status_reason` for BLOCKED), `notes`; §8.1):
- **`filed_on` / `restates`** (K-VINTAGE orders vintages by them, §4.1, §3.6). `filed_on` is the filing or publication date read from each capture's own header at fetch (the plan gives none for Lehman; never guessed): the Q2-2008 10-Q, the Q1-2008 10-Q, the BLOCKED FY2007 10-Qs (from the EDGAR index entry the 404 capture was looked up by; empty if unknown, with the reason in `status_reason`), and the Valukas report's publication date for SRC-LEH-001/-003. `restates` is `[]` for every Lehman row unless a later 10-Q labels a comparative column restated or "as adjusted"; then it names the earlier filing, and the comparative cell is a separate fact of the later vintage (K-VINTAGE then forces the later vintage on any T that reads that cell, e.g. a 2008-02-29 or 2007-11-30 line printed by both 10-Qs). Record what each filing says in `notes`.
- **SRC-LEH-001.** Valukas examiner report, Vol. 3: p.889 "Gross and Net Balance Sheet Ratios", p.734 fn 2854 (definitions), fn 3365 (printed p.874; the dated balances), pp.891 and 897. `investigative_finding` ("the examiner reported"). `anchor_scheme`: `page{printed page, line range}` for prose and footnotes, `table_cell{table, row label, column label}` for p.889, p.891 and p.897.
- **SRC-LEH-002.** LBHI 10-Q Q2 2008 (EDGAR `0001104659-08-045115`; Internet Archive capture, so `retrieval_route = archive_capture` and `original_hash_compared = false` until OD 1), printed pp.86 and 89.
  - `filer_reviewed`: the review legend reads "We have reviewed the consolidated statement of financial condition … as of May 31, 2008" (re-verify at authoring). `assurance` records "reviewed" with `assurance_fact = "Q208-LEGEND"` (A1a: the sourced fact whose sentence establishes it). The sentence itself is bound only by that fact's `quote_sha256` and is never written into `assurance`, because OD 2a gates committed quote text.
  - It renders "reported (reviewed; a review is not an audit)".
  - The assurance of its 2007-11-30 comparative column is determined from the filing, never assumed (§2.2). A source row has one `assurance`, so that column's assurance is recorded in `notes`, bound to the sourced fact whose sentence states it (proposed id `Q208-LEGEND-2007-11-30`), and carried into L-T-01's `assurance` for that date (L2).
  - `anchor_scheme`: `page{…}` for the legend, `table_cell{…}` for the statement of financial condition and the p.86/p.89 tables.
- **SRC-LEH-003.** Valukas Appendix 17: Repo 105 accounting-policy excerpts (p.8, p.3) and the §E table, pp.36–37 (56 dated observations). `investigative_finding`. `anchor_scheme`: `page{…}` for p.8/p.3, `table_cell{…}` for §E.
- **The Q1-2008 10-Q.** A new row, for a 2008-02-29 statement footing: `OK`, or `BLOCKED{reason}`. The plan assigns it no id; take the next free `SRC-LEH-NNN` and record it in the landing.
- **The FY2007 10-Qs.** Recorded `BLOCKED{reason}` (their captures returned 404, §8.1, §1.2), each with its own next free id, empty `sha256` and no `extraction`. No fact may cite them.
- **Capture check (§15 L1).** "Check that each capture prints a full condensed statement of financial condition." For SRC-LEH-002 the research corpus's text extraction (lines 284–290) shows 2008-05-31 and 2007-11-30 (§8.3). Record the result per filing and per date in the row's `notes` (L2 foots only the dates recorded as full).
- `redistribution_basis` from §4.1's closed set: SRC-LEH-002 (and the other 10-Qs) `public-record/sec-filing`; SRC-LEH-001/-003 `public-record/court` where the captured bytes are the court-filed report (determine at authoring and record the docket in `notes`; 11 U.S.C. §107(a) is a statement about access, not copyright, §1.3).

**`facts.toml`** (§8.2), one fact per sentence or table cell, each with `source`, `anchor_kind`, `anchor`, `quote_sha256`, `about_scope`, `granularity` and, for every `statement_line` fact, `cell` (A1a's vintage-independent `<line>@<date>` key, e.g. `total_assets@2008-05-31`, which K-VINTAGE compares across the two 10-Qs, A3b), with its values as `[[value]]` rows (A1a: `fact`, `ordinal`, `literal`, `rule`, `param`, `value`, `unit`, `precision`; §2.1's `values`) (§2.1, §2.3). Fact ids are this round's proposal (the plan names none): `V889-<row>-<date>`, `V891-…`, `V897-…`, `V734-FN2854-<n>`, `Q208-SFC-<line>-<date>`, `Q208-P86-<row>-<date>`, `Q208-P89-<row>-<date>`, `Q208-LEGEND`, `A17-P8-ENTRY`, `A17-P8-REPO108`, `A17-20080827-<supported|manual|combined>`. `<date>` is the column's quarter end (`2008-05-31`).
- **Anchor strings** (A1a's grammar): prose `p<printed page>:l<first>-<last>` (e.g. `p734:l…` for fn 2854, `p874:l…` for fn 3365's sentences), table cells `<table>|<row label>|<column label>` with the table, row and column labels read from the receipted extraction (e.g. `p889|(b) Net assets|<column header>`).
- **Value-bound table cells.** Every cell of p.889, p.891, p.897, the 10-Q tables and §E is `anchor_kind = table_cell` and binds by exact cell value, not by sentence alignment (§4.1, as amended after polish round 1); its receipt has `alignment = "value"`. The cell's printed literal (for example `327,774`) is a literal value and is committed with the fact (§1.3, §4.2). Its `[[value]]` row (A1a) reads that literal under A2's literal rule `scale{multiplier}`, the way §2.1 writes "$560 million" and W2 and E2d write their $M cells: `literal = "327,774"`, `rule = "scale"`, `param = 6`, `value = "32777400000000"` (327,774,000,000.00 USD as A1a's integer string at USD's scale 2), `unit = "USD"`, `precision = 6` ("stated to $1M"). A book leg posts that value directly with A1b's `amount_rule = "value:<cell fact>#1"`, so no separate dollar fact exists. Each $M table's unit caption is its own sourced fact (`<table>-UNITS`, e.g. `V889-UNITS`, `Q208-P86-UNITS`; bind its wording at authoring). No foundation check ties a `scale` row's `param` to another fact (A2's rule reads only the row's own `literal` and `param`, as E2d notes), so the case test `lehman_scale_param_matches_its_table_caption` checks that every $M cell has `param = 6` and that the table its anchor names has a caption fact.
- **Prose facts** (the review legend, p.734 fn 2854's definitions, Appendix 17 p.8's entry form and Repo 108 sentence, p.3, the 2008-08-27 "manual addition" sentence) are `page` anchored and sentence-aligned (receipt `alignment = "sentence"`). Until OD 2a they carry only `quote_sha256` and the anchor: the author computes `quote_sha256` from the normalized sentence-aligned span at authoring, and `verify` enumerates the sentence-aligned spans at the anchor and selects the one span whose SHA-256 matches; zero or several matches is a FAIL (§4.4).
- **Valukas p.889.** Seven quarter ends from 2006-11-30 to 2008-05-31, one `table_cell` fact per printed cell (granularity `statement_line` for (a)–(d) and the ratio rows, `dated_aggregate` for (e)):
  - (a) total assets;
  - three deductions: segregated cash, collateralized lending agreements, identifiable intangibles;
  - (b) net assets, (c) stockholders' equity, (d) tangible equity capital;
  - (e) Repo 105/108 usage;
  - the reported and adjusted ratio rows and the two percentage rows.

  Values ($M), in the order the plan quotes them: (b) = 327,774 / 396,673 / 372,959 / 357,102 / 337,667 / 300,797 / 268,936; (e) = 50,383 / 49,102 / 38,634 / … (the plan gives only the first three). The plan does not pair these with dates: bind each value to its column's quarter end from the receipted table at authoring, never by assuming the column order.
  - The research recomputed all 49 cells. The additive lines close exactly; the 4 ratio rows match at 0.1x and the 2 percentage rows at 1%. Those are display-precision agreements (C), not exact equalities, and no expectation here asserts them.
  - The ratio cells are facts with their printed display unit (0.1x) recorded in their `[[value]]` row (literal `13.9` → integer 139 tenths, precision "stated to 0.1x"; the subset parser accepts no floats, `crates/fa-registry/src/toml.rs:1-9`), because L-C-01 compares the harness's recomputed adjusted net leverage with Valukas's adjusted 13.9x within that unit (§8.3). Bind the 13.9x cell to its quarter end at authoring; the plan does not restate it.
- **p.734 fn 2854.** The definitions of (a)–(e) and the ratios, one fact per sentence (L2's derivation of (b) and (d) names them).
- **The 10-Q (pp.86, 89).** For 2008-05-31, 2008-02-29 and 2007-11-30:
  - total assets, deductions and net assets (p.86);
  - equity, junior subordinated notes (5,004 / 4,976 / 4,740), intangibles and tangible equity (p.89);
  - net leverage 12.06x / 15.44x / 16.14x (integers 1206 / 1544 / 1614 hundredths, precision "stated to 0.01x").

  The plan lists these values in the same order as the three dates; confirm each pairing against the column header at authoring.
  - Also every printed line of the condensed consolidated statement of financial condition at 2008-05-31 and 2007-11-30, one `Q208-SFC-<line>-<date>` fact per printed line and per printed total. These are L-T-01's posted lines and printed totals.
  - (e) is single-sourced (Valukas). The 10-Q never mentions Repo 105.
- **fn 3365.** 36 dated end-of-day balances on **irregular** dates (none between 2007-11-30 and 2008-01-29, nor between 2008-05-30 and 2008-07-14), each labelled "Repo 105 usage".
- **Appendix 17 §E.** 56 dated observations headed "Total Repo 105", whose quarter-end values equal p.891's combined 105/108 totals. So both series are combined 105/108, with no split.
- **The two dated series are whole tables** (OD 2b). Until OD 2b is decided they are fetched, extracted and verified in the author's cache, and their per-observation facts (`V874-FN3365-<date>`, `A17E-<date>`, one `table_cell` fact each) are not committed. Each series is still committed now as one series fact (proposed ids `V874-FN3365` and `A17E`: `sourced`, `granularity = "dated_aggregate"`, a `rows_file` that stays absent until OD 2b, and `quote_sha256` over its canonical rows, as M2a's complaint rows fact), so L3's and L4's expectations can name it in their `basis` and A7a prints them UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` from A1a's `rows_committed = false`; without it their basis and the `ledger` book would name facts that are not committed (A1c's foreign keys). Requires A1a to accept `rows_file` on a `dated_aggregate` fact: it admits it on `ledger_row` facts only. After OD 2b, they are committed as one fact per observation. The facts that summarize them (the irregular-dates sentence, the §E heading, the p.891 equality) and the quarter-end cell values other tables print (p.889, p.891, p.897) are cited literal values and are committed now (§1.3).
- **Run-time consequence (§3.2b).** Tests never read the cache (§4.3), so until OD 2b every expectation built on the dated series (L4's L-D-01 and L-N-02, L3's optional L-R-03) prints `UNRUN <id> … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS, and stays out of `case.toml` `claims` until the landing that commits the rows (A7a: an unclaimed row fails the case test only on FAIL). The extractor and the harness are built and tested on fixtures meanwhile.
- **Inconsistencies, carried as separate facts:**
  - Repo-105-only usage on p.891 versus p.897: Q3 2007 29,054 vs 29,075; Q4 2007 29,727 vs 29,916; Q1 2008 42,200 vs 41,844 (six `V891-repo105-<quarter>` / `V897-repo105-<quarter>` facts);
  - for 2008-08-27, Appendix 17 gives $17.847B (supported), $22.067B (with "a manual addition of $4.220 billion … There is no underlying support"), and $24.601B (the combined series): three facts.
- **Accounting form (Appendix 17 p.8, `A17-P8-ENTRY`).** "The re‐characterization entry is: Dr. Repo $100 / Dr. Long inventory‐derivative $5 / Cr. Inventory $105." This is a 3-leg entry (values 100, 5, 105). Repo 108 differs in collateral (equities) and haircut (8) (`A17-P8-REPO108`).
  - The quote's U+2010 hyphens are kept: normalization does no Unicode normalization (§4.4), so `quote_sha256` is computed over the typographic characters.

**`roles.toml`** (§2.8): only the harness labels the Lehman books use (`case-second-reader`, two `case-approver-*`, `examiner-witness`) and one reconstruction-principal label that uploads the stubs and posts every Lehman intent (L2's statement lines, L3's scenario, L4's native entry and ledger rows; Appendix 17 p.8 is a policy illustration, so no historical person is represented); the K-NAMES deny list as SHA-256 hashes of the normalized name tokens of every person the receipted extractions name, never in clear.

**`receipts.toml`.** Generated by `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch|extract|verify lehman` (A9), with the project User-Agent, at most 1 request per second, archive captures unless `FA_SEC_CONTACT` is set (OD 1). One `[[receipt]]` per committed sourced fact (§4.4): `source`, `fact`, `anchor`, `verified_utc` (the cache entry's fetch time), `tool_version`, `extraction_sha256`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (SHA-256 of the fact's canonical literal values and `about_scope`, so a value or scope edited after `verify` is detected offline by K-BIND), `alignment` (`sentence` for the `page`-anchored prose facts, `value` for every `table_cell` fact), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`, and `original_hash_compared` copied from the source's row (false for SRC-LEH-002's archive capture until OD 1; it is not a fifth binding boolean). Never hand-edited. The tool exits 0 when every fact verifies, 1 with `FAIL ` lines, 4 with `UNRUN ` lines when a system tool or the network is missing, and prints `VERIFY <fact> PASS` per verified fact (A9).

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
- Authoring: `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch lehman`, `… extract lehman`, `… verify lehman`. Expected: exit 0, no line starting `FAIL ` or `UNRUN`. Byte identity: copy `receipts.toml`, re-run `verify` on the unchanged cache, `cmp` the two (identical, because `verified_utc` is the fetch time). The second reader repeats `fetch|extract|verify` from a second `$FA_CASES_CACHE` (§4.5); its receipts agree with the author's on every field except `verified_utc`, which is each cache's own fetch time.
- Offline gate: `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` (A10a) and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_lehman`.

**Expected lines** (A3a/A10a own the format; the values below are what each field must contain): `CHECK lehman K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, `CHECK lehman K-BIND PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, `CHECK lehman K-SCOPE PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, `CHECK lehman K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, each with n > 0, where a check that reads a series fact's rows counts the two series facts (`V874-FN3365`, `A17E`) as unrun inputs and prints `examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=2 (OD 2b)` (A10a: an absent rows file is never examined and never a FAIL); `CHECK lehman K-DERIVE UNRUN examined=0/0` (L1 commits no derived fact; L2's `difference` facts are its first inputs, and A10a reports a check with no input rows UNRUN without failing the test); `SOURCE SRC-LEH-002 original_hash_compared=false route=archive_capture` (and one `SOURCE` line per other row); `EXCERPTS lehman facts_with_quote=0 words=0` before OD 2a. A check with no input rows prints UNRUN; one that examines fewer rows than its inputs is a FAIL. The receipts-consistency part prints no line of its own; a failure prints `FAIL` lines.

**Receipt checks** (offline, `ledgers_validate_offline`): every committed sourced fact has exactly one receipt; the receipt's `quote_sha256` and `anchor` equal the fact's; its `values_sha256` equals the hash of the fact's committed values and `about_scope`; `alignment` is `sentence` for prose facts and `value` for table cells; all four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) are true for every fact (for a table cell, `aligned` records value alignment: the quote is the whole printed cell, never a fragment); `original_hash_compared` equals the source row's value.

**Planted negatives** (load-time, each a named `#[test]` in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs` over an in-memory copy of the embedded case with one edit; the committed files are untouched; each asserts the refusal names the check, the fact id and its line):
- `lehman_v889_b_value_off_by_one_fails_k_bind`: the (b) cell printed `327,774` gets `value = "32777500000000"` (327,775 $M) while its literal stays `327,774` → K-BIND refuses (the value is not the literal under the literal rule).
- `lehman_v889_b_literal_and_value_edited_fails_receipt`: literal `327,775` and value `32777500000000` edited together → the recomputed `quote_sha256` and `values_sha256` no longer equal the receipt's → K-BIND refuses, naming the fact.
- `lehman_prose_value_edited_after_verify_fails_values_sha256`: `A17-P8-ENTRY`'s haircut value 5 edited to 6 (no quote text is committed, so only the receipt binds it) → K-BIND refuses with a `values_sha256` mismatch naming `A17-P8-ENTRY`. Before round 3 this edit was visible only to a re-run of `verify`.
- `lehman_scope_edited_after_verify_fails_values_sha256`: the review-legend fact's `about_scope` edited to name another quarter end than the May 31, 2008 one its sentence states → K-BIND refuses (`values_sha256` covers `about_scope`), naming the fact.
- `lehman_scale_param_edited_fails_k_bind`: a $M cell's `param` changed from 6 to 3 with its `value` unchanged → K-BIND refuses (the value is not the literal under its rule), naming the fact; with `value` re-scaled to match (`32777400000`), K-BIND still refuses through `values_sha256` (the receipt bound the original row).
- `lehman_scale_param_matches_its_table_caption` (over the committed facts) and its planted negative `lehman_scale_param_without_its_caption_fails`: a $M cell whose `param` is not 6, or whose anchor names a table with no `<table>-UNITS` fact → fails, naming the cell and its table.
- `lehman_ok_row_without_capture_is_refused`: a FY2007 10-Q row copied with `status = "OK"` and empty `sha256` → ledger well-formedness refuses the row.
- `lehman_fact_citing_blocked_row_is_refused`: a fact whose `source` is a FY2007 10-Q (`BLOCKED`) row → refused (facts cite only `OK` rows).
- `lehman_receipt_flipped_boolean_is_refused`: `scope_ok = false` on one receipt → refused.
- `lehman_original_hash_compared_mismatch_is_refused`: a receipt with `original_hash_compared = true` for SRC-LEH-002 (archive capture, row says false) → refused.
- `lehman_contested_facts_never_feed_an_expectation`: no Lehman expectation's basis, taken transitively, contains a `V891-repo105-*`, `V897-repo105-*` or `A17-20080827-*` fact (§17); a planted expectation citing `V891-repo105-<Q3 2007>` fails naming it. (Runs on whatever expectations exist; examined = 0 prints UNRUN until L2 lands rows.)
- `lehman_typographic_hyphen_is_not_folded`: on a synthetic string (no vendored quote text), normalization keeps U+2010, so its digest differs from the ASCII-hyphen variant's.

**Planted negatives at authoring** (observed by the tool, recorded in the landing with the command and its output; never committed):
- `A17-P8-ENTRY`'s `quote_sha256` recomputed from the ASCII-hyphen variant of the sentence → `verify lehman` finds zero matching spans at the anchor and prints a `FAIL ` line for that fact, exit non-zero.
- a (b) cell's literal edited by one digit → `verify` prints `FAIL ` (`values_in_quote` false), exit non-zero.
- `fetch` against an `OK` row whose capture does not exist prints a `FAIL ` line (or `UNRUN` with the network unavailable), never exit 0.

**Logging.** `case_fetch.py` prints `FAIL `/`UNRUN` lines at column 0; `receipts.toml` is the durable record. The case runner's JSONL log is not involved (tests never read the cache, §4.3). The validator reports the excerpt volume for the case (§4.2): zero quote words before OD 2a.

## Notes
- **Edge.** ← A9 (the tool).
- **Names.** Directory `crates/fa-oracles/cases/lehman/`; variants `native`, `statement`, `ledger` (plain kind stems, fixed this round); generated rows `L-SELF-<variant>` and `L-N-90` (the id prefix is the case letter, as §5.1's `<case>-NOTE-NN` is spelled `W-NOTE-01`).
- **Owner decisions.**
  - (OD 2b) gates committing the dated series as tables: fn 3365's 36 balances and Appendix 17 §E's 56 observations (§14 item 2b). Until it is decided, they stay in the cache, and the `ledger` book's rows (L4's L-D-01/L-N-02 and L3's optional L-R-03) cannot be committed, since tests never read the cache. OD 2b is a `related` link, not a blocking edge (§15 L1 "(OD 2b) for the dated series"). The p.889/p.891/p.897 and 10-Q cells are cited values, committed under §1.3, not whole tables.
  - OD 1 gates `original_hash_compared`; OD 2a gates quote text; OD 3 gates quote text with names.
- **Settled: table cells.** §4.1 says a `table_cell` fact binds by exact value, not sentence alignment, and its receipt records `alignment = "value"` with `aligned` meaning value alignment (§4.4 after round 2). This bead's reading is that a value-bound cell's quote is its printed literal, so committing the literal (a literal value, §4.2) lets K-BIND recompute `quote_sha256` offline (A3a: "Its quote is the cell's text or the fact's value"). If A9/A3a define a value-bound cell's `quote_sha256` differently, follow them; the value-edit negative stays observable through `values_sha256`.
- **Settled: values bound offline.** Round 2 flagged that a receipt carried no values, so a prose fact's value edited after `verify` was invisible offline. §4.4 now adds `values_sha256` (values and `about_scope`), so the two `…_fails_values_sha256` negatives above are offline load-time negatives; the authoring-time `verify` negatives are kept as well.
- **Foundation fields (re-checked at r4a).** A1a (Receipt type), A9 (writer) and A3a/A10a (K-BIND) now carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and the boolean `aligned` (round 2's `sentence_aligned` is gone), and A1a loads `filed_on`, `restates`, `assurance_fact` and `cell`. Still required: A1a to accept `rows_file` on a `dated_aggregate` series fact (above); and A1a/A2 to state how a unitless ratio `[[value]]` is written (13.9x as 139 tenths, 12.06x as 1206 hundredths), since A1a defines `value` at a unit's scale and gives an empty `unit` only for dates and periods, and A2 has no ratio literal rule. The $M cells need no new form: A2's `scale{multiplier}` literal rule gives their USD value (above; round 5 replaced the earlier separate `scale` dollar facts, which needed a two-input derived `scale` that A2 does not define and an `amount_rule` naming a derived fact that A1b does not define).
- **Not here.** The harness-derived (b), (d) and ratios (L2), the scenario (L3), the ledger rows (L4).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `sources.toml` carries SRC-LEH-001, -002 and -003, the Q1-2008 10-Q row (`OK` or `BLOCKED{reason}`) and the FY2007 10-Qs `BLOCKED`, each with every §4.1 field (including `filed_on`, read from the capture's header and never guessed, and `restates`, `[]` unless a later 10-Q labels a comparative column restated) and its `anchor_scheme`. The full-statement capture check is recorded per filing and date, and SRC-LEH-002's `assurance` names its review-legend fact (`assurance_fact = "Q208-LEGEND"`, A1a) without quoting the sentence (OD 2a).
- [ ] positive: every committed §8.2 sourced fact, including the carried inconsistencies as separate facts, has a receipt from the author and from an independent second reader with a second cache (agreeing on every field except `verified_utc`; a re-run on an unchanged cache is byte-identical): `alignment` = `sentence` for prose facts and `value` for table cells, all four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) true, `values_sha256` equal to the hash of the fact's committed values and scope, and `original_hash_compared` as copied from the source row (false on SRC-LEH-002's archive capture until OD 1). The adjusted-ratio cell L-C-01 reads (13.9x) carries its 0.1x display unit. Every `statement_line` fact carries A1a's `cell` key, and each dated series is committed as one series fact whose `rows_file` stays absent until OD 2b.
- [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` prints `CHECK lehman <K-ID> PASS examined=<n>/<n>` with n > 0 for K-PROV, K-BIND, K-SCOPE and K-ANCHOR (a check that reads the series facts' rows reports them `unrun=2 (OD 2b)`, A10a), and `CHECK lehman K-DERIVE UNRUN` until L2 commits the first derived fact; `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_lehman` passes.
- [ ] negative: a planted wrong (b) value fails K-BIND offline, a prose fact's value or `about_scope` edited after `verify` fails K-BIND offline through `values_sha256`, and an edited literal fails `verify` at authoring.
- [ ] negative: ASCII hyphens in the p.8 quote's hash fail `verify` (zero matching spans).
- [ ] negative: an `OK` row without a capture, a fact citing a `BLOCKED` row, a flipped receipt boolean, a mismatched `original_hash_compared` and an edited `scale` param (with or without its value re-scaled) are each refused by the named test, and a $M cell without its table's caption fact, or with `param` other than 6, fails `lehman_scale_param_matches_its_table_caption`.
- [ ] no-claim: receipts bind quotes and values to captured bytes, not to the EDGAR originals unless `original_hash_compared = true`. Carrying the Valukas inconsistencies is not resolving them, and nothing here judges Lehman's accounting. Until OD 2b, the dated series is not committed, so nothing here shows any ledger-book row runs.

title: [cases] L2: Lehman L-T-01 statement footing at 2008-05-31 and 2007-11-30, L-R-01 read-backs, and harness-derived (b), (d) and net leverage
description:
## Why L-T-01 is Lehman's T (claim type T; L-R-01 is R). H-014 is deferred with a narrowed scope (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §8.3). The statements surface certifies only two definitions, whose lines select whole account types, and formula lines are add/subtract only (§3.8). So: - the lines below type level (net assets (b), tangible equity (d), segregated cash) are per-account balances, and are R rows where they read back a posted value; - the harness derives (b), (d) and the ratios, and labels them harness-derived; - the T is the type-level footing. The footing reproduces the filer's own arithmetic on a reviewed statement. The rendering states that the review is not an audit (§2.2). ## What to build **Files** under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/lehman/`: `case.toml` (created here), `books/statement.toml`, and the L-T-01/L-R-01 rows of `expectations.toml`; the derivation function and its unit tests in `crates/fa-oracles` (tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`); the run-time negatives in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`. **`case.toml`** (§3.2, §3.2b, §12.2): `id = "lehman"` (the directory name), `letter = "L"` (prefixes every expectation and generated id: `L-T-01`, `L-SELF-statement`, `L-N-90`), `kind = "case"`, `title`, `version`, `scope`, the pinned commit `8196f5e40`, the variants `native`, `statement`, `ledger`, and `claims`, the completeness claim the runner enforces (A7a): L2 claims L-T-01 and L-R-01; L3 adds L-R-02 and L-C-01; L4 adds L-N-01. L-N-02, L-D-01 and the optional L-R-03 rest on the dated series, so each joins `claims` only in the landing that commits its rows under OD 2b (§3.2b; until then they print UNRUN unclaimed, which fails the case test only on FAIL), and L-R-03 only if L3 finds it feasible. The declared capabilities this item's rows exercise, as A1a's tokens `:[@]`: `verb:statement` (balance-sheet and trace, `--certify`), `statement:balance-sheet`, `verb:explain`, `verb:tb`, `verb:query` (`EFFECTIVE BETWEEN … AS KNOWN AT`), `verb:checkpoint`, `verb:bundle`, `verb:replay`, `verb:export` with `export:ads`, `verb:verify` (`book`, `export ads|beancount`). L3 and L4 add theirs. **`books/statement.toml`** (§3.2a): - `[book]`: `variant = "statement"`, `calendar = "custom"`, `base_unit = "USD"` (scale 2), `opening_date` = the first day of the first period below (a declared default). - `[[period]]` (labels; the runner maps each to the code `fa period create` reports and logs the map): `FY2007Q4` (2007-09-01 … 2007-11-30, `fiscal_year = 2007`), `FY2008Q1` (2007-12-01 … 2008-02-29, `fiscal_year = 2008`), `FY2008Q2` (2008-03-01 … 2008-05-31, `fiscal_year = 2008`). The quarter ends are the 10-Q's column dates; the start days are the day after the previous end (book context, named in every premise list). All three are created and opened; none is closed (no issuance or restatement on this book). - `[[principal]]`: the reconstruction principal that uploads the stubs and posts (a `roles.toml` label from L1) and `case-second-reader`, which reviews the stubs it did not upload. - `[[account]]`: one account per printed line of the 10-Q's condensed consolidated statement of financial condition (L1's `Q208-SFC--` facts), `name_fact` = that line's fact, `type` via `role_map` (interpretive; Asset / Liability / Equity, `registries/account_types.toml:33`, `:39`, `:45`). Codes are the author's choice; none starts with `9` (no filler). Map each L-R-01 quantity (segregated cash, collateralized lending agreements, identifiable intangibles, stockholders' equity, junior subordinated notes) to the printed lines at authoring and record the mapping in a `[[default]]` row: - it equals one printed line → that line's account; - it is the sum of several printed lines → its R row reads each of their accounts and the harness sums them (rendered "harness-summed"); - it is a component of one printed line (for example junior subordinated notes inside a borrowings line, if the statement prints them that way) → that line is posted as two leaf accounts, the component (sourced, p.89) and the rest (a `difference` derived fact: printed line − component), both of the line's type. - If L-R-01's 2008-02-29 rows are needed (below), three remainder accounts, one per type (§3.8). - `[[document]]`: the citation stub of SRC-LEH-002 (`stub_of = "SRC-LEH-002"`, `grade = "AgentUpload"`, `reviewed_by = "case-second-reader"`), and of the Q1-2008 10-Q if L1 recorded it `OK`. Every intent's `evidence` is the stub of the filing that prints its figures (§2.7). - `[[intent]]` and `[[leg]]` (class `Original`, a declared default with the rationale "a filer's printed figure posted as presented"; a stock leg's `amount_rule` is `value:#1`, the line cell's `[[value]]` row read under `scale` with `param = 6` (L1), a change leg's is `derived:difference` over its line's two cell facts (how a leg names that derived fact is open, Notes), and `amount_literal` is that value): - `Q208-SFC--2007-11-30` (the stock intent): effective 2007-11-30, one leg per printed line at 2007-11-30 (assets Dr, liabilities and equity Cr). Its `fact` is the line fact its first leg posts, so its id is that fact id (A1b refuses any other id for an intent whose `fact` is a sourced fact, `BadId`; E4 names its multi-line A intents the same way), and every other leg names its own line fact through `amount_rule`. It balances because the printed statement balances; it posts no total. - `Q208-SFC-2008-05-31`: effective 2008-05-31, one leg per printed line, each a `difference` derived fact (the line at 2008-05-31 − the line at 2007-11-30), on the side its sign gives. If the Q1-2008 10-Q is `OK` and prints a full statement, the change is split at 2008-02-29 (`Q108-SFC-2008-02-29`, then `Q208-SFC-2008-05-31` against 2008-02-29) and 2008-02-29 is footed too. - **2008-02-29 without a Q1-2008 full statement** (L-R-01 only): intent `Q208-P86P89-2008-02-29`, effective 2008-02-29, posts for each L-R-01 account the `difference` (its p.86/p.89 value at 2008-02-29 − its 2007-11-30 line), and balances each account type with that type's remainder account, whose leg is the negated sum of that type's posted differences. The remainder is computed from posted A-side values only, never from a printed total (§3.8, K-TAUT). `Q208-SFC-2008-05-31` then posts, for those accounts, the change from their 2008-02-29 value, and the exact negation of each remainder leg, so every remainder balance is 0 at 2008-05-31 and at 2007-11-30. No T is asserted at 2008-02-29. - `[[step]]`, in order: `period_open` for the three labels; `intent Q208-SFC--2007-11-30`; (`intent Q208-P86P89-2008-02-29` or `intent Q108-SFC-2008-02-29`); `intent Q208-SFC-2008-05-31`; `checkpoint`. The `period_open` and `checkpoint` steps run no intent, so each names its `principal`, the reconstruction principal (A1b refuses a missing one, `MissingField`). The engagement (`fa engagement open lehman-provenance --kind investigation --period … --overall "0.00 USD" --performance "0.00 USD" --clearly-trivial "0.00 USD"`, then `fa engagement file` per stub, rendered "no materiality stated", §2.7) and the stubs' `fa document add` / `fa document attest review` are built by the runner (A7a) before the history. - No filler. The runner generates the `jet.self_sourced_evidence` row `L-SELF-statement` (A7a; `registries/procedures.toml:97-105`); it is not authored here. **`expectations.toml` rows.** - `[[expectation]] id = "L-T-01"`, `type = "T"`, `kind = "footing"`, `book_variant = "statement"`, `granularity = "statement_line"`, `basis` = the `Q208-SFC-*` line facts (and `Q108-SFC-*` if footed), `vintages = ["exhibit:SRC-LEH-002"]` (A1c's `:` form, role `exhibit` for a footing; SRC-LEH-002 is EDGAR `0001104659-08-045115`; plus `exhibit:` if 2008-02-29 is footed), `assurance` = `filer_reviewed` at 2008-05-31 and the 2007-11-30 column's assurance as L1 determined it. Its predicate names every intent on the book as an input, and `published` names the printed totals. **K-VINTAGE** (A3b) orders the 10-Qs by L1's `filed_on`/`restates`: a 2007-11-30 or 2008-02-29 cell printed by both the Q1-2008 and the Q2-2008 10-Q is read from the later vintage (SRC-LEH-002) unless the expectation names `AS REPORTED IN` the earlier one; where the two differ, each is its own fact, and a 2008-02-29 footing of the Q1-2008 statement then names its vintage explicitly. - `[[target]]` rows, one per (total, date): `Q208-SFC-total-assets-`, `Q208-SFC-total-liabilities-`, `Q208-SFC-total-liabilities-and-equity-` for 2008-05-31 (`FY2008Q2`) and 2007-11-30 (`FY2007Q4`). Read: `fa statement balance-sheet --for --certify`, lines `assets`, `liabilities` and `liabilities_and_equity` (`registries/statements/balance-sheet.toml:16`, `:22`, `:58`). The printed totals are never posted. - A multi-account footing total cannot be asserted (`fa assert-balance` is single-cell, §5.3), so there is no kernel twin. - `[[expectation]] id = "L-R-01"`, `type = "R"`, `book_variant = "statement"`: one `[[target]]` per (quantity, date) for the five quantities at 2008-05-31, 2007-11-30 and, while no Q1-2008 footing exists, 2008-02-29. Read: the account's row of `fa tb --period --certify --json`, a stock read ("Balances from inception through the latest selected period's inclusive end", `crates/fa-registers/src/lib.rs:1120-1124`), which returns the posted value; a quantity mapped to several printed lines sums their rows (harness-summed). `fa explain balance --period ` is not this read: it covers one period's register cells (`balance_explained`, `registries/verbs.toml:2445`; `crates/fa-registers/src/explain.rs:230-233`), so at `FY2008Q1` and `FY2008Q2` it returns that period's change, not the stock the 10-Q prints. Valukas's agreement with these values is a published two-source observation with no FA computation, never PASS/FAIL. **Harness-derived values** (not expectations; no id; rendered "computed by the harness from certified balances; franken_accounting has no ratio operator", `crates/fa-statements/src/custom.rs:214-223`; H8): - (b) = (a) − (segregated cash + collateralized lending agreements + identifiable intangibles); - (d) = (c) + junior subordinated notes − identifiable intangibles; - net leverage (b)/(d), kept as an exact reduced fraction; its rendered value at the 10-Q's 0.01x display uses `HalfEven` (`registries/rounding_laws.toml:21-22`), a declared rendering default (§2.4: no rounding without a named law). - A pure fa-oracles function (checked i128, no float; name proposed: `cases::ratios::net_leverage`) takes the certified balances the runner read and returns (b), (d) and the fraction. The 10-Q's printed 12.06x / 15.44x / 16.14x and junior notes 5,004 / 4,976 / 4,740 are rendered beside the derived values, but no comparison is asserted (no C id is registered for them). **Witnesses and checks** (A11b, A12, §12.1, §12.7): - Contributing-entry: `fa explain balance --period

--certify --json` reads one period's register cells (`registries/verbs.toml:2445`; `crates/fa-registers/src/explain.rs:230-233`), while the balance sheet is a stock read (`crates/fa/src/statements.rs:447`) and this book posts the 2007-11-30 stock and then per-period changes. So for a target in period q, every leaf account its total selects is explained in every period from `FY2007Q4` through q, as E4 does for its stock lines: the union of the contributions must be exactly the book's intents effective on or before q's end (the stock intent alone at 2007-11-30; every intent at 2008-05-31), none carrying a printed total, and must re-add to the certified line. Requires A11b's leaf-account path to read every period up to the T's for a stock read and to compare each target with the named inputs effective by its coordinate (L-T-01's predicate names every intent on the book, and its targets span two dates); A11b reads the T's period only. A total selecting more than 8 accounts also reads `fa statement trace --definition balance-sheet --for --before --after --certify` (`registries/verbs.toml:543`: the definition form requires `--for `; its usage line does not list `--certify`, which the statement verb's general "Add --certify to retain an immutable certificate" text and plan §3.7 imply, so confirm at authoring that the definition form certifies, else the witness reads the trace uncertified and logs that), and `fa_reference::statements::render` recomputes the line from the explained balances; the two must agree. - Outsider: `fa checkpoint create --grant witness`; `fa bundle produce --certificate ` (`registries/verbs.toml:784`); `fa-verify bundle --key K --receipt R --json` and `fa-verify report --key K --checkpoint C --receipt R --json` as literal argv through `fa_verify::cli::run` (`crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700`), both exit 0, with `report`'s recomputation of each total equal to the printed total; `fa replay ` byte-identical (FA-INV-11). - ADS: `fa export ads --period --out

--with-proofs`, then `fa-verify ads --key K` (`registries/verbs.toml:917`). - Second read path: `fa query "' AND '' AS KNOWN AT >" --certify` (`registries/verbs.toml:652`), legs netted per unit and side by the harness, must equal the fold-path value for every T and R value (an R-class cross-check, never independent evidence). - Integrity and interop: `fa verify book --json` exits 0 (`registries/verbs.toml:929`); the ADS extract re-imports byte-identically; `fa verify export beancount|ads` passes. ## Tests & logging **Run.** - `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact lehman` (the Lehman `#[test]`, A7a; libtest filter on the test name; A7a defines no per-expectation filter). Under 60 s warm (§16). - `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- lehman_neg_` (this item's run-time negatives). - `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_lehman` (the derivation unit tests). **Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; these are the values each field must contain; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `/`; a FAIL or UNRUN carries its reason in A7a's trailing `reason=` field, a FAIL is followed by `REPRODUCE fa --book `, and the run ends `LOG `): ``` PASS L-T-01 T statement Q208-SFC-total-assets-2008-05-31/default kind=footing read=statement balance-sheet,assets,FY2008Q2 value= published= contrib=holds outsider=report:verified gql=ok PASS L-T-01 T statement Q208-SFC-total-liabilities-2008-05-31/default kind=footing read=statement balance-sheet,liabilities,FY2008Q2 value=… published=… contrib=holds outsider=report:verified gql=ok PASS L-T-01 T statement Q208-SFC-total-liabilities-and-equity-2008-05-31/default kind=footing read=statement balance-sheet,liabilities_and_equity,FY2008Q2 value=… published=… contrib=holds outsider=report:verified gql=ok ``` and the same three at 2007-11-30 (`FY2007Q4`), and at 2008-02-29 (`FY2008Q1`) only if the Q1-2008 10-Q is footed. Then one line per L-R-01 target, for example ``` PASS L-R-01 R statement Q208-P89-junior-subordinated-notes-2008-05-31/default kind=read_back read=tb,,FY2008Q2 value= published= gql=ok ``` (the posted value is the p.89 junior-notes figure L1 binds to that date; the plan lists 5,004 / 4,976 / 4,740 $M in the order 2008-05-31 / 2008-02-29 / 2007-11-30), and the generated `L-SELF-statement` line (A7a), the A7c budget lines `BUDGET lehman statement book= invocations= wall_ms=`, and A16's generated `L-N-90` line for this book. The runner also logs the harness-derived (b), (d) and net-leverage fraction at each footed date with the printed ratio beside it; never at an unfooted 2008-02-29, where the certified total assets is still the 2007-11-30 total because the remainders net each type's change to zero. **Derivation unit tests** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`; synthetic integers, so no quote text is vendored): - `net_assets_is_total_minus_three_deductions`: (a) 1,000,000; deductions 100,000 / 200,000 / 50,000 → (b) 650,000. - `tangible_equity_adds_junior_notes_less_intangibles`: (c) 40,000, junior notes 5,000, intangibles 4,000 → (d) 41,000. - `net_leverage_is_exact_reduced_fraction`: (b) 650,000 / (d) 41,000 → 650/41; rendered at 0.01x under HalfEven → `15.85`. - `net_leverage_half_even_boundary`: (b) 12,345, (d) 1,000 → 12.345 → `12.34` (HalfUp would give `12.35`; the test pins the named law). - `non_positive_tangible_equity_is_refused`: (d) = 0 and (d) = −1 each return a named error, never a value. - `checked_overflow_is_refused`: (a) = i128::MAX with a negative deduction returns an overflow error, never a wrapped value. - `planted_wrong_deduction_changes_b`: the first test with one deduction off by one minor unit yields (b) 649,999 and fails an equality with 650,000 (the test asserts the inequality). - `net_leverage_runs_on_committed_10q_facts`: over L1's committed 10-Q facts for each date, the function returns (b), (d) and a fraction without error, and logs them beside the printed 12.06x / 15.44x / 16.14x; it asserts no equality with the printed ratios. **Planted negatives** (run-time, `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, each on a temp copy of the case directory with one edit; the committed files are untouched; each asserts the named lines and a non-zero case verdict): - `lehman_neg_line_plus_one_minor_unit`: in `Q208-SFC-2008-05-31`, one asset leg +0.01 USD and the equity leg +0.01 USD (so the intent still balances), both legs re-pointed to `amount_rule = "synthetic"` (with their `difference` rules kept, K-DERIVE/K-BIND would refuse the two legs at load, A1b, since each `amount_literal` would differ from its rule's value, and every line would then read FAIL with the load failure, A7a) → `FAIL L-T-01 … total-assets-2008-05-31 … value= published=` and `FAIL … total-liabilities-and-equity-2008-05-31 …`, while `PASS … total-liabilities-2008-05-31 …` and every 2007-11-30 line still PASS. - `lehman_neg_printed_total_posted`: a planted intent posting the printed 2008-05-31 total assets to an asset account (balanced against a planted liability account) (its legs' `amount_rule = "value:Q208-SFC-total-assets-2008-05-31#1"`, the printed total's own cell, so the static trace reaches B) → K-TAUT re-types L-T-01 R at load (A3b re-types the expectation, so its lines print type `R`; L-T-01 is claimed, so each reads `FAIL L-T-01 R … reason=retyped T→R K-TAUT`, A7a), and the log names K-TAUT and the planted intent; the contributing-entry witness also names the planted posting. - `lehman_neg_foreign_receipt` (its edit is to a run artifact, not a case file: `run_planted`'s `PlantedEdit` covers case files only, so it requires A7a to let a test substitute an outsider step's input, here the receipt path, as M0's `_selftest_neg_ledger_refusing_member` requires for a rendered batch): the bundle of one run verified with the receipt of a second run's book → `fa-verify bundle` exits non-zero, each L-T-01 line shows `outsider=report:failed` (A12), and the case FAILs whatever its expectations say (§12.1). **Load-time negative** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`, an in-memory copy with two edits, as W6's `w_t_02_remainder_fed_by_b`): - `lehman_remainder_fed_by_b_never_stays_t`: a planted derived fact that takes L-T-01's B, the printed 2008-05-31 total assets, among its inputs and recomputes to the 2008-02-29 asset remainder's own amount (W6's `plant-rem` construction), and that remainder leg's `amount_rule` re-pointed at it, so the balance check and K-DERIVE still pass → `run_load_checks` reports `RETYPE L-T-01 T→R K-TAUT path=[…]` naming the remainder (A3b: a remainder whose inputs reach a T's B re-types every T on the lines it partitions; the remainder account is of a type the `assets` line selects). The earlier form, a remainder fed by the printed 2008-02-29 total, re-types nothing: no T is asserted at 2008-02-29, so that total is no T's B, and K-TAUT re-types rather than refuses. **JSONL log** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord` with `record = "step"` and `binds`, one per step, plus one `VerdictRecord` per expectation line; in the test's temp dir, copied to `$FA_CASES_LOG_DIR/lehman.jsonl` when set; path printed at the end; argv printed on any FAIL; certificate placeholders `$C_BS_` in `binds`): `verb = "book"` (create, with `book_id`); the period label → code map (A7a); `verb = "document"` (add and attest review per stub); `verb = "engagement"` (open, file); `verb = "post"` per intent (`exit = 0`); `verb = "statement"` per date with `certificate_kind` set to the balance-sheet certificate's kind; `verb = "explain"` per leaf account; `verb = "tb"`; `verb = "query"`; `verb = "checkpoint"`, `verb = "bundle"`, `verb = "replay"`, `verb = "export"`, `verb = "verify"`, each with its exit; the literal `fa-verify` argv and exits (A12); the per-book invocation count and wall time (A7c). ## Notes - **Why each edge exists:** - **L1:** the facts and stubs. - **A3b:** K-TAUT and K-VINTAGE. - **A7b:** certified statement reads. - **A11b:** the contributing-entry and trace witnesses. - **A12:** the outsider checks. - **Book shape (decided here).** One `statement` book: the 2007-11-30 stock, then per-line `difference` changes, so both dates' totals are certified folds of posted lines and no total is ever posted. The 2008-02-29 remainder construction is used only for L-R-01's read-backs while no Q1-2008 full statement is retrieved. - **Ratio comparisons.** A comparison of a harness ratio with a printed ratio is display-precision agreement, which is C by §5.3. The plan's one Lehman C row, L-C-01 (adjusted net leverage vs Valukas's 13.9x), belongs to L3's scenario. No C id is registered for the reported net leverage (12.06x / 15.44x / 16.14x), so L2 renders those values as harness-derived and asserts no comparison; adding one needs a C row id first. - **Names (§3.2b).** Directory `lehman`, letter `L`; variant stems are plain kinds (`native`, `statement`, `ledger`); the generated self-disclosure ids are `L-SELF-` and the guidance N is `L-N-90`. A statement posting's intent id is the fact id of the figure it posts (§3.2b), so the stock intent carries the id of the line fact its first leg posts (`Q208-SFC--2007-11-30`; A1b's `BadId` rule), and the change intents (`fact = "derived:difference"`, which need only a unique id, A1b) are named `Q208-SFC-`/`Q108-SFC-` after the date whose lines they post. There is no restatement case on this book, hence no `L-CASE-*` row. - **Foundation (re-checked at r4a).** A1a now loads `letter` and takes the id prefix from it, with `id = "lehman"` as the directory, and A7a names the case test `lehman` and accepts `lehman_neg_` tests, so nothing is required of them here. Open: A1b's `amount_rule` forms (`value:#`, `derived:`, `branch:`, `synthetic`) have none that names a derived fact, such as the `difference` facts the change legs post (`derived:` names the rule, not the fact; E4's `derived:difference` legs share the need); requires A1b to say how a leg names one. The stock legs need no such form: `value:#1` reads the cell's `[[value]]` row under `scale` (L1). - **Related.** fa-sa4w: the statement book joins its bean-check/hledger differential once that harness exists, reported UNRUN when the binaries are absent (§12.7). - **Related tracker bead fa-qh60** (journaled custom StatementDefinitions, open; link added in round 4): once custom definitions are surfaced and certified, (b) net assets and (d) tangible equity could be read as certified custom lines instead of harness-computed values (H8); nothing in L2 changes until then.
acceptance_criteria:

The contributing-entry witness (every leaf account explained in each period from FY2007Q4 through the target's, the union of its contributions exactly the intents effective by the target's date) and, where a line selects > 8 accounts, the trace witness agree, `fa-verify report`'s recomputation equals each printed total, `fa replay` is byte-identical, `fa verify book --json` exits 0, and the `fa query --certify` value equals the fold path.

(b), (d) and net leverage are computed from certified balances at each footed date, logged and rendered as harness-derived, with no comparison to the printed ratios asserted. 2008-02-29 is footed only if its 10-Q was retrieved and prints a full statement.

(b), (d) and the ratios are harness arithmetic, not certified statement lines. Valukas's agreement with the 10-Q is a published observation, not an FA result.

title: [cases] L3: Lehman Repo 105/108 secured-borrowing scenario — L-R-02 certified scenario diff (±e read-back), L-C-01 adjusted 13.9x within 0.1x; optional L-R-03 Canon backtest on ledger
description:
## Why
The scenario is the but-for view the litigation-consultant reader works from (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.3): on a scenario branch, `fa scenario run` recharacterizes (e) as secured borrowing (+e assets, +e liabilities; §8.3). Scenario statement reads are uncertified, so the certified artifact is the `fa scenario diff` certificate (§3.3 step 7). The scenario-fork probe is not used as a T witness, because scenario diffs are per-account rows, not statement lines (§3.7 item 2).

The plan types what this scenario can show, and none of it is T (§8.3, retyped in the current plan from an earlier "L-T-02"):
- **L-R-02** (R). The certified diff shows exactly +e on assets and +e on liabilities. Since (e) is posted by the scenario's own intents, that is a read-back, not a T (K-TAUT).
- **L-C-01** (C). The harness recomputes adjusted net leverage ((b) + e) / (d) from the certified balances and the diff. It must equal Valukas's adjusted 13.9x within its printed 0.1x display unit, so it is C, never T. All its inputs come from the same p.889 table that prints the ratio, so it reproduces the examiner's own arithmetic.
- **L-R-03** (R; optional, low priority; formerly "L-T-02-CF-01"). A Canon rule-version comparison on the `ledger` book: a read-back of the posted ±(e) through `fa rule backtest --compare`. It adds no claim and is "the only honest Canon exercise the record allows" (§8.3). Feasibility is checked here.

Claim types: R and C.

## What to build
**Files** under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/lehman/`: additions to `books/statement.toml` (the scenario intent, its document and steps), the L-R-02 / L-C-01 / L-R-03 rows of `expectations.toml`, and, if L-R-03 is feasible, two rule source files under `rules/` plus additions to `books/ledger.toml`; the band function and its unit tests in `crates/fa-oracles` (tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`); the run-time negatives in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`.

**The quarter end Q\*.** The column whose adjusted ratio p.889 prints as 13.9x (L1 binds it at authoring; the plan does not restate it). The fork, the diff, (b), (d) and e all use Q\*. If Q\* is not a date whose full statement L2's book foots (2008-05-31, 2007-11-30, or 2008-02-29 when the Q1-2008 10-Q is footed), (b) cannot be read from certified balances, and L-C-01 is never computed from the printed (b). No runner rule can see this (A7a's `needs:<item>` reasons name a missing prerequisite, and A1c has no expectation-level `pending`), so it is settled at authoring: L3 then authors no L-C-01 (and L-R-02 only if Q\* falls in a period of L2's book), records the outcome as a `[[decision]]` row in `case.toml` (A1a's form: `id = "L3-qstar"`, `outcome = "qstar_not_footed"`, `facts` = the 13.9x cell fact, `reason`), and cannot close, since its acceptance needs both rows PASS.

**The scenario** (on L2's `statement` book; §8.3a):
- `[[document]]`: the fact-level citation stub of `V889-e-<Q*>` (SRC-LEH-001), `AgentUpload`, `reviewed_by = "case-second-reader"`. A scenario figure cites the source that publishes it (§2.7); (e) is single-sourced (Valukas).
- `[[intent]] id = "V889-e-<Q*>"`, `scenario = "lehman-repo105"`, class `Original` (declared default), `effective_date` = Q\*, `evidence` = that stub. `[[leg]]` rows: Dr the account L2 posts for the 10-Q's inventory line, and Cr the account L2 posts for its repurchase-agreements liability line, each `amount_rule = "value:V889-e-<Q*>#1"`, the (e) cell's `[[value]]` row read under `scale` with `param = 6` (L1). The account choice is a `[[default]]` with its rationale: Appendix 17 p.8's entry (`A17-P8-ENTRY`) debits Repo and credits Inventory, so undoing it as a secured borrowing restores those two lines.
- `[[step]]` rows after L2's last Q\* posting, each naming the reconstruction principal as its `principal` (A1b: a step that runs no intent must name one): `scenario_fork` (`fa scenario fork lehman-repo105 --at <seq> --from <Q*>`, `registries/verbs.toml:227`), `scenario_run` (`fa scenario run lehman-repo105 --intent <file> --evidence <oid>`), `scenario_diff` (`fa scenario diff lehman-repo105 --period <code> --certify`). The diff is exact per (account, unit) against trunk as known at the fork, and `--certify` retains a replayable certificate; `fa replay C:<oid>` re-materializes the scenario's intents and reproduces the diff byte for byte.

**L-R-02** (`[[expectation]] id = "L-R-02"`, `type = "R"`, `book_variant = "statement"`, `basis = ["V889-e-<Q*>"]`, `granularity = "dated_aggregate"`). `read` = the scenario-diff certificate's rows: A1c's R read fields (`read_verb = "scenario diff"`, `read_target` the inventory and repurchase-agreements accounts, `read_coordinate` Q\*'s period code) and `posted = "V889-e-<Q*>"` (A1c: the intent or fact whose posted value it reads back). Passes when the diff lists exactly two rows, (inventory account, USD, +e) and (repurchase-agreements account, USD, +e) in each account's normal-balance direction, and nothing else, with e = the USD value of `V889-e-<Q*>`'s `[[value]]` row. The outsider check for scenario expectations is the certificate itself, replayed with `fa replay` (§12.1).

**L-C-01** (`[[expectation]] id = "L-C-01"`, `type = "C"`, `book_variant = "statement"`, `basis` = the p.889 cells at Q\* for (a), the three deductions, (c), (d)'s inputs, (e) and the adjusted ratio, plus p.734 fn 2854's definitions).
- Inputs: (b) and (d), harness-derived from certified balances on L2's book at Q\* (L2's `net_leverage` derivation), and e from the certified diff.
- Computation: in fa-oracles' own checked i128 arithmetic, as an exact rational; no rounding law is needed because the C test compares exactly against the display band.
- C fields (§5.3): `display_unit` = the 13.9x cell fact `V889-adjusted-net-leverage-<Q*>` (A1c: the fact stating the display unit; its recorded unit is p.889's 0.1x, L1); per-row test |((b) + e) / (d) − 13.9| ≤ 0.1, evaluated exactly as |10·((b) + e) − 139·(d)| ≤ (d) (with 139 the cell's integer in tenths); cumulative band one 0.1x display unit; detection limit stated concretely as the interval of e the test accepts, e ∈ [⌈(138·(d) − 10·(b)) / 10⌉, ⌊(140·(d) − 10·(b)) / 10⌋] in minor units: any change of (e) inside it is not detected.
- A pure fa-oracles function (name proposed: `cases::ratios::within_display_band(num, den, printed, unit)`, all integers) returns pass/fail plus the detection interval; the runner calls it with num = (b) + e, den = (d), printed = 139, unit = 1 (tenths).
- Rendering: "computed by the harness from certified balances and a certified scenario diff; franken_accounting has no ratio operator" (`crates/fa-statements/src/custom.rs:214-223`; H8), and "agrees with the examiner's adjusted 13.9x at its printed 0.1x precision", never "reproduces exactly".

**Second read path (§12.7).** The scenario's two balances are also read with `fa query "<MATCH … AT BRANCH 'scenario:lehman-repo105'>"` (`registries/verbs.toml:652`; `AT BRANCH 'scenario:<name>'` is the same as `--branch scenario:<name>`), netted by the harness, and must equal the fold-path value. The read is uncertified: verbs.toml:652 says a branch read is "read at the replay's head, uncertified, with the branch in the envelope's coordinate (no AS KNOWN AT and no certification beside it)", and `crates/fa-cli/src/query.rs:64-73` refuses `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` or `AS KNOWN AT` with a branch. This is an R-class cross-check of two FA read paths, never independent evidence.

**L-R-03** (`[[expectation]] id = "L-R-03"`, `type = "R"`, `book_variant = "ledger"`; optional):
- The `ledger` variant is M0's (schema, `reads_evidence`, batch posting, K-EVID), hence the L3 ← M0 edge. The Lehman ledger book posts net-change entries derived from Appendix 17 §E's 56-observation combined series (§8.3a), and L-R-03's `basis` names L1's series fact `A17E`, whose `rows_file` stays absent until OD 2b, so A7a prints it UNRUN until then; L4 builds the same book for L-D-01 and L-N-02, with no edge between L3 and L4, so either item may land the book first and the other extends it.
- Events: one `sale` event per positive `difference` between consecutive §E observations (a declared default), recorded with `fa event record --code <c> --kind sale --occurred-on <observation date> --evidence <Appendix 17 stub oid> --resource <label>:<amount>` (`registries/verbs.toml:507`). Events are records, not postings, so they do not enter L4's populations.
- Two rule versions over `sale` events, two source files under `rules/` (names the author's). Version A books the documented recharacterization (Appendix 17 p.8, without the haircut leg the series lacks: Dr Repo e / Cr Inventory e). Version B books a secured borrowing; its encoding is a `[[default]]` with its rationale. `fa rule propose <rule-file>` journals each version, addressed by its IR digest (`registries/verbs.toml:664`).
- `fa rule backtest <version-A file> --compare <version-B ir_digest> --from <first> --to <last>` runs the candidate over every recorded event of its kind in range, counts same / differs / refused / no_baseline, and posts nothing. Passes when differs = n (the number of derived `sale` events, computed at load), same = refused = no_baseline = 0, and each differing row's legs differ by ±(e) of its event.
- Feasibility check, recorded in this bead and the case: whether `sale` events can be recorded on the ledger book with the derived amounts as resources, and whether both rules compile (`fa rule check`) against its accounts and units at 8196f5e40. If any step refuses, L-R-03 is not authored and a `[[decision]]` row in `case.toml` records it (A1a's form: `id = "L-R-03-feasibility"`, `outcome = "not_feasible"`, `sources = ["SRC-LEH-003"]`, `reason` = the observed refusal id and the step that raised it), never forced; the row is optional (§8.3), so no runner line stands in for it.
- K-EVID admits R rows on a `ledger` variant (it bars P, CF, `no_refusal` N and evidence-reading D/N there, §3.6), so retyping the former CF as L-R-03 removes the earlier conflict.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
- `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact lehman` (the Lehman `#[test]`, A7a; whole case runs; under 60 s warm).
- `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- lehman_neg_` (run-time negatives).
- `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_lehman` (band unit tests and load-time negatives).

**Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; these are the values each field must contain; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `<target>/<cell>`, the FAIL/UNRUN reason in A7a's trailing `reason=` field):
```
PASS L-R-02 R statement V889-e-<Q*>/default kind=read_back read=scenario diff,lehman-repo105,<Q* code> value=rows:[(<inventory>,USD,+e),(<repo>,USD,+e)] published=e=<V889-e dollars> outsider=replay:verified gql=ok
PASS L-C-01 C statement V889-adjusted-net-leverage-<Q*>/default kind=display_band read=harness((b)+e)/(d) value=<num>/<den> published=13.9x unit=0.1x test=|10·num−139·den|≤den band=0.1x detection=e∈[<e_lo>,<e_hi>]
PASS L-R-03 R ledger -/default kind=read_back read=rule backtest,--compare <B digest>,<first>..<last> value=differs:<n>,same:0,refused:0,no_baseline:0 published=differs:<n>,±e per event
```
or, until OD 2b commits the dated series, `UNRUN L-R-03 R ledger -/default reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`; never PASS. An L-R-03 found not feasible, or an L-C-01 whose Q\* is not footed, is not authored and prints no line; its `[[decision]]` row says why.

**Claims (A7a, §3.2b).** L3 adds L-R-02 and L-C-01 to `case.toml` `claims` (if Q\* is not footed, L-C-01 is not authored, the `L3-qstar` `[[decision]]` row records why, and L3 cannot close). L-R-03 joins `claims` only in the landing that commits the ledger rows under OD 2b and only if feasible; until then it is unclaimed, prints UNRUN, and fails the case test only on FAIL (A7a's unclaimed-row rule). The `case.toml` `capabilities` tokens L3 adds (A1a's `<kind>:<name>[@<version>]`; L2 lists the rest): `verb:scenario` (fork, run, diff `--certify`) and, with L-R-03, `verb:event` and `verb:rule`.

**Band unit tests** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`; synthetic integers):
- `band_exact_printed_value_passes`: num 1,390, den 100, printed 139 → |13,900 − 13,900| = 0 ≤ 100 → pass.
- `band_edges_are_inclusive`: num 1,380 and num 1,400 (den 100) → |±100| = 100 ≤ 100 → pass (the plan's "≤ one display unit").
- `band_one_past_edge_fails`: num 1,379 and 1,401 → 110 > 100 → fail.
- `band_planted_printed_13_7_fails`: num 1,390, den 100, printed 137 → 200 > 100 → fail.
- `band_detection_interval`: (b) 1,290, (d) 100 → e ∈ [90, 110].
- `band_non_positive_den_refused` and `band_overflow_refused`: named errors, never a verdict.

**Load-time negatives** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`, in-memory copy with one edit):
- `lehman_l_r_02_declared_t_never_stays_t`: L-R-02 declared `type = "T"` with the fields a T row needs (A1c), among them `kind = "per_account"`, `published = "V889-e-<Q*>"` and `vintages = ["source:SRC-LEH-001"]` (a copy that changed only `type` would be refused by A1c's loader before K-TAUT runs) → K-TAUT re-types it R, `RETYPE L-R-02 T→R K-TAUT path=[…]` (the published e is posted by the scenario's own intent, A3b).
- `lehman_l_c_01_declared_t_never_passes`: L-C-01 declared `type = "T"` → refused at load: a T row needs a T `kind` and certified read fields (A1c), and L-C-01's C fields (`display_unit`, `per_row_test`, `band`, `detection_limit`) are not T fields, so the copy never loads as a T and can never print `PASS L-C-01 T`. No load check re-types a display-band row to C (K-ORACLE re-types only `oracle_output` inputs, A3b), and an exact-equality FAIL is a run-time observable this load-time test cannot see.

**Run-time negatives** (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, temp copy of the case, one edit, each asserting the named lines and a non-zero case verdict):
- `lehman_neg_scenario_e_plus_one_minor_unit`: both scenario legs e + 0.01 USD, re-pointed to `amount_rule = "synthetic"` (under their `value:V889-e-<Q*>#1` rule, K-DERIVE/K-BIND would refuse both legs at load, A1b, and every line would read FAIL with the load failure, A7a) → `FAIL L-R-02 … value=rows:[(…,+e+0.01),(…,+e+0.01)]`.
- `lehman_neg_extra_scenario_intent`: a second balanced scenario intent on two other accounts → `FAIL L-R-02 …` naming four rows where two were expected.
- `lehman_neg_c01_e_one_minor_unit`: both scenario legs set to 0.01 USD with `amount_rule = "synthetic"` (as above) → the test computes the detection interval from the committed facts and asserts `FAIL L-C-01 …` when 0.01 lies outside it (the expected case: p.889 prints different reported and adjusted ratios); if 0.01 lies inside, the negative fails itself as vacuous.
- `lehman_neg_r03_identical_versions` (only when L-R-03 runs): version B replaced by a copy of A → `FAIL L-R-03 … value=differs:0,same:<n>`.
- `lehman_neg_r03_missing_ledger_book_fails_at_load`: the ledger book file emptied → A1b refuses it at load (no `[book]` table), so the case stops before any book is built and every Lehman line reads FAIL with that load failure (A7a), never PASS; the test calls `.expect_err`. Removing the file is refused the same way (A1c: `book_variant = "ledger"` must name a `books/<stem>.toml` file). An UNRUN cannot be produced this way; L-R-03's UNRUN path is its pending rows.

**JSONL log** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord`/`VerdictRecord`; copied to `$FA_CASES_LOG_DIR/lehman.jsonl` when set; path printed at the end; argv printed on FAIL; the diff certificate bound as `$C_SCEN_lehman-repo105` in `binds`, A7b): `verb = "document"` for the V889 stub; `verb = "scenario"` for fork, run and diff, the diff with `certificate_kind` set to the scenario-diff certificate's kind; `verb = "replay"` on that certificate (exit 0); `verb = "query"` with `--branch scenario:lehman-repo105`; on the ledger book `verb = "event"` (one per recorded `sale`), `verb = "rule"` (check, propose ×2, backtest), each with its exit and any `refusal_id`. L-C-01's line logs (b), (d), e, the exact fraction, the band and the detection interval.

## Notes
- **Edges.** ← L2: the `statement` book, its certified balances, and the harness-derived (b) and (d). ← M0: the `ledger` variant L-R-03 runs on (§15 L3: "← L2, M0").
- **Retyping (current plan, §8.3).** "L-T-02" is now L-R-02 + L-C-01 and "L-T-02-CF-01" is now L-R-03. Nothing here may render as T; a row that had already landed as T would need a `Weakened-tests:` trailer, never an edited check.

Tests never read the cache (§4.3), so until then L-R-03 prints `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` and stays unclaimed (§3.2b); the band function, the rule sources and `fa rule check` on them are built and tested now, the rules on a synthetic fixture event.
