title: [cases] L4: Lehman L-N-01 no repo-as-sale law (native), L-N-02 events.subsequent over entry class, L-D-01 jet.period_end_timing (ledger)
description:
## Why L4 lands Lehman's limits and its one D (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §8.3, §8.3a). Claim types N and D. - **L-N-01** is an N result with a product question (H6). It runs on the `native` variant, because a `no_refusal` N is barred on `ledger` (K-EVID). - **L-N-02** shows that `events.subsequent`'s silence depends on an unsourced attribute, so it is B(entry_class), not unconditional. - **L-D-01** is the lowest-ranked claim in the program: it runs on derived net-change entries from a dated aggregate series. N rows are published with the same prominence as D/P/T (§0.3). Every claim states its coarsest granularity: "on 56 dated aggregate observations on irregular dates", never "daily" or "the Repo 105 entries" (§2.3). ## What to build **Files** under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/lehman/`: `books/native.toml`, `books/ledger.toml` (or its rows, if L3 created the file first), and the L-N-01 / L-N-02 / L-D-01 rows of `expectations.toml`; load-time negatives in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`; run-time negatives in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`. **`books/native.toml`** (§3.2a): - `[book]`: `variant = "native"`, `calendar = "custom"`, `base_unit = "USD"` (scale 2), `opening_date` = the first day of `FY2008Q1`. - `[[period]]`: `FY2008Q1` (2007-12-01 … 2008-02-29) and `FY2008Q2` (2008-03-01 … 2008-05-31), `fiscal_year = 2008`. Appendix 17 p.8 is a per-$100 policy illustration with no date, so these periods and the effective dates below are `[[default]]` rows with that rationale. - `[[principal]]`: L1's reconstruction-principal label (it prepares the entry and signs its ManualAssertion, `crates/fa-journal/src/attestation.rs:873-877`). - `[[account]]` via `role_map` (interpretive, named in the claim): Repo → Liability; Long inventory-derivative → Asset; Inventory → Asset (`registries/account_types.toml:33`, `:39`). Codes are the author's; none starts with `9`. - `[[intent]] id = "A17-P8-ENTRY"`, `fact = "A17-P8-ENTRY"`, class `Original` (a declared default with its rationale; the twin relies on it, because an Original in a Closed period is `FA-REF-010` in W-P-03's table, while an Adjusting entry would meet `FA-REF-011`/`-012` first), `effective_date = "2008-05-31"` (declared default: the Open period's last day), `evidence = "manual_assertion:InternalTransfer"`. Its assertion is recorded and the entry planned in one command, then committed from that plan (§3.3; A7a): `fa document attest manual --intent --reason InternalTransfer --statement "reconstruction placeholder: Appendix 17 p.8 describes this entry form; no Lehman entry document is public" --plan-out

` (`registries/verbs.toml:483`; `crates/fa-cli/src/document.rs:1753` records the assertion over the sealed proposal, `:1761` plans it), then `fa commit --plan

`. A second `fa post --intent` would reseal the description with fresh entropy (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:8137`) and the assertion would no longer cover it. The assertion is marked `encoding{reconstruction_placeholder}` (§2.7). OD 5's `NotInPublicRecord` replaces `InternalTransfer` if adopted. - `[[leg]]`: (1) Dr Repo `100.00` USD, (2) Dr Long inventory-derivative `5.00` USD, (3) Cr Inventory `105.00` USD, each `amount_rule` naming `A17-P8-ENTRY`'s values. - `[[step]]`: `period_open FY2008Q1`, `period_open FY2008Q2`, `period_soft_close FY2008Q1`, `period_close FY2008Q1` (`fa period close --reason … --yes`), `intent A17-P8-ENTRY`; each period step names its `principal`, the reconstruction principal (A1b: a step that runs no intent must). FY2008Q1's close is book context (the entry is admitted in the Open quarter after a Closed one). The twin (below) is a harness-only run the runner generates from the expectation on its own book (A11c), never an authored intent. - No filler (no D runs on it). The runner generates `L-SELF-native` (A7a). **`books/ledger.toml`** (M0's variant): - `[book]`: `variant = "ledger"`; `[[period]]`: the Lehman fiscal quarters covering Appendix 17 §E's first to last observation date (bound at authoring from the observations). - Rows (one `[[intent]]` each): the first observation posts as an opening entry of its own value (`A17E-`, sourced); each later observation posts its net change, `A17E-chg-` with `fact = "derived:difference"` (the observation minus its predecessor, `from` both observation facts), dated on the observation date. Legs follow one declared two-leg encoding per sign (a `[[default]]` with its rationale; the plan fixes only that the haircut legs and the 105/108 split are omitted, because the series lacks them). Each row cites the Appendix 17 citation stub (SRC-LEH-003). - Posting: first one `period_open` step per quarter, in calendar order, each naming the reconstruction principal: the runner creates every declared period and opens none (A7a and A1b, round 5), and a period is born `Future`, which admits nothing (`registries/admissibility.toml:55`), so only the book's own `period_open` steps open its quarters, as on L2's book and the native book above. Then one `batch` step (`ref = "A17E-..A17E-chg-"`, A1b's intent-range grammar), `fa batch --intent ` (`registries/verbs.toml:350`), 56 entries (≤ 8,190, `registries/limits.toml:99-101`), with the idempotency key derived as M0 specifies (≤ 64 bytes, `registries/limits.toml:33-35`). Each row `[[intent]]` carries its own authored `idempotency_key` (≤ 51 bytes, A1b), distinct within the batch: an entry intent without one is refused (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:7596`), and two members sharing one refuse the batch (`crates/fa-intents/src/lib.rs:593-597`; M0). - Book context for `events.subsequent`'s path (b) (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:705-715`): after the batch, one `period_soft_close` step for each quarter whose end precedes the last observation; declared in the book, named in L-N-02's premises. Then one `finding_record` step per procedure (`ref = "jet.period_end_timing@1"` and `ref = "events.subsequent@1"`, A1b's grammar), from which A7a runs `fa finding record` (`registries/verbs.toml:881`); the JSONL below already logs those runs. Every step that runs no intent names its `principal`, the reconstruction principal (A1b). (At 8196f5e40 path (b) also counts merely opened periods; see Notes. Soft-closing every quarter but the last makes the predicted set the same under the code's rule and under its comment's.) - No filler: the derived rows are the population. The same book carries L3's optional L-R-03 (§8.3a); there is no edge between L3 and L4, so whichever lands first builds the book and the other extends it. The runner generates `L-SELF-ledger` (A7a). - **OD 2b (§3.2b).** Until OD 2b allows committing the series, the §E observation facts and these rows are not committed; tests never read the cache (§4.3). The book file is committed without them: its header, periods, document, principal, defaults and its period-open, soft-close and finding steps, but no `[[intent]]`/`[[leg]]` rows and no `batch` step, whose range would not resolve (A1b). L-D-01's and L-N-02's `basis` names L1's series fact `A17E`, whose `rows_file` stays absent (A1a's `rows_committed = false`), so L-D-01 and L-N-02 print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS. They join `case.toml` `claims` only in the landing that commits the rows; until then they are unclaimed, and an unclaimed UNRUN fails the case test only on FAIL (A7a). L-N-01 (native) does not depend on the series and is claimed by this item now. The load-time prediction functions and their unit tests run on a synthetic fixture series meanwhile; L4 cannot close until its OD-2b rows PASS. Requires M0's pending-book rule (keyed today on a `[[ledger_map]]` rows fact) to cover this authored-row book too, so the runner builds no `ledger` book and prints `L-SELF-ledger` and the ledger's `L-N-90` UNRUN, never a PASS on an empty book. **L-N-01** (`[[expectation]] id = "L-N-01"`, `type = "N"`, `kind = "no_refusal"`, `book_variant = "native"`, target `A17-P8-ENTRY`). "No registered law refuses a repo recharacterized as a sale. There is no derecognition or repurchase law." - **Mechanism.** The entry is admitted by every numbered step of `prepare_post_in` (`crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1594` structure … `:3814` seal; §2.6 rule 6), none of which is a derecognition or repurchase law; and no planted Canon rule can refuse a posted intent: Canon rules turn recorded events into legs, and "Rule families bound to intents are not in this build" (`registries/verbs.toml:664`). The `mechanism` field cites both. - **Twin: a harness-observability twin, not a law-level one** (§8.3, §8.3a). No law-level twin exists at 8196f5e40. The harness-only twin posts the same entry (same legs, class, evidence and effective date 2008-05-31) on its own twin book (A11c), where `FY2008Q2` has been soft-closed and closed before the intent (attribute flipped: `period_state_at_commit`, and only it; `twin_kind = "harness_observability"`, `twin_attribute = "period_state_at_commit"`, `twin_value = "Closed"`, `twin_expect = "refuses FA-REF-010"`, A1c), as E3's E-N-01 twin does. Re-dating it to 2008-02-29 in the Closed `FY2008Q1` would also change `effective_date`, a second attribute, which A11c's one-attribute twin rule refuses. It must observe `FA-REF-010` (exit 7, safety; `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:102`). It runs as the same two-step ManualAssertion flow under its own idempotency key (A7c `cell_key`: the intent's key plus a 12-hex suffix, ≤ 64 bytes): `fa document attest manual --intent … --plan-out

` records the twin's assertion (`document.rs:1753`; `crates/fa-journal/src/attestation.rs:1511-1591` reads no period state) and is then refused at its planning step (`document.rs:1761`) with `FA-REF-010`, so no entry is committed (the attestation is that step's only write); period law (step 5) precedes the evidence minimum (5b), so the refusal does not depend on the assertion. It shows that the harness observes refusals of this exact intent shape on this book, not that a derecognition law would fire; the rendering says so. When H6 lands a kernel law, an intent-bound Canon family or a Lantern detector, L-N-01 flips and gains a law-level twin (§13). L4 has no H6 edge. **L-N-02** (`[[expectation]] id = "L-N-02"`, `type = "N"`, `kind = "no_finding"`, `book_variant = "ledger"`, `procedure = "events.subsequent"`, `version = 1`). It reports nothing on the natural encoding. - Defaults: `window_days` 30, `min_amount` 100000 (= 1,000.00 at scale 2) (`registries/procedures.toml:1427-1447` at 8196f5e40: `events.subsequent`@1, claim `statistical`, calibration `planted`). - **Related product bead H18 (fa-yugf.98).** H18 fixes path (b)'s period selection (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:646-655` lists every period with any recorded transition, see Notes) and bumps `events.subsequent`'s version. L-N-02 is H18's regression oracle: when H18 lands, L4 re-runs L-N-02's cells against the new version (a new tier row and `version` here), re-computes the load-time prediction under the new selection rule, and records any cell that moves; the L4 ↔ H18 link is `related`, not blocking. - Mechanism: repurchases are new Original entries. Path (b)'s class gate admits only Reversal / Replacement / Restatement / PriorPeriodAdjustment / Adjusting (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:689-696`), and path (a) needs a supersession (`cutoff.rs:681-687`, `:699-704`; window 30). Path (b) flags an entry of a gated class whose effective date `eff` satisfies `eff > end` and `eff − end ≤ window_days` for some other period in its "closed" list, where `end` is that period's end as the snapshot holds it (`cutoff.rs:705-715`; exclusive, per the comment at `crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:187-188`), and only if its largest leg magnitude is at least `min_amount`. The finding cites the entry, its own period and the matched prior period (`cutoff.rs:718-721`), at severity High with statistic `subsequent_event_amount` = that magnitude (`cutoff.rs:717-740`). The load-time prediction uses exactly this rule. - One `[[branch_class]]` (A1b: `id`, `attribute = "entry_class"`, `rule` from A5a's `case_branch_rules.toml`, `values = ["Original", "Adjusting"]`) over the repurchase (negative-change) rows, and one `[[branch_cell]]` per value (A1c): `Original` with `default = true`, and `Adjusting`; `record_consistent = false` on both, because no fact states the class (`default` and `record_consistent` are `[[branch_cell]]` fields, A1c). The Adjusting cell is a separate build of the ledger book (a whole-book cell). - `[[branch_cell]]` expected verdicts: Original → no finding (from a run with no refusal and no error); Adjusting → findings on exactly the repurchase rows that path (b)'s rule above selects (effective within 30 days after another quarter's end), which per §8.3 fall at 2 of 4 quarter ends; if the computed set disagrees with that count at authoring, the computed set is the expectation and the landing records the difference. The expected cite set is computed at load by fa-oracles from the derived rows' dates, the declared closes and the two parameters, never from a run. - So the N is B(entry_class), not unconditional. Its mutation twin (§3.7 item 3) is the Adjusting cell: it flips the one attribute the mechanism names and must report. A1c's twin fields: `twin_kind = "mutation"`, `twin_attribute = "entry_class"`, `twin_value = "Adjusting"`, `twin_expect = "reports"`; `mechanism = "crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:689"` (the class gate). **L-D-01** (`[[expectation]] id = "L-D-01"`, `type = "D"`, `book_variant = "ledger"`, `procedure = "jet.period_end_timing"`, `version = 1`, `granularity = "dated_aggregate"`; derived entries; lowest rank). - Tier C; claim `statistical`; calibration `corpus`; `window_days` default 3 (`registries/procedures.toml:50-64` at 8196f5e40). - Predicate: an entry is cited iff `days_to_end = period_end − 1 − effective_date` is in [0, `window_days`) (`crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:189-190`; a period's `end` is exclusive), with severity the constant Low (`jet.rs:199`) and statistic `days_to_period_end` = that value (`jet.rs:200`), citing the entry and its period. - `[[target]]` rows: one per ledger row the predicate selects (the opening `A17E-` row included: the procedure reads every live posting, `crates/fa-lantern/src/jet.rs:181`), computed at load by fa-oracles from the rows' dates and the book's quarter ends (no registered §2.4 rule names this predicate; the computation is the code's rule above, and A5a's `inside_window{window_days}` class rule where it applies). Statuses: cite Sd (derived entries under `difference` and the declared encoding), severity S (Low), statistic Sd. The expectation also requires that no other row is cited. - The claim holds only for quarter ends with observations inside the window, and renders "on derived net-change entries from a dated aggregate series". K-ERRRATE renders the `corpus` clause. - Reference differential (A4r): the cite set is compared with `fa_reference::lantern::period_end_timing` (`crates/fa-reference/src/lantern.rs:108-117`); `disagree` is FAIL. - A11a's witness applies (at least 2 runs, so 2 book ids, and its harness-only variants on filler accounts that start with `9`), as M-D-01 requires on `ledger` (§9.3). **Tier rows (A4).** `jet.period_end_timing` and `events.subsequent` must record `reads_evidence = false`; otherwise no D or N row may sit on `ledger` (§2.5, M0). **Capabilities.** The `case.toml` `capabilities` tokens L4 adds (A1a's `:[@]`; L2 lists the rest): `procedure:events.subsequent@1`, `procedure:jet.period_end_timing@1`, `refusal:FA-REF-010`, `verb:document` (`attest manual --plan-out`), `verb:commit`, `verb:period` (soft-close, close), `verb:batch` and `verb:finding` (record). ## Tests & logging **Run.** - `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact lehman` (the Lehman `#[test]`, A7a; whole case runs; under 60 s warm). - `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- lehman_neg_` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_lehman`. **Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; these are the values each field must contain; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `/`, a FAIL or UNRUN reason in A7a's trailing `reason=` field): ``` PASS L-N-01 N native A17-P8-ENTRY/default kind=no_refusal target=admitted,exit=0 twin=refused FA-REF-010 exit=7 (harness-observability, period_state_at_commit=Closed) PASS L-N-02 N ledger -/entry_class=Original kind=no_finding events.subsequent@1 target=no finding twin=reported (entry_class=Adjusting) PASS L-N-02 N ledger A17E-chg-/entry_class=Adjusting events.subsequent@1 cite=B:[A17E-chg-,period:,period:] severity=B:High statistic=B:subsequent_event_amount= PASS L-D-01 D ledger A17E-chg-/default jet.period_end_timing@1 cite=Sd:[A17E-chg-,period:] severity=S:Low statistic=Sd:days_to_period_end=<0|1|2> ref=agree ``` one Adjusting-cell line per predicted repurchase row and one L-D-01 line per predicted row, plus the generated `L-SELF-native` and `L-SELF-ledger` lines (A7a) and A16's `L-N-90` line per book. Until OD 2b: `UNRUN L-N-02 N ledger -/entry_class=Original reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` (and the same for the Adjusting cell) and `UNRUN L-D-01 D ledger -/default reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS, while L-N-01 runs and PASSes. **Load-time negatives** (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_lehman.rs`, in-memory copy with one edit, each naming the check, the row and its line): - `lehman_no_refusal_n_on_ledger_fails_k_evid`: L-N-01 declared with `book_variant = "ledger"` → K-EVID refuses. - `lehman_reads_evidence_tier_row_on_ledger_fails_k_evid`: a test copy of `events.subsequent`'s tier row with `reads_evidence = true` → K-EVID refuses L-N-02 on `ledger`. - `lehman_d01_predicted_set_tracks_window`: the load-time predicted cite set at `window_days` 3 vs 4 differs exactly by the rows with `days_to_end = 3` (a unit test of the computation, on the synthetic fixture series until OD 2b commits the rows and on the committed rows after; it vendors no Valukas data). **Run-time negatives** (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, temp copy of the case, one edit, each asserting the named lines and a non-zero case verdict). `lehman_neg_n01_twin_into_open_period` lands now; the three ledger negatives need committed rows, so they land in the OD 2b landing that commits them (as M7's `blmis_neg_one_cent`), and `lehman_d01_predicted_set_tracks_window` exercises the same prediction meanwhile, never as a vacuous UNRUN-only test: - `lehman_neg_n01_twin_into_open_period`: the twin's flipped value set to Open (its twin book leaves `FY2008Q2` Open) → the twin is admitted, no `FA-REF-010` is observed, and `FAIL L-N-01 … twin=admitted` (vacuous N). - `lehman_neg_d01_date_moved_across_window`: one row's `effective_date` moved across its quarter's last-3-days boundary → the observed cite set equals the predicted set with exactly that row toggled, and `FAIL L-D-01 …` names it. (If a load-time check ties an intent's date to its fact, the move cannot be planted at run time: a receipt cannot be regenerated in a test, since tests never read the cache (§4.3), so the negative becomes a load-time test asserting that check's refusal; either way the committed data is untouched.) - `lehman_neg_d01_window_param_4`: the `finding_record jet.period_end_timing@1` step given `params = ["window_days=4"]`, which the runner passes as `fa finding record jet.period_end_timing --param window_days=4` (`registries/verbs.toml:881`) → the observed set equals the load-time prediction at 4, and the window-3 expectation FAILs. A1b's `[[step]]` has no parameter field today, so this requires A1b to accept `params` (a one-line array of `name=integer`) on a `finding_record` step and A7a to pass each as `--param`. - `lehman_neg_n02_twin_not_flipped`: the twin's flipped value set back to `Original` → the twin reports nothing, and `FAIL L-N-02 … twin=not reported` (a twin that does not flip the mechanism's attribute makes the N vacuous). **JSONL log** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord`/`VerdictRecord`; copied to `$FA_CASES_LOG_DIR/lehman.jsonl` when set; path printed at the end; argv printed on FAIL): on `native`, `verb = "period"` (open, soft-close, close), `verb = "document"` (attest manual `--plan-out`, `exit = 0`) and `verb = "commit"` for the entry (`exit = 0`), and `verb = "document"` for the twin on its own book (`book_variant = "native~twin"`, A11c, after that book's `FY2008Q2` soft-close and close; `exit = 7`, `refusal_id = "FA-REF-010"`, at its planning step; twin steps are logged but never rendered); on `ledger`, one `verb = "batch"` record (the batch's idempotency key in `argv_redacted`, `exit = 0`), `verb = "period"` opens and soft-closes, `verb = "finding"` records with `finding_procedure = "jet.period_end_timing"` and `"events.subsequent"`, and `branch_class = "entry_class=Adjusting"` on every step of the Adjusting build; the per-book invocation count and wall time (A7c). ## Notes - **Why each edge exists:** - **L2:** the Lehman case scaffolding (`case.toml`, the engagement and the stubs) is first created there. This is a reading; the plan does not state the reason. - **M0:** the `ledger` variant and its K-EVID clause. - **A4:** the tier rows and `reads_evidence`. - **A11a:** invariance. - **A11c:** the mutation twins. - **H18 (`related`, already in the graph):** L-N-02 is its regression oracle; no blocking edge (§15 H18: "L4 re-checks L-N-02 when it lands"). - **No H6 edge.** H6 is research into a kernel law, an intent-bound Canon family or a Lantern detector (§13); whichever lands flips L-N-01. The edge L4 ← H6 was removed from the plan (§15 L4). - **Owner decision (OD 2b).** It gates committing the dated series (L1), and so the ledger rows' committed form. Until it is decided, L-D-01 and L-N-02 cannot run offline (tests never read the cache), print UNRUN and stay unclaimed (§3.2b; see the ledger book above). OD 2b is not a bead edge. - **Reason code (OD 5 / H14).** `InternalTransfer` is used until `NotInPublicRecord` exists. The assertion carries `--statement "reconstruction placeholder: ⟨…⟩"` (§2.7). - **Plan vs code (path (b)'s closed periods).** Plan §8.3 says path (b) reads which periods are closed. At 8196f5e40 it lists every period with any recorded transition (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:646-655`: `!trs.is_empty()`, under the comment "Identify closed/soft-closed periods"); the snapshot records every `PeriodTransition` control (`crates/fa-lantern/src/snapshot.rs:136-157`), and a period open commits one (`crates/fa-journal/src/period.rs:288-330`). So an opened, never-closed period also counts. L4 follows the code in its prediction and soft-closes every quarter but the last, so the expected set does not depend on which reading holds. The mismatch is product bead H18 (fa-yugf.98, `related`), whose fix selects only periods whose latest transition is SoftClosed, Closed or Locked; L-N-02 is its regression oracle (see L-N-02 above). - **Native ManualAssertion flow (§3.3).** A ManualAssertion is bound to one sealed proposal, so the entry and its twin each go through `fa document attest manual … --plan-out` and (for the admitted entry) `fa commit --plan`, each with its own idempotency key; the twin is never committed. - **Names.** Generated rows are `L-SELF-native`, `L-SELF-ledger` and `L-N-90` (the case letter, as §5.1's `-NOTE-NN` is `W-NOTE-01`); intent ids follow L1's fact ids (`A17-P8-ENTRY`, `A17E-chg-`), this round's convention. - **Related links added in round 4.** The OD bead (L-D-01 and L-N-02 wait on OD 2b) and H14 (L-N-01's entry uses `InternalTransfer` until `NotInPublicRecord` exists, OD 5).
acceptance_criteria:

Until OD 2b, L-D-01 and L-N-02 print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS, and are unclaimed until the landing that commits the rows; L4 cannot close before they PASS.

title: [cases] M0: ledger book variant: schema, reads_evidence tier field, fa batch row posting within budget, and K-EVID's ledger clause
description:
## Why
BLMIS Exhibit B is the only real, row-level transaction data in the program: 3,793 rows across 13 accounts in 3 complaints (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §9.4). The `ledger` variant (§3.2) is how such rows enter a book:
- **No filler.** The rows are the population.
- **Evidence.** Each row cites the citation stub of the exhibit it reproduces (§2.7).
- **Allowed rows.** Only procedures that do not read evidence may carry D or N there, because every row's evidence is a self-uploaded stub (§2.5 `reads_evidence`, §2.7).

The Lehman net-change entries derived from a `dated_aggregate` series also use it (L-D-01, L-N-02, and L3's optional L-R-03).

Claim types it hosts: T, C and R, plus D and N of non-evidence-reading procedures. Never P, never CF. M0 is harness capability: schema, posting path, load-time rule and budget. The real Exhibit B rows post in M2a–M2c, which depend on M0 (§15 M0); M0 itself measures the budget on a same-shape fixture.

## What to build
**`ledger` in `crates/fa-oracles` (module `cases`).** `[book] variant = "ledger"` in `books/<stem>.toml` (§3.2a; the stem is `ledger`, and the kind is the stem's prefix), with the §3.2 rules enforced at load:
- each row's evidence is the citation stub of its exhibit (`fa:case-source-stub:v1`, `AgentUpload`, Reviewed by `case-second-reader`; `[[document]]` rows with `stub_of` = the complaint's source id);
- no filler variant may be declared;
- allowed rows: T, C and R, plus D and N of procedures whose tier row records `reads_evidence = false`. No P, no CF, no `no_refusal` N, no evidence-reading D/N.

**Row → intent mapping (the ledger schema §15 M0 assigns here; §3.2a has no ledger-specific table, so the field names are this bead's proposal and A1b's loader must accept them).** Ledger rows are facts by reference (M2t's generated `exhibit_b_rows.toml`), never 3,793 hand-written `[[intent]]` rows. A `[[ledger_map]]` row per trustee account declares how its rows become entry intents:
- `source` (the complaint `[[fact]]` id), `account` (the trustee account id, e.g. `1ZR176`), `book_account` (its investor account code: the trustee id where the chart accepts it, else a declared code mapped 1:1), `party` (the `[[party]]` id of the account's holder, below), `cash_account` (the code holding the `cash` role), `transfer_account` (the declared counterpart of TRANS rows: an account with neither the `cash` nor the `investor_capital` role), and `amount_columns` (the layout's principal-movement columns by printed header, from M1).
- **Parties (§3.2a).** One `[[party]]` row per trustee account: `id` (e.g. `P-1ZR176`), `label` = the account holder's role label from `roles.toml` (§2.8; names appear only as hashed K-NAMES tokens), `kind` (as `fa party add` accepts), `relations = []` (a ledger carries no ownership edges). One party per account is AN-401's rule (§9.3: v3 retains every party with attributed cash in as an investor, so the book holds only customer cash movements, one party per account). The runner creates each with `fa party add` before the first batch.
- The runner renders one two-leg entry intent per row: the investor leg on `book_account` (Equity type or the `investor_capital` role, `role_map`, interpretive) with leg `party` = the account's `[[party]]` id (the party dimension `ponzi.net_investment` and `numbers.relative_size_factor` read), and the contra leg, with no party, on `cash_account` (cash rows) or `transfer_account` (TRANS rows); `class` = `Original` (the CLI's default when `class` is absent, `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:7514-7520` at 8196f5e40; a batch admits only Original, Adjusting, Reversal, Pending or Resolution members, `registries/verbs.toml:263`); `effective_date` = the row's printed date; `evidence` = the complaint stub, carried in each member (`fa batch` takes no `--evidence`, and its usage puts evidence in each member intent, `registries/verbs.toml:345`, `:350`); intent id `<account>:<page>:<line>` (the row's identity: rows are facts by reference, so the id names the row it posts, as §3.2b names an intent by its fact). The rendered JSON is a derived artifact and is never committed (§3.1).
- Running principal is compared under a declared sign rule (`[[default]] attribute = "sign"`: the printed balance against the investor account's credit-normal running balance), stated once in the book file, never by flipping posted amounts.
- A ledger book may instead, or also, carry ordinary authored `[[intent]]` + `[[leg]]` rows when its population is a short derived series rather than an exhibit: Lehman's 56 net-change entries derived from Appendix 17 §E (L4, §8.3a). They obey the same clauses (no filler, each row citing its exhibit's stub, K-EVID's ledger clause) and post through the same `batch` step, keyed `<case>:ledger:<batch label>:<first 16 hex of the batch body's SHA-256>` (≤ 64 bytes).

**Pending rows: an uncommitted rows file (OD 2b; §3.2b).** Tests never read the fetch cache (§4.3), and committing a whole exhibit's rows waits for OD 2b. So a ledger book whose complaint rows fact names a `rows_file` that is not in the embedded index (BLMIS before OD 2b) still loads: its header, periods, accounts, parties, documents, `[[ledger_map]]` and `[[step]]` rows are committed, and the cited cell-level values are committed as literal values (§1.3). The runner builds no book for that variant and prints every expectation on it, generated rows included (`M-SELF-ledger`, `M-N-90`), as `UNRUN <id> <type> ledger <target>/<cell> reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS. This is not A1c's `[[branch_cell]] pending` field (§5.1, PLAN_DELTA after polish round 4): no authored field marks these rows (the loader finds the file absent, A1a's `rows_committed = false`), their reason is never `needs:<item> (<what>)`, and `PendingClaimed` does not police them; a premature claim is caught by A7a's completeness rule instead (a claimed UNRUN fails the case `#[test]`). Such rows join `case.toml` `claims` only in the landing that commits the rows under OD 2b; until then they are unclaimed, so their UNRUN does not fail the case `#[test]` (A7a: an unclaimed row fails it only on FAIL), and the harness and fixtures land on main meanwhile. The `_selftest` fixture generates its rows, so it is never pending. A1a (`rows_committed = false`), A3a (K-BIND reports the rows fact unexamined, never PASS for it), A10a (`examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, never a skipped row) and A7a (the runner's OD 2b UNRUN) now accept an uncommitted `rows_file`; requires A3a/A10a to count every fact derived from a pending rows fact (K-DERIVE) as a pending input the same way, since A10a's exception names only the rows fact itself.

**Batch posting.** `[[step]] kind = "batch"` posts rows through `fa batch --intent <batch.json>` (`registries/verbs.toml:342-351`; usage at `:350`).
- The batch shape is `{"idempotency_key": "...", "intents": [<entry intent>, ...]}`.
- A member that refuses refuses the batch and names its index, and nothing is posted (`crates/fa-journal/src/batch.rs:255-260`: "batch member {index}: …; nothing in the batch was recorded"). An identical retry returns the recorded outcome (`batch_posted` with `already_recorded = true`, `registries/verbs.toml:1932-1935`). A single entry intent (a document with no `intents` array) is refused (`crates/fa-cli/src/typed.rs:854-858`), but a one-member batch is admitted (`PostBatch::new` takes 1..=`max_batch_entries` members, `crates/fa-intents/src/lib.rs:560-577`), so an account with one row, or the last batch of a split, still posts through `fa batch`.
- At most 8,190 entries per batch (`registries/limits.toml:99-101`, `max_batch_entries`). An account's rows post as one batch when they fit, as every BLMIS and every fixture account does (§15 M0's "at most one batch per account"); an account of more than 8,190 rows would split, in row order, into ⌈n / 8,190⌉ batches (`ledger_batches_split_at_8190`). Each batch has a derived idempotency key of at most 64 bytes (`registries/limits.toml:33-35`, `max_idempotency_key_bytes`), e.g. `<case>:ledger:<account>:<first 16 hex of the batch body's SHA-256>`. Each member intent carries its own derived key too, a pure function of its row identity (e.g. `<case>:<account>:<page>:<line>`, at most 64 bytes): an entry intent without `idempotency_key` is refused (`crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs:7596`), and two members sharing one key refuse the batch (`crates/fa-intents/src/lib.rs:593-597`; `registries/verbs.toml:263`: members are entries "of one principal with distinct keys").
- The runner (A7a) replays these steps and logs one JSONL line per batch.

**Calendar.** `calendar = "custom"`, an opening date before the earliest row, and one period per calendar year the rows span, each created (`fa period create --fiscal-year N`) and opened (`fa period open`), because periods are born `Future` and admit nothing (`registries/admissibility.toml:55`). The yearly grain is a declared book-context choice: it bounds the number of period-ending balances M3 bundles.

**`reads_evidence`.** The two-reader boolean on `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_procedure_tiers.toml` rows (A4 records it, §2.5) becomes required for any expectation on a `ledger` or `statement` variant. A missing value is refused.

**K-EVID's ledger clause (§3.6):**
- no P, CF, `no_refusal` N or evidence-reading D/N on a `ledger` variant;
- `about = "reconstruction"` rows are exempt;
- the self-disclosure procedure `jet.self_sourced_evidence` runs on the variant through the runner-generated row (§2.7, A7a): `M-SELF-ledger` on BLMIS, `L-SELF-ledger` on Lehman, `_selftest-SELF-ledger` on the fixture.

**The same-shape fixture (the positive).** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/_selftest/books/ledger.toml` (`kind = "harness_selftest"` in `_selftest/case.toml`: no sources, never rendered, exempt from K-BASIS by kind). 13 synthetic accounts, 13 synthetic `[[party]]` rows (one per account, harness role labels) and 3,793 rows, the shape of §9.2: five accounts carry the row counts §9.2 states (117, 75, 51, 57 and 1,050), and the fixture declares its own counts for the other eight (2,443 rows in total), since §9.2 gives none for them. Rows are generated at load as a pure function of SHA-256(`_selftest` ‖ `ledger` ‖ seed) (amounts are integers in cents, dates fall in the fixture's periods, a few TRANS rows between fixture accounts), so no rows file is committed for the fixture. It uses the same `[[ledger_map]]` path as the real book: the generated rows carry M2t's `[[row]]` fields and render through the same code. Because `_selftest` has no sources and no rows fact, the fixture declares its population instead of naming one (field forms this bead's proposal; requires A1b to accept them on a `harness_selftest` case only): each fixture `[[ledger_map]]` row names `source = "synthetic"` (as a synthetic intent's `fact`, A1b) and its account's row count `rows = <n>`; the seed is a constant of the generator; and every generated row cites one `[[document]]` stub whose `stub_of` is a `synthetic` `[[fact]]` of `_selftest` (`facts.toml`, with its `src/cases/embedded.rs` line; A1b's fact-stub form), reviewed by `case-second-reader`, so `_selftest-SELF-ledger` sees reviewed `AgentUpload` stubs and reports Medium (`registries/procedures.toml:105`). Its `period_open` and `batch` steps name `case-poster-1` (A8a's harness label) as their `principal`, as M3's do. Naming a rows fact instead would make the fixture pending (above), which it never is.

**Budget.** Under 60 s per case on a warm worker (§16). A7c's per-book invocation count and wall time are logged.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
- `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- ledger_` (the load-time unit tests below, next to the ledger-variant loader in module `cases`).
- `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact _selftest` (the `_selftest` case's `#[test]`, named after its directory, §3.2b), and `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- _selftest_neg_ledger_` for the run-time negative. Builds go through `rch`.

**fa-oracles unit tests, each a planted negative on an in-memory copy (asserting the check id, the row id and its line in A3a's form `FAIL <K-ID> <file>:<line> <row>: <reason>`):**
- `ledger_evidence_reading_d_refused`: a D whose procedure's tier row has `reads_evidence = true` declared on `ledger` → `FAIL K-EVID books/ledger.toml:<line> <expectation id>: …`;
- `ledger_p_refused`, `ledger_cf_refused`, `ledger_no_refusal_n_refused`: a P, a CF and a `no_refusal` N on `ledger`, each → K-EVID;
- `ledger_reconstruction_row_exempt` (positive): an `about = "reconstruction"` D on `ledger` loads;
- `ledger_filler_variant_refused`: a filler variant declared on `ledger` → refused, naming the variant;
- `ledger_missing_reads_evidence_refused`: a `ledger` expectation whose procedure's tier row lacks `reads_evidence` → refused, naming the tier row;
- `ledger_map_unknown_account_refused`: a `[[ledger_map]]` row whose `book_account` is not in the chart → refused;
- `ledger_map_transfer_account_with_cash_role_refused`: a `transfer_account` holding the `cash` role → refused (TRANS rows must not look like cash);
- `ledger_batch_key_derivation`: the derived batch key is a pure function of the batch body (same body → same key; one cent changed → different key) and is at most 64 bytes, and every member key is at most 64 bytes and distinct within its batch;
- `ledger_batches_split_at_8190`: an account of 8,190 rows renders as one batch, and a synthetic account of 16,381 rows as batches of `[8190, 8190, 1]` (no batch above `max_batch_entries`); every real BLMIS account is one batch (the three complaints hold 3,793 rows in all, fewer than 8,190);
- `ledger_fixture_shape`: the generated `_selftest` fixture has 13 accounts, 13 parties (one per account) and 3,793 rows, and two loads with the same seed are byte-identical;
- `ledger_map_party_missing_refused`: a `[[ledger_map]]` row whose `party` names no `[[party]]` row → refused (`DanglingKey`), naming the row; and `ledger_two_accounts_one_party_refused`: two `[[ledger_map]]` rows naming one party → refused (AN-401's one party per account);
- `ledger_pending_rows_file_loads_and_reports_unrun` (positive): a copy whose rows fact names a `rows_file` absent from the embedded index loads, and the check report counts that fact as a pending input in A10a's form (`examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=1 (OD 2b)`), never examined and never PASS; the runner-level UNRUN lines are the pending-rows rule above.

**Runner test (`_selftest`, through the real binary).**
- Expected output (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `<target>/<cell>`; the values are what each field must contain):
  - `PASS _selftest-SELF-ledger D ledger -/default jet.self_sourced_evidence@1 cite=S:[every row posting] severity=S:Medium statistic=…` (A7a spells the self-test's generated id `_selftest-SELF-<variant>`; §3.2b gives `_selftest` no letter);
  - the A7c per-book summary `BUDGET _selftest ledger book=<n> invocations=<n> wall_ms=<n>` (13 `fa party add` steps, 13 `batch` steps, 3,793 entries) and `BUDGET _selftest total_ms=<n> warm_invocation_ms=<n> budget_ms=60000 PASS`;
  - `fa verify book --json` exit 0.
- Run-time negative `_selftest_neg_ledger_unbalanced_member_refuses_the_batch`: on a temp copy, the rendered `batch.json` of one account (a derived artifact, §3.1) has one member's investor leg raised by 0.01 before its `fa batch` step runs → that step exits 3 with `refusal_id = FA-REF-001` (UNBALANCED, `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:25`; balance law, `crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2086`) and a message naming the member index; `fa tb` afterwards shows no posting from that batch (the account's balance is zero), and the test asserts both. No case-file edit can plant this (a `[[ledger_map]]` row renders both legs from one amount, and A1b refuses an unbalanced authored intent at load, `Unbalanced`); requires A7a to let this test edit a rendered step input, which `run_planted`'s case-file edits (`PlantedEdit { file, old, new }`) do not cover.
- **JSONL (§3.5).** One StepRecord (`record = "step"`) per step: per `party add` step `verb = "party"`; per batch step `verb = "batch"`, `exit`, `elapsed_ms`, `book_variant = "ledger"`, `filler_variant` empty, `binds` mapping each row's `$<account>:<page>:<line>` placeholder to the `batch_posted.members` entry that produced it; the refusing member's step adds `refusal_id = FA-REF-001`. Runner-level records relied on: the period label → CLI code map per book (A7a), the fact↔vid map, and the per-book invocation count and wall time (A7c). On FAIL `REPRODUCE fa --book <retained dir> batch --intent …` is printed; the last line is `LOG <jsonl path>` (copied to `$FA_CASES_LOG_DIR/_selftest.jsonl` when set).

## Notes
- **Why each edge exists:**
  - **A1b:** the book-variant schema the `ledger` kind extends.
  - **A4:** the tier rows and `reads_evidence`.
  - **A7a:** the runner core and verb table.
- **K-EVID ownership.** K-EVID is A3c's check, and §15 gives M0 no ← A3c edge. A3c's bead now carries the ledger clause itself (its `ledger` bar, `no_refusal_n_on_a_ledger_variant_fails_k_evid`, `ledger_row_citing_another_stub_fails_k_evid`); whichever of A3c and M0 lands first implements it, and the other adds only its own tests.
- **Settled: the positive is a same-shape fixture.** §15 M0: "a same-shape fixture of 3,793 rows over 13 accounts posts within budget, at most one batch per account. The real Exhibit B rows post in M2a–M2c, which depend on M0." The real rows exist in a test only after M2t extracts them and OD 2b admits committing them (tests never read the cache, §4.3).
- **Settled: the M2b/M2c edges.** The bead graph now carries M2a, M2b and M2c ← M0, matching §15 M0's text; the round-1 note about a missing edge is withdrawn.
- **Names.** Book variant stems follow §3.2b (`<kind>[-<suffix>]`: `ledger`, `migration`); the `[[ledger_map]]` table and its field names are this bead's proposal (§3.2a has no ledger-specific table); A1b now accepts them and checks their codes, party and `transfer_account` role. Generated ids carry the case letter from `case.toml` (`M-SELF-ledger`, `L-SELF-ledger`, `M-N-90`; §3.2b).
- **Parties.** A1b accepts §3.2a's `[[party]]` shape (`id`, `label`, `kind`, `relations`, with its `<kind>:<party id>;basis=<code>;valid_from=<date>` tokens) and the leg `party` field, the old `[[party_relation]]` table folded into `relations`; a ledger book's `relations = []` needs no token.
- **Checked at 8196f5e40.** `fa batch` row `registries/verbs.toml:342-351` (usage `:350`); `batch_posted` event `:1932-1935` (`already_recorded`); member refusal `crates/fa-journal/src/batch.rs:252-260` ("batch member {index}: …; nothing in the batch was recorded", `:255`); `FA-REF-001` UNBALANCED `refusal_catalog.toml:25`, exit `refusal` (3), raised at `crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:2086`; `max_batch_entries` 8190 `registries/limits.toml:99-101`; `max_idempotency_key_bytes` 64 `:33-35`.
- **Shared variant.** L4 and every M expectation item build on this variant.
acceptance_criteria:

A7c's `BUDGET` lines log the invocation count and wall time, `_selftest-SELF-ledger` prints PASS, and `fa verify book --json` exits 0.
- [ ] positive: `[[ledger_map]]` renders each row as one two-leg intent (investor leg carrying the account's `[[party]]` id; cash or transfer contra with no party), and the `ledger_*` fa-oracles unit tests pass (batch key derivation, the 8,190 split, the fixture's shape and determinism, one party per account).
