title: [cases] M1: BLMIS sources and receipts: Picard v. Glantz (Exhibits B-1..B-6), Square One, Magnify; layouts, footnotes and rounding note as facts
description:
## Why
Case M (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §9) is the receiver or trustee case (§12.3). It contributes footing, C rows and the transfer gap (§18 item 4). Its sources are the trustee's avoidance complaints, with per-account Exhibit B ledgers hosted outside PACER at `madofftrustee.com` (§1.1). Their assertion status is `trustee_computation` (an allegation in a complaint), rendered "the trustee computed" (§2.2).

Every M row rests on these sources: T (M-T-01..03), C (M-C-01), D/N (M-D-01, M-N-01, M-D-10…). The research re-verified 3 complaints, 13 accounts and 3,793 rows (DEBATE-001, §9.2). Exhibit B is the only real row-level data in the program (§9.4).

## What to build
**Files.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/blmis/case.toml` (M1 is the first item to commit files under `cases/blmis/`, so it authors the header the loader needs: `id = "blmis"` (the directory name, §3.2b), `letter = "M"` (prefixes every BLMIS expectation and generated id), `title`, `version`, `kind = "case"`, `scope`, `claims = []`, `capabilities = []`, `pinned_commit`, `variants = []`; the first of M2a–M2c, which creates `books/ledger.toml`, adds `"ledger"`, and M3 adds the ledger claims and capabilities), `sources.toml`, `roles.toml`, the source-level `[[fact]]` rows in `facts.toml` (the per-row facts are M2a–M2c's), the generated `receipts.toml`, and each file's line in `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/embedded.rs` (A1a's index test fails on an unlisted file). A1a loads `letter`, refuses a `case` without one, and takes the id prefix from it (§3.2b).

**`sources.toml`** (every §4.1 field; §9.1):
- **SRC-BLM-001.** Picard v. Glantz et al., complaint, Exhibits B-1 … B-6.
  - madofftrustee.com `008796-glantzcomplaint10-05394docket93.pdf`; SHA-256 `751a8a55bf02b022076af39c8637086630090b41164f70e2a04184c0d003dec1`.
  - 9 columns, ending "Balance of Principal | 2-Year Fraudulent Transfers - Fictitious Profits" (no 6-year column).
  - `trustee_computation` (allegation in a complaint).
- **SRC-BLM-005.** Picard v. Square One Fund (`009665-squareonecomplaint10-04330docket0167.pdf`).
  - 12 columns, including a 6-year column; 709 cells marked `*` under footnote [1].
  - `trustee_computation`.
- **SRC-BLM-006.** Picard v. Magnify (Adv. 10-05279).
  - 11-column layout, including "Six Year Transfers"; the note "Numbers might not add to totals shown due to rounding."
  - `trustee_computation`.
- **In re BLMIS, 654 F.3d 229.** The net-equity method, cited in `ponzi.net_investment`'s doc comment at `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:2653-2654` (and in its `registries/procedures.toml:1628` row summary). `court_ruling`, with a sources row only when the case quotes the opinion.
- **Excluded: SRC-BLM-004** (the "United Congregations" file). It is a SIPC reply memorandum with no Exhibit B, so it is not a case source. Record the exclusion in the ledger's comments.
- Per row: `retrieval_route = original` when fetched directly from madofftrustee.com, the hosting publisher, so `original_hash_compared = true`; `filed_on` = the complaint's filing date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), read at fetch from the filed copy's docket header, never guessed (§4.1: K-VINTAGE orders vintages by `filed_on`/`restates`; there is no BLMIS restating vintage, but every filing carries the date); `restates = []`; `format = pdf`; `extraction` = `pdftotext -layout` + its version + the SHA-256 of the extracted text; `redistribution_basis` from §4.1's closed set, `public-record/court` or `third-party-hosted` (a bankruptcy-court filing hosted by the trustee rather than the court; the author records which, with §1.3's two facts in `notes`: 11 U.S.C. §107(a) makes bankruptcy-court filings public records, which is a statement about access, not copyright; madofftrustee.com publishes no terms of use the research could find); `assertion_status = trustee_computation`; `assurance` empty (not a filer statement); `status = OK`.
- `anchor_scheme` per row (§4.1's five kinds): `page{printed page, line range}` for the footnotes and Magnify's rounding note (prose, sentence-aligned), and `table_cell{table, row label, column label}` for the column headers and the per-row cells (value-bound by exact cell text, not sentence alignment).

**Source-level facts, with receipts** (granularity `ledger_row` for all of them, §2.3's value for BLMIS Exhibit B: "layout facts" is not one of A1a's six granularities, which K-PROV checks against the closed set, and `statement_line` would bring A1a's `cell` key, `<line>@<date or period label>`, which a header or footnote does not have):
- each complaint's column headers in printed order, one `table_cell` fact per header (row label `header`, column label = its printed ordinal). These are the layouts M2t's tool names: Glantz 9, Square One 12, Magnify 11;
- the Exhibit B footnotes [1]/[2] read by the interpretive `trustee_transfer_credit` rule: credit = min(statement amount, max(0, originating principal)) (§2.4), one `page` fact per footnote sentence;
- Square One's footnote [1] (the `*` cells), a `page` fact;
- Magnify's rounding note (cited by M-C-01), a `page` fact whose `about_scope` is the Magnify exhibit.
- Hash-first (§1.3, §4.4): each fact carries `anchor_kind`, `anchor`, `quote_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the normalized span, computed at authoring) and `about_scope`; no `quote` text until OD 2a (and OD 3 where the span names an account holder).

**`roles.toml`.** Account holders are role-labelled: their names appear in Exhibit B headers (§2.8). Account numbers such as `1ZR010` are trustee identifiers and are kept. The K-NAMES deny list is stored as SHA-256 hashes of normalized name tokens, never in clear. The harness labels `case-poster-1` (M3's poster: it posts every batch and runs the `period_open` steps), `case-second-reader` and `case-approver-*` (for M6's migration approvals) are declared here too, because A1b resolves every `[[principal]] label` against `roles.toml` (a label it does not hold is a `DanglingKey`).

**Receipts.** `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch blmis`, then `extract blmis`, then `verify blmis`, with the project User-Agent and at most 1 request per second. `pdftotext -layout` extracts the PDFs; if it is absent the tool prints `UNRUN ` and exits 4 (A9's environment exit), never 0. Until OD 2a, `verify` enumerates the sentence-aligned spans at each prose anchor in the normalized extraction and selects the one span whose SHA-256 equals the fact's `quote_sha256` (zero or several matches is a FAIL); a `table_cell` fact is found by exact cell text at its anchor. `receipts.toml` (regenerated whole, never hand-edited) gets one `[[receipt]]` per sourced fact: `source`, `fact`, `anchor`, `verified_utc` (the cache entry's fetch time), `tool_version`, `extraction_sha256`, `quote_sha256`, `values_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the fact's committed literal values and `about_scope`, so an edit after `verify` is caught offline), `alignment` (`sentence` for the `page` facts, `value` for the `table_cell` header facts), the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`, and `original_hash_compared` copied from the source row (§4.4). Anchor strings use A1a's grammar (`page` = `p<printed page>:l<first>-<last>`, `table_cell` = `<table>|<row label>|<column label>`, here `ExhibitB-<n>|header|<ordinal>`).

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
- Authoring: `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py fetch blmis && python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py extract blmis && python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py verify blmis` → exit 0, no `FAIL ` line. Byte identity: copy `receipts.toml`, re-run `verify` on the unchanged cache, `cmp` the two (identical, because `verified_utc` is the fetch time).
- Second reader (§4.5): a second agent, with a second `$FA_CASES_CACHE`, runs the same three commands; its receipts must equal the author's except `verified_utc`.
- Offline: `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` (A10a), and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_blmis` (the load-time negatives below).

**Expected output.** The authoring tool prints one `VERIFY <fact> PASS` line per fact and exits 0. The offline check report (A3a/A10a own the format; the values are what each field must contain): `CHECK blmis K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, `CHECK blmis K-BIND PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, `CHECK blmis K-SCOPE PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, `CHECK blmis K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<n>/<n>`, each with n > 0 over the source-level facts (a check is UNRUN only when the case has no rows of its input kind; `examined` below the input count is a FAIL), `SOURCE SRC-BLM-00<k> original_hash_compared=true route=original` for each of the three rows, and `EXCERPTS blmis facts_with_quote=0 words=0`. Every receipt has `alignment` = `sentence` (the `page` facts) or `value` (the header cells), all four binding booleans true, `values_sha256` equal to the hash of the fact's committed values and scope, and `original_hash_compared = true` as copied from its route-`original` source row.

**Planted negatives.**
- Authoring-time, each on a temp copy of the case directory against the real cache, with the `FAIL ` line and exit code recorded in the landing:
  - one `sha256` altered in `sources.toml` → `fetch blmis` prints `FAIL ` naming SRC-BLM-00n and exits 1;
  - a fact whose `quote_sha256` is the hash of the fragment "Numbers might not add to totals" of Magnify's note → `verify` prints `FAIL ` (no sentence-aligned span matches) for that fact;
  - a header fact whose cell text is not at its `table_cell` anchor → `verify` prints `FAIL ` naming the fact and anchor.
- Offline, in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_blmis.rs` (each edits an in-memory copy and asserts the check id, the row id and its line):
  - `blmis_receipt_quote_hash_mismatch`: a receipt whose `quote_sha256` differs from its fact's → K-BIND FAIL naming the fact;
  - `blmis_receipt_flipped_boolean_fails`: a receipt with `values_in_quote = false` → K-BIND FAIL;
  - `blmis_header_value_edited_after_verify_fails`: one header fact's committed cell value edited (one word of a Glantz header) while its receipt is unchanged → K-BIND FAIL naming the fact (`values_sha256` mismatch), offline;
  - `blmis_rounding_note_scope_edited_after_verify_fails`: the rounding-note fact's `about_scope` changed to the Glantz exhibit → K-BIND FAIL (`values_sha256` covers `about_scope`);
  - `blmis_receipt_alignment_wrong_kind_fails`: a header (`table_cell`) receipt with `alignment = "sentence"` → K-BIND FAIL naming the fact and its anchor kind;
  - `blmis_fact_citing_excluded_source_is_refused`: a fact citing SRC-BLM-004 (absent from the ledger) → refused, naming the fact;
  - `blmis_name_in_role_text_fails`: a role label carrying a deny-listed token → K-NAMES FAIL.
- **Logging.** The tool's stdout follows the gate vocabulary (`FAIL `/`UNRUN` at column 0); `receipts.toml` is the durable record. The case runner's JSONL log does not involve this item (tests never read the cache, §4.3).

## Notes
- **Edge.** ← A9 (the tool, its normalization, sentence alignment and receipt writer).
- **Owner decisions.**
  - OD 2b is in §15's ← list for M1: it gates committing whole numeric exhibits, that is, all Exhibit B rows (§14 item 2b). It therefore governs M2a–M2c's committed form, not M1's source rows. It is a `related` link, not a bead edge.
  - OD 3 gates quote text containing the account holders' names.
  - OD 2a gates quote text generally.
  - OD 1 does not gate this item: the sources are not on sec.gov.
- **Settled by the plan as it now reads.** Receipts carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`, plus the copied `original_hash_compared`, which is not a binding boolean (§4.4); `table_cell` facts bind by exact value (`alignment = "value"`, §4.1); before OD 2a a fact is found by hash among the sentence-aligned spans at its anchor (§4.4). Sources carry `filed_on` and `restates` (§4.1). A1a (Receipt and Source types), A9 (writer) and A3a/A10a (K-BIND reads `values_sha256`) now carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned` (round 2's `sentence_aligned` is gone from all four).
- **OD 2b at run time (§3.2b).** Tests never read the cache; until OD 2b allows committing the rows, every BLMIS expectation prints `UNRUN <id> … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` and is unclaimed (M0's pending-rows rule). This item's source-level facts and receipts are committed now.
- **Checked at 8196f5e40.** `ponzi.net_investment`@3 (`registries/procedures.toml:1628`) cites 654 F.3d 229 in its summary and at `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:2653-2654`; A9's tool exits are 0 / 1 `FAIL ` / 4 `UNRUN ` / 2 usage.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `crates/fa-oracles/cases/blmis/sources.toml` carries SRC-BLM-001, -005 and -006 with every §4.1 field (route `original`, `filed_on` read at fetch, `restates = []`, five-kind `anchor_scheme`) and SHA-256s matching the captured bytes, and records SRC-BLM-004's exclusion and its reason; `case.toml` declares `id = "blmis"` and `letter = "M"`.
- [ ] positive: the layout headers (9 / 12 / 11 `table_cell` facts), the footnotes and Magnify's rounding note have receipts with `alignment` = `value` (headers) or `sentence` (notes), all four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) true, `values_sha256` equal to the hash of each fact's committed values and scope, and `original_hash_compared = true` as copied from the source row, from the author and from an independent second reader with a second cache; re-running `verify` on the unchanged cache is byte-identical.
- [ ] positive: `ledgers_validate_offline` prints `CHECK blmis K-PROV|K-BIND|K-SCOPE|K-ANCHOR PASS` with a non-zero examined count equal to its input count over the source-level facts.
- [ ] negative: an altered `sha256` fails `fetch` (exit 1).
- [ ] negative: a note fragment fails `verify` (no sentence-aligned span matches its hash).
- [ ] negative: a header not found at its anchor fails `verify`.
- [ ] negative: offline, a receipt hash mismatch, a flipped binding boolean, a header value or a note's `about_scope` edited after `verify` (`values_sha256` mismatch) and a value-bound receipt with `alignment = "sentence"` each fail K-BIND; a fact citing SRC-BLM-004 is refused; a deny-listed token in role text fails K-NAMES.
- [ ] no-claim: receipts bind quotes to the bytes retrieved from madofftrustee.com. They do not show those bytes equal the court's filed copies, and they say nothing about whether the trustee's computations are right.

title: [cases] M2t: case_fetch.py exhibit-b: Exhibit B layouts to a generated exhibit_b_rows.toml, with structural checks and arithmetic diagnostics
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: on the three fixture documents (9, 12 and 11 columns, declared by printed header), `exhibit-b` writes one `[[row]]` per printed row with every field (`complaint`, `account`, `page`, `line`, `date`, `transaction_description` token, `amount_literal`, `column`, `star`, `balance_literal`, `cells`), including `star = true` on the starred cell. A re-run is byte-identical, the three committed Rust-side fixtures equal the tool's output (`test_rust_fixture_matches_tool_output`), the rows file loads under the fa-oracles TOML subset (`exhibit_b_rows_fixture_loads`), and `rows_sha256` agrees in Python and Rust on one literal digest (`test_rows_block_hash`, `exhibit_b_rows_block_hash_matches`).
- [ ] positive: every named unittest in `tools/case-fetch/test_exhibit_b.py` passes under `python3 -B -m unittest discover tools/case-fetch` (run by A9's gate test), and `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_fetch.sha256` pins every new or changed file under `tools/case-fetch/`. Until OD 2b the real rows file stays in the cache and the expectations built on it print UNRUN (`reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`), never PASS.
- [ ] negative: a planted extra column FAILs (`test_extra_column_fails`).
- [ ] negative: a planted dropped row FAILs (`test_dropped_row_fails`).
- [ ] negative: an unknown layout or header, an unparseable amount, and an unmapped description each FAIL (exit 1); a missing extraction reports UNRUN (exit 4), never 0.
- [ ] negative: a planted balance disagreement (and a footer disagreement) is logged to stderr and does not fail (exit 0).
- [ ] no-claim: the tool shows that rows were extracted under the declared layout with matching counts. It says nothing about whether the trustee's arithmetic closes; that T/C classification is the case's (§9.2).

title: [cases] A3a: load-time checks K-PROV, K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR, K-DERIVE with quote normalization and quote_sha256 binding
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the pilot facts pass K-PROV, K-BIND, K-SCOPE, K-ANCHOR and K-DERIVE. The check report prints `CHECK <K-ID> PASS|FAIL|UNRUN examined=<n>/<inputs>` per check and lists the rows each examined, and a check that examined zero rows reports UNRUN.
- [ ] positive: Rust and Python normalization produce identical bytes, and identical `quote_sha256` values, on the shared `crates/fa-oracles/data/binding_fixtures.toml` rows; sentence alignment and the scope word check agree on its `[[sentence]]` and `[[scope]]` rows.
- [ ] negative: the SEC ¶29 → F12 misbinding fails K-SCOPE; the "entered and approved" fragment fails K-BIND's sentence alignment; a quote occurring twice fails; the FIPS 180-4 vectors fail if altered.
- [ ] negative (derived): a receipt whose found range lies outside the fact's declared anchor, or an anchor kind its source's `anchor_scheme` does not name (`paragraph`, `table_cell` and `xbrl` included), fails K-ANCHOR; a quote-less fact whose receipt records `values_in_quote = false` fails K-BIND; a fact value or `about_scope` edited after `verify` fails K-BIND through `values_sha256`; a receipt whose `alignment` does not match its anchor kind fails K-BIND; a `table_cell` or `xbrl` fact whose value differs from its cell or fact value fails K-BIND; an interpretation with one reader fails K-PROV.
- [ ] negative (derived, §2.1, §3.2b): a quote naming a period outside its `scheme:` range, an inverted range, or a range tail that does not parse fails K-SCOPE, while a rangeless scheme is reported `range=none`; a rows fact whose file is uncommitted, and every fact derived from it, is counted `unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, never examined or PASS, while its receipt is still checked; the rows-fact hash is recomputed over the complaint's exact block bytes; a case-scoped check runs only on its case; an `exhibit` anchor is accepted only on a `rows_file` fact with `alignment = value`; a heading-only line quoted whole is one sentence and any part of it fails alignment.
- [ ] no-claim: K-BIND shows that the vendored values occur in the vendored quote or its receipt. Only the receipt binds the quote to source bytes, and only `original_hash_compared = true` binds those bytes to the publisher's.

title: [cases] M2a: Glantz Exhibit B rows as ledger_row facts (6 accounts), oracle_output flags on trustee-credited transfers, and derived transfer credits
description:
## Why
Picard v. Glantz (SRC-BLM-001) holds six of the case's accounts, every TRANS row, and both transfer pairs recomputable within one complaint (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §9.2). These rows feed:
- M-T-01 on 1T0026, 1ZA192, 1ZB143 and 1ZB010;
- M-C-01 on 1ZR010 and 1ZR176;
- M-T-02 (the 2 pairs);
- M-D-01 (1ZR176) and M-N-01 (the transfer accounts);
- the §9.4 sweep. Glantz alone exceeds Benford's 500-leg minimum.

13 of the trustee's transfer credits can only be copied from the trustee's columns. They must carry `role = "oracle_output"`, so that K-ORACLE lets them feed a T only as named inputs (§2.1, §5.3). Claim types T, C, D and N.

## What to build
**File.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/blmis/facts.toml` (the Glantz rows; M2b and M2c add theirs to the same file). Every row is a scalar or a one-line array (`crates/fa-registry/src/toml.rs:1-9`). Hash-first: no `quote` text (OD 2a, OD 3).

**`[[fact]]` rows authored here:**
- **The complaint rows fact** (one, §15 M2t): `provenance = "sourced"`, `source = SRC-BLM-001`, `granularity = ledger_row`, `rows_file = "exhibit_b_rows.toml"` with `complaint = SRC-BLM-001` (the `ledger_row` facts by reference; A1a's Fact type accepts `rows_file` and `complaint` on a `ledger_row` fact), `anchor_kind = table_cell`, `anchor` = the Exhibits B-1 … B-6 page range, `quote_sha256` = `rows_sha256(SRC-BLM-001)`, M2t's hash of this complaint's contiguous `[[row]]` block (exact bytes, computable by `verify` and by K-BIND alike), and `about_scope` naming the Glantz Exhibit B. Its receipt uses the §4.4 fields: `alignment = "value"`; `aligned` = every row is a whole printed line, never a fragment; `values_in_quote` = every row's amount, balance and date occur at its (page, line) in the extraction; `values_sha256` covers its `about_scope` (it has no `[[value]]` rows; the rows are bound by `quote_sha256`).
- **Committed now, pending until OD 2b (M0's rule).** The rows fact and its receipt are committed now; the rows file is not (OD 2b). K-BIND then checks the receipt's consistency with the fact and counts the rows-hash recomputation as a pending input (`unrun=<k> (OD 2b)` in its CHECK line, A10a), never PASS; every fact below whose `from` includes the rows fact is pending the same way in K-DERIVE.
- **Per-account facts** for the values the expectations read, each `sourced`, `table_cell` (value-bound, anchor `<exhibit>|p<page>:l<line>|<column header>` in A1a's `<table>|<row label>|<column label>` grammar), `granularity = ledger_row`, `about_scope = account:<id>`, their literal values committed now (§1.3): the printed closing "Balance of Principal" of 1T0026, 1ZA192, 1ZB143, 1ZB010, 1ZR010 and 1ZR176; 1ZR010's Deposits footer 5,979,184; and a `derived` fact (`rule = sum`, `from` = the rows fact) for 1ZR010's displayed Deposits rows, 5,979,193 (M4 reads both; pending until OD 2b).
- **TRANS facts** (17 TRANS rows across the 4 transfer accounts: 1T0026 10, 1ZA192 3, 1ZB143 3, 1ZB010 1):
  - 13 `sourced` facts with `role = "oracle_output"`, one per copied transfer amount (1T0026's 10, and one each on 1ZA192, 1ZB143 and 1ZB010), each anchored `table_cell` `<exhibit>|p<page>:l<line>|<column header>` to its row, value committed now;
  - the two recomputable pairs (§9.2), each as: the originating row's statement amount (`sourced`), the originating ledger's printed principal on the row before the transfer (`sourced`), the credit (`derived`, `rule = trustee_transfer_credit`, `from` = those two facts; fact ids `1ZA192>1ZB143@1993-10-20` and `1ZB143>1ZA192@2005-12-23`, M3's M-T-02 targets; recomputable now, since both inputs are cell-level facts), and the receiving row's printed credit (`sourced`, `table_cell` `<exhibit>|p<page>:l<line>|<column header>` at that row's transfer column, value committed now; not `oracle_output`, because the pair recomputes it), which is M-T-02's `published`:
    - 1993-10-20, 1ZA192 → 1ZB143, statement amount 4,000,000, originating principal 4,855,000 → credit 4,000,000 (full credit);
    - 2005-12-23, 1ZB143 → 1ZA192, statement amount 200,000, originating principal (4,854,688) → credit 0.
    The receiving rows' printed credits are committed as these cell facts as well as rows of the rows file, so that M-T-02's `published` is never the rows fact its own legs trace to; M-T-02 (M3) compares the rule's output, taken from the certified principal, with them.
- **Per-account net TRANS principal** (`derived`, `rule = sum` over the account's TRANS-row principal amounts, `from` = the rows fact, so pending until OD 2b), the quantity M-N-01 reads (§9.3: 1T0026 +2,384,266; 1ZA192 −3,462,634; 1ZB010 −200,000; 1ZB143 +3,955,000). Recompute at authoring; a value that differs from §9.3 is committed as the rows give it and M5's expectation is reopened, never silently kept.
- **`same_day_display_reorder`** (interpretive, §2.4): one `derived` fact for 1ZB010's same-day CHECK / STOP PAYMENT pair, naming both rows (page, line) and their computation order, which M3's within-day comparison follows (`from` = the rows fact; pending until OD 2b; posting order cannot carry it, because one batch's members share one recorded sequence and gl detail orders their same-day lines by entry digest, M3). Every claim that uses it names it.

**Accounts (§9.2):**

| Account | TRANS rows | Running sum vs printed balance | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1T0026 | 10 | exact at every row (117) | T footing; its 10 transfer credits are trustee outputs |
| 1ZA192 | 3 | exact (75) | T footing; its transfers include one recomputable pair |
| 1ZB143 | 3 | exact (51) | T footing; as above |
| 1ZB010 | 1 | exact under `same_day_display_reorder` (interpretive; one CHECK/STOP PAYMENT pair) | T footing under a named rule |
| 1ZR010 | 0 | 50/57 rows off cumulatively, closing gap $9; the Deposits footer 5,979,184 agrees with the balance column, while the displayed rows sum to 5,979,193 | C (display unit whole dollars; cause inferred) |
| 1ZR176 | 0 | intermediate gaps ≤ $1, closes at 0 | C |

**`[[ledger_map]]` and `[[party]]` rows** (M0's schema) in `books/ledger.toml` for the six Glantz accounts: one `[[party]]` per account (`id` e.g. `P-1T0026`, `label` = the account holder's role label from `roles.toml`, `kind`, `relations = []`; one party per account, AN-401), and one `[[ledger_map]]` per account: `source` = the complaint rows fact, `account`, `book_account`, `party` (that `[[party]]` id; the rendered investor leg's `party`), `cash_account`, `transfer_account`, `amount_columns` (Columns 4–7, the principal-movement columns, by printed header from M1). This bead uses the M0 edge only to check that every Glantz row maps to exactly one rendered intent. Because A1b resolves every code and party a `[[ledger_map]]` row names and `ledgers_validate_offline` loads every committed book (A10a), the file is committed loadable: whichever of M2a–M2c lands first creates it with M3's `[book]` header (`variant = "ledger"`, `calendar = "custom"`, `base_unit = "USD"`, an opening date before the earliest row of the three complaints) and the two shared accounts (the `cash`-role account and the declared transfer counterpart), and adds `"ledger"` to `case.toml` `variants` (A1a: the header lists the book-variant stems, so it matches the tree from that landing on), and each bead adds the investor-capital `[[account]]` its accounts' `book_account` names (M3's account rules); M3 and M4 add the principals, documents, periods, defaults and steps.

**Names.** Account holders are role labels (§2.8; K-NAMES). The assertion status is `trustee_computation`.

## Tests & logging
**Run.**
- Authoring: `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py exhibit-b blmis` (prints `ROWS SRC-BLM-001 rows=<n> sha256=<hex>`), then `verify blmis` (receipts for every sourced fact above: `alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok` true, `values_sha256` over each fact's committed values and scope, `original_hash_compared` copied from SRC-BLM-001's row); copy `receipts.toml`, re-run `verify`, `cmp` (byte-identical).
- `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_blmis -- glantz_ trustee_transfer_credit_`.

**Expected output** (A3a/A10a own the format; the values are what each field must contain): `CHECK blmis K-PROV PASS examined=<n>/<n>` and `CHECK blmis K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<n>/<n>` over every Glantz fact; `CHECK blmis K-BIND PASS examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=<k> (OD 2b)` (A10a's form), examining the cell-level facts (closing balances, footer, the 13 credits, the pair inputs and the two receiving credits) and counting the rows fact among the `unrun` inputs (never a skipped row); `CHECK blmis K-DERIVE PASS examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, examining the two pair credits and counting the six row-derived facts (the 1ZR010 row sum, the four net-TRANS sums and the reorder fact) as `unrun` until OD 2b, after which all eight are examined (the case totals grow as M2b, M2c, M6 and M7 add theirs). Until OD 2b admits committing `exhibit_b_rows.toml`, the rows fact and every fact derived from it stay pending inputs (tests never read the cache, §4.3), never PASS, while the cell-level facts bind and PASS; the census and mapping tests then run on M2t's committed synthetic fixture (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/exhibit_b/rows_9col.toml`, the Glantz layout) and say so in their output.

**Unit tests (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_blmis.rs`):**
- `trustee_transfer_credit_1993_full_credit`: amount 4,000,000.00, originating principal 4,855,000.00 → 4,000,000.00;
- `trustee_transfer_credit_2005_zero_credit`: amount 200,000.00, principal −4,854,688.00 → 0.00;
- `trustee_transfer_credit_boundary_equal`: amount = principal = 1,000.00 → 1,000.00; principal 0.00 → 0.00; principal 999.99 for amount 1,000.00 → 999.99;
- `glantz_trans_census`: over the Glantz rows (M2t's synthetic 9-column fixture before OD 2b, the committed file after), every TRANS row is covered by exactly one of: an `oracle_output` fact anchored at it, or a recomputable pair (as the pair's originating row, whose statement amount is a pair fact, or as its receiving row, whose printed credit is); the real counts are 17 = 13 + 4, per account 10 / 3 / 3 / 1;
- `glantz_rows_map_one_intent_each`: every Glantz row resolves to exactly one `[[ledger_map]]` row and one rendered intent id (`<account>:<page>:<line>`); a row of an unmapped account fails.

**Planted negatives (load-time, in-memory copies; each asserts the check id, the fact id and its line):**
- `glantz_row_amount_plus_one_dollar_fails`: on a test copy whose rows file is M2t's synthetic fixture (the rows fact's `quote_sha256` and receipt re-pinned to the fixture's `rows_sha256`, so the copy binds), one row's amount changed by $1 → K-BIND FAIL on the complaint rows fact (`rows_sha256` no longer equals `quote_sha256`), naming the fact and line; it runs now, before OD 2b. At authoring, the same edit against the cache makes `verify` print `FAIL ` (value not at its page and line), exit 1;
- `glantz_closing_balance_edited_after_verify_fails`: 1ZR176's committed closing-balance value changed by $1 while its receipt is unchanged → K-BIND FAIL naming the fact (`values_sha256` mismatch), offline (round 2 could catch this only at authoring);
- `glantz_pair_1993_credit_wrong`: the 1993 credit planted as 4,855,000 → K-DERIVE FAIL naming the fact, expected 4,000,000.00;
- `glantz_trans_census_unflagged_fails`: one copied credit's `role = "oracle_output"` removed → `glantz_trans_census` FAILs, naming the TRANS row (account, page, line).

**Diagnostics.** The per-account row counts and running-sum diagnostics that M2t logs must match the table above (on 1ZB010 the display-order sum is expected to be off only within the same-day CHECK / STOP PAYMENT pair, which the reorder rule names), and M2t's `ROWS SRC-BLM-001 rows=<n>` line must read 1,429 ("all 1,429 Glantz Exhibit B rows", §1.3; with §9.2's 117 + 75 + 51 + 57, that leaves 1,129 rows for 1ZB010 and 1ZR176), or the mismatch is recorded in `facts.toml` comments and the account's class re-decided (never silently kept). No runner (`cases.rs`) rows land here.

## Notes
- **Why each edge exists:**
  - **M1:** sources, layouts and footnotes.
  - **M2t:** the rows file.
  - **A3a:** the K-* checks.
  - **M0:** the `ledger` variant and its `[[ledger_map]]` schema these facts post through (§15 M0: "The real Exhibit B rows post in M2a–M2c, which depend on M0"; M2b and M2c carry the same edge).
- **Owner decisions.** OD 2b gates committing the rows (the whole Exhibit B). Until it is decided, the rows file stays in the cache, every runner row that needs it prints `UNRUN <id> … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` and is unclaimed (M0's pending-rows rule; §3.2b), and the facts derived from the rows are pending. The values of the individual facts above (balances, footer, credits, pair amounts) are cited literal values and are committed now like every case's (§1.3). OD 3 gates quote text with names.
- **Receipt shape.** Receipts carry `values_sha256`, `alignment` and the four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`, plus the copied `original_hash_compared` (§4.4). A1a, A9 and A3a/A10a carry them, and A1a/A3a/A10a accept an uncommitted `rows_file` fact (M0's OD 2b pending rows, which no field declares; not A1c's `[[branch_cell]] pending`). Requires A3a/A10a to count the facts derived from it (K-DERIVE) as pending inputs too: A10a's OD 2b exception names only the rows fact, so the six row-derived facts would otherwise read as an examined count below the input count, a FAIL.
- **Risk: transfer credits.** The 13 non-recomputable credits support only "given the trustee's credits as inputs" statements (K-ORACLE). Nothing here independently computes the trustee's net equity.
- **Field names.** `rows_file` and `complaint` (A1a), the `[[ledger_map]]` fields and §3.2a's `[[party]]` shape (A1b) are accepted by their foundation beads.
- **Rows-fact anchor.** A1a's `table_cell` grammar is `<table>|<row label>|<column label>` and its `page` grammar names one page, so neither spells the Exhibits B-1 … B-6 page range; requires A1a (and K-ANCHOR, A3a) to give a whole-exhibit `rows_file` fact an anchor form.
- **Row selections.** A2's `sum` adds its inputs; the 1ZR010 row sum and the four net-TRANS sums select rows of the rows fact (account, column, and the `TRANS` token), so requires A2's `sum` to take that selection as `params` when its input is a rows fact.
- **Hash definition.** The rows fact's hash is M2t's `rows_sha256` (exact bytes of the complaint's contiguous row block), replacing round 2's "as `fa_registry::toml` canonically re-serializes them", which Python's `verify` could not compute without porting `Document::canonical_bytes`.
- **Owner-decision link (round 4).** Related to the OD bead: §14 item 2b names M2a–M2c as gated by OD 2b (committing the Exhibit B rows).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the Glantz facts load: the complaint rows fact (bound by `rows_sha256` and its receipt; a pending input, counted `unrun=<k> (OD 2b)` by K-BIND and never PASS, until OD 2b commits the rows file, as are the facts derived from the rows in K-DERIVE; expectations on them print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`), the per-account closing balances and 1ZR010's footer, the 13 `oracle_output` credits, both pairs, the per-account net-TRANS sums and the 1ZB010 reorder fact, with receipts carrying `alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans (`quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok`) true, `values_sha256` over each fact's committed values and scope, and `original_hash_compared` as copied; one `[[party]]` per Glantz account.
- [ ] positive: both transfer credits recompute under `trustee_transfer_credit` (4,000,000.00 and 0.00), and the `trustee_transfer_credit_*` unit tests pass, boundary cases included. `glantz_trans_census` covers all 17 TRANS rows (13 flagged + 4 pair rows; 10 / 3 / 3 / 1 per account) and `glantz_rows_map_one_intent_each` maps every row to one intent.
- [ ] positive: the per-account counts and diagnostics agree with §9.2's table (exact on 1T0026, 1ZA192 and 1ZB143; exact under the named rule on 1ZB010; the stated gaps on 1ZR010 and 1ZR176), and the Glantz total is 1,429 rows (§1.3), or the mismatch is recorded and the class re-decided.
- [ ] negative: a $1 row change fails K-BIND on a fixture-backed copy, offline, now (`glantz_row_amount_plus_one_dollar_fails`); a closing balance edited after `verify` fails K-BIND through `values_sha256` (`glantz_closing_balance_edited_after_verify_fails`).
- [ ] negative: a wrong derived credit fails K-DERIVE (`glantz_pair_1993_credit_wrong`).
- [ ] negative: a stripped `oracle_output` flag fails the TRANS-row census test (`glantz_trans_census_unflagged_fails`).
- [ ] no-claim: the facts reproduce what the trustee's exhibits print (`trustee_computation`, in a complaint). They say nothing about whether the trustee's net-equity determinations or the 13 copied credits are right.

title: [cases] M2b: Square One Exhibit B rows as ledger_row facts (account 1FR048, 12-column layout, 709 starred cells under footnote [1])
description:
## Why
Picard v. Square One Fund (SRC-BLM-005) supplies account 1FR048: a C account with a $3 closing drift (cumulative metric: 1,010/1,050 rows off, max $3) (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §9.2). Its rows feed M-C-01 (C) and the §9.4 sweep (D/N, `record_label = "silent"`).

Its layout carries a 6-year column and 709 cells marked `*` under footnote [1]. Any expectation that reads a starred cell must name that footnote in its premises (§15 M2t).

## What to build
**File.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/blmis/facts.toml` (the Square One rows; same file as M2a and M2c). Hash-first: no `quote` text (OD 2a, OD 3).

**`[[fact]]` rows authored here:**
- **The complaint rows fact** for SRC-BLM-005, as M2a's: `provenance = "sourced"`, `source = SRC-BLM-005`, `granularity = ledger_row`, `rows_file = "exhibit_b_rows.toml"`, `complaint = SRC-BLM-005`, `anchor_kind = table_cell`, `anchor` = the Exhibit B page range, `quote_sha256` = `rows_sha256(SRC-BLM-005)` (M2t's hash of this complaint's contiguous `[[row]]` block), `about_scope` naming the Square One Exhibit B. Committed now and pending until OD 2b, with its receipt checked for consistency (M0's pending-rows rule; M2a).
- **Per-account facts** for 1FR048: the printed closing "Balance of Principal" (`sourced`, `table_cell` `<exhibit>|p<page>:l<line>|<column header>`, value-bound, `about_scope = account:1FR048`), its literal value committed now (§1.3).
- **The starred cells.** They stay in the rows file with `star = true` and their printed amount (M2t); this bead adds no per-cell fact. A census test counts the cells carrying the `*` marker (over each row's printed `cells`, M2t) and must find 709 (§9.1), or the mismatch is recorded.
- **The footnote premise: a load check this bead adds to module `cases`.** Square One's footnote [1] is M1's source-level fact. Square One's only account is 1FR048, whose rows hold all 709 starred cells (§9.1, §9.2), so every expectation whose basis, or one of whose `[[target]]` bases, reaches the SRC-BLM-005 rows fact or a fact derived from it reads starred cells and must list the footnote [1] fact id in `premises` (§15 M2t: "An expectation that reads a starred cell names the footnote in its premises"). Otherwise it is refused at load (`StarPremiseMissing`, this bead's error name), naming the expectation and, where the rows are present, the first starred row's page and line. The rule needs no committed rows, so it binds before OD 2b.

**`[[ledger_map]]` and `[[party]]`** (M0's schema) in `books/ledger.toml` for 1FR048: one `[[party]]` (`id = "P-1FR048"`, `label` = the account holder's role label, `kind`, `relations = []`; one party per account, AN-401) and one `[[ledger_map]]`: `source` = the complaint rows fact, `account = "1FR048"`, `book_account`, `party = "P-1FR048"`, `cash_account`, `transfer_account`, `amount_columns` (the principal-movement columns by printed header, M1). The file is committed loadable as M2a states (the first of M2a–M2c to land creates its `[book]` header and the shared `cash` and transfer accounts); this bead adds 1FR048's investor-capital `[[account]]`.

**Layout.** 12 columns, including the 6-year column, named by the complaint's own headers (M1).

**Names.** Role labels and K-NAMES as for M2a. The assertion status is `trustee_computation`.

## Tests & logging
**Run.** `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py exhibit-b blmis` and `verify blmis` at authoring (receipts with `alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok` true, `values_sha256` over each fact's committed values and scope, and the copied `original_hash_compared`; a second `verify` on the unchanged cache is byte-identical under `cmp`); offline `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_blmis -- square_one_`.

**Expected output** (A3a/A10a own the format): `CHECK blmis K-PROV|K-BIND|K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<n>/<n>` (n > 0, over every BLMIS fact the check reads). Until OD 2b commits the rows file, K-BIND counts the complaint rows fact as a pending input (`examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, A10a), never examined and never PASS.

**Diagnostics.** M2t's logged row count and running-sum diagnostic for 1FR048 must show §9.2's figures (1,050 rows; 1,010 rows off; max $3; $3 closing drift), or the mismatch is recorded in `facts.toml` comments and the class re-decided.

**Planted negatives (load-time, in-memory copies, in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_blmis.rs`):**
- `square_one_row_amount_plus_one_dollar_fails`: on a test copy backed by M2t's synthetic 12-column fixture (`rows_12col.toml`; the rows fact re-pinned to its `rows_sha256`), a row amount changed by $1 → K-BIND FAIL on the complaint rows fact (`rows_sha256` ≠ `quote_sha256`), naming the fact and line; runs now;
- `square_one_closing_balance_edited_after_verify_fails`: 1FR048's committed closing-balance value changed by $1 while its receipt is unchanged → K-BIND FAIL naming the fact (`values_sha256` mismatch), offline;
- `square_one_star_read_without_footnote`: a test expectation whose basis is the Square One rows fact and whose `premises` omit footnote [1] → refused at load (`StarPremiseMissing`), naming the expectation (on a copy backed by `rows_12col.toml`, also the first starred row's page and line); runs now;
- `square_one_star_count` (positive): the starred-cell count is 709 on the committed rows after OD 2b (before it, the census runs on `rows_12col.toml` against that fixture's declared count and says so);
- `square_one_star_marker_removed_fails`: a copy with one `*` marker removed fails the census, naming the expected and found counts (its own test, so its slug carries a ratchet token, `scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`).

## Notes
- **Edges.** ← M1 (sources and the footnote fact), M2t (the rows), A3a (the checks) and M0 (the `ledger` variant and its `[[ledger_map]]` schema these facts post through).
- **Settled: the M0 edge.** §15 M0's text ("The real Exhibit B rows post in M2a–M2c, which depend on M0") and the bead graph now agree: M2b ← M0. The round-1 note that this item had no M0 edge is withdrawn.
- **Owner decisions.** OD 2b gates committing the rows; until then runner rows that need them print `UNRUN <id> … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` and are unclaimed (M0's pending-rows rule; §3.2b). The 1FR048 closing balance is a cited literal value and is committed now (§1.3). OD 3 gates quote text with names.
- **Requires.** A1a, A9 and A3a/A10a carry the receipt fields `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned` and accept an uncommitted `rows_file` fact (M0's OD 2b pending rows, not A1c's `[[branch_cell]] pending`), and A1b accepts §3.2a's `[[party]]` shape; the rows fact's page-range anchor still needs the A1a anchor form M2a's Notes name.
- **Consumers.** M4 (M-C-01) and M7; each of their expectations over 1FR048's rows lists the footnote [1] fact in `premises` (the load check above).
- **Owner-decision link (round 4).** Related to the OD bead: §14 item 2b names M2a–M2c as gated by OD 2b (committing the Exhibit B rows).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the Square One facts load: the complaint rows fact (bound by `rows_sha256` and its receipt; a pending input counted `unrun=<k> (OD 2b)` by K-BIND, with expectations on it printing `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS, until OD 2b), 1FR048's printed closing balance (receipt with `alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans true, `values_sha256` matching), its `[[party]]` row, and a starred-cell census of 709; the starred cells carry `star = true`, and the logged diagnostics reproduce §9.2's figures for 1FR048 (1,010/1,050 rows off, max $3, $3 closing drift) or the mismatch is recorded.
- [ ] negative: a $1 row change fails K-BIND on a fixture-backed copy (`square_one_row_amount_plus_one_dollar_fails`); a closing balance edited after `verify` fails K-BIND through `values_sha256` (`square_one_closing_balance_edited_after_verify_fails`).
- [ ] negative: a starred-cell read without footnote [1] in its premises is refused (`square_one_star_read_without_footnote`).
- [ ] negative: a removed `*` marker fails the 709-cell census (`square_one_star_marker_removed_fails`).
- [ ] no-claim: the facts reproduce the trustee's printed rows. They say nothing about the meaning of the `*` footnote beyond its words, or about the trustee's computation.

title: [cases] M2c: Magnify Exhibit B rows as ledger_row facts (1FN025, 1FN097, 1FR051 exact; 1FN024, 1FN037, 1FN073 off by -$42, +$16, +$1)
description:
## Why
Picard v. Magnify (SRC-BLM-006) supplies six accounts (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §9.2):
- **three T accounts**, whose pure running sums match the printed balances exactly: 1FN025, 1FN097, 1FR051. They feed M-T-01;
- **three C accounts**: 1FN024 (−$42), 1FN037 (+$16) and 1FN073 (+$1). They feed M-C-01, citing Magnify's note "Numbers might not add to totals shown due to rounding."

All six feed the §9.4 sweep. Claim types T, C and D/N.

## What to build
**File.** `crates/fa-oracles/cases/blmis/facts.toml` (the Magnify rows; same file as M2a and M2b). Hash-first: no `quote` text (OD 2a, OD 3).

**`[[fact]]` rows authored here:**
- **The complaint rows fact** for SRC-BLM-006, as M2a's: `provenance = "sourced"`, `source = SRC-BLM-006`, `granularity = ledger_row`, `rows_file = "exhibit_b_rows.toml"`, `complaint = SRC-BLM-006`, `anchor_kind = table_cell`, `anchor` = the Exhibit B page range, `quote_sha256` = `rows_sha256(SRC-BLM-006)` (M2t's hash of this complaint's contiguous `[[row]]` block), `about_scope` naming the Magnify Exhibit B. Committed now and pending until OD 2b, with its receipt checked for consistency (M0's pending-rows rule; M2a).
- **Per-account facts**: the printed closing "Balance of Principal" of each of the six accounts (`sourced`, `table_cell` `<exhibit>|p<page>:l<line>|<column header>`, value-bound, `about_scope = account:<id>`), literal values committed now (§1.3).
- **Per-account closing drift** (`derived`, `rule = difference`: the displayed rows' running sum minus the printed closing balance, `from` = the rows fact and the account's closing-balance fact, with the sign convention declared once in `facts.toml` comments) for 1FN024, 1FN037 and 1FN073, which must equal §9.2's −$42, +$16 and +$1, and 0 for 1FN025, 1FN097 and 1FR051; recompute at authoring and record any mismatch. The values are committed now; because their input includes the rows, K-DERIVE lists them as pending until OD 2b (M0's rule) and recomputes them once the rows are committed.
- **TRANS rows.** §9.2 leaves them "(per account, at authoring)". Every trustee-credited transfer amount copied from the exhibit is a `sourced` fact with `role = "oracle_output"` (`table_cell` `<exhibit>|p<page>:l<line>|<column header>`, value committed now), unless a named rule derives it; the per-account TRANS counts found at authoring are recorded in `facts.toml` comments.
- **The rounding note** is M1's source-level fact; M4 cites it.

**`[[ledger_map]]` and `[[party]]`** (M0's schema) in `books/ledger.toml` for the six accounts: one `[[party]]` per account (`id` e.g. `P-1FN024`, `label` = the account holder's role label, `kind`, `relations = []`; one party per account, AN-401) and one `[[ledger_map]]` per account: `source` = the complaint rows fact, `account`, `book_account`, `party` (that `[[party]]` id), `cash_account`, `transfer_account`, `amount_columns` (the principal-movement columns by printed header, M1). The file is committed loadable as M2a states (the first of M2a–M2c to land creates its `[book]` header and the shared `cash` and transfer accounts); this bead adds the six accounts' investor-capital `[[account]]` rows.

**Layout.** 11 columns, including "Six Year Transfers" (M1).

**Names.** Role labels and K-NAMES. The assertion status is `trustee_computation`.

## Tests & logging
**Run.** `python3 -B tools/case-fetch/case_fetch.py exhibit-b blmis` and `verify blmis` at authoring (receipts with `alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans `quote_found_once`, `aligned`, `values_in_quote`, `scope_ok` true, `values_sha256` over each fact's committed values and scope, and the copied `original_hash_compared`; a second `verify` on the unchanged cache is byte-identical under `cmp`); offline `cargo test -p fa-oracles -- --exact ledgers_validate_offline` and `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_blmis -- magnify_`.

**Expected output** (A3a/A10a own the format): `CHECK blmis K-PROV|K-BIND|K-ANCHOR PASS examined=<n>/<n>` (n > 0, over every BLMIS fact the check reads). Until OD 2b commits the rows file, the complaint rows fact (K-BIND) and the six drift facts (K-DERIVE) are counted as pending inputs (`examined=<n>/<inputs> unrun=<k> (OD 2b)`, A10a), never examined and never PASS; after it, K-DERIVE examines the six drift facts too.

**Diagnostics.** M2t's diagnostics must show exact running sums on 1FN025, 1FN097 and 1FR051, and closing drifts of −$42, +$16 and +$1 on 1FN024, 1FN037 and 1FN073, or the mismatch is recorded and the account's class re-decided.

**Planted negatives (load-time, in-memory copies, in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_blmis.rs`):**

- `magnify_closing_balance_edited_after_verify_fails`: 1FN024's committed closing-balance value changed by $1 while its receipt is unchanged → K-BIND FAIL naming the fact (`values_sha256` mismatch), offline;
- `magnify_trans_census` (positive, the census the next negative breaks): over the Magnify rows (`rows_11col.toml` before OD 2b, the committed file after), every TRANS row is covered by exactly one fact anchored at it, an `oracle_output` fact or a named rule's fact, and the per-account TRANS counts equal those recorded in `facts.toml` comments;
- `magnify_trans_census_unflagged_fails`: a copied transfer credit without `oracle_output` (and no named rule) → the Magnify TRANS-row census FAILs, naming the row (account, page, line);
- `magnify_drift_wrong`: on the fixture-backed copy (now), a fixture account's drift fact planted one dollar off its rows' value → K-DERIVE FAIL naming the fact, expected and computed; after OD 2b the same test also plants 1FN024's drift as −$41 → K-DERIVE FAIL, expected −42.00.

## Notes
- **Edges.** ← M1 (sources and the rounding-note fact), M2t (the rows), A3a (the checks) and M0 (the `ledger` variant and its `[[ledger_map]]` schema these facts post through).
- **Settled: the M0 edge.** §15 M0's text and the bead graph now agree: M2c ← M0. The round-1 note that this item had no M0 edge is withdrawn.
- **Owner decisions.** OD 2b gates committing the rows; until then runner rows that need them print `UNRUN <id> … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` and are unclaimed (M0's pending-rows rule; §3.2b). The closing balances and copied credits are cited literal values and are committed now (§1.3); the drift values are committed now and recomputed by K-DERIVE once the rows are committed. OD 3 gates quote text with names.
- **Requires.** A1a, A9 and A3a/A10a carry the receipt fields `values_sha256`, `alignment` and `aligned` and accept an uncommitted `rows_file` fact (M0's OD 2b pending rows, not A1c's `[[branch_cell]] pending`), and A1b accepts §3.2a's `[[party]]` shape. Still required: A3a/A10a to count facts derived from a pending rows fact (the six drift facts) as pending inputs, since A10a's exception names only the rows fact; A2's `difference` to take one account's running sum over the rows (a row selection, as M2a's `sum`) when an input is a rows fact; and the A1a anchor form for the rows fact's page range (M2a's Notes).
- **Consumers.** M3 (M-T-01), M4 (M-C-01) and M7.

title: [cases] M3: BLMIS M-T-01 footing (certified gl detail running principal = every printed balance) on 7 accounts; M-T-02 on the 2 transfer pairs
description:
## Why DEBATE-001 ruled that a ledger whose opening balance plus its displayed rows equals every printed day-end balance is a bridge T (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §5.5). The same ruling refuted "Exhibit B is an exact T oracle on every account": 6 of 13 tested accounts drift by $1–$42 (H-022). So M-T-01 runs only on the 7 accounts whose rows close exactly. - **M-T-01's predicate names the trustee's transfer credits as inputs** (K-ORACLE). It reproduces the exhibit's own arithmetic exactly. It is not an independent reproduction of the trustee's net-equity determination on transfer accounts. - **M-T-02** is the independent part: the two intra-complaint pairs recomputed from their originating ledgers under a named interpretive rule. Both are T rows, an exact observation that is replayable and refolded by `fa-verify` (§5.3). ## What to build **Files.** In `crates/fa-oracles/cases/blmis/`: `case.toml` (authored by M1 with `id = "blmis"`, `letter = "M"`, `kind = "case"`; M3 adds the declared capabilities, §12.2 (`variants = ["ledger"]` arrives with `books/ledger.toml`, from the first of M2a–M2c), and adds M-T-01/M-T-02 to `claims` only in the OD 2b landing that commits the rows, §3.2b), `books/ledger.toml` (M0's variant; M2a–M2c commit its `[book]` header, accounts, parties and `[[ledger_map]]` rows so the file loads at each of their landings, and M3 adds the principals, documents, defaults, periods and the T accounts' steps below), and the M-T-01 / M-T-02 rows of `expectations.toml`, each with its line in `src/cases/embedded.rs`. **`books/ledger.toml`** (§3.2a plus M0's `[[ledger_map]]`): - `[book] variant = "ledger"`, `calendar = "custom"`, `base_unit = "USD"`, an opening date before the earliest row; one `[[period]]` per calendar year the rows span (labels such as `1992`; the runner maps each to the code `fa period create` reports and logs the map), each created and opened. - `[[principal]]`: `case-poster-1` (a Human with `post`; the label M1 declares in `roles.toml`; it posts every batch and runs the `period_open` steps), `case-second-reader` (reviews the three complaint stubs). No filler variant. - `[[account]]`: one investor-capital account per trustee account (Equity type or the `investor_capital` role, `role_map`, interpretive; `name_fact` = the account's per-account fact), one account holding the `cash` role, one declared transfer counterpart (no `cash` or `investor_capital` role). Account holders appear only as role-labelled parties: the `[[party]]` rows M2a and M2c author (one per account, §3.2a `id`/`label`/`kind`/`relations`), named by each investor leg's `party`; the runner creates them with `fa party add` before the first batch. - `[[document]]`: one citation stub per complaint (`stub_of` = SRC-BLM-001 / -005 / -006, `grade = AgentUpload`, `reviewed_by = case-second-reader`); every row cites its exhibit's stub. - `[[ledger_map]]`: the rows M2a–M2c author for all 13 accounts; M3 posts the seven T accounts (M4 adds the six C accounts' `batch` steps). - `[[default]]`: the sign rule (the printed principal against the investor account's credit-normal running balance) and the period grain, each with its rationale. - `[[step]]`: `period_open` per year, then one `batch` per account in account order (each batch ≤ 8,190 entries, derived key; each `period_open` step names its `principal`, which A1b requires on a step that runs no intent, and each `batch` step names the poster in A1b's optional step `principal`, since a rendered ledger intent has no `[[intent]] principal`). 1ZB010's batch is rendered like the others: the computation order of its same-day CHECK / STOP PAYMENT pair (the `same_day_display_reorder` fact) enters through the within-day comparison of the certified read below, because posting order inside one batch does not order gl lines (every member commits at the batch's one recorded sequence, `crates/fa-journal/src/batch.rs:706-711`, and gl detail breaks the tie by entry digest, `crates/fa/src/general_ledger.rs:355-363`). **M-T-01** (`[[expectation]]`: `type = T`, `kind = footing`, `book_variant = ledger`, `granularity = ledger_row`, `basis` = the Glantz and Magnify complaint rows facts (SRC-BLM-001, -006) and the per-account closing balances, `published` per target = that account's closing-balance fact (M2a, M2c; never the rows fact, to which every leg on the account traces, so K-TAUT, A3b, would re-type the row R; the earlier printed balances are the rows' `balance_literal`, which no leg posts, since `amount_columns` names only the principal-movement columns), `inputs_named` = every `oracle_output` credit fact on the seven accounts (M2a's 13 Glantz credits, plus any credit M2c flags on 1FN025, 1FN097 or 1FR051; an unnamed one re-types its target C, K-ORACLE), `vintages = ["exhibit:SRC-BLM-001", "exhibit:SRC-BLM-006"]` (A1c's `:`; `exhibit` is A3b's K-VINTAGE role for a footing), `assurance` = none (`trustee_computation`)). One `[[target]]` per account: 1T0026, 1ZA192, 1ZB143, 1ZB010 (under the interpretive `same_day_display_reorder`, named in the target), 1FN025, 1FN097 and 1FR051, each with its first and last row dates. - **Predicate.** "given the trustee-credited transfer amounts (Columns 4–7) as inputs, franken_accounting's certified running principal equals every printed balance". - **Certified read.** One `fa gl detail --account --from --to --certify` per account. Rows are matched to gl lines by entry key, never by position: `gl_line` carries `entry_digest`, `leg_index`, `debits`, `credits` and `running_balance` (`registries/verbs.toml:3227-3229`), and a row's digest is the `entry_digest` of its `batch_posted.members` entry (`batch_member`, `:3102-3104`; M0's `binds`). gl detail orders an account's lines by effective day, recorded sequence, entry digest and leg ordinal (`crates/fa/src/general_ledger.rs:4-6`, sort at `:355-363`), and all members of one batch share its recorded sequence (`crates/fa-journal/src/batch.rs:706-711`), so rows of one date appear in entry-digest order, which is not the exhibit's order and varies between runs (the digest covers the book id, `crates/fa-model/src/entry.rs:1951-1954`, and book ids are random, §3.4). Each printed balance (`balance_literal`, M2t, under the book's sign rule) is therefore compared one of two ways: - **day-end:** the printed balance of a date's last displayed row equals the certified `running_balance` after that date's last gl line (order-invariant; §5.5's "every printed day-end balance"); - **within the day:** every earlier row's printed balance equals the certified day-opening balance (the previous date's last `running_balance`, or the line set's opening) plus that date's certified movements (`debits` − `credits`) up to and including the row, taken in the exhibit's display order (for 1ZB010's pair, the computation order the `same_day_display_reorder` fact declares). These comparisons compose certified values in an order the harness takes from the exhibit; a non-last line's own `running_balance` is never compared. - `fa replay C:` must reproduce the certificate. - **Independent refold.** At each printed balance that ends a period (the last row of each year), `fa bundle produce --account --from --to --balance :USD:` (`registries/verbs.toml:780-784`) is verified in-process by `fa_verify::verify_bundle`, and the refolded balance must equal the printed value. **M-T-02** (a T over the interpretive rule, rendered with the rule's name; §5.3's five kinds do not cover it, so it is A1c's `kind = "rule"` with `rule = "trustee_transfer_credit"`, template `T.rule`, and `vintages = ["source:SRC-BLM-001"]`, A3b's role for a `rule` kind). Two `[[target]]` rows: - 1993-10-20, 1ZA192 → 1ZB143, $4,000,000: full credit (originating principal 4,855,000); - 2005-12-23, 1ZB143 → 1ZA192, $200,000: credit 0 (originating principal (4,854,688)). - The rule's input is the originating account's certified running principal on the row before the transfer (from the same `gl detail` certificate, composed as in the within-day comparison when that row shares the transfer's date), which must equal M2a's sourced principal; its output must equal the receiving row's printed credit, the target's `published` (M2a's sourced cell fact; never the rows fact, for M-T-01's K-TAUT reason). The read is on the originating account, where the published credit is not posted (K-TAUT). **Witnesses and checks:** - **Contributing-entry witness (A11b).** `fa explain balance --period

--certify --json` at each period-ending coordinate. The contributions must be exactly the account's row postings, and none may carry the printed balance. - **Outsider checks for `ledger` footing (A12, §12.1):** the `gl detail` certificates and account bundles above; the ADS extract (`fa export ads --period

--out

--with-proofs`, then `fa-verify ads --key K`); ADS re-import byte identity; `fa verify export beancount|ads`. - **Second read path (§12.7).** `fa query --certify` on the same coordinates must equal the fold path (an R-class cross-check). - **Integrity.** `fa verify book --json` exits 0. ## Tests & logging **Run.** `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact blmis`; negatives `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- blmis_neg_`; load-time and evaluator tests `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_blmis -- footing_ m_t_0`. **Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; requires A7a to print one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `/`; the values are what each field must contain; `contrib=` is A11b's token and `outsider=:verified|failed` A12's, its read kind here being the gl-detail `fa replay`, the per-period bundle refold and the ADS checks of §12.1; `query=ok`, the §12.7 GQL second read (A12 item 7), is this bead's token, since A12 prints none for it): - `PASS M-T-01 T ledger 1T0026/default kind=footing read=(gl detail --certify,1T0026,..,head) rows=117 matched=117 day_ends= inputs_named=10 contrib=holds outsider=:verified query=ok` (`day_ends` counts the matched balances compared with the certified `running_balance` directly; the rest matched by the within-day composition); - the same for 1ZA192 (`rows=75`, `inputs_named=1`), 1ZB143 (`rows=51`, `inputs_named=1`), 1ZB010 (`rule=same_day_display_reorder`, `inputs_named=1`), and 1FN025, 1FN097, 1FR051 (row counts as M2c records them; `inputs_named` = that account's flagged credits); - `PASS M-T-02 T ledger 1ZA192>1ZB143@1993-10-20/default rule=trustee_transfer_credit principal=4855000.00 value=4000000.00 published=4000000.00`; - `PASS M-T-02 T ledger 1ZB143>1ZA192@2005-12-23/default rule=trustee_transfer_credit principal=-4854688.00 value=0.00 published=0.00`; - `PASS M-SELF-ledger D ledger -/default jet.self_sourced_evidence@1 …` (generated by A7a) and the guidance N `PASS M-N-90 N ledger -/default audit_offered=false placeholder_offered= expected= twin=matcher:reported` (generated by A16, in A16's form). - **Until OD 2b commits `exhibit_b_rows.toml`** (§3.2b), the runner builds no ledger book (M0's pending-rows rule), and every M-T-01 and M-T-02 line, M-SELF-ledger and M-N-90 included, reads `UNRUN ledger /default reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)`, never PASS. These rows join `case.toml` `claims` only in the landing that commits the rows; until then they are unclaimed, so the `blmis` `#[test]` fails only on a FAIL (A7a), and the harness and fixtures land on main as §3.2b intends (this replaces round 2's "the case exits non-zero and stays on a train branch"). The bead's positive cannot be met, and the bead cannot close, before OD 2b. The evaluator unit tests below run now. **Evaluator unit tests (pure, `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_blmis.rs`; inputs are certified-line fixtures, no binary):** - `footing_rows_equal_printed_balances`: three lines whose running balances equal the printed balances → PASS; - `footing_one_dollar_move_fails_first_balance_after`: one row +1.00 → FAIL naming that row's (page, line) and gap 1.00, and every later row off by 1.00; - `footing_matched_by_entry_key`: the same lines in another order still match by entry key; a missing key FAILs; - `footing_same_day_lines_in_digest_order`: three rows on one date whose gl lines arrive in an order other than the exhibit's (as entry digests order them) → the date's last printed balance matches the certified `running_balance` after the last line, the two earlier rows match by the within-day composition in the exhibit's order, and the earlier lines' own `running_balance` values (which differ from the printed ones) are not compared → PASS; - `footing_same_day_reorder`: a 1ZB010-shaped same-day CHECK / STOP PAYMENT pair matches only in the declared computation order; without the rule the intermediate printed balance FAILs; - `m_t_02_rule_over_certified_principal`: principal 4,855,000.00, amount 4,000,000.00 → 4,000,000.00; principal −4,854,688.00, amount 200,000.00 → 0.00. **Planted negatives** (run-time ones edit a temp copy of the case directory and re-pin the copy's `rows_sha256` in its fact and receipt, so load passes and the run itself must catch the edit. They need committed rows, so the `blmis_neg_*` run-time tests land with the OD 2b landing; no vacuous run-time test that can only see UNRUN is landed before it, and the same edits are exercised now by the pure `footing_*` evaluator tests): - `blmis_neg_row_plus_one_dollar`: one 1ZA192 row amount +1.00 → `FAIL M-T-01 T ledger 1ZA192/default … first_mismatch=: value= published=

`, where `:` is the edited row, whose own printed balance is the first to include the change; - `blmis_m_t_01_credit_missing_from_inputs_named_retyped_c` (load-time, offline; a re-type, so the slug carries `missing` for the ratchet, `scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`): one 1T0026 credit removed from `inputs_named` → K-ORACLE (A3b) re-types the 1T0026 target as C, and the other six stay T (requires A3b to re-type per `[[target]]`; its text says "the row"). K-ORACLE reaches a copied credit only through the legs the rows render, and no rows are committed before OD 2b, so until the OD 2b landing the test runs on a fixture-backed in-memory copy (M2a's pattern: the Glantz rows fact backed by M2t's `rows_9col.toml` and re-pinned to its `rows_sha256`; a test `oracle_output` fact anchored at the fixture's TRANS row, a `[[ledger_map]]` row and an M-T-01 target for each fixture account, and that fact in M-T-01's `inputs_named`): removing it re-types the TRANS account's target C and leaves the other fixture target T. The real 1T0026 form joins it in the OD 2b landing. Both need A3b's `posted_from` to put into a ledger-rendered leg's closure, besides the rows fact, every sourced fact anchored at the leg's own row and rendered column (`|p:l|`, the row's `column`, M2a, M2t); without that join no `oracle_output` credit is in any leg's closure and K-ORACLE can never re-type M-T-01. The join stops at the rendered column, so a closing-balance fact ("Balance of Principal", M-T-01's `published`) never enters a leg's closure and K-TAUT keeps the row T; - `blmis_neg_printed_balance_posted`: 1ZB143's rows replaced in the copy by one posting of its printed closing balance on the last row's date → the contributing-entry witness finds a contribution carrying the published value, and, M-T-01 being claimed by then, the line reads `FAIL M-T-01 R ledger 1ZB143/default … contrib=retyped(contribution carries B) reason=retyped T→R contributing_entry` (A11b's token, A7a's claimed re-type; never PASS as T), so the test calls `.expect_err`; - `blmis_neg_pair_principal_low`: an earlier 1ZA192 row edited so that the running principal before 1993-10-20 is 3,999,999.00 → `FAIL M-T-02 … principal=3999999.00 value=3999999.00 published=4000000.00`, and M-T-01 on 1ZA192 FAILs at the edited row (both asserted). **JSONL (§3.5).** Records with `book_variant = ledger`, `filler_variant` empty: `period create`/`period open` per year; `document add` and `document attest review` per complaint stub; one `batch` per account (`exit = 0`, `elapsed_ms`); one `gl detail` per account (`certificate_kind` = the gl-detail report certificate, event `report_certificate`, `registries/verbs.toml:2125-2128`); `replay` per certificate; `bundle produce` per period-ending balance (`certificate_kind` = bundle) and the in-process `fa_verify::verify_bundle` step as A12 logs it; `explain balance --certify` per witness coordinate; `query --certify`; `export ads`, `fa-verify ads`, `verify export`; `verify book`. Runner-level: the period label → code map (A7a), the fact↔vid map (rows by `::`), and A7c's per-book invocation count and wall time (about 3,793 rows once M4 adds the C accounts). On FAIL the exact `fa gl detail …` argv is printed; the log path is printed at the end. ## Notes - **Why each edge exists:** - **M2a, M2c:** the Glantz and Magnify T accounts. - **A3b:** K-BASIS, K-TAUT, K-ORACLE and K-VINTAGE; K-ORACLE decides M-T-01's type (§15 M3: "K-ORACLE decides M-T-01's type"). The plan lists M3 ← A3b and the bead graph carries it. - **A7b:** certified reads, including `gl detail --certify`. - **A11b:** the contributing-entry witness. - **A12:** `gl detail` certificates, account bundles, the ADS extract and `fa-verify`. - **OD 2b.** The rows file is a whole numeric exhibit; until the owner rules, no test can post the real rows (tests never read the cache, §4.3), so this item's runner rows print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` and stay unclaimed (M0's pending-rows rule). The cited per-account values (closing balances, credits, pair inputs) are committed now (§1.3). - **Budget risk.** One bundle per period-ending balance per account multiplies invocations; A7c measures it. A case above the 60 s warm budget fails, never caps silently; the declared yearly grain is the lever (fewer, longer periods), stated with its rationale. - **Not in scope.** §12.6's optional `fa production` set adds no claim. - **Plan vs code: same-day order.** §9.3 says each `gl_line.running_balance` must equal its row's printed balance; at the live tree gl detail sorts one account's lines by (effective day, recorded sequence, entry digest, leg ordinal) (`crates/fa/src/general_ledger.rs:355-363`) and a batch commits at one recorded sequence (`crates/fa-journal/src/batch.rs:706-711`), so that equality is order-independent only on a date's last row. The certified read above compares day-ends directly (§5.5's "every printed day-end balance") and earlier same-day rows by composing certified values in the exhibit's order, and `same_day_display_reorder` selects that order, not a posting order. - **Related.** fa-sa4w: the ledger book joins its bean-check/hledger differential once it exists (UNRUN when the binaries are absent). - **Names.** The directory `blmis`, `letter = "M"` and the `ledger` stem are §3.2b's; the target spellings (account ids for M-T-01; M2a's pair-credit fact ids `1ZA192>1ZB143@1993-10-20` and `1ZB143>1ZA192@2005-12-23` for M-T-02) and the `[[ledger_map]]` fields are this round's choices; requires A1b/A1c to accept them. - **Checked at 8196f5e40.** `gl_line` shape `registries/verbs.toml:3227-3229` (`entry_digest`, `leg_index`, `running_balance`); `bundle produce` row `:776-785` (flags `:780`, usage `:784`, example `--account … --balance :USD:`); `report_certificate` event `:2125-2128`; `gl` row `:583-593` (`gl detail` usage `:592`). - **Owner-decision link (round 4).** Related to the OD bead: case M prints UNRUN until OD 2b commits the rows file (§3.2b), and this bead's positives need the committed rows.
acceptance_criteria:
