title: [cases] C1: LinkedIn PPA: C-T-01 footing with goodwill named as an oracle_output input, C-R-01 goodwill read-back, C-C-01 consideration within ±$50M
description:
## Why This is the CPA-audit (business combination) reader's case (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.3), covering claim types T, R and C. Its book holds a filer's own footing, which offers an agent nothing to find, so Case C has no campaign card (§12.5). The plan types the three rows strictly (§11.1): - **C-T-01** reproduces the filer's own footing, with the filer's goodwill residual named as an input (K-ORACLE). It is not an independent goodwill computation. - **C-R-01.** Reading goodwill back is R, not T. - **C-C-01.** Consideration agrees only at its declared precision, so it is C, never T. ## What to build **Files** in `crates/fa-oracles/cases/mergers/`: `books/statement-linkedin.toml`, `expectations.toml` (C-T-01, C-R-01, C-C-01), `roles.toml` (the harness labels this book uses: `case-preparer-1`, `case-second-reader`, `examiner-witness`, each with its harness description; no report roles, so the K-NAMES deny list holds only the hashed tokens of names the receipted extraction carries, §2.8), additions to C0's `case.toml` (`claims = ["C-T-01", "C-R-01", "C-C-01"]`, the completeness claim A7a enforces; `variants = ["statement-linkedin"]`; declared capabilities as A1a tokens: `verb:statement`, `statement:balance-sheet`, `verb:explain`, `verb:tb`, `verb:query`, `verb:checkpoint`, `verb:bundle`, `verb:replay`, `verb:export`, `export:ads`, `verb:verify`, §12.2); the declared-precision check in fa-oracles' `cases` module with tests in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/case_mergers.rs`; run-time negatives `mergers_neg_*` in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`. The case's `#[test]` there is `mergers`. **`books/statement-linkedin.toml`** (a `statement` variant, §3.2: T, C and R rows only; no filler): - `[book]`: `variant = "statement-linkedin"`, `calendar = "custom"`, `base_unit = USD`, opening date before 2016-12-08. - `[[period]]`: one period whose range contains 2016-12-08, labelled by the case and mapped to its CLI code by the runner; no other posting in it. - `[[account]]`: one per component, typed through X2's `role_map` (`us-gaap-xbrl-v1`; interpretive, named in the claim): cash (Asset, role `cash`), short-term investments, other current assets, PP&E (Asset, role `fixed_asset`), each intangible component (or the intangibles line), goodwill (Asset), short-term debt, other current liabilities, deferred tax, other (Liability); plus one Equity-typed `consideration` account with no role, which every component entry balances against. - `[[principal]]`: `case-preparer-1`, `case-second-reader`, `examiner-witness`; `[[document]]`: the filing's citation stub (`stub_of = SRC-MSFT-LNKD-PPA`, `grade = AgentUpload`, `reviewed_by = case-second-reader`); the provenance engagement with "no materiality stated" (§2.7). - `[[intent]]` per component (C0's fact ids): `id` = `fact` = the fact id (A1b's id rule), `principal = case-preparer-1`, `idempotency_key` an authored key of at most 51 bytes (A1b's limit; the fact ids embed the concept local name and can be longer), `class = Original`, `effective_date = 2016-12-08`, `evidence` = the filing stub; two `[[leg]]` rows: an asset component Dr its account / Cr `consideration`, a liability component Dr `consideration` / Cr its account, `amount_literal` = the committed value. Post the four intangible components where C0 found them tagged, else the 7,887,000,000 line; never both. The total 27,009,000,000 is never posted (K-TAUT), and neither is any of C0's check facts. - `[[step]]`: `period_open`; `engagement_file` (ref = the stub's `[[document]]` id, so the provenance engagement files it, §2.7, A7a); `intent` per component; `checkpoint`. Each step that runs no intent names its `principal` (A1b; `case-preparer-1`). The certified reads below are not steps (A1b's closed step kinds have none): they are the expectations' reads, which the runner runs after the history (A7a, A7b). - The `jet.self_sourced_evidence` self-disclosure row `C-SELF-statement-linkedin` is generated by the runner (§2.7, A7a), not authored here. **C-T-01** `footing`. `[[target]]` `fact` = C0's "Total purchase price" fact, `basis` = the component facts, `inputs_named` = [the goodwill fact] (16,803,000,000, `oracle_output`, the filer's residual: consideration − net identifiable assets; K-ORACLE), `vintages = ["exhibit:SRC-MSFT-LNKD-PPA"]` (A1c's `:`; if C0 recorded a later filing re-tagging a cited cell, K-VINTAGE forces that latest vintage or an explicit `AS REPORTED IN` the earlier one), `assurance` as C0's row records it. Read (A1c's T fields: `read_verb = statement balance-sheet`, `read_target = equity`, `read_coordinate` = the period label, no `read_selector`; `published` = the total fact; `kind = footing`): `fa statement balance-sheet --for

--certify`, line `equity` ("Posted equity", `registries/statements/balance-sheet.toml:28`), which selects only the `consideration` account. It must equal 27,009,000,000 exactly: the certified value equals the published literal at its declared precision with no rounding of the certified side, so a one-cent difference is a FAIL. Components: cash 1,328,000,000; short-term investments 2,110,000,000; other current assets 697,000,000; PP&E 1,529,000,000; intangibles 7,887,000,000; goodwill 16,803,000,000; short-term debt 1,323,000,000; other current liabilities 1,117,000,000; deferred tax 774,000,000; other 131,000,000. **C-R-01.** `[[target]]` `fact` = the goodwill fact; A1c's R field `posted` = the goodwill fact (its intent's id). `fa explain balance --period

--certify --json` (and `fa tb --period

--certify`) returns the posted 16,803,000,000. R. **C-C-01.** `[[target]]` `fact` = the consideration fact (27,000,000,000, `decimals="-8"`). It compares C-T-01's certified 27,009,000,000 with 27,000,000,000 within the declared precision of ±50,000,000 (half of 10^8, from `decimals`). The row cites that precision, passes the exact test |27,009,000,000 − 27,000,000,000| = 9,000,000 ≤ 50,000,000, and states its band (±50,000,000) and its detection limit (a difference above 50,000,000 is detected; one at or below it is not) (§5.3). It is never reported as T. The check is a fa-oracles function `within_declared_precision(observed, published, decimals, scale) -> (band, diff, pass)` in checked integer arithmetic over minor units at the unit's scale (USD scale 2, `registries/units.toml:17`): band = 10^(−decimals) × 10^scale / 2 minor units, i.e. 5,000,000,000 cents (= $50,000,000) for `decimals = -8`; the dollar figures in this bead are those minor-unit values shown in dollars. C fields (A1c): `display_unit` = the consideration fact (its `decimals`), `per_row_test` = |observed − published| ≤ band, `band` = ±50,000,000.00, `detection_limit` = 50,000,000.00. **Witnesses and checks:** - **Contributing-entry witness (A11b).** `fa explain balance --period

--certify --json`: the contributions are exactly the posted component entries' consideration legs, none carries 27,009,000,000, and they re-add to the certified value; `fa explain balance --certify` also runs over each component account, and `fa_reference::statements::render` recomputes the `equity` line from those explained balances. - **Outsider check (A12, §12.1)**, for the BS certificate: `fa checkpoint create --grant witness`; `fa bundle produce --certificate `; `fa-verify bundle --key K --receipt R --json` and `fa-verify report --key K --checkpoint C --receipt R --json` through `fa_verify::cli::run` (`crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700`), both exit 0, with `report`'s recomputed `equity` line = 27,009,000,000; `fa replay ` byte-identical. - **ADS.** `fa export ads --period

--out

--with-proofs`, then `fa-verify ads --key K`. - **Second read path.** `fa query --certify` (§12.7), legs grouped by unit and side and netted by the harness, must equal the fold path for C-T-01 and C-R-01. - **Integrity and interop.** `fa verify book --json` exits 0. ADS re-import identity holds, and `fa verify export beancount|ads` passes. ## Tests & logging **Run.** `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact mergers`; `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- mergers_neg_`; `cargo test -p fa-oracles --test case_mergers`. **Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; A7a prints one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `/`; a FAIL is followed by `REPRODUCE fa --book `, the run ends `LOG `): - `PASS C-T-01 T statement-linkedin lnkd../default kind=footing read=statement balance-sheet,equity,

value=27009000000 published=27009000000 inputs_named=[lnkd..] contrib=holds outsider=report:verified` - `PASS C-R-01 R statement-linkedin lnkd../default read=explain balance,,

value=16803000000 posted=16803000000` - `PASS C-C-01 C statement-linkedin lnkd../default read=statement balance-sheet,equity,

value=27009000000 published=27000000000 decimals=-8 diff=9000000 band=50000000 detection_limit=50000000` - `PASS C-SELF-statement-linkedin D statement-linkedin -/default jet.self_sourced_evidence@1 …` (generated by A7a; `registries/procedures.toml:97`, calibration `planted`) - the generated guidance N `C-N-90` (A16) and `BUDGET mergers statement-linkedin book=1 invocations= wall_ms=` / `BUDGET mergers total_ms= … budget_ms=60000 PASS` (A7c) **Unit tests** (`case_mergers.rs`): - `within_declared_precision_band`: `decimals = -8` → band 50,000,000 (5,000,000,000 minor units at scale 2); `-6` → 500,000; `-3` → 500; `INF` → 0 (exact); - `within_declared_precision_c_c_01`: observed 27,009,000,000, published 27,000,000,000, `-8` → diff 9,000,000, pass; - `within_declared_precision_boundary`: diff exactly 50,000,000 → pass; 50,000,001 → fail; - `within_declared_precision_overflow`: values near i128::MAX → a named overflow error, never a wrapped difference. **Planted negatives** (run-time ones copy the case to the test's temp dir and edit the copy; the committed files are never edited): - `mergers_neg_goodwill_not_named`: goodwill removed from C-T-01's `inputs_named` → K-ORACLE re-types the claimed row C, so it prints `FAIL C-T-01 C statement-linkedin … reason=retyped T→C K-ORACLE` (A7a) and the case test exits non-zero (`.expect_err`); - `mergers_neg_total_posted_directly`: the component intents (their `[[intent]]`, `[[leg]]` and `intent` `[[step]]` rows) replaced by one balanced intent, Dr `cash` / Cr `consideration` 27,009,000,000, both legs `amount_rule = value:#` (so A1b's balance check and K-DERIVE admit it) → K-TAUT and the contributing-entry witness re-type C-T-01 R: `FAIL C-T-01 R statement-linkedin … reason=retyped T→R K-TAUT`, and the case test exits non-zero; - `mergers_neg_component_one_minor_unit`: cash's two legs moved by 0.01 (`amount_literal` 1328000000.01 on both, and their `amount_rule` changed from `value:#` to `synthetic` in the copy: K-DERIVE recomputes a `value:` rule against its literal, A3a, and a FAIL load check stops the case before any read, A7a) → `FAIL C-T-01 T statement-linkedin … value=27009000000.01 published=27009000000`; - `mergers_neg_c_c_01_typed_t`: C-C-01's comparison declared as a T. Re-typing the row in place would be refused at load (a T row takes a `T.*` template, the T fields and a `-T-NN` id, A1c), so the copy adds an unclaimed T row `C-T-99` (a test-only id) with C-T-01's read, `basis` and `inputs_named`, `published` = the consideration fact, `kind = footing` and `vintages = ["exhibit:SRC-MSFT-LNKD-PPA"]` → `FAIL C-T-99 T statement-linkedin lnkd../default … value=27009000000 published=27000000000` (exact equality fails by 9,000,000; an unclaimed FAIL fails the case, A7a), so the comparison can only be C; the renderer never renders it as T. **JSONL** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord` with `record = "step"` and `binds`, plus one `VerdictRecord` per expectation; copied to `$FA_CASES_LOG_DIR/mergers.jsonl` when set; the BS certificate bound as `$C_BS_`): `case = mergers`, `book_variant = statement-linkedin`; one `post` record per component (exit 0); `certificate_kind` on the balance-sheet certificate, each explained balance, the query, the bundle and the replay; `fa-verify` runs logged with their argv and exits; `verify book` exit 0. Runner-level: the period map, the fact ↔ vid map, per-book invocation count and wall time. On FAIL the reproduce argv; the log path at the end; 60 s warm budget; no `#[ignore]`; any UNRUN exits non-zero. ## Notes - **Why each edge exists:** - **C0:** the facts. - **X2:** the us-gaap → FA `role_map` for the modelled concepts. - **A3b:** K-ORACLE, K-TAUT and K-BASIS. - **A7b:** the certified-read plumbing the runner uses (the plan does not say which A7b stage C1 uses; C1 needs no case lifecycle and no `assert-balance`, because C-T-01 is a multi-account footing, which cannot be kernel-attested, §5.3). - **A11b:** the contributing-entry witness. - **A12:** the outsider checks. - **Balancing encoding** (proposed; the plan does not fix one): one two-leg entry per component against the Equity-typed `consideration` account. Its balance is the fold of the component legs, so 27,009,000,000 is never posted, directly or through a derivation, to the line or account the T checks (K-TAUT), and the balance sheet identity holds (30,354,000,000 = 3,345,000,000 + 27,009,000,000). - **A naming clash.** "PPA" here means purchase-price allocation. In §2.7's evidence rules, "PPA" means PriorPeriodAdjustment. - **Further work.** The stronger merger T (consolidation on an Article 11 pro forma) is C2 / C3. - **Naming** (§3.2b): case directory `mergers`, letter `C` (C0's `case.toml`), stem `statement-linkedin`, generated ids `C-SELF-statement-linkedin` and `C-N-90`; a statement posting's intent id is the fact id of the figure it posts (C0's ids). No restatement case, so no `C-CASE-*` row. - **Anchors checked at 8196f5e40.** `registries/statements/balance-sheet.toml:28` (`equity`, "Posted equity", Equity only), `registries/account_roles.toml:46-47` (`fixed_asset` admits only Asset) and `:64-65` (`cash` admits only Asset), `registries/units.toml:15-17` (USD scale 2), `crates/fa-verify/src/cli.rs:1700` (`pub fn run`). - **Foundation names, now carried:** A7a names the case test after its directory (`mergers`), runs `mergers_neg_` tests and prints `/`. - **Requires A11b** to take a T's named inputs from the intents of its `basis` facts: C-T-01's contributions are the component entries, while its `inputs_named` lists only the K-ORACLE input (goodwill, A1c); read as the named-input set, `inputs_named` would re-type C-T-01 R. - **Band.** §5.3's generic C test is |ΔP − d| ≤ one display unit; §11.1 states C-C-01's band as ±50,000,000, half the 10^8 unit of `decimals = -8`, and this bead follows §11.1. The observed 9,000,000 passes either way. - **Priority (round 4).** P3: plan §18 item 5 puts mergers last, and no bead waits on C0 or C1.

title: [cases] A3b: load-time checks K-BASIS, K-TAUT, K-ORACLE, K-VINTAGE (re-type to R or C, refuse superseded or unnamed vintages)
description:
## Why
Plan: `docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §15 A3b, §3.6, §5.3, §5.5, §3.8, §10.4.

These four checks stop the failures the plan names as its central risk, "a reconstruction can silently become a test of what we planted" (§0.2):
- a claim with no sourced basis;
- a tie-out that reads back its own published value ("Tautological T": answered by "type-independent K-TAUT; K-ORACLE; contributing-entry witness; R and C types", §17);
- a tie-out that silently reproduces the reference method's own output;
- a tie-out pinned to a superseded vintage. Draft v0 of the plan itself had exactly this error: "an Enron T pinned to a superseded vintage" (Appendix Z.3).

They serve T, C and R (re-typing) and every claim type through K-BASIS. DEBATE-001 makes T exact equality between independently sourced, accession-named values (A + ΣΔ = B, §5.5). These checks enforce the "independently sourced" and "accession-named" halves at load time.

## What to build
**Files and public API** (introduced here; each adds its report to A3a's `run_load_checks`):
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/check/{basis,taut,oracle,vintage}.rs`, one function per check returning a `CheckReport`.
- Re-typing is a result, not a refusal: `CheckReport` gains `retypes: Vec<Retype { expectation, target: Option<String>, from, to, check, path }>`, where `path` is the chain of fact ids and rules that caused it, and `Case::effective_type(expectation_id, target)` returns the declared type after every re-type. A re-type is per `[[target]]` where the T's read fields sit on its targets (A1c: X5's groups, M3's accounts), so one account's unnamed oracle input re-types that target and leaves the others T; it is per expectation (`target = None`) where they sit on the expectation. The runner (A7a) evaluates and prints the effective type per line; the renderer (A14) renders it.
- A shared helper `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/trace.rs`: `pub fn fact_closure(case, fact) -> BTreeSet<FactId>` (transitive over `derived.from` and `interpretation.from`) and `pub fn posted_from(case, variant, accounts) -> Vec<(IntentId, LegOrdinal, BTreeSet<FactId>)>` (for each leg on the given accounts, the facts its `amount_rule` traces to, through A1b's `value:`/`derived:` forms and A2's rules; for an intent the runner renders from a `[[ledger_map]]` row (M0), the leg traces to the complaint rows fact and its row).

**K-BASIS.**
- Every expectation's basis, taken transitively over `derived.from` and `interpretation.from` (`fact_closure`), contains ≥ 1 sourced fact and no synthetic fact.
- Non-sourced premises are listed: the report records, per expectation, the interpretation and derived facts in its closure, which the renderer prints as premises.
- Cases of `kind = "harness_selftest"` are exempt by kind (§15 A8a); the report then reads `CHECK K-BASIS UNRUN examined=0` with the reason `exempt: harness_selftest`, never PASS.

**K-TAUT** (static half; type-independent).
- For every expectation asserting equality with a published value, whatever its declared type (T, C or R with a `published` fact), let P be the published fact B plus every fact derived from it (the facts whose closure contains B). The accounts the read selects are its account, or for a type-level line or an exported concept (`round_trip`) every account of the line's account types in the variant (§3.8). If any leg on those accounts traces (`posted_from`) to a fact in P, the row (or, where reads sit on targets, that target) is re-typed R, with the trace as its `path`.
- The cases the plan names:
  - §3.8: a T on any line whose published comparison value (B) fed a `remainder` account. A remainder takes its A side from A values and its Δ from published Δs, never from a B value (§3.8, §7.2), so a `remainder` derivation whose inputs reach a B fact re-types every T on the lines it partitions R;
  - §10.1: a finer value only implied (FY − 9M YTD) is a `difference` derivation, which bars a T on the line it came from;
  - §7.2 E-T-02: a Δ derived as B − A "is a derivation tautology and renders R";
  - W-T-03: 818 is never posted;
  - W-T-04: the sourced "$54.4 million" is never posted.

**K-ORACLE.** An `oracle_output` fact (§2.1, `role = "oracle_output"`) in the closure of any leg a T reads feeds that T only if the T names that fact id in `inputs_named` (A1c lets `inputs_named` also hold intent ids, which A11b adds to its contributing-entry input set; naming an intent does not name the oracle facts its legs trace to); otherwise the row is re-typed C, per target where the reads sit on targets. Examples: BLMIS trustee-credited transfers, which M-T-01 names as inputs (Columns 4–7), one account target each, so a credit missing from `inputs_named` re-types only its account's target C (M3); LinkedIn goodwill, which C-T-01 names.

**K-VINTAGE** (reads A1c's tagged `vintages` and A1a's source `filed_on`/`restates` and fact `cell`).
- Accessions are named per T kind: `bridge` names `A:`, `D:` and `B:`; `footing` names `exhibit:` (one or more: M-T-01 names two complaints); `per_account` names `source:`; `allocation` names `source:` (the source of its sourced total and parts, W-T-04's SRC-WC-001); `delta` names its `D:` accession(s) and has no A or B (§5.3, E-T-03); `rule` (A1c's kind for M-T-02, §9.3) names `source:`; `round_trip` (A1c's kind for X-T-02, §10.1) names `B:`. A missing role is refused.
- **The published source.** Each kind has one role that names the source of its published value: `B` for `bridge` and `round_trip`, `exhibit` for `footing`, `source` for `per_account`, `allocation` and `rule`, `D` for `delta`. Every `published` fact's `source` must be a source named under that role (a footing's printed totals come from its exhibit); a published fact from an unnamed source is refused.
- **Latest vintage (§3.6: "a later restating vintage in `sources.toml` that differs on an asserted cell").** Let S be a published fact's source and c its `cell`. A source S′ supersedes S on c when S′ is filed later than S (`filed_on`), S′ is a restating vintage of the same figures (its `restates` closure contains S, or contains a source that S's `restates` closure contains), and S′ has a fact with `cell = c` and a different value. The co-restater clause is what E4 needs: E-T-04's B source is the 8-K (SRC-ENR-002), which no source restates, while the later 10-Q (SRC-ENR-003) restates the same as-filed rows (SRC-ENR-008, SRC-ENR-402) and differs on 20 of 30 cells (E1's Notes, E2d). A superseded T is refused unless its `read_selector` is `reported_in:<label>[#<n>]` and the `issue` step it names (A1c) files a citation stub of S, the earlier vintage (precedent E-T-04: the 8-K issuance). Reading the stub needs the `issue` step's filing-stub document from A1b's step table.
- When the restater's A differs from the filed A, both are carried as facts and the T names which one its `A:` role uses (§10.4; WorldCom 98,727 vs 98,903).
- The A posting cites the filing whose figure it posts: the as-filed filing, or the restating filing's "as previously reported" column when the bridge uses the restater's A (§2.7, "(K-VINTAGE; W-T-02)"). K-VINTAGE checks that the A intent's `evidence` document's `stub_of` is the `A:` source.

**Report.** Rows examined per check, in A3a's `examined=<n>/<inputs>` form; a target counts as one row where the reads sit on targets. A check whose input kind the case has (equality expectations for K-TAUT and K-ORACLE, T rows for K-VINTAGE, any expectation for K-BASIS) must examine every such row; a case with none reports UNRUN (§3.6).

## Tests & logging
Unit tests in the files above, run by `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; negative names follow `scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`. The T fixtures live in `crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/t_kinds/` (one small case with one T of each kind and synthetic, labelled values).
- **Positive.** `one_t_of_each_kind_passes_basis_taut_oracle_vintage`: the `t_kinds` fixture (`bridge`, `footing`, `per_account`, `allocation`, `delta`, and A1c's `rule` and `round_trip`) passes all four checks, each reporting the rows it examined, with no re-type. `reported_in_selector_naming_the_earlier_vintage_passes_k_vintage`: the co-restater shape below with `read_selector = reported_in:<label>#2` naming the issuance that files the earlier source's stub passes. `pilot_has_no_t_rows_so_taut_oracle_vintage_are_unrun`: on the T-free pilot fixture, K-TAUT, K-ORACLE and K-VINTAGE report UNRUN (zero rows), never PASS, and K-BASIS passes over its D/P/N rows.
- **Negatives from §15,** each a planted edit of the `t_kinds` fixture:
  - `read_back_t_with_b_posted_never_stays_t`: the bridge's B fact posted as a leg → `RETYPE <id> T→R K-TAUT path=[B, leg …]`;
  - `oracle_output_missing_from_inputs_named_is_retyped_c`: an `oracle_output` input absent from `inputs_named` → `T→C`; the same fixture with it named → no re-type;
  - `t_on_a_superseded_vintage_is_refused`: a later restating source with the same `cell` and a different value, the T reading the earlier one without `AS REPORTED IN` → `FAIL K-VINTAGE … superseded by <source>`;
  - `delta_t_naming_no_delta_accession_is_refused` → `FAIL K-VINTAGE … delta names no D: accession`.

  A re-type returns no `Err`, so each re-type test's name carries a ratchet token (`never`, `missing`; `scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`), and each asserts its `RETYPE` line.
- **Derived negatives (§3.6, §2.7, §3.8):**
  - `basis_without_a_sourced_fact_is_refused` and `basis_reaching_a_synthetic_fact_is_refused` (K-BASIS);
  - `bridge_whose_a_posting_cites_another_filing_is_refused` (K-VINTAGE: the A intent's evidence stub is not the `A:` source);
  - `t_on_a_line_whose_remainder_a_b_value_fed_never_stays_t` (K-TAUT through a `remainder` derivation);
  - `delta_derived_as_b_minus_a_never_stays_t` (E-T-02's derivation tautology);
  - `t_on_an_earlier_co_restater_without_reported_in_is_refused` (K-VINTAGE, the E4 shape: sources S1 and S2 each `restates` S0, S2 filed later, a fact of each with the same `cell` and different values; the T's B fact is S1's and it has no `read_selector` → `FAIL K-VINTAGE … superseded by S2`), and `reported_in_naming_an_issuance_of_another_vintage_is_refused` (the selector's `issue` step files S2's stub);
  - `published_fact_from_a_source_its_vintages_do_not_name_is_refused` (a footing whose printed total comes from a source not under `exhibit:`);
  - `oracle_output_missing_from_one_target_inputs_named_retypes_only_that_target` (M3's shape: two account targets, one credit unnamed → `RETYPE <id>/<target> T→C K-ORACLE`, the other target stays T).
- **Logging.** One `CHECK <K-ID> PASS|FAIL|UNRUN examined=<n>/<inputs>` line per check (A3a's form), one `FAIL` line per refused row, and one `RETYPE <id>[/<target>] <from>→<to> <check> path=<fact/rule chain>` line per re-type.

## Notes
- **Dependencies.** A1b (to trace which intents and legs post what to which account), A1c (the expectations and their `published` / `inputs_named` / `vintages` fields), A2 (to follow derivations transitively).
- **Fields this check reads.** Source `filed_on` and `restates` (§4.1 lists them since polish round 2), and two fields A1a and A1c add: fact `cell` and the tagged `vintages` roles. Without them "a later restating vintage … differs on an asserted cell" (§3.6) is not computable from the data.
- **Variant kinds.** Every rule that names a `statement` or `ledger` variant reads the stem's kind prefix (§3.2b), so `statement-bridge` and `statement-sunpower` are statement variants.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main, `cargo test -p fa-oracles`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the `t_kinds` fixture.
- **Static vs dynamic.** K-TAUT here is the static half. The dynamic half, that no contributing posting carries B, is A11b's contributing-entry witness (§3.7 item 2).
- **fa-wrrw.** Related: K-VINTAGE's explicit `AS REPORTED IN ⟨earlier⟩` rests on fa-wrrw's selectors (`--as-reported-in`, §3.3 step 7).
- **Plan vs bead (polish round 5).** Round 4's text applied the latest-vintage rule only to a source that restates the T's B source; §3.6 says "a later restating vintage … that differs on an asserted cell", which also covers a later co-restater of the same as-filed figures (E4's E-T-04, E1's Notes), so the rule above covers both. The roles for `allocation` (`source:`) and `round_trip` (`B:`), the published-source check and per-target re-typing (M3) are this bead's; the selector form `reported_in:<label>[#<n>]` is A1c's. A co-restater is never manufactured: E1 adds a `restates` entry only where the filing's own words say it restates, quoted in `notes`.
- **A1b's `issue` step `document` (polish round 5).** A1b's `issue` step names, in its required `document` field, the filing stub it issues with (the `--document` of `fa statement issue`, A7b), which is how K-VINTAGE checks which vintage a `reported_in` selector reads. A3b ← A1b (§15), so the field exists when this check lands.
- **T fixtures.** They are fixtures, not case data, with synthetic values labelled as such. They must not reuse a case's published values as if verified before the case's receipts exist (§4.5).
- **No registry edit.**
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: a fixture with one T of each kind, A1c's `rule` and `round_trip` kinds included (`crates/fa-oracles/tests/fixtures/t_kinds/`), passes K-BASIS, K-TAUT, K-ORACLE and K-VINTAGE, each reporting the rows it examined. On the T-free pilot, K-TAUT, K-ORACLE and K-VINTAGE report UNRUN, never PASS.
- [ ] negative: a planted read-back T is re-typed R; an oracle-output-fed T becomes C unless the input is in `inputs_named`; a T on a superseded vintage is refused; a `delta` T that names no Δ accession is refused. Each re-type prints `RETYPE <id> <from>→<to> <check> path=…`.
- [ ] negative (derived): an expectation whose transitive basis has no sourced fact, or reaches a synthetic fact, is refused by K-BASIS.
- [ ] negative (derived, §2.7, §3.8): a bridge whose A posting cites a filing other than the A accession it names is refused by K-VINTAGE; a T on a line whose remainder a B value fed is re-typed R by K-TAUT.
- [ ] negative (derived, §3.6): a T whose B source is superseded on its cell by a later co-restater (both restate the same as-filed source) is refused by K-VINTAGE unless its `reported_in` selector names an issuance that files the earlier vintage's stub; a published fact from a source the T's vintages do not name is refused; an `oracle_output` input missing from `inputs_named` re-types only the target whose read it feeds. Each re-type test's name carries a ratchet token.
- [ ] no-claim: static checks over the authored data. They do not show that any T holds or that a published value is right, and the dynamic half of K-TAUT is A11b's.

title: [cases] C2: Research: find a Regulation S-X Article 11 pro forma combined balance sheet that closes exactly; close with a decision record
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the merger case's `sources.toml` has one row per filing examined, with accession, `filed_on`, SHA-256 (or `BLOCKED` with its reason), its per-line closure class and its consolidation shape (goodwill yes/no with amount; investment vs the controlling share of contributed capital; stake in basis points) in `notes`, and the bead's close reason names the selected filing, or states that a filing closes exactly but carries goodwill (FA-REF-194 at 8196f5e40; a product bead filed, consolidation shown only as a labelled scenario), or that none closes exactly. A selected filing has receipted `table_cell` facts for every line (`alignment = "value"`, all four binding booleans true, `values_sha256` matching, `original_hash_compared` copied; each `cell` naming its column) and an `assurance_fact` for its row's `assurance`, and `selected_filing_closes` classifies every line `Exact`; its record names which printed lines are whole-type totals.
- [ ] negative: a candidate whose columns close only within a display band is classified C-only and not selected; an all-`Exact` candidate with goodwill is classified `ExactNotConsolidatable` and not selected; an edited adjustment FAILs `selected_filing_closes`, and a committed value edited after `verify` fails K-BIND offline; a candidate value not literal in its capture makes `verify` print `FAIL`.
- [ ] no-claim: failing to find an exactly closing, consolidatable Article 11 filing does not show that none exists. Finding one says nothing yet about `fa consolidate` (C3, C-T-02); a goodwill-carrying filing records a capability gap, not a defect of the filing.

title: [cases] C3: Consolidation T on C2's pro forma filing via fa consolidate (two entities, OWNS edge, eliminations, PPA adjustments), only if C2 finds one
description:
## Why
This is the merger case's strongest T: `fa consolidate`'s certified consolidation of two entities, with an OWNS edge, eliminations and PPA adjustments, reproducing a published pro forma combined column exactly (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §11.2). It is conditional twice over (§15 C3): it runs only if C2 anchors a filing that closes exactly, **and** only if `fa consolidate` admits that filing's investment. `fa consolidate` refuses "an investment that is not the controlling share of capital (goodwill and pre-acquisition retained earnings are not modeled)" with FA-REF-194, exit 3 (`registries/verbs.toml:640`; `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:1178`), so a combination carrying PPA goodwill needs that capability before C3 can run (§11.2). C2's `selectable_for_c3` encodes both conditions. Otherwise C3 closes on C2's decision record. Claim type T; the expectation id is **C-T-02** (§11.2, §15 C3).

## What to build
**Files** in `crates/fa-oracles/cases/mergers/`: `books/statement-proforma.toml`; the T's `[[expectation]]` / `[[target]]` rows in `expectations.toml`; run-time negatives `mergers_neg_proforma_*` in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`. It runs in the merger case's `#[test]` (`mergers`). The facts are C2's (the selected filing's `table_cell` line facts).

**Expectation id.** `C-T-02` (the plan now names it, §11.2 and §15 C3; round 2's "registered by a plan edit, written `C-T-<n>`" is superseded). It joins `case.toml` `claims` only in the landing that authors its rows, which happens only when C2 has selected a filing; the same landing adds `statement-proforma` to `case.toml` `variants` (A1a: the book-variant stems) and `verb:consolidate` to its `capabilities`.

**`books/statement-proforma.toml`** (a `statement` variant, no filler):
- `[book]`: `variant = "statement-proforma"`, `entities = ["<acquirer code>:<name>", "<target code>:<name>"]` (A1b's optional field; names from the entity-name fact of each combining company), which the runner passes as two `fa book create … --entity <code>[:<name>]` members sharing the base unit (A7a; `registries/verbs.toml` `book create` usage), the calendar holding the pro forma balance-sheet date.
- `[[period]]`, `[[principal]]` (the labels of C1's `roles.toml`), `[[document]]` (the selected filing's citation stub: `stub_of` = C2's selected source id, `grade = AgentUpload`, `reviewed_by = case-second-reader`) and the provenance engagement, as in C1's book (§2.7).
- `[[account]]`: per entity, one account per printed line, typed through X2's `role_map`; the consolidation roles set with `fa chart role <account> <role>`: `investment_in_subsidiary` (Asset, the parent's), `contributed_capital` (Equity, the target's), and `intercompany` / `intercompany_activity` / `noncontrolling_interest` / `noncontrolling_interest_income` where the filing needs them.
- The OWNS edge, between the two legal entities. `fa consolidate` keeps only OWNS edges whose ends are the book's entities (`crates/fa/src/consolidation.rs:316-334`), and `fa party relate` resolves a code to a party before a legal entity (`crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:183-206`), so the edge names the entity codes and no `[[party]]` row reuses one (the CLI test relates entity codes, `crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs:22826-22842`). It is A1b's relation token `owns:<target entity code>;basis=<code>;valid_from=<YYYY-MM-DD>;pct=<bps>/10000` (`basis` a code of `registries/relationship_bases.toml`; `pct` whole basis points), posted as `fa party relate <acquirer code> <target code> --kind owns --pct <bps>/10000 --basis <code> --valid-from <date>` (`registries/verbs.toml` `party` row :824; usage :832, "owns needs an exact --pct; from and to are party or legal-entity codes or vids"), active on the period's last day. Requires A1b to carry that token with both ends `[book] entities` codes (its `relations` live on `[[party]]` rows and resolve to `[[party]]` ids) and A7a to post it without a `fa party add`.
- `[[intent]]`: the acquirer's historical column (entity 1), the target's historical column (entity 2), and each footnoted pro forma adjustment, each citing the filing's citation stub; every `[[leg]]` names its `entity` (A1b's leg field; "in a multi-entity book every leg names one", `registries/verbs.toml:263`): the acquirer's code on its column, the target's on its column, and on an adjustment the entity whose balance it moves; the combined column is never posted (K-TAUT).
- `[[step]]`: `period_open`; `engagement_file` (the stub); the intents; `checkpoint`; each step that runs no intent names its `principal` (A1b). `fa consolidate --period <code> --certify` (`registries/verbs.toml:632-640`; `writes = false`, events `consolidation_run`, `report_certificate`) is not a step (A1b's closed step kinds have none): it is C-T-02's read, which the runner runs after the history. Requires A7b to add it to its certified reads (`reads.rs` lists `explain balance`, `gl detail`, the two statements and `scenario diff`).

**Precondition and feasibility check (code fact at 8196f5e40).** `fa consolidate` refuses, exit 3 with `FA-REF-194` (CONSOLIDATION_REFUSED, `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:1178`), "an investment that is not the controlling share of capital (goodwill and pre-acquisition retained earnings are not modeled)", a missing role, an unmatched intercompany balance, a stake that is not whole basis points, and several other shapes (`registries/verbs.toml:640`). A pro forma combination usually creates goodwill. The precondition is therefore C2's record, not an encoding choice here: C3 builds the book only for a filing C2 classified `Selected` (all lines `Exact`, no goodwill, the parent's investment equal to the controlling share of the target's contributed capital, a whole-basis-point stake). It never re-shapes a goodwill-carrying combination (for example by posting goodwill as an ordinary adjustment against a reduced investment) to get past the refusal: that encoding would not be the filing's investment, and a T on it would be manufactured. If `fa consolidate` still refuses the selected filing's encoding with `FA-REF-194` for another shape, C3 records the observation (the refusal id, exit 3 and its argv, logged), files a product bead for that shape (or for goodwill, when C2 recorded an exact-but-goodwill filing, with that filing as the bead's oracle), and closes without a T; it never forces a T. Consolidation is then demonstrated only as a labelled scenario (§11.2).

**The T (C-T-02).** `[[expectation]] id = "C-T-02"`, `type = "T"`, `kind = "footing"` (posted columns folded by a certified consolidation to printed combined totals that were never posted, §5.3), `book_variant = "statement-proforma"`, `vintages = ["exhibit:<C2's selected source id>"]`, `assurance` as C2's row records it. A1c's read fields: `read_verb = consolidate`, `read_target` = the line code, `read_coordinate` = the period label. One `[[target]]` per printed combined total that a whole-type line of the consolidated balance sheet reports (`assets`, `liabilities`, `equity`, `total_equity`, `liabilities_and_equity`): `fact` = the combined-column fact, `basis` = the acquirer, target and adjustment facts for that line. The certified consolidated line (`fa consolidate --certify`, read from its report) equals the printed combined value exactly at the printed precision. A printed line below type level (cash, goodwill, …) is not a target: the report's balance sheet is the embedded type-level `balance-sheet` definition (`crates/fa-statements/src/concordat.rs:1988`, rendered at `crates/fa-cli/src/consolidate.rs:319`), and the `consolidation_run` event carries members, eliminations, the equity reconciliation and the two statements, no per-account consolidated balance (`consolidate.rs:322-334`; §3.8). Its arithmetic stays C2's `selected_filing_closes`, and the gap is recorded (§13).

**Checks:**
- the contributing-entry witness (A11b): `fa explain balance --certify` over each account a line selects, and `fa_reference::statements::render` recomputing the line; requires A11b to add the report's elimination legs (the `eliminations` of `consolidation_run`) to that recomputation: they are not postings, so on any line an elimination touches the explained balances alone cannot re-add to the consolidated value;
- the outsider check (A12, §12.1). `fa bundle produce --certificate` replays "a sequence-selected native trial balance, balance sheet or income statement" (`registries/verbs.toml:784`); whether it accepts a consolidation report certificate is checked at authoring. If it does not (its usage refuses "Other scopes"), the outsider check is `fa replay C:<consolidation certificate>` byte for byte (the consolidate usage: "fa replay C:<oid> re-executes it byte for byte", `registries/verbs.toml:640`), and the gap is recorded; requires A12 to add that read kind (A12's outsider checks cover TB/BS/IS certificates, finding replays, scenario diffs and account bundles);
- the `fa query --certify` second read path;
- `fa verify book --json` exits 0.

## Tests & logging
**Run.** `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- --exact mergers`; `cargo test -p fa-cli --test cases -- mergers_neg_proforma_`.

**Expected lines** (field order is §16's; A7a owns the serialization; A7a prints one line per (expectation, target, cell) with the cell field written `<target>/<cell>`), one per target line: `PASS C-T-02 T statement-proforma <combined fact>/default kind=footing read=consolidate,<line>,<period> value=<v> published=<v> contrib=holds outsider=report:verified|replay:verified`, plus the runner-generated `PASS C-SELF-statement-proforma D statement-proforma -/default jet.self_sourced_evidence@1 …` (A7a). If the feasibility check fails, no T line exists, and the log carries the `consolidate` step with `exit = 3`, `refusal_id = FA-REF-194`.

**Planted negatives** (temp copies of the case; the committed files are never edited):
- `mergers_neg_proforma_adjustment_one_minor_unit`: one adjustment whose two legs sit on different account types moved by one minor unit on both legs (`amount_literal` edited and `amount_rule` set to `synthetic` in the copy: K-DERIVE recomputes a `value:` rule against its literal, A3a, and a FAIL load check stops the case before any read, A7a) → `FAIL C-T-02 T statement-proforma <combined fact>/default …` on each target line it moves, naming the line;
- `mergers_neg_proforma_owns_removed`: the OWNS edge removed → the target stays a member (every `[book]` entity is one, `crates/fa/src/consolidation.rs:728-737`) but is no longer a subsidiary, so its contributed capital is not eliminated against the parent's investment and nothing is refused (the roles are checked only when a subsidiary exists, `:435-447`); the T FAILs on every target line that elimination feeds (the asset and equity totals), naming each, and the case test exits non-zero;
- `mergers_neg_proforma_total_posted`: one combined total posted directly (a balanced intent whose legs' `amount_rule` is `value:<combined fact>#<ordinal>`, each leg naming an entity) → K-TAUT and the contributing-entry witness re-type that row R: `FAIL C-T-02 R statement-proforma <combined fact>/default … reason=retyped T→R K-TAUT` (A7a), and the case test exits non-zero.

**JSONL** (§3.5, A7a's `StepRecord`/`VerdictRecord`, copied to `$FA_CASES_LOG_DIR/mergers.jsonl` when set): `book_variant = statement-proforma`; `party relate`, `chart role` and `post` records (exit 0); the `consolidate` record with `certificate_kind` for its report certificate (or exit 3 and `refusal_id = FA-REF-194`); bundle, replay and query records. On FAIL the reproduce argv; the log path at the end; 60 s warm budget; no `#[ignore]`.

## Notes
- **Why each edge exists:**
  - **C2:** the filing.
  - **A7b:** certified reads.
  - **A11b:** the contributing-entry witness.
  - **A12:** the outsider checks.
- **Risk: double elimination.** A pro forma adjustments column often already contains the eliminations. `fa consolidate` computes its own eliminations from the roles, so the encoding must not eliminate twice; the contributing-entry witness exposes it.
- **Priority.** P3, conditional on C2.
- **Naming** (§3.2b): stem `statement-proforma` (only if C2 selects a filing), letter `C`, T id `C-T-02` (plan §11.2), generated `C-SELF-statement-proforma`.
- **Anchors checked at 8196f5e40.** `registries/verbs.toml:632` (consolidate row; flags `--period`, `--certificate-out`, switch `--certify`; events `consolidation_run`, `report_certificate`; exits include 3), `:640` (usage: FA-REF-194 shapes; `fa party relate <owner> <owned> --kind owns --pct <bps>/10000`; roles read by `fa chart role`), `:784` (`bundle produce` "replays a sequence-selected native trial balance, balance sheet or income statement"), `registries/refusal_catalog.toml:1178` (FA-REF-194, exit refusal = 3); `book create` takes `--entity` (verbs.toml book row :86); `:263` (post usage: every leg of a multi-entity book names its entity); `:832` (party usage: from and to are party or legal-entity codes); `crates/fa/src/consolidation.rs:316-334` (OWNS edges kept only between group entities), `:435-447` (roles checked only when a subsidiary exists), `:728-737` (every book entity is a member); `crates/fa-cli/src/rea.rs:183-206` (a code resolves to a party before a legal entity); `crates/fa-statements/src/concordat.rs:1988` (the consolidated balance sheet is the embedded `balance-sheet` definition), `crates/fa-cli/src/consolidate.rs:319`, `:322-334` (the report's fields); `crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs:22826-22842` (OWNS edges between entity codes).
- **Related tracker bead fa-76hy** (consolidation runs, in progress; link added in round 4): C-T-02 runs `fa consolidate`; a change to its eliminations, NCI or the `FA-REF-194` goodwill refusal changes C-T-02's precondition and fold.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: if C2 selected a filing (all lines `Exact` and a consolidation shape `fa consolidate` admits: no goodwill, investment = the controlling share of contributed capital, whole-basis-point stake), every printed pro forma combined total that a whole-type line of the consolidated balance sheet reports equals that certified `fa consolidate --certify` line exactly (lines below type level, which the report does not carry, are recorded, not claimed), with the combined totals never posted; the contributing-entry witness, the outsider check (or the recorded `fa replay` fallback) and `fa verify book --json` pass, as `PASS C-T-02 T statement-proforma …` lines.
- [ ] positive: if C2 recorded only an exact-but-goodwill filing, or the selected filing's encoding is still refused (`FA-REF-194`, exit 3), the refusal or C2's record is logged with its argv, a product bead is filed with that filing as its oracle, no T is claimed, and the combination is never re-shaped to pass the refusal.
- [ ] positive: if C2 found none, this bead closes on C2's decision record with no rows.
- [ ] negative: `mergers_neg_proforma_adjustment_one_minor_unit` FAILs the T on its line.
- [ ] negative: `mergers_neg_proforma_owns_removed` FAILs the T on the lines the capital-against-investment elimination feeds, with no refusal.
- [ ] negative: `mergers_neg_proforma_total_posted` re-types the row R and the case exits non-zero.
- [ ] no-claim: the T reproduces the published pro forma arithmetic on our two-entity encoding. Pro forma information is illustrative, not the combined company's actual results, and the T says nothing about the fair values behind the adjustments.

title: [cases] H1: ponzi.net_investment v4 follows investor_capital transfers under a named rule; the BLMIS case (M-N-01) is the regression oracle
description:
## Why

Product finding H1 (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §13): `ponzi.net_investment` v3 credits only cash-role legs (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:2475`, `:2662`). On the BLMIS `ledger` book, M-N-01 (§9.3) records that v3 diverges, on every account with a TRANS row, by exactly the net principal transferred: 1T0026 +2,384,266; 1ZA192 −3,462,634; 1ZB010 −200,000; 1ZB143 +3,955,000. An investor whose principal arrives by inter-account transfer is therefore mis-stated by the procedure that implements the net-equity method (In re BLMIS, 654 F.3d 229, cited at `cutoff.rs:2653`). The plan's remedy is a v4 that follows `investor_capital` transfers under a named rule, with the BLMIS case as the regression oracle. Today the case shows this as an N of kind `exact_gap` (M-N-01, §5.2: a value gap the mechanism explains exactly; its twin is 1ZR176, an account with no TRANS row, where the gap is 0); H1 is the product change that closes the gap.

## What to build

**Code (fa-lantern).**
- `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs`, `collect_investor_positions` (`:2475`; entry loop from `:2508`, attribution `:2552-2618`, retention filter `:2624-2628`). At 8196f5e40 a leg on a `cash`-role account updates `cash_in`/`cash_out` (`:2530-2541`); every other leg only marks `investor_contra` and becomes a funder or payee (`:2543-2548`), and a partition's cash is attributed only to its funders and payees (`attribute`, `:2553-2554`), so a partition with no cash leg moves no investor's figures, whatever its legs are.
- **The two transfer encodings v4 must follow.**
  - *One-sided transfer legs: the encoding the BLMIS `ledger` book posts.* M0's `[[ledger_map]]` renders every Exhibit B row as its own two-leg entry: the investor leg on the account's investor account (Equity type or the `investor_capital` role) naming the holder's party, and the contra, naming no party, on the declared `transfer_account` for a TRANS row (an account holding neither `cash` nor `investor_capital`, M0, M5). A transfer from 1ZA192 to 1ZB143 is therefore two entries in two exhibits, each with one investor leg; no entry carries two investor legs, and the receiving leg already carries the trustee-credited amount (Columns 4–7, `role = "oracle_output"` for the 13 Glantz credits, M3). A trigger that needs two `investor_capital` legs naming two parties in one partition never fires on this book, so it could not move M-N-01's gap.
  - *Two-party transfers*, one entry with an investor leg debited for one party and an investor leg credited for another, and no cash leg.
- **v4's rule.** In a partition with no cash leg: (i) an investor leg naming a party, whose other legs are all on accounts holding the transfer role below, counts at its posted amount as that party's principal in (credit) or out (debit); (ii) investor legs naming two parties count as the credited party's principal in and the debited party's principal out, at the amount the named rule gives. A party whose only principal in arrives by transfer is retained in the population (the retention filter, `:2624-2628`, admits it), and the comment below states whether a transfer-in sets `first_inflow_date` (the cohort date).
- **The transfer role.** v4 registers one account role for the transfer counterpart (proposed `investor_transfer`: a clearing account through which principal moves between investor accounts; `account_types = ["Asset", "Liability"]`, as `suspense` admits; `consumers = ["ponzi.net_investment"]`), with its `ROLE_POPULATIONS` pair in `crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs:133-155`, which a test holds together with `registries/account_roles.toml` (its header: "Lantern selects a population by role, never by an account's code or the words in its name"). The rejected alternative, treating any cash-free entry against an investor account as a transfer, would move principal for a fee charged to an investor's account or a reclassification between equity accounts. The name is fixed in the comment below with the rule.
- **Shared helper, so scope the change.** `collect_investor_positions` is also called by `distribution.rising_tide` (`cutoff.rs:3081`) and `distribution.pro_rata` (`:3254`), both at version 3 (`:3056`, `:3229`). Either gate the transfer rule to `ponzi.net_investment` (for example a parameter of the helper that only `PonziNetInvestment::run`, `:2697`, sets) or bump both distribution procedures in the same landing with their own regression tests. A change that moves their output without a version bump is refused by the project rule that certificates replay by (id, version).
- `PonziNetInvestment::version` returns 4 (`cutoff.rs:2671-2673`), and the type's doc comment (`:2652-2661`) names the rule. `fa_lantern` refuses to run a procedure whose code version differs from its registry row (`crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs:1015-1018`), and `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs:1916` asserts code version = row version, so code and registry move together.

**Registry and pins (one landing).**
- `registries/procedures.toml` row (`:1628-1643`, its `[[parameter]]` included): `version = 4`, and a summary that names the transfer rule beside the existing v1/v3 history sentences.
- `crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/extended.rs:58`: `("ponzi.net_investment", 4)` replaces the v3 entry. The length assertion `EXTENDED_CERTIFIABLE_PROCEDURES.len() == 41` (`crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/tests/extended.rs:51`) stays 41, because the row is replaced, not added.
- Checked at 8196f5e40 with `rg`: no other test pins `ponzi.net_investment` at version 3. `crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs:146-147` and `registries/account_roles.toml:67`, `:73` name the procedure's roles, not its version, and stay; the transfer role adds one `[[role]]` row (`consumers = ["ponzi.net_investment"]`) and one `ROLE_POPULATIONS` pair beside them.
- The v4 summary names the transfer role and the rule (an investor movement can also be a cash-free leg against the transfer role).
- Any `registries/*.toml` edit invalidates every crate verdict (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`); the landing says so. The robot-schema pin (`registries/robot_schema/1.jsonl`) carries no procedure rows, so it does not move.

**The named rule.** The plan does not name it. For form (i) the amount is the leg as posted, so on the BLMIS book v4 reproduces the trustee's own arithmetic from its credited transfer legs (M3's M-T-01 predicate). Form (ii) needs the rule. The record's own reading is the harness's interpretive `trustee_transfer_credit` (§2.4: Exhibit B footnotes [1]/[2] read as credit = min(statement amount, max(0, originating principal)), tested on 2 in-file pairs only). This bead chooses the product rule and records the choice as a comment on this bead before code lands, with:
- its name and exact integer semantics (no float; any division names a registered rounding law, AGENTS.md doctrine 4);
- where it is registered: in the v4 summary, plus a `[[parameter]]` row if the procedure lets a caller select it (parameters are integers, `fa procedure run … --param <name>=<integer>`, `registries/verbs.toml:668-677`);
- whether it equals `trustee_transfer_credit` or deliberately differs. It must be a product rule in fa-lantern, never an import of the case harness's interpretation (fa-oracles stays engine-independent, plan §3.1).

**Case expectation.** A v4 expectation on the BLMIS ledger book replaces the v3 divergence lock (M5's M-N-01), as set out in Notes. The landing also assigns the transfer role to the ledger book's declared `transfer_account` (`[[account]] role`, `fa chart role`) and to the `_selftest` ledger fixture's (M0), case-data edits made in the same landing as the version tokens (Notes); M0's rule that the account holds neither `cash` nor `investor_capital` still holds.

## Tests & logging

- **fa-lantern unit tests** in `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern/party_attribution.rs`, reusing its `party`, `entry`, `assign`, `of` and `investors` helpers (`:16`, `:45`, `:89`, `:104`, `:336`) and the precedent `ponzi_and_distribution_preserve_investor_margins` (`:387`). The test introduces:
  - `ponzi_v4_credits_an_investor_funded_only_by_a_transfer`: investor B is funded only by a two-party transfer from investor A (form ii). Under the named rule, B's net investment equals the transferred principal and A's falls by the same amount, and B is retained in the population. The expected margins are literals written from the economic history, not from the implementation (the module's own rule, `:5-7`).
  - `ponzi_v4_credits_one_sided_transfer_legs_against_the_transfer_role` (form i, M0's shape): A's TRANS-out entry (Dr A's investor account naming A / Cr the transfer-role account) and B's TRANS-in entry (Dr the transfer-role account / Cr B's investor account naming B), each its own entry; A's net investment falls and B's rises by exactly the legs' literal amounts.
  - planted negative `ponzi_v4_never_moves_principal_for_a_cash_free_entry_without_the_transfer_role`: the same one-sided entries with the contra on an account that holds no transfer role (and, in a second book, a fee: Dr an investor account naming P / Cr a Revenue account) leave every investor's figures exactly as v3 gives them.
  - planted negative `ponzi_v4_without_the_transfer_leg_moves_by_exactly_its_amount`: the same book with the transfer entry removed. Both investors' figures move by exactly the leg's amount, and the test's assertion against the transfer-bearing literal fails, which the test observes and asserts.
  - `distribution_procedures_are_unchanged_by_the_ponzi_transfer_rule` (if the rule is gated to ponzi): `distribution.rising_tide` and `distribution.pro_rata` give byte-identical findings on the transfer book before and after.
- **Version agreement:** `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs:1916` and the extended-certificate test (`crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/tests/extended.rs:51-60`) pass at version 4. A certificate recorded under v3 still replays under v3, because replay keys on (id, version).
- **Case regression (BLMIS ledger book, M5):** the v4 run on 1T0026, 1ZA192, 1ZB010 and 1ZB143, compared with the trustee's printed closing principal, with the trustee-credited transfer legs named as inputs (`inputs_named`, K-ORACLE). The runner prints `PASS|FAIL|UNRUN <id> <type> ledger <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses> [reason=…]` per (expectation, target, cell) (A7a), the `REPRODUCE fa …` argv on failure and the JSONL log path at the end (§16); each `fa procedure run ponzi.net_investment` step's JSONL record carries `finding_procedure = ponzi.net_investment` (§3.5). Until OD 2b commits the Exhibit B rows these rows print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` (§3.2b), so the four-account equality is observed at the OD 2b landing.
- **Through the binary before OD 2b:** `ponzi_v4_counts_the_selftest_ledger_fixtures_trans_rows` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, on M0's committed `_selftest` ledger fixture, whose generated rows must include TRANS rows between fixture accounts against its transfer account; M0 gives the fixture §9.2's shape without listing its row kinds, so the test first asserts at least one TRANS row out of one account and one into another, and fails naming the fixture otherwise, never passing without exercising form (i)): for every fixture account, v4's net investment from `fa procedure run ponzi.net_investment --json` equals the fixture's own principal sum (deposits − withdrawals + TRANS in − TRANS out, computed by fa-oracles from the generated rows), and v3's differs by exactly the account's net TRANS sum. Synthetic rows, so no claim; on failure it prints the account, both values and the `REPRODUCE` argv.
- Every applied product change lands a regression test (AGENTS.md). Name planted-negative tests so the gate-evidence ratchet counts them (`scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`: `without`, `fails`, `wrong` …).

## Notes

- **← M5:** "It needs the BLMIS oracle" (§15 Phase H): M-D-01 and M-N-01 on the ledger book.
- **Tier row:** the version bump changes the `procedures.toml` row digest, which invalidates `ponzi.net_investment`'s tier row (K-TIER, A4) and requires a fresh two-reader classification. M-D-01 is conditional on that row confirming S-party (§9.3). Bumping the distribution procedures (if not gated) invalidates their tier rows too, where they have one.
- **M-N-01 flips:** it is an `exact_gap` N whose projection pins `ponzi.net_investment` v3 (§5.4). When v4 lands, the v3 lock cannot run and the gap on the four TRANS accounts should be 0. Re-express it as a v4 expectation (the trustee-equality form, with the credited transfer legs in `inputs_named`) and retire the v3 row with a `Retired-tests:` trailer (and `Weakened-tests:` if any cite or type is weakened) per §16. Its twin, 1ZR176 with gap 0, stays a regression row under v4.
- **OD 2b.** The BLMIS rows are committed only after OD 2b (§14 item 2b, the owner-decision bead); until then the case-book acceptance below prints UNRUN and H1's binary-level evidence is the `_selftest` fixture test above. H1 closes on the BLMIS observation, so it waits on OD 2b as M5 does.
- **Requires of other beads (none blocking):** M0/M3's `transfer_account` gains the transfer role in H1's landing (above); M0's `ledger_map_transfer_account_role` refusal (cash role) is unaffected.
- **K-ORACLE:** 13 of the Glantz transfer credits can only be copied from the trustee's columns (`role = "oracle_output"`, §9.2). An equality on those accounts is the exhibit's own arithmetic with named inputs, not an independent net-equity determination (§9.3).
- **H2 collides with this bead.** H2's predicate fix edits the same helper (the retention filter `:2624-2628`) and also bumps the version. Whichever lands second takes the next version (5) and re-updates `extended.rs:58`, the tier row and H9's calibration rows.
- **AN-401 / H2:** v3 also retains every party with attributed cash in as an investor (`cutoff.rs:2626`).
- **fa-6l8g** (in progress at 8196f5e40) owns v3's per-party attribution in the same function (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff/attribution.rs`); coordinate edits through Agent Mail on its thread.
- **fa-v0m2.** fa-v0m2 (open, P1), the CLI/MCP companion campaign for fa-6l8g's corrected semantics, has landed `creditor_and_investor_margins_survive_public_workflow` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/forensic_semantics.rs`, a6f633573 per its 2026-10-24 comment): through the real `fa` it runs `ponzi.net_investment` on a two-investor book (INV-A 100.00, INV-B 200.00) and `distribution.pro_rata` with `distributable_pool=9000` (30.00 / 60.00) (`:283-300` in the tree read for polish round 4). The change here runs through the same `collect_investor_positions`, so that test is a regression gate for it and stays green unchanged; it pins no `ponzi.net_investment` version, so a version bump does not move it. No other bead plans this change (searched: fa-6l8g, fa-v0m2, fa-m35p, fa-kxc4, fa-b6xs), so this bead carries it.
- **H9:** the case calibration rows are keyed by procedure version and are updated in the same landing.
- Calibration stays `planted` (§5.6) unless measured.
- **Case files that name the version.** The landing also updates BLMIS's `case.toml` capability token (`procedure:ponzi.net_investment@3` → `@4`, A13's declared ⊆ exercised check) and the expected lines that print `ponzi.net_investment@3` (M5), and re-seeds the A4 tier row (a harness-table edit).
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; `cargo test -p fa-lantern -p fa -p fa-cli`; `bash scripts/check.sh` (`registries/procedures.toml` and `registries/account_roles.toml` edits: global verdict invalidation). A v3 test removed or narrowed needs a `Retired-tests:` or `Weakened-tests:` trailer naming it.
- **Polish round 5.** The earlier trigger (a cash-free partition with two `investor_capital` legs naming two parties) never fires on M0's encoding (each TRANS row an investor leg against the `transfer_account`, checked at `cutoff.rs:2508-2548` in `polish/r3b/cutoff_8196.rs`), so the BLMIS acceptance could not be met; v4 now covers both encodings through a registered transfer role.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: on the BLMIS ledger book (once OD 2b commits its rows; UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` until then), whose TRANS rows post one-sided against the `transfer_account` carrying the new transfer role, v4's net investment on 1T0026, 1ZA192, 1ZB010 and 1ZB143 equals the trustee's printed closing principal, with the trustee-credited transfer legs named as inputs: the M-N-01 divergence (+2,384,266 / −3,462,634 / −200,000 / +3,955,000) is gone, and 1ZR176 still shows gap 0. Before OD 2b, `ponzi_v4_counts_the_selftest_ledger_fixtures_trans_rows` passes through the real binary.
- [ ] positive: `ponzi_v4_credits_an_investor_funded_only_by_a_transfer` and `ponzi_v4_credits_one_sided_transfer_legs_against_the_transfer_role` pass in fa-lantern; the transfer role is a `registries/account_roles.toml` row with its `ROLE_POPULATIONS` pair; the `procedures.toml` row reads `version = 4` with the rule and the role named in its summary; `PonziNetInvestment::version` is 4; `EXTENDED_CERTIFIABLE_PROCEDURES` lists `("ponzi.net_investment", 4)` and still has 41 rows; the rule's name and semantics are recorded as a comment on this bead.
- [ ] positive: `distribution.rising_tide` and `distribution.pro_rata` are either unchanged on the transfer book (rule gated to ponzi) or bumped with their own regression tests in the same landing.
- [ ] negative: the planted fixture that drops the transfer leg (`ponzi_v4_without_the_transfer_leg_moves_by_exactly_its_amount`) moves both investors' figures by exactly that leg's amount, and the assertion against the transfer-bearing literal is observed to fail; a cash-free entry whose contra holds no transfer role (or a fee against an investor account) moves no investor's figures (`ponzi_v4_never_moves_principal_for_a_cash_free_entry_without_the_transfer_role`).
- [ ] no-claim: v4's equality on transfer accounts reproduces the trustee's own arithmetic given its credited transfers as inputs; it is not an independent net-equity determination, and the procedure's output is a statistical finding, never an accusation.

title: [cases] H2: ponzi.net_investment v3 keeps every party with attributed cash in as an investor (AN-401): fix the predicate or the summary
description:
## Why

Product finding H2 (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §13; AN-401): v3 retains every party with attributed cash in as an investor (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:2626`), contrary to its registry summary, which defines an investor movement as one whose contra leg is on an Equity account or one holding the `investor_capital` role. A vendor refund or any other non-investor inflow therefore makes its party an "investor". The BLMIS case works around it by building a book of customer cash movements only, one party per account (§9.3). §2.5 treats this as a membership question, not a dependence of the target's own figures; it still misstates what the procedure computes.

## What to build

Either fix the population predicate, so that a party is an investor only under the summary's investor-movement test, or fix the summary so that it states the retained rule exactly (§13: "fix the population predicate or the summary"). Record the choice, with its reason, as a comment on this bead before code lands.

**Code facts at 8196f5e40.**
- The retention filter is `p.cash_in > 0 || explicit_investor_party.contains(k)` (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:2624-2628`). `explicit_investor_party` is filled only when a partition's contra leg is on an Equity account or an `investor_capital` account (`investor_contra`, `:2543-2545`, `:2580-2582`), which is exactly the summary's test. So the minimal predicate fix retains only `explicit_investor_party` members.
- The summary is the `registries/procedures.toml` row at `:1628-1643` (the sentence "an investor movement's contra leg is on an Equity account or one holding the `investor_capital` account role").
- **Shared helper.** The filter lives in `collect_investor_positions` (`cutoff.rs:2475`), which `distribution.rising_tide` (`:3081`) and `distribution.pro_rata` (`:3254`) also call. A predicate fix therefore changes three procedures' output: either scope it to `ponzi.net_investment`, or bump all three, each with a regression test.

**Predicate fix (behaviour change).**
- `PonziNetInvestment::version` (`cutoff.rs:2671-2673`) and the `procedures.toml` row `version` move together (`crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs:1015-1018` refuses a mismatch; `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs:1916` asserts agreement).
- `crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/extended.rs:58` lists the new version (the length test at `crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/tests/extended.rs:51` stays 41), and likewise the distribution rows (`:59-60`) if they bump.
- The summary keeps its v1/v3 history and adds the new version's sentence.

**Summary fix (text only).** Edit the row's `summary` to state the retained rule exactly (a party with attributed cash in, or one touching an Equity or `investor_capital` account), with no version change, because no output moves.

Either way this is a `registries/*.toml` edit, which invalidates every crate verdict (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`); the robot-schema pin carries no procedure rows and does not move.

## Tests & logging

Placed in `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern/party_attribution.rs`, reusing `party` (`:16`, which registers parties as `PartyKind::Vendor`, so the kind is not what the predicate reads), `entry` (`:45`), `assign` (`:89`) and `of` (`:104`). The test introduces:
- **`ponzi_vendor_refund_party_is_never_an_investor`** (the §13 vendor-party negative). The book holds an investor (Dr cash / Cr an `investor_capital` account, naming the investor) and a vendor refund (Dr cash / Cr an Expense account, naming the vendor). Under a predicate fix, the vendor is absent from the investor population and receives no `ponzi.net_investment` finding, while the investor's finding is unchanged.
- **Observed red first:** on the unfixed v3 code the test fails, because the vendor's attributed cash in retains it at `:2626` and it receives a net-loser finding. The landing records that failure, observed before the fix.
- **Under a summary fix** the test is instead `ponzi_summary_states_the_retained_population_rule`. It asserts that the vendor *is* retained, and that the row's `summary` (read through `fa_registry::procedures::Procedures::embedded()`, `crates/fa-registry/src/procedures.rs:184`) contains the retained rule's sentence. A copy of the old summary fed to the same check must fail (`..._fails_on_the_old_summary`).
- Also, either way, `ponzi_and_distribution_preserve_investor_margins` (`party_attribution.rs:387`) stays green.
- **BLMIS case:** if the runner is present, M-D-01's runner lines (`PASS|FAIL|UNRUN M-D-01 D ledger <target>/<cell> <projection-with-statuses> [reason=…]`, one per (expectation, target, cell), A7a) are unchanged, because the case book holds only customer cash movements (§9.3); until OD 2b commits the Exhibit B rows they print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` (§3.2b). Under a predicate fix the projection carries the new version, so M5's row is re-pinned in the same landing.
- Name the negatives so the gate-evidence ratchet counts them (`scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`).

## Notes

- **No dependencies** (§15: H2 ← none).
- **Tier row:** either fix changes the `procedures.toml` row (its digest covers the summary), which invalidates the `ponzi.net_investment` tier row (K-TIER, A4) and requires a fresh two-reader classification before M-D-01 can run.
- **H1 collides with this bead.** H1's transfer rule edits the same helper and also bumps the version. Whichever lands second takes the next version and re-updates `extended.rs:58`, the tier row and H9's calibration rows.
- **Case effect:** a predicate fix would let the BLMIS book carry non-customer movements; until then §9.3's one-party-per-account constraint stays.
- **Coordination:** H1 and fa-6l8g (in progress; `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff/attribution.rs`) edit the same function. Coordinate through Agent Mail on the bead thread.
- **fa-v0m2.** fa-v0m2 (open, P1), the CLI/MCP companion campaign for fa-6l8g's corrected semantics, has landed `creditor_and_investor_margins_survive_public_workflow` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/forensic_semantics.rs`, a6f633573 per its 2026-10-24 comment): through the real `fa` it runs `ponzi.net_investment` on a two-investor book (INV-A 100.00, INV-B 200.00) and `distribution.pro_rata` with `distributable_pool=9000` (30.00 / 60.00) (`:283-300` in the tree read for polish round 4). The change here runs through the same `collect_investor_positions`, so that test is a regression gate for it and stays green unchanged; it pins no `ponzi.net_investment` version, so a version bump does not move it. No other bead plans this change (searched: fa-6l8g, fa-v0m2, fa-m35p, fa-kxc4, fa-b6xs), so this bead carries it.
- **Case files that name the version** (predicate fix only): BLMIS's `case.toml` capability token and M5's expected lines move to the new version in the same landing, with the A4 tier row re-seeded.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; `cargo test -p fa-lantern -p fa`; `bash scripts/check.sh` (a `registries/procedures.toml` edit either way).

The choice is recorded as a comment on this bead.

title: [cases] H3: fa demo init usage lists 5 scenarios Scenario::parse rejects and omits ghost-payroll; make usage match the 7 that exist
description:
## Why

Product finding H3 (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §13): the `fa demo` usage lists scenarios that `Scenario::parse` rejects (saas, manufacturing, nonprofit, holding, crypto) and omits ghost-payroll. fa-v6j's close reason claims 11 scenarios; the code has 7. An agent that follows the usage hits a refusal, which is exactly the ergonomics failure the Polish Bar forbids. The case program also leans on the demo list: A13's `not_exercisable` rows may name "the fa-demo scenario" as `covered_by` (§12.2), and §12.4 discusses fa-demo's `worldcom` scenario (owner decision 6), so the list agents and the coverage table read must be the real one.

## What to build

**The stale list appears in five places at 8196f5e40** (checked with `rg saas`): `registries/verbs.toml:1050` (the `demo init` usage) and four literals in `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs`:
- `:3990`, the fix of "--scenario may be supplied only once";
- `:3998`, the example passed to `args.require("--scenario", …)`;
- `:4003`, the fix of "unknown demo scenario";
- `:4215`, the fix in the argument pre-check (`UsageError { fix: … }`).

Every one becomes the implemented list.

- **cli.rs:** build the list once from `fa_demo::SCENARIO_NAMES` (`crates/fa-demo/src/lib.rs:74`; fa-cli already depends on fa-demo) as `SCENARIO_NAMES.join("|")`, and use it at all four sites. `usage()` takes `impl Into<String>` (`cli.rs:207`) and `Args::require` takes `&str` (`crates/fa-cli/src/args.rs:94`), so no `'static` literal is needed and the four strings cannot drift again.
- **verbs.toml:1050:** the usage names exactly retail|bank|ponzi|shell-network|worldcom|channel-stuffing|ghost-payroll. The registry is text, so the test below pins it.

**Code facts.** `SCENARIO_NAMES` (`fa-demo/src/lib.rs:74-82`) and `Scenario::ALL` (`:85`, 7 entries) agree. `Scenario::parse` (`:109-120`) also accepts aliases (clean-retailer, kiting, kiting-loop, ponzi-funnel, shell_network, worldcom-capex, channel_stuffing, ghost_payroll), which the usage need not list.

**Elsewhere.**
- Record the correction on fa-v6j (closed) as one comment naming the 7 implemented scenarios; its close reason names 11. That comment is the fa-ldfy-protocol comment described in Notes, not a second one.
- Implementing the five missing scenarios would be a separate feature, outside this bug.
- `demo init` is a registered MCP exclusion (host-only, `registries/verbs.toml:3998-4001`), so no MCP tool text changes.

## Tests & logging

- **Regression test** `demo_usage_names_exactly_the_implemented_scenarios`, in `crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs`, through the real binary. It checks three things:
  - the `demo` row's first usage string from `fa_cli::verbs::registry()`, and the `fix` of the error line of `fa demo init --scenario saas --book <tmp> --json` (exit 2, checked with `check_robot_output` as `cli.rs:78-96`'s `fa()` helper does), each name exactly the set `fa_demo::SCENARIO_NAMES`;
  - every name in `SCENARIO_NAMES` parses (`fa_demo::Scenario::parse`);
  - `fa demo init --scenario ghost-payroll --seed 7 --book <tmp> --json` exits 0 with one `demo_initialized` event.
- **The comparison** is a small helper in the test file, `scenario_list_mismatch(text, names) -> Vec<String>`, which extracts the `a|b|c` list after `--scenario` and returns the names missing or extra.
- **Planted negative** `scenario_list_check_fails_on_an_unknown_scenario`: the helper fed `--scenario retail|saas|bank` reports `saas` as extra and `ponzi`… as missing. A list without `ghost-payroll` reports it missing. Both are asserted, so the check is shown to bite.
- **Pins:** the robot-schema pin (`registries/robot_schema/1.jsonl`) carries the envelope, `[[event]]` and `[[shape]]` rows only, never usage text, so it does not move. `the_robot_schema_is_pinned_byte_for_byte` (`crates/fa-cli/tests/robot_schema.rs:14`) must stay green with the pin unchanged.
- **Logging:** the test prints the observed list, the expected list and any mismatch on failure.

## Notes

- **No dependencies** (§15: H3 ← none).
- Registry edit (`registries/verbs.toml`) → global crate-verdict invalidation (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`); state it in the landing, and run `bash scripts/check.sh` because a non-`.rs` file changed. Before main, `bash scripts/tier0.sh` exits 0 (or the change goes through a merge-train branch). The planted negative's name carries `fails`/`unknown`, so the gate-evidence ratchet counts it.
- **Case interaction:** no expectation waits on H3, but any A13 `covered_by` naming a fa-demo scenario must name one of the 7 that parse.
- OD 6 (WorldCom-labelled synthetic artifacts) is separate: it concerns the content and label of the `worldcom` scenario, not this usage text.
- **fa-v6j (closed) and fa-ldfy (tracker truth audit, open, P1).** fa-v6j's close reason claims "all 11 deterministic scenarios (retail, saas, manufacturing, nonprofit, holding, crypto, bank, ponzi, shell-network, worldcom, channel-stuffing)"; at 8196f5e40 `Scenario::parse` accepts 7, five of the named ones are refused, and ghost-payroll, the seventh (`crates/fa-demo/src/lib.rs:74-82`), is not named. fa-v6j carries no comment saying so, and fa-ldfy's list of closures with unmet acceptance does not include it. Following fa-ldfy's protocol (a dated comment with file:line evidence and the corrective bead, never a reopen of another owner's closure), H3's landing adds that comment to fa-v6j, naming H3. No open bead plans the usage fix, so H3 carries it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `fa demo init --help`, robot-docs and every `--scenario` fix string in `crates/fa-cli/src/cli.rs` (`:3990`, `:3998`, `:4003`, `:4215`, now built from `fa_demo::SCENARIO_NAMES`) list exactly the 7 implemented scenarios; `fa demo init --scenario ghost-payroll --seed 7 --book <dir> --json` exits 0; `demo_usage_names_exactly_the_implemented_scenarios` passes.
- [ ] negative: `scenario_list_check_fails_on_an_unknown_scenario` shows the check reports `saas` as extra and an omitted `ghost-payroll` as missing; `fa demo init --scenario saas` still exits 2 with a fix that names only implemented scenarios.
- [ ] positive: the robot-schema pin is unchanged and `the_robot_schema_is_pinned_byte_for_byte` stays green (usage text is not in the pin).
- [ ] no-claim: the usage now matches the code; nothing about whether any demo scenario's planted attributes match a real case (OD 6).
