title: [cases] H9: case-derived calibration rows: crates/fa-oracles/data/case_calibration.toml with loader and resolution/label-agreement test
description:
## Why

fa-gen plants its own motifs, so its precision is 100% by construction (`registries/lantern_calibration.toml:22-32`; the fa-4psc finding, §0.2). docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.4 names three things case books contribute that fa-gen cannot: predicate-level negatives from documented scheme entries (F2, F6, F7 and F8 are documented parts of the WorldCom scheme that fall outside `expense.capitalization`'s predicate, W-N-01; BLMIS accounts that move principal by transfer, M-N-01); externally labelled positives (entries the investigators documented, not entries we planted); and real-data exposure (the §9.4 counts). H9 makes those rows data a calibration review can read. The program does not change `lantern_calibration.toml`, and no case result is ever reported as a precision or recall figure (§0.5, §12.4).

## What to build

**Files** (introduced here):
- `crates/fa-oracles/data/case_calibration.toml`, a harness table (§2.4: `schema_version = 1`, a Consumer (fa-4psc's calibration review) / Gate (the two tests below) / Retire (with the program; it becomes a registry only if a product consumer appears) header, embedded with `include_str!` and listed in `src/cases/embedded.rs`).
- `crates/fa-oracles/src/cases/calibration.rs`: `pub struct CalibrationRow`, `pub fn rows() -> Result<Vec<CalibrationRow>, LoadError>`, and `pub fn check(rows, cases, procedures) -> CheckReport` (the static gate).
- Tests: `case_calibration_rows_resolve_and_label_by_source` (unit, fa-oracles) and `case_calibration_cited_agrees_with_the_run` (cross-cutting, `crates/fa-cli/tests/cases.rs`, reading A7a's memoized `outcome(case)`).

**Row schema (§15 H9):** `procedure`, `version`, `case`, `expectation`, `fact`, `label` (`scheme_part` or `unlabelled`), `cited` (bool), `source` (the fact's source id).

**Label rule.** A documented entry is `scheme_part` only where the source names it part of the scheme (WorldCom F1–F13; BLMIS rows the trustee's complaint flags): the row's `source` must be the source of a sourced fact in the fact's basis closure (A3b's `fact_closure`). Nothing is labelled "legitimate": the denominators are the case's own labelled rows, never a negative class (§12.4).

**Consumer.** fa-4psc's calibration review reads the rows as case evidence beside its fa-gen corpus figures; nothing reports them as a rate.

**Gate.**
- Static (`check`): every row's `case`, `expectation` and `fact` resolve; `procedure`@`version` is a row of `registries/procedures.toml` and equals the expectation's; `label` is one of the two values; a `scheme_part` row's `source` meets the label rule; `cited` agrees with the expectation's declared cite component for that fact (A1c's `cite` field).
- Runtime (`case_calibration_cited_agrees_with_the_run`): the expectation's verdict in the same `cargo test` invocation (A7a: the worst of its per-(target, cell) lines) is PASS, and the cite set of its line for the row's fact (the line whose `<target>` is that fact) contains the fact iff `cited = true`. A row whose expectation is UNRUN reports UNRUN with the expectation's reason (A7a's `reason=`), and is counted, without failing the test (the rows are evidence, not claims); a FAIL fails it.
- **Branch cites.** Where the expectation's cite component is a branch status (B, as W-D-01's on F4 and F9), the cite set differs by cell, so `cited` reads the expectation's default cell (`<target>/default`, the cell A11a compares B components on), both gates compare that cell, and the log line names it (`cell=default`).
- **BLMIS rows before OD 2b.** M-D-01 and M-N-01 run on the `ledger` book, whose Exhibit B rows wait on OD 2b, so their runtime rows report UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` until then (§3.2b); their static gate runs now, and their runtime agreement is observed at the OD 2b landing.

## Tests & logging

- **Positive:** rows for W4's expectations (W-D-01, W-D-03, W-D-04, W-N-01, W-D-02) and M5's (M-D-01, M-N-01) load, every `expectation` and `fact` resolves, and each row's `cited` agrees with its expectation's verdict.
- **Planted negatives** (each a test-only copy of the table): `row_whose_fact_does_not_resolve_fails`; `row_whose_cited_disagrees_with_the_expectation_fails` (`cited = true` where the verdict does not cite the fact); `label_legitimate_is_refused` (a label outside {`scheme_part`, `unlabelled`}); `scheme_part_row_whose_source_is_not_in_the_basis_fails`; `row_at_a_stale_procedure_version_fails` (version 1 for `ponzi.net_investment`, registered at 3).
- **Logging:** runs in `cargo test -p fa-oracles` and the runner test; one line per row, `CALIBRATION <case> <expectation> <fact> <label> cited=<bool> [cell=default] PASS|FAIL|UNRUN [reason=…]`, and a failure names the row and the disagreeing verdict line. A final `CALIBRATION rows=<n> scheme_part=<n> unlabelled=<n> unrun=<n>` gives counts, never a rate.

## Notes

- **← W4:** WorldCom's D and N verdicts on `native` and `migration`. **← M5:** M-D-01 and M-N-01 on the BLMIS ledger book. The rows record their verdicts.
- **Never a "legitimate" denominator:** F2, F6, F7 and F8 are not legitimate look-alikes and must never enter a "legitimate / near-miss" denominator (§12.4; Appendix Z.2 records that mislabel's correction).
- **Version keying:** rows carry the procedure version, so a version bump (H1's v4, a predicate fix in H2, any H17 follow-on) requires the affected rows to be updated in the same landing; the stale-version negative enforces it.
- **fa-4psc** (in progress at 8196f5e40) is the consumer; this bead does not edit `lantern_calibration.toml`.
- **Landing gates.** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; `cargo test -p fa-oracles -p fa-cli --test cases`; `bash scripts/check.sh` for the data file.
- **No registry edit** (the table lives in `crates/fa-oracles/data/`).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: `case_calibration.toml` rows for the W4 and M5 expectations load, every `expectation` and `fact` resolves, and each row's `cited` agrees with its expectation's declared cite and with the verdict line of the same `cargo test` run (W4's rows now; M5's report UNRUN `reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` until OD 2b, then agree).
- [ ] negative: a planted row whose fact does not resolve fails; a planted row whose label or `cited` disagrees with its expectation's verdict fails; a label of "legitimate" is refused; a row at a stale procedure version fails.
- [ ] no-claim: the rows are case evidence with their own denominators; they are not a precision or recall figure and are never reported as a rate.

title: [cases] H10: fresh-agent campaign (fa-y6eu) on case books: examiner, investigator, litigation-consultant and receiver cards over fa-mcp
description:
## Why

docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §12.5: once two cases are green, a fresh-context agent is given only a case book (no facts file, no expectations), under an Agent-profile token, and works through fa-mcp. Case books are the sandboxes for four fa-y6eu cards: examiner (W, X), investigator (E), litigation consultant (L) and receiver (M). Case C has no campaign card: its one book holds a filer's own footing, which offers an agent nothing to find, and its README walkthrough is the CPA reader's. The measures are fa-y6eu's (useless_error outcomes and steps), and "Documented entries reached: k of n" is recorded per run as a count, never aggregated into a rate (§0.5). It tests the agent-ergonomics release gate (G3) on real-shaped books rather than on fa-demo sandboxes.

## What to build

- **Four cards** in fa-y6eu's card format. fa-y6eu's plan places them at `scenarios/agent-cards/*.md` (that directory does not exist at 8196f5e40; fa-y6eu creates it). The cards are examiner (WorldCom and SunPower books), investigator (Enron), litigation consultant (Lehman) and receiver (BLMIS); there is no card for C. Each card states the goal, the sandbox book and the success predicates. The list of documented entries a run is scored against (by fact id) stays with the grader, outside the agent-visible card, so the card leaks no expectation.
- **Sandbox preparation.** The CLI runner's outsider kit (`FA_CASES_OUT=<dir>`, §12.1, A12) writes each case's book directory and public key. The campaign copies only those two into a fresh run directory.
  - It never copies the kit's `VERIFY.txt`, bundles, canonical finding workpapers or ADS extract, nor anything under `crates/fa-oracles/cases/` (facts, expectations, README, `AGENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`). Those reveal the expected findings.
  - It keeps, outside the agent's view, the run log's fact↔vid map (A7a), which scores "reached".
- **Agent token.** Issued on the copied book with `fa capability issue --holder <agent label> --profile agent --op read --op produce … --out <new-file> --as <issuer> --grant issue_capability` (usage at `registries/verbs.toml:203`). It is then bound with `fa-mcp --book <dir> --token <file>` (`crates/fa-mcp/src/main.rs:163`). An Agent-profile token cannot write trunk (`FA-REF-013`); agents work on drafts.
- **Runs.** Fresh-context agents get only the card, the book and in-tool docs (`fa robot-docs`, MCP tool docs), launched through fa-y6eu's harness. The book-building and MCP-launch helpers come from A15's `crates/fa-mcp/tests/cases_mcp.rs`.
- **Per-run record.** fa-y6eu's useless_error outcomes and steps, and "Documented entries reached: k of n", as counts. A documented entry is *reached* when its entry VId (from the fact↔vid map) appears in a tool result the agent requested: a finding's cite, `explain entry`/`explain evidence`, `gl detail`. The plan does not define "reached"; this predicate is recorded in each card, and changing it is a card version change.
- First runs are on the two green cases this item depends on (W4's WorldCom books, X3's SunPower book).

## Tests & logging

- Each run's transcript, its book's tree hash and counts are recorded through fa-y6eu's harness, which logs every tool call and result. Regressions it surfaces are pinned as tests per fa-y6eu's own scope (each useless_error becomes a refusal-text or fix regression test).
- **Derived negatives:**
  - the sandbox step refuses to start a run whose run directory contains any file other than the book directory and its public key: a planted `facts.toml` copy is rejected as invalid, with the offending path named;
  - a card whose case book does not exist yet reports UNRUN, never a result.
- **Counts:** per run `reached k of n` is printed beside the card id and the book's tree hash; nothing sums runs into a rate.

## Notes

- **Why each edge:** fa-y6eu supplies the campaign harness, card format and measures; W4 and X3 are the "two green cases" (§12.5); A15 supplies the fa-mcp case runner.
- **E, L and M cards:** §15 gives H10 no edges to the Enron, Lehman or BLMIS items, so those cards report UNRUN until their books exist (E3/E4, L2–L4, M3–M7).
- Counts are per run and never become a rate or a claim about agents finding fraud (§0.5).
- The kit is never committed (ids vary per run, §3.4), so each campaign run regenerates its sandbox from a fresh runner pass.
- **Case directories** are the §3.2b names (`worldcom`, `xbrl`, `enron`, `lehman`, `blmis`); the sandbox step copies from `FA_CASES_OUT/<dir>/`.
- **Landing gates.** Code this item lands (the sandbox check) passes `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main and its tests; the cards are non-`.rs` files, so `bash scripts/check.sh` runs too.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: the examiner card runs on the WorldCom and SunPower case books with fresh agents given only the card, the book directory and its public key (copied from the outsider kit, never the kit's VERIFY.txt, bundles, workpapers or any case data file), under an Agent-profile token bound with `fa-mcp --token`; each run records useless_error outcomes, steps and "documented entries reached: k of n" as counts, with the card's recorded "reached" predicate and the book's tree hash.
- [ ] negative: a run whose run directory includes a facts, expectations or kit file is rejected as invalid, naming the path; a card whose case book does not exist reports UNRUN.
- [ ] no-claim: per-run counts on a handful of reconstructions; no rate, and nothing about any agent's ability to find fraud on real books.

title: [cases] H16: fa triage/next offer the audit program under an open audit, examination or investigation engagement, and never a placeholder
description:
## Why

Product finding H16 (docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md §13, §12.5): `fa triage` and `fa next` never offer the audit program when no finding run exists (`crates/fa-cli/src/triage.rs:798-890`). On an all-closed book they offer a write step with a placeholder, `fa period open <code>` (`:809-815`), which fa-mcp's own detector refuses (`crates/fa-mcp/src/detect.rs:251`). Agents are the primary operators, and first-try success from the product's own guidance is a release gate (AGENTS.md, Agent Ergonomics). A16 locks the current behaviour as a per-case ergonomics N; this change flips it.

## What to build

**Code** (`crates/fa-cli/src/triage.rs`, the next-steps survey at `:798-890` that `fa triage` (`book_triage`) and `fa next` (`next_step`) share; MCP `fa_orient_next` and `fa_orient_triage` (cluster `fa.orient`, `registries/verbs.toml:4115-4130`) dispatch through the same front door, so they follow):
- **Offer the audit program:** when the book has an open engagement of kind audit, examination or investigation (`fa engagement open <id> --kind audit|review|examination|investigation|litigation`, `registries/verbs.toml:736`; read with `fa::Book::engagements()`, `crates/fa/src/book.rs:1988`) and no finding run exists, the survey adds read-only steps `fa jet --json` and `fa procedure list --json` (both verbs are `writes = false`, `registries/verbs.toml:668-670`, `:680-683`), with a `why` naming the engagement.
- **No placeholder tokens:** the survey never emits a `<…>` placeholder token (§13 H16). Today it also emits `fa chart import <chart.json> --json` (`triage.rs:801`), `fa period create --fiscal-year <N> --json` (`:806`), `fa period open <code>` when no period is Future (`:813-814`), and `fa resolve --intent <resolution.json> --json` with its draft form `fa draft plan resolve-holds --intent <resolution.json> --json`, which fa-mcp's detector (`detect.rs:251`) does not all flag, so the test uses the any-`<…>`-token rule, not the detector's.
- **All-Closed fallback (§13):** on a book with no Open and no Future period, triage offers the read-only `fa period list --json` and names `fa period create --fiscal-year N+1 --json`, with N+1 computed from the latest fiscal year the book holds; both are concrete commands.
- **The other placeholder branches.** The plan fixes only the all-Closed fallback. For the rest the implementer replaces each token with a computed value or a concrete read-only offer (for example the year in `fa period create --fiscal-year` from the calendar's first declared year without created periods, and the template listing `fa chart templates --json` for an empty chart), and the any-token test is the gate.
- **Surfaces.** No new verb, flag, event or field: `next_actions` stays (command, why) pairs. If the `book_triage` or `next_step` event `doc` text or the `triage`/`next` usage lines are edited to describe the new steps, that is a `registries/verbs.toml` edit (global crate-verdict invalidation, `scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`), and an event `doc` change moves the robot-schema pin (event docs are in `registries/robot_schema/1.jsonl`; regenerate it and keep `the_robot_schema_is_pinned_byte_for_byte`, `crates/fa-cli/tests/robot_schema.rs:14`, green). A usage-only edit does not move the pin. The MCP `[[mcp.tool]]` rows for `triage` and `next` keep their flags, so the parity gate (`crates/fa-mcp/tests/parity.rs`) is unaffected; no write-authority row changes (no writing command is added).

## Tests & logging

- **fa-cli tests** in `crates/fa-cli/tests/triage.rs` (the triage test file), through the real binary with `check_robot_output`:
  - `open_investigation_engagement_offers_jet_and_procedure_list`: a book with an open investigation engagement and no finding run offers `fa jet --json` and `fa procedure list --json` in `next_actions`; `same_book_without_an_engagement_offers_no_audit_step`; `audit_steps_disappear_once_a_finding_run_exists` (the survey's existing "finding run" branch takes over);
  - `all_closed_book_offers_period_list_and_names_the_next_fiscal_year`: with FY2026 Closed and no Future period, `next_actions` holds `fa period list --json` and names `fa period create --fiscal-year 2027 --json`;
  - `no_triage_branch_emits_a_placeholder_token`: on every triage branch (no chart, no fiscal year, no Open period with or without a Future one, pending resolutions, the engagement branch) no `next_actions` entry contains a `<…>` token, in its command or its `why` (§13: "triage never emits a `<…>` placeholder token"; the acceptance reads all triage and next output).
- **MCP parity:** `fa_orient_next` returns the same steps as `fa next` on the investigation-engagement book, in `crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs` (under an Agent launch, `rank_for` at `triage.rs:919` may reorder but not drop a read step the session can run).
- **Planted negative:** `restored_placeholder_fails_the_any_token_test`: a test-only copy of the survey output with `fa chart import <chart.json> --json` restored fails the test, naming the branch and the token.
- **Binary-level flip:** A16's probe twin covers only its matcher; this item supplies the binary-level flip, observed when the probe runs on a case book (each opens an `investigation` engagement, §2.7) and finds a read-only `fa jet` offer.
- **Case effect:** each case's A16 guidance N then fails, as designed (`FAIL W-N-90 N native -/default audit_offered=true …`, `<case>` being the case letter), and is retired with a `Retired-tests:` trailer (§12.5, §16) in the same landing, so the case gate stays green: A16's generator (`fa_oracles::cases::guidance::guidance_n`) stops emitting `<case>-N-90`, and the probe's walk keeps running and logging what triage offers.

## Notes

- **No dependencies** (§15: H16 ← none). It flips §12.5's guidance N (A16; related link).
- **fa-g8em (triage, next and bare `fa`, open, P2)** works on the same survey (`triage.rs`). Its landed slices (StormyLion, per its comments) added triage fields (`register_watermark_lag`, `open_drafts`, `drafts_awaiting_promotion`, `finding_runs`, `open_findings_by_severity`, `pending_approvals`, `cases_awaiting_approval`), capability-ranked `fa next` (`rank_for`) and the draft form of the resolve step (`NextStep.draft`, the `fa draft plan resolve-holds --intent <resolution.json>` placeholder this bead removes); its open item is `unmatched_bank_lines`. It does not plan the audit-program offer, the any-`<…>`-token rule or the all-Closed fallback, so H16 carries them. Coordinate `triage.rs` edits with fa-g8em's claimant through Agent Mail, and keep fa-g8em's tests (`fields_match_dedicated_commands`, `next_respects_caller_capability`, `bare_fa_detects_book_and_daemon`, `an_agent_is_offered_a_draft_for_the_holds_it_cannot_resolve`, all in `crates/fa-cli/tests/triage.rs`) green: that last test asserts the Agent's offered command `fa draft new resolve-holds --json`, already concrete, and that its `why` names `fa draft plan resolve-holds --intent`. Today that `why` carries `<resolution.json>` (`triage.rs:872-875`, the `draft` field), so the any-token rule, which reads `why` too, needs the form named without the token (for example "… `fa draft plan resolve-holds --intent` with the resolution intent file …"); the test's substring check still holds.
- **fa-zgn (Engagement objects, in progress, LavenderSwan)** provides the engagements this bead reads (`Book::engagements`, `fa engagement open`); H16 reads them only and changes nothing in fa-zgn's scope.
- **Code check at 8196f5e40, other placeholders:** triage emits `fa chart import <chart.json> --json` (`triage.rs:801`), `fa period create --fiscal-year <N> --json` (`:806`), `fa period open <code>` when no period is Future (`:813-814`), and `fa resolve --intent <resolution.json> --json` with its draft form. `placeholder_in` (`detect.rs:251-283`) flags `<N>` and `<code>` but not `<chart.json>` or `<resolution.json>`, because a `.` fails its `wordy` test. That is why §12.5 and §13 define a placeholder as any `<…>` token.
- **Read-only, plan vs code.** `NextStep.writes` (`triage.rs:30-40`) is not emitted in `next_actions`, which are (command, why) pairs (`triage.rs:1003`, `:1124`). The plan defines read-only as a verb row with `writes = false` or a deciding `[[bound]]` rule with `ops = ["read"]` (§12.5, since polish round 2), so the offered `fa jet` and `fa procedure list` are read-only through their rows, and the fallback's `fa period list` through its `[[bound]]` rule (`registries/verbs.toml:5738-5741`; the `period` row itself is `writes = true`, `:148`). A16's walk follows all three. The flip still comes from the `fa jet` offer.
- The plan names audit, examination and investigation; review and litigation, the other registered engagement kinds, are left as they are.
- **Gates:** `bash scripts/tier0.sh` before main; `cargo test` (fa-cli, fa-mcp); `bash scripts/check.sh` if verbs.toml text or the robot-schema pin changes. The retired N-90 rows carry the `Retired-tests:` trailer in the same landing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: on a book with an open audit, examination or investigation engagement and no finding run, `fa triage`, `fa next` and MCP `fa_orient_next` offer read-only `fa jet` and `fa procedure list` entries; on an all-Closed book with no Future period, triage offers the read-only `fa period list` and names `fa period create --fiscal-year N+1`, with N+1 computed from the latest fiscal year.
- [ ] negative: no triage or next output on any test book contains a `<…>` token (including `<N>`, `<chart.json>`, `<resolution.json>`), and a planted one fails the test; each case's A16 guidance N (`<case>-N-90`) fails as designed on the real binary once this lands, and is retired with a trailer.
- [ ] no-claim: offering the audit program shows the commands are reachable from guidance; it does not show an agent will run them or that any finding matters.

title: [cases] H17: research whether Lantern findings should carry supersession lineage when a target is restated (W-D-07 / W-D-08)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] positive: a decision record, recorded as a comment on this bead under the fixed headings, answers the question for `expense.capitalization`, `jet.round_amounts` and `jet.post_closing` with the code anchors above (including whether the Replace-versus-Restates asymmetry of `live_postings_through`, `snapshot.rs:509-513`, is intended), and files a follow-on bead if a change is adopted, whose acceptance names the version bumps, both certificate tables, the tier rows, H9's rows and a planted-negative test.
- [ ] negative: a proposal that hides or edits the restated entry, rather than annotating findings or changing a predicate under a version bump, is rejected as contrary to append-only doctrine 5.
- [ ] no-claim: research only; W-D-07/W-D-08 stay locked observations until a product change lands, and a finding remains a finding, never an accusation.

title: [cases] H18: events.subsequent selects only periods whose latest transition is SoftClosed/Closed/Locked, not every period with any transition
description:
## Why
Product finding H18 (`docs/FORENSIC_CASE_STUDIES_PLAN.md` §13; related to L4's L-N-02, §8.3). `events.subsequent` is the Lantern procedure for "material postings, reversals, or restatements effective within `window_days` after a closed or soft-closed period boundary (or superseding an entry in an earlier period)" (its doc comment, `crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:598-601`; plan §11.7, AS 2801 / IAS 10). It is what an examiner runs to ask what was booked against a quarter after that quarter closed.

At 8196f5e40 the procedure decides which periods are "closed/soft-closed" by asking only whether a period has any recorded transition (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs:646-655`):

    // Identify closed/soft-closed periods and their end dates
    for (pcode, trs) in &snapshot.transitions {
        if !trs.is_empty() && let Some(p) = snapshot.periods.get(pcode) {
            closed_periods.push((pcode.clone(), p.end));
        }
    }

Every period is born `Future` and admits nothing until it is opened (`registries/admissibility.toml:55`), and `fa period open` is itself a journaled transition. `Snapshot::transitions` holds every `PeriodTransition` control by period, ascending by commit (`crates/fa-lantern/src/snapshot.rs:91`, filled at `:128-160`, each `Transition { recorded_at, from, to }`, `:73`). So every period that was ever opened counts as "closed", including one that is still Open. The effect is a false positive: an Adjusting, Reversal, Replacement, Restatement or PriorPeriodAdjustment entry (`cutoff.rs:689-696`) effective within `window_days` after the end of an Open period is reported as a subsequent event of that period (`cutoff.rs:705-715`). The comment and the registry summary say "closed or soft-closed"; the code does not do that. Claim type served: D and N (the case's L-N-02 reads this procedure; §5.2).

## What to build
**Code** (`crates/fa-lantern/src/cutoff.rs`, `SubsequentEvents::run`, `:617-744`):
- Select a period into `closed_periods` only when its latest transition at the snapshot's known-at ends in SoftClosed, Closed or Locked: `trs.last().map(|t| t.to)` is `PeriodState::SoftClosed | Closed | Locked` (the list is sorted by `recorded_at`, `snapshot.rs:191-194`). A period whose latest transition is to Open (opened, or reopened after a soft-close or close) is not selected.
- **Locked stays selected.** §13 now reads "select only periods whose latest transition is SoftClose, Close or Lock (Locked periods stay selected, as today)" (PLAN_DELTA after polish round 3; it earlier named SoftClose and Close only). v1 selects Locked periods, the procedure's own doc ("a closed or soft-closed period boundary") covers them, and only a Close reaches Locked (Closed → Locked). `subsequent_events_still_selects_a_locked_period` pins it.
- The prior-supersession path (`cutoff.rs:681-688`, `:699-704`) is unchanged: it compares effective dates of a superseding entry and its target and never consults period state.
- **Version bump.** `SubsequentEvents::version` (`cutoff.rs:611-613`) returns 2, the `registries/procedures.toml` row (`:1427-1447`, with its `window_days` and `min_amount` parameters) reads `version = 2` with a summary sentence naming the selection rule beside the v1 history, and `EXTENDED_CERTIFIABLE_PROCEDURES` (`crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/extended.rs:46`, `("events.subsequent", 1)`) becomes `("events.subsequent", 2)`; the length test (`crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/tests/extended.rs:51`, 41 rows) is unchanged because the row is replaced. `fa_lantern` refuses a procedure whose code version differs from its row (`crates/fa-lantern/src/lib.rs:1015-1018`) and `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs:1916` asserts agreement, so code and registry move in one landing. A certificate recorded under v1 still replays under v1 (replay keys on id and version).
- **fa-reference.** It has no naive model of this procedure: none of `fa_reference::lantern`'s functions (`crates/fa-reference/src/lantern.rs`; the ten A4r compares, `round_amounts` … `relative_size_factor_by_account`, plus `thin_descriptions`, `sequence_gaps`, `round_trips`, `structuring`, `trace`, the Benford tables and others) reads period transitions for subsequent events, so A4r reports `events.subsequent` targets `not_modelled`; no oracle change.
- **Fixtures.** Re-pin any certificate or golden whose output moves, naming each in the commit message. The existing fixture at `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs:4693-4701` soft-closes its January period (`:4340-4347`, `Open → SoftClosed`) and expects the Reversal `VId(92_006)` reported; its latest transition is SoftClosed, so it stays green under v2.

## Tests & logging
- **fa-lantern, beside the existing fixture** (`crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs`, its `harness()` / `h.snapshot()` pattern with `snapshot.transitions.insert`, `:4229-4347`, and `run_over`):
  - `subsequent_events_never_selects_a_period_that_was_only_opened` (the planted negative is v1's behaviour): monthly periods P1, P2, P3; P1's transitions `Future → Open, Open → Closed`; P2 and P3 `Future → Open` only. Entry A, an Adjusting entry of at least `min_amount` effective on P2's 10th day: reported under v2, citing P1 (its end precedes A by 10 days, within `window_days` = 30). Entry B, the same shape effective on P3's 10th day: 10 days after P2's end and more than 30 after P1's, so v1 reports it (P2 has a transition) and v2 must not. The test asserts B's absence under v2 and records, in a comment and a companion assertion over a `v1_selection` test-only copy of the old predicate, that the old rule reports it.
  - `subsequent_events_never_selects_a_period_reopened_after_soft_close`: P2's transitions `Future → Open, Open → SoftClosed, SoftClosed → Open`; B is not reported.
  - `subsequent_events_still_selects_a_locked_period`: P1 `… → Closed → Locked`; A is reported (the Locked reading above).
  - `subsequent_events_window_boundary`: an entry effective exactly `window_days` after P1's end is reported, one day later is not (the `days <= window_days` test, `cutoff.rs:709`).
- **Version agreement.** `crates/fa-lantern/tests/lantern.rs:1916` and `crates/fa/src/procedure_certificate/tests/extended.rs:51-60` pass at version 2.
- **CLI** (`crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs`, beside the existing `fa procedure run` tests, `:14335-14361`, on the custom-calendar flow of `:15494-15530`): a book with P1 closed (`fa period close --reason … --yes`) and P2 opened only; `fa finding record events.subsequent --json` records a run whose findings (`fa finding list --certificate C:<run> --json`) cite exactly entry A, never B; `fa finding export --certificate C:<run> --export-format canonical --out <f>` then `fa finding replay <f> --certificate C:<run> --known-at <seq>` reproduces it. (`fa procedure run` takes no `--certify`, `registries/verbs.toml:668-677`; a certified run is `fa finding record`.)
- **Case regression (L4, related).** L4's L-N-02 soft-closes every quarter whose end precedes its last observation (L4's book context), so its predicted verdict does not depend on the defect. It runs on the Lehman `ledger` book, built from the Valukas dated series, so until OD 2b commits that series its lines print `UNRUN … reason=rows file not committed (OD 2b)` (L4, §3.2b) and its re-check against v2 runs at the OD 2b landing; the fa-lantern and CLI tests above are H18's evidence meanwhile; when H18 lands, L4's rows that print `events.subsequent@1` are re-pinned to `@2`, the Lehman `case.toml` capability token moves with them (A13), and the A4 tier row for `events.subsequent` is re-seeded with a fresh two-reader classification (K-TIER fails it until then). L4 re-checks L-N-02's branch cells against v2.
- **Logging.** Test failures print the period code, its transitions and the entry's effective date; runner lines follow A7a's notation, one per (expectation, target, cell) (`PASS L-N-02 N ledger <target>/<cell> … events.subsequent@2 …`), and each `fa finding record` step's JSONL record carries `finding_procedure = events.subsequent` (§3.5).
- The two planted-negative names carry `never`, a token the gate-evidence ratchet counts (`scripts/gate_evidence_check.sh:151-155`).

## Notes
- **No dependencies** (§15: "H18 (`events.subsequent` period selection) ← none. L4 re-checks L-N-02 when it lands"). Related: L4 (fa-yugf.66; L4 carries the `related` link).
- **Registry edit.** `registries/procedures.toml` changes, so every crate verdict is invalidated (`scripts/crate_verdicts.py:13-15`); the landing states it. The robot-schema pin carries no procedure rows and does not move.
- **Tier row and coverage.** The version and row-digest change invalidates `events.subsequent`'s A4 tier row (K-TIER). A13's coverage row names the procedure id, not its version, so the closure is unaffected; the declaring `case.toml` token moves (above).
- **H9.** No case calibration row names `events.subsequent` (H9's rows are W4's and M5's), so none moves.

title: The CONTROLS relation is reused for Entry→MigrationRun edges: give migration membership its own relation so related-party/control traversals never walk into migration runs

book still reads correctly.

title: Cryptographic segregation of duties: approvals and attestations signed by principal keys, verified at commit; `--as <human>` without that human's key cannot satisfy dual control; doctor warns when an agent process can read book.keys
description:
## WHY
At 0d338c0 any CLI caller can claim any principal and grant: `principal(args)` = `principal_vid(--as or "operator")`
(fa-cli/src/cli.rs:3069-3071); `Capability::embedded` self-issues a Human capability with any ops
(fa-policy/src/capability.rs:845-856; used at cli.rs:1102). Tokens (fa capability issue, --token, FA_TOKEN) exist but are
opt-in. The CLI's own dual-control test gets its "second principal" by passing `--as controller` from the same process.
So SoD, the Agent profile and the collusion mitigation hold only against agents with no shell access to the book
directory. fa-yok (P0) keeps the embedded-owner posture by design; this bead makes dual control independent of it.

## WHAT
Builds on fa-kae (principal Ed25519 keys as TrustAnchorSet rows) and fa-651f (Principal objects): every Approval and
Attestation carries a signature by the approving principal's key held by the client; the kernel verifies against the key
valid at that sequence; SoD counts distinct verified signers, not distinct names; embedded-owner posture still works for
single-principal operations but cannot manufacture a second approver; every robot envelope's `authority` names the
posture; `fa doctor` warns when the invoking process (or an agent-profile session) can read book.keys.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: two distinct key holders approve a dual-control Lock; both signatures verify in-kernel and in fa-verify.
- [ ] planted negatives: same process with `--as controller --as reviewer` and one key cannot reach two approvals; a
  signature over a different proposal digest refused; a key rotated out before the approval's sequence refused.

```acceptance-tests
fa-journal::policy::dual_control_requires_two_verified_signers
fa-cli::cli::as_flag_cannot_manufacture_second_approver
fa-verify::tests::bundle_approval_signatures_verify
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: signature transcript construction and verification; key-validity windows. E2E: two-terminal-style test with two distinct key files performing a dual-control Lock via the real binary; a bundle of it verified by fa-verify. Logging: approvals log signer key id, transcript digest and validity window.

title: Wire Teller to the surfaces: fa bank import (camt.053/052, BAI2, OFX, MT940, CSV) as BankLine documents and fa bank match (scoreboard WF-ACM-03)
description:
## Why (found 2026-10-18 by claude-opus-5-5; scoreboard row WF-ACM-03)
Vision row VC-15 ("the agent closes a month": import and match a CAMT.053 statement) has no surface. Every bank statement parser exists, tested and fuzzed, in fa-formats::bank:
- camt.053 and camt.052;
- BAI2;
- OFX/QBO;
- MT940;
- CSV.
Reconciliation folds exist in fa-registers::reconciliation and the oracle (fa-2ek, closed 2026-10-16). But `fa bank import` does not exist, so no surface can import a statement. Until 2026-10-18 the scoreboard row cited fa-9x4, a bead that was never in the tracker.

## What to build
1. `fa bank import <statement> --format camt053|camt052|bai2|ofx|mt940|csv --account <code>`. It records the statement as a content-addressed Docket document with its import receipt, and every line as a BankLine document DERIVED_FROM it. Re-importing the same statement is idempotent by content.
2. `fa bank match` over the existing matching and decision-card logic, with the deterministic pinned fallback. Match decisions are journaled objects and never change an amount.
3. verbs.toml rows (verbs, events, an on-demand MCP cluster fa.teller or fa.evidence tools), parity, and the robot-schema pin.

## Acceptance
- The scoreboard row WF-ACM-03 works.
- A camt.053 fixture imports, and its lines reconcile against posted cash entries.
- A duplicate import writes nothing.
- A statement whose closing balance does not equal opening plus lines is refused (verify_internal_balance).
- Planted negative: a float amount in a CSV statement is refused.

fd68920a raised FA-REF-083 DOCUMENT_INTAKE with exit `refusal` from two places:
- fa-journal import/bank.rs `continuity()`;
- fa bank.rs `predecessor_error()`, which covers the different bank account or currency, the chain-depth bound, and a history that already contains this source statement.

The catalog row for FA-REF-083 is `usage`, and ten other sites raise it with `usage` for malformed uploads. As a result, `the_catalog_and_every_declared_refusal_agree_three_ways` had failed on main since fd68920a.

Both continuity functions now raise a new additive code: FA-REF-165 BANK_CONTINUITY (owner fa-journal, exit refusal, cite plan §9.5). FA-REF-083 is unchanged.

`predecessor_mismatches_refuse_without_publishing_any_new_import` used to assert only `status != 0`. It now asserts exit 3 and FA-REF-165 for each of: gap, opening, date, bank, self, and sequence overflow. I traced each case to `continuity()` or `predecessor_error()`.

Not changed:
- The owner's commit note says scratch replay with renumbered sequences still needs an explicit SeqMap bridge for the original predecessor coordinate.

**Exact retry after linkage (2b8aa746).** A read-only review of fd68920a found one behavior defect.
- **The sequence:** import S unlinked (M1/R1); link S to its predecessor (M2 plus the link); repeat the first import exactly.
- **The bug:** that repeat was refused with FA-REF-032, exit 6, because the BankStatementLink check ran before the exact-manifest receipt lookup.

- **Also fixed:** a non-manifest `--previous-import` no longer says "--import must name …"; the fix names the right flag for each verb.

title: Embedded API conformance: &Cx on every Book method that does I/O, a Coordinate type, and a capability on every read
description:
## WHY
Plan §15.2 "Every method takes &Cx"; doctrine 3 (Cx everywhere) and 8 (authorization precedes observation). The sync
`fa::Book` opens and reads without a Cx (book.rs:614/643/675) and `Book::trial_balance(periods)` takes no capability
(book.rs:3841); the fa client runs daemon socket I/O under Budget::INFINITE (client.rs:47). AsyncBook does take
PurposeContexts — the sync facade should be a thin adapter that still names its context.

## WHAT
Sync Book methods take `&Cx` (or a purpose context) and a capability on reads; introduce `Coordinate {branch, known_at,
effective}` per §4.8 accepted by every read; client socket I/O under a bounded budget. Coordinate with fa-0x0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: every pub Book method that touches the database takes a context; cancellation of a long TB is observed.
- [ ] planted negative: a new pub Book read without a capability parameter fails an API lint (xtask).

```acceptance-tests
fa::book::tests::sync_reads_require_capability_and_context
tools/xtask::api_lint::tests::book_reads_require_capability
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: API lint over the pub surface. E2E: cancellation of a long TB through the sync facade observed within one checkpoint. Logging: lint prints offending signatures.

title: Bulk migration protocol at plan scale: staged chunk manifests over the live loader with one finalizing publication; entries larger than one row through fa-nd7g chunks
description:
## WHY
Plan §5.8 and Appendix G: a 50M-line migration uses the substrate bulk protocol — chunked, gap-free, source-row-digested
manifests, staged and finalized through one transaction. Today each MigrationRun chunk is an ordinary Entry publication
(two fsyncs) and an Entry must fit one 16 KiB substrate row (about 500 legs; fa-fdt), so 50M lines means 100k+
publications and no single activation. MigrationRun semantics (modes, invisible staging, tie-out) are otherwise WORKING
(fa-journal/src/migration.rs).

## WHAT
Use the live bounded loader (`bulk_load`, `BulkLoadPolicy`, `BulkLoadCheckpoint`; Appendix H R-BULK) under
FrankenAccounting-level chunk manifests (gap-free sequence, source-row digests, resume token journaled); Finalize stays one
control publication; large entries ride the fa-nd7g chunked object layer. Update operation_costs bulk row truthfully.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] positive: a 1M-line fa-gen legacy import completes with ≤ N publications (N registered), resumes after a crash at
  every chunk boundary, and ties out; the 50M timing belongs to fa-ykbp.
- [ ] planted negatives: a gap in chunk sequence refuses Finalize; a corrupted source-row digest refuses the chunk.

```acceptance-tests
fa-registers::migration::bulk_import_one_million_lines_bounded_publications
fa-registers::migration::bulk_import_resumes_after_crash_at_chunk_boundary
fa-registers::migration::finalize_refuses_chunk_gap
```

## TESTS & LOGGING
Unit: chunk manifest codec, gap detection, digest checks. E2E: fa-cli `fa migrate import` of a 1M-line fa-gen legacy export with a crash injected at a chunk boundary (lab VFS where available), resumed, finalized, tie-out verified. Logging: per chunk {seq, rows, digest, publication seq, duration}; publication count reported.

description:

   fa-kaf7) spliced `the_audit_cluster_draws_and_evaluates_the_clis_sample` into the middle of
   `inline_fx_rates_keep_agent_provenance_and_functional_reports_match_the_cli` at its `cli_data(&[`.

   - fa-registry lib `g0::tests::embedded_g0_registries_parse_and_agree_with_code` (25 vs 24)
   - fa-verbs lib `tests::inconsistent_registries_are_refused` (planted mutation no longer changes the text)
   - registry-check `tests::real_workspace_registries_pass` ("mcp.tool count 41 on the default surface exceeds plan §15.4
     limit of 40")
   - fa-mcp lib `registry::tests::finding_run_discovery_preserves_cursor_and_cutoff_under_read_only_authority` (41 vs 40)
   - fa-mcp parity `no_cluster_has_more_than_seven_tools_and_the_limit_is_seven`,
     `every_verb_and_subcommand_is_one_tool_or_a_registered_exclusion` (bank reconcile exclusion),
     `closing_reads_lower_to_exact_history_and_mutations_remain_host_only` (3 vs 2)
3. `DeltaCursorRetired { asked: CommitSeq(0), retained_after: …}` after reopen (plan §5.3 contract: call
   ensure_delta_window after every open; never read from 0 on a reopened book):
   - fa lib: settlement_group::tests::review::complete_proposal_approval_refresh_reopen_and_exact_commit_retry;
     settlement_group_review::tests::approval::independent_approver_without_post_authority_records_one_full_proposal_approval;
     settlement_group_review::tests::reopened_review_accepts_approval_publications_then_one_commit_and_exact_plan_retry;
     settlement_review::tests::approval_publication_reopen_and_resume_preserve_the_exact_payment_and_retry_receipt
   - fa allocation_review: portable_review_can_be_planned_after_reopen_without_resealing_the_description;
     approval::approval_after_restart_uses_original_ciphertext_and_current_authority
   - fa balance_allocation: independently_saved_source_and_review_can_be_revalidated_after_reopen
   - fa balance_allocation_review: only_saved_bytes_and_one_digest_survive_the_entire_approval_posting_lifecycle;
     credit_source_with_signed_rounding_residual_survives_reopen
4. Behavioral regressions:
   - fa-cli fx_revaluation (2): retained_review_plan_and_cli_post_preserve_signed_cumulative_adjustments_and_exact_retries;
     a_later_invoice_invalidates_saved_review_and_plan_without_publishing_stale_amounts (panic at fx_revaluation.rs:28 "class")
   - fa-cli fx_stock (2): known_at_bounded_reader_can_read_its_stock_prefix_after_later_period_postings;
     historical_period_stock_hydrates_cold_compacted_history_before_resolving_the_period (exit 7, expected 0)
   - fa-registers fx_stock: migration_stock_appears_only_at_finalization_and_uses_its_activation_watermark
     (Kernel(Corrupt("migration visibility integrity: run … has an invalid control lifecycle")))
   - fa-cli read_scope: every_command_that_does_not_judge_its_reach_refuses_a_scoped_token (FA-REF-007 vs FA-REF-011)
   - fa-cli cli: audit_samples_are_reproducible_from_the_seed_at_a_recorded_sequence (issued-token auditor refused);
     allocate_and_settle_review_approve_plan_and_commit_workflows
   - fa-journal bank_matches: reconciliation_replay::scratch_refuses_cash_match_and_import_sources_hidden_as_deleted_maintenance
     (FA-REF-113)
5. Possibly host-specific (confirm on a Linux gate worker before fixing):
   - fa-verify evidence_prefix_cli: non_utf8_prefix_checkpoint_and_document_paths_remain_usable (macOS APFS: "Illegal byte
     sequence") — make the test skip with an explicit UNRUN reason on filesystems that reject non-UTF-8 names.
   - fa-cli daily_usage: daemon_issuer_credentials_stay_inside_the_configured_files_root (likely /var vs /private/var
     canonicalization).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `git archive 0d338c0 | tar -x -C <empty-dir>` (an isolated tree, so concurrent folds cannot change files mid-build).
2. In that dir: `rch exec -- cargo check -p fa-mcp --tests` → "mismatched closing delimiter" at crates/fa-mcp/tests/e2e_stdio.rs:3957/3985.

- [ ] host-specific tests either pass on macOS or report an explicit skip reason, never a silent pass.

**What the branch does:**

  - **Open** journals the Engagement: kind, firm principal, capability commitment, scope periods and the stated materiality parameters in the base unit, with 0 <= clearly trivial <= performance <= overall.
  - **Propose** journals a draft correcting entry. It never posts. It must balance per unit on posting leaves dated in scope, and it is numbered by compare-and-set.
  - **Book** names the committed entry that makes the correction: a standing trunk posting (not pending, not a migration chunk, not reversed or replaced), recorded after the proposal, effective in the proposal's scope period, with exactly the proposal's legs. One entry books one proposal; a concurrent booking of the same entry, or a concurrent reversal of it, conflicts at commit. Booking reads the entry, so it needs `read` as well as `produce` (kernel, CLI admission and the bound rule).
  - **Pass** records a reason from the new `reason_codes.toml` scope `adjustment_pass`.
  - A proposal is decided once (FA-REF-181). New refusal codes are FA-REF-180..184.
- **Authority:** `sod_policy.toml` rules `engagement-open|propose|book|pass` require `produce`, which the Auditor template holds. An Agent is refused for every one of them (tested for open, propose, book and pass).
- **CLI:**
  - `fa engagement open|list|show|sud` and `fa adjustment propose|book|pass`.
  - Propose's default key is the proposal's content, so an identical retry dedupes and different proposals never collide.
  - **MCP:** `engagement` and `adjustment` tools in the on-demand `fa.audit` cluster.
- **`fa engagement sud`** (plan `audit.sud`):
  - the effect on income, assets, liabilities and equity of each passed proposal, and of each booked one whose entry was later reversed or replaced (the decision stays on the record with `superseded_by`), had the correction been booked and stood;
  - legs in other units are listed, never converted;
  - rollover and iron-curtain totals;
  - mechanical comparisons with clearly trivial, performance and overall.
  - No prior-period engagement is carried forward yet, so the two totals sum the same items. The event says so with `prior_period_carry_forward: false`.
- **Shipped earlier for this bead's "sample.mus evaluate" item:** `fa sample evaluate`, the Stringer UML. 9747767e adds the plan's planned MUS interval from tolerable and expected misstatement.

**Review:** a fresh-context review of the uncompiled slice found a borrow error, an MCP tool whose stdin flag was not exposed (the registry would not load), booking holes (reversed, pending, out-of-period and earlier entries were accepted), a produce-only principal able to probe entries, two exit classes that disagreed with the catalog, an integer_flags collision with `fa time approve --proposal`, and a per-proposal full edge scan. All are fixed in the last commit of the range; the reviewer's SoD suggestion (booker != poster) was not taken, because no registered rule makes it a breach.

**Still open:**

- **Represented and Confirmed attestations.** Confirmed is audit-grade only from the engagement's principal (AS 2310).
- **SUD per statement line**, through a statement definition rather than per line type.
- **Tests not written:** an fa-journal lab test that interleaves the concurrent paths (decide-once compare-and-set, two bookings of one entry, booking vs reversal), and a CLI case booking a pending entry.

- The out-of-period scan read the stored `effective_period`, which a dated intent never sets. It now resolves the period from the date (`fa_registers::entry_period`).

Both pass their targeted tests (fa-notary 1/0, fa-cli engagement); they land after their own gate.

title: Reversal effective date must fall in the target's period or later, and only registered classes may target a special period (Adjustment/Closing/Opening) — enforced in the kernel and independently in the oracle
description:
WHY (verified at e606b46): plan §8.1 "Reversal: exact negation of one target entry, same or later period"; §7.3 "only Adjusting, Closing, Elimination, Revision, Restatement, and Migration classes may target a special period, and a Normal target is the default". (a) The reversal path (crates/fa-journal/src/post.rs:1218-1399) checks target existence, exact side-swap and reversed-once but not that the reversal's effective date/period is ≥ the target's; the oracle has the same omission (crates/fa-reference/src/lib.rs:1766-1795), so the differential cannot catch it — a reversal can be back-dated into an earlier period than the fact it reverses. (b) Period resolution accepts `effective_period` naming a live Adjustment/Closing/Opening period for any admitted class (crates/fa-time/src/period.rs:208-216; no class check in post.rs:617-638), so an Original can be routed into adjustment period 13.

WHAT: (1) registry: add a `special_period_classes` table (or `[[kind]]` class rows) in registries/admissibility.toml naming exactly the classes allowed per special kind; kernel and oracle both derive from it (oracle via its own reader, fa-vfu). (2) kernel: after resolving the target (point witness on the target entry), resolve both periods in the calendar's order and refuse a reversal whose period precedes the target's (new FA-REF code, catalog row with fix "post the reversal in <target period> or a later open period"); refuse special-period targeting by unlisted classes (FA-REF-010 family). (3) oracle: independent implementation of both rules.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: same-period and later-period reversals commit; Adjusting into P13 commits; [ ] planted negatives: reversal dated one period before its target → refused; Original with effective_period = P13 → refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-03, FA-INV-08) + differential + exhaustive class × kind test generated from the registry; [ ] consumers: fa-oz3, fa-4o0 (close), fa-xwv; [ ] no-claim boundary: period ordering per the book's calendar order, not civil-date order alone (P12 vs P13 share dates).

TESTS: genesis.rs negatives; fa-registry exhaustive table test; differential with seeds.
close_reason: Implemented fiscal-period chronological ordering and special_period_classes admission for reversals (FA-REF-053) in fa-journal and fa-reference; verified by crates/fa-journal/tests/genesis.rs::reversals_cannot_precede_the_target_period_but_may_use_an_earlier_day_in_it and special_period_classes_and_reversal_order_are_enforced_even_on_shared_dates.

comments.text: Implementation trap found during fresh source review (c2137f3): FiscalCalendar::periods_for_year in crates/fa-time/src/calendar.rs assigns Opening ordinal normal_count+1 and appends it after all normal periods, even though its effective date is the fiscal-year start. Therefore neither raw vector position nor (fiscal_year, ordinal) is a valid chronological comparison for the reversal rule: Opening-to-P01 would be falsely refused. Civil date alone also cannot distinguish final Normal vs Adjustment vs Closing. Define the semantic calendar order explicitly (Opening before normals/Historical, then adjustments, then Closing, with per-kind ordinal ordering and fiscal year), check it against normative period law, and include Opening-to-P01 and same-date final-Normal/Adjustment/Closing cases alongside prior-period refusal. Do not mutate durable existing ordinals to make comparison convenient. Source reconnaissance only; no implementation or runtime claim.
